title: Pengaruh Faktor Makroekonomi Terhadap Dana Pihak Ketiga dan Market Share pada Bank Umum Syariah di Indonesia Tahun 2020-2024
abstract: This research investigates the impact of broad economic factors, specifically inflation, interest rates, and currency exchange rates, on Third Party Funds (DPK) and the market presence of Islamic commercial banks in Indonesia from 2020 to 2024. Even though Islamic banks do not operate on an interest-based model, macroeconomic variables such as inflationary trends, primary interest rates, and fluctuations in exchange rates can still influence customer savings behavior and the ability of Islamic banks to grow their market share. This study utilizes a quantitative methodology involving multiple linear regression analysis. The secondary data used in this analysis were sourced from official reports provided by Bank Indonesia, the Financial Services Authority, and Statistics Indonesia. The research results reveal that inflation does not have a noticeable effect on Third Party Funds; however, interest rates and exchange rates significantly impact these funds. On the other hand, inflation plays a key role in market share dynamics, while interest rates and exchange rates show no significant effect on the market share of Islamic commercial banks. These findings offer crucial insights for regulators and professionals in the Islamic banking sector to formulate strategies aimed at enhancing fund mobilization and ensuring the stability of fund accumulation, especially amidst economic fluctua…
venue: Jurnal BAABU AL-ILMI: Ekonomi dan Perbankan Syariah

title: Consumers’ motivations behind sustainable clothing consumption in an emerging market: a means-end approach
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the underlying motivations influencing Millennials and Generation Z to consume sustainable clothing. The objective is to uncover how these consumer groups connect product attributes to deeper personal values through the lens of the Means-End Chain (MEC) theory. Design/methodology/approach This qualitative study uses the means-end theory and laddering technique to examine the motivational values of Millennials and Generation Z consumers. This approach reveals how consumers evaluate product attributes based on benefits that align with their values. Findings The study identifies key attributes such as quality, recyclability, sustainable material, sweatshop-free labour conditions, style, price and cruelty-free options as significant to both cohorts. These attributes are linked to higher-order values, including peace of mind, conservation of resources, planetary well-being, environmental protection, self-confidence, physical well-being, social justice, self-expression, social recognition and biodiversity protection. Notably, generational differences emerge in the prioritisation and interpretation of these values. Practical implications The findings offer actionable insights for sustainable fashion brands and marketers by providing a checklist of attributes, benefits and values. By aligning product development and marketing strategies with the i…

title: Making sense of barriers to integrating into the Quebec labour market: the experiences of Anglophone highly skilled African immigrants
abstract: Purpose Highly skilled African immigrants (HSAIs) in Quebec often encounter several challenges when seeking employment in the Canadian labour market. Despite their qualifications and experience, HSAIs regularly face higher unemployment rates and lower wages than non-immigrant workers, primarily due to racial and ethnic discrimination. The study utilized a qualitative methodology involving in-depth interviews with 16 HSAIs across Montreal, exploring their lived experiences and the intersecting challenges at the crux of race, immigration status, and professional identity. Design/methodology/approach The study utilized a qualitative methodology involving in-depth interviews with 16 HSAIs across Montreal, exploring their lived experiences and the intersecting challenges at the crux of race, immigration status, and professional identity. Findings Through a thematic analysis, the key findings reveal that proficiency in French is not just a linguistic requirement but a gatekeeper to employment opportunities and social integration. Furthermore, HSAIs' foreign qualifications are often undervalued, exacerbating the struggle to find appropriate employment that aligns with their expertise. The study also highlights the role of systemic discrimination, where African immigrants are unfavourably stereotyped, affecting their job prospects and upward mobility within Quebec's labour market. title: Climate policy uncertainty and domestic–international grain-market risk spillovers: a TVP-VAR-BK analysis with machine learning early warning
abstract: Background Climate-policy transition uncertainty may affect grain-market risk transmission. Methods We use 2010–2025 daily data for Chinese and US corn and wheat, US soybean landed cost, and GCPU in a TVP-VAR-BK connectedness model and machine-learning warning exercise. Results TCI averages 15.29% and peaks at 57.32%; short-horizon transmission dominates; XGBoost achieves PR-AUC of 0.986/0.949/0.781 at 1/5/20-period horizons. Conclusion Climate-policy uncertainty is dynamically associated with grain-market risk and can support market-stability monitoring, but the evidence is associational rather than causal.

title: Leaf Spot Disease in Oil Palm (Elaeis guineensis Jacq.) Nurseries in Tanah Laut Regency
abstract: The nursery stage is a critical phase determining the optimal growth of oil palm plants in the field; seedlings are particularly susceptible to leaf spot disease, which can manifest from the early nursery stage through to the production phase. This study aimed to analyze the incidence and severity of leaf spot disease in oil palm nurseries in Tanah Laut Regency. A survey method employing stratified purposive sampling and supporting questionnaires was used, with observations conducted diagonally on 125 sample plants per location. Data were analyzed descriptively by tabulating disease incidence and severity. The results showed an average disease incidence of 40% and a severity level of 31%, both falling into the moderate category. Soil pH and moisture levels were relatively optimal for oil palm nurseries, ranging from 5.0 to 6.5 and 60% to 90%, respectively. Fungicides frequently used by farmers in the field included Antracol (active ingredient: 70% Propineb) and AmistarTop (active ingredients: azoxystrobin and difenoconazole).

title: Investigating the Effectiveness of Inquiry-Based Hands-on Activities and ICT Simulations in Teaching Electricity Concepts to Elementary Students
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of two different instructional approaches for teaching basic electricity concepts in primary education: an inquiry-based hands-on intervention using experimental activities and a technology-supported intervention using an ICT simulation environment. The study focuses on students’ understanding of electricity, electrical circuits, conductors and insulators. The sample consisted of 35 students from the 3rd Primary School of Ioannina: 16 fifth-grade students participated in the hands-on inquiry intervention, and 19 sixth-grade students participated in the ICT-based intervention using the Edison virtual environment. A structured questionnaire was administered before and after the interventions to record students’ prior conceptions, identify alternative ideas, and measure conceptual improvement. The findings show that both approaches contributed to improved learning outcomes. The fifth-grade hands-on inquiry group achieved higher final achievement on most questionnaire items, while the sixth-grade ICT group often showed larger percentage gains due to lower initial performance. Overall, the results support the educational value of both experimental and virtual learning environments, with the hands-on inquiry approach appearing more effective for final conceptual understanding in this study. The results also indicate that simulations can suppo…

title: Beyond the white cube: a practice-oriented theory of the art museum
abstract: Purpose This article develops a practice-oriented theory of the art museum to address the tension between traditional institution-focused theories and the need to attract a diverse public. It posits that a museum's function emerges dynamically from visitor practices, with value co-produced through the interplay of visitor behavior and service design, rather than being institutionally predetermined. Design/methodology/approach A structured, participant observation study was conducted across 30 geographically and typologically diverse art museums. Data from field notes, visual documentation and archival materials were analyzed using a three-stage grounded theory approach (open, axial and selective coding) to identify and categorize core visitor practices. Findings The analysis reveals four distinct, co-existing visitor practices: (1) Aesthetic Wandering (contemplative exploration), (2) Goal-oriented Learning (structured education), (3) Social Performance (identity performance and sharing) and (4) Community Use (utilizing the museum as a “third place”). These practices emerge through interaction with service design: Aesthetic Wandering is facilitated by white cube spaces, Goal-oriented Learning by interpretive technologies, Social Performance by immersive installations and Community Use by amenities and policies. The white cube service design partially supports the first two but i…

title: Finding the marketing sweet spot: when and where it works best
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the relationship between marketing intensity (MI), research and development (R&D) intensity and firm performance (FP) in the pharmaceutical sector in India. Specifically, it explores R&D intensity, listing status and product complexity as potential moderators in shaping the relationship between MI and FP. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of 948 Indian pharmaceutical firms from 2010 to 2024, this study applies a generalized method of moments (GMM) estimator to test the main effects and moderation effects. Findings The results indicate strong linkages between MI and FP. Specifically, it has a strong positive impact on firms operating in a moderately R&D-intensive sector, while the relationship becomes negative in extremely low or very high R&D sectors. Furthermore, R&D exhibits threshold effects, documenting insignificant relationships in the short term and positive and significant effects in the long run. Research limitations/implications The study findings are based on data from Indian pharmaceutical firms, which may limit their generalizability to other sectors. Future research should explore the cross-sectoral and international settings. Practical implications Managers can enhance FP by aligning R&D and marketing efforts based on product complexity to boost marketing effectiveness. Social implications The strategic integration of R&D …

title: Meat your conscience: a semiotic square analysis of meat consumption through the lens of self-awareness theory
abstract: Purpose Meat consumption is increasingly contested because of health risks, environmental impacts and animal welfare concerns. However, the shift towards plant-based diets remains underexplored in marketing research. This study aims to examine how consumers make sense of their dietary choices – whether to continue eating or to reject meat. Design/methodology/approach This study uses an exploratory qualitative design, drawing on semi-structured interviews with 21 participants representing meat and meat-free dietary profiles. The participants were recruited through purposive convenience sampling. The interview transcripts were systematically analysed using a lexical and thematic approach. Self-awareness theory (SAT) was then mobilised as an interpretive lens, first to make sense of the emerging themes and subsequently to structure a semiotic square analysis, revealing and clarifying the semantic meaning categories underlying dietary choices. Findings The semiotic square identifies four consumer typologies – the Convinced Reflective, the Tormented Silent, the Committed Activist and the Anxious Conformist. These profiles illustrate how meat consumption or rejection relates to the interplay between private self-awareness (self-affirmation versus self-criticism) and public self-awareness (commitment versus conformity). Across the profiles, choices are shaped by intertwined hedonic, u…
venue: Qualitative Market Research: An International Journal

title: Logistics HR Capabilities, Iot Integration, and Service Quality on Operational Performance: Mediating Delivery Timeliness
abstract: Background: The development of digital logistics demands companies to improve the speed, accuracy, transparency, and quality of operations. This study seeks to examine how logistics human resource capabilities, Internet of Things (IoT) integration, and service quality influence the company's operational performance, both directly and via delivery timeliness acting as a mediating variable within the digital logistics services of PT Pos Indonesia (Persero). Method: This research applies a quantitative approach using the Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (SEM-PLS) method operated through SmartPLS. Data were collected from 145 internal respondents who were familiar with digital logistics services, Service Level Agreements, tracking systems, service quality, logistics HR capabilities, and operational performance. The analysis includes testing measurement models, structural models, hypotheses, and mediating effects. This research emphasizes the importance of employee capabilities, technology integration, and service quality in improving delivery timeliness and operational performance. Results: The findings reinforce scholarship on digital operations and logistics management and offer recommendations for firms to enhance performance by developing logistics human resource capabilities, leveraging IoT, raising service quality, and managing delivery times. Conclusion: Th…
venue: Journal of Business, Social and Technology

title: DIGITAL-BASED PUBLIC SERVICE INNOVATION: TRANSFORMING LICENSING GOVERNANCE THROUGH THE SIPINTER APPLICATION IN CIMAHI CITY
abstract: This study aims to analyze in depth the public service innovation process through the SIPINTER (Integrated Service Information System) application developed by the Cimahi City Investment and One-Stop Integrated Service Agency (DPMPTSP). The study uses a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data collection techniques were carried out through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation studies. The analytical tool used refers to the perspective of co-creation-based public sector innovation, with a focus on four main dimensions: real-time data accuracy, public participation, governance transparency, and legitimacy. The results show that SIPINTER has contributed significantly to increasing the efficiency and transparency of licensing services through the provision of real-time data and openness of service process information. However, public participation is still instrumental and has not fully developed into deliberative participation, while the legitimacy of innovation is highly dependent on system reliability, human resource capacity, and consistent institutional support. This study confirms that the success of digital public service transformation is determined not only by technological aspects, but also by institutional and relational factors that shape public trust. Theoretically, this research enriches the study of public sector innovation by offering an u…
venue: Politik Indonesia: Indonesian Political Science Review

title: Implementation of the CITAR Work Culture in Responding to the Dynamics of Public Service at PT KAI Regional Division I North Sumatra
abstract: This study examines the implementation of the CITAR work culture in responding to the dynamics of public service at PT Kereta Api Indonesia (PT KAI) Regional Division I of North Sumatra and identifies factors influencing its implementation. Growing demand for railway transportation has increased service complexity, requiring frontline personnel to maintain quality while adapting to operational pressures. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, using direct observation, in-depth interviews with management, frontline employees, and passengers, and document analysis. Informants were selected through purposive sampling, and data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that the CITAR work culture, which emphasizes Commitment, Integrity, Teamwork, Accountability, and Responsibility, has been integrated into employees’ daily work practices and contributes to more responsive, disciplined, and customer-oriented public services. This implementation is supported by leadership, systematic supervision, and continuous performance evaluation. However, several challenges persist, including procedural rigidity, limited information dissemination, inconsistent service responsiveness, and inadequate accessibility for passengers with disabilities. The study concludes that strengthening organizational policies, improving service proc…
venue: Indonesian Journal of Social Responsibility Review (IJSRR)

title: National enabling conditions, institutional governance and online service development: longitudinal evidence from Asia
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how national enabling conditions and institutional governance are associated with online public service development across Asian economies. Design/methodology/approach A longitudinal panel of 46 Asian economies across eight biennial waves from 2010 to 2024 is analyzed using the United Nations Online Service Index as an outcome. Two-way fixed-effects models examine economic capacity, human capital and digital connectivity, alongside six Worldwide Governance Indicators. Primary inference uses country-clustered CR2 standard errors with Satterthwaite-adjusted degrees of freedom, supplemented by conventional country-clustered and Driscoll–Kraay inferences. Findings Economic capacity and digital connectivity exhibit robust positive within-country associations with the development of online service delivery. Human capital remains positively associated with the outcome but is only marginally significant when enabling conditions are considered. Despite positive descriptive correlations, none of the six governance dimensions exhibited a robust within-country association beyond the enabling conditions under the primary inference procedure. Originality/value This study avoids equating national enabling conditions with dynamic capabilities and separates cross-country governance relationships from the within-country evidence. The findings qualify the assump…

title: POLICY NETWORK IN BERPENDAR SERVICE INNOVATION AT THE POM CENTER IN YOGYAKARTA
abstract: This article aims to analyze the role of policy networks in supporting public service innovation through a study of the Joint Program for Assistance to MSMEs to Obtain Distribution Permits (BERPENDAR) implemented by the Food and Drug Monitoring Agency (BPOM) in Yogyakarta. The study used a qualitative approach supported by descriptive quantitative data through a single case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 15 key informants, a survey of 66 MSMEs participating in BERPENDAR, document studies, and network structure mapping using Social Network Analysis (SNA). The analysis was conducted using Frans van Waarden's seven-dimensional policy network framework. The results show that the effectiveness of BERPENDAR is not solely determined by formal regulatory design, but rather by the configuration of the policy network that works adaptively and collaboratively. The SNA findings emphasize the Center's central role in coordinating regional government actors, academics, the private sector, facilitators, and MSMEs. In terms of outcomes, BERPENDAR contributes to accelerating the issuance of distribution permits, increasing MSME satisfaction with services, and strengthening business actors' confidence in accessing wider markets.
venue: Politik Indonesia: Indonesian Political Science Review

title: Frequency of neuro-ophthalmological diseases in a tertiary care center in Mexico
Diabetic cataract at type 1 diabetes onset: frequency and characteristics
abstract: Abstract Objectives Pediatric diabetic cataract is a rare acute complication of diabetes mellitus and may result in permanent visual impairment. Reported prevalences range from 0.25 % to 3.4 %, while data from Germany remain limited. This study aimed to describe the prevalence and clinical characteristics of cataract in children with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes at a German tertiary medical center. Methods We retrospectively evaluated children and adolescents admitted to the Department of Pediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, University Medical Center Ulm, with newly diagnosed type 1 diabetes between January 2008 and February 2024 who underwent ophthalmologic screening at the Department of Ophthalmology of the same center. A final cohort of 141 patients was analyzed. Results Cataract was diagnosed in 6 of 141 patients, corresponding to 4.3 % of the ophthalmologically examined cohort. The median age of patients with cataract was 12.4 years. Mean HbA 1c was significantly higher in patients with cataract than in those without cataract (15.8 % vs. 12.4 %; p<0.05). Visual acuity was significantly lower in patients with cataract than in those without cataract (0.19 vs. 0.03 logMAR; p<0.05). The predominant morphology was snowflake-like posterior subcapsular cataract. Retinal findings were normal in all patients, irrespective of cataract status. Conclusions In this single-center coho…
venue: Journal of Pediatric Endocrinology and Metabolism

title: Regulation and reform: The challenge of the Cultural, Religious and Linguistic Rights Commission to neo-Pentecostal prophetism
abstract: Background: Questionable religious practices within neo-Pentecostal prophetism that border on the commercialisation of religion and the violation of congregants’ human rights have prompted the Commission for Cultural, Religious and Linguistic Communities Rights to advocate for the regulation of churches in South Africa. This demand presents a direct challenge to the prophetic role of neo-Pentecostal prophetic churches. Objectives: To examine the implications of the proposed regulation of churches for neo-Pentecostal prophetism in South Africa, considering that the movement’s controversial practices have largely instigated this call. Methods: The study employs a comparative literature review of relevant scholarly and policy sources. Results: The article argues that churches within neo-Pentecostal prophetism should view the call for regulation as an opportunity to reform from questionable practices and move towards a credible, Christlike prophetic movement. Conclusion: Neo-Pentecostal prophetic churches, together with the broader church in South Africa, must repudiate practices that compromise their credibility and, instead, embody their vocation as salt and light in a dark and sinful world. Contribution: The study contributes to Pentecostal scholarship by emphasising the need to safeguard the integrity of the Christian prophetic message through ethical accountability and the rej…

title: Frequency of plastic occurrence varies across phylogeny but not ecology in seabirds
abstract: Abstract Seabirds are especially vulnerable to ingesting plastic pollution. However, we have a limited understanding of which traits might increase their risk of plastic ingestion. Here, we use a dataset of seabird plastic occurrence records (93 281 birds from 240 species) to investigate which species accumulate plastic and whether this is related to diet, foraging method, pelagic specialism, body mass or phylogenetic position. In our dataset, 182 of the 240 species (76%) contained plastic. Within orders, the highest levels were in pelicans (Pelecaniformes; 67%) and the lowest in penguins (Sphenisciformes; 5%). In our phylogenetically informed analysis, accounting for artefacts of study design (e.g. sample size, year, ocean, source, age class and sampling method), none of the ecological traits we tested had a consistent effect on plastic occurrence. Instead, phylogenetic relatedness was the best predictor in our models, reflecting the tight correlation between seabird phylogenetic groupings and their traits. This suggests that phylogenetic position may serve as a rapid way to identify species likely to accumulate plastic. Future research should focus on developing predictions of plastic accumulation risk for understudied species, implementing standardized methodologies and investigating species-specific morphological and environmental variables that may affect their risk of pla…

title: From Radio Waves to On-Demand Video: A Dual-Platform Approach to Chinese American Mental Health Outreach
Does Illness Perception Influence Treatment Outcomes in Erectile Dysfunction? an Observational Study on Depressive Symptoms and Short-Term Treatment Response
abstract: Objective: To investigate the relationship between illness perceptions, depressive symptoms, and erectile function (EF) in men with erectile dysfunction (ED) and to evaluate longitudinal changes following treatment.Materials and Methods: Patients with ED (IIEF-5 ≤21) were enrolled at a tertiary urology outpatient clinic between June and October 2025. Participants completed the International Index of Erectile Function-5 (IIEF-5), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), and Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (B-IPQ) at baseline and at 1 and 3 months. All patients received lifestyle counseling and phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor therapy. Associations were analyzed using correlation and multivariable linear regression analyses.Results: A total of 120 patients completed follow-up. More negative illness perceptions were significantly associated with higher depressive symptom severity and worse ED severity (p < 0.05). B-IPQ scores increased progressively across categories of both depressive symptoms and ED severity. title: Response to: “Aspirin Omission in CH-VAD Support: The Importance of Exposure Timing and Anticoagulation Assessment”
Improving humanitarian logistics through GDP-based quality-assured logistics controls and cross-organisational training: empirical evidence from Malaysia’s flood response
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the key determinants of humanitarian logistics effectiveness in Malaysia’s flood disaster management and develop the good humanitarian logistics practices model (GHLPM) as an integrated framework to enhance coordination, quality assurance and operational readiness. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative approach using five focus group discussions (FGDs) involving government agencies, non-governmental organisations and community representatives directly engaged in flood response operations. Thematic analysis was used to identify recurring patterns and generate key dimensions influencing logistics performance. Findings The findings identify four interrelated dimensions: Community preparedness literacy, multi-agency coordination capacity, GDP-based quality-assured logistics controls and cross-organisational training integration, which collectively shape relief logistics performance outcomes. The results indicate that effective logistics extends beyond infrastructure and speed, requiring alignment between governance mechanisms, coordination structures and organisational capabilities. GDP-based controls enhance transparency and traceability, while cross-organisational training functions as a strategic capability that strengthens the effectiveness of coordination and quality implementation. Practical implications The GHLPM provid…
venue: Journal of Humanitarian Logistics and Supply Chain Management

title: Health Outcomes and Medical Response in Military Maneuvers: A Study of Morbidity, Treatment, and Evacuation
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Military maneuvers represent a health care challenge: They are essential for preventing occupational accidents and providing rapid and appropriate care for injuries and conditions resulting from physical exertion and extreme environments. OBJECTIVE: To describe and analyze medical support during military maneuvers and evaluate morbidity, treatments applied, and evacuation protocols in units from the Ceuta Command. METHODS: A prospective, observational, and analytical study was conducted over 2 weeks of maneuvers in Zaragoza, Spain. Demographic and clinical variables were included (type of injury, treatment, need for evacuation, and follow-up). Statistical analysis employed descriptive statistics and comparative tests (χ 2 test and Student t test), considering P < .05 as the level of significance. RESULTS: A total of 219 medical consultations were recorded. Traumatic injuries accounted for 46.1% of the cases, followed by infections (20.1%). Only 6.8% required medical evacuation, and 14.2% required subsequent follow-up, demonstrating the effectiveness of in-field management ( P < .05). CONCLUSIONS: Medical support deployed during the maneuvers presented a high rate of in-field resolution (93%) and confirmed that traumatic injuries are the leading cause of consultation. These findings highlight the need to maintain robust health care protocols and strengthen preventi…

title: Hashtags of hope: technology, stakeholders and disaster response
abstract: Purpose This research examines how individuals exercised digital agency by reaching out to emergent actors on Twitter (now called as X), and how this reshapes understandings of stakeholder salience in humanitarian supply chain management (HSCM) during disaster response for humanitarian organisations. Design/methodology/approach A corpus of 120,057 tweets collected via hashtag-based Application Programming Interface extraction is analysed through three complementary methods: (1) descriptive frequency analysis of stakeholder callout patterns, (2) social network analysis (SNA) and (3) topic modelling to establish the purposive, humanitarian intent of the identified interactions. Findings Affected populations directed the majority of callouts to celebrities, exceeding appeals to government, media and NGOs. Accounts of the top celebrities structurally bridged disconnected stakeholder clusters. Finally, the interactions were found to be purposive and humanitarian, spanning direct appeals, donation mobilisation, information diffusion and volunteer coordination. Practical implications Humanitarian organisations should establish pre-crisis partnership agreements with verified celebrity amplifiers and invest in specialist digital intelligence intermediation units, structurally separate from operational command, to filter, verify and route social-media-sourced signals to field commanders.…

title: The immunogenicity control axis: a multi-omics framework for integrating epigenetic, DNA damage response, and immune states in cancer
abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed cancer treatment, yet therapeutic responses remain heterogeneous and are incompletely explained by immune-centric biomarkers alone. We propose the Immunogenicity Control Axis (ICA), a testable multi-omics framework integrating three complementary dimensions of tumor state: epigenetic regulation, DNA damage response (DDR), and immune activity. The central hypothesis is that epigenetic permissiveness influences immune-relevant transcription and antigen presentation, while DDR-associated genomic processes contribute to antigenic variation; together, these tumor-intrinsic features interact with the immune state to shape tumor immune visibility. To make this hypothesis quantitatively testable, the ICA is operationalized through independently derived Epigenetic, DDR, and Immune scores that are standardized and integrated into a composite ICA Score. Using cervical cancer as an initial disease context, patient-derived TCGA-CESC analyses provide exploratory assessment of ICA-associated molecular states and prognostic relationships, while synthetic analyses are used separately to illustrate specific analytical procedures. The framework is further extended to perturbational analysis, in which CMap/LINCS transcriptional signatures and network information are used to prioritize candidate natural compounds predicted to oppose ICA-associated molecular states. title: Sustainability integration in risk assessment and management accounting: insights from Iran
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to investigate the adoption of sustainability principles by Iranian firms in their strategic planning, risk management and management accounting (MA) practices. It aims to build a structural model that demonstrates how industry-driven, sustainable risk assessment tools can enhance organizational responsibility, adaptability and adherence. Design/methodology/approach The research adopted a survey approach, serving 103 Iranian companies from different sectors of the business world. To examine these relations of strategic planning, sustainable risk assessment tools and integration of sustainability in MA systems, structural equation modeling (SEM) was used. Procedural and statistical remedies were used to check and control the common method bias. Findings The findings indicate that enterprises using sustainable risk assessment instruments are significantly more advanced with respect to the inclusion of environmental issues in MA. Environmental and social risk assessments are highly determined by strategic planning, as sustainable risk assessment tools become an important mediator between the integration of sustainability in MA and global organizational sustainability performance. Yet, there are many companies without unit-level sustainability departments or that still report sustainability within the traditional accounting systems, suggesting e…

title: Dynamic performance assessment of historic public assembly buildings using system dynamics
abstract: Purpose Historical structures are representations of a nation's cultural and architectural heritage, yet most were built in eras when modern energy efficiency, occupant comfort and indoor air quality (IAQ) were not prioritized in building design. Such challenges are intensified in naturally ventilated public assembly structures where climatic variations and intermittent high-occupancy events create substantial temporal variations. Design/methodology/approach This study presents a holistic framework for evaluating the hourly performance of naturally ventilated public assembly buildings over a year. The building behavior is represented by combining hourly values of key performance indicators (KPIs), extracted from a Building Information Modeling model, into a system dynamics model that simulates cumulative effects and cause-and-effect relationships. The outputs are aggregated into an hourly Building Performance Index. The chosen approach adopts a dynamic weighting strategy built upon a hybrid analytic hierarchy process–entropy baseline weighting scheme. Adaptive monthly adjustments informed by variability in performance KPIs as well as seasonal and occupancy-related adjustments are applied. Findings The results demonstrate that static weighting scenarios tend to smooth temporal variability and mask critical operational periods, while dynamic scenarios reveal pronounced performanc…

title: KostKu: Integrating Search, Maps, and Digital Payments in a Web–Android Boarding House System for Kudus Regency (Case Study: Kudus Regency)
abstract: Although boarding house information systems are widely available, integrated platforms tailored to search and rental needs in Kudus Regency remain limited. This study aims to design and develop KostKu, a boarding house search and rental information system accessible through a website and an Android application. A research and development (R&D) approach was employed using a prototyping method comprising requirements gathering, preliminary design, iterative prototype evaluation, testing, and implementation. The system was developed using Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, Supabase, Leaflet, and Capacitor. KostKu supports three user roles and integrates search and filtering based on multiple criteria, interactive maps, booking, payment processing through Midtrans, reviews, favorites, and administrative verification of boarding houses and owners. Black-box testing confirmed that the main functional scenarios operated according to specifications. These findings demonstrate the functional integration of boarding house search and rental services across web and Android platforms. KostKu provides a practical means of streamlining accommodation searches and rental processes for tenants and boarding house owners, contributing to the development of integrated accommodation information systems.

title: Physiotherapeutic Management of Adhesive Capsulitis of the Shoulder: A Narrative Review
abstract: Adhesive capsulitis, also known as frozen shoulder, is a common musculoskeletal disorder characterized by progressive pain and significant limitation of both active and passive glenohumeral range of motion. The condition results from chronic inflammation, fibrosis, and contracture of the joint capsule, leading to impaired upper limb function and reduced quality of life. The prevalence in the general population is estimated at 2–5%, with a markedly higher incidence among patients with diabetes mellitus and thyroid disorders. The aim of this narrative review was to summarize current evidence regarding the pathophysiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and physiotherapeutic management of adhesive capsulitis. The review was based on scientific literature indexed in the PubMed and Scopus databases, with particular emphasis on recent systematic reviews, clinical guidelines, and randomized controlled trials. Current evidence indicates that physiotherapy is the cornerstone of conservative treatment. Rehabilitation should be individualized according to the stage of the disease and tissue irritability and should combine patient education, therapeutic exercise, manual therapy, and, when indicated, pharmacological interventions. During the painful stage, treatment should focus on pain reduction, preservation of shoulder mobility, and prevention of secondary functional impairments. Duri…
venue: Journal of Education, Health and Sport

title: Factors that facilitate artificial intelligence integration into global talent management: A systematic review
abstract: Orientation: Digital technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), are rapidly transforming human resource functions by enhancing the efficiency and effectiveness of human resource practices. Research purpose: This systematic review examines the factors that facilitate the integration of AI into global talent management (GTM) and explores how these factors collectively inform theory on technology-enabled talent management systems. Motivation for the study: Research on the use of AI in GTM remains limited, and its theoretical implications are not yet well established. Research approach/design and method: A systematic literature review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews framework. The review encompassed eight databases (Google Scholar, Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, ProQuest, Emerald Insight, Sabinet and Elsevier) using a comprehensive and structured search strategy. Peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and 2025 were screened. Twenty-three empirical studies meeting the inclusion criteria were subjected to full-text analysis. Main findings: The analysis revealed that AI integration into GTM is influenced by several interconnected enablers, including the strategic alignment of AI with talent objectives, adequate capabilities and digital infrastructu…
venue: SA Journal of Human Resource Management

title: Patterns of RPA adoption: a qualitative comparison between India and North America
abstract: Purpose Robotic process automation (RPA) is a deterministic technology that is expected to build synergies with probabilistic technologies such as agentic AI. The study aims to investigate how organizations embark on the RPA journey, implement RPA, and support RPA through changes in organization structure, roles, and skills. Design/methodology/approach Our study is based on thematic analysis complemented by a qualitative case-based research design. Empirically, the study draws on 30 in-depth interviews with senior leadership representatives from 30 distinct organizations, ensuring balanced representation across geographies. Findings We find similarities and differences in the patterns of adoption of RPA in India and North America. The presence of a relative advantage and strategy for deployment emerge as necessary conditions for business case development and implementation of RPA. Top management support and having a centre of excellence are common configurations for organization support in both locations. Originality/value We contribute methodological support on approaches to study emerging technology adoption. Our study provides alternate paths for practitioners to design their unique journey of RPA adoption in India and North America. Since RPA lies on the AI continuum, this study is relevant for the adoption of other AI technologies in the AI ecosystem.

title: Establishment of a maternal haploid induction system in petunia via CRISPR/Cas9-mediated editing of PhDMP8/9
PromptIQ: An AI-Assisted Prompt Analysis and Refinement System Using Chrome Extension, JavaScript and Rule-Based Scoring
abstract: Large language models such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude are increasingly used for education, software development, data analysis, content creation and decision support. The quality and usefulness of their responses are strongly influenced by how users formulate prompts. However, many users do not have a systematic way to judge whether a prompt is clear, contextual, specific and efficient before submitting it. This paper presents PromptIQ, a browser-based prompt analysis and refinement system designed to provide immediate feedback while a user is interacting with supported AI platforms. The proposed system uses a Chrome extension to detect prompt text through a content script and pass it to a local JavaScript scoring engine. The current scoring model evaluates four dimensions: clarity, context, specificity and efficiency, combined into an overall score on a 0-100 scale. Functional testing of the implemented modules is used to evaluate the reliability of the system. The proposed system demonstrates how browser-based and rule-based technologies can be combined to develop an accessible, transparent prompt-quality feedback platform, with a future version expected to integrate an external language model for explanation and automatic prompt refinement. Keywords— Prompt Engineering, Large Language Models, Prompt Analysis, Prompt Optimization, Chrome Extension, Natural Language Process…
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: Predicting the patient’s remaining length of stay for real-time decision-making: a process mining approach
abstract: Purpose This research aims to develop a structured methodology to estimate the remaining length of stay (RLoS) throughout a patient’s care journey, thereby providing decision-makers with timely information to support real-time operations. Design/methodology/approach We developed a structured methodology for predictive process monitoring based on advanced process mining techniques. To test our method, we conducted a case study at a major Italian transplant hospital, extracting a dataset of 31,521 real events from 4,809 surgical patients using several hospitals' information systems. Findings Our results show that RLoS estimates become more accurate as the care process unfolds, offering valuable insights for real-time decision-making. Research limitations/implications Findings derive from single-procedure surgical pathways at one specialized center, with lower accuracy for prolonged stays that often end in transfer rather than discharge. Future research should address multicentre validation, competing terminal events and concept drift. Practical implications The proposed structured methodology transforms hospital event logs into real-time operational insights for the management of surgical inpatients, whose care unfolds through a defined pre-operative, operative, and post-operative sequence. Within this scope, it supports more proactive bed management, patient flow coordination, a…

title: CosmoForge. I. A unified framework for quadratic maximum likelihood power spectrum estimation and pixel-based likelihood analysis
abstract: Optimal power spectrum estimation on the largest angular scales of the cosmic microwave background relies on the quadratic maximum likelihood (QML) estimator. Existing public implementations, however, each address only a subset of the problem, and none combines power spectrum estimation with a self-consistent pixel-space likelihood within a single framework. We present ̧f, a public Python framework that unifies QML power spectrum estimation and pixel-based Gaussian likelihood evaluation for spin-0 and spin-2 fields on the sphere, with general (non-diagonal) noise covariances. The framework is split into three installable packages: ç (infrastructure), (łmax^4) for arbitrary noise covariances, with (Fisher and QML estimation), and (pixel-space likelihood). A common interface exposes two interchangeable computation bases -- a harmonic basis built on the Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury identity and a direct pixel-space basis -- selecting whichever is cheaper for the configuration at hand. Exact algorithmic optimisations reduce the Fisher cost to mathcal O Numba JIT compilation of the hot kernels and MPI parallelisation of the likelihood scan. ̧f reproduces the Planck low-ell Fortran reference implementation across both the QML and pixel-space likelihood pipelines, consistently with double-precision arithmetic. Native multipole binning and three output normalisations (deconvolved, de-co…

title: The power of inclusive practices for teaching mathematics
abstract: While every child has the right to an education, disabled and neurodivergent children are not always included in powerful mathematics instruction. In this article, we report on a collaborative research study that supported primary school teachers to develop inclusive mathematics lessons using a lesson study approach and universal design for learning principles. The aim was to support teachers to understand the barriers to belonging and rich learning in mathematics that some children can face, and to explore the strategies teachers might use to overcome those barriers so that all children experience inclusion and high-quality learning.

title: Exploration of Ethnomathematics in the Kabihu Kinship System from the Perspective of Set Theory and Relations
abstract: This study was motivated by the importance of linking mathematics learning to local cultural contexts so that mathematical concepts become more meaningful. The kabihu kinship system in Sumba society has a social structure that can potentially be interpreted through mathematical concepts, particularly sets and relations. This study aims to explore the structure of the Praikaraha kabihu in Raja Prailiu Village, East Sumba, and to identify the forms of sets and types of relations that can be interpreted mathematically. The study employs a qualitative approach using ethnography. Three informants were selected through purposive sampling based on the following criteria: understanding the history and structure of the kabihu, being involved in traditional life, and being able to provide information regarding kinship relationships within the kabihu. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, non-participant observation, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted through the stages of ethnographic analysis, which include the identification of cultural domains, the grouping of categories, and the interpretation of cultural meanings, and was supported by Miles and Huberman’s interactive model through data condensation, data presentation, and the drawing and verification of conclusions. Data validity was examined through source triangulation, methodological triangulation, a…

title: Managing change in the era of digital transformation. The case of Greek public sector
abstract: Purpose This study examines the crucial process of implementing digital transformation in the Greek public sector, investigating how organizational framework, organizational sustainment, and employee digital readiness influence the successful integration of technological changes and digital reforms. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative survey was conducted with 233 Greek civil servants attending undergraduate and postgraduate programs in Public Administration. The study employed validated measurement scales including Holt et al.'s (2007) Readiness for Organizational Change scale, Miller's (1997) Integration of Change scale, and Westerman et al.'s (2014) scales for Organizational Frame and Sustainment of Digital Challenge. Data were analyzed using confirmatory factor analysis, Cronbach's alpha coefficients, Pearson correlations, multiple regression models, and bootstrapped mediation analysis via Hayes' (2022) PROCESS macro (Model 4, 5,000 resamples) to test hypotheses regarding direct and indirect effects. Findings Results demonstrate that organizational frame of digital challenge and organizational sustainment of digital transformation significantly and positively affect both employee readiness for digital change and successful integration of digital initiatives. Employee readiness partially mediates the relationships between organizational conditions (framing and sustain…

title: Management-oriented decision framework for grid-support technology selection in islanded power systems: a comparative analysis of STATCOMs and synchronous condensers
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a management-oriented decision framework to guide the selection and deployment of static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) and synchronous condensers in islanded power systems, addressing the gap between engineering analysis and infrastructure governance in the energy sector. Design/methodology/approach The framework integrates key managerial criteria − system efficiency, capital expenditure, deployment time, maintenance complexity and system strength and resilience − within an analytic hierarchy process (AHP)-based decision architecture. Taiwan’s islanded power system serves as the primary case, with Australia’s National Electricity Market as an international reference. The framework is validated through expert elicitation involving five industry professionals with an average of 28.6 years of experience, using structured AHP questionnaires. A scenario-based sensitivity analysis examines how different managerial priorities shift technology preferences. Findings Under the baseline weighting, system strength and resilience receives the highest priority weight (0.396), followed by operational efficiency (0.264). Expert validation confirms this prioritization, with system strength and resilience receiving the highest group consensus weight (0.472). STATCOMs score higher under cost- and speed-driven scenarios (composite score 0.63 vs 0.37), where…
venue: International Journal of Energy Sector Management

title: Reply to Ariano et al
Symbiotic relationship of prefabricated building supply partners under different government incentive policies
abstract: Purpose This study examines the co-evolutionary behavior of contractors and component suppliers in prefabricated building (PB) supply chains under bounded rationality and different government incentive policies. It aims to clarify how asymmetric incentive allocation and contractor–supplier interactions shape symbiotic outcomes and to provide a theoretical basis for the coordinated promotion of PB. Design/methodology/approach By integrating symbiosis theory with game payoff matrices, an asymmetric independent symbiosis density-game model was constructed between contractors and component suppliers. By analyzing the model's stability conditions and employing system dynamics simulations, this study examines the decision-making dynamics and evolutionary trajectories of contractors and component suppliers under different government incentive policies. Findings The results indicate that the model exhibits distinct, stable equilibria under different initial conditions, with stability conditions closely tied to the government's incentive allocation and the behavioral choices of game participants. Greater supply chain interconnectedness effectively promotes co-adoption of PB. Moderate increases and appropriate incentive allocation, coupled with greater supply chain interconnectedness, facilitate the adoption and development of prefabricated construction. Originality/value This study exte…

title: Challenges affecting revitalization and sustainability in forest-based land reform projects: lessons from the Thuthukani and Jabulani communities, South Africa
abstract: Introduction South African forest plantations are managed as multifunctional landscapes, which are crucial for biodiversity sustainability while providing ecosystem services that positively contribute to the livelihoods of rural communities. This study examined the challenges affecting the efforts of the Thuthukani and Jabulani community property associations to successfully revitalize and sustain their plantation. Methods The two communities were purposively selected because they were both beneficiaries of the forest plantations resulting from the successful settlement of land restitution claims. Descriptive and inferential statistics were used to analyze the household survey data, while content analysis was used to analyze the FGD data. Results Both communities cited difficulty obtaining resources to combat forest fires; in Jabulani, 46.7% of respondents reported it was fairly difficult, compared with 40% in Thuthukani. Furthermore, FGD participants from both communities emphasized the difficulty of securing funding, which prevents them from pursuing efforts to revitalize and sustain their plantation to a functional state. Due to a lack of financial resources, the community beneficiaries were unable to revitalize and sustainably manage their forested land, sustain the resources, and continue accessing various ecosystem services. Notably, the other challenge, directly related …

title: Reconstructing Religious Policy Governance for Social Cohesion in Plural Societies
abstract: Religious diversity can enrich plural societies, yet it may also intensify exclusion and social tension when public institutions privilege dominant traditions, restrict minority participation, or implement religious policies inconsistently. This study reconstructs religious policy governance as an integrated institutional process for supporting social cohesion while safeguarding equal citizenship and freedom of religion or belief. Using a qualitative integrative review and comparative conceptual synthesis, the study examines peer-reviewed scholarship on religious diversity governance, institutional participation, rights protection, interreligious engagement, accountability, and social cohesion. The literature was analysed through combined deductive and inductive thematic procedures, with provisional analytical domains serving as sensitizing concepts for identifying recurring governance problems, institutional mechanisms, and relationships across different socio-religious contexts. Cross-source comparison and conceptual refinement consolidated the evidence into four interconnected dimensions: inclusive institutional governance, deliberative and participatory governance, rights-based recognition and accommodation, and dialogue-based conflict transformation. The analysis indicates that institutional coordination may improve responsiveness, while participation can strengthen policy…
venue: AMUYA: INDONESIAN JOURNAL OF MANAGEMENT REVIEWS

title: Socio-technical TQM configurations and technological innovation ambidexterity: balanced and combined pathways
abstract: Purpose This study examines how different configurations of social and technical total quality management (TQM) practices shape technological innovation ambidexterity (TIA). Specifically, it distinguishes between balanced and combined TQM practices configurations and investigates their effects on balanced and combined forms of TIA. Design/methodology/approach A configurational framework grounded in socio-technical systems theory and organizational ambidexterity theory was tested using survey data from 113 ISO 9001-certified Tunisian manufacturing firms. The hypotheses were assessed using PLS-SEM. Findings Combined TQM practice configurations positively affect combined TIA but negatively affect balanced TIA. Balanced TQM practice configurations have no significant effect on either form of TIA. These findings indicate that the strong joint development of social and technical TQM practices supports innovation intensity rather than innovation balance. Research limitations/implications The study is limited by its cross-sectional design and its focus on a single-country manufacturing sample. It contributes to the TQM literature by showing that the effect of TQM on innovation depends on the configuration of social and technical TQM practices and on the specific form of ambidexterity considered. Practical implications Managers should configure TQM practices in line with their innovatio…
venue: International Journal of Quality & Reliability Management

title: ALCAM Revisited: A System Dynamics Framework for Aircraft Life Cycle Costing under Contemporary Acquisition Conditions
abstract: The global defense environment has undergone significant transformation since the original development of the Aircraft Life Cycle Cost Analysis Model (ALCAM), marked by great power competition, rapid technological disruption, and supply chain vulnerabilities. This research extends and updates the ALCAM framework to address contemporary defense acquisition challenges by incorporating digital transformation, supply chain resilience, sustainability requirements, and emerging technology integration. The study analyzes three primary procurement strategies: indigenous R&D, technology transfer with co-production, and off-the-shelf acquisition. Utilizing a generic System Dynamics simulation framework, the methodology captures non-linear relationships, feedback loops, and time-dependent variables across the system lifecycle. The enhanced model integrates Machine Learning estimates with simulation models to improve predictive capability and employs an internal numerical risk matrix to quantify uncertainties. Results demonstrate that life cycle cost differentials between procurement strategies have widened substantially due to supply chain vulnerabilities, accelerated technology obsolescence, and sustainment cost escalation. Simulation outcomes reveal that the off-the-shelf option, despite lower initial acquisition costs, projects significantly higher total life cycle costs due to long-te…
venue: Journal of Scientific Technology and Engineering Research

title: When fear of missing out silences sharing social comparison, satisfaction, and consumer experience in concert tourism
abstract: Purpose This study examines how fear of missing out (FOMO) influences social media engagement, concert satisfaction, post-event regret, and future concert destination preference among concert tourists. The study draws on the Social Comparison Theory (SCT) to explain why FOMO may suppress engagement rather than drive it in high-visibility event settings. The study also tests if these relationships differ across generational cohorts. Design/methodology/approach The research used snowball sampling via a two-wave survey to collect data from 703 Coldplay concert attendees, who actively posted on social media. The study statistically examined the proposed relationships using structural equation modelling. Also, multi-group analysis was used to identify differences between generational cohorts. Findings Based on the results, the data showed that FOMO negatively affected social media engagement. This could indicate that in a high-visibility setting heightened FOMO suppressed social media sharing. Social media engagement in turn increased concert satisfaction and reduced post-event regret. Satisfaction and regret each mediated the effect of social media engagement on future concert destination preference. Multigroup analysis showed that the satisfaction-to-preference and regret-to-preference paths were stronger for Generation X than for Millennials and Generation Z. Research limitations…
