title: A framework for capability maturity in GCC’s mobile payment ecosystem: insights from Qatar
abstract: Purpose This study explores the factors influencing the adoption and growth of mobile payment (m-payment) ecosystems in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), a region where fintech capabilities remain underdeveloped. The focus is on the competencies of m-payment service providers and their role in sustaining ecosystem growth. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative, multi-case study approach was employed to understand the capability maturity of service providers in creating value. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 24 stakeholders, including founders, employees, merchants and customers. Findings The study develops an integrated framework grounded in Dynamic Capabilities Theory and positions the Technology–Organization–Environment (TOE) model as a precursor to dynamic capability development. The proposed framework explains how technological, organizational and environmental conditions enable or constrain service providers' ability to develop and deploy dynamic capabilities across different stages of their life cycle. Practical implications The framework provides m-payment service providers with a capability-development roadmap by showing how resources and ecosystem conditions become important across different stages of growth. The findings also highlight how regulators, incubators, banks and technology partners can support provider capability development…

title: An integrated BIM-based approach for maintenance management of educational facilities: a practical case study
abstract: Purpose This study develops an integrated building information modeling (BIM)-based model for predictive maintenance management in educational buildings by combining building condition assessment (CA) and deterioration prediction (DP) using a Markov chain model. Design/methodology/approach The methodology involves categorizing building assets into a hierarchy, calculating relative weights (RW) for components and optimizing maintenance schedules and resource allocation. The integration of the BIM model with facility management (FM) software enhances data exchange and decision-making, providing facility managers with graphical representations of data and a platform for managing both preventive and corrective maintenance. Findings The effectiveness of the model was validated using data from a real educational facility, which demonstrated improvements in maintenance, and cost reduction. Specifically, the model supports proactive maintenance scheduling, and task prioritization, leading to reduction in maintenance costs and enhancing the efficiency of maintenance operations. Through a real-world case study, the model achieves 22% maintenance cost reduction, and 89% prediction accuracy, demonstrating its practical advantages over reactive. Originality/value This approach not only extends the lifecycle of building assets but also improves overall asset management practices in education…

title: Hybrid ARIMA-Prophet-LSTM with SHAP Interpretation for Forecasting Outpatient Visits by Medical Specialty
abstract: Background: Accurate forecasting of outpatient visits is important for hospital staffing, scheduling, facility utilization, and resource allocation. Outpatient demand in the study data shows strong weekly seasonality and holiday-related variation, creating challenges for both forecasting accuracy and model interpretation. Objective: This study evaluates ARIMA, Prophet, LSTM, and four hybrid configurations for daily outpatient-visit forecasting across five medical specialties and interprets the best-performing hybrid model using SHAP. Method: Historical daily outpatient-visit data from Internal Medicine, Orthopedic and Traumatology Surgery, Cardiology, Pediatrics, and Neurology were modeled using ARIMA, Prophet, LSTM, ARIMA-Prophet, ARIMA-LSTM, Prophet-LSTM, and ARIMA-Prophet-LSTM. Time-series cross-validation with an expanding window was used, with MAE, RMSE, and MAPE as performance metrics. Friedman and post hoc Nemenyi tests were applied for model comparison, and SHAP's GradientExplainer was used for the LSTM component of Prophet-LSTM. Results: Prophet achieved the best performance in four specialties, whereas Prophet-LSTM was best in Neurology. The triple hybrid was significantly worse than Prophet (p = 0.017) and did not differ significantly from ARIMA-Prophet (p = 0.9996). SHAP identified day-of-week cyclical features as the most influential predictors across specialties, …

title: Energy Consumption Modeling and Forecasting for Medical AI Systems in Nigerian Hospitals: A Climate-Calibrated Simulation Framework
abstract: Increasing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare raises energy-demand questions that are especially acute in resource-limited regions. Because operational, application-level energy-metering data for medical AI systems in Sub-Saharan African hospitals are not yet publicly available, this study develops a climate-calibrated simulation framework that couples real facility profiles (bed capacity for six Nigerian teaching hospitals, from institutional and published sources) with real long-term climate normals (temperature and humidity for each hospital city) and a transparently parameterized medical-AI workload overlay (diurnal, weekly, and holiday patterns informed by prior literature). Statistical models (ARIMA, SARIMA, Holt-Winters exponential smoothing) and machine-learning models (a purpose-built LSTM and a hybrid LSTM-ARIMA) were evaluated on the resulting 58-month (January 2020-October 2024) simulated series using a consistent walk-forward, one-step-ahead protocol. Seasonal statistical models achieved the lowest forecast error (Holt-Winters MAPE=0.36%, SARIMA MAPE=0.37%), outperforming the hybrid LSTM-ARIMA (MAPE=0.51%) and a standalone LSTM (MAPE=0.61%), while the hybrid was most accurate at very short (1-day) horizons. Diurnal peak-hour (0800-1400) demand exceeded off-peak demand by 35%, and dry/harmattan-season demand exceeded the annual mean by 1.4-5.3% d…

title: Estimating magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction from ultrasound attenuation and clinical parameters in pediatric hepatic steatosis: development of a prediction model
Research-Embedded Schools as Educational Research Infrastructure: A Comparative Analysis of Research Capacity in Europe
abstract: Laboratory schools, university schools, and research-intensive training institutions are vital to educational research. Their distribution and capabilities across Europe are rarely explored systemically. This study considers research-embedded schools educational research infrastructure. It compares school-based research capacities in the EU, Nordics, Balkans, and England and Ireland. Using documentary analysis and secondary literature, national education systems are characterized as high, medium, or low research intensity depending on school research institutionalization. Results show a significant European research capacity disparity. In a few nations, high-intensity systems employ permanent laboratories or university schools for large-scale design-based, longitudinal, and discipline-based education research. Teacher-training schools dominate medium-intensity systems, providing continual but scattered research. Experimental and pilot schools dominate low-intensity systems, focusing on policy execution rather than knowledge development. The findings show that institutional infrastructures, not financing or academic traditions, shape national education research capacity. The study found that European research capacity must move from project-based innovation to long-term investment in research-embedded educational infrastructures.

title: Government Personnel Capacity Gaps and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise Resilience in Pangkep Archipelagic Governance
abstract: Purpose: This descriptive pilot maps local-government capacity gaps and, in parallel, MSME resilience and digital readiness across four island subdistricts in Pangkep. It does not test relationships between the two datasets; it identifies mechanisms for later qualitative and main-survey evaluation.Method: The preliminary quantitative stage of an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design includes 20 local-government personnel and 21 enterprise operators. The datasets are not linked at respondent or service level. We used descriptive statistics, gap scores, cross-tabulations, and juxtaposition across subdistricts. Item-level responses are unavailable, so we did not estimate reliability or construct validity.Results: The pilot reveals a substantial mismatch between perceived actual and required local-government capacity, with policy and digital capacity showing the largest mean gaps. Policy implementation quality is moderate, with implementer disposition scoring lowest. Among MSMEs, mean resilience exceeds mean digital readiness, and digital literacy is the weakest dimension. Twelve of the 21 enterprises score below the midpoint on digital readiness, while five fall below the midpoint on resilience. Subdistrict and business-type cells vary, but small and uneven sizes permit only exploratory case selection. Because the two datasets are independent and unlinked, we cannot establis…

title: Social capital, knowledge sharing, and performance in family firms: the central role of absorptive capacity
abstract: Purpose This study evaluated the effects of social capital, knowledge sharing, and absorptive capacity on the performance of family firms. Design/methodology/approach Data collection was carried out using a questionnaire with Likert-type scales. The sample of 108 respondents was planned using G*Power software. Findings Seven hypotheses were tested, and five were supported. The results reveal that social capital and knowledge sharing do not directly impact the performance of these firms. However, these variables proved to be important antecedents of absorptive capacity, which, in turn, influenced organizational performance. Research limitations/implications Since the study does not represent the universe of family businesses, it is not generalizable. The scale used to measure performance, may not encompass all relevant indicators related to performance. Practical implications This study provides strategic guidelines for managers, reinforcing the importance of recognizing and managing social capital and encouraging knowledge sharing to strengthen absorptive capacity, thereby enhancing firm performance. Originality/value The research revealed that the relationship between social capital, knowledge sharing and absorptive capacity are more complex and indirect than usually assumed. While social capital and knowledge sharing do not directly contribute to performance, they are essenti…

title: Developmental photoperiod alters the onset and capacity for reproduction in male dark-eyed juncos ( Junco hyemalis )
abstract: Abstract Natural selection favours individuals able to physiologically adjust to seasonal environmental cues, such as photoperiod, and time their reproduction accordingly. Although it is known that differences along the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal (HPG) axis can explain differences in reproductive timing across the dark-eyed junco (Junco hyemalis) range, it remains unknown whether these differences arise from local adaptation or early-life environmental effects. We exposed nestlings from a single population to photoperiods mimicking development at the northern and southern extents of the species’ breeding range. In autumn, we adjusted the photoperiod in the northern treatment to mimic southward migration, after which all birds experienced the same daylengths through the winter to simulate mixed overwintering flocks in the wild. Beginning early March, birds were injected with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) to measure induced testosterone as a proxy for HPG axis maturation; brood patches, cloacal protuberances and fat were also measured. Males raised under northern developmental photoperiods delayed the onset of reproductive readiness compared with control males. Sample date affected females’ GnRH-induced testosterone and fat deposition but not in clear patterns. These results indicate the daylength under which male songbirds develop can influence their reproductive sch…
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences

title: Investigating X-ray emission from radio-detected broad- and narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies
abstract: This paper presents a study of the X-ray emission for a sample of radio-detected (RD-) broad- and narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxies (BLS1s and NLS1s). Our aim is to investigate the X-ray emission properties of early-stage accretion activity or early jets in RD-NLS1s. By fitting XMM-Newton X-ray spectra and combining them with multi-band data from SDSS and FIRST, we conducted a statistical comparative study on the X-ray emission and multi-band correlations of RD-NLS1s and RD-BLS1s. RD-NLS1s and RD-BLS1s show no significant difference in their soft X-ray blackbody temperatures, but RD-NLS1s exhibit steeper hard X-ray photon indices and optical-to-X-ray slopes (( ̊m ox )). Moreover, correlation analyses of various parameters reveal intrinsic differences in the X-ray emission between the two samples. For instance, at comparable optical luminosities, RD-NLS1s exhibit a higher ( α_ ̊m ox ) (i.e. weaker X-ray emission), marginally distinct dependencies between the radio luminosity and black hole mass in the fundamental plane, and different correlations between ( α_ ̊m ox ) and radio loudness. Based on the relationship between the UV luminosity and ( α_ ̊m ox ) in radio-quiet (RQ-) active galactic nuclei (AGNs), the estimated X-ray excess (( Δ α_ ̊m ox )) in both samples is positively correlated with the radio loudness. RQ-BLS1s generally display an X-ray excess (( Δ α_ ̊m ox < 0 )), wher…

title: Broadband non-thermal emission predictions based on 3D simulations of supernova explosions within active galactic nuclei jets
abstract: Thermonuclear and core-collapse supernovae are statistically expected to happen within extragalactic jets, as these jets cross the inner regions of their host galaxies, and supernova ejecta--jet interactions can potentially lead to strong non-thermal activity. We model the non-thermal emission from a supernova interacting with a jet on kiloparsec scales, using detailed numerical simulations of the interaction. Using a post-processing method, we applied a non-thermal model of the acceleration and transport of electron and their synchrotron and inverse Compton emissions, simplified and tuned for flexibility and computational speed, to the results of a three-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics simulation of the ejecta of a supernova interacting with an extragalactic jet. For typical magnetic field strengths, a jet power 10^ 44 , , , and an electron energy distribution characteristic of diffusive shock acceleration, we predict: synchrotron emission that peaks in X-rays but reaches up to 100 MeV, with an overall luminosity of a few times 10^ 41 and emission from inverse Compton scattering mostly off galactic infrared photons, peaking at ∼ 1 TeV and with a luminosity up to ∼ 10^ 40 We also computed the evolution of the emission, and the distribution of the flux in the sky at its maximum, for five different energy bands: radio, optical, X-rays, high-energy and very high-energy γ-ra…

title: Insights into energy consumption and carbon emissions from freight industry in China
abstract: Against China’s commitments to peak carbon emissions before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, the freight industry, a major energy consumer and emitter, demands attention. This study estimated the energy consumption and carbon emissions from the freight industry in China based on the data of 2022–2024 official turnover, energy source types and IPCC “top-down” CO 2 emission factors. The results showed the total freight volume and turnover in China grew, and the total energy consumptions from the freight industry in China increasing from 593.25 million tce (2022) to 665.45 million tce (2024). The road freight dominated volume (≈73.53%) and energy consumption (87.55%–88.12%). The total CO 2 emissions from the freight industry in China increased from 1308.44 million tons in2022 to 1466.38 million tons in 2024. To meet the 2030/2060 carbon goals, it is recommended that cargo be shifted to electrified rail and coastal waterways, that electric-truck deployment be accelerated, that sustainable fuels be integrated in air and shipping, and that freight be included in an expanding carbon market. Overall, achieving deep decarbonization in China’s freight sector requires a systemic transition driven by transport mode optimization, accelerated fleet electrification, alternative fuel adoption, and market-based policy instruments.

title: Reshaping Insulin Fibrillation at the Nano-Bio Interface Using Carbon Quantum Dots: Implications for Amyloid Inhibition
abstract: Abstract Insulin (Ins), a 51-residue α-helical hormone, is prone to forming insoluble aggregates during administration, production, and storage, which poses significant challenges to its stability, effectiveness, and formulation. In this regard, nanoparticles have attracted tremendous interest owing to their unique physicochemical properties and high affinity for biomolecules. Carbon quantum dots are one of the newly emerged nanoparticles found effective against amyloid fibrillation due to aromaticity, hydrophobicity, and strong H-bonding ability. Herein, we studied the effect of hydrothermally synthesized CQDs on the Ins fibrillation under normal conditions. The 2–3 nm CQDs with graphitic-core and oxygenic surface functionalities were synthesized using l-ascorbic acid and their effect on Ins fibrillation kinetics was studied. Thioflavin-T (ThT) fluorescence assay showed that CQDs can reduce Ins fibrillation in a dose-dependent manner. Transmission electron microscopy indicated significant inhibition of fibril formation in 1.5 mg/mL Ins with 0.15 mg/mL CQDs at physiological pH. This was further validated by the disappearance of the β-sheet signature peak in CD spectra and lower β-sheet content in the amide-I region of the Raman spectra. Thermodynamic analysis suggested that the interaction between CQDs and Ins relies largely on H-bonding and dispersion forces, leading to ground…

title: Extended gamma-ray emission in the vicinity of the Westerlund 1 massive star cluster and Kes 41 supernova remnant seen by the Fermi Large Area Telescope
abstract: There is growing evidence of cosmic-ray acceleration in massive stellar clusters. Furthermore, extended gamma-ray emission suggests that particle transport in the vicinity of their sources is influenced by physical processes markedly different from large-scale diffusion in the Milky Way. We characterize extended gamma-ray emission in the direction of the stellar cluster and supernova remnant using more than 16 years of data from the Large Area Telescope (LAT) at energies greater than 0.8 GeV. Westerlund 1 Kes 41 Fermi We tested whether clusters of gamma-ray sources not associated with multiwavelength counterparts are better described by extended emission components and characterized their spatial and spectral properties as well as their correlation with interstellar structures. We report the detection of three new extended emission components with soft spectra toward regions of high gas column density in the Galactic plane. One extended component is associated with the natal cloud of and is statistically preferred over the point source previously reported toward the supernova remnant shell. The other two overlap with neutral gas within ∼100 pc from the edge of the superbubble. The extended emission may be explained by either mismodeled gas in the interstellar background model or the local injection of particles. Under the latter hypothesis, explaining the component associated w…

title: Does corporate participation in rural revitalization improve carbon performance? Evidence fromknowledge resource integration and green innovation
abstract: Purpose In the context of China’s “dual carbon” goals and the rural revitalization strategy, whether corporate social participation can translate into environmental benefits remains a critical yet underexplored question. Drawing on the knowledge-based view and organizational learning theory, this study aims to investigate whether and how corporate participation in rural revitalization improves corporate carbon performance. It further explores the mediating mechanisms of green innovation and financing constraint alleviation, as well as the moderating role of internal governance characteristics and external institutional environments. Design/methodology/approach This study utilizes a panel dataset of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2016 to 2021, comprising 1,016 listed companies and 5,513 unbalanced panel observations. Corporate carbon performance is measured using industry-level carbon emission data from the CEADs database, and rural revitalization participation is captured by both the logarithm of poverty alleviation fund investments and a dummy variable indicating whether a firm participates in rural revitalization. Fixed-effects models are employed to test the hypotheses, and a series of robustness checks – including replacing the dependent variable, propensity score matching (PSM), excluding carbon trading pilot cities and excluding municipalities directly under the centra…

title: The Impact of Quality Management Maturity on Carbon Reduction Performance in Intelligent Manufacturing Enterprises: An Empirical Analysis Based on Digital Transformation Capability
abstract: With the rapid development of intelligent manufacturing and the increasing global demand for carbon neutrality, improving carbon reduction performance has become a critical objective for manufacturing enterprises. This study investigates the impact of quality management maturity on carbon reduction performance in intelligent manufacturing enterprises and examines the mediating role of digital transformation capability. Based on survey data collected from manufacturing enterprises, an empirical model is established using structural equation modeling to explore the relationships among quality management maturity, digital transformation capability, and carbon reduction performance. The results indicate that quality management maturity significantly promotes carbon reduction performance by enhancing operational efficiency, optimizing resource allocation, and strengthening environmental management practices. Furthermore, digital transformation capability plays a significant mediating role by facilitating data-driven decision-making, intelligent process optimization, and sustainable production management. This study extends the existing literature on quality management and green manufacturing by integrating digital transformation capabilities into the framework of carbon performance improvement. The findings provide practical implications for intelligent manufacturing enterprises see…

title: Energy expenditure of bonobos across their locomotor repertoire
abstract: Abstract Unlike quadrupedal mammals, primates use diverse locomotor modes adapted to arboreal environments. Such diversity of movements challenges allometric models, which underestimate energetic costs by focusing on steady-state walking. To address this, we combined ethological and biomechanical approaches to estimate the net metabolic cost of transport in bonobos (Pan paniscus). Using three-dimensional tracking and a point-mass model, we derived this estimate from net mechanical power and muscle efficiency across locomotor modes. Our results show that quadrupedalism in bonobos (10–12 J kg⁻¹ m⁻¹) exceeds mammalian predictions (approx. 3 J kg⁻¹ m⁻¹), whereas vertical ascent (26–32 J kg⁻¹ m⁻¹) is the most costly mode. However, arboreal locomotion incurs no major energetic penalty, given the high potential for energy recovery via kinetic/potential energy exchange during vertical descent and suspensory locomotion. By integrating these data with field-derived locomotor repertoires, we estimate that daily travel distances (0.4–6 km) account for 3–53% of bonobos’ daily energy expenditure. Reversing quadrupedal/bipedal proportions in this model shifts costs to 4–62%. Notably, even with 35% bipedalism, 2 km daily travel remains energetically feasible for bonobos. This suggests that early hominins could have incorporated bipedalism into diverse repertoires without facing energetic const…

title: Anchored Targeted Projection Pursuit for Hypothesis-Driven Quality Control of Drill-Cuttings Geochemical Data
abstract: Wellsite X-ray fluorescence (XRF) analysis of drill cuttings provides multi-element profiles for chemostratigraphy, well correlation and reservoir characterization, but the data are exposed to artefacts of the drilling workflow, such as drilling-fluid residue, carry-over between samples and detector drift. Quality control (QC) usually relies on principal component analysis (PCA), which ranks samples by variance rather than geological meaning, or on supervised classifiers, which need labels that do not exist at the QC stage. In practice, analysts often suspect a problem and can point to a few samples that show it. We introduce anchored targeted projection pursuit (anchored TPP), which builds its projection target from these anchors alone and leaves all other samples unconstrained. The fit reduces to a weighted orthogonal Procrustes problem with a closed-form solution and no tuning parameters. It remains well posed when variables outnumber samples, and its loadings name the elemental contrast behind each flag. We test it on a synthetic XRF benchmark and on a semi-synthetic experiment that plants a potassium chloride (KCl) brine mud signature into real cuttings data from an unconventional hydrocarbon well. Anchored TPP detects contamination that PCA and single-element thresholds miss, and log-ratio pre-treatment more than doubles its recovery. Positive--unlabelled learning recover…

title: Lecture material on an energy-budget perspective on climate change, climate change forcings and feedbacks
From migrants into Frenchmen: the republican model of linguistic integration reconsidered
abstract: Abstract Over the last two decades, European migration policies have increasingly mandated official language proficiency as a prerequisite for residency and citizenship. While ostensibly a functional tool for social participation, linguistic integration is heavily criticized by scholars for its normative ambiguity. The article focuses on the specific case of France, where language requirements are justified through the “republican model”. In this framework, political integration is the foundation of social cohesion; however, this approach often promotes a unitary culture and monolingualism as essential to the civic community. The author aims to challenge the coherence of the French institutional discourse by comparing it with the republican ideals found in political philosophy, particularly the work of Ronald Dworkin. Ultimately, the text argues that a true republican ideal should not demand linguistic homogenization. Instead, it should recognize linguistic diversity as a vital source of cultural reflexivity and a central component of the common life shared by citizens in modern and diverse democracies.

title: Association of energy poverty, import and export diversification with agricultural sector performance in South Asia
abstract: This paper examines the association between energy poverty, import diversification, export diversification, and agricultural sector performance in South Asia, while controlling for carbon dioxide emissions from agriculture and employment in agriculture. Using panel data for eight South Asian countries—Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka—covering the period from 2000 to 2023, the study constructs an Energy Poverty Index through Principal Component Analysis based on six energy-related indicators. The Feasible Generalized Least Squares results show that better energy conditions and lower energy poverty are positively associated with agricultural sector performance. In contrast, import diversification and carbon dioxide emissions from agriculture are negatively associated with agricultural sector performance, while export diversification is positively associated with it. Employment in agriculture shows a positive but statistically insignificant association. These findings remain robust when Panel-Corrected Standard Errors and Driscoll–Kraay standard error estimators are applied. Overall, the results suggest that improved energy access, environmentally sustainable agricultural practices, and strategic trade diversification are closely linked to agricultural sector performance in South Asia.

title: Regulatory framework towards fusion energy in Germany: preliminary results and open issues
abstract: Abstract The paper introduces preliminary results of the German project for regulation of future fusion facilities (ReFus) which was started in January 2025. It presents the existing German regulatory framework and how it was applied for the licensing of the stellarator Wendelstein 7-X. The analysis demonstrates that the German radiation protection law and its subsequent rules and regulations are already generally applicable to fusion. However, certain adaptations and clarifications are recommended to simplify the licensing process, especially with respect to a graded safety approach considering the broad scope of future facilities from demonstrators up to full size power plants.

title: An enterprise integration framework for blockchain-enabled payment automation in construction projects
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to propose an enterprise integration framework that integrates blockchain-enabled smart contracts, enterprise project management systems, and IoT-supported verification for automated payment management in construction projects. Design/methodology/approach A three-stage research methodology was adopted, comprising a systematic literature review, the development of an enterprise integration framework, and expert validation through which the proposed framework was refined. Findings The findings indicate that blockchain alone is insufficient for payment automation in construction projects. Effective implementation requires integration with enterprise project management systems, IoT-supported verification, and governance mechanisms. The validated enterprise integration framework demonstrates how these technologies can be combined to support transparent, automated, and reliable construction payment processes. Research limitations/implications The framework is conceptually validated and has not yet been implemented in real construction projects. Future research should evaluate its operational performance and interoperability across different enterprise project management environments. Originality/value Unlike previous studies focusing primarily on blockchain technology, this study proposes an enterprise integration framework that combines enterprise project man…
venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology

title: Deciphering Myocardial Energy Metabolism in the Transplanted Heart
Artificial intelligence-assisted surrogate networks for thermal energy transport in radiative nanofluid model containing oxytactic microorganisms with mass flux-free conditions
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explore the thermal energy transfer in radiative nanofluid flow of oxytactic microorganisms under zero mass flux conditions with potential application in engineering systems. The investigation concerns free convection over an isothermal perpendicular cone in a permeable medium filled with a nanofluid. Design/methodology/approach A deep learning-based nonlinear autoregressive exogenous neural network optimized with Levenberg–Marquardt backpropagation (NARX-DNN-LMBP) is designed for the model of the radiative nanofluidic flow with microorganism (RNF-MO). It includes the effects of Brownian motion, solar radiation, thermophoresis, convective heating, suspended nanoparticles and oxytactic microorganisms along with zero mass flux boundary conditions. The synthetic data set is created using the Lobatto IIIA numerical solver and then randomly split into training, validation and test sets used to develop the neural network. Findings The proposed NARX-DNN-LMBP approach is found to be effective in predicting the RNF-MO model for various physical scenarios with mean squared error as low as 10−10. It is further evaluated with the mean squared error convergence trends, error histograms and error autocorrelation analysis to show accurate and reliable computational performance. Originality/value The novelty is achieved by coupling the NARX-DNN-LMBP deep learning fra…
venue: International Journal of Numerical Methods for Heat & Fluid Flow

title: Research on the Impact of Data Element Agglomeration on Urban Energy Efficiency
abstract: Data elements, as a new type of production factor, inject new momentum into enhancing urban energy efficiency and hold significant importance for achieving China's energy conservation, emission reduction, and green development goals. Based on panel data from 280 prefecture-level cities in China from 2011 to 2023, this study empirically examines the relationship between data element agglomeration and urban energy efficiency using a multi-period difference-in-differences model. The findings reveal that data element agglomeration significantly enhances urban energy efficiency. Mechanism tests indicate that data element agglomeration improves urban energy efficiency by promoting energy-saving technological progress and optimizing energy allocation. Heterogeneity analysis shows that the effect of data element agglomeration on urban energy efficiency is more pronounced in cities where officials have long-term performance perspectives, environmental regulations are stringent, and in resource-based cities. Further analysis demonstrates that data element agglomeration has a positive spatial spillover effect on urban energy efficiency, with the optimal spillover range observed within 200KM to 650KM from the city. This study provides important insights for governments to improve data element institutions and formulate energy conservation and emission reduction policies.

title: Energy-saving hydrogen production coupled with PET-derived ethylene glycol oxidation: Reaction mechanisms, catalyst design, and reactor engineering
abstract: Abstract The growing accumulation of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) waste and the increasing demand for clean hydrogen call for integrated electrochemical strategies. Ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), derived from PET hydrolysis, offers a thermodynamically favorable alternative to the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and can be coupled with the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) to simultaneously produce value-added chemicals and H2. This review provides a system-level overview of EGORHER paired electrolysis, spanning reaction fundamentals, catalyst design, cell configuration, and future challenges. First, the competing EGOR pathways toward C1 products (such as formate/formic acid) and C2 products (such as glycolate/glycolic acid) are discussed. Key energetic descriptors, including cell voltage, overpotential, Faradaic efficiency, and energy efficiency, are then summarized to clarify the advantages of replacing OER with EGOR. Recent advances in catalysts, including precious metals, transition-metal compounds, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), organic catalysts, and hybrid systems, are reviewed with attention to their bifunctional or compatible activity for EGOR and HER. Reactor design is further discussed by comparing single-cell and dual-cell H-type reactors with membrane-free and membrane-separated flow-cell reactors, emphasizing their different roles in ma…

title: Teachers as SDG gatekeepers: educator roles in Sustainable Development Goal integration among secondary students in Lebanon and Dubai
abstract: Purpose This study explores how teachers and school leaders influence secondary school students' engagement with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Lebanon and Dubai, UAE. Although the two contexts share a regional setting, they differ significantly in their institutional capacity to support sustainability education. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-methods approach was used. Quantitative data were collected through a survey of 267 Lebanese secondary school students. In Dubai, qualitative data came from focus group discussions with 30 students in three international schools. Semi-structured interviews were also conducted with 11 education professionals across both contexts. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests and inductive thematic coding. Findings The results show a clear structural difference between the two contexts. In Lebanon, sustainability education was described by participants as depending largely on individual teacher or school leadership initiatives. Where such initiative was absent, participants reported that the topic was less likely to be raised in class. In Dubai, participants described sustainability as already present through several national and institutional frameworks before it reached the classroom; the focus group discussions showed high self-reported SDG awareness and strong thematic engagement …
venue: International Journal of Comparative Education and Development

title: Stress-correlated stereom organization in the echinoid tubercle reveals hierarchical mechanical integration
abstract: Abstract Echinoid tests consist of a highly porous skeletal microstructure (stereom) optimized in terms of functional performance. One of the most mechanically demanding components of the test is the tubercle, which forms the mechanical interface between the test plates and spines and is subjected to complex loads generated by motion of the spine. However, the mechanical behaviour of tubercles under realistic loading conditions remains poorly explored. Here, we investigate the tubercle of Prionocidaris baculosa using high-resolution X-ray microscopy and finite-element analysis to simulate physiologically relevant loading, identify the main stress directions, and assess mechanical efficiency through topology optimization. By correlating experimental and numerical results, we quantify the relationship between stress distributions and stereom organization, providing new insights into the mechanical complexity of echinoid skeletons. We found a strong correlation between experimentally determined density and different stress parameters (von Mises stress, principal stress trajectories and mean normal stress), supporting the hypothesis of a functionally graded and mechanically optimized stereom architecture. These findings highlight the echinoid skeleton as a naturally optimized, load-adaptive structure with potential relevance for bioinspired design. In particular, stereom-inspired a…

title: Following Photoexcited Structural Dynamics across Potential Energy Surfaces in Solids
abstract: Abstract

title: Why No One Has Implemented the Turing Test: Identifying Turing’s Design and Putting it into Practice
abstract: Abstract In October 1950, Alan Turing proposed that a machine’s success in an imitation game provides a criterion for thinking. Turing’s test became one of the philosophical foundations of AI, but three-quarters of a century later, it is widely claimed that generative AI models pass the test, rendering it obsolete. Our aim here is to establish definitively Turing’s conceptual design for his game. We argue that influential interpretations of Turing’s design are mistaken, with the consequence that his test has not been passed. We also present the results of carrying out, for the first time, Turing’s experiment as he proposed it.

title: From compliance to performance: bridging normative standards, user experience and digital inspection in building handover
abstract: Purpose This study aims to evaluate the alignment between building inspection and handover practices and the methodological requirements established by IBAPE-MG 004:2016, examine user experience during handover and propose a digitally supported, performance-oriented inspection framework. Design/methodology/approach An exploratory-descriptive mixed-method approach combined a narrative review of five Brazilian case studies with empirical evidence from 26 residential units. Documented inspection practices were compared against nine methodological requirements of IBAPE-MG 004:2016, while user perceptions of communication, documentation, satisfaction and defect identification were assessed through questionnaires. The two evidence streams were subsequently integrated through data triangulation. Findings The documented case studies fulfilled between 4/9 and 6/9 of the assessed methodological requirements, with recurring gaps in document verification, graphical defect localization, photographic traceability and formal reporting. The residential survey indicated generally positive satisfaction while identifying shortcomings in communication, documentation delivery and defect management. Together, these findings indicate opportunities to strengthen inspection as a structured diagnostic and performance-management process. Research limitations/implications The comparative analysis was limi…

title: Design and performance evaluation of a GPON-based fiber-to-the-campus network: a case study of the University of Kufa/Faculty of Engineering
abstract: Abstract Campus-wide broadband infrastructure increasingly requires optical access solutions that overcome the distance, capacity, and interference limitations of copper-based digital subscriber lines, yet comparatively few studies evaluate a GPON-based architecture on a university campus using real, surveyed building geometry and a controlled comparison of candidate optical-fiber types. This study designs and simulates a GPON-based fiber-to-the-campus (FTTCampus) network connecting the eight departmental buildings of the Faculty of Engineering, University of Kufa, Iraq, to a single optical line terminal (OLT) through a 1 × 8 passive splitter, with drop-fiber distances (0.095–0.27 km) obtained from Google Earth site imagery. The topology was modeled in OptiSystem at a bit rate of 1 Gbit/s for three candidate fiber configurations, single-mode step-index, multimode step-index, and multimode graded-index, evaluated through eye-diagram analysis, quality factor (Q-factor), and bit-error rate (BER), and the optical link budget of every department link was reconstructed to explicitly include the 1 × 8 splitter insertion loss. The single-mode step-index configuration achieved the highest signal quality (Q-factor up to 136.2), clearly outperforming both multimode configurations. With the splitter loss included, every department link remained functional, retaining an available margin of …

title: Health Policy for Obesity and Metabolic Syndrome in Asian Health Systems: Three Design Principles, Three Binding Constraints, and the Governance That Decides between Them
Design of an intralayer data-based controller for laser powder bed fusion processing
abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a data-based approach to reduce defect-prone process conditions during the additive manufacturing of Ti-6Al-4V alloy parts using the laser powder bed fusion technique. The focus is on controlling melt pool emissions intensity used as a temperature-related proxy generated as the laser interacts with the alloy powder to avoid processing conditions which generate defects such as lack-of-fusion (LOF) or keyhole porosity. A data-based controller is developed using photodiode signals from the melt pool emissions to predict future melt pool data and then update the control input accordingly. The prediction is achieved by estimating the Markov parameters and constructing a finite impulse response (FIR) model of the process. This controller, termed the data-based predictive FIR-based proportional controller, adjusts the laser energy input by applying a proportional correction to deviations of the melt pool emissions from their setpoint, thereby mitigating under- or overheating of the melt pool. The developed approach is investigated for the printing of spinal cage medical devices and evaluated through a closed-loop MATLAB simulation to assess its potential for intralayer control. A threshold-based anomaly detection approach is then employed to quantitatively evaluate the controller’s effectiveness in reducing defect-prone signal excursions. Results demonstra…
venue: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology

title: Development of EDP.AI: An AI-integrated engineering design module to enhance student engagement in STEM learning
abstract: STEM education is a national priority in Malaysia; however, clear gaps in learning outcomes and student participation remain, particularly in rural areas. In Sabah, very low Indeks STEM Murid (ISM) scores, coupled with declining enrolment in the STEM Package A stream, indicate persistent challenges in the quality and continuity of STEM learning at the lower secondary level. These trends suggest that many students do not experience STEM learning as sufficiently meaningful or structured to build confidence and sustain their interest in STEM pathways. This paper reports Phase 1A of a Design and Development Research (DDR) study, focusing on the needs analysis and conceptualisation of EDP.AI, an AI-assisted module designed to scaffold the Engineering Design Process (EDP) for lower secondary students in rural Sabah. Document analysis was conducted to examine challenges related to STEM learning, EDP implementation, artificial intelligence in education, and Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) in low-resource contexts. The evidence was synthesised using design rationale mapping to translate theoretical and contextual insights into actionable design decisions. The outcomes of Phase 1A include the identification of key needs and challenges, the formulation of preliminary design requirements and design principles, and the development of a conceptual model to guide the design of EDP.AI. The propose…

title: Theoretical analysis of energy transport in magnetised bioconvective micropolar nanofluid flow over a stretching sheet: a Cattaneo-Christov model
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we examine the magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) stagnation-point flow of an electrically conducting micropolar nanofluid over a stretching sheet in a porous medium. Mathematically, the model integrates the combined effects of non-Fourier Cattaneo-Christov thermal flux, Arrhenius activation energy with binary chemical reaction, Joule heating, thermal radiation, and bioconvection due to gyrotactic microorganisms in a novel manner. The problem is governed by nonlinear boundary layer partial differential equations which are transformed into a system of coupled ordinary differential equations using similarity transformations and solved numerically using the MATLAB solver bvp5c with the addition of a firing technique. The computational results show that the mainline velocity increases with an increase in the stretching ratio parameter whilst the micro-rotation of the particle is decreased. Cattaneo- Christov thermal relaxation decreases the heat penetration. The thermal boundary layer thickness decreases with Cattaneo- Christov thermal relaxation. Thermal radiation, viscous dissipation and Joule heating increase the temperature dispersion considerably. The increase in activation energy reduces the consumption of species and improves the concentration field of nanoparticles. The bioconvective Lewis and Peclet numbers lower the density of motile microorganisms in the …

title: An interpretable, physics-constrained model for woody-plant evapotranspiration under heat and drought extremes in China
abstract: Evapotranspiration (ET) integrates the water, energy and carbon economy of woody-plant ecosystems and is a primary channel through which climate change acts on forests. Yet existing ET products diverge markedly over forested terrain, and purely data-driven models tend to lose skill precisely under the hot, dry and high vapour pressure deficit (VPD) conditions that increasingly threaten woody plants. Here, an interpretable, physics-constrained adaptive-weighting framework was developed to estimate daily latent heat flux (LE) for woody-plant ecosystems and was evaluated across a climate gradient from tropical rainforest to boreal larch forest in China. The framework couples a Penman–Monteith physical branch, in which a machine-learning model predicts surface resistance, with a data-driven branch that predicts LE directly, and fuses the two through a sample-level adaptive weight learned from the data. The model was trained and validated on 17,515 daily eddy-covariance observations from twelve woody-plant flux sites, together with reanalysis meteorology, satellite vegetation indices and a spaceborne canopy-height product. Under random cross-validation, the adaptive model and the data-driven branch performed comparably ( R 2 = 0.83), whereas the physical branch alone was weaker ( R 2 = 0.40). Under extrapolation to unseen climate extremes, the data-driven branch explained less varia…

title: Plant–microbe–nematode interactions in soilborne disease complexes: emerging concepts and sustainable management
Identification photosynthesis-related genes in peanut ( Arachis hypogaea L.) by hyperspectral phenomics, GWAS and RNA-seq
abstract: Abstract Peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) contributes importantly to the global food supply, and its yield potential is closely linked to leaf photosynthetic efficiency. However, conventional measurement of leaf net-photosynthetic-rate (Leaf Pn) is time- and labor-intensive, limiting its application to large breeding populations. We established a phenomics-driven framework integrating hyperspectral reflectance and genome-wide association studies for high-throughput evaluation and genetic dissection of Leaf Pn. Machine-learning models were trained on preprocessed spectral data from 1,200 leaf samples collected in four environments. Random forest performed best after Savitzky-Golay (S-G) smoothing and first-derivative transformation (R2 = 0.81, root mean square error [RMSE] = 1.50), outperforming the vegetation index-based model (R2 = 0.66). Applying this model to a panel of 173 peanut genotypes identified two quantitative trait loci, qPn5.1 and qPn13.1, encompassing seven candidate genes. Integrated analyses prioritized Arahy.K5L3ZW, which encodes protein kinase 2B. Silencing this gene increased Leaf Pn, whereas transient overexpression decreased it, indicating that Arahy.K5L3ZW negatively regulates Leaf Pn. This framework enables high-throughput genetic dissection of seedling photosynthetic capacity and identifies a candidate target for improving photosynthetic efficiency in peanut…

title: Bioinspired Self-Floating Hydrogel-Coated Foam for Synergistic Solar Power Generation and Desalination
abstract: Abstract Interfacial solar-driven evaporation provides a sustainable route for freshwater generation, but practical implementation remains limited by salt accumulation, insufficient understanding of water/ion transport, and inefficient utilization of the evaporated vapor. Herein, we report an interfacially engineered self-floating hydrogel-coated foam evaporator constructed by anchoring Ketjen black/sodium alginate/tannic acid/Fe3+ networks onto a melamine foam skeleton. The Fe3+ ions serve as multivalent coordination centers, simultaneously interacting with the carboxylate groups of sodium alginate and the phenolic groups of tannic acid, thereby forming a stable hydrophilic coating with enhanced surface wettability and robust interfacial adhesion. The open-cell macroporous foam provides low-resistance water supply pathways, while the hydrophilic hydrogel coating promotes surface-mediated water spreading and salt redissolution. Under 1 sun illumination, the optimized evaporator exhibits an evaporation rate of 3.56 kg m–2 h–1 and a solar-to-vapor efficiency of 92.4%. This performance is attributed to broadband solar absorption, localized heat management, and reduced effective evaporation enthalpy of interfacial water. The evaporator maintains stable evaporation in seawater for 120 h without obvious salt crystallization, mainly owing to capillary rewetting, concentration-gradient…

title: Risk assessment of wind-solar coupled compressed air energy storage power station in high-altitude areas
Distinct root apoplastic barrier distribution and conserved peroxidase function in desert trees
abstract: Abstract The formation of extracellular barriers in roots plays a critical role in maintaining water balance and nutrient homeostasis; however, their molecular composition and physiological roles in desert-adapted plants remain largely unexplored. Here, we examine apoplastic barrier formation in the roots of two arid-adapted, ecologically and economically important tree species: date palm (Phoenix dactylifera) and grey mangrove (Avicennia marina). In date palm, lignin and suberin showed complementary distribution patterns within the outer root layers. In mangrove roots, lignin accumulated in the epidermis and exodermis, whereas suberin was concentrated in the exodermis. Label-free Raman spectroscopy imaging confirmed these spatial patterns. Noninvasive Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed that water distribution mirrored barrier localization: date palms retained water in the vasculature and outer tissues, whereas mangroves concentrated water in the xylem. Transcriptome analysis identified a type III PEROXIDASE (PER) highly expressed in the exodermis of both species. The PER protein localized to Golgi-derived vesicles and the plasma membrane and interacted with a component of the Golgi apparatus. Expression of date palm and mangrove PER in Arabidopsis thaliana leads to ectopic lignin deposition in the root epidermis. Together, our findings suggest that type III PEROXIDASES …

title: The power of co-teaching mathematics
abstract: Co-teaching mathematics lessons, including collaborative planning, teaching, and reflection, has the potential to support teachers and learners in primary classrooms to thrive. In the context of a noisy landscape of competing ideas about mathematics education, co-teaching can sharpen teacher noticing, build professional confidence, and support equitable, impactful teaching. Small adjustments towards more collaborative teaching can create significant benefits for teachers and learners, helping all to thrive in a rapidly changing educational environment.

title: Energy Extraction from Rotating Black Hole in Effective Quantum Gravity via Comisso-Asenjo Magnetic Reconnection Process
abstract: Abstract We investigate the energy extraction from a rotating quantum corrected black hole in effective quantum gravity through the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism. We determine the allowed parameter space for the energy extraction and evaluate the extraction efficiency for both circular and combined plasma streamlines. For circular streamlines, increasing the quantum parameter generally shrinks the allowed parameter space. For combined streamlines, the plunging phase significantly expands the accessible radial range and broadens the extraction domain, while the relative influence of quantum corrections diminishes. Our results indicate the existence of a critical quantum parameter, above which energy extraction ceases. In contrast to circular streamlines, the allowed parameter space for combined streamlines exhibits asymmetry relative to the orientation angle, suggesting a preference for positive optimal angles. We show that the quantum correction enhances the overall extraction efficiency and reduces the optimal reconnection radius. These results suggest that the magnetic-reconnection-driven energy extraction may serve as a probe of effective quantum gravity effects in the rotating black hole spacetime.

title: Didactic Approaches for Teaching Energy Concepts in Early Childhood Education
abstract: This paper examines didactic mediation strategies for instructing essential energy concepts to children aged 4 to 6, based on Cultural Historical Activity Theory (CHAT). This study highlights the culturally contextualized and socially facilitated learning necessary to render energy ideas comprehensible and significant, acknowledging the abstract nature of energy and the developmental preparedness of preschoolers. The essay conducts a thorough literature review to identify obstacles in early energy education and emphasizes the significance of experiential, cooperative, and contextually pertinent teaching techniques. The suggested educational framework integrates familiar experiences, interactive activities, and multimedia tools to enhance scientific literacy and environmental consciousness among young students. The educator"s function as a mediator facilitates children"s active participation, inquiry, and reflection, so fostering higher-order thinking in alignment with CHAT principles. The article addresses practical issues such as teacher preparedness and resource constraints and delineates strategies for formative evaluation and pilot implementation in kindergarten environments. The study integrates didactic mediation with CHAT, providing a comprehensive educational framework that empowers instructors and fosters sustainable ideals from a young age. This study enhances early c…

title: First-principles investigation of hydrogen adsorption and storage mechanisms on Ni- and Pt-decorated SiCNTs toward green energy applications
abstract: Introduction Hydrogen storage and efficient hydrogen adsorption issues still pose significant frontiers for next-generation clean energy applications. The study provides a comprehensive first-principles investigation of the hydrogen adsorption on pristine and metal-decorated silicon carbide nanotubes (SiCNTs). Methods Structural stability and adsorption behaviour, electronic structure and charge redistribution mechanisms were systematically investigated using the spin-polarized density functional theory within the GGA-PBE framework. Successive hydrogen adsorption was investigated by considering one, two, and three H 2 molecules. Results Furthermore, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations performed at 300 K confirmed the thermal stability of both Ni–SiCNT+H 2 and Pt–SiCNT+H 2 systems, with no noticeable metal desorption or severe structural distortion observed during the simulation period. The calculated binding energies of −1.44 eV for Ni and −4.10 eV for Pt confirm stable metal anchoring on the SiCNT surface, leading to enhanced hydrogen adsorption behavior compared with pristine SiCNT. For a single H 2 molecule, the adsorption energies follow the order Ni–SiCNT (−1.991 eV) > Pt–SiCNT (−1.747 eV) > pristine SiCNT (−0.184 eV). As the hydrogen loading increases, the average adsorption energy gradually decreases to −1.353 and −0.882 eV/H 2 for Ni-decorated SiCNT and to −0…

title: Pavement vibration-based estimation of vehicle speed and axle spacing for intelligent transportation infrastructure
abstract: Vehicle speed and axle spacing are key parameters that shape the pavement vibration response and serve as essential prior inputs for downstream models such as axle-load estimation and hidden-void detection. Obtaining them from external systems such as video is vulnerable to weather and to time-synchronisation errors between systems, whereas estimating them from the pavement vibration signal itself enables closed-loop interpretation of traffic information and structural state within a single embedded system. Using field data from embedded MEMS accelerometers, this study reconstructs the signal with complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) and dominant-frequency screening, builds an instantaneous total-energy curve via the continuous wavelet transform, and estimates speed and axle spacing by pairing prominent energy peaks across two sensors; the method is compared, under identical criteria, with a time-domain envelope peak method. For 12 field passes of a four-axle truck (25.00–55.62 t, 40–60 km/h), both methods succeed in every case. Over the ten cases evaluated against the 7750 mm total wheelbase, the two methods have similar median errors (6.5% vs. 6.8%), whereas the wavelet energy method has a lower mean (6.2% vs. 8.8%), a narrower interquartile range (3.3 vs. 4.8 percentage points) and a much lower maximum (10.5% vs. 33.8%); in the two cas…

title: An age-stratified semiquantitative urine ACR triage strategy for quantitative confirmation: a retrospective diagnostic accuracy study with temporal validation
abstract: Abstract Objectives Early detection of albuminuria is important for identifying individuals at risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. Semiquantitative urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) strips may serve as an initial laboratory screening or triage tool. However, screening strategies generally apply a single fixed threshold, regardless of patient age. Because CKD prevalence increases with age, a single cut-off does not account for differences in pre-test probability across age groups, potentially resulting in different trade-offs between quantitative confirmation and false-negative classification. We evaluated an age-adjusted threshold approach to improve diagnostic safety while reducing the number of quantitative ACR confirmations required. Methods Semiquantitative ACR strip results (UC-3500, Sysmex) and quantitative ACR values (Alinity c, Abbott) were collected and analyzed. Diagnostic performance indicators for ACR strip testing were evaluated across different decision thresholds in the overall population and among age groups (18–44, 45–64 and ≥65 years), using quantitative ACR measurement as the reference standard. Results Selected thresholds were 30, 30, and 15 mg/g creatinine for the 18–44, 45–64, and ≥65-year age groups with false omission rates (FOR) of 1.36 %, 3.97 % and 4.47 %, respectively. Overall, the age-stratified strategy yielded a sensitivity of …

title: Semantic distance for hypothesis generation in differential diagnosis: a framework to support the pivot and cluster strategy
abstract: Abstract The pivot and cluster strategy (PCS) is an emerging approach to diagnostic hypothesis generation. In this strategy, clinicians generate an initial intuitive diagnosis (the pivot) along with a cluster of diseases with similar clinical representations for systematic consideration. Although PCS was proposed to prevent diagnostic error, a knowledge gap remains in its practical implementation: existing differential diagnosis lists rely primarily on individual expertise, lacking reproducibility and scalability. We have previously proposed that deliberately exploring diseases at a moderate semantic distance, that is, diseases moderately similar to the pivot, may foster diagnostic creativity. Building on that proposal, this paper specifies it as a rank-defined, auditable research programme, drawing on two established methods: ranking candidate diagnoses by embedding-based similarity, and building disease vectors from clinical presentation, not disease names. Each disease is represented as a disease concept vector and positioned within a high-dimensional semantic space (the disease map). Diseases with similar clinical features are thereby intended to lie close together, a testable design rather than an established property. Candidate diagnoses are ranked by cosine similarity to a given pivot disease. Because training is stochastic and corpus-dependent, the ranking is auditable …

title: Social Capital as the Foundation for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Strategy: A Case Study of the Goat Village Oro-Oro, Supported by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga AFT Juanda
abstract: Implementing Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) through a community development approach requires strategies tailored to a community’s social characteristics so that programs are participatory and sustainable. However, CSR strategies are often formulated without considering community social capital as a basis for program planning. This study aims to analyze the social capital characteristics of the Kelompok Kambing Oro-Oro goat farmers and to explain their implications for the CSR strategy of PT Pertamina Patra Niaga AFT Juanda. A qualitative case study design was employed. Data were collected through interviews, observation, and documentation, and analyzed interactively through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing. The results show that the group’s social capital is reflected in three dimensions: trust, norms, and social networks. Together, these dimensions shape the community’s social capacity, which serves as a foundation for a CSR strategy that is more contextual, participatory, and sustainability-oriented, and which has shaped the distinct community development-based CSR approach of PT Pertamina Patra Niaga AFT Juanda. This study argues that identifying social capital is a foundational step in the pre-intervention stage and can serve as a basis for formulating CSR strategies before community empowerment programs are implemented.

title: Understanding AI visual search adoption in secondhand fashion retail
abstract: Purpose Secondhand fashion markets are characterised by high uncertainty, heterogeneous products and fragile trust, complicating consumers’ search and evaluation processes. This study employs the technology acceptance model while incorporating consumer trust to explain AI visual search adoption in a high-uncertainty secondhand C2C retail context. Design/methodology/approach Data were obtained from 299 Chinese consumers, and the model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Findings Perceived intelligence and perceived enjoyment enhance perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness and consumer trust, indicating their roles as core cognitive and affective drivers of adoption. Perceived risk negatively influences consumer trust, whereas perceived complexity reduces perceived ease of use. Perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness and consumer trust collectively shape adoption intention. Additionally, technology-related discomfort attenuates the effect of perceived ease of use on perceived usefulness. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of accurate AI-powered visual search, trust-building interface design and user support in facilitating adoption of AI visual search under conditions of high information uncertainty. Originality/value This research extends the TAM by demonstrating that consumer trust plays a central role in AI vi…

title: StarQuest Qur'an: A Reward-Based Interactive Media for Teaching Surah Al-Humazah to Grade II MI Students
abstract: Qur'an learning for Grade II Madrasah Ibtidaiyah students needs to be adjusted to the thinking of children aged seven to eight years, who prefer real things, attractive visuals, and pleasantly packaged presentations. This research uses the Research and Development (R&D) method with the ASSURE model, including needs analysis, goal setting, material selection, media utilization, student involvement, and evaluation, to produce StarQuest Qur'an interactive learning media on Surah Al-Humazah. Development starts with analyzing student characteristics, preparing materials, and designing a child-friendly display. Two experts' feasibility assessment showed that material experts rated it 93.75% and media experts 94.79%, both in the very feasible category. This research is limited to product feasibility assessment and does not test its direct impact on students. This media is expected to be an interesting learning alternative that supports students in understanding the meaning and moral message of Surah Al-Humazah, and further research is suggested to test its direct impact on students.

title: Reconceptualizing green innovation as an organizational capability: an integrated approach
abstract: Purpose This paper reconceptualizes green innovation as an integrative organizational capability rather than a standalone environmental or technological initiative. It examines how organizational, institutional and technological conditions shape its contribution to sustainable organizational performance. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a narrative literature review, drawing on the natural resource-based view (NRBV) to synthesize research on organizational capabilities, organizational learning, stakeholder relationships, institutional conditions and digital technologies. Findings The review shows that green innovation contributes to sustainable performance when supported by complementary capabilities, organizational learning, stakeholder collaboration, favorable institutional conditions and digital technologies. It further suggests that technologies alone are insufficient; outcomes depend on aligning organizational capabilities with contextual conditions. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual review, the proposed framework requires empirical validation across different organizational and institutional contexts. Practical implications Managers should embed green innovation within organizational strategy, strengthen learning, strengthen stakeholder collaboration, leverage digital technologies and adopt context-specific sustainability strategies. Originalit…

title: Manufacturing leaders’ perspectives on green employability skill development through multi-level organizational learning
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how manufacturing industry leaders understand the development of green employability skills through multi-level organizational learning (OL) processes and the role this development plays in building organizational sustainability competencies. Design/methodology/approach An interpretive qualitative design was used using reflexive thematic analysis. Sixteen manufacturing leaders representing diverse organizational sizes, functional areas and geographic regions across the United States were recruited through purposive and snowball sampling in collaboration with a state-level manufacturing trade association. Findings Three themes emerged: Learning Agility for Green Role Evolution, in which individual employees develop adaptive capacity for continuous skill renewal as green roles evolve; Green Employability Co-Design with Educational Ecosystems, in which organizations and educational institutions collaboratively develop sustainability-aligned curricula and credentials; and Green Learning Culture as a Catalyst for Organizational Change, in which embedded sustainability values and Human Resource Development (HRD) infrastructure drive enterprise-wide transformation. Practical implications Manufacturing leaders and HRD practitioners would benefit from designing learning interventions that operate across individual, team and organizational levels, integ…

title: Pengaruh Model Project Based Learning Berbasis Pembelajaran Mendalam terhadap Kemampuan Menulis Teks Deskripsi Siswa Kelas VII SMP Muhammadiyah 16 Lubuk Pakam Tahun Pelajaran 2025/2026
abstract: This study examined the descriptive text writing ability of seventh-grade students at SMP Muhammadiyah 16 Lubuk Pakam before and after implementing Project-Based Learning integrated with a Deep Learning approach and assessed the significance of the difference between their scores. The study employed a quantitative experimental method with a one-group pretest–posttest design. The population comprised all seventh-grade students at the school, while 20 students from the VII Leader class were selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using descriptive text writing tests administered before and after the intervention. Students’ writing was assessed using a rubric covering content, text structure, language conventions, vocabulary, spelling, and punctuation. The learning activities integrated project work with meaningful, mindful, and joyful learning principles. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and a paired-samples t-test in SPSS version 32. The findings showed that the mean pretest score was 46.09, categorized as poor, whereas the mean posttest score increased to 86.71, categorized as very good. The mean score increased by approximately 40.63 points. The paired-samples t-test indicated a statistically significant difference between pretest and posttest scores (t = −38.216, p < 0.001), below the 0.05 significance threshold. These findings indicate that st…

title: Industry 4.0 technologies and environmental sustainability performance in supply chains: an exploratory statistical and machine learning analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examines how key Industry 4.0 technologies relate to environmental sustainability performance in supply chains. Specifically, it examines Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Digital Twin and Cloud Computing, and explores their relative associations with sustainability outcomes using both statistical and machine learning techniques. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 268 supply chain and logistics professionals across multiple industries. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS software version 31.0.2. Machine learning analysis was carried out using Orange Data Mining to perform feature importance ranking and decision tree modeling, with model performance evaluated using 10-fold cross-validation. Findings Correlation and hierarchical regression analyses reveal no statistically significant association between any individual Industry 4.0 technology and environmental sustainability performance and tested pairwise interaction effects are likewise non-significant. Exploratory machine learning feature rankings order the technologies differently across three methods, and cross-validated models do not outperform a mean-only baseline, indicating no detectable predictive signal in these data. Research limitations/implica…

title: Reproduction of substorm auroral currents in the ionosphere using a machine-learning-based emulator and SuperDARN data assimilation
abstract: Auroral electrojet dynamics during isolated substorms are reproduced using a machine-learning-based emulator with SuperDARN data assimilation. Representing such short-timescale variability is important for improving space-weather prediction relevant to technological systems. Reproducing this variability remains challenging for the SMRAI emulator (Surrogate Model for the REPPU Auroral Ionosphere; Kataoka et al., 2024, https://doi.org/10.1029/2023SW003720), where REPPU is the REProduce Plasma Universe global magnetohydrodynamic simulation. SMRAI is trained on ionospheric outputs from a REPPU MHD simulation and primarily produces smooth and gradual variations in auroral currents during substorms. Therefore, we evaluate the performance of SMRAI with SuperDARN line-of-sight velocity data assimilation (Nakano et al.,2025, https://doi.org/10.1029/2025SW004488), referred to as the SMRAI–SD framework. Two isolated substorm events on 30 and 31 October 2023 are analyzed to assess the performance of the SMRAI–SD. The SMRAI–SD reproduces auroral current variability in closer agreement with observations than SMRAI, as indicated by improved correspondence with the AL and AU indices. Although reproducing AE indices is not the primary objective, they are used to evaluate the performance of the SMRAI–SD approach and to identify its strengths and limitations through comparison with observations a…

title: Socially guided individual learning mitigates the double-edged sword of pedagogy
abstract: Abstract Social learning and innovation are fundamental processes in cultural evolution, yet their interaction remains poorly understood. Prior research suggests that inheriting social information reduces exploration. However, most studies have focused on the transmission of fully fledged solutions. Here, we investigate whether alternative types of information can facilitate cumulative cultural evolution without reducing exploration. Specifically, we conducted a pre-registered experiment with 400 adult participants comparing the inheritance of solutions with that of heuristics—simple rules that guide problem solving. We found that social learners who inherited a heuristic explored more frequently and broadly than those who received a solution. Their productions were also less similar to those of their demonstrators, suggesting that heuristics foster more independent exploration. Despite these differences, both heuristics and solutions enabled learners to surpass their demonstrator's performance. These findings highlight that the type of social information transmitted plays a crucial role in the evolvability of culture.
