title: Machine learning, molecular docking, and experimental validation identify shared molecular signatures between idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension and malignant pleural mesothelioma: a retrospective study
abstract: Background Idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension (IPAH) exhibits cancer-like features, yet its pathogenesis remains unclear. Given molecular similarities between IPAH and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM), this study aimed to uncover shared transcriptomic patterns. Methods GEO datasets for IPAH and MPM were analyzed. Overlapping DEGs and WGCNA modules were identified. PPI network analysis combined with LASSO, random forest, and SVM-RFE was used to identify candidate biomarker genes. A classification model was constructed and evaluated using leave-one-out cross-validation and bootstrap optimism correction. Immune infiltration was evaluated by ssGSEA. Molecular docking and MD simulations assessed drug binding to candidate target proteins. qRT-PCR validated candidate biomarker gene expression. Results Six concordantly upregulated and eleven concordantly downregulated DEGs were shared between IPAH and MPM. Upregulated genes were enriched in cell cycle regulation, while downregulated genes were enriched in neutrophil chemotaxis. WGCNA identified 58 overlapping genes. CXCR2, S100A9, and LCN2 were identified as candidate biomarker genes. A ROTS sensitivity analysis confirmed that all 1710 MPM DEGs were reproducible and directionally concordant at the matching FDR <0.05 threshold despite the imbalanced case–control ratio. The classification model achieved AUCs of 0.909 and 0…

title: The Impact of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) on Reducing Anxiety and Enhancing School Engagement: A Case Study at ‘Androkli Kostallari’ Elemantary School
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of a Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) intervention in reducing anxiety and enhancing students' school engagement at Androkli Kostallari School in Shkozë. The target group consists of first, second, and fifth-grade students, selected due to a high prevalence of students from divorced families, a demographic known to face heightened emotional and behavioral challenges. The study employs a qualitative methodology, integrating descriptive data to assess the impact of the SEL intervention. Teachers, trained in SEL techniques, implemented activities in the classroom while receiving continuous mentorship. Data were collected through teachers' reports on student progress, with a focus on emotional, behavioral, cognitive, and physical aspects of student well-being. The results indicated significant improvements in students' emotional regulation, behavior, cognitive skills, and physical well-being, contributing to a more positive and engaging school environment. This study underscores the importance of SEL in fostering emotional resilience and academic success, particularly for students facing family-related stressors.
venue: Journal of Social Research and Behavioral Sciences

title: Development and preliminary evaluation of ROMI using Articulate Storyline for sixth-grade learning about Earth’s rotation
abstract: Background- Critical thinking is an important skill for students, particularly in learning science concepts such as Earth’s rotation. Preliminary assessment showed that students’ critical thinking ability had a low category. Objectives- This study aimed to develop and conduct a preliminary evaluation of Rotation Media Interactive (ROMI) using Articulate Storyline for sixth-grade. Method- This study employed the ADDIE development model. The participants were sixth-grade students at a public elementary school in Palembang. The developed media was evaluated through expert validation, individual and small-group trials, and a field evaluation involving 18 students. Data were collected using expert validation sheets, student response questionnaires, and critical thinking tests. Results- ROMI obtained an average feasibility score of 94.71% from material, media, and practitioner validation, categorized as very feasible. Student responses indicated high practicality, with average scores of 93.06% in the individual trial and 93.15% in the small-group trial. In the field evaluation, the mean critical thinking test score increased from 62.89 to 93.89 after implementation, with a mean N-Gain of 0.835, categorized as high. Conclusions- ROMI received favorable expert evaluations and student responses and showed promising results in the preliminary field evaluation. However, the observed score…

title: Explainable machine learning for anticipating county-level disaster recovery burden in the built environment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop and evaluate an explainable machine-learning framework to anticipate county-level high recovery burden from natural disasters one year ahead using only public administrative and social-vulnerability data. Its substantive aim is to help built-environment decision makers shift from reactive post-event allocation to earlier, place-based prioritization of recovery and mitigation effort. Design/methodology/approach A county-year panel was assembled for 3,042 US counties over 2014–2022 by combining FEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries with county-level CDC/ATSDR social vulnerability index data. The outcome was a high-burden county-year, defined as repeated county-level declarations involving public assistance and/or hazard mitigation programme activity. Class-weighted logistic regression, random forest and XGBoost were benchmarked using a temporally ordered train-validation-test split. SHAP values and model coefficients were used to interpret predictive drivers. Findings The benchmark produced a moderate but decision-relevant predictive signal. Class-weighted logistic regression achieved the strongest out-of-sample performance on the hold-out period (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.626; area under the precision–recall curve 0.140; F1-score 0.262) and outperformed the more flexible tree-based models. Across models, stronger p…

title: Movement in mathematics teaching and learning
abstract: As mathematics and dance teachers, we are interested in how movement, dance, and mathematics are entwined. Increasingly, research shows how movement is integral to mathematical thinking and knowing—for novice to expert—and for exploring early mathematical concepts to more complex mathematical ideas. With movement so integral to mathematical thinking, how can we recruit movement into the mathematics classroom? What kinds of movement will enhance students’ mathematical thinking and knowing? We share some practical activities designed to support the mathematical learning of our ākonga by developing their mathematical thinking and knowing through movement.

title: Penerapan Model Experiential Learning Berbasis Culturally Responsive Teaching untuk Meningkatkan Hasil Belajar Materi Penerapan Norma
abstract: Students’ difficulties in analyzing the application of norms and determining appropriate actions indicate the need for Pancasila Education instruction that connects concepts with everyday experiences. This study aimed to improve students’ learning outcomes on the topic of applying norms through an experiential learning model based on culturally responsive teaching (CRT) that integrates the cultural context of Madura. The study employed the Kemmis and McTaggart classroom action research (CAR) design and was conducted over two cycles involving 27 students in Class V-A at UPTD SDN Kamal 2. Data were collected through tests, observation, and documentation, then analyzed using quantitative descriptive analysis based on mean scores and the percentage of students in the class achieving learning mastery. Reflection on Cycle I informed improvements to the intervention in Cycle II by shifting concrete experiences from role play to learning stations, simplifying instructions, and grouping students according to their learning readiness. The results showed an increase in the mean score from 57.04 in the pre-cycle phase to 63.70 in Cycle I and 88.89 in Cycle II. The percentage of students achieving learning mastery increased from 33.33% in the pre-cycle phase to 59.26% in Cycle I and 88.89% in Cycle II. These findings indicate that implementing CRT-based experiential learning, accompanied by…

title: Knowledge transfer and learning through global disruption: coactive vicarious learning in multinational enterprises
abstract: Purpose Global exogenous shocks disrupt established knowledge transfer routines in multinational enterprises (MNEs) and challenge assumptions about organizational learning. While prior research emphasizes learning after crises, less is known about how MNEs learn during simultaneous disruption and shared uncertainty. This study aims to examine how knowledge transfer and learning unfold during such shocks and how subsidiary managers facilitate collective learning. Design/methodology/approach Adopting an interpretivist epistemological stance, this study uses a phenomenon-driven, exploratory sequential mixed-methods design. Data were collected during the COVID-19 pandemic through a Delphi study, survey, in-depth interviews and a follow-up poll conducted one year later, from chief executive officers and managing directors of Australian subsidiaries of foreign-owned MNEs. Data were analyzed abductively, iterating between empirical patterns and theory to develop propositions and a conceptual model grounded in organizational learning and knowledge management theory. Findings Learning during global exogenous shocks is initiated through managerial interpretation rather than objective timelines. Subsidiary managers’ perceptions reconfigure the salience of units within the MNE network, prompting a search for experiential knowledge from subsidiaries perceived as having earlier exposure. Per…

title: Analysis of the Influence of the Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on Students' Critical Thinking Abilities in Learning
abstract: This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) use affects students' critical thinking skills in learning. The study uses a quantitative, explanatory research design. The study population consisted of students in the Economics Education Study Program who used AI-based applications for learning. The study collected data through a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire from 64 respondents who met the research criteria. The researchers analyzed the data using validity and reliability tests, assumption tests, and simple linear regression in SPSS. The results show that using AI has a positive and significant effect on students' critical thinking skills. The t-test yielded t = 4.670 (p = 0.000), and the regression coefficient was 0.431. The R-square value of 0.260 indicates that AI use explains 26% of the variation in students' critical thinking skills, while other factors account for the remaining 74%. These findings suggest that appropriate AI use can support students' ability to analyze, evaluate, and solve problems.

title: Corrigendum: Improving business process performance in SMEs through predictive modeling: a comparative study of statistical and machine learning models
Talking probability across languages: Translanguaging as a resource for learning
abstract: Many students in Aotearoa New Zealand mathematics classrooms routinely use more than one language in their everyday lives. However, in mathematics and statistics classrooms, these linguistic resources are often overlooked or discouraged in favour of English-only approaches. There is increasing awareness of the potential of translanguaging for enabling learners to draw upon their full linguistic repertoire during mathematical learning opportunities. However, there are currently limited specific examples of how translanguaging can be used within a secondary multilingual classroom to support learners’ conceptual understanding. This article shows how translanguaging—the flexible use of multiple languages—can support students’ understanding of probability concepts.

title: Parametric study for the sustainable optimisation of T-shaped deep cement mixing columns
abstract: The sustainable application of T-shaped deep cement mixing (DCM) columns necessitates optimisation to improve cost efficiency while maintaining structural performance. This study presented a novel column called a varied strength T-shaped DCM column. A parametric optimisation is carried out by integrating numerical modelling with performance-based assessment, considering three cases of T-shaped DCM columns, namely variations in depth-based strength and localised strength variations in the core of the head and body sections. Results show that settlement is minimally affected by lower column strength, with load-bearing capacity mainly governed by the head and upper three-fifths of the column body. Increasing body strength with depth yields a non-linear increase in bearing capacity, while deformation remains concentrated in the head and its transition area with the body. The optimised construction costs for the three columns are approximately 0.847, 0.970, and 0.933 times the normalised cost, respectively. Variation in strength within the core of the column body appears to have minimal effect on bearing capacity characteristics. However, the T-shaped DCM column with depth-based strength variation exhibits better overall performance and notably lower construction costs, surpassing other configurations. The findings will support the sustainable development of T-shaped columns by inte…

title: Improving the efficiency of helitack crew deployment through spatial optimization
abstract: Background Improving the deployment of helitack crews is crucial for limiting the growth of newly ignited wildfires. Aims We evaluated whether an optimization model could improve deployment in areas where high-intensity fires could occur compared with the current heuristic approach. Methods The model maximized coverage of areas with high potential intensity values using a fixed number of deployment sites. Model performance was compared with historical deployment for 280 days in Quebec, Canada, from 2018 to 2022. Key results The model consistently improved spatial coverage of high-intensity areas. While historical deployment captured more fire starts than the model when restricted to the agency’s 18 primary deployment sites, expanding the pool of available potential deployment sites significantly enhanced overall performance. Under this extensive scenario, combining the model with this expanded network outperformed historical deployment across all metrics, increasing the coverage of both high-intensity zones and fire ignitions. Conclusions These findings suggest that optimization models can identify strategic locations for new deployment bases and support decision-making, particularly when resources are scarce. Implications The framework enables agencies to evaluate deployment site effectiveness and better address evolving wildfire landscapes.

title: Data-driven stochastic reduced-order modelling of parametrized dynamical systems
abstract: Abstract Modelling complex dynamical systems under varying conditions is computationally intensive, often rendering high-fidelity simulations intractable. Although reduced-order models (ROMs) offer a promising solution, current methods often struggle with stochastic dynamics and fail to quantify prediction uncertainty, limiting their utility in robust decision-making contexts. To address these challenges, we introduce a data-driven framework for learning continuous-time stochastic ROMs that generalize across parameter spaces and forcing conditions. Our approach, based on amortized stochastic variational inference, leverages a reparametrization trick for Markov Gaussian processes to eliminate the need for computationally expensive forward solvers during training. This enables us to jointly learn a probabilistic autoencoder and stochastic differential equations governing the latent dynamics, at a computational cost that is independent of the dataset size and system stiffness. Additionally, our approach offers the flexibility of incorporating physics-informed priors if available. Numerical studies are presented for three challenging test problems, where we demonstrate excellent generalization to unseen parameter combinations and forcings, and significant efficiency gains compared with existing approaches.
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Science

title: A hierarchical collaborative dynamic particle swarm optimization method for triaxial magnetometer error calibration
abstract: Purpose This study aims to improve the calibration accuracy of triaxial magnetometers by developing a hierarchical collaborative dynamic particle swarm optimization (HCD-PSO) algorithm for error parameter estimation. Design/methodology/approach An HCD-PSO algorithm is proposed for triaxial magnetometer error parameter estimation and calibration. The proposed method improves the standard particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework by incorporating an adaptive parameter collaborative regulation mechanism, a low-quality particle information source reconstruction mechanism, and a dual-population competitive collaborative evolution mechanism, thereby enhancing population diversity and improving convergence performance and parameter estimation accuracy. Findings Simulation results demonstrate that HCD-PSO can achieve stable error estimation results with low calibration errors under different noise conditions. Comparative experiments further show that HCD-PSO outperforms PSO, two-Swarm learning particle Swarm optimization and Sand Cat Swarm Optimization in terms of parameter estimation accuracy and convergence efficiency. In addition, parameter sensitivity analysis confirms that the proposed algorithm maintains stable optimization performance under different parameter search range settings. Additional comparisons with two classical calibration methods, further show that HCD-PSO achiev…

title: Gaussian process inference of stochastic magneto-active dynamics and viscosity in Swift J1727.8-1613
abstract: Linking X-ray variability to the underlying magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) dynamics of black hole X-ray binaries remains challenging. We systematically investigate the stochastic and oscillatory variability of the black hole X-ray binary candidate Swift J1727.8-1613 during its 2023 outburst using Gaussian process (GP) regression applied to Insight-HXMT multi-band light curves. The variability is modelled with a physically motivated composite kernel comprising one stochastically driven damped simple harmonic oscillator (SHO) and two damped random walk (DRW) components. The SHO term robustly recovers quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) with frequencies ν_0 ∼ 0.07--5 Hz, consistent with the fundamental Alfvén mode of a contracting magnetically confined disk--coronal cavity. The quality factor rises from Q ∼ 3 to Q ∼ 10, suggesting increasing coherence of the magnetic cavity. We also find an anti-correlation between QPO frequency and the short DRW damping timescale, supporting our proposed stochastic magneto-active dynamics scenario. We associate the short and long DRW timescales with the local turbulent turnover and thermal adjustment timescales, respectively. Under this proposed interpretation, our results are consistent with an effective viscosity parameter α ∼ 0.1. Strikingly, near the jet-ejection epoch around MJD 60206, the short DRW timescale is unresolved, while the long DRW time…

title: Tuning the mechanical integrity and corrosion performance of open-cell copper foams: identification of an optimization threshold
abstract: Abstract In this work, Porous copper foam samples were fabricated by a space-holder technique with water-atomized copper powder and sodium chloride (NaCl) particles in weight fractions ranging from 10 to 35 wt%. The powders were mechanically mixed at a 10:1 ball-to-powder ratio and 150 rpm for 2 h. The effects of space-holder content on the physical, mechanical, tribological, and electrochemical performance were systematically investigated. Increasing the NaCl fraction precisely controlled the total porosity, from 39.15% to 57.76%, and reduced the bulk density from 5.452 to 3.785 g/cm³. XRD and SEM analyses confirmed a single-phase FCC copper matrix and a structural transition from isolated pores to a highly interconnected open-cell network. Consequently, Vickers hardness, compressive yield strength, energy absorption capacity decreased from 52.12 to 29.23 HV, 18.25 to 1.65 MPa, and 35.73 to 10.46 MJ/m³, respectively, following a modified Gibson–Ashby model (R 2 = 0.95). Concurrently, the coefficient of friction and specific wear rate increased (reaching a maximum of 0.73 mm³/N·m under 15 N for 35 wt% NaCl) due to strut thinning and localized delamination. Electrochemical evaluation in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution revealed an optimization threshold for sample fabricated with 25 wt% NaCl, which exhibited the lowest corrosion rate of 0.918 mm/y, and the highest polarization resistance (…

title: Developing Community Capabilities through Local Potential-Based Economic Empowerment: A Case Study of the KANERGI Program at PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Integrated Terminal Kendari
abstract: Community empowerment through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) should be assessed not only by the assistance and activities provided but also by communities’ ability to use these resources sustainably. This study analyzes community capability development through the KANERGI Program, implemented by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga Integrated Terminal Kendari, which builds on local fisheries potential in Mata Urban Village. Using a qualitative case study approach, data were collected through interviews with five administrators and members of the Permata Mitra Bersama group, observation, and documentation. The data were analyzed thematically, with the Capability Approach as the primary framework and Asset-Based Community Development as a supporting perspective. The findings show that program interventions contributed to the development of production, business management, marketing, and collective capabilities. These capabilities were manifested in independent production of fish floss and fish meatballs, financial record-keeping, and participation in marketing activities. The group’s involvement in business decisions, including setting selling prices, indicates the emergence of agency. However, the absence of a stable market shows that marketing capabilities still need strengthening. The study demonstrates that CSR-based empowerment can be understood as a process of converting resourc…

title: ABO Blood Group and Coronary Artery Disease Risk and Severity: Evidence from a Multi-Method Analytical Framework
abstract: Objective: The association between ABO blood groups and coronary artery disease (CAD) has been extensively investigated, yet findings remain inconsistent. This study aimed to evaluate this association in angiographically confirmed CAD using multiple complementary analytical approaches.Materials and Methods: This retrospective case-control study enrolled 2,470 participants, comprising 1,305 patients with angiographically confirmed CAD and 1,165 controls. The association between ABO blood groups and CAD was assessed using unadjusted logistic regression, multivariable logistic regression adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors, and propensity score matching (PSM). Subgroup analyses stratified by sex, age, and diabetes mellitus status were performed with interaction testing. Disease severity was evaluated using the Gensini score.Results: ABO blood group distribution did not differ significantly between CAD patients and controls (p=0.212). No significant association between ABO blood groups and CAD was identified in any of the three analytical approaches: univariable (overall p=0.215), multivariable (overall p=0.304), or PSM analysis (overall p=0.324). Subgroup analyses and interaction tests detected no significant effect modification by sex, age, or diabetes status. Gensini scores did not differ significantly across ABO blood groups among CAD patients (p=0.259).Conclusion: No sign…

title: Effectiveness of multi-component, dynamic begging displays as honest signals of nestling hunger
abstract: Abstract Parent–offspring communication depends on offspring signals that help parents assess need and allocate care. Nestling begging is often treated as a graded, information-rich and therefore honest signal of hunger, as predicted by costly signalling models. We quantified how effectively visual and acoustic begging components encode food deprivation in spotless starling (Sturnus unicolor) nestlings using field observations and a controlled laboratory experiment. We combined random-regression models with information-theoretic measures of uncertainty reduction and receiver-based machine-learning decoding. In wild broods, begging order and maximum postural intensity increased with deprivation time, yet posture and calling together reduced uncertainty about deprivation by less than 5%. Distinct postural levels overlapped widely among deprivation states and followed a stereotyped sequence—rapid escalation to maximum intensity followed by relaxation—yielding poor resolution of intermediate hunger. Adding components improved decoding only marginally beyond the first few cues. Parental allocation was correspondingly rapid, although display duration could provide additional information once the full bout was perceived. Discrete coding analyses confirmed that simple postural schemes were most consistent and that begging reliably distinguished only coarse, extreme hunger states. Overa…

title: Donor-aware multi-cohort single-cell analysis identifies an LXR-linked tubular cholesterol-handling state in membranous nephropathy with a coordinated five-gene lipid-remodeling signature across renal tumors
abstract: Background Membranous nephropathy (MN) is an immune-mediated glomerular disease in which sustained proteinuria exposes renal tubular epithelial cells to an abnormal filtered-protein load. The tubular metabolic response to this exposure remains incompletely characterized. We investigated whether MN is associated with a reproducible tubular cholesterol-handling transcriptional state and assessed its relationship to protein overload in vitro . We further evaluated whether an experimentally anchored five-gene subset showed a coordinated tumor-associated transcriptional shift across major renal cancer histologies. Methods Three kidney single-cell RNA-sequencing datasets and one glomerular bulk-transcriptomic cohort were analyzed using the donor as the biological replicate. GSE241302 was used for complete-case exploratory discovery, OEP004186 for formal donor-aware support, GSE171458 for directional support, and GSE200828 for tissue-level disease context. A frozen 47-gene LXR-linked cholesterol-handling program and its nested 37-gene cholesterol transport/efflux component were evaluated by donor-level pseudobulk analysis, leave-one-donor-out and leave-one-gene-out sensitivity analyses. HK-2 cells were exposed to protein overload, followed by quantitative reverse-transcription PCR for representative transport and lipid-remodeling genes. The same experimentally anchored five-gene panel…

title: Understanding how and where AI can enhance the effectiveness of PMM-mediated organisational change: a conceptual framework
abstract: Purpose To develop a social complexity-based understanding of how and where artificial intelligence (AI) and generative artificial intelligence (GAI) can enhance the effectiveness of performance measurement and management (PMM) mediated organisational change. Design/methodology/approach This article draws on a social complexity interpretation of PMM, conviction narrative theory and the AI and GAI literature, to present a conceptualisation of AI-augmented PMM-mediated organisational change that describes how and where machine-based and human-based decision-making processes can augment performance measurement systems and performance management practices. Findings AI's and GAI's inability to replicate human reflexivity and judgement in equivocal and indeterminate situations limits what these technologies can do in PMM-mediated organisational change. AI and GAI can augment decision-making processes associated with performance measurement and the execution of performance management-initiated interventions; however, creating these interventions relies on human reflexivity and judgement. Originality/value This conceptual investigation highlights the limitations of AI and GAI technologies in PMM-mediated organisational change and explains why human-based decision-making continues to play a distinctive role. It contributes to our understanding of how AI and GAI can influence organisatio…
venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management

title: Brand evangelism on social media: the role of social endorsement
abstract: Purpose Ordinary consumers can promote brands through like-based social endorsements on social media. This study aims to develop a research model to examine the influences of two types of social endorsement on consumers’ tribal and evangelistic behaviors as well as the mediating effects of two identification processes on these influences. The findings enrich the understanding of consumers’ roles as brand promoters. Design/methodology/approach An online experiment was conducted among 329 participants recruited through Amazon Mechanical Turk. Multivariate analysis of variance and variance-based structural equation modeling were used for data analysis. Findings The results indicate that social endorsement has significant direct effects on brand tribalism and evangelism. Social endorsement is a self-expressive behavior that initiates brand–self and brand–social connections. These two identification processes facilitate the establishment of brand tribalism and evangelism with varying magnitude. The findings suggest that brand tribalism drives brand evangelism, highlighting the crucial role of end users in promoting brands on social media. Practical implications This study enriches the understanding of the active role of customers and the impact of consumer–brand relationships on brand evangelism by providing insights into how social endorsement contributes to strong brand support. T…

title: Open for all, valued by few? How open branding dilutes perceived brand status
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how open (vs closed) branding – a permissive (vs restrictive) governance stance toward unauthorized consumer appropriation of brand-related intellectual property – shapes perceived brand status. It examines reference group association as the mediator and product status relevance as a boundary condition. Design/methodology/approach Five between-subjects online experiments (n = 958) tested the hypotheses. Studies 1a–3 used single-factor designs manipulating branding strategy (open vs closed branding), with Study 1a adding a no-response baseline. Study 4 used a 2 (branding strategy: open vs closed branding) × 2 (product status relevance: high vs low) design. Findings Open branding produces lower perceived brand status than closed branding. This relative status disadvantage arises because open branding weakens associations with higher-status reference groups and is stronger when product status relevance is high. Practical implications Firms should treat open branding as an intellectual property governance signal rather than a generic engagement tactic. Particularly for high-status-relevant products, managers should selectively govern participation, collaboration partners and core status-bearing symbols to preserve the brand’s desired reference group associations. Originality/value This article extends open branding research beyond its common f…

title: Do women on boards strengthen internal control to drive firm sustainability in emerging markets? Evidence from Fiji
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore whether women on boards strengthen internal control to enhance Global Reporting Initiative (GRI)-based sustainable disclosure performance (GRISP) in emerging markets. Women on boards refer to board gender diversity (BGD) or female directors Design/methodology/approach Multiple regression, instrumental variable and system Generalized Method of Moments methods, along with bootstrapping and Propensity Score Matching, were used to analyze a sample of Fijian listed entities. Findings Female board representation is positively associated with internal control and GRISP, as it strengthens governance mechanisms that translate inclusive leadership into improved outcomes. Originality/value This study examines the role of internal control in linking female board representation to GRISP within a New Institutional Economics (NIE) framework.
venue: Gender in Management: An International Journal

title: Leading Digital Transformation in Salaf Islamic Education: Negotiating Technology and Tradition
abstract: Digital transformation in Salafi Islamic education presents leadership challenges, as the use of technology must be aligned with the traditions and institutional identity of the pesantren. This study aims to analyse how leaders navigate digital transformation within the context of Salafi Islamic education. The research employs a qualitative approach using a case study design at the Al-Anshoriyah Islamic Boarding School. Data were collected through interviews with three key informants the pesantren director, the chair of the board of trustees, and the headteacher as well as through observation and documentation. The data were analysed thematically by comparing information from the three data collection methods. The research findings identified three interrelated leadership practices: the selective adoption of technology, the gradual management of organisational change, and the negotiation between the utilisation of technology and the continuity of Salaf traditions. Key findings indicate that the continuity of traditional practices does not necessarily signify resistance to digitalisation, but can form part of leadership considerations in determining the scope of technological change. This study offers a perspective on ‘tradition-sensitive digital leadership’, which emphasises the role of leaders in aligning the use of technology with the identity and educational commitments of I…
venue: At Tadbir: Islamic Education Management Journal

title: Food, Dietary Supplement, and Gut Microbiome Interactions in Oral Anticancer Therapy: Mechanisms, Clinical Consequences, and Management
abstract: Background: The shift toward oral targeted therapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in oncology has introduced pharmacokinetic variability driven by food–drug interactions (FDIs), which can cause therapeutic failure or increased toxicity. Areas of Uncertainty: FDI effects depend on drug composition and food-intake timing. Evidence for traditional antineoplastic drugs is well documented, but data on newer targeted therapies and on diet-mediated or microbiome-mediated modulation of ICI efficacy remain inconsistent—dietary fiber and probiotic supplementation, for example, appear associated with divergent clinical outcomes. The role of high-dose antioxidant supplementation during cytotoxic therapy also requires further study. Data Sources: A structured search of Web of Science, PubMed, and Embase (through July 2026) informed this narrative review of pharmacokinetic mechanisms, clinical outcomes, and management strategies for the concomitant use of food, dietary supplements, and antineoplastic drugs. Results: Food can alter oral antineoplastic drug bioavailability through changes in gastric pH, cytochrome P450 (CYP) modulation, and efflux-transporter inhibition (eg, P-glycoprotein). High-fat meals increase exposure to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) such as lapatinib and abiraterone, while newer agents (sotorasib and lorlatinib) show different food-interaction profiles. I…

title: A HYBRID VAE-HUFFMAN GENERATIVE COMPRESSION FRAMEWORK FOR IMAGE TRANSMISSION IN WIRELESS SENSOR NETWORKS
abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid image compression framework that integrates a tunable β-Variational Autoencoder (β-VAE) with Huffman entropy coding to achieve efficient, low-complexity compression suitable for wireless sensor networks (WSNs) and resource-constrained embedded systems. The model jointly optimizes latent representations and entropy-aware symbol distributions, improving both rate-distortion performance and theoretical coding efficiency. Trained on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet and evaluated on the Kodak dataset, the approach attains over 32 dB PSNR and SSIM above 0.90, and an average compression ratio of 18.22:1. When compared with the JPEG standard, the proposed method provides comparable perceptual quality while enabling deterministic, lightweight decoding that substantially reduces computational and energy demands. The results demonstrate that combining generative latent representation modeling with classical entropy coding offers a scalable, hardware-friendly alternative for next-generation learned image compression systems.
venue: Suranaree Journal of Science and Technology

title: From General-Purpose Large Language Models to Domain-Specific Financial Models: A Structured Review and Comparative Case Analysis
abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) in finance has expanded rapidly, yet general-purpose systems face recurring problems in high-risk and regulated applications: Unsupported factual generation, weak reasoning across text, tables, charts, and numerical data, and limited traceability of model-assisted decisions. This study conducts a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta Analyses (PRISMA)-informed structured review of 67 studies, principally published between January 2020 and March 2026, with three foundational pre-2020 studies retained through backward citation tracking. It develops a qualitative analytical and diagnostic framework with three pathways: Specialized knowledge modeling, task-constrained multimodal reasoning, and Trust-by-Design. A study-level evidence map and an explicit coding protocol show how the pathways were derived. The framework is used to compare BloombergGPT, FinGPT, FinTral, Fin-o1, Fin-R1, and Agentar-Fin-R1 through common criteria for knowledge controls, modality handling, lifecycle governance, evidence quality, and deployment maturity. The case analysis distinguishes model-paper design descriptions, developer reported benchmark results, platform-level deployment reports, and prospective applications. The analysis indicates that financial LLMs differ materially in how they organize domain knowledge, coordinate heterogeneous input…

title: Design, Finite Element Analysis, and Experimental Investigation of Basalt Fiber Reinforced Polymer (BFRP) Composite for Oil and Gas Applications
abstract: The pipelines used for transporting oil and gas need to have sufficient strength, durability, and resistance to any form of corrosion. The usual metallic pipes are prone to corrosion and weigh quite a lot. In this research, the use of Basalt Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composite Pipe has been studied using computer aided design and finite element analysis among others. A BFRP pipe with 200 mm length, 50 mm inner diameter, and 10 mm wall thickness was modeled using orthotropic material property assumptions and studied under an internal pressure of 55 MPa. The maximum equivalent stress predicted through FEA was 210 MPa and the maximum displacement was 0.45 mm. The hardness obtained from the experimental test was 84.2 HRB, axial compressive strength was 178 MPa, and lateral performance stability was noted up to 12 kN. There was an approximate difference of 3.8% between the experimental and simulation axial compressive strengths of 185 MPa. The results indicate that there is potential for BFRP material to be used as a light and corrosion-resistant material for pipeline structures.

title: The 2026 Reform of adult guardianship in Japan – an assessment from the perspective of self-determination
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the 2026 Reform of Japan’s adult guardianship system and evaluate it from the perspective of self-determination and Article 12 of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD). Design/methodology/approach This study analyzes the background to the 2026 Reform, outlines its principal features and assesses its implications through doctrinal analysis of the amended legislation, legislative materials and relevant CRPD standards. Findings The reform introduces the principle of necessity, places greater emphasis on the individual’s will and preferences and increases flexibility within the adult guardianship system. However, the continued reliance on powers of consent and rescission indicates that substitute decision-making remains a central feature of the Japanese system. Research limitations/implications As the reform has not yet entered into force, the analysis is limited to the legislative framework. Future research will be required to evaluate how the new provisions are interpreted and implemented in practice. Practical implications The reform requires family courts, assistants and other professionals to place greater emphasis on the ascertainment of the individual’s will and preferences. The practical effectiveness of the reform will depend on how these actors implement the new statutory duties in practice. Social implications…

title: JAK-STAT pathway heterogeneity governs immunotherapy response in breast cancer
abstract: The JAK-STAT pathway (JSP) is a well-known oncogenic cascade; however, recent clinical trials have detected JSP upregulation in breast cancer following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. This paradoxical observation warrants further investigation into JSP’s intercellular heterogeneity, tumor dynamics, molecular mechanisms, and clinical implications for immunotherapy. JSP expression showed dynamic shifts during breast cancer progression, with higher levels in T cells and paracancerous epithelial cells. In human breast cancer tumor cells, elevated JSP is highly correlated with malignant phenotypes. JSP-high tumor cells overexpressed oncogenic pathways, while exhibiting increased immunosuppressive signaling via the MIF-CD74 signaling axis. In T cells, higher JSP levels were associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved differentiation, and reduced exhaustion, reflecting robust anti-tumor immunity. Analysis of immunotherapy datasets revealed that higher JSP levels were associated with improved responses toward PD-1 inhibitors, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients, with JSP serving as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy sensitivity. As a key JSP component, STAT4 exerts dual roles in breast cancer: it drives tumorigenesis in malignant cells, sustains breast epithelial cell proliferation, and bolsters T-cell anti-tumor functionality, while also acting as a …

title: Hypotension Prediction Index versus Mean Arterial Pressure Alarm for Preventing Intraoperative Hypotension in Elective Noncardiac Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial
abstract: Background: Intraoperative hypotension is common during surgery and has been retrospectively associated with acute kidney injury, myocardial injury, and increased mortality. The Hypotension Prediction Index was developed to support proactive blood pressure management but shows a strong correlation with mean arterial pressure. Observational data suggest that a mean arterial pressure alarm set at 72 mmHg may perform similarly to the default Hypotension Prediction Index alarm (greater than 85). The authors hypothesized that a 72 mmHg mean arterial pressure alarm is noninferior to the Hypotension Prediction Index in preventing intraoperative hypotension. Methods: In this single-center, blinded, randomized controlled trial, adults undergoing moderate- or high-risk elective noncardiac surgery with continuous arterial pressure monitoring were assigned to either a mean arterial pressure alarm (less than 72 mmHg) or a Hypotension Prediction Index alarm (greater than 85). The primary outcome was the area under the threshold for mean arterial pressure less than 65 mmHg. Secondary outcomes included the incidence and severity of hypo- and hypertension, duration of active alarms, incidence of acute kidney and myocardial injury, 30-day mortality, hospital length of stay, and cumulative dosages of vasoactive medication and fluids. Results: A total of 143 participants were included in the final…

title: DksA-dependent stringent stress response drives virulence and gastrointestinal persistence of Klebsiella pneumoniae
abstract: ABSTRACT Successful gastrointestinal (GI) colonization by bacterial pathogens requires adaptation to nutrient competition and host-derived stresses in the gut, with adaptation via the bacterial stringent stress response playing a critical role. Epidemiological data suggest that the GI tract serves as a reservoir from which K. pneumoniae can spread and cause invasive disease or transmit to another host. DksA is a conserved stringent response transcriptional regulator that was identified in an in vivo transposon mutagenesis screen as an important K. pneumoniae gut determinant. However, its role in K. pneumoniae pathogenesis and gut colonization remain uncharacterized. Here, we demonstrate that DksA is required for survival against membrane-targeting antibiotics, consistent with a role in cell envelope stress tolerance. In addition, DksA positively influences capsule biosynthesis gene expression and hypermucoviscosity, and is essential for robust biofilm formation. Using a murine model, we establish that DksA functions as a determinant of GI colonization, despite disruption of the resident gut microbiota. Furthermore, we demonstrate that DksA is important for environmental survival and transmission by regulating RpoS, thereby providing a mechanistic link between the stringent stress response, environmental survival, and subsequent transmission. Together, these findings establish D…

title: Farmers market as public quick commerce infrastructure: a conceptual policy framework for digital transformation
abstract: The rapid digitalization of food retail through private quick commerce platforms has transformed urban food consumption patterns in India. Despite the investments in digital infrastructure, Uzhavar Sandhai (Farmers Market), a farmer-to-consumer direct marketing system in Tamil Nadu, is still limited to traditional physical markets. This study suggests a strategic rethinking of Farmers Market as a public quick commerce infrastructure layer, incorporating digital marketplaces, hyperlocal logistics and cooperative governance to boost farmer market competitiveness and promote public value, food system resilience and equitable digital market access. In this study, the Farmers Market Digital Platform model is developed by applying the conceptual policy design approach to convert the Farmers Market platform into a decentralized public quick commerce network. This study identifies the institutional, technological and governance reforms necessary to support the digital transformation of farmer markets using publicly governed digital infrastructure. This reorientation of Farmers Market to public digital infrastructure could form the policy roadmap for platformization of agriculture in Tamil Nadu, which would benefit small farmers, urban consumers, and municipalities and help alleviate inefficiencies in supply chains. As a conceptual policy framework, the proposed model has not been empir…

title: Competition and Challenges Facing Lululemon in the Chinese Market
abstract: In the era of emotional consumption, emotions have become an important bond for brands to establish deep connections with consumers and a key factor driving consumer decisions. Lululemon is a successful model constructed with the core emotional prototypes of "self-care" and "community belonging". Enter the female yoga market and continuously deepen the cultivation of female sports consumption. While maintaining a caring, genuine and inclusive brand image, it also targets the physical experience, identity recognition and emotional needs of female consumers, constantly innovating and reforming in aspects such as product design, brand ambassador selection, advertising communication, community activities and consumer experience. This article takes Lululemon as an example to explore its brand emotional construction strategies, which include establishing emotional connections through products, building emotional identification through communities, and establishing emotional trust through experiences. Analyze the possible impact of product issues, brand expansion, and market competition on consumer sentiment, and provide references and reflections for other brands.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Effect of Market Capitalization and Company Size on Stock Returns at PT Sariguna Primatirta Tbk 2017–2025
abstract: This study examines the relationship of Market Capitalization and Company Size with Stock Returns at PT Sariguna Primatirta Tbk during 2017–2025. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data from annual financial reports and historical stock prices. The data comprised nine annual observations and were analyzed using multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics 25. The results indicate that neither Market Capitalization nor Company Size is a statistically significant predictor of Stock Returns individually or jointly within the research model. The (R^2) value of 0.008 indicates that the model explains 0.8% of the variation in Stock Returns. These findings should be interpreted cautiously because the study is limited to nine annual observations from a single company, which restricts the generalizability of the results. Future research could include more companies, longer observation periods, and additional variables

title: Geopolitical conflict, global uncertainty and equity market resilience in the MENA region: evidence from a quantile machine-learning framework
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examines how global uncertainty and domestic geopolitical conflict affect equity market resilience in six Middle East and North Africa (MENA) economies across stress, normal and expansion regimes. Design/methodology/approach Using monthly MSCI country-index series with country-specific starting dates between 2010 and 2016 and observations through 2025, the study constructs a Geopolitical Fatal Conflict Index (GFCI) from ACLED violent events and fatalities. The GFCI is combined with the Geopolitical Risk Index (GPR), the Financial Stress Index (FSI) and the Volatility Index (VIX) in a Quantile Gradient Boosting (QGB) framework. SHAP values are used to compare the relative contribution and direction of these predictors at Q10, Q50 and Q90. Findings The results are heterogeneous across countries and quantiles rather than following a single regional pattern. At Q10, global indicators lead the SHAP ranking in Egypt, Morocco and Tunisia, whereas GFCI is the leading predictor in Jordan, Palestine and Saudi Arabia. At Q50 and Q90, GFCI remains or becomes prominent in Egypt, Palestine and Saudi Arabia, while VIX or FSI remain important in Jordan, Morocco and Tunisia. In the reported Q50 robustness comparison, including GFCI reduces MAE and RMSE and increases R² in all six markets. Practical implications The findings support country- and quantile-specific monit…
venue: International Journal of Islamic and Middle Eastern Finance and Management

title: Synergizing electricity decarbonization and substitution to achieve clean electrification: a dynamic CGE model
The Mediating Role of Emotional Intelligence Between Investor Behavior and Welfare: Indonesian Cryptocurrency Market Evidence
abstract: Background: Indonesia’s cryptocurrency market has expanded rapidly, exposing a growing retail-investor population to high volatility, overconfidence, herding, and uneven financial capability. Objective: This study examines the relationships of overconfidence, herding behavior, risk perception, financial literacy, and investment experience with investor welfare, and tests emotional intelligence as the mechanism connecting these factors to welfare. Its novelty lies in positioning emotional intelligence as a mediator between behavioral and capability-based antecedents and an ultimate welfare outcome in Indonesia’s cryptocurrency context. Methods: A cross-sectional explanatory survey obtained 449 valid responses from Indonesian cryptocurrency investors selected through purposive sampling. The model was estimated using prediction-oriented PLS-SEM in SmartPLS 4.0.0.9 because it contains multiple latent constructs, direct paths, and mediation paths and does not require multivariate normality. Results: Overconfidence and herding behavior were negatively associated with investor welfare, whereas risk perception, financial literacy, investment experience, and emotional intelligence were positively associated with welfare. Emotional intelligence partially mediated all five antecedent–welfare relationships. Financial literacy showed the strongest association with emotional intelligence (β …

title: Application of the Differential and Lagrange Mean Theorems to the Existence of Market Equilibrium and Consumption Stratification
abstract: The accumulation of household consumption data in the data economy provides a foundation for studying consumption differences. Traditional economics mostly relies on qualitative analysis, with insufficient mathematical deduction, making it difficult to depict consumer stratification and market equilibrium. This article is based on the Lagrange mean theorem and differentiation as tools, combined with consumption statistics data to explore the conditions for market equilibrium and the characteristics of consumer stratification among residents. By using differentiation to reflect the instantaneous changes of economic variables, the Lagrange mean theorem is applied to analyze the average variation law of indicators within the interval. Empirical analysis is carried out using official Consumer Price Index (CPI), agricultural wholesale price and household income expenditure panel data from Chinese statistical authorities. Studies show that, by combining two mathematical tools, the income threshold for consumption stratification can be determined, verifying that market equilibrium still holds in some non-traditional scenarios. This study applies mathematical theory to economic reality, providing mathematical references for consumer trend analysis and related economic decision-making.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Global tanker shipping market under geopolitical shifts: current situation, transmission mechanisms and development trends
abstract: Purpose Against the backdrop of eastward shift of global refining capacity, tightening environmental regulations and shipping cyclical fluctuations, geopolitical conflicts have become the key exogenous shock reshaping tanker shipping market fundamentals. This paper aims to reveal the inner transmission logic of geopolitical shocks on global tanker market, identify long-run structural market trends, and propose adaptive strategic principles for industrial stakeholders. Design/methodology/approach Based on systems theory and maritime economics, this paper constructs an Situation-Mechanism-Trend (SMT) analytical framework for geopolitical shocks. A mixed-method approach is adopted, including systematic literature coding, event-driven comparative case analysis and descriptive statistical verification using datasets from Clarkson, IEA and Baltic Exchange. Findings Five parallel and mutually reinforcing transmission mechanisms of geopolitical shocks are identified: the trade restructuring effect, shipping lane disruption effect, operating cost escalation effect, geopolitical policy compliance constraint effect, and market expectation volatility effect. Six major structural market trends are verified: regionalized trade patterns, long-distance-oriented shipping routes, structurally differentiated tanker capacity, high-volatility freight pricing, green-oriented fleet upgrading, and dig…

title: Competition law and sustainable market design: regulating dominant positions to preserve competitive viability in India's telecom and aviation sectors
abstract: Purpose This study critically evaluates existing legislations to examine its scope and limitations regarding the sustainability of market design (MD) and effective regulation of abuse of dominant position (ADP) to protect consumer sovereignty in India. It aims to identify principal factors causing gradual shrinkage of the Indian telecommunications and aviation sectors and to examine the role of concerned market regulators from legal and policy design perspectives to identify mechanisms adopted to keep competitiveness viable which is a quid pro quo for economic development and consumer-welfare. The methodology is doctrinal, qualitative and analytical. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a doctrinal legal research design employing qualitative analysis through the interpretation of provisions, regulatory instruments, judicial decisions, official market studies, policy documents and authoritative secondary literature and therefore does not seek to establish statistically validated causal relationships between regulatory intervention and market concentration. The qualitative nature of the study lies in the interpretative examination of legal and institutional frameworks rather than empirical qualitative methods such as interviews, surveys or thematic coding. Therefore, the original contribution is analytical and inferential. Findings consequently identify patterns, regulat…

title: Hyperlocal Branding Strategy of Oil Products in Facing Market Competition After the National Cooking Oil Crisis
abstract: Adequate water depth is a critical factor in ensuring safe and efficient ship docking and undocking operations at shipyards. Effective dredging management is essential for maintaining operational reliability, preventing service disruptions, and optimizing shipyard performance. This study aimed to analyze the role of dredging management in supporting ship docking and undocking operations at PT Indonesia Marina Shipyard Gresik. A descriptive qualitative research approach was employed, with data collected through observations, interviews, and document analysis. The findings revealed that dredging management at PT Indonesia Marina Shipyard Gresik had not been implemented effectively due to several constraints, particularly high dredging costs and the company's limited financial capacity, which restricted the allocation of funds for routine dredging operations. Furthermore, the implementation of the four management functions—Planning, Organizing, Actuating, and Controlling (POAC)—remained suboptimal, adversely affecting the planning, coordination, execution, and monitoring of dredging activities. Consequently, inadequate dredging management disrupted ship docking and undocking operations by limiting the number of vessels that could access the shipyard and increasing docking delays. These operational constraints negatively affected service efficiency, shipyard productivity, and compa…

title: Stock Market Prediction Using A 3-ML Fusion Approach
abstract: Stock market prediction is still a significant challenge due to the non-linearity, dynamism, and volatility of the financial time series. Accurate stroke price prediction plays a major role in investment decisions, risk management, and financial planning. This research presents a novel 3-ML framework, which uses a combination of the Random Forest, Decision Tree and XGBoost Regression models to predict the next day's closing price of NIFTY-50 index. Moreover, a Random Forest (RF) classifier is used to classify market trends such as UP, DOWN or NEUTRAL, improving the decision-making process. Data from the market is preprocessed and enhanced by feature engineering through the use of technical indicators like moving averages and daily returns. The proposed framework implements a form of a Flask-based web application along with a MySQL database. It has been experimentally evaluated and shown that the framework developed has an accuracy of 97.7% and better stability of prediction and lower forecasting errors.

title: The impact of digital investment on AGVC resilience-with a discussion on the moderating role of domestic market size
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to examine the impact of digital investment on Agricultural Global Value Chain (AGVC) resilience and investigate whether this effect varies with domestic market size. Design/methodology/approach Using country-industry-year fixed effects with nine-year panel data from the University of International Business and Economics Global Value Chain Database and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development Inter-Country Input-Output Tables, this study investigates the relationship between digital investment and AGVC resilience, analyzing heterogeneity by digital investment type, processing segment, and digital investment source. A triple interaction term-combining domestic market size, digital investment, and value chain downstreamness-is introduced to capture the interdependence of these determinants. Findings This study finds that digital investment strengthens AGVC resilience through improved institutional environments and optimized resource allocation, with labor substitution serving as a key mechanism-particularly in high-income economies. Market scale amplifies this via reverse-pull and agglomeration effects. Gains are strongest in deep-processing sectors and domestic-digital-driven chains but absent in primary processing. Foreign digital reliance offers no benefit and may weaken resilience. The positive interaction between digital inp…

title: Financial Shared Services at SAIC Motor: Market Response and Outcomes
abstract: Under the background of digital transformation of enterprises, the financial sharing center has gradually transformed from accounting reimbursement center to data value creation center, and the construction of financial sharing architecture of large diversified groups has become a hot spot in practice. This paper takes SAIC as a research case to explore the market performance and implementation effect of the financial sharing model of automobile manufacturing diversification group. It is found that SAIC has achieved results in reducing operating costs, strengthening capital risk management and promoting the integration of industry and finance by adopting the differentiated path of building financial sharing centers in different sectors, but at the same time, there are practical pain points such as non-uniform standards, insufficient cross-departmental coordination, redundant approval process and difficult personnel transformation. This study enriches the case study of financial sharing of automobile diversification groups and provides practical reference for similar large-scale automobile enterprises to optimize the construction of financial sharing and release the value of digital financial management.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Rising demand, robust triage? Service evaluation of the triage process in a young-onset dementia service
abstract: Aims and method To evaluate referrals to our local Young Onset Dementia Assessment Service (YODAS), analyse referral trends and re-referral patterns between 2020 and 2024, and review reasons for non-acceptance of referrals at triage. A retrospective review of electronic referral records was undertaken using descriptive analysis. Results Referrals to YODAS almost doubled over the study period, while non-acceptance rates remained relatively stable, rising from 52.6% in 2020 to 57.3% in 2024. Among 760 patients whose referrals were not accepted, the most common reasons for non-acceptance were: absence of features suggestive of neurodegeneration, cognitive symptoms better explained by mental health conditions, and insufficient referral information. Over one-quarter were re-referred, with two-thirds subsequently accepted. Only 6% of individuals whose referrals were initially not accepted later received a dementia diagnosis, indicating effective triage. Clinical implications A rise in the demand for dementia assessment from a younger patient population requires a careful triage to ensure the individuals with possible features of neurodegeneration are appropriately assessed, and cases where alternative explanations are more likely are directed to more appropriate pathways.

title: Evaluation of the Laboratory Leadership Service Leadership Curriculum and Leadership Assessment, 2025
abstract: ABSTRACT Context: Training laboratory professionals as public health leaders is essential for building resilient public health systems. Public health leadership training is complex and requires intentional investment in developing soft skills (eg, communications, emotional intelligence, building trust). Program: The US Center for Disease Control and Prevention's Laboratory Leadership Service (LLS) fellowship program trains laboratory professionals to be future public health leaders. In 2022, LLS implemented an enhanced leadership curriculum designed to empower LLS officers to take ownership of their roles and effectively apply leadership skills to expand their professional development and the performance of their teams. Implementation: LLS's enhanced leadership curriculum includes didactic leadership training, senior leader panels, peer-to-peer leadership activities, and personalized coaching regarding individual leadership action plans targeting specific growth areas within defined competencies. Officers complete pre- and postprogram assessments to reflect on and monitor leadership development progress. Assessment: We analyzed qualitative feedback from LLS officers, self-reported officer assessment data, and supervisor evaluations of officers' leadership-related attitudes and behaviors. We assessed possible effects of the enhanced leadership curriculum on officer leadership-re…
venue: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice

title: Between Clicks and Careers: Institutional Decoupling in Indonesia’s Digital Civil Service Performance Management
abstract: Background: Indonesia’s expansion of e-Kinerja has made civil-service performance records more visible and portable across a national digital architecture. Platform use remains an incomplete indicator of reform because recorded activities may not be interpreted through dialogue or translated into development, talent management, career mobility, recognition, and sanctions. Objective: This study examines how formal digital performance-management requirements become separated from performance dialogue and strategic HR consequences across documented Indonesian public organizations. It also identifies institutional mechanisms that may enable their recoupling. Methods: The study employed qualitative comparative document analysis. Purposive criterion sampling retained 15 documents from 20 candidates: three regulatory or technical instruments, five official publications, and seven peer-reviewed empirical studies representing seven central and subnational contexts. Twenty-seven evidence units were analyzed through hybrid deductive–inductive thematic analysis, cross-case comparison, and negative-case testing. Results: Three patterns emerged: digital visibility without substantive accountability; the supervisor as the system’s hidden interpretive architecture; and fragmented movement of appraisal information into strategic HR consequences. Problematic cases documented retrospective or acc…

title: Evaluating Contributions and Career Outcomes of Recent CDC Epidemic Intelligence Service Alumni Using a Cross-Sectional Survey
abstract: ABSTRACT Context: Well-trained epidemiologists are a vital part of the nation's public health workforce, supporting preparedness and response to health threats at home and abroad. Program: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC's) Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) is a 2-year fellowship that trains clinicians and scientists in applied epidemiology. Postfellowship, we expect EIS alumni to join the public health workforce and serve as leaders in public health and epidemiology. Implementation: In 2023, we conducted a survey among EIS alumni to understand the postfellowship positions that alumni hold 1, 3, and 5 years after the fellowship. The alumni survey included questions about type of work, career advancement, and leadership responsibilities of alumni. Evaluation: Among the 200 alumni in the three surveyed classes, 78% completed or partially completed the survey (156/200). Among those who responded, 98% (153/156) reported being employed full-time or being employed and furthering their education simultaneously. Ninety-three percent of employed respondents (143/153) were primarily working in public health. Among employed alumni, 69% (106/153) were working in the US federal government, such as CDC, and 13% (20/153) were working at a US state, tribal, local, or territorial health agency. Most often, alumni working in public health described their current work a…
venue: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice

title: Ka Ora Telecare, a national after-hours telehealth service for rural Aotearoa New Zealand: a descriptive cross-sectional evaluation with particular attention to equity of access and outcomes
abstract: Introduction Rural communities in Aotearoa New Zealand have reduced access to primary care, particularly after hours, with greater impact on Māori, Pacific peoples and those in areas of higher deprivation. Ka Ora Telecare is a national after-hours telehealth service established to address these gaps without replacing local services. Aim This study aims to describe service use and clinical outcomes for Ka Ora, with attention to rurality, ethnicity and socioeconomic position. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive evaluation of routinely collected, de-identified, aggregated service data, with the consultation as the unit of analysis, was performed. Variables were ethnicity (prioritised), age band, Community Services Card status, deprivation quintile, rurality by the Geographical Classification for Health (GCH), provider type and clinical outcome. Analysis was descriptive. Results Across the 24 month study period, 69,337 consultations carried a valid GCH code: 63.1% in R1 (rural, close to an urban centre), 27.1% in R2 and 5.6% in R3. Māori representation fell from 22.5% in R1 to 16.8% in R3, and Pacific from 3.8% to 1.1%. Of 16,369 clinician-led consultations, 88% were resolved or partially resolved via telehealth and 8% required same-day escalation. Outcomes were similar across ethnic groups, and Māori and Pacific use was concentrated in higher deprivation quintiles. Discussion Ka…

title: Enhancing pre-service teachers' GenAI literacy and teaching self-efficacy through teacher-guided GenAI use: a quasi-experimental study
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into teacher education, requiring pre-service teachers to develop GenAI literacy and teaching confidence in its pedagogical use. This study examined whether teacher-guided GenAI use was associated with higher posttest GenAI literacy and Teaching Self-efficacy than self-directed use and traditional instruction after accounting for pretest scores. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design involved 102 pre-service teachers at a Chinese teacher education college. Data came from a GenAI literacy test, a Teaching Self-efficacy scale, and semi-structured interviews. ANCOVA showed significant overall effects of instructional condition on both outcomes after controlling for pretest scores (partial η 2 = 0.17 and 0.08) No significant differences emerged between the self-directed and traditional groups. Interviews highlighted prompt design, output evaluation, and teaching-related confidence. By combining a test-based literacy measure with a three-group comparison, this study provides preliminary quantitative evidence relevant to distinguishing structured teacher guidance from GenAI tool access alone.

title: Medical cannabis for the treatment of insomnia
From the world of action to the world of words: reflections on transitioning from military service to mental healthcare
abstract: Purpose The transition from active military service to employment within mental healthcare remains an underexplored area of research. This article aims to describe the lived experience of a former British Army serviceman who transitioned into a career in mental health and to identify both the challenges and opportunities associated with this career change. Design/methodology/approach A reflective approach was adopted, drawing on the first author’s experiences of leaving military service, engaging in higher education and progressing into mental healthcare. Key stages of educational and professional development were examined to identify themes relating to adjustment, identity, support and the transferability of skills. Personal reflections were used to explore the subjective experience of adapting to a new professional culture and role. Findings The transition involved a range of challenges, including adapting to unfamiliar social and professional dynamics, managing changes in identity and navigating educational and occupational systems that differed substantially from military environments. However, military experience provided several advantages that facilitated adjustment. These included confidence in high-pressure situations, resilience, professionalism, strong communication and presentation skills and high standards of organisation and timekeeping. These attributes were perc…

title: Retrospective Evaluation of Contributions From CDC's Epidemic Intelligence Service Graduates to the US Public Health Workforce—2011–2024
abstract: ABSTRACT Context: Preparedness and response to emerging public health threats requires a well-trained workforce in epidemiology. Program: Established in 1951, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC's) Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) is a 2-year, competency-based fellowship in applied epidemiology. We sought to more fully understand and describe recent graduates' contributions to the public health workforce in the United States. Implementation: We conducted annual exit surveys among EIS officers ≤30 days before fellowship completion, collecting data regarding graduates' initial post-EIS employment. We defined US public health workforce positions as those at CDC, another Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) agency, or a US state, tribal, local, or territorial health agency. Evaluation: During 2011–2024, 1056 EIS officers completed the fellowship, and 908 (86%) reported post-EIS positions. Among these, 744 (82%) reported post-EIS positions in the US public health workforce. The positions included 662 (73%) positions or additional training at CDC, 64 (7%) at a state, tribal, local, or territorial health agency, and 18 (2%) at other HHS agencies. The remaining 164 (18%) reported positions with other employers, including non-HHS government agencies, clinical settings, academia, and training or educational programs. Postfellowship positions were stratifi…
venue: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice

title: Reliable service function chaining for satellite edge networks via transformer-based primary-backup deployment
Design Research on an AI-Assisted Everyday Food Therapy Service System: A Case Study of the "Food Rhythm" Digital Food Therapy 4S Store
abstract: This study addresses three problems in everyday food therapy services: insufficient explanation of recommendations, weak continuity between digital advice and offline fulfilment, and unclear boundaries of AI assistance. Taking the "Food Rhythm" Digital Food Therapy 4S Store as a design case, this research adopts a research-through-design approach that combines literature review, competitor analysis, semi-structured interviews, and service system design. The proposed system connects low-burden need expression, explainable AI recommendation, physical constraint-card interaction, offline ingredient display, open preparation, and feedback. Its core design logic is to treat AI not as a medical decision-maker, but as an auxiliary service capability that helps users understand, adjust, verify, and continue everyday food-therapy suggestions. By coordinating the mobile app, interaction terminal, physical cards, store environment, and backstage support, the design translates algorithmic output into an inspectable service journey. The study contributes a service-system framework for applying AI to daily health-related services while maintaining transparency, user control, and non-medical safety boundaries.

title: Sexual Health Service Use Among High School Students Accessing School-Based Versus Non–School-Based Sites in a Health Center System
abstract: ABSTRACT Objectives: To preliminarily compare health care utilization, sexual behaviors, and sexual health outcomes among high school students accessing school-based health centers (SBHCs) vs. non-SBHCs and develop an initial hypothesis on the potential impact of SBHCs. Design: Retrospective chart review. Setting: Three SBHC locations and 5 non-SBHCs locations within an adolescent and young adult health center system in Houston, Texas. Participants: Random sample of 189 high school students receiving care between August 2022 and May 2023 at a SBHC (n = 129) or non-SBHCs (n = 60). Main Outcome Measure: Demographic characteristics, health center utilization patterns, sexual behaviors, and sexual health outcomes, including sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing and results. Results: Students accessing SBHCs were more likely to be male (35.9% vs. 21.7%, P = .03) and Spanish-speaking (24.8% vs. 8.3%, P = .01) compared with students accessing non-SBHCs. Students accessing SBHCs also tended to be uninsured at higher rates (70.3% vs. 54.7%, P = .06), although the difference was not statistically significant. SBHC users were less likely to report having a primary care provider (22.5% vs. 41.7%, P = .01) or being sexually active (30.2% vs. 60.0%, P < .001). No significant differences were observed in STI testing rates or STI outcomes between groups. Conclusions: These preliminary d…
venue: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice

title: Suicide in South Wales: comprehensive review of suicides reported to the South Wales Central Coroner’s Service, 2016–2023
abstract: Aims and method An analysis of coronial inquest data provides contextual information rarely available in routine surveillance systems, including a nuanced understanding of proximal circumstances preceding death of value to mental health services. Inquest records of more than 750 suicides occurring within the South Wales Central Coroner’s jurisdiction between 2016 and 2023 were reviewed, including the COVID-19 pandemic years, to assess the effects of lockdown and social isolation. Detailed information was extracted, including medical records, toxicology, police reports, witness statements and suicide notes.
