Results Several patterns emerged relating to age, gender, method of death, trigger factors, local authority area, and engagement with mental health services. Hanging was the predominant method, particularly among men. Depression was the most common trigger factor, followed by relationship problems, alcohol/drug misuse, health concerns, psychotic illness and bereavement. Clinical implications Key structural and psychosocial risk factors identified highlighted the need for tailored, context-specific suicide-prevention strategies, with circumstances preceding suicide integrated into public health planning.

title: Reported infant safety information and perinatal service engagement among birth partners and co-parents. An exploratory cross-sectional survey at a large UK teaching hospital
abstract: Background Infant mortality in the United Kingdom is higher in areas of socioeconomic deprivation and within several minority ethnic groups. Preventive strategies rely in part on safety information reaching families during the perinatal period. The extent to which birth partners and co-parents report exposure to that information is not well characterised. Objective To describe self-reported exposure to selected infant safety topics and reported engagement with perinatal services among birth partners and co-parents attending one large UK teaching hospital, and to explore variation across respondent profiles defined by ethnicity and parity. Methods An exploratory cross-sectional survey of 73 birth partners and co-parents was conducted at University Hospitals Leicester NHS Trust between October 2022 and July 2023. Eight self-reported knowledge or awareness items and six self-reported engagement items were collected. Item-level proportions were summarised with Wilson 95 percent confidence intervals. Group comparisons used Fisher's exact test with Haldane-corrected prevalence ratios and Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment applied separately within each demographic comparison. Composite Knowledge Proportion Scores and Engagement Proportion Scores were computed for respondents with at least half of the relevant items answered. Internal consistency was estimated with the Kuder-Richardson 20 …

title: The collaborative economy from a service-dominant logic lens: a conceptual typology
abstract: Purpose Despite the rise of collaborative, peer-based exchanges that have reshaped service provision, there remains a need for research that (1) accounts for the complexity of collaborative service systems, (2) explicates submarkets and exchange behaviors, (3) addresses theoretical underpinnings and (4) proposes future research directions. This article addresses these gaps by introducing an integrative typology of the Collaborative Economy (CE) grounded in Service-Dominant (S-D) logic. Design/methodology/approach We conducted an interdisciplinary review of CE conceptualizations and used creative synthesis to develop a typology based on three dimensions: compensated versus free, mediated versus direct and access versus ownership. The framework identifies four CE markets and eight collaborative exchange behaviors (CEBs). Findings Existing CE typologies provide valuable but partial perspectives, often emphasizing isolated dimensions or excluding noncommercial and nonmediated exchanges. The framework conceptualizes CE markets as institutionalized service arrangements that differ in how actors integrate resources, coordinate exchange and cocreate value. Collaborative exchanges may substitute for, coexist with or become institutionalized alongside traditional market forms. Research limitations/implications The typology supports cumulative CE research and offers a research agenda addr…
venue: Journal of Service Theory and Practice

title: Inclusive leadership and extra-role customer service behaviours: the mediating role of work adjustment and the boundary conditions of social well-being and perceived service climate
abstract: Purpose Service organisations compete on effort they cannot contractually require, and that effort is becoming harder to obtain. This study asks what still leads frontline employees to exceed their formal role, arguing that inclusive leadership (IL) facilitates such behaviour by reducing employees' uncertainty about what an appropriate response requires and how their judgement will be received. Drawing on Social Exchange Theory (SET), it tests work adjustment (WA) as the mechanism is linking inclusive leadership to extra-role customer service (ERS), with social well-being (SW) and perceived service climate (SC) conditioning different stages of that process. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 344 frontline expatriate employees across five service sectors in the UAE. The measurement model was assessed in AMOS, and the hypothesised relationships were tested using regression-based conditional process analysis. Findings Inclusive leadership was positively associated with extra-role customer service, and this relationship was partially mediated by work adjustment. Work adjustment, therefore, represents one pathway through which inclusive leadership relates to discretionary customer service, although other mechanisms may also operate. Social well-being strengthened the relationship between inclusive leadership and work adjustment, whereas perceived service cli…

title: A Practical Guide for Academic Labs to Navigate EPA’s 2024 Methylene Chloride (Dichloromethane) Regulation
abstract: Abstract Methylene chloride is a widely used lab solvent for extractions, purifications, and synthesis due to its polarity, aprotic nature, and low boiling point. In April 2024, EPA issued the final risk management rule for methylene chloride, prohibiting nearly all uses of methylene chloride, with one of the exceptions being use as a lab chemical. This ruling greatly impacts higher education academic and research labs, where methylene chloride is widely used, requiring stricter workplace protections and adding administrative, operational, and financial challenges. In response to the ruling, resources were developed to assist with these additional challenges. This paper summarizes the Final Risk Management Rule for Methylene Chloride and works through a researcher and safety professional perspective on opportunities to eliminate, substitute, or work with methylene chloride using the hierarchy of controls as a framework for risk assessment and risk mitigation.

title: The proof-of-concept for raindrop size distribution retrieval using combined dual-frequency radar DFR
abstract: Accurate retrieval of raindrop size distributions (DSDs) is essential for understanding cloud and precipitation microphysics. The dual-frequency ratio (DFR) measured by dual-frequency radars is independent of the normalized intercept parameter (Nw) and depends solely on the mass-weighted mean diameter (Dm). This characteristic makes DFR a powerful parameter for DSD retrieval. However, the DFR–Dm relationship is subject to a dual-solution ambiguity, particularly for smaller particles. This study demonstrates that W-band reflectivities obtained through scattering simulations based on measured raindrop size distributions, combined with the DFR(Ka, W) constraint, effectively mitigate the DFR(X, Ka)–Dm dual-solution ambiguity. The results demonstrate that incorporating the DFR(Ka, W) constraint substantially reduces the DFR–Dm ambiguity, raising the proportion of data with a unique Dm solution from 35.38 % (DFR(X, Ka) alone) to 87.5 %. The proposed framework shows potential advantages over conventional approaches, particularly for weak echoes (< 20 dBZ), where conventional methods fail but the proposed framework maintains robust accuracy. This proof-of-concept study provides a reference framework for future three-frequency radar DSD retrieval.

title: Frequency, kinetics, and clinical significance of HHV-6 DNAemia after PTCy-based hematopoietic cell transplant
abstract: Abstract The clinical significance of human herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6) after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) is debated. We prospectively collected weekly whole-blood HHV-6 in 217 posttransplantation cyclophosphamide (PTCy)–based HCT recipients. Overall, 149 patients (69%) had HHV-6 detected, at a median of 21 days after HCT; in 63 (29%) patients, HHV-6 DNAemia spiked to ≥4 × log10 copies per mL (high-level HHV-6 DNAemia) at median day +27. Hematologic malignancy, myeloablative conditioning, HLA-partially mismatched donor, marrow graft, PTCy dose, and sirolimus use were univariates associated with high-level HHV-6 DNAemia. All spikes precipitously declined spontaneously, but after initial decline, 27% persisted at ≥3 × log10 copies per mL for >1 month. Those with HHV-6 spikes had lower day +28 CD4+ T-cell counts. During initial spikes, there was a strong correlation between plasma and whole-blood HHV-6 DNAemia. By contrast, in patients with HHV-6 persisting for >1 month, HHV-6 was predominantly found within CD4+ T cells but not in plasma. Only 1 patient developed HHV-6–associated encephalitis. High-level HHV-6 DNAemia was associated with significantly increased rates of otherwise unexplained fever (35% vs 21% in patients without high-level HHV-6 DNAemia), rash (27% vs 12%), transaminitis (52% vs 27%), and gastrointestinal symptoms (23% vs 7%), as well as increas…

title: The Legal Battle Over Mifepristone and the Future of FDA Regulation
The emerging role of ARE1 in the molecular regulation of nitrogen use efficiency: opportunities for genome editing
Longitudinal effects of compassion training on emotion regulation and prosocial moral development among adolescents
abstract: This cluster-randomized trial compared eight weeks of compassion training with an intensity-matched relaxation program in 876 adolescents from 34 classes in four Chinese secondary schools. Assessments occurred at baseline, post-intervention, and 3- and 12-month follow-ups. Three-level models showed greater baseline-to-follow-up change under compassion training at all post-baseline waves for emotion regulation (ER) and prosocial moral development (PMD; all p < 0.001). At 12 months, differential change was 2.203 points for ER (approximate 95% CI 1.266–3.140; baseline-SD-standardized effect 0.317) and 2.649 points for PMD (1.526–3.772; standardized effect 0.278). Piecewise models showed larger intervention-period gains followed by partial attenuation, supporting H1 and H2 and partially supporting H3. In the compassion condition, ER predicted subsequent PMD across all three intervals, whereas the reverse paths were significant in the first two intervals only. Between-condition Wald tests were nonsignificant for all six cross-lagged parameters ( p = 0.067–0.648), providing no support for H4. Retention at 12 months was 59.6%. Differential changes remained positive and significant across delta-adjusted sensitivity scenarios, although their magnitudes decreased as departures from MAR increased. Compassion training was associated with sustained relative advantages in this sample, wit…

title: A redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulation: a hypothesis on NLRP3-Mediated regulation
abstract: Ovulation is a highly coordinated biological process involving endocrine regulation, tissue remodeling, immune activation, metabolic adaptation, and redox signaling. Although inflammatory responses are recognized as essential components of follicular rupture, the mechanisms integrating oxidative stress, metabolic alterations, and inflammasome activation during ovulatory progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we propose a hypothesis-driven redox-inflammasome threshold model of ovulatory regulation, in which NLRP3 inflammasome signaling may serve as an important integrator of redox and metabolic cues that modulate inflammatory remodeling during the periovulatory period. This model suggests that successful ovulation requires a precisely balanced inflammatory threshold, whereas insufficient or excessive inflammasome activation may disrupt follicular homeostasis and contribute to ovarian dysfunction. Importantly, NLRP3 is proposed not as an indispensable determinant of follicular rupture, but as one regulatory component within a complex network involving cytokines, prostaglandins, matrix metalloproteinases, immune cells, and hormonal signals. By integrating current evidence linking mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, metabolic stress, and inflammation, this hypothesis provides a conceptual framework for understanding ovulation as a redox-sensitive immune–metabolic proc…

title: Unraveling the role of RDM1 in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: insights into DDR regulation and antioxidant response
abstract: Advanced Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinomas (HNSCCs) pose a significant clinical challenge due to their poor survival rates. The DNA damage response (DDR) pathway plays a crucial role in the progression and treatment of advanced HNSCC, prompting the need to identify the underlying molecular mechanisms and develop innovative therapeutic strategies. One promising candidate is the RAD52 motif-containing protein 1 (RDM1), which functions as a regulator of DDR and exhibits context-dependent roles in tumorigenesis. However, the precise function and molecular mechanism of RDM1 in HNSCC remain poorly understood. In our study, we observed a relatively high expression of RDM1 in HNSCC tumor tissues. Functional experiments revealed that RDM1 contributed to increased cell proliferation and suppressed apoptosis in HNSCC cells, indicating its oncogenic role in HNSCC development. By modulating the levels of RAD52/TP53 and CDKN1A/CDK6 proteins, RDM1 played a critical role in regulating DDR and the cell cycle in HNSCC cells. Additionally, our investigations uncovered a novel role of RDM1 in the antioxidant response, wherein it facilitated the accumulation of NRF2 proteins. Interestingly, we found that RDM1 interacted with KEAP1 protein to promote NRF2 accumulation, ultimately promoting HNSCC progression. These findings establish the oncogenic role of RDM1 in HNSCC and emphasize the novel RD…

title: Lightweight frequency-aware hybrid vision transformer for fine-grained plant disease recognition
abstract: Plant diseases can substantially reduce crop yield and quality, while accurate disease recognition on edge devices remains challenging because images often contain subtle lesion textures and complex backgrounds. This study proposes a lightweight frequency-aware Dual-Embedding Hybrid Vision Transformer, termed DE-HVT, for fine-grained plant disease recognition. Here, “frequency-aware” does not denote an explicit or orthogonal separation into independent frequency bands. Instead, it refers to complementary frequency-biased processing by two spatially aligned embedding branches: OBPE preserves slowly varying structural cues, whereas the CDC-based TexPE branch has a zero response at zero spatial frequency under the linearised θ = 1 analysis and therefore exhibits difference-sensitive, high-pass-like responses to lesion boundaries and textures. Their outputs are fused by element-wise addition before MHSA, while ConvFFN introduces local spatial filtering after global token interaction. Experiments were conducted on the Plant Pathology and PlantVillage datasets using the same training and evaluation protocols for all compared models. Across three independent runs, DE-HVT achieved a mean Top-1 accuracy of 93.51 ± 0.44 % and a mean macro-averaged F1 score of 93.64 ± 0.40 % on the more challenging Plant Pathology dataset. On the controlled-background PlantVillage dataset, all evaluated m…

title: Digital governance capacity and CBDC development: cross-national evidence from harmonized public data
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explain cross-national differences in central bank digital currency (CBDC) development by distinguishing broad digital-state capacity from observed digital-payment use. It treats CBDCs as public digital infrastructures and asks whether advancement is associated separately with administrative capability and with the salience of digital-payment use. Design/methodology/approach The study reconstructs a reproducible complete-case dataset of 109 jurisdictions by merging the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) CBDC project database as of 1 March 2024, the World Bank Global Findex 2021 indicators and the United Nations E-Government Development Index (EGDI) 2024. Ordered logit models estimate four CBDC stages. Diagnostics include a Brant-style proportional-odds test, correlation and variance-inflation analysis, a retail-CBDC outcome, an alternative account-reach measure, Firth penalized logit and simulated predicted probabilities. Findings In the preferred model, EGDI is positively associated with higher CBDC project stages, while digital-payment use remains positive but is marginal at the 5% threshold (p = 0.054); high-income status is negatively associated after conditioning on both digital variables. The proportional-odds restriction is not rejected and preferred-model VIFs remain at or below 3.11. The retail-CBDC ordered-logit model yields positive a…

title: Serotonergic regulation of neuronal excitability and glutamatergic synaptic transmission in rat claustrum
abstract: The claustrum (CLA) receives dense serotonergic innervation from dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) serotonin (5-HT) neurons, which are implicated in regulating sleep and stress homeostasis. However, the mechanisms by which 5-HT regulates the excitability of CLA neurons remain poorly defined. In the present study, we combined whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, 5-HT uncaging, and receptor pharmacology to examine the effects of 5-HT on the excitability of CLA neurons and their glutamatergic synapses. We found that 5-HT consistently induced membrane hyperpolarization or depolarization in regular-spiking type I and type II neurons, whereas it predominantly induced hyperpolarization in strongly adapting CLA neurons. The 5-HT-induced membrane hyperpolarization and depolarization were mediated by 5-HT1A receptors (5-HT1ARs) and 5-HT2A receptors (5-HT2ARs), respectively. Furthermore, we showed that activation of presynaptic 5-HT2ARs inhibits glutamatergic synaptic transmission in the CLA by reducing glutamate release. This effect was not mediated by the canonical phospholipase C (PLC) signaling cascade. Collectively, these findings reveal cell type-specific and multifaceted serotonergic modulation of the intrinsic excitability and synaptic transmission in the claustrum.

title: Ways of Thinking About Time and Mood Regulation Expectancies
abstract: The aim of the experiment was to examine the relationship between extraversion, negative mood regulation expectancies, and the ego-moving or time-moving perspective on time. The research was largely based on the so-called theories of embodied cognition, according to which various abstract concepts are rooted in the common domain of space. The participants (N = 101) were divided into three groups: the ego-moving group, the time-moving group, and the control group. The ego-moving group participants were stimulated to think about time in ego-moving terms, while the time-moving group participants were stimulated to think about it in time-moving terms. The activation of a given perspective on time was carried out by means of an exercise that involved moving events to selected days of the week. The results showed that both in the case of the ego-moving and time-moving perspective extraversion was positively related to expectancies for negative mood regulation. For extraverts, thinking about time as controllable or uncontrollable does not have much impact on their belief that they can cope with negative mood. The results may be of a practical significance for therapy and psychological counseling.

title: A Novel Approach for the Characterization of Triangular Modulated Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave Low Probability of Intercept Radar Signals in High Noise Environments by Means of the Reassigned Spectrogram and the Spectrogram
abstract: Digital intercept receivers have moved away from Fourier-based analysis techniques, towards classical time-frequency analysis techniques, for the purpose of analyzing low probability of intercept radar signals. This paper presents the novel approach of characterizing low probability of intercept frequency modulated continuous wave radar signals through utilization and direct comparison of the Spectrogram versus the Reassigned Spectrogram. Triangular modulated frequency modulated continuous wave signals were analyzed. The following metrics were used for evaluation: percent error of: carrier frequency, modulation bandwidth, and modulation period. Also used were: percent detection, lowest signal-to-noise ratio for signal detection, and time-frequency localization (x and y direction). Experimental results demonstrate that overall, the Reassigned Spectrogram produced more accurate characterization metrics than the Spectrogram.
venue: Global Journal of Researches in Engineering

title: Editors’ Choice—Regulation of the Groove Profile in Jet Electrochemical Machining by Using an Embedded Auxiliary Electrode
abstract: Jet electrochemical machining (Jet-ECM) is a promising approach for fabricating micro-meso structures such as grooves on difficult-to-machine materials. However, the electric field distribution within the machining gap usually follows a Gaussian distribution, leading to U-shaped profiles which is difficult to alter merely by adjusting the processing parameters. This limitation hinders the application expansion of the method. To realize controllable regulation of groove cross-sectional profiles, a novel machining method is proposed in this study. An auxiliary electrode is fixed at the central position of the tubular cathode via a dedicated fixture. With the machining voltage between the workpiece and the cathode maintained constant, the potential of the auxiliary electrode is adjustable. Simulation results demonstrate that applying different potentials to the auxiliary electrode significantly alters the electric field conditions, including current lines and the current density distribution on the workpiece, thereby changing the groove cross-sectional profile. In groove machining experiments conducted at a machining voltage of 15 V, the groove cross-sectional profile sequentially transforms from V-shape to U-shape and finally to W-shape as the auxiliary electrode potential is gradually increased from 0 V to 20 V. This confirms that the groove profile can be effectively regulated …

title: When digitalization fuels divergence: the Digital Matthew Effect and regional innovation divide in Europe
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine whether digitalization promoted regional convergence across the European Union between 2015 and 2023 or reinforced a persistent Digital Matthew Effect. This study focuses on how regional Digital Intangible Capital, combining research capacity, specialized human capital, digital adoption and institutional maturity, relates to economic performance and whether digital advantages spread beyond established innovation hubs. Design/methodology/approach The study analyzes 233 EU NUTS-2 regions in 2015, 2019 and 2023. It integrates New Economic Geography with a technological condensation framework, constructs an entropy-weighted Digital Intangible Capital Index and estimates time-stratified Spatial Durbin Models. Robustness is assessed using alternative index weights and k-nearest-neighbor matrices ranging from k = 2 to k = 15. Findings The results indicate a persistent Digital Matthew Effect and a stable core-periphery structure. Although aggregate dispersion in the index declines, this largely reflects convergence in basic digital access, while innovation-intensive capabilities remain concentrated. Direct effects of Digital Intangible Capital are positive and significant, whereas indirect spatial effects remain statistically insignificant across years and specifications. Research limitations/implications The analysis relies on three cross-sectional s…

title: Effects of regional integration, crisis response financing and official development assistance on environmental quality in developing economies with the moderating role of renewable energy consumption
Linking systemic inflammation nutrition status to the tumor immune microenvironment: integrated biomarkers of neoadjuvant response in locally advanced rectal cancer
abstract: Background Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet response remains heterogeneous. The inflammation-nutrition prognostic score (INPS), defined as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) divided by the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), integrates systemic inflammatory burden and nutritional-immunological reserve and may provide complementary information in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). Methods We retrospectively analyzed 312 patients with LARC who received standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT), with or without concurrent PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, followed by total mesorectal excision (TME). Pretreatment INPS was calculated as NLR/PNI. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR); secondary endpoints included pathological complete response (pCR) and progression-free survival (PFS). ROC, logistic regression, interaction, sensitivity, and Cox analyses were performed. Results Among 312 patients, 94 (30.1%) received ICI-containing regimens. Low INPS (<0.058) was associated with higher ORR (61.3% vs. 29.4%, P < 0.001) and pCR (38.7% vs. 11.8%, P < 0.001). INPS yielded an AUC of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.714–0.816) for ORR, compared with 0.712 for NLR, 0.668 for PNI, and 0.660 for PD-L1 CPS. In multivariable analysis, low INPS (OR = 3.31, 95% CI: 1.95–5.60, P < 0.001), MSI-H/dMMR status (OR…

title: Evaluating student perceptions of image-based audience response questions in medical education
abstract: Audience response systems have been extensively utilized in medical and pharmacy education to improve learner engagement and knowledge retention. Unlike traditional ARSs that utilize text-based multiple-choice questions Hotspot is an image-based ARS integrated into PointSolutions that allows students to answer questions by selecting areas of interest on images and figures, rather than choosing from multiple-choice options. The purpose of this study was to evaluate student perceptions of integrating Hotspot into pharmacology and biomedical curricula, including perceived engagement, learning reinforcement, usability and preferences relative to traditional MCQs. Faculty at California Northstate University incorporated Hotspot questions into the lectures of first- and second-year courses across three matriculating classes. Following these sessions, students completed an anonymous survey. Survey items assessed student perceptions of engagement, perceived learning, and ease of use on a seven-point Likert scale. Learners reported that Hotspot technology made it easier to pay attention during lectures (median Likert score of six out of seven [interquartile range (IQR) 5–7]; n = 99). They felt the questions were a good use of class time (6 out of 7 [interquartile range 6–7]; n = 99) and indicated that the interactive format challenged them and reinforced their understanding better than …

title: Comparative effectiveness of neoadjuvant treatment strategies and predictors of pathological complete response in locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a real-world retrospective cohort study
abstract: Objective To compare pathological complete response (pCR) across different neoadjuvant treatment strategies in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and to identify clinicopathological factors associated with pCR. Methods In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 247 consecutive patients with locally advanced ESCC who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2024 and June 2025 were included. Patients were categorized into four treatment groups: chemotherapy alone (CT, n = 50), chemoradiotherapy (CRT, n = 38), chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (CT+IO, n = 142), and chemoradiotherapy plus immunotherapy (CRT+IO, n = 17). Pathological complete response was defined as ypT0N0. Clinicopathological characteristics were compared using χ² or Fisher’s exact tests. Factors associated with pCR were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Results Overall, 63 patients (25.5%) achieved pCR. The pCR rate was lower in the CT group than in the CT+IO group (6.0% vs. 26.8%). After adjustment for potential confounders, chemotherapy alone remained associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO (OR = 0.174, 95% CI, 0.046-0.658, P = 0.010). No significant differences were observed between CT+IO and either CRT or CRT+IO. Receipt of more than two neoadjuvant treatment cycles was associated wi…

title: Fabrication of green and powerful magnetic nanocomposite for the removal of oil from seawater: Optimization using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Traditional techniques for adding modifiers to solid support materials are time-consuming and require significant energy and materials. This study focuses on modifying agricultural waste using a quick, simple, and easy solid-phase extraction approach. This work reports the design, fabrication, and laboratory evaluation of Alfalfa straw biomass (Alf. S) decorated with magnetic iron-oxide nanoparticles (Fe3O4 MNPs) for oil-water separation. This novel magnetic nanocomposite adsorbent was synthesized via in situ coprecipitation. FTIR, XRD, and SEM characterized the newly developed nanocomposite (Fe3O4 MNPs@Alf. S biomass). In this study, the Box-Behnken experimental design (BBD) was used to determine the optimal values of three independent variables affecting oil removal efficiency from seawater: the amount of Fe3O4 MNPs@Alf. S biomass, the amount of oil in grams, and adsorption time (min). The maximum adsorption capacity was 1300 mg/g with 300.0 mg of adsorbent, 10.0 mL of used motor oil, and an adsorption time of 1 min. The data also confirm successful fabrication and oil adsorption, as the high R2 value and close proximity to R2(adj) indicate that the BBD model was significant.

title: Systemic inflammatory response index as an independent predictor of all-cause mortality in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Purpose Chronic kidney disease (CKD) represents a major global public health burden, with affected individuals facing substantially elevated risks of morbidity, mortality, and healthcare resource utilization. In this context, the present study was undertaken to evaluate the prognostic value of the systemic inflammatory response index (SIRI) in patients undergoing maintenance hemodialysis. Patients and methods A total of 534 maintenance hemodialysis patients were included in the study. The median follow-up duration was 26.0 months. The primary endpoint of this study was all-cause mortality. We compared a comprehensive panel of laboratory parameters between the survival and non-survival groups, including metabolic markers (serum triglycerides, total cholesterol, uric acid, calcium, sodium, and potassium), renal function indices (serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen), hematological parameters (hemoglobin, hematocrit, white blood cell, platelet, neutrophil, lymphocyte, and monocyte counts), and inflammatory markers (albumin and C-reactive protein). Furthermore, we derived five composite inflammatory indices from the complete blood count: NLR, PLR, MLR, SIRI, and SII. Results During a median follow-up period, 105 of 534 patients (19.7%) died. Compared with survivors, non-survivors were significantly older and exhibited higher levels of inflammatory markers, including CRP and SIR…

title: Reliability and validity of the Chinese version of the spouse response inventory in individuals with chronic pain
Editorial: Beyond conventional biomarkers: unlocking immunotherapy response through novel biomarkers or combinatorial approaches
Racism as context and resilience as infrastructure: the racism–resilience response framework for equity-focused implementation
abstract: Past and present experiences of racism in minoritized communities shape the environments where health interventions are implemented and create a distinct health infrastructure built from adaptive resilience responses. Implementation science has a unique opportunity to advance health equity by examining the barriers and facilitators that determine implementation success. Yet most implementation frameworks overlook racism mediated resilience, treating racism as a background risk factor rather than a multilevel implementation determinant. They also tend to imply a linear model of implementation, though interventions are introduced into dynamic systems shaped by structural racism, institutional disinvestment, organizational constraint, mistrust, and community-generated resilience. In these settings, implementation is an iterative process shaped by interacting forces across levels and over time. This article brings together evidence on how racism drives health inequities in minoritized communities and on the adaptive strategies communities use to navigate these conditions—such as mutual aid networks, community-based organizations, faith institutions, and trusted messengers. I argue that these resilience systems function as parallel public health infrastructures and that implementation strategies that fail to engage them miss opportunities to increase implementation success and promo…

title: Detecting pathological response to neoadjuvant therapy in rectal cancer by [18F]-FDG and [18F]-FAPI-42 PET/MRI
18F-FDG PET/CT radiomics across treatment timepoints for predicting response to neoadjuvant therapy in locally advanced esophageal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy is achieved in only about 20%–40% of patients with locally advanced esophageal cancer (LAEC), yet it is the strongest determinant of long-term survival. 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) radiomics can enable automated, non-invasive prediction of response, but the optimal imaging time point remains undefined. Standardized uptake value (SUV) is only one of multiple biomarkers of PET/CT evaluation of LAEC. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the diagnostic accuracy of 18 F-FDG PET/CT radiomics for predicting pCR according to imaging time points, incorporating various feature extractions of 18 F-FDG PET/CT at baseline (pre-treatment), restaging (post-treatment), and delta (pre-to-post change). Methods PubMed/MEDLINE, Cochrane Library, Scopus, and EBSCO were searched from inception to March 2026. Eligible studies applied 18 F-FDG PET/CT radiomics to predict strictly defined pCR after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (NACRT), neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI), with surgical histopathological examination as the reference standard. Studies were assigned to three temporal pools, and for each study and time point, a single, pre-specified AUC was extracted. The AUCs were pooled separately within each time point, provided a minimum…

title: Circular Water Conservation Pathways for Long-term Urban Supply–demand Planning: A System Dynamics Assessment of Auckland, New Zealand
abstract: Abstract Urban water systems face increasing pressure from rising demand, constrained supply capacity, water losses, and long-term freshwater stress. This study assesses how circular water conservation pathways could influence Auckland’s long-term urban water supply–demand balance by integrating Reduce, Reuse, Recycle, and Recover scenarios into an exploratory System Dynamics Model (SDM). Literature-informed intervention ranges were translated into changes in domestic demand, industrial water intensity, leakage, and alternative usable supply. Conservative, moderate, and ambitious implementation levels were simulated from 2027 to 2050. Under the baseline, the supply–demand ratio falls below 1.0 in 2033 and reaches 0.78 by 2050. All Circular Economy (CE) scenarios improve the long-term balance, although their effectiveness depends on the model pathway and implementation level. At the conservative level, Reduce, Reuse, and Recover delay but do not avoid long-term imbalance, whereas Recycle-Conservative remains slightly above the balance threshold. Moderate and ambitious Reduce, Recycle, and Recover pathways provide larger long-term margins, while Reuse-Ambitious remains close to the threshold and is sensitive to uncertainty. The combined conservative Reduce–Recycle portfolio reaches a supply–demand ratio of 1.29 in 2050 and remains above the balance threshold in all 10,000 simulat…

title: Cost comparison of pdVWF/FVIII prophylaxis and on-demand therapy in type 3 von Willebrand disease in the United States
abstract: Abstract Von Willebrand factor (VWF) concentrate prophylaxis is recommended for patients with severe von Willebrand disease (VWD) or VWD with frequent bleeding symptoms but remains underused due, in part, to the high direct cost associated with regular concentrate administration. Robust cost-effectiveness data for VWF prophylaxis are limited, with most analyses relying on literature-based assumptions rather than prospective clinical data. A trial-based cost-effectiveness analysis was developed to estimate the long-term economic impact of plasma-derived VWF/factor VIII (Wilate) prophylaxis vs on-demand therapy in patients with type 3 VWD in the United States, from both payer and societal perspectives. Clinical inputs were derived directly from phase 3 clinical studies, whereas health care costs were obtained from published sources. Productivity losses during bleeding events were incorporated into the societal analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed for adults and adult women with type 3 VWD, and evaluations were conducted for both 1-year and lifetime horizons. The payer analysis highlighted potential cost savings with Wilate prophylaxis across all groups, with estimated annual savings of $10 898 per individual in the overall type 3 VWD cohort, $53 264 among adults, and $125 712 among women. Savings were higher in the societal perspective, with the largest benefit observed in …

title: Meteorology of hot and cloudy, high energy demand days in eastern Australia
abstract: Abstract As renewable energy capacity in Australia’s power system increases, questions arise about whether supply can meet demand on days with high electricity consumption. We examine the meteorology of very hot days in eastern Australia when there is also sufficient cloud cover to reduce electricity supply from solar photovoltaics. We show that these days are relatively rare, with hot, cloudy conditions occurring on 1.5%–3.5% of days during November–April, although they may have potential impacts on the electricity system on hourly time-scales. We find that hot, cloudy conditions in southeastern Australia generally occur on days preceding a cold front. Increased moisture is the main difference between hot-cloudy and hot-sunny days in southeastern Australia, while more local aspects of the meteorology may drive hot, cloudy conditions further north. Maps of satellite-derived surface global irradiance suggest that there can be spatially coherent regions of hot, cloudy conditions in the southeast, with a higher likelihood of temporally and spatially compounding events in this region. Differences in wind energy availability on hot-cloudy and hot-sunny days suggest that deficits in solar energy on hot-cloudy days may be mitigated by favourable wind resources. This work demonstrates that a scenario-based approach that matches the meteorological drivers of both renewable energy supply…

title: Reader Response: High- and Low-Fat Dairy Consumption and Long-Term Risk of Dementia: Evidence From a 25-Year Prospective Cohort Study
Response by Munir et al to Letter Regarding Article, “CXCR6 + T Cells Drive Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis”
Family firm heterogeneity and corporate social responsibility: a literature review on internal family governance
abstract: Purpose This study summarizes earlier research on the impact of internal family governance on corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance and CSR reporting as a major element of family firm heterogeneity. Design/methodology/approach Relying on a literature review, internal family governance is separated into group-related characteristics (e.g. board level, (top) management level) and individual internal governance attributes (e.g. chief executive officer (CEO) board chair). Fifty-five studies published between 2004 and the present were examined. Potential country effects were analyzed by grouping country-specific studies according to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) membership and board structure. Findings Most studies examined the influence of family CEOs on CSR performance, while other aspects of internal family governance – such as family board chair or a family (top) management member – and CSR reporting received less attention. Overall, the relationship between internal family governance and CSR was inconclusive, which is consistent with the two distinct perspectives of socioemotional wealth (SEW) (SEW-as-inspiration and SEW-as-restriction). However, in line with the SEW-as-restriction view, we stress some tendencies toward a negative relationship between group-related family governance and CSR outcomes in non-OECD countries and countr…

title: Reframing responsible GenAI as ethical fit: integrating human collaboration, trust and dynamic capabilities for sustainable business performance
abstract: Purpose This research grounds on person-environment fit theory, to examine the effects of employee GenAI collaboration, GenAI trust and dynamic capability on business performance through the mediating role of responsible and explainable GenAI (REGAI). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 315 professionals via the Prolific Academic platform using purposive sampling. The hypothesized model was tested using covariance-based structural equation modeling (CB-SEM). Findings The results demonstrate that GenAI trust, dynamic capability, and employee-GenAI collaboration significantly enhance REGAI, which in turn exerts a strong positive impact on business performance. Dynamic capability directly influences performance, while employee-GenAI collaboration and GenAI trust exert indirect effects through REGAI. Originality/value The research highlights that strengthening algorithmic transparency, fostering employee GenAI partnership and embedding ethical justice into GenAI governance can jointly create “ethically intelligent” organizations.

title: The genome sequence of a leafhopper, Ribautiana ulmi (Linnaeus, 1758) (Hemiptera: Cicadellidae)
abstract: We present a genome assembly from an individual male Ribautiana ulmi (leafhopper; Arthropoda; Insecta; Hemiptera; Cicadellidae). The genome sequence has a total length of 1 631.34 megabases. Most of the assembly (98.33%) is scaffolded into 9 chromosomal pseudomolecules, including the X sex chromosome. The mitochondrial genome has also been assembled, with a length of 17.46 kilobases. This assembly was generated as part of the Darwin Tree of Life project, which produces genomes for eukaryotic species found in Britain and Ireland.

title: Development and Promotion of “Discipline Specific Research Eco-System” among University Students
abstract: For academic advancement, in-depth knowledge, development of critical thinking, and for more clarity of career objective, discipline specific research is crucial for student life as it enables them to understand the core concept regarding the topic with its practical applicability. By keeping above mention idea at centre, this article efforts to explore the three important points: first, what ways to adopt to encourage the students for involving in active research. Second, what should be proper structure of discipline-oriented research proposal? So that scholar would not deviate from research objective. Third, to explore and identify suitable and authentic funding institutions and to understand their norms/process to pump blood into the study. Overall, this article reflects how young minds can be redirect towards innovation by research
authors: Dr. Sanjay Prasad and Dr. Priya Jain
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: A novel endoscopy-guided airway management strategy for lateral decubitus endoscopic procedures
abstract: Background This study investigates the feasibility and safety of gastrointestinal endoscopy-guided endotracheal intubation in patients undergoing elective gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery under general anesthesia requiring airway management in the lateral decubitus position. Methods Forty patients undergoing elective gastrointestinal endoscopy in the left lateral decubitus position were enrolled. Standardized anesthesia induction included midazolam, etomidate, sufentanil, and atracurium. Under endoscopic visualization, endotracheal intubation was performed using a stiff stylet-assisted tube inserted through a bite block's right lateral port. Primary outcomes were first-attempt success rate and intubation time. Secondary outcomes included hemodynamic stability, adverse events, and procedural complications. Results The first-attempt intubation success rate was 100%. The mean intubation time was 30.95 ± 6.58 s. Hemodynamic parameters showed a transient hypotensive response following induction in 15 out of 40 patients (37.5%); MAP had returned to ≥65 mmHg by the post-intubation measurement, and no vasopressor agents were administered. Repeated-measures ANOVA revealed a statistically significant main effect of time on both MAP [F (3.048, 118.888) = 23.05, p < 0.001, partial η 2 = 0.372] and HR [F (4, 156) = 3.258, p = 0.013, partial η 2 = 0.077], with a transient stress respon…

title: Increasing Sensitivity to Trailed Solar System Objects in Archival JWST NIRCam Imaging with Group Differencing
abstract: Abstract The JWST archive contains thousands of NIRCam exposures distributed across the sky. Small solar system bodies (SSSBs) are present in many of these fields, but are often trailed and more difficult to detect. The standard pipeline produces a single image by fitting a slope to a sequence of N cumulative “up-the-ramp” groups of the detector. Thus, each JWST image comprises a time series of cumulative reads. We demonstrate that transforming the ramp into a series of group difference images reduces the per-image trail length of moving sources, producing an ( N − 1)-group photometrically calibrated time series from an N -group integration. This enables higher-cadence trajectory-based searches using as few as a single JWST exposure. A generalized least-squares fit of the group difference images along the trajectory of a moving source recovers the source flux at higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) when compared to the ramp fit, with the improvement scaling with the reduction in trailing. We validate our procedure on 13 moving objects detected in archival JWST NIRCam images. To estimate our increase in sensitivity, we perform an injection/recovery simulation on the JWST imagery. Trailed moving objects recovered via group differencing show higher SNRs, improving completeness to moving sources compared to standard calibrations. For typical integration lengths of N = 4 or 6 for arch…

title: The integration of artificial intelligence and Industry 4.0 in digital supply chains: A systematic review of e-commerce evolution under Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030
abstract: Background: Saudi Arabia prioritises adopting artificial intelligence (AI) and Industry 4.0 for e-commerce and digital supply chains under Vision 2030, but implementation and alignment with diversification goals remain insufficiently synthesised in the literature. Objectives: The study examines the impact of AI and automation on digital supply chains, identifies drivers and obstacles in Saudi Arabia’s e-commerce, and assesses their alignment with Vision 2030’s sustainability and diversification goals. Method: Following preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses, 30 peer-reviewed articles from 2020 to 2026 were reviewed from IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, using bibliometric and thematic analysis. Results: Findings indicate that AI accounts for 46% of variability in sustainable performance; hybrid machine learning models reduce demand prediction error by 8.58% and achieve forecasting accuracy of up to 92%. Saudi Arabia’s 99% internet penetration supports Internet of Things development, but organisational barriers such as cultural resistance, cost, and job displacement (0.51) dominate adoption challenges over technical issues. Conclusion: Digitalisation success relies on technical and social systems, including government training and cybersecurity, to leverage AI for economic diversification beyond oil under Vision 2030. Contribution: The s…

title: Two hands of green innovation: how digital social responsibility fuels circular economy practices and net-zero outcomes
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how digital social responsibility contributes to sustainability transformation by examining its effects on green innovation, circular economy practices, and net-zero-based green performance. Drawing on Stakeholder Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study explores the mechanisms through which digitally enabled responsibility shapes innovation-based environmental outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design is employed, using survey data collected from technology-based firms in Vietnam. Structural equation modeling is applied to test the proposed relationships among digital social responsibility, exploitative and exploratory green innovation, circular economy practices, and net-zero-based green performance. Findings The results indicate that digital social responsibility is positively associated with exploratory green innovation but not with exploitative green innovation. Exploratory green innovation is positively associated with circular economy practices, and both green innovation and circular economy practices are positively associated with net-zero-based green performance. In addition, digital social responsibility shows significant positive associations with both circular economy practices and net-zero-based green performance. Originality/value This study advances digital sustainability literature by redefining…
venue: International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management

title: Flexible paper-based self-sensing biomechanical ergonomics monitoring system for early warning of carpal tunnel syndrome risks
abstract: One of the most prevalent workplace-related musculoskeletal disorders is Carpal Tunnel Syndrome (CTS), which is caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist due to prolonged improper wrist posture. Continuous monitoring of wrist posture is essential to prevent serious complications, including the need for surgery. Current monitoring methods are often limited by high cost and poor portability because they rely on expensive electronics, rigid sensors, or vision-based systems. Wearable, flexible sensing technologies have emerged as an attractive solution for early detection and prevention of musculoskeletal disorders, as well as for continuous health monitoring. This work presents a low-cost, wearable, flexible, silver-conductive ink-patterned paper patch for continuous wrist posture monitoring and identification of ergonomic factors associated with CTS. Silver nanoparticles were synthesised by a chemical reduction method owing to their high electrical conductivity and superior oxidation resistance compared with copper, and the silver conductive ink was formulated using suitable binders. The conductive ink pattern printed on a flexible paper substrate undergoes mechanical deformation during wrist movement, resulting in detectable variations in resistance that correlate with changes in wrist bending angle. An Arduino-based system continuously monitored the resistance vari…

title: Revealing hydrochemical regimes and health risks in an urban karst spring system
abstract: Groundwater in urban karst spring systems is increasingly impacted by coupled natural processes and anthropogenic nitrogen loading, yet the linkage between hydrochemical evolution, nitrate-related health risk, and contaminant transport remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops an integrated framework for the Baiquan spring system by combining hydrochemical analysis, entropy-weighted water quality index (EWQI), probabilistic health-risk assessment, numerical transport modelling, and multivariate clustering. Groundwater is characterized by moderate mineralization, Ca-dominated cation chemistry, and mixed HCO 3 − –Cl - anion compositions. EWQI results indicate generally good to medium water quality, with distinct deterioration hotspots in the central and southwestern sectors. Deterministic hazard quotients (HQ) range from 0.02 to 1.93, and Monte Carlo simulations reveal high exceedance probabilities (0.80–0.99) in these hotspots despite low regional risk. Process-based simulations using a coupled MODFLOW–MT3DMS model show that nitrate contamination remains spatially heterogeneous over time, with gradual attenuation of the central hotspot but persistent elevated concentrations in the southwestern sector under the regional EPM representation. Clustering further distinguishes a dilute recharge-dominated regime from a mineralized, anthropogenically influenced regime that co…

title: Two-mode hyperradiant lasing in a system of two quantum dots embedded in a bimodal photonic crystal cavity
abstract: Abstract We propose a scheme for two-mode hyperradiant lasing in a system of two incoherently pumped semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) strongly coupled to a bimodal photonic crystal cavity. Exciton–phonon interactions are treated within a time-local polaron-transformed master equation framework, allowing us to capture both resonant and off-resonant light–matter coupling regimes. We investigate collective emission through the radiance witness (RW), mean intracavity photon numbers, and intra- and intermode second-order photon correlations. In the off-resonant regime, we show that phonon-assisted cooperative two-mode, two-photon processes significantly enhance intermode correlations and drive the system into a hyperradiant steady state, characterized by a RW exceeding the superradiant limit. By deriving Scully-Lamb-type cavity-field rate equations, we quantify the relative contributions of single-photon and two-photon emission and absorption channels and establish a direct connection between enhanced radiance and spectral linewidth narrowing. A comparison between single-mode and bimodal cavity configurations reveals that bimodal coupling leads to stronger cooperative emission and a substantial suppression of the emission linewidth. Our results highlight the constructive role of phonons in enabling cooperative multiphoton processes and demonstrate the potential of bimodal QD-cavity …
venue: Journal of Physics B: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics

title: The use of educational drama in the management of phobias in primary school children.
abstract: This essay was carried out with the aim of researching whether and to what extent the use of educational drama positively contributes to the management of phobias in primary school children. This is an action research, where the sample of the research was 24 students, aged 11 and 12 in the 6th grade of Koutsouras and Makris Gialos Primary Schools in Lasithi. Twelve scheduled interventions were carried out, during the school year 2022 - 2023, where the techniques of the Educational Drama were used, which was the independent variable of the research, to control the management of phobias, the appeasement of negative emotions (strengthening the emotional world) and the improvement of social shyness, which were the dependent variables of the research. The Self-report Questionnaire of Children"s Fears (FSSC-GR), translated into Greek and adapted to the needs of the present research, was a means of collecting quantitative data. Qualitative data collection was ensured by observation diary and field notes, sample tasks, audio and video recording and semi-structured interviews. The results showed that the educational drama, in its digital form, had a beneficial effect on the students, helped them to strengthen their individual skills and self-confidence, in order to manage their phobias in an efficient way, negative emotions and social shyness. The results of this research cannot be gene…

title: The protein expression system impacts the efficacy of Phlebotomus papatasi SP32 as a marker of exposure in humans, dogs, and mice
abstract: Abstract Background Phlebotomus papatasi (Diptera: Phlebotominae) females are bloodfeeding insects that transmit sand fly-borne pathogens of medical and veterinary importance. Control measures include serological assays that evaluate anti- P. papatasi saliva antibodies elicited in repeatedly bitten hosts as a marker of exposure. Recombinant P. papatasi salivary protein SP32, produced in mammalian HEK cells, has recently been validated for use in assessing human exposure to this sand fly species. Methods To improve assay performance, we compared the reactivity of recombinant SP32 produced in three different expression systems: (1) HEK cells, as used in previous studies, (2) Escherichia coli , a widely used and cost-effective option, and (3) Sf9 insect cells, which should provide the most natural option for producing recombinant sand fly proteins. We assessed the reactivity of these three proteins using sera from three different host species—humans and dogs naturally exposed to sand flies in endemic areas, and mice experimentally exposed to a single insect species. Results Using salivary gland homogenate as the reference antigen, SP32 produced in Sf9 cells provided comparable results to, or even outperformed the other two recombinant proteins in terms of assay sensitivity and specificity, correlation, and insect species specificity. The SP32-Sf9 protein was the most effective mar…

title: The Causal Effect of Cross‑Border E‑Commerce Pilot Zones on Urban Export Growth: Evidence from Multi‑period Difference‑in‑Differences
abstract: Amid the rapid expansion of digital trade, China's Cross-border E-commerce Comprehensive Pilot Zones (CECPZs) represent a key institutional innovation to boost urban foreign trade. Using the CECPZ rollout as a quasi-natural experiment in a prefecture-level city panel (2000-2024) and a multi-period Difference-in-Differences design, baseline TWFE estimates indicate that designation substantially raises urban exports. The point estimate is about 0.24 log terms (roughly 27% increase) and remains robust to excluding pandemic years and municipalities, using alternative clustering schemes, and conducting spatial placebo tests. Province-level clustering yields around 0.244 (p < 0.01); robustness checks with municipality and pandemic-year exclusions give about 0.236-0.258 (p < 0.05–0.01). Heterogeneity shows larger gains in eastern coastal cities (~0.247, p < 0.01) and in regions with lower government intervention (~0.208, p < 0.05); inland and high-intervention areas display smaller effects. Subsample analyses suggest stronger effects where digital infrastructure and policy absorption are most developed. The results reveal spatially differentiated macro-level benefits and imply that policy design may need regional tailoring. Limitations include potential measurement error and residual endogeneity concerns; future research could employ alternative identification strategies and investiga…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Green Dam Based on the Envision Sustainability Rating System and Blockchain-BIM
abstract: Background: Sustainable dam infrastructure requires a cost-management framework that aligns with green certification standards and digital transformation. However, an integrated model for managing green cost performance in dam construction through digital technologies remains limited. The integration of blockchain and Building Information Modeling (BIM), hereafter referred to as Blockchain-BIM, offers potential solutions for improving transparency, efficiency, and sustainability in infrastructure projects. Objective: This study aims to examine the influence of Green Dam, the Envision Sustainable Infrastructure Rating System guidelines, and Blockchain-BIM integration on cost performance in the Kuningan Dam project in West Java, Indonesia. Methods: A quantitative research approach was employed using a structured questionnaire distributed to 80 respondents comprising project owners, consultants, contractors, and subcontractors. The data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with SPSS to evaluate the partial and simultaneous effects of Green Dam (X1), Envision Guidelines (X2), and Blockchain-BIM (X3) on cost performance (Y). Results: Blockchain-BIM (X3) was found to have a significant partial effect on cost performance (β = 0.611; t = 6.425; p < 0.001), whereas Green Dam and Envision Guidelines did not demonstrate significant partial effects. Collectively, the three variab…

title: The impact of top management team regulatory focus on accounting conservatism
abstract: Purpose Drawing on regulatory focus theory, this study aims to examine how top management teams' (TMTs) motivational orientations (promotion versus prevention focus) influence accounting conservatism and further explores the internal and external situational conditions that shape this relationship. Design/methodology/approach Using textual analysis to quantify TMT regulatory focus from management discussion and analysis (MD&A) across Chinese A-listed firms, this study applies multivariate regression analysis to assess the impact of regulatory focus on accounting conservatism. Findings Our results show that promotion-focused TMTs are more likely to diminish accounting conservatism, whereas prevention-focused TMTs enhance it. TMT restricted stock (internal situational factor) attenuates both the negative effect of promotion focus and the positive effect of prevention focus on accounting conservatism. Analyst coverage (external situational factor) weakens the negative effect of promotion focus on conservatism while amplifying the positive effect of prevention focus. Further subgroup analyses reveal that the effects of TMT regulatory focus are more pronounced in non-SOEs and firms with lower ownership concentration and are significantly moderated by auditor industry expertise and product-market competition, highlighting the role of internal governance and external market factors as…

title: Energy price resilience under environmental and policy uncertainty: evidence from a multiscale wavelet quantile-on-quantile framework
abstract: Purpose This study is an extension of recent studies concentrated on the interconnectedness of energy markets as they relate to various sources of uncertainty. The purpose of this study is to achieve an understanding of the non-linear, asymmetric and multi-scale dependencies between various energy products and geopolitical risk (GPR), climate and economic uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach The author use the wavelet quantile-on-quantile methodology that combines wavelet decomposition with quantile regression analysis to assess oil market time-frequency dynamics and the different responses exhibited between uncertainty shocks over a variety of quantiles. Findings The empirical results show a time- and quantile-dependent response heterogeneity of oil markets to uncertainty shocks. Short-run effects are generally negative, with increased volatility and risk aversion of investors. Medium-run effects experience stabilization in markets as gradual adjustment of expectations takes place, whereas long-run effects are mostly favorable, reflecting structural adjustment to economic, political and GPRs. The detailed results indicate that crude oil retains its resilience in the face of climatic and geopolitical uncertainties, while gasoline and heating oil appear more vulnerable in the immediate run, but show increased resilience over extended horizons. Practical implications The resu…
venue: International Journal of Energy Sector Management

title: Research on the Impact of Social Media Marketing on Consumers' Purchase Decisions: Taking the Brand Communication of Uniqlo, H&M, and Brandy Melville on the Xiaohongshu Platform as an Example
abstract: Regarding the influence of social media marketing on consumers' purchasing decisions, this article takes the marketing activities of Uniqlo, H&M, and Brandy Melville(BM) on the Xiaohongshu platform as examples. By analyzing the published content, user interaction data, and marketing strategies of these three enterprises on the Xiaohongshu platform, this study summarizes the impact of different marketing models on consumers' purchasing choices. The research results show that Uniqlo relies on users' spontaneous discussions and sharing to understand consumers' needs better, and its simple style enables consumers to reduce the cost of trial and error and trust the brand more; H&M uses influencers to promote products to increase brand awareness, while also promoting limited-time offers, new product launches, etc. to attract consumers to make purchases; BM stimulates aesthetic recognition through dressing styles and store experiences, thereby prompting consumers to make purchasing decisions. The three marketing methods reveal the diverse strategies social media uses in the consumer decision-making process.

title: Evolving trends and technological shifts in library management research: a seven-decade bibliometric analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examines the evolution of library management research over nearly 7 decades, highlighting publication trends, major themes, and the influence of emerging technologies. Design/methodology/approach A bibliometric analysis was performed on 1,104 articles from 357 journals indexed in the Web of Science (WOS) database. Key aspects such as publication volume, authorship patterns, citation metrics and keyword diversity were analyzed. Thematic mapping and conceptual structure analysis were used to identify research trends and thematic clusters spanning 1956 to 2025. Findings The field of library management demonstrates steady growth and a strong tradition of individual scholarship, though international collaboration remains limited, indicating potential to expand global reach. Research activity was low initially but surged in the early 2000s, driven by increased academic interest and technological progress. The research focus has shifted significantly from foundational topics like library systems to advanced areas including digital libraries, RFID, artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things. Despite a broadening scope, citation rates remain relatively low, suggesting opportunities to improve research visibility and influence. The journal Library Management stands out as the leading publication venue, with 119 articles and an H-index of 15, emphasizing its cen…

title: A University and Community Partnership to Address Diaper Insecurity Among Infants in Suburban Communities Through Home Visiting Services
abstract: ABSTRACT Context: Despite overall affluence in a suburban county, diaper insecurity affects many families in low-income communities where poverty rates are 3 times the county average. Existing federal assistance programs do not cover diapers, and transportation barriers in this car-dependent suburb limit access to traditional diaper bank models. Objective: To describe and evaluate a university-community-federally qualified health center (FQHC) partnership model for addressing diaper insecurity among Medicaid-eligible families with infants and toddlers through community health worker (CHW) home visiting services. Design: Mixed-methods program evaluation using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis of open-ended survey responses. Setting: Nassau County, New York. Participants: Medicaid-eligible families with infants and toddlers enrolled in the Perinatal and Infant Community Health Collaborative (PICHC) program who received 3 or more diaper deliveries (n = 88). Intervention: A community diaper bank established through a university-FQHC partnership distributed diapers to families via CHW home delivery, eliminating transportation barriers and leveraging existing CHW-client relationships. Main Outcome Measure(s) Diaper distribution volume, participant demographics, financial trade-offs made to afford diapers, psychosocial well-being, and child health outcomes. Results: From Ma…

The Effect of Product Quality and Price Perception on Brand Switching with Brand Dissatisfaction As A Mediating Variable (A Study of Switching from International Skincare Brands to Local Skincare Brands Among Generation Z in Surabaya)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Product Quality and Price Perception on Brand Switching, with Brand Dissatisfaction as a mediating variable, among Generation Z consumers in Surabaya City who switched from international skincare brands to the local skincare brand Somethinc. This study employed a quantitative approach using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method. The sample consisted of 100 respondents selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using SmartPLS 4.1.1.8. The results indicate that Product Quality and Price Perception have a positive and significant effect on both Brand Switching and Brand Dissatisfaction. Furthermore, Brand Dissatisfaction has a positive and significant effect on Brand Switching. The indirect effect analysis demonstrates that Brand Dissatisfaction partially mediates the effect of Product Quality and Price Perception on Brand Switching. All seven proposed hypotheses were supported. These findings suggest that consumers' evaluations of the product quality and price perception of international skincare brands contribute to the formation of Brand Dissatisfaction, which subsequently increases Generation Z consumers' tendency to switch to the local skincare brand Somewhat.

title: Using AI-powered modelling for drought forecasting in the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea
abstract: Context The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is vulnerable to drought due to monsoon-driven variable precipitation that affects agricultural production and water security. Reliable multi-timescale drought forecasting aids risk mitigation; however, nonlinear non-stationary drought signals are hard to capture indata-scarce regions. Aims This study developed and validated a Complete Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition with Adaptive Noise-Long Short-Term Memory (CEEMDAN-LSTM) hybrid Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) drought forecasting model. Its performance is systematically compared against a standalone LSTM for multiple SPEI timescales under DPRK climatic conditions. Methods Monthly meteorological records from 10 stations collected over a period of 60 years were used to derive SPEI time series. CEEMDAN decomposed SPEI into intrinsic mode functions for noise reduction and trend extraction as LSTM inputs; hyperparameters were optimised by Bayesian optimisation. Model performance was assessed with Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE), Kling-Gupta Efficiency (KGE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). Key results CEEMDAN-LSTM generally outperformed standalone LSTM with timescale-dependent skill. Short-term SPEI predictions had inherent accuracy limits (NSE < 0.5) yet reduced relative errors. Medium- to long-term SPEI yiel…

title: Comparative analysis of post-listing drug price changes under South Korea’s price reduction system
abstract: Abstract Background Pharmaceutical spending has risen steadily across health systems, intensifying concerns about patient access to medicines and the financial sustainability of health insurance systems. While newly listed drugs are a major contributor of expenditure growth, increasing policy attention has focused on how drug prices evolve after reimbursement listing through post-listing price regulation mechanisms. Methods We conducted a longitudinal empirical analysis using administrative data from South Korea’s National Health Insurance system. All new drugs approved by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety and listed for reimbursement between 2013 and 2022 were identified, and their reimbursement prices were followed through September 30, 2024 to identify post-listing price adjustment events. Price reduction mechanisms were classified into four categories: indication expansion, price–volume agreements, transaction price-based adjustments, and patent expiry with generic entry. The reduction rate for each event was calculated relative to the reimbursement price immediately preceding that event. Descriptive analyses examined the timing and magnitude of price reductions over the product life-cycle, together with subgroup analyses by orphan and/or oncology status. Results Among 212 newly listed drugs, 160 (75.5%) experienced at least one post-listing price reduction. By 36 months…

title: NoDE: noise-decorrelation embedding for robust long-term multivariate time series forecasting
abstract: Abstract In long-term multivariate time–series forecasting, longer input windows are often assumed to help. However, on some standard benchmarks we observe that, for certain model–dataset combinations, performance becomes non-monotonic and unstable as the look-back length grows. Taking a data-mining perspective, we first characterize correlated input noise on the Weather benchmark, a widely used multivariate forecasting dataset. Residual-denoising analyses on this dataset show that, for some variables and time periods, input perturbations exhibit substantial short-lag autocorrelation rather than behaving as white noise. Building on this evidence, we provide a window-conditional second-order interpretation that relates whole-window embeddings to variance inflation (for linear forecasters) and curvature-dependent bias (for nonlinear forecasters) arising from residual lag covariance under temporally correlated perturbations, and discuss how this interpretation connects to both squared and absolute error criteria used in evaluation. To address this issue in real-world datasets, we introduce NoDE (Noise-Decorrelation Embedding) , a simple and model-agnostic structured linear embedding that reduces effective lag covariance via downsampling, permutation-based reshaping (shuffle/unshuffle), and shared affine mappings, while preserving a drop-in interface to common backbones. Our protoc…

title: Machine learning-based prediction of HCV-related cirrhosis and the exploratory analysis of drug use influence
abstract: Introduction Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection easily progresses to liver cirrhosis, and drug users represent a special high-risk population with accelerated liver damage and insufficient early screening strategies. Methods This study aimed to develop a machine learning model for identifying HCV-related cirrhosis, with stratified analysis between drug-using and non-drug-using subgroups. We enrolled patients with chronic HCV infection and collected blood routine, liver function, lymphocyte subsets, and drug use data. Results Among the seven models compared, the XGBoost model achieved the best performance, with an AUC of 0.86 on the test set. Stratified analysis showed significantly better predictive performance in drug users (AUC = 0.87) than in non-drug users (AUC = 0.72, p < 0.05). Drug use did not independently improve model performance and showed significant interactions with only a limited number of key features (e.g., ADA). SHAP and decision curve analysis validated the model’s reliability and clinical benefit, especially in drug users. Discussion The XGBoost model enables noninvasive and accurate cirrhosis prediction and is suitable for early screening in high-risk drug-using populations.

title: Novel approach to enhance formability in Ti–6Al–4V alloy via stress relaxation prediction with a dislocation-based finite element model
abstract: Abstract Pulsating forming techniques are advanced metal forming processes that apply cyclic or pulsed mechanical or hydraulic loads to the workpiece, enhancing formability and reducing defects compared to conventional static forming. Pulsating forming emerges as a transformative solution to overcome the intrinsic limitations of room-temperature formability in Ti–6Al–4V alloys. However, the lack of predictive, physics-based models hinders their industrial application. To address this gap in the literature, a novel hybrid finite element model was developed, which integrates a time-dependent Bergström dislocation model with the Gurson-Tvergaard-Needleman (GTN) damage criterion. The integration of stress relaxation, a pivotal mechanism in pulsating forming, was achieved through the modification of the Bergström model with a time-dependent differential equation. A correlation was established between this relaxation time and the GTN void nucleation parameter f N in order to directly simulate damage delay. The model was calibrated with monotonic tensile and relaxation tests, after which it was thoroughly validated against pulsating tensile and cylindrical cup hydroforming experiments. The accuracy of this method was subsequently demonstrated. The simulation showed an average error of 7.92 % for rupture pressures across nine cylindrical cup hydroforming scenarios. The present work pro…

PRIMA: An Intelligent Prediction-Driven Framework for Proactive Cloud Resource Management
abstract: Traditional cloud resource management software typically perform workload prediction, VM allocation and migration policies independently, yielding sub-optimal resource utilization and excessive migration overhead. This study presents PRIMA, an optimization-driven prediction-assisted resource management framework for efficient resource management in cloud environment. The framework leverages neural model to forecast memory and CPU utilization of VMs, wherein Raindrop Optimization Algorithm is employed to enhance prediction accuracy. Based on the predicted workload, VMs are proactively mapped to physical servers to optimize resource utilization and minimize server overload. Additionally, a multi-objective VM migration strategy consolidates workloads by minimizing active servers without compromising service quality. Experimental evaluation using real-world Bitbrains workload traces along with additional validation using the Google Cluster Dataset demonstrates that PRIMA attains consistent improvements in resource management performance, yielding up to 9.63% reduction in power consumption, 75% reduction in conflicting servers and 73.24% reduction in VM migrations, and a 13.46% enhancement in resource utilization in comparison to RNN-LSTM, SVM, ARIMA, and HHO-based prediction-assisted baseline frameworks. Overall, PRIMA provides a unified and proactive alternative to conventional pr…
