title: AIRIME: a scalable adaptive RIME algorithm for feature optimization and data-driven monkeypox disease prediction
A Transferable Descriptor for Accurate Prediction of Excitonic Couplings in A-D-A Organic Photovoltaic Acceptors
abstract: Abstract Exciton diffusion length (LD) is a key parameter determining the power conversion efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs), yet its fast and accurate calculation is computationally challenging due to thin-film structural disorder and the long-range nature of excitonic coupling. Herein, we introduce a coarse-grained Coulomb matrix (CG-CM) descriptor that enables rapid and accurate prediction of excitonic couplings. By mapping molecular conjugated backbones onto a fixed number of beads, our descriptor eliminates the dimensionality dependence on the number of atoms, allowing the machine learning model to generalize across molecules with different sizes and chemical structures. The model achieves high accuracy with a coefficient of determination (R2) exceeding 0.92 across diverse nonfullerene acceptor systems, including Y-type and ITIC-type materials. We further demonstrate the model’s reliability in capturing excitonic coupling fluctuations, predicting LD in disordered thin films, and reproducing LD anisotropy in crystalline systems. This work provides a powerful and efficient tool for high-throughput screening of high-performance organic photovoltaic materials.

title: A Comparative Study of Deep Time-Series Models for Lithium-Ion Battery State-of-Health Prediction
abstract: Model rankings in battery SOH prediction can change with the input representation and battery split. This study therefore evaluated five deep time-series models—Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), PatchTST, TimesNet, and ModernTCN—on the NASA battery aging dataset under chronological and cross-battery protocols using the same input pipeline. The chronological protocol predicts later cycles of B0005, B0006, and B0007, whereas the cross-battery protocol trains on these three batteries and evaluates on the unseen B0018 battery. All models use the same 20-cycle input window and 14 cycle-level features derived from voltage, current, temperature, discharge duration, and historical capacity. The prediction target is the one-step-ahead SOH, defined as \(C_t/C_0\). Each configuration was trained with five random seeds (42–46), and the results are reported as the mean ± sample standard deviation. Under chronological evaluation, GRU achieved the lowest mean MAE, \(0.02513 \pm 0.00708\), while PatchTST obtained the lowest mean RMSE, \(0.03429 \pm 0.00851\), and the highest mean \(R^2\), \(0.73132 \pm 0.13911\). On the unseen B0018 battery, TimesNet performed best, achieving an MAE of \(0.01726 \pm 0.00394\), an RMSE of \(0.02213 \pm 0.00438\), and an \(R^2\) of \(0.88631 \pm 0.04139\); ModernTCN produced closely comparable results. title: A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
abstract: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. Under a prefix-disjoint protocol in which no evaluation context occurs in training, the true continuation is retained in the five-candidate pool more often than by a first-order predictor or an exact prefix-lookup table on identical pairs. Because Stage 3 both selects on and is scored by detection-rule density, the chains are re-scored against …

title: Individual dependency behavior in multimodal AI-assisted knowledge acquisition: influencing factors and explainable prediction
abstract: Purpose This study aims to identify the key factors shaping individual dependency behavior in multimodal artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted knowledge acquisition and develops an interpretable prediction model to inform strategies for optimizing knowledge internalization. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. Open, axial and selective coding of 32 semi-structured interviews yielded five factors: task execution, information processing, individual cognition, technology experience and knowledge management. Saturation Assessment Curve (SAC) confirmed theoretical saturation. Theoretical coverage reached over 97% by the 17th interview. An expert panel of 20 domain specialists reviewed the framework and confirmed satisfactory content validity indices (S-CVI/Ave > 0.80). Subsequently, 2,002 valid survey responses were analyzed using machine learning classification. A support vector machine (SVM) was selected for its superior accuracy and F1-score, and the Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) algorithm was applied to quantify feature contributions. Findings Task execution exerts the strongest influence on dependency behavior, reflecting individuals’ reliance on multimodal AI under task pressure and goal-driven conditions. Information processing and individual cognition positively contribute as secondary drivers, while technology experience and …

title: Deep learning prediction of overall survival in glioblastoma patients using pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data
abstract: Purpose Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits variable treatment response and patients shown a median survival of 15 months. A major challenge lies in the difficulty of reliably assessing treatment response at an early stage, as it can usually only be evaluated on anatomical MRI performed up to three months after the start of treatment, when early interpretation may be complicated by the risk of pseudoprogression. Accurately predicting short-term and long-term survivors before radiotherapy and chemotherapy is therefore crucial. The objective of this study is to develop an AI model designed to predict survival outcomes based exclusively on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI and clinical data. Material and methods A total of 1,575 retrospective T1-Gd brain images were obtained from 175 patients treated for GBM between 2018 and 2023. A ResNet-51Q model pretrained on ImageNet was fine-tuned on pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI using transfer learning. To incorporate clinical data, deep hybrid learning (DHL) models were trained. Results At patient-level, the AI model achieved 81.08% (CI 95%: 67.57–91.89), 68.42% (CI 95%: 47.06–88.89) and 94.44% (CI 95%: 81.82–1.00) for accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, respectively, for the classification of short-term and long-term survivors using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI. At patient-level, the three-class model using only pre-chemoradiotherapy MRI, achieved 87.1…

title: A model for prediction of a twin live birth following in vitro fertilization–embryo transfer in women of advanced age
abstract: Introduction The aim of this study was to construct a model for prediction of the probability of a twin live birth in women of advanced age in vitro fertilization and embryo transfer cycles. Methods This retrospective analysis included 10,089 transfer cycles from women aged ≥35 years, stratified by whether they had a live twin birth. Taking a twin live birth as the positive outcome (Y = 1) and cycles with a singleton or no live birth as the negative outcome (Y = 0). A multivariate logistic regression analyses was built based on candidate variables, followed by nomogram construction. The discrimination ability of the model was assessed by the area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve, with 500 bootstrap resamples for internal validation. Results There were significant differences in age, endometrial thickness, number of usable embryos, number of embryos transferred, and embryo type between the groups (all P < 0.05). Multivariate logistic regression identified the following five predictors of a twin live birth: age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.69, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.66–0.73, P < 0.001), endometrial thickness ≥7 mm (aOR 2.79, 95% CI 1.30–5.99, P = 0.009), blastocyst transfer (aOR 1.88, 95% CI 1.36–2.60, P < 0.001), two good quality embryos (aOR 2.20, 95% CI 1.71–2.82, P < 0.001), and two embryos transferred (aOR 19.45, 95% CI 11.57–32.69, P &lt…

title: Computational Algorithms for Early-Age Creep and Buildability Prediction in Extrusion-Based 3D Concrete Printing: A Critical Survey
abstract: Early-age deformation is a major limitation on the buildability of extrusion-based 3D-printed concrete because each deposited layer must carry increasing self-weight while hydration, thixotropic rebuilding, stiffness, and strength are still evolving. This survey reviews experimental, rheological, analytical, and numerical approaches used to characterize and predict creep and related deformation during printing. The reviewed experiments include compression, creep-recovery, digital image correlation, and full-scale printing tests. Analytical approaches include Burgers, generalized Kelvin, power-law, and hydration-coupled viscoelastic formulations, whereas numerical studies employ continuum finite elements, lattice and voxel activation, damage-rheology laws, particle finite elements, computational fluid dynamics, and coupled fluid-solid models. Across these approaches, predicted buildability depends strongly on material age at loading, load duration, deposition interval, layer geometry, and interface behavior. The literature shows that elastic models are useful for rapid screening, but viscoelastic, plastic, or damage mechanisms become important when printing duration is long or stress approaches the evolving resistance. Remaining priorities are standardized early-age tests, independent validation, uncertainty quantification, and transferable models that connect material character…

title: Risk prediction and probabilistic inference of carotid atherosclerosis based on machine learning algorithms and Bayesian network analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Carotid atherosclerosis, an important subclinical manifestation of vascular injury, is closely associated with stroke, cardiovascular events, and systemic atherosclerotic burden. This study aimed to identify stable predictive factors for carotid atherosclerosis, characterize the interrelationships among these factors, and quantify their probabilistic impact on carotid atherosclerosis. Methods A total of 22,012 participants who underwent carotid ultrasound examinations at the Health Management Center of a tertiary hospital in Lanzhou, Northwest China, between 2023 and 2024 were included. Carotid atherosclerosis was defined as the presence of carotid plaques detected by ultrasonography. The dataset was randomly divided into training and testing sets at a ratio of 7:3. Five machine learning models were developed: LASSO-regularized logistic regression, support vector machine, random forest, decision tree, and CatBoost. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, precision-recall curves, and decision curve analysis. Variables consistently identified by the best-performing models were used to construct a Bayesian network. Research on Multi-source Data Fusion Quality Risk Prediction Model for Drug Registration Compliance
abstract: Drug registration compliance management faces practical challenges such as complex submission documents, dispersed risk sources, and diversified review stages. Traditional manual review methods have difficulty identifying potential quality risks in a timely manner, especially when cumulative risk is formed by cross source, cross stage, and cross type information. Against this background, a multi source data fusion quality risk prediction model was developed for the drug registration scenario. The model integrated submission and review texts, historical deficiency records, inspection results, manufacturing change information, and regulatory provisions. Unified preprocessing, feature extraction, fusion modeling, and stratified training were then applied to achieve risk level identification. The results showed that the multi source fusion model outperformed single source models in Accuracy, Recall, F1, and AUC. Among them, the fusion XGBoost model achieved the best overall performance and significantly reduced the miss rate of high risk cases. The interpretability analysis further indicated that historical deficiency frequency, regulatory terminology deviation rate, abnormal inspection ratio, and manufacturing change density were the key factors affecting risk judgment. This study provides a computable, verifiable, and early warning oriented technical path for drug registration co…

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury
abstract: Background Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. Methods In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort ( n = 409) and a validation cohort ( n = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was …

title: Gut microbiome taxonomic and functional capacity alterations in CHD and HFpEF
abstract: The gut microbiome is known to modulate metabolic health, yet its role in coronary heart disease (CHD) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains unclear. In the present study, we profiled the gut microbiome of 234 participants using shotgun metagenomic sequencing across controls ( n = 43), individuals with low-risk atherosclerosis (LRAS, n = 23), and patients with CHD + HFpEF ( n = 168). Species richness was significantly increased in CHD + HFpEF, with no disruption in taxonomic evenness. LRAS did not diverge significantly in alpha metrics. In contrast, beta diversity analysis demonstrated significant divergence of both LRAS and CHD + HFpEF taxonomic structure from controls, with the greatest divergence in CHD + HFpEF, particularly in older patients. Notably, all differences were attenuated when comparing obese controls and disease groups. However, significant heterogeneity in multivariate dispersion was observed, and a contribution of differences in variation cannot be excluded. Further differential analysis, adjusting for age, BMI, sex, and glucose and lipid profiles, revealed significant associations between specific taxa and CHD + HFpEF, including depletion of the saccharolytic fermenter Bifidobacterium and enrichment of taxa linked to proteolytic or inflammatory metabolism (notably Prevotella and Bilophila ), regardless of age and BMI. Subsequent a…

title: Regulatory capacity is not a scalar: metrics, perturbations, and viability in network physiology
abstract: Biological regulatory capacity is commonly represented by a scalar: a summed biomarker index, standardized composite, risk count, or single recovery parameter. Such measures can be useful, but they do not identify capacity independently of the conditions under which they are constructed. This article argues that regulatory capacity is not an intrinsic scalar property of an organism. It is a conditional relation among the architecture and current state of a regulatory system, the perturbations that reach it, the metric or cost functional used to evaluate its response, the viability criterion, and the time horizon. Near an operating state, systems with identical eigenvalue spectra can incur different integrated burdens and reverse their apparent ranking when the perturbation channel or burden metric changes. For a declared quadratic burden in a stable local linearization, the observability Gramian associated with a virtual cost output represents accumulated weighted recovery burden, and the measurement map, burden-evaluation map, and latent state representation must be distinguished. For network physiology, allostasis, and allostatic-load measurement, routine choices about biomarkers, scaling, thresholds, and challenge paradigms are therefore constitutive assumptions rather than neutral preprocessing. Biological adaptation is likewise not equated with stability, compensation, rec…

title: Comparative Assessment of Group Contribution Models for Estimating the Isobaric Heat Capacity of Ionic Liquids
abstract: Abstract Eight widely used group-contribution models were evaluated for their ability to estimate the isobaric heat capacity (Cp) of ionic liquids (ILs). A curated database containing 9037 experimental data points for 142 ILs, covering eight cation families, temperatures from 190 to 524.87 K, and heat capacities from 93.0 to 1805.7 J·mol–1·K–1, was assembled to assess model performance under diverse conditions. Three main evaluation criteria were applied: predictive accuracy, functional-group flexibility, and ability to represent structural diversity of cation–anion combinations. Among the evaluated models, “GAR”, “SOR”, and “MIA” exhibited the best predictive accuracy, with overall % AARD values of 5.10%, 4.30%, and 4.22%, respectively. The “MIA” model is particularly suitable for imidazolium- and pyridinium-based ILs, relevant in industrial contexts. The “SAT” model also proved promising for CAMD applications due to its flexible atomic-contribution framework. Overall, the study offers practical guidance for selecting group-contribution methods when experimental data are unavailable.

title: Long-term monitoring of a full-scale parallel-unit downflow hanging sponge system with adaptive capacity for fluctuating wastewater flows in Japan
abstract: Abstract This study presents a 30-month full-scale evaluation of a parallel-unit downflow hanging sponge (DHS) system with adaptive downsizing capability at the Susaki Sewage Treatment Plant, Japan. The DHS reactor comprised ten identical units operated in parallel, allowing capacity adjustment by varying the number of active units. The system (primary sedimentation tank → DHS → moving bed biological filter) was monitored under normal, low-temperature (winter), partial downsizing, and sponge sheet installation (upper part of the sponge media-filled segment) conditions. Dichromate-based chemical oxygen demand (COD Cr ), biochemical oxygen demand (BOD), total suspended solids (TSS), NH₄⁺–N, NO₃⁻–N, total nitrogen, and Escherichia coli were analyzed weekly and monthly to evaluate organic removal, nitrification, and microbial reduction. DHS effluent (77–85% COD Cr , BOD removal, and a 1.5 log₁₀ reduction in E. coli ) consistently met Japanese discharge standards. Downsizing to nine units, that is, reducing the hydraulic retention time, maintained effluent quality, confirming the system’s flexibility under declining inflows. Statistical comparison among operational periods showed no significant difference in NH₄⁺–N loading rate, whereas NH₄⁺–N removal efficiency was significantly higher after sponge sheet installation. The sponge sheet enhanced hydraulic dispersion and nitrification…

title: Green absorptive capacity and environmental sustainability: unveiling the interplay and moderating roles of blockchain and supply chain finance
abstract: Purpose Drawing on dynamic capability theory and the natural resource-based view, this study aims to examine how green absorptive capacity (GAC) enhances environmental sustainability performance (ESP) through financial performance (FP) and operational performance (OP) and how blockchain technology (BCT) and supply chain finance (SCF) strengthen these indirect relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from 522 organisations in Egypt and 508 in Jordan. Covariance-based structural equation modelling was used to test the moderated mediation model. Findings The results show that in both Egypt and Jordan, GAC improves ESP indirectly through FP and OP. In Jordan, blockchain technology strengthens the indirect relationship through both financial and operational performance, whereas in Egypt these blockchain effects are not supported. Supply chain finance strengthens the indirect relationship through operational performance in both countries, but not through financial performance. The nested model comparison indicates that whilst the overall model applies to both contexts, BCT and SCF exert varying degrees of influence in Egypt and Jordan. Research limitations/implications The results can support policymakers and organisational stakeholders by showing how digital technologies and green financing mechanisms can be used to strengthen the impact of green knowledge on p…

title: Exercise capacity and handgrip strength following dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training in patients with bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a prospective single-arm study
abstract: Background Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS) is a severe complication after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) and is associated with impaired exercise capacity. Feasible rehabilitation strategies for this population remain limited. Objectives To evaluate changes in functional exercise capacity and handgrip strength following a 12-week dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training program in patients with BOS after allo-HSCT and to explore associations of these changes with selected baseline characteristics. Methods This prospective, single-center, single-arm pre–post interventional study included 31 patients with BOS after allo-HSCT. Participants completed a 12-week dumbbell-assisted diaphragmatic breathing training program. Six-minute walk distance (6MWD) and bilateral handgrip strength were assessed at baseline and week 12. Within-participant changes were evaluated using paired tests according to the distribution of change scores. Associations with selected baseline characteristics were examined in exploratory analyses. Results Following the 12-week intervention, mean 6MWD increased from 406.3 m at baseline to 425.9 m at week 12, corresponding to a mean within-participant increase of 19.6 m (95% CI: 9.3–29.9 m; p < 0.001). Mean bilateral handgrip strength increased from 23.2 kg to 25.0 kg, corresponding to a mean increase of 1.8 kg (…

title: Rural resilience as adaptive capacity: Governing permanent change
abstract: Debates on rural resilience typically examine how rural areas respond to disruptive shocks, long-term pressures and uneven development trajectories. This paper approaches rural resilience as the capacity to engage with permanent change. Drawing on sixteen qualitative interviews with regional planning and administrative actors in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, it explores how these actors interpret rural change and the conditions they associate with regional adaptation. Adaptive capacity serves as a literature-derived heuristic rather than an empirically observed outcome. The analysis identifies four interrelated dimensions in the interview accounts: reframing rurality through peripheral conditions and locally specific strengths; normalising change as a recurrent feature of regional development; locating adaptive capacities in economic diversity, social relations and practical problem-solving; and negotiating planning, policy and administrative constraints across levels. The paper conceptualises rural adaptive capacity as interpretative, relational and governed. It shows how planning actors make capacities and vulnerabilities legible, while also revealing how successful development paths, institutional routines and competing spatial claims can limit future adaptability.

title: Iberulite fall and formation mechanism during a Sahara dust event in Switzerland in February 2021
abstract: Saharan dust events can produce micrometer-sized spherical mineral aggregates called iberulites, typically found on the Iberian Peninsula. To our knowledge, iberulites have not yet been reported from central Europe. Two formation mechanisms – in-cloud and below-cloud scavenging – have been proposed. A strong iberulite fall (IF) was observed in Switzerland in February 2021, when large amounts of dust were transported from the Moroccan–Algerian border toward central Europe during a Saharan dust event (SDE). Unlike previous IFs observed on the Iberian Peninsula, this IF occurred under low-temperature conditions near the freezing point, both in the cloud and at the surface. The relative humidity in the first 1000 m below the clouds dropped from 70 % to 40 %. Comparison of the particle size distribution (PSD) of the iberulite constituents with that in the free atmosphere revealed a deficit of particles in the 0.3–1.0 µm range relative to the dust in the free atmosphere. The meteorological conditions and the microstructure of the iberulites suggest that frozen hydrometeors act as scavengers and that below-cloud scavenging is the most probable formation mechanism. Further discoveries of iberulites in Swiss SDE samples indicate that this phenomenon is widespread and not limited to regions near the dust source.

title: Emerging Patterns of Mental Health Comorbidities Among Those With Blast or Blunt Mechanism TBI: Leveraging Total Brain Diagnostics Data
abstract: Objective: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is associated with postinjury mental health (MH) sequelae, yet associations between injury-related risk factors (eg, injury mechanism, multiple injuries) and outcomes remain poorly understood. We leveraged a newly harmonized national dataset to evaluate relationships between TBI characteristics and MH outcomes. Data Sources: We analyzed data from the Total Brain Diagnostics (TBD) dataset, a harmonized data source including 2 large, multisite, longitudinal prospective cohort studies: the Long-term Impact of Military-relevant Brain Injury Consortium's (LIMBIC) and the Translational Research Center for TBI and Stress Disorders (TRACTS). Participants: Veterans and Service Members ( n = 3771). Design: Pooled cross-sectional analyses of harmonized data. Main Measures: TBI Characteristics (Predictors): Number of TBIs, whether the participant had experienced a blast-related TBI, and whether the participant had experienced loss of consciousness secondary to a TBI. Mental Health Conditions/Symptoms (Outcomes): Probable post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), probable depression, probable anxiety, suicidal ideation, suicide attempts, and probable unhealthy alcohol use. Results: Blast TBI was associated with greater odds of probable PTSD (OR 1.85, P < .001, 95% CI: 1.57–2.17), probable depression (OR 1.66, P < .001, 95% CI: 1.42–1.95), and probable an…

title: From sensing to leveraging: the collaborative enhancement mechanism of intelligent construction enabled by digital twin
abstract: Purpose As intelligent construction advances, understanding how subsystems within digital twin (DT) architectures interact to drive Collaborative Project Performance (CPP) becomes essential. This research explores internal collaborative mechanisms among Ubiquitous Sensing Network (USN), Semantic Knowledge Fusion (SKF), Algorithmic Decision Making (ADM), and Interoperability Standards (IS). Guided by Resource Orchestration and Complementarity theories, it aims to examine how resources are orchestrated via structuring, bundling, and leveraging, offering insights for digital coordination. Design/methodology/approach This research adopts structural equation modeling (SEM) and moderated mediation analysis based on survey data from intelligent construction projects. It examines direct effects of USN, SKF, and ADM on CPP, sequential mediating roles of SKF and ADM, and whether IS moderates the USN-SKF and SKF-ADM relationships. Findings Results indicate that USN, SKF, and ADM positively contribute to CPP, with SKF showing the strongest effect. SKF and ADM mediate the relationship between USN and CPP, consistent with a theoretically grounded structuring-bundling-leveraging trajectory. The moderating effects of IS on the USN-SKF and SKF-ADM relationships are not statistically significant. Nevertheless, the interaction coefficients exhibit different directional patterns, indicating potent…

title: Non-PML neuroinvasive infections reported with multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapies: a mechanism-based pharmacovigilance study, 2004–2025
abstract: Background Multiple sclerosis (MS) disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) alter host immunity and may produce pathogen-specific susceptibility to neuroinvasive infection. Comparative evidence is limited because events are rare and postmarketing research focuses mainly on progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Methods We analyzed deduplicated US FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) reports from 2004Q1 to 2025Q4 using a prespecified case–non-case design. Tier A comprised direct high-certainty non-PML neuroinvasive infection terms. Tier B comprised a possible CNS infectious syndrome plus pathogen evidence elsewhere in the report, without CNS confirmation; tier A+B was a lower-certainty expanded endpoint for sensitivity and pathogen composition analyses. We estimated overall reporting (E1), pathogen composition within tier A+B (E2), and same-pathogen CNS localization (E3). Five DMT mechanisms were compared with contemporaneous active DMTs using calendar-year Mantel–Haenszel reporting odds ratios and covariate-adjusted Jeffreys-prior penalized logistic models. Results Among 492,514 reports, 675 were tier A and 82 additional reports were tier B. Tier A aRORs (95% CIs) were 0.82 (0.63–1.05) for anti-CD20 therapies, 1.77 (1.44–2.16) for S1P modulators, 1.32 (1.06–1.64) for natalizumab, 3.28 (2.24–4.66) for alemtuzumab, and 0.56 (0.21–1.19) for cladribine. Fingolimod accoun…

title: Mechanism-based classification of in vitro–in vivo correlation failures and model-informed strategies for drug product development
abstract: Abstract In vitro–in vivo correlation (IVIVC) links in vitro dissolution to in vivo drug exposure, enabling the prediction of systemic pharmacokinetics and supporting formulation optimization, dissolution specification setting, and regulatory biowaivers for modified-release dosage forms. Its classical success relies on the assumption that the in vitro release profile remains the dominant surrogate of the in vivo input function, enabling point-to-point Level A relationships between the dissolved and absorbed fractions. This paradigm remains effective in dissolution-controlled systems, where formulation-dependent release rate differences reliably predict in vivo input rates. However, conventional IVIVC breaks down when systemic exposure is governed by drug-specific absorption properties, formulation-dependent post-dissolution phase behavior, physiology-sensitive luminal variability, or inherently complex multi-process release systems. This review proposes a conceptual framework that organizes these previously recognized challenges into four categories: absorption process–driven, formulation-driven, physiological variability–driven, and complex release–driven. The categories may coexist in a single product, and each is linked to modeling strategies reported to improve predictive performance. Physiologically based biopharmaceutics modeling, population pharmacokinetic-based IVIVC, a…

title: Fibroblast Activation Protein Inhibitors: Structural Evolution, Binding Mechanisms, and Theranostic Applications in Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography Imaging
abstract: α-Fibroblast activation protein (α-FAP) is overexpressed in cancer-associated fibroblasts within the tumor microenvironment of most epithelial cancers, making it an attractive target for cancer-specific imaging and therapy. This article summarizes the structural features, binding mechanisms, radiolabelling strategies, and clinical potential of FAP inhibitors (FAPIs). FAPI molecules generally consist of three functional modules: a quinoline-based core for target recognition, a linker, and a DOTA/NOTA chelator for radionuclide labelling. The interaction between FAPIs and α-FAP is primarily mediated by several amino acid residues, each engaging a specific structural module of the inhibitor, but residues involved are not fixed and may shift with structural variation among FAPI derivatives. The evolution from early boronic acid compounds to UAMC-1110 marks a transition from non-selective dipeptidyl peptidase inhibitors toward FAP-selective warheads, while later modifications (e.g., cyano to α-ketoamide) addressed the need for prolonged target residence. PET/CT is the combination of functional and structural scanning, increasing diagnostic accuracy. The same targeting principle also enables therapeutic applications when labelled with β-emitting radionuclides. The clear specificity of FAPI also helps overcome many limitations of 18 F-FDG.

title: Biochar addition enhances soil aggregate stability by modulating soil internal forces: the critical role of readily oxidized organic carbon and particulate organic carbon
abstract: Degradation of soil structure and function is a significant obstacle to sustainable agriculture, yet using biochar is known to be an effective way of increasing soil organic carbon and boosting structure. Aggregate stability is greatly influenced by soil internal forces (SIFs), such as van der Waals, hydration, and electrostatic forces. However, it is still not clear which specific organic carbon components play a significant role in the stability of aggregates and the action of soil internal forces. In this study, a field simulation experiment was conducted using maize straw and wheat straw biochars to investigate how biochar addition affects soil aggregate stability. The findings showed that as the rate of biochar application increased from 0 % to 10 % over 180 and 365 d, the contents of soil light fraction organic carbon (LFOC), particulate organic carbon (POC), dissolved organic carbon (DOC), readily oxidized organic carbon (ROC), as well as soil specific surface area and surface charge number, increased. The content of different carbon fractions decreased with prolonged incubation time, while soil electrochemical parameters continued to increase throughout the incubation period. Pearson correlation and redundancy analyses showed that soil active organic carbon fractions were strongly correlated with soil surface electrochemical properties, with ROC and POC being the primar…

title: Biochar-based carbon nanomaterials: precursor variability and structure-property heterogeneity for energy-environmental applications
abstract: Abstract Biomass-derived carbon nanomaterials offer potential renewable alternatives to fossil-based carbon materials. It is, however, difficult to predict their performance since biomass composition, inorganic constituents, moisture, particle characteristics, and processing conditions all have strong influences on carbonization and structural evolution. The purpose of this review is to critically examine how precursor properties, carbonization/activation strategies, pore architecture, graphitic domains, defects, surface functionalities, and heteroatom configurations collectively affect the performance of materials. The paper discusses microwave-assisted pyrolysis as a rapid conversion route with distinct energy transfer and structural regulation characteristics, while also highlighting the challenges associated with energy absorption, temperature distribution, reactor design, and dielectric property reporting. The present study establishes an integrated precursor-process-structure-performance framework for biomass-derived carbon nanomaterials, in contrast to previous reviews that were primarily concerned with synthesis or applications. A standardized reporting approach and data-driven approaches are further recommended to improve reproducibility, enable reliable comparisons, and support scalable and application-oriented biochar research. Highlights Biomass can be converted int…

title: The rise of artificial intelligence in algorithmic trading: a bibliometric study
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to provide a comprehensive bibliometric mapping of research on artificial intelligence in algorithmic trading by analyzing 417 publications from 1993 to 2025. It seeks to identify publication trends, influential journals and authors, collaboration patterns, and the field's main thematic structures, in order to clarify the intellectual foundations, emerging research fronts, and future directions of this rapidly evolving interdisciplinary domain. Design/methodology/approach The study employs a bibliometric research design based on 417 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (1993–2025). Descriptive indicators are used to analyze publication trends and source productivity. Network-based techniques, implemented through VOSviewer, are applied to conduct citation analysis, co-authorship mapping, and term co-occurrence analysis. These methods enable the identification of influential contributions, collaboration structures, thematic clusters, and emerging research fronts within artificial intelligence–driven algorithmic trading. Findings The results show a sharp growth in publications since 2018, indicating the rapid consolidation of AI-driven algorithmic trading as a research field. A small number of highly cited studies act as intellectual anchors, while most authors and institutions remain weakly connected, revealing fragmented collabor…

title: Weathering-derived calcium supports carbon storage in grassland soils
abstract: Abstract Dark colored grassland soils, known as Mollisols, are intensively farmed and rich in organic matter, and hence have an important role in the carbon cycle. Organic carbon storage in Mollisols may result from interactions between organic matter and calcium released by carbonate and silicate weathering. Here we test this hypothesis by using a geochemical model to simulate calcium release from weathering in soils across the USA. We find that calcium released by mineral weathering is associated with soil organic carbon storage and that this effect is stronger in Mollisols than in non-Mollisols. Our model also shows that agriculture has increased calcium inputs to cultivated USA Mollisols 4-5 fold, indicating that humans have fundamentally changed the geochemical conditions that sustain organic carbon in these soils. By implication, moderating the quantity of and timing of calcium release may help to preserve and restore carbon in the world’s most intensively farmed landscapes.

title: Analysis of the Relationship Between the Proportion of Surface Atoms and Light Emission Competition in Semiconductor Nanomaterials
abstract: Because of their quantum size effects and surface effects, semiconductor nanomaterials show a wide range of optical properties, making them a core part of strategic industries like high-definition displays, solid-state lighting, and biomedical detection. Its light-emitting mechanism mainly includes exciton emission and defect emission. The coexistence and competition between the two is one of the key factors affecting performance. But traditional studies mostly attribute it separately to quantum size effects and surface effects, lacking a unified structural parameter. This article introduces 'surface atom ratio' as a parameter to uniformly describe this competitive relationship, and also analyzes its role as a bridge connecting quantum size effects and surface effects. Using a theoretical analysis approach, starting from the three major effects of nanomaterials, the aim is to derive the relationship between the proportion of surface atoms and size, and explain their connection to enhanced quantum confinement and defect state density; through systematically analyzing the effects of size and surface passivation on competition, the rules of luminescence competition centered on the proportion of surface atoms are summarized. This article found that this parameter can indeed effectively regulate the coexistence and competition between the two, and provides a reference for designing …

title: Comparison of wastewater treatment processes through a water-energy-carbon lens: insights from South Korean sewerage statistics and process-based modelling
abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluated water-energy-carbon performance of municipal wastewater treatment plants in South Korea by integrating the Korean Sewerage Statistics Yearbook (2018–2024) with process simulations. Greenhouse gas emissions were evaluated following the 2019 refinement of Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change guidelines. The public data analysis showed that electricity-related emissions accounted for 44.9% of total greenhouse gas emissions, while direct emissions of nitrous oxide and methane from bioreactors accounted for 42.6%. Environmental performance of six processes was assessed using an integrated water–energy–carbon coupling index combining effluent quality, energy consumption, and carbon footprint. As a result, each process had weakness on following factors: energy consumption for anaerobic-oxic (AO), effluent quality for modified Ludzack-Ettinger, and greenhouse gas emission for AO, anaerobic-anoxic-oxic, and four-stage biological nutrient removal. Multi-linear models for estimating direct emissions with operational factors based on simulation results were built. Dissolved oxygen and sludge retention time had a negative relationship with direct emissions. Simulation results further indicated that higher effluent ammonia concentrations were associated with increased direct emissions. Simulation would be a powerful tool for finding weakness of process and …

Socio-legal conditioning of criminal protection of the order of carbon units
abstract: The article examines the socio-legal conditions for establishing a criminal prohibition on violating the procedure for handling carbon units. The formation of a legal regime for carbon units in the Russian Federation, the development of registry accounting for the results of climate projects and the emergence of criminogenic risks in this area require an assessment of the limits of criminal legal impact. The carbon unit is considered as a normatively defined, accounted for and economically significant result of environmental activities, illegal impacts in this area can undermine the reliability of climate accounting and harm public and property interests. The subject of the research is the socio-legal, criminal-legal, and criminological prerequisites for establishing criminal liability for intentional violations of the procedure for the circulation of carbon units. The purpose of the research is to substantiate the need to ensure the criminal-legal protection of social relations that arise in the field of the circulation of carbon units. The research methods include dialectical, inductive, deductive, comparative legal, analysis, synthesis, concretization, and criminological forecasting. The object of the study is the social relations that ensure the established procedure for the issuance, accounting, verification, circulation, and offsetting of carbon units as an element of the…

title: CO2-Product-Driven Integrated Carbon Capture and Utilization to Produce Cyclic Carbonates
abstract: Abstract There is an urgent need to develop energy-efficient solutions for CO2 capture and utilization, because current integrated processes remain limited by the compatibility of the capture and conversion stages. This work proposes a novel product-driven carbon capture and utilization concept, in which the CO2-derived cyclic carbonate product is sequentially employed as a physical CO2 absorbent and subsequently as the reaction medium for its own synthesis, eliminating the intermediate solvent regeneration step. Density, viscosity, and CO2 solubility were experimentally determined for four cyclic carbonates, while cycloaddition reactions were performed under representative integrated process conditions using the ionic liquid [bmim]I as a catalyst. The complete process for natural gas purification was evaluated through conductor-like screening model (COSMO)-based/Aspen process simulation and life cycle assessment. Experimental and computational results demonstrate that propylene, butylene, and hexylene carbonates provide competitive CO2 absorption performance, extending the applicability of the proposed concept to other CO2-derived cyclic carbonates. More importantly, the direct use of the CO2-rich cyclic carbonate stream as the reaction medium was experimentally validated without significant thermodynamic or kinetic limitations despite the high product concentration. The propo…

title: The underestimated emission reduction effect of green credit: a systematic study based on peer effects
abstract: Against the backdrop of global efforts to address climate change and advance the low-carbon transition, green credit is widely regarded as a financial instrument that directs financial resources toward low-carbon activities. However, most existing studies focus on the direct effects of green credit on individual firms while overlooking interactions among firms. This study systematically examines the peer effects of green credit on corporate carbon reduction at the industry and city levels and explores the underlying mechanisms. To this end, a theoretical model is developed to explain how green credit induces peer effects on corporate carbon reduction. The theoretical predictions are then tested using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms. The results show that greater access to green credit among peer firms significantly reduces the carbon emission intensity of focal firms, indicating that green credit generates carbon-reduction peer effects at both the industry and city levels. Market competition and learning and imitation are important mechanisms through which these peer effects operate. The carbon-reduction peer effects of green credit are more pronounced among firms in industries not subject to green-credit restrictions and among those located in Green Finance Reform and Innovation Pilot Zones. This study advances theoretical modeling and empirical research on green fina…

title: Risk-coupling assessment system to improve the safety of urban subway construction
abstract: Purpose This study develops and evaluates a dynamic risk-coupling assessment system for urban subway construction that identifies how human, equipment, environmental, and management risks interact over time and supports stage-specific risk control. Design/methodology/approach Risk indicators were compiled from academic and industry sources and refined through consultation with 20 subway-construction experts. The study also collected 396 questionnaire responses to evaluate the indicators and test measurement reliability and effect. Indicator weights were estimated by combining the Analytic Hierarchy Process and the Entropy Weight Method. System Dynamics was applied to simulate 24-month risk trajectories and feedback relationships, while a Cloud Model represented the fuzziness and randomness of expert judgments. Sensitivity analysis was used to examine the influence of the risk dimensions. Findings Human-related risk remained the dominant upstream driver throughout the simulated construction period. Equipment risk ranked second and showed a marked mid-project increase around the 12th month, creating an early-warning window for preventive maintenance and inspection. Environmental risk was comparatively stable, while management risk declined as procedures and coordination matured. The integrated model therefore supports structural decoupling of reinforcing pathways and temporal dec…

title: From fragmentation to integration: digital health as a catalyst for universal health coverage in Somalia
abstract: Universal Health Coverage (UHC) remains a major challenge in Somalia, where prolonged conflict, weak governance, fragmented service delivery, and donor dependence continue to undermine health system performance. Although digital health has emerged as a promising strategy for strengthening health systems, its implementation in Somalia has largely been characterized by fragmented, donor-driven, and disease-specific initiatives with limited integration into national health system reform. This Perspective argues that a major barrier to digital health-enabled progress toward UHC in Somalia is the fragmentation of governance, financing, health information systems, and implementation, rather than simply the absence of digital technologies. Drawing on recent evidence from Somalia and other low- and middle-income countries, we propose reframing digital health as strategic public infrastructure that integrates governance, service delivery, information systems, and financing to support health system transformation. We identify five strategic priorities: strengthening digital health governance, building interoperable digital architecture, accelerating digitally enabled primary health care, ensuring sustainable financing through effective public–private collaboration, and advancing digital equity with workforce capacity. Collectively, these priorities provide a policy-oriented framework for…

title: Post-mining flooding-induced ground displacements, microseismicity, and gas anomalies: a synthesis of research on the abandoned Ruhr, Saar, and Ibbenbüren hard coal districts in Germany
abstract: Abstract Raw material depletion, uneconomic production, and government policies will result in the abandonment of hundreds to thousands of underground mines worldwide within the next years. Hence, mine drainage becomes operationally and economically dispensable. Consequently, the mine flooding is initiated by the mine operator. This increases the subsurface pore fluid pressure potentially inducing seismicity and ground displacements. Here, we present a synthesis on published and unpublished research on three abandoned hard coal mining districts in Germany (Ruhr, Saar, Ibbenbüren), which are currently undergoing flooding. The interdisciplinary approach (3D fault modelling and stress analysis, seismological, ground displacement, and outgassing monitoring) suggests that flooding correlates with the temporal occurrence of post-mining microseismicity (mainly M L < 2) and ground displacements (centimeters-decimeters). Flooding-induced microseismicity in the Ruhr area is focused in pillar areas below the mine panels and is not correlated with the activation of large-scale fault systems. Anomalous outgassing into soil is a temporally variable process in the Ruhr area. Ground displacements from InSAR measurements show complex spatio-temporal patterns that correspond to developing mine water levels in different parts of the mines. The ground displacements analyzed vary during different p…

title: An expert-based AHP decision framework for prioritizing greywater reuse integration criteria in sustainable urban development
abstract: ABSTRACT This study develops a decision-support framework for integrating greywater reuse into sustainable urban environments using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). The study prioritizes multi-scale criteria that influence greywater system implementation and translates them into a practical planning tool. A structured literature review identifies four main criterion groups (urban, infrastructure, environmental, and architectural) and twenty-three sub-criteria. The study analyzes expert judgments from a panel of sixteen specialists through AHP pairwise comparisons, eigenvector weighting, and consistency validation. The results demonstrate that infrastructure is the most significant criterion (0.4125), followed by urban factors (0.3526), with environmental and architectural dimensions ranking lower. At the sub-criteria level, ventilation and permeability, infrastructure resilience, and sub-surface irrigation networks are identified as the most influential variables. These priorities form a multi-scale operational framework structured around urban baseline assessment, smart infrastructure integration, and building-scale ecological execution. An evidence-qualified benchmarking using four international case studies demonstrates the framework's capacity to distinguish between spatial readiness and operational implementation capability. The findings indicate that district-scale…

title: Network-on-Chip Technology for Chiplet Integration Architecture
abstract: In today's era, the marginal benefits of transistor scaling are continuously decreasing, and Chiplet heterogeneous integration has become the mainstream path for scaling AI chip computing power. Meanwhile, on-chip interconnect performance is increasingly becoming the key factor limiting system computing power and energy efficiency. This paper focuses on on-chip network technology for Chiplet-integrated AI chip architectures, providing a systematic review and analysis of its technical principles, research status, existing limitations, and development directions. The study first breaks down the on-chip network's dual-layer architecture of 'physical architecture layer - protocol mechanism layer,' clarifying the functional roles of each core hardware unit and protocol mechanism and the complete data transmission logic. Next, from the perspectives of topology, routing algorithms, switching mechanisms, and flow control mechanisms, it summarizes the evolution of on-chip network technology and the customized research results for AI computing features and Chiplet heterogeneous scenarios. It then identifies two core current issues—inter-chiplet interconnect performance bottlenecks and lack of cross-layer collaborative design, as well as insufficient dynamic load adaptation and lagging industry standards — and outlines the key paths for future technology optimization. title: Temperature dependence of the main optical constants of a-Si:H
abstract: The present study examines the influence of temperature on the interband optical absorption coefficient of hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si:H) through comprehensive experimental characterization and in-depth theoretical modeling, providing valuable insights into the underlying absorption mechanisms. Optical absorption spectra were recorded over a wide temperature range, enabling the evolution of the absorption edge to be traced, as well as the features of interband transitions and their sensitivity to thermal influences to be identified. Particular attention is paid to the analysis of the exponential absorption tail (Urbach tail), which reflects the degree of structural disorder in the material. The experimental data were processed using modern approximation methods based on established optical absorption models, enabling the determination of key energy parameters, including the band gap and Urbach energy. The temperature dependence of the characteristic phonon energy in a-Si:H was estimated using the Bose–Einstein model and the empirical Varshni relation, which describe the influence of electron–phonon interactions on the band structure and optical properties of the material. It was shown that, with increasing temperature, a noticeable shift of the optical absorption edge to lower energies is observed, caused by enhanced thermal vibrations and an increase in the degree of …

title: Free Energy and Diffusivity in the Fokker–Planck Theory of Polymer Translocation
abstract: Abstract A robust theoretical framework describing polymer translocation through nanopores is important for developing novel applications of nanopore technology in single-molecule characterization of biological and synthetic polymers. In this work, we revisit the Fokker–Planck based theory of driven polymer translocation through a narrow nanopore. A bead–spring model of a uniformly charged polyelectrolyte chain translocating through a semi-implicit model of a nanopore embedded in a membrane are used to gain insights into the underlying free energy landscape and kinetics of translocation. The free energy landscape is predicted using metadynamics simulation, an enhanced sampling method. A direct comparison with the theoretical free energy formulation proposed in the literature allows us to introduce a modification related to the entropic contribution in the theory. Additional classical Langevin dynamics simulation runs are performed to obtain the translocation time distribution for polymers of lengths N driven by voltages V through nanopores of radii rp. In agreement with earlier reports, a scaling of the mean translocation time ⟨τLD⟩ ∼ Nα/V is observed, with α ∼ 1.40–1.48 depending on the nanopore size. Fitting the mean exit time ⟨τFP⟩ given by the Fokker–Planck theory to Langevin dynamics simulation results helps gain insights into the diffusivity kFP used in the theory. We rep…

title: Why customer knowledge is not enough: supply chain integration and environmental strategic ambidexterity as drivers of green product innovation
abstract: Purpose This study examines how knowledge-intensive organisations develop green product innovation. Specifically, it examines how external knowledge generated through customer collaboration is transformed into green product innovation, highlighting the roles of supply chain integration and environmental strategic ambidexterity. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the knowledge-based view of the firm, the study develops a conceptual model linking customer collaboration, supply chain integration, environmental strategic ambidexterity, and green product innovation. The model is empirically tested using survey data from 301 medium-sized manufacturing firms, analysed through partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results show that customer collaboration contributes to green product innovation through supply chain integration and environmental strategic ambidexterity. Supply chain integration facilitates the alignment of externally generated knowledge, while environmental strategic ambidexterity enables its transformation into green product innovation. These findings show that green product innovation emerges through the alignment and transformation of externally generated knowledge, with environmental strategic ambidexterity emerging as its strongest predictor. Originality/value This study contributes to the literature by reconceptualising gre…

title: Hybrid photovoltaic–thermoelectric generator renewable energy systems-a comprehensive review and bibliometric analysis
abstract: Advancing renewable energy sources is crucial to meeting the growing energy demand. Solar energy conversion systems, such as photovoltaic (PV) cells and thermoelectric generators (TEG), play a significant role in addressing this need. PV systems primarily convert visible and ultraviolet (UV) light from sunlight, while TEGs utilize the infrared (IR) spectrum to generate electrical energy. Combining PV systems with TEGs allows for more comprehensive utilization of the solar spectrum, resulting in improved energy production. Recent research has focused on PV/TEGs hybrid generation systems (HGSs) to boost conversion efficiency. By harnessing the heat released from the PV system, TEGs can enhance the hybrid system’s overall power output and efficiency, potentially leading to superior performance. However, integrating these systems presents challenges due to their differing characteristics. This review aims to explain the fundamental principles of PV and thermoelectric generators, analyze recent research findings in enhancing this hybrid system’s performance, and explore various approaches to optimizing the performance of these hybrid systems. In sum, a review of previous works shows compelling evidence for integration between PV and TEG. For instance, previous works have demonstrated overall efficiency gains of 7.33%–32.09%. Furthermore, reported results confirm that TEG integration…

title: Decreased expression of Acsm2 disrupts energy metabolism and affects cell death in acute kidney injury
abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a clinical syndrome characterized by high morbidity and a significant risk of mortality. Early diagnosis of AKI provides a crucial therapeutic window for treatment. There is an urgent need for universal biomarkers for the early diagnosis of AKI. Methods We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data of AKI and found that Acsm2 was downregulated in the S1, S2, and S3 segments in AKI. Differential analysis, enrichment analysis, and pseudotime trajectory analysis were performed, in conjunction with animal experiments and transcriptome datasets, to explore the expression pattern and role of Acsm2 in AKI. Results Our study found that Acsm2 was significantly downregulated in the S1, S2, and S3 segments of renal tubules during the early stages of AKI. Acsm2 expression was correlated with key metabolic pathways, including fatty acid metabolism and mitochondrial function. The downregulation of Acsm2 in AKI was associated with disrupted energy metabolism and increased cell death, including apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis in proximal tubular cells (PTCs). Conclusion Downregulation of Acsm2 in AKI is correlated with impaired energy metabolism and cell death in PTCs, suggesting that Acsm2 may serve as a potential biomarker for the early diagnosis and intervention of AKI. Further studies on its mechanistic role could provide new insight…
