title: Advancing knotted protein design with ESM3: guided generation and topological insights
Heterogeneous Computing Systems: A Review of Architectural Evolution and Design Methodologies
abstract: Heterogeneous computing has emerged as an important architectural response to the slowdown of conventional semiconductor scaling, particularly in the post-Moore era. This review follows the shift from homogeneous multicore processors toward integrated platforms that place CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, and domain-specific accelerators on the same die. The transition is closely related to two long-standing technology constraints, namely the slowing of Moore's Law and the breakdown of Dennard scaling, while Amdahl's Law still limits the speedup that can be obtained from parallel acceleration. From the system perspective, the review focuses on three recurring obstacles: the memory wall, cache coherence in shared-memory heterogeneous architectures, and on-chip communication supported by Network-on-Chip (NoC) designs. I also reviewed low-power VLSI approaches, especially clock gating and low-swing flip-flop designs, together with design methodologies such as SystemC-based high-level synthesis (HLS), the Catapult HLS flow, and latency-insensitive design. Based on these 24 research contributions, I organize the discussion into a multi-level technical framework for heterogeneous SoC design in AI and IoT applications.

title: Harmonic Tubular Bell Design Optimization Using Finite Element Analysis
abstract: The tubular bell chime is an orchestral percussion instrument with a naturally inharmonic frequency spectrum. Inharmonic overtones can decrease the perception of clear pitch but spectral tuning for perceptual optimization has not previously been explored for tubular bells. The method uses finite element analysis to solve the inverse spectral problem of designing a harmonic tubular bell, through optimizing locations of diameter reductions to minimize spectral frequency-matching errors with a harmonic series. An initial design was generated using constrained minimization within Timoshenko beam theory. Then, the design was refined using gradient descent of simulated three-dimensional finite element analysis. The final design was prototyped using a manual lathe, and experimentally characterized via frequency response measurements. Prior to modification, the stock material had overtones up to the fifth mode between 24 and 158 ¢ from a fundamental-based harmonic series. Following shape optimization, the first five resonant frequencies of the manufactured chime were between 3 and 12 ¢ away from the target harmonic series, showing a substantial perceptible increase in harmonicity. The results prove that applied local mass and stiffness changes can modally tune a tubular bell, unlocking novel timbral features for chime-type instruments.

title: Safety and Resilience in Slope Engineering Design for New Buildings under Extreme Rainstorm Climates
abstract: The safety of construction slopes holds significant importance in engineering and architecture, with the lack of resilience against extreme weather conditions being particularly critical. This paper systematically examines the fundamental flaws in traditional design theories regarding the limitations of compression-shear stress paths and the assumption of constant soil parameters. It delves into the systemic vulnerabilities in resilience across the entire lifecycle caused by operational supervision gaps and post-event regulatory gaps in the current construction system. Additionally, it reveals the consequences of mechanistic isolation between structural support and ecological protection, as well as the oversimplified engineering approach resulting from outdated drainage system standards, through real-world disaster case studies. Based on this, this article proposes a theoretical revision direction for constructing a tension shear fluid-solid coupling unsaturated soil mechanics system, explores a differentiated zoning control mechanism based on quantitative risk analysis (QRA), and integrates digital Bayesian pre-evaluation methods with on-site observations. The research aims to provide rigorous theoretical support for the disaster-resistant design of high-risk building slope engineering, and promote the transformation of slope engineering from static defense to a dynamic resili…

title: AI Adoption Intensity and SME Innovation: A Configurational Perspective Based on Organizational Readiness and Learning Capability
abstract: This paper explores the configurations through which AI adoption intensity acts as a catalyst for innovation performance in SMEs. Based on configurational theory, a theoretical framework integrating AI adoption intensity, organizational readiness (IT infrastructure readiness, resource readiness, and culture readiness) and organizational learning capabilities (knowledge acquisition capability, knowledge integration and application capability) is developed. The findings of the fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis based on survey data collected from 196 SMEs in China indicate that none of the individual conditions is a necessary condition for achieving high levels of innovation performance. Three sufficient configurations are identified with a solution consistency score of 0.847 and a coverage score of 0.631. AI adoption intensity serves as a central condition in two configurations and a peripheral condition in one configuration, suggesting that its configurational role is context-dependent rather than uniform.

title: Temperate marine macrophytes are highly variable sources of Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds – a comparative study from the Baltic Sea and NE Atlantic
abstract: Biogenic Volatile Organic Compounds (BVOC), emitted by Earth's ecosystems, affect several chemical processes in the atmosphere that have profound climate impacts. Despite their climate relevance, global BVOC budget estimations are still highly uncertain, with ocean-derived emissions being particularly poorly constrained. Marine macrophytes (i.e. macroalgae and seagrass) are a large and widespread organismal group whose BVOC emission rates are particularly poorly quantified. In this study, we set out to address this knowledge gap by quantifying ex situ the BVOC emission rates of three temperate macrophytes ( Zostera marina , Fucus vesiculosus and Ulva intestinalis ) with a Vocus proton-transfer-reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometer (Vocus PTR-TOF-MS). To capture and improve our understanding of the variability of macrophyte BVOC emissions, our quantifications were repeated across two contrasting coastal regions: the northeastern Atlantic (Ireland) and northern Baltic Sea (Finland). The three macrophytes emitted a wide range of BVOCs, with a total of 166 different compounds detected. Although many BVOCs were emitted by all macrophytes, significant differences were observed in the total emission profiles, both between and within species. Interestingly, the seagrass Zostera exhibited significantly higher overall BVOC emission rates per unit biomass than the two macroalgae and s…

title: The Effect of Benefit Perception, Digital Literacy on the Application of Electronic Medical Records at Bhakti Mulia Hospital with Organizational Culture as a Mediating Variable
abstract: The implementation of electronic medical records (EMRs) at Bhakti Mulia Hospital is essential for improving healthcare service efficiency and effectiveness. However, several challenges remain, including the continued use of manual documentation, incomplete recording of patient handover processes, and inadequate training and evaluation procedures. This study aimed to examine the effects of perceived benefits and digital literacy on EMR implementation, with organizational culture as a mediating variable. A quantitative approach with an explanatory, cross-sectional research design was employed. The study population consisted of 171 nursing personnel, of whom 154 met the inclusion criteria and were included in the analysis using a total sampling approach. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4. The results indicated that perceived benefits, digital literacy, and organizational culture collectively explained 61.8% of the variance in EMR implementation (R² = 0.618; p < 0.001). Perceived benefits demonstrated the strongest direct effect on EMR implementation, whereas digital literacy did not exhibit a significant direct effect. Organizational culture mediated the relationships between perceived benefits and EMR implementation and between digital literacy and EMR implementation. These findings highlighted the import…

title: Research on functional insole optimization design based on plantar pressure and material properties using FEM
abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a functional insole that balances cushioning, comfort and support. Using finite element simulation and material testing, it evaluates how different insole structures and materials affect plantar pressure distribution and foot stability to provide optimized design solutions for daily and sports footwear. Design/methodology/approach First, a foot–insole–ground finite element model was built to simulate pressure and displacement under standing conditions. Then, material tests (air permeability, water-vapor transmission, abrasion resistance) were conducted on six commercial insoles. Based on the results, a new insole with a honeycomb structure, arch support and a heel cup was designed and validated. Findings The optimized insole effectively reduced peak pressure in the heel and forefoot, while providing better arch support. It showed good air permeability and water-vapor transmission, and maintained low mass loss under abrasion. It also improved comfort and stability. Originality/value This study combines finite element simulation with material performance testing to optimize insole design in a quantitative way. The honeycomb structure with targeted arch and heel support offers a new solution for balancing cushioning, breathability and stability, providing a practical reference for functional footwear development.
venue: International Journal of Clothing Science and Technology

title: Design and Implementation of a Smart Control Panel Using Cloud Computing for Real-Time Electrical and Environmental Monitoring
abstract: In the pursuit of efficient and reliable operation of electrical systems, this paper presents the design and implementation of a cloud-connected smart control panel for real-time monitoring and remote control of electrical devices in a poultry-farm application. The proposed system enables continuous monitoring of electrical and environmental parameters, including voltage, current, power, temperature, humidity, and vibration, with the acquired data transmitted to a cloud server for remote observation. In addition, the system facilitates remote control of connected electrical devices through relay- and contactor-based switching. The proposed control panel integrates real-time monitoring and remote load control within a unified platform, providing centralized access to the operating conditions and connected devices of the electrical system.
authors: Dr. Rashmi A. Keswani, Ms. Amisha Moon
Ms. Khushi Bhongade, Mr. Om Guru
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: Design for safety in construction in developing countries: a review
abstract: Design is widely recognised as a key contributor to poor occupational safety and health (OSH) outcomes in construction, prompting the emergence of design for safety (DfS) as a practice. Although a growing body of literature examines DfS in developing countries, no study has comprehensively synthesised existing research to assess its current state, identify gaps, and chart future directions. This study addresses that void. Through a systematic literature review, this study maps the DfS research landscape in developing countries. The review reveals that most studies have concentrated on implementation factors including challenges, barriers, drivers, and opportunities alongside DfS competence dimensions such as awareness, knowledge, attitude, skills, and practice. However, areas like DfS education and the role of digital technologies remain underexplored. Methodologically, quantitative approaches dominate, with limited use of qualitative and mixed-method designs. Geographically, research is concentrated in sub-Saharan Africa and Asia, leaving other developing regions underrepresented. This study proposes a future research agenda targeting these gaps, advocating for greater attention to underexplored thematic areas, particularly DfS education, and expanded geographic coverage, especially in the Middle East and North Africa, to inform policy and practice.
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Management, Procurement and Law

title: Design approach for padding patterns of anti-vibration gloves and their influence on dexterity, strength, and muscle activity
Strategic External Embedding of Quantum Dots Proposes a High-Performance Design AlGaN-Based Deep-Ultraviolet
Research on hybrid estimation algorithm for dynamic center-of-mass parameters of tracked agricultural transport platform
abstract: To address dynamic centroid shift and reduced control accuracy caused by complex terrain and multi-device collaborative loading on tracked agricultural transport platforms, a hybrid estimation algorithm (CBA-IPSO-UKF) is proposed. This algorithm is designed for platforms operating in unstructured outdoor environments and combines a deep learning-based model with intelligent optimization techniques. First, the limitations of traditional UKF algorithms—which depend heavily on physical models and struggle with strong nonlinear disturbances—are overcome by developing a CNN-BiLSTM hybrid model with attention mechanisms. This model replaces conventional state and observation equations. Second, to reduce systematic errors from model mismatch, a constant-coefficient compensation vector is incorporated into the estimation framework. An improved particle swarm optimization algorithm, enhanced with genetic algorithm crossover and mutation operators, is used to optimize global parameters and minimize residuals. Real-vehicle data were collected from a self-developed tracked agricultural platform, resulting in a dataset of 18, 000 valid samples. Comparative experiments were carried out under typical circular driving conditions in unstructured environments. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves high accuracy and steady-state performance in both attitude and velocity est…

title: Pre-harvest UV-B radiation during the dark period enhances phenolic compounds in Agastache rugosa cultivated in a plant factory with artificial lighting
Canopy rainfall partitioning and hydrological nitrogen and phosphorus losses under contrasting fertilization regimes in a flue-cured tobacco field
abstract: Introduction Fertilization can alter both soil properties and crop canopy characteristics, with potential implications for hydrological nutrient export, yet field evidence on the relationship between canopy rainfall redistribution and nutrient-loss patterns remains limited. Methods During the 2023 tobacco-growing season, we conducted a field experiment in a flue-cured tobacco–faba bean rotation system in the Erhai Lake Basin, China. We compared conventional fertilization (CF), organic substitution (OS, in which chemical-fertilizer N under CF was fully replaced on an equal-N basis with commercial organic fertilizer), and optimized fertilization (OF, with chemical-fertilizer N and P inputs reduced by 25% and K input increased by 25% relative to CF). Soil properties, aggregate stability, tobacco growth and nutrient status, canopy rainfall partitioning during three late-season rainfall events, and seasonal N and P losses through runoff and leaching were quantified. Results Compared with CF, OS reduced soil bulk density by 8.53% and increased soil organic matter, porosity, and moisture content by 9.71%, 11.61%, and 15.35%, respectively, while also improving aggregate stability. OS increased leaf N concentration, maximum leaf area, and yield by 25.44%, 17.25%, and 11.14%, respectively, despite nonsignificant differences in leaf area index and canopy coverage. Fertilization regime sig…

title: Topology-aware few-shot segmentation improves rice leaf-cell boundary and count fidelity, while correction is risky under tested domain shifts
abstract: Introduction Plant-cell measurements require adjacent cells to remain separated, yet few-shot segmentation is usually assessed mainly by foreground overlap. Methods We developed domain-aware topology prompt adaptation (DTPA), which trains a small topology head over a frozen microscopy-specific Segment Anything backbone. We evaluated matched 10-shot segmentation on a leakage-free RiceCell split, conducted a secondary eight-image audit, and assessed label-free routing and selective correction on locked external tests. Results DTPA improved boundary F1 and reduced cell-count error relative to ConvNeXt, while reducing Dice. The boundary advantage persisted across one- to five-pixel tolerances and against two matched instance baselines. The secondary audit linked this trade-off to improved cell-count and typical-cell-area fidelity, but not to every image-derived measurement. The label-free router reduced severe under-counting on a locked PlantSeg root test. Selective correction was less reliable under the tested tissue shifts: 14 of 45 accepted Ovules retries were harmful, and the only accepted floral-meristem retry was harmful. Discussion Topology-aware prompting and routing are computational tools for plant microscopy, not evidence of biological discovery or universal model superiority. A correction-abstention rule derived after the external audit is only a deployment proposal and…

title: Dispersal ability of seed morphs predicts germination sensitivity to competition cues in a heterocarpic plant
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims Seed germination is often regulated by cues that indicate future competitive conditions, and such cues have been shown to either accelerate or suspend germination across species. However, much less is known about how these responses might vary within species, particularly in plants that produce seeds with different dispersal abilities. In seed-heteromorphic species, dispersing and non-dispersing seed morphs may differ in their likelihood of encountering kin competition, potentially selecting for contrasting germination strategies. Methods We studied the effect of light competition cues on the germination percentage and speed of dispersing and non-dispersing achenes (single-seeded fruits) of the heterocarpic plant Heterotheca subaxillaris. In a greenhouse experiment, we experimentally exposed both achene morphs to one of three light environments: full light, neutral shade (reduced irradiance), and simulated vegetative shade (reduced irradiance and red:far-red light ratio). Key Results Dispersing, pappus-bearing achene morphs of H. subaxillaris exhibited consistently high germination percentage and speed, which were unaffected by the light treatments. In contrast, germination percentage of the non-dispersing morphs were strongly reduced under simulated vegetative shade and moderately reduced under neutral shade, compared to full light. Conclusions The…

title: Salt marsh porewater alkalinity varies with plant species identity and growth stage
abstract: Salt marshes are increasingly recognized as important sources of total alkalinity (TA), contributing to coastal carbon sequestration. While hydrological drivers are well studied, plant-mediated effects on TA export remain poorly constrained. Here, we assess how plant species identity and diversity influence TA production in a marsh mesocosm experiment including eight species and two- and five-species mixtures. On average, porewater TA concentrations were nearly twice as high in vegetated sediments (~4200 µmol kg - ¹) compared to unvegetated controls (~2400 µmol kg - ¹). However, responses varied strongly among species, with monocultures ranging from values comparable to unvegetated sediments (e.g., Puccinellia maritima ) to >5000 µmol kg - ¹ ( Triglochin maritima ). TA increased with plant growth stage, belowground biomass, sediment water content, and more reducing soil conditions, indicating tight coupling between plant traits and sediment biogeochemistry. However, TA did not increase consistently with plant species richness, as mixtures generally converged toward intermediate values. Lower TA production was often associated with higher TA:DIC ratios, suggesting a greater relative buffering capacity despite lower absolute alkalinity generation. These findings suggest that species identity and development may be important factors influencing salt marsh alkalinity production,…

title: Regional climate effects of photovoltaic power plant in desert revealed by high-resolution numerical simulation
abstract: The rapid expansion of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power plants in arid regions is an important strategy toward global carbon neutrality. Beyond cutting CO 2 emissions, extensive PV coverage also fundamentally alters land surface properties and induces feedback to regional climate. However, the climate responses to different deployment scales remain elusive for desert environments. To address this gap, this study investigates the seasonal, model-based regional climate responses to PV deployment in the Kubuqi Desert using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model coupled with a PV parameterization scheme. Four scenarios were simulated under selected meteorological conditions, including a baseline without PV, the current actual deployment, and two future projections based on energy policies. We assess the impacts of PV deployment on temperature, wind speed, atmospheric moisture, and surface energy balance. The results reveal a scale-dependent photovoltaic heat island effect. As the deployment scale expands, a distinct daytime heat island effect intensifies due to reduced albedo and enhanced sensible heat flux, with the 2 m air temperature increasing by up to 0.63 ° C in the extreme scenario. The nighttime temperature exhibits warming (+0.31 ° C) in winter, in contrast to slight cooling in summer. Additionally, the simulations estimate that PV arrays reduce the 10 m wind …

title: Metabolomic diversity and reprogramming dictate biotic and abiotic stress tolerance in sorghum
Teacher and Student Experiences during First-Trial Chemistry Lessons in Immersive Virtual Reality
abstract: Abstract Virtual reality (VR) is becoming increasingly popular and is being implemented across many areas and levels of chemistry education. When planning to incorporate this technology into teaching, several factors must be considered, such as the cost of these devices, the time required to prepare a VR lesson, and the exhaustion they can cause. Is it worth it? A 90 min lesson in Nanome was prepared and tested with 32 students from lower secondary schools (K8) and 59 students from upper secondary schools (K11). Feedback was collected through a short questionnaire completed by students and semistructured interviews conducted with teachers. This paper presents experiences, opinions, and evaluations from 91 students and two teachers regarding their first attempt to implement VR-based teaching and learning at the secondary school level. VR offers exciting potential for school chemistry education by overcoming physical laboratory limitations and enabling interactive, immersive molecular modeling that boosts student motivation. However, successful integration requires dedicated technical and spatial support to help teachers navigate hardware challenges, lesson preparation, and varying student reactions based on students’ ages and prior VR experience. Successful VR integration requires clear learning goals and an initial time investment, but once teachers master the technology, reusa…

title: The genome sequence of Viola tricolor L., 1753 (Malpighiales: Violaceae)
abstract: We present a genome assembly of Viola tricolor (Wild Pansy; Streptophyta; Magnoliopsida; Malpighiales; Violaceae). The assembly consists of two haplotypes with total lengths of 1 824.03 megabases and 1 796.62 megabases. Most of haplotype 1 (97.62%) and haplotype 2 (97.26%) are each scaffolded into 13 chromosomal pseudomolecules. The mitochondrial sequences have lengths of 134.37, 131.95 and 152.16 kilobases and the plastid genome assembly has a length of 155.57 kilobases. Gene annotation of this assembly on Ensembl identified 78 587 protein-coding genes. This assembly was generated as part of the Darwin Tree of Life project, which produces reference genomes for eukaryotic species found in Britain and Ireland.

title: Relative bench-press strength and jump power are associated with distinct tracking-based in-game shares in professional ice hockey
abstract: Background Ice hockey is an intermittent, high-intensity team sport, yet the transfer from preseason off-ice testing to tracking-derived in-game impact metrics remains underexplored in professional settings. Objective To examine associations between preseason off-ice fitness and tracking-derived 5-on-5 in-game impact in a Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL) team across three seasons. Methods Retrospective analysis of 28 male professional skaters ( N = 50 player-seasons after listwise deletion, up to three observations per player). Predictors were 30 m sprint, countermovement jump (CMJ), relative single-leg strength (Bulgarian split squat 1RM per body mass, SLS/BM), relative upper-body strength (bench press 1RM per body mass, BP/BM), estimated maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max), body fat percentage, and age. Outcomes were two team-relative share metrics derived from the league's official player-tracking system: the relative expected-goals-for percentage (xGF%Rel), defined as a player's on-ice share of expected goals minus the team's share with the player off the ice, capturing chance quality; and the relative Fenwick-for percentage (FF%Rel), the corresponding on-minus-off share of unblocked shot attempts, capturing territorial play. Ordinary least squares models included season fixed effects and player-clustered robust standard errors; multiplicity across predictors was controlled using t…
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: A Stabilized Virtual Element Method for the Stokes Eigenvalue Problem
abstract: In this paper, we propose and analyze a stabilized lower-order and equal-order virtual element method for the Stokes eigenvalue problem. The proposed method employs the same lowest-order conforming virtual element space and the same degrees of freedoms for both velocity and pressure. By adopting a mesh-dependent stabilization term associated with the pressure to the local bilinear form, we show the inf-sup condition and derive the stability for the source problem. We moreover employ the discrete spectral theory of compact operators to study the spectral approximation and obtain the optimal order for the eigenvalues. The proposed stabilized conforming lowest-order VEM of the Stokes eigenvalue problem is new, to the authors’ knowledge. Numerical results on polygonal and polyhedral meshes are presented to illustrate the performance of the proposed method and the theoretical results obtained.
venue: Numerical Mathematics: Theory, Methods and Applications

title: Comparative physiological and photosynthetic responses of three mangrove species to salinity stress and exogenous melatonin
abstract: Extreme salinity is a major environmental constraint affecting plant growth and physiological performance in coastal ecosystems. Although mangroves are naturally adapted to saline environments, their tolerance and physiological responses vary among species, and the effects of exogenous melatonin (MT) under different salinity levels remain insufficiently understood. This study compared the physiological and photosynthetic responses of Aegiceras corniculatum , Kandelia obovata , and Rhizophora stylosa under NaCl-only and corresponding NaCl + MT treatments. Seedlings were subjected for 84 days to seven treatments: control (T1), 100 mM NaCl (T2), 200 mM NaCl (T3), 400 mM NaCl (T4), 100 mM NaCl + 100 μM MT (T5), 200 mM NaCl + 100 μM MT (T6), and 400 mM NaCl + 100 μM MT (T7). Each species × treatment combination comprised one container–reservoir treatment experimental unit containing five seedling subsamples. At 200 mM NaCl, predicted maximum leaf area (K) was 14.6% and 43.0% higher in A. corniculatum and K. obovata , respectively, under the corresponding NaCl + MT treatment than under NaCl alone. Severe salinity (T4) net photosynthetic rate (P N ) was 70.18% and 64.17% lower in A. corniculatum and K. obovata , respectively compared with the control. Whereas R. stylosa maintained comparatively higher photosynthetic activity across treatments. Furthermore, reductions were observed in …

title: PPNet: a deep learning framework for rice seedling localization and distribution from UAV orthomosaics
abstract: Field-scale information on rice seedling distribution is crucial for transplanting quality assessment, site-specific seedling-stage management, and precision agricultural operations. However, seedlings in UAV orthomosaics are small, closely spaced, and easily confused with soil, shallow water, plastic mulch, and shadows, which makes accurate localization challenging. Meanwhile, under high-density planting, existing segmentation-based networks often generate adhesive responses between neighboring seedlings, leading to missed detections and biased counting. To address these issues, this study proposed PPNet, a deep learning framework for rice seedling localization and distribution mapping from UAV orthomosaics. The framework uses root-based point annotation and integrates a rice-point perception module (RPPM), an adjacent decoupling module (ADM), and an aggregated attention module (AAM). These modules enhance seedling-point responses, separate adjacent seedlings, and introduce row-structure information. Experiments were conducted on a UAV orthomosaic dataset containing 3,013 image tiles and 220,553 seedling point annotations from different rice-growing regions. PPNet achieved an F1 score of 0.9029, an AP of 0.8881, a counting MAE of 6.99, and an R2 of 0.9553. The method also generated field-scale seedling point maps and density maps under different planting densities and field ba…

title: Improving Digital Literacy Competence through Virtual Application with Creative Training for Middle School Teachers in Jakarta
abstract: Improving teachers’ digital literacy competencies is a key requirement for innovative learning that enhances students’ creative, collaborative, and critical thinking. However, the utilization of virtual-based digital technology by middle school teachers remains low. Learning remains conventional and impractical. This community service program (CSP) aims to improve digital literacy competencies through creative, virtual application-based training for middle school teachers in Jakarta. This community service program uses a participatory action research (PAR) approach that focuses on active collaboration. The method consists of four main stages: initial observation; digital content design; implementation and training; evaluation and follow-up. Participants were teachers of SMPN 217 Jakarta. The results of the activity showed an increase in teachers’ digital literacy competencies through virtual application-based creative training. The percentage increase in the "ability to access information" indicator was 93.75%; the "ability to evaluate information" indicator was 90.63%; and the "ability to create content" indicator was 93.75%. This community service program contributed positively to improving teachers’ digital literacy competencies and supported quality learning in schools.

title: Genome-wide identification of the BES1 gene family and functional study of VcBES1.3 under salt stress in blueberry (Vaccinium corymbosum)
abstract: BES1 (BRI1-EMS-SUPPRESSOR 1) transcription factors mediate brassinosteroid signaling and regulate plant growth, development, and stress responses. The BES1 family has not been characterized in blueberry ( Vaccinium corymbosum L.). We identified 16 VcBES1 family members and classified them into four groups based on phylogenetic analysis. Promoters of the BES1 genes mainly contain cis -elements associated with abiotic stress and phytohormone signaling. Tissue-specific expression analysis showed that the VcBES1 family is expressed predominantly in roots and stems. All members except VcBES1.8 and VcBES1.9 responded positively to salt stress. Among them, VcBES1.3 displayed the strongest salt induction. The protein accumulated in the nucleus. Overexpression and RNA interference (RNAi) experiments established that VcBES1.3 enhances salt tolerance. This study characterizes the VcBES1 family, defines its tissue-specific and stress-responsive expression patterns, and demonstrate that VcBES1.3 as a positive regulator of salt tolerance in blueberry.

title: Utilization of grain milling waste for plant growth and nutrient availability in soil
abstract: This study optimized fermentation process of grain milling waste (wheat bran, wheat flour and mill dust) using Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (LP) or Bacillus subtilis (BS). The experiment included two parts: (I) in vitro optimization and evaluation of the fermentation of mill waste in two inoculum levels and three mill waste ratios; (II) fermented mill waste (FMW) was tested in a pot experiment. Three different application routes were tested: soil incorporation, foliar and soil drenching. FMW was compared with NPK fertilization, compost and vermicompost. Growth parameters of the Zea Mays and soil quality of were evaluated. Results in vitro showed a two-fold increase in total protein concentration, a 6.5-fold increase in lactic acid concentration, and a two-fold increase in free phosphorus availability in FMW compared to control. Soluble mineral ions were significantly ( p < 0.05) increased Ca (3–9 mg/L), Fe (4.5–9.9 mg/L), Mg (7.5–13 mg/L), Mn (13–15 mg/L) and Zn (8.5–9.3 mg/L) compared to control in dependence of microorganism dosing and mill waste composition. FMW soil fertilization increased soil N min (22.2 mg/kg) compared to control (12.95 mg/kg). FMW applied directly into the soil or via soil drenching resulted in increased content of P (23%), K (50%), Ca (31%), S (36%) Fe (40%), and Mn (86%) compared to control. In contrast with control (9.02 mg/kg), compost (13.37 mg…

title: Investigation of cold stress tolerance in seedlings of pepper (Capsicum annuum) following application of meta-topolin
abstract: This study investigated the anatomical and physiological effects of exogenous meta-topolin (mT) at different concentrations (0, 0.25, 0.50 mM) on the leaves of cold-susceptible cultivar Kahramanmaraş-1 (KM-1) and cold-tolerant cultivar Çoban F1 (ÇF1) of pepper (Capsicum annuum) before cold stress (4°C). Leaf thickness of ÇF1 was higher than KM-1 at optimum (25°C) and low temperatures. Long-term cold stress reduced stomatal density while increasing leaf thickness in KM-1. At 48 and 60 h of stress, both cultivars showed increased malondialdehyde (MDA) and ion leakage, while FW, actual water content (AWC), and relative water content (RWC) decreased. Under cold stress, 0.25 mM mT increased RWC, AWC, and FW in KM-1 at 48 and 60 h, and at 60 h in ÇF1, without changing DW. It decreased the upper stomatal density of ÇF1 and index ratio at 60 h. At 24 h of stress, all mT concentrations increased ferric-reducing antioxidant power (FRAP), peroxidase (POD) activity, protein, phenolic compounds, H2O2, MDA, and leaf thickness. At 48 h, ÇF1 showed higher flavonoid, FRAP, and POD activity when compared with KM-1. All mT applications increased total protein content and decreased MDA levels at 48 and 60 hcompared with stress alone. mT positively supported tolerance to cold stress in pepper through anatomical and physiological mechanisms.

title: Untargeted metabolomics and antioxidant responses reveal tissue- and species-specific metabolic profiles in three Epimedium species
abstract: Objectives This study systematically analyzed the antioxidant responses, untargeted metabolomic profiles, and secondary metabolic pathways of three representative Epimedium species. Methods Meteorological data (atmospheric pressure, temperature, relative humidity, and precipitation) were recorded from July 2022 to July 2025 to provide environmental background context. Antioxidant indexes including H 2 O 2 and O 2 - levels, as well as CAT, POD and SOD activities in different plant tissues were determined. Untargeted metabolomics was performed to explore metabolic differences. PCA, differential metabolite analysis, KEGG and MSEA enrichment were conducted to screen key metabolic pathways, and correlation analysis was employed to explore exploratory associations between antioxidant enzyme activities and secondary metabolite abundances. Results The levels of H 2 O 2 and O 2 - were generally higher in roots than in stems and leaves. CAT activity showed no significant differences among tissues or species, whereas POD and SOD activities presented distinct tissue-specific and species-specific patterns. A total of 2730 MS features were detected. PCA and differential metabolite analysis revealed remarkable metabolic separation and diverse metabolite changes among the three Epimedium species. KEGG and MSEA enrichment indicated that differential metabolites were mainly involved in phenylpro…

title: Smart Plant Disease Detection Using Deep Learning
abstract: Plant diseases can damage crops and reduce both the quality and quantity of agricultural production. Finding a disease early is important because farmers can take action before it spreads. However, checking plant leaves by looking at them manually is not always easy, especially when different diseases have similar symptoms. This research presents a Smart Plant Disease Detection system that uses deep learning and image classification. The system is designed to identify tomato leaf conditions from images and classify them into three categories: Healthy, Early Blight, and Late Blight. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) was trained using a plant disease image dataset. The images were prepared and used to teach the model the visual patterns of different leaf conditions. The trained model was tested with a new image and successfully identified the condition of the leaf. In the project test, a healthy tomato leaf was predicted with 99.99% confidence. A simple Gradio interface was also created, allowing a user to upload a leaf image and get a prediction. The system can make plant disease identification quicker and easier and may help farmers and other agriculture-related users take early action..
authors: Nisha Amar Bhosale and Dr. Kiran Tikar
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: Medicinal Plant Leaf Classification: From Hand-Crafted Features to Real-Time Mobile Deep Learning
abstract: Medicinal plant leaves are central to traditional healthcare in biodiversity-rich countries such as Indonesia, yet high visual similarity between species makes manual identification error-prone. Classification methods for medicinal and herbal leaves have shifted from hand-crafted feature classifiers to deep convolutional and attention-based architectures, and more recently to real-time, on-device deployment. This narrative review traces that progression and identifies open gaps. Twenty primary studies published between 2016 and 2026 were identified through Scopus, Google Scholar, ScienceDirect, and Springer and grouped into five categories: hand-crafted features, CNN transfer learning, attention-based fusion, YOLO-based detection, and mobile/edge deployment. Unlike earlier reviews, each study is also coded for whether its model was validated on physical mobile or embedded hardware. The review finds a clear shift toward deep transfer learning models, many reporting accuracies above 90%, and toward architectures designed for on-device use. However, only three of the nine medicinal-leaf-specific studies tested their models on real hardware; these rarely report standardized latency or frame-rate figures, and public benchmark datasets for Indonesian species remain scarce. These gaps motivate work that evaluates classification accuracy and on-device inference performance together.

title: From Soldering to Sintering: Novel Interconnection Technology for SiC Power Device Package
abstract: As new energy vehicles and wide-bandgap semiconductor power devices have been used more widely, higher requirements have been put forward for packaging interconnections, above all under repeated thermomechanical loading, at high operating temperature, and at high current density. Conventional solder joints do not perform well in such a situation, since intermetallic compounds grow, voids form, and fatigue damage develops during long service, and the long-term reliability is thus weakened; therefore, three typical interconnection technologies of next-generation power devices are reviewed in this paper, that is, transient liquid-phase sintering/bonding, silver sintering, and copper sintering. Their bonding mechanisms, processing characteristics, mechanical properties, electrical and thermal performance, and major challenges are compared. TLPS can achieve low-temperature bonding and high-temperature service, but its reliability is restricted by brittle intermetallic compounds and void evolution. Ag sintering provides excellent thermal conductivity, electrical conductivity, bonding strength, and high-temperature stability, but high cost, electrochemical migration, and large-area bonding remain important concerns. Cu sintering offers low cost, good conductivity, and better resistance to electrochemical migration, while oxidation sensitivity and pressure-dependent densification limit…

title: Towards an understanding of distributed business models in rural grassroots initiatives: peer coordination and collective effectuation
abstract: Purpose This exploratory study investigates the emergence of distributed business models within grassroots initiatives in rural areas, with a focus on food systems, transportation and decentralised energy production and consumption. Building on business model research, Ostrom's work on commons governance and Sarasvathy's effectuation theory, the study examines how community actors develop alternative business models through experimentation and peer governance. Design/methodology/approach Based on ten open-ended interviews and field observations in a rural area of a Nordic country, the study identifies three main patterns: peer coordination and local reciprocity, collective effectuation and institutional misfit. Findings Based on ten open-ended interviews and field observations in a rural area of a Nordic country, the study identifies three main patterns: peer coordination and local reciprocity, collective effectuation and institutional misfit. The findings show that these grassroots arrangements can generate social, practical and ecological value, but remain vulnerable to limited coordination capacity, regulatory constraints, technical lock-ins and weak municipal or institutional support. Originality/value The paper contributes to business model research by showing how distributed value creation can operate as a socially embedded activity system rather than as a centrally orche…

title: Joule-Heated Woven Fiber Contactors for Direct Air Capture
abstract: Abstract Practical direct air capture (DAC) demands a sorbent contactor that simultaneously delivers high active-material loading, low flow resistance, efficient mass transfer, and rapid regeneration─requirements that conventional sorbent architectures rarely satisfy together. Here, we present a woven fiber contactor that addresses these requirements by interlacing dry-fabricated zeolite Y/PTFE fibers with copper wire supports into a structured contactor. Compared to a stacked laminate configuration, the woven sorbent exhibited markedly more efficient mass transfer, yielding a narrower mass transfer zone (LMTZ = 4.4 mm and 11.1 mm at 50 sccm) and a steeper breakthrough front. This structural advantage translated into robust sorption performance, with CO2 capture capacity varying by only 11.7% across a 10-fold increase in feed flow rate (50–500 sccm, corresponding to superficial velocities 5.79 × 10–3 to 5.79 × 10–2 m/s) compared to 19.2% for the stacked laminate. The woven architecture further reduced pressure drop by 7- to 18-fold over a wide range of superficial velocities (1.16 × 10–2–5.79 × 10–1 m/s). The integrated copper wires enabled electrified temperature swing adsorption (e-TSA) with near-instantaneous heating, driving CO2 desorption within 1 min. Over 10 consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles, the module retained an average capacity of 1.01 mmol/gsorbent with less …

title: A rapid beyond-design-basis check for critical building structures based on energy-bound critical excitation
abstract: Critical facilities must remain operational after rare earthquakes. However, spectrum-compatible analysis may underrepresent resonance-amplified structural responses. This limitation persists even when a beyond-design-basis earthquake (BDBE) philosophy—used initially for nuclear facilities—is desired for essential buildings. The contribution of this study is a supplementary BDBE screening framework for critical buildings that integrates established energy-bounded critical excitation (CE) mechanics with conventional ASCE nonlinear response-history analysis. The approach compares conventional responses obtained from PEER NGA-West2 recorded motions spectrally matched to the site-specific design basis earthquake (DBE) and risk-targeted maximum considered earthquake (MCE R ) target spectra with synthesized CE motions constrained by Arias intensity, peak ground acceleration (PGA), and peak ground velocity (PGV), and shaped to concentrate admissible energy near the dominant modal range. The three CE responses are summarized by their minimum, mean, and maximum values for base shear and interstory-drift. We evaluated 8- and 20-story steel buildings in both fixed-base and base-isolated configurations under conventional DBE and MCER suites and CE motions. The comparisons show that the relationship between conventional suite-mean demands and the CE response range varies with building heigh…

title: Numerical analysis of melting heat transfer in stratified Casson nanofluid flow over an inclined wedge for energy-efficient thermal systems
abstract: Purpose Given the diverse applications of nanoparticles, blood transport and stratified flow in medical and industrial domains, this study was conducted. Design/methodology/approach Nonlinear thermal stratification is used to capture realistic, high-gradient thermal environments where linear models fail under extreme industrial conditions. Energy transport is further enhanced by accounting for nanoparticle shape effects via the Hamilton–Crosser model, considering spherical, blade, brick and cylindrical geometries of copper nanoparticles suspended in water. The governing nonlinear partial differential equations are transformed into ordinary differential equations via similarity transformations and solved numerically using NDSolve. Findings Results reveal significant variations in velocity and temperature fields under controlling parameters, with strong agreement with existing literature. The velocity magnitude rises as the mixed convection parameter increases, while the opposite pattern is seen when the concentration of nanoparticles increases. Viscous dissipation and thermal radiation both contributed significantly to thermal enhancement. A greater Eckert number and thermal stratification characteristics lead to greater Nusselt numbers. Originality/value The novelty of this study is the numerical examination of nonlinear mixed-convective stratified nanofluid flow over an inclin…

Diagnostic efficacy of a novel bedside dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry device for the diagnosis of osteoporosis: a prospective cohort study
abstract: Background Osteoporosis is a prevalent systemic skeletal disorder with reduced bone mineral density (BMD) and elevated fracture risk, constituting a major global public-health burden. Conventional axial dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), the WHO-endorsed diagnostic gold-standard, requires dedicated radiology facilities, limiting its use for hospitalized, bedridden and elderly patients. This prospective cohort study (Xuzhou Medical University Affiliated Hospital, March-June 2026) assessed diagnostic performance of a novel portable bedside DXA for osteoporosis (WHO criterion: T-score ≤ −2.5). Outpatient peripheral and axial DXA served as reference comparators; peripheral DXA was not treated as diagnostic gold-standard, as WHO criteria rely primarily on central axial DXA. Methods In total, 140 patients (mean age 68.2 ± 10.5 years, 91.4% female) completed four DXA scans within 72 h. An independent composite reference was built from three conventional DXA modalities, strictly excluding bedside DXA to avoid incorporation bias. Each conventional DXA modality was assessed against a leave-one-out independent reference standard that excludes the index modality itself. Pairwise head-to-head analyses between modalities were interpreted as comparative agreement between measurement tools rather than absolute diagnostic accuracy. Supplementary sensitivity analysis used a central-DXA-only…

title: On Local Laplacian Energy of Graphs
abstract: For a simple graph $G$ with Laplacian eigenvalues $\mu_1 \ge \cdots \ge \mu_n$, and average degree $\bar d$, the Laplacian energy is defined by $\operatorname{LE}(G)=\sum_{i=1}^n \left|\mu_i-\bar d\right| .$ This paper studies how $\operatorname{LE}(G)$ changes when a single vertex is deleted. For $v\in V(G)$, the local Laplacian energy at $v$ is defined by $\operatorname{LEG}_G(v)=\operatorname{LE}(G)-\operatorname{LE}(G-v)$, and the total local Laplacian energy of $G$ is defined by $\operatorname{le}(G)=\sum_{v\in V(G)} \operatorname{LEG}_G(v)$. Using a trace-norm approach, we derive two-sided bounds for $\operatorname{LEG}_G(v)$, obtain computable Frobenius-norm inequalities, and refine global bounds for $\operatorname{le}(G)$ in terms of degree variance and extremal degrees. In addition, we present an algorithmic procedure, supported by numerical examples, for computing local Laplacian energy values.

title: From the workforce to the boardroom: firm feminisation and corporate renewable energy use
abstract: Purpose Drawing on similarity attraction, gender socialisation, homophily and upper echelon theories, this study aims to investigate the firm feminisation’s role in firms’ renewable energy use by examining the interactions among women employees, women executives and women directors in firms. Design/methodology/approach The authors study an international set of firms between 2007 and 2023 and run fixed-effects regression analysis. The endogeneity threat is mitigated through using a one-year lag model, two-stage least squares regression, propensity score matching and entropy balancing techniques. Findings The authors observe that women employees, executives and directors per se reinforce renewable energy use. More importantly, interactions between women employees and directors, women executives and directors and women employees and executives enhance firms’ renewable energy use. Further analysis shows that energy efficiency policies, environmental management teams and executive ESG compensation policies reinforce the positive effect of firm feminisation on renewable energy use. Finally, they find that this effect is stronger in countries with higher-quality institutions, particularly those with stronger public governance and greater economic development. Originality/value For the first time, by drawing on similarity attraction, gender socialisation, homophily and upper echelon th…

title: Enhancing Hydrate Exploitation from Reservoirs by Depressurization Combined with Electrical Resistance Heating
abstract: Abstract Natural gas hydrate (NGH) production by depressurization can be constrained by the temperature decline associated with endothermic hydrate dissociation and the resulting potential for secondary hydrate formation. To address these limitations, this study investigates electrical resistance heating (ERH), which generates Joule heat within hydrate-bearing sediments. A laboratory-scale electrical–thermal–hydraulic–chemical (ETHC) coupled model is developed, incorporating Joule heating, multiphase flow, heat transfer, and hydrate dissociation kinetics. Following validation against the Masuda core experiment, three production scenarios are compared: depressurization alone (Case A), depressurization combined with ERH (Case B), and depressurization combined with ERH and external thermal replenishment (Case C). Under a constant external boundary temperature of 273.15 K, gas production in Case A declines rapidly as dissociation-induced cooling inhibits further hydrate dissociation. ERH in Case B promotes dissociation within the core, although the same boundary temperature continues to constrain dissociation near the periphery. In Case C, raising the external boundary temperature to 280.15 K alleviates this constraint and promotes more spatially extensive hydrate dissociation. Compared with Case B, Case C increases the peak gas production rate by 64% and accelerates the dissociati…

title: Deep learning reconstruction and dual-energy CT in hepatocellular carcinoma: considerations for clinical translation
Building antifragile humanitarian supply chains: the role of transactive memory systems and big data analytics culture
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how big data analytics culture (BDAC) contributes to the development of antifragile humanitarian supply chains. Specifically, this study examines the mediating role of transactive memory systems (TMSs) and the moderating role of the frequency of natural disasters in the relationship between TMS and antifragility. Design/methodology/approach The authors collected 290 survey responses from key humanitarian professionals involved in disaster response operations. To test the proposed relationships among BDAC, TMS, antifragility and disaster frequency, the authors used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results of this study reveal that BDAC enhances antifragility only when fact-based decision-making improves information credibility, member specialization and coordination, core manifestations of TMS. TMS fully mediates the relationship between BDAC and antifragility, while the positive effect of TMS on antifragility is stronger in contexts with frequent natural disasters. Originality/value This paper advances the literature by empirically demonstrating TMS as the underlying mechanism linking BDAC to antifragility in humanitarian supply chains, showing how TMS operate as microfoundations of dynamic capabilities that enable collective sensing, coordinated decision-making and the reconfiguration of practices…

title: Energy development is a key driver of land cover dynamics in the Permian Basin, United States
abstract: Abstract The Permian Basin, which accounts for nearly half of U.S. oil production, has experienced substantial energy development activity over the past two decades. However, the extent of land cover dynamics driven by this expansion and associated biophysical impacts remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we utilized multi-temporal remote sensing data and geospatial information for areas surrounding more than 56 000 oil and gas wells in the basin to quantify shrubland to impervious surface transitions, changes in vegetation condition using the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and changes in surface reflectance using albedo from 2008 to 2024. We compared three-year pre-development (2008–2010) and post-development (2022–2024) composites and evaluated changes across buffer distances ranging from 50 m to 50 km around wells and paired control sites that remained stable shrublands throughout the study period. Results reveal highly concentrated land transformation near wells, where relatively small spatial footprints accounted for disproportionately large shares of shrubland to impervious surface transitions (e.g. 0.83% of basin area within 100 m of wells accounted for over 22% of basin-scale transitions). Transition rates were highest within 50 m of wells and declined with increasing distance. County-level regression models further confirmed the positive association …

title: Label-Declared Caffeine, Taurine, and Co-Ingredient Disclosure in 532 Energy Drinks: A Cross-Sectional Survey across Eleven Markets
abstract: Energy drinks are sold worldwide as a compositionally defined category, with no harmonized definition across jurisdictions. Typical concentrations have been reported market by market, but whether they are set product by product or held constant across a market, and whether the amounts determining co-ingredient exposure can be read from the label, remain unknown. This study examined label-declared caffeine and co-ingredient composition in a cross-sectional convenience sample of 532 commercially available ready-to-drink products from 43 brands across eleven markets with differing compositional and labeling regulations; products entered the sample where composition was published for the market concerned, so the findings describe the sampled products rather than national markets. One caffeine concentration recurred across the category, as did one taurine concentration among products stating an amount, held at the market level in several European markets, though not in the United States or Japan. The two varied independently, so the fixed ratio they appear to form is arithmetic rather than a formulation rule. Most co-ingredient declarations carried no amount, and the labeling regime, not the ingredient, decided whether one appeared, with quantification scarcest for constituents carrying published safety thresholds. Where a concentration is a market constant, intake is governed by th…

title: Participation in later life: how civic and political engagement relates to affective well-being
abstract: Inroduction Population ageing has emerged as one of the major demographic challenges of the 21st century, raising important concerns about how mental health can be sustained in later life. In Europe, increasing longevity intersects with social, economic, and institutional inequalities that shape older adults’ opportunities for well-being beyond the absence of disease. Although civic and political participation is widely promoted within active ageing agendas as a positive resource, it is often conceptualised as a homogeneous phenomenon, overlooking the possibility that different forms of engagement may have distinct psychological implications. Methods Using data from Round 11 of the European Social Survey (2023), this cross-sectional study examines adults aged 65 years and older across European countries. Affective well-being was operationalised using an index based on the CES-D8. Civic and political participation was captured through four sub-indices (Dutiful, Activating, Expressive and Cooperative profiles) reflecting the typology proposed by Ekman and Amnå. A multiple linear regression model was estimated, controlling for sociodemographic, economic and health-related factors. Results The findings indicate that perceived health and household income are strongly associated with affective well-being. Cooperative participation shows the strongest positive association with affecti…

title: Factors influencing the social participation of individuals with disabilities
abstract: Despite international declarations promoting the social inclusion of persons with disabilities, recent research data confirm the persistence of negative attitudes among the general population toward this right of persons with disabilities. Models of disability have at times influenced the perceptions of policymakers, and today the human rights model is the one through which equality, dignity, and respect for the rights of all people, regardless of social status, identity, ethnicity, or health status (Article 1, CRPD). Based on this model, a research tool was developed to identify the factors that influence the social inclusion of persons with disabilities. Two hundred and forty-four people participated, aged 20–60, from various professional groups. Data analysis was conducted using exploratory, parallel, and confirmatory factor analysis, which yielded three distinct factors: (a) social interaction, (b) negative attitudes, and (c) need for social inclusion.

title: Students’ Participation in Interdisciplinary Activities (Art, Culture, Sports, and Mathematics): Design, Implementation and Evaluation of a Holistic Educational Intervention
abstract: The present study investigates the design, implementation, and evaluation of interdisciplinary educational activities in primary education, aiming to enhance experiential learning and students’ active participation. The activities included art, culture, sports, and mathematics-related tasks, integrated within a student-centered teaching framework. The research adopted a mixed-methods approach, involving 17 primary school teachers. Data were collected through a questionnaire and qualitative tools and were analyzed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis. The findings revealed a high level of teacher satisfaction (88.3%) and a significant enhancement in students’ participation, collaboration, creativity, and critical thinking. The results highlight the contribution of interdisciplinary and experiential approaches to improving the learning process and emphasize the need for the systematic integration of such practices into the school curriculum.

Ultrastable Cycling of Sodium Metal Battery at Rates Exceeding 20 C Achieved with a NaB3H8-SiO2 Composite Solid Electrolyte
abstract: Abstract Solid-state sodium metal batteries are promising candidates for grid-scale energy storage due to their inherent safety and low cost. However, the development of solid electrolytes that support high-rate (>20 C) cycling for fast-charging applications remains a major challenge. Herein, we explore how adding SiO2 affects the ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression of NaB3H8, to develop superior solid electrolytes for high-rate batteries. The composites featuring an amorphous passivating layer with B–O bonds were fabricated via ball milling. Among them, NaB3H8-40%SiO2 exhibits the best conductivity, reaching 0.62 mS cm–1 at 25 °C, 2 orders of magnitude higher than that of pristine NaB3H8. Crucially, by reducing electronic conductivity and enhancing mechanical strength, it possesses a high critical current density of up to 6.5 mA cm–2, significantly higher than that of other reported hydridoborates. The Na/NaB3H8-40%SiO2/TiS2 batteries exhibit superior rate capability (216.4 mAh g–1 at 1 C and 143.1 mAh g–1 at 20 C) and long-term cycling stability (nearly 100.0% capacity retention after 2000 cycles at 20 C) at 30 °C. This work offers a promising approach for the development of innovative solid electrolytes in fast-charging or high-power-density sodium metal batteries.

title: Business Structure and Environmental Sustainability Strategy in China's EV Battery Industry: A Comparative Case Study of CATL and BYD
abstract: This study examines how business structure shapes the design and implementation of environmental sustainability strategies in China's EV-battery industry by comparing CATL, a specialised battery supplier, with BYD, a vertically integrated battery-and-vehicle producer. Using a qualitative comparative case-study design, it analyses corporate ESG and annual reports, official policy documents, academic literature and market-share data from 2023 to mid-2025. Drawing on sustainable supply chain management, global value-chain governance and the natural-resource-based view, the analysis identifies two overlapping coordination pathways. CATL's model is associated with more formalised inter-organisational carbon governance, supplier coordination and product-footprint accounting. BYD's integration supports closer links among battery-vehicle design, manufacturing efficiency and internal energy management, while still requiring upstream supplier governance. Market leadership can amplify implementation capacity but does not measure sustainability. The study shows that organisational boundaries shape where sustainability decisions and capabilities are coordinated across the value chain.

title: Biomass-Assisted Hydrometallurgy and Pyrometallurgy for Sustainable Recovery of Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Cathodes
abstract: Abstract Biomass-assisted metallurgy, defined as an umbrella term encompassing recycling technologies that utilize biomass in any form (living microorganisms, biomass-derived chemical compounds, or thermally converted biomass products) as lixiviants, reductants, and/or energy sources, has emerged as a cost-effective, sustainable, and carbon-neutral approach for recovering critical metals from spent lithium-ion battery (LIB) cathodes. Unlike previous reviews that address bioleaching or organic-acid leaching separately, this review establishes a unified framework categorizing biomass-assisted recycling into three distinct technological routes: (i) microbial bioleaching, where acidophilic bacteria (Acidithiobacillus spp.) and fungi (Aspergillus niger) generate biogenic acids and oxidants to solubilize metals via acidolysis and redoxolysis; (ii) biomass reduction leaching, where biomass-derived substances (e.g., polyphenols, reducing sugars, organic acids) serve as green reductants to replace hazardous H2O2, enabling efficient metal extraction under mild conditions; and (iii) biomass reduction roasting, where lignocellulosic wastes provide reducing gases (e.g., H2, CO) and biochar for in or ex situ carbothermal reduction, enabling selective lithium recovery as water-soluble Li2CO3. The distinctive contribution lies in the synergistic valorization strategy─biomass wastes (e.g., lign…

title: Mixed –N/–O Surface Terminations Enable Fast Ammonium-Ion Storage in Ti3C2T x MXene
abstract: Abstract Aqueous ammonium-ion batteries are promising for safety, low cost, and fast energy storage. However, the influence of electrode surface chemistry on NH4+ storage remains poorly understood. Two-dimensional Ti3C2Tx MXene, with metallic conductivity, tunable interlayer spacing, and abundant surface terminations, serves as an ideal platform to elucidate NH4+ storage mechanisms. Herein, the role of MXene surface termination in regulating NH4+ storage behavior is systematically investigated using density functional theory calculations and experimental validation. The calculations reveal that the –N terminations offer moderate NH4+ adsorption and high electronic conductivity for rapid charge transfer and ion transport, whereas the –O terminations exhibit stronger ion affinity and enhanced surface stability. Importantly, the mixed –N/–O terminations effectively balance adsorption strength and transition-state stabilization, resulting in the lowest NH4+ migration barrier among the modeled pathways. The calculations employ idealized vacuum-separated surfaces with isolated NH4+ and do not explicitly include solvation or electrolyte effects. Guided by these findings, a mixed –N/–O terminated Ti3C2Tx MXene is constructed via a urea-assisted hydrothermal strategy. The optimized NTC-20 electrode delivers 107 mAh g–1 at 1 A g–1, retains 67% capacity at 10 A g–1, and maintains 91% capa…

title: Mapping the knowledge of scientific production on the ALPHA-Fitness battery at school age: bibliometric analysis (2010–2025)
abstract: Introduction Numerous studies have used the Assessing Levels of Physical Activity and Fitness (ALPHA) battery to evaluate physical fitness (PF) and its positive impact on the health of school-age children, assessing various components of fitness. Despite its widespread use, no bibliometric review has systematically examined research trends or scientific output related to the ALPHA-Fitness battery. This study aimed to conduct a bibliometric review to identify research trends on the ALPHA-Fitness battery. Materials and methods Theoretical study using bibliometrics as a research technique, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) methodology. A total of 266 documents published between January 1, 2010, and February 28, 2025, were identified in the Web of Science, Scopus, and PubMed databases and analyzed using VOSviewer software (v.1.6.19). The search was independently reviewed and verified by two researchers. The final search equation applied was (Alpha fitness test OR alpha fitness battery OR Alpha-fitness test OR fitness alpha test OR alpha fitness test battery AND physical fitness). Results The final sample consisted of 266 documents, mostly published as research articles (98.87%). Scientific output was highest between 2019 and 2024 ( n = 184), with 2019 also recording the most citations ( n = 807), followed by 2017 ( n = 767). L…

TUNGVLM: A High-Efficiency Structured-Output Multimodal Framework For Vehicle Recognition
abstract: Vehicle make, model, and color recognition (MMCR) is a critical perception task in intelligent transportation systems (ITS), requiring both high accuracy and low latency. While recent vision-language models provide strong semantic representation capabilities, their autoregressive decoding process introduces semantic uncertainty and substantial computational overhead, limiting real-time deployment. To address these challenges, we propose TungVLM, a deterministic multimodal framework for efficient vehicle recognition. The proposed architecture reformulates the language backbone as a global semantic stabilizer to enhance semantic consistency and robustness, while a make-guided hierarchical classification head design guides the model toward fine-grained discrimination among visually similar vehicle models. To improve domain generalization, global-scale vehicle datasets are jointly optimized with real-world Taiwanese vehicle imagery. Experimental results on the unseen CHNTU surveillance dataset demonstrate an exact match accuracy of 81.29% with only 129 ms inference latency, outperforming GPT-4o (71.53%) and Florence-2 (50.13%). These results validate the effectiveness of TungVLM for real-time, high-throughput ITS applications.

title: Micronization-assisted pulsed electric field treatment on functional and structural modification of red pepper seed protein isolates
abstract: Background Red pepper seeds are an underutilized source of plant proteins with functional potential, but their poor solubility and limited functionality restrict food applications. This study investigated the effects of micronization-assisted pulsed electric field (PEF) treatment on the structural, physicochemical, and functional properties of red pepper seed protein isolates (RPSPIs). Methods RPSPIs were subjected to micronization pretreatment followed by PEF treatment under different electric field strengths and processing conditions. The effects of combined treatment on surface hydrophobicity, turbidity, Free Sulfhydryl (SH) Content, particle size distribution, surface morphology, secondary conformation, thermal stability, solubility, emulsifying properties, and foaming characteristics were systematically evaluated. Structural modifications were characterized using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), fluorescence spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC). Results The combined treatment significantly impacted the functional properties, including zeta potential and particle size of RPSPI-treated samples, enhancing stability compared to control samples. The structural data revealed important molecular modifications, including enhanced SH − content and reduced fluorescence intensity,…

title: Pedestrian interaction with highly automated vehicles in shared spaces: the roles of vehicle kinematics, external human–machine interfaces, and social cues
abstract: Abstract Highly automated vehicles (HAVs; SAE Levels 4–5) will increasingly operate in mixed traffic, raising challenges for pedestrian interaction—especially in shared-space environments where coordination relies on negotiation rather than formal right-of-way rules. Prior research has largely examined one-to-one pedestrian–HAV encounters, while the role of social cues from additional pedestrians remains underexplored. This study investigated how pedestrians integrate (a) an additional pedestrian’s behavior (absent vs. present–stopping vs. present–continuing to walk), (b) vehicle kinematics of the HAV (yielding vs. non-yielding), and (c) a visual light-based external human-machine interface (eHMI; present vs. absent) when forming willingness to cross and perceived safety in a shared-space scenario. In a video-based online experiment ( N = 136; 3 × 2 × 2 within-subjects), participants rated willingness to cross and perceived safety after each 9-s rendered video clip. Vehicle kinematics had a strong influence on both willingness to cross and perceived safety. The eHMI increased willingness to cross and perceived safety under yielding kinematics, but had no effect under non-yielding kinematics, indicating that eHMIs are beneficial primarily when congruent with vehicle kinematics. Additional pedestrian behavior affected both willingness to cross and perceived safety, but only when …

Traversability assessment for wheeled vehicles using point cloud data with vehicle geometric and kinematic constraints
abstract: Subject of research: simulation and mathematical modeling methods for robot mechanics, algorithms for constructing cross-country maps, and methods for identifying and integrating the characteristics of a specific wheeled platform. Purpose of research: a method for constructing a global obstacle map that takes into account the interaction of a wheeled vehicle platform with terrain. Research methods: methods of terrain traversability analysis, simulation modeling, processing of sensory data, formalization of obstacle criteria and geometric constraints. Objects of research: the process of constructing an adaptive obstacle map for wheeled vehicles taking into account the interaction of the platform with the terrain. Research findings: a method for constructing a comprehensive assessment of the cross-country ability of an environment has been developed, taking into account the design and kinematic characteristics of the platform and the geometric properties of the environment.

title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.

title: From Green Approval to Purchase Readiness: Malaysia’s Electric Vehicle Adoption Conversion Problem
abstract: Electric vehicles have moved from a niche technology to a central instrument of transport decarbonisation, yet Malaysian consumer adoption remains modest relative to policy ambition. This narrative review argues that the persistent gap is best understood as a conversion problem: general approval of cleaner mobility becomes purchase intention only when consumers judge the vehicle to be worth its sacrifices and believe that purchase and use are practically controllable. The review integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior with the Value-Based Adoption Model and critically synthesises Malaysian and international evidence on economic, environmental, functional, symbolic, and experiential benefits; vehicle, battery, charging, and behavioural barriers; and the conditional roles of environmental concern and government incentives. The literature converges on the importance of attitude and perceived value but conflicts over subjective norm, perceived behavioural control, infrastructure, environmental concern, and incentives. These disagreements are traced to differences in market stage, respondent experience, vehicle definition, policy design, model specification, and the widespread use of cross-sectional intention measures. A value–control conversion framework is proposed in which environmental concern changes benefit salience, whereas incentives and infrastructure primarily change aff…
