Business Portfolio Diversification and AI-driven Growth Strategy: Case Study of Microsoft
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, large-scale technology firms generally face the challenge of balancing the stability of mature businesses with new growth opportunities. Taking Microsoft as an example, this paper discusses the relationship between business portfolio diversification and AI-driven growth strategy. This article focuses on how Microsoft can maintain revenue stability through its business segments—such as productivity software, cloud computing, personal computing, and gaming—while also creating new growth opportunities through AI-related businesses. This paper uses a case study approach, along with Microsoft annual reports, investor information, and public market data, to analyze business-segment revenue, AI-related growth, stock returns, volatility and market risk characteristics. This article does not regard AI as an independent product, but analyzes how it is embedded in Microsoft's overall business portfolio through Azure, Microsoft 365, GitHub and other channels. The results show that Microsoft's diversified business segments provide a relatively stable revenue base for AI‑driven growth, while cloud computing and AI-related businesses further enhance the company's growth potential. From 2021 to 2025, Microsoft's cumulative return and annualized return were 131.53% and 18.33%, respectively, higher than the S&P 500's 84.98% and 13.12%; howev…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Multi-factor Stock Selection Strategy: Value, Profitability, and Momentum
abstract: This study examines whether sequentially combining value, profitability, and momentum improves stock-selection performance in the U.S. equity market. Utilize company-level accounting and monthly return data from Compustat and Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP) to build annually rebalanced, equally weighted portfolios of the 600 largest eligible firms over the 2016-2024 formation period for the analysis. Stocks are first screened by book-to-market ratio, then by return on equity, and finally by 12–1 momentum. Portfolio performance is shown by annualized return, volatility, the return-to-volatility ratio and maximum drawdown. The added factors do not always improve performance, according to the results. The value portfolio has an annual return of 10.39%, rises slightly to 10.74% after adding profitability, and then falls to 10.36% after the momentum screen. All factor-screened portfolios underperform the 11.50% return of the Top-600 benchmark and have higher volatility and larger drawdowns. Robustness tests using gross profit-to-assets and earnings-to-price also show that the results are sensitive to factor definitions and screening order. These findings caution against assuming that greater model complexity necessarily enhances performance. Overall, multi-factor performance depends on factor measurement, sequencing, and portfolio concentration.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Course reassignment and learning engagement: the intervention strategy of AI-attributed reassignment
abstract: Introduction Course reassignment is a common practice in university registration systems, yet reassigned students often exhibit lower learning engagement than those in self-selected courses, and the underlying psychological mechanism remains unclear. This study examined the impact of course reassignment on learning engagement, the mediating role of self-efficacy, and the buffering effect of AI-attributed course reassignment. Methods Two scenario-based online experiments were conducted with university students randomly assigned to conditions. Experiment 1 ( N = 393) used a single-factor between-subjects design comparing reassignment vs. self-selection. Experiment 2 ( N = 293) added an AI-attributed reassignment condition in which an AI engine matched students' interests, traits, and abilities with the most suitable available courses (participants in the AI condition read a simulated AI-generated learning analysis report.). Participants completed a learning task and reported learning engagement and self-efficacy. Mediation analyses were conducted using bootstrapping. Results Experiment 1 showed that course reassignment was associated with lower learning engagement compared with self-selection, and this effect was mediated by self-efficacy (indirect effect B = 0.198, SE = 0.051, 95%CI [0.096, 0.299]). Experiment 2 demonstrated that AI-attributed reassignment attenuated this negati…

title: Introverting as a route into reflective practice for leadership
abstract: Purpose To consider the value and process of introverting and Moments of Introverting (MOIs) for leadership practice. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative, including visual methods. Findings Moments of Introverting (MOIs) help balance contrasting leadership demands. Originality/value The research shows the value of processification to stretch understanding of a personality trait and the value of MOIs for leadership development.

title: Bio-inspired Air-Shield Strategy Enables Zero-Contact Repellency
abstract: Abstract Minimizing interfacial liquid–solid contact is central to self-cleaning and protective fabrics, yet passive microtextures generally permit transient contact during impact. Here, we demonstrate a bio-inspired airflow-mediated strategy that converts superhydrophobic fabrics from passive low-adhesion surfaces into pressure-programmable active repellent interfaces. This strategy is implemented by covalently anchoring continuous nanoscale superhydrophobic shells onto the microscale fibers, which maintains a low-adhesion interfacial Cassie-type wetting state at the nanoscale even after 20,000 abrasion cycles, 15,300 scrub resistance cycles, and 3000 bending cycles, and delivering airflow through interconnected fabric pores to supply a replenishable interfacial counter-pressure required for levitating and redirecting impacting droplets of 2–20 μL (equivalent spherical diameters ≈ 1.6–3.4 mm). A pressure-controlled sequence is resolved from contact rebound to suspended rebound and finally to an operational zero-contact rebound, defined as no liquid–solid contact. Compared with conventional optical imaging, synchrotron X-ray imaging at 10,000 frames s–1 with 2 μm spatial resolution enhanced the detection resolution. Nanostructure-reinforced surface superhydrophobicity reduces interfacial adhesion and pore-invasion risks and provides fail-safe repellency below the zero-contact a…

title: Encapsulation Strategy Suppresses Cadmium Release from Ceramic Pigment Toward Robust Porcelain Applications
Mills Brand Marketing Communication Strategy in Increasing Brand Awareness Through Instagram Social Media
abstract: Background: This study analyzes Mills' marketing communication strategy in increasing brand awareness through Instagram social media. Method: A qualitative case study design was employed because the research focuses on communication processes, strategic meanings, and audience engagement in a real-life digital context. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with key informants, observation of Mills' Instagram content, and documentation of posts, captions, visual elements, and audience interactions. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing, supported by source triangulation and member checking. Results: The findings show that Mills uses Instagram as a strategic communication infrastructure by integrating structured content planning, consistent visual identity, influencer and athlete collaboration, active audience interaction, and performance-based evaluation. These elements strengthen brand awareness by increasing repeated exposure, reinforcing recognition, supporting recall, and building associative positioning in the sports apparel market. Conclusion: The study provides practical benefits for sports apparel brands that need to manage digital communication consistently and theoretical benefits for integrated marketing communication studies in social media environments.

title: Effect of Blended Learning Strategy on Learning Motivation of Early Childhood Education Pupils in Katsina State, Nigeria
abstract: Purpose: This study examined the effect of a blended learning strategy on the learning motivation of Early Childhood Education (ECE) pupils in Katsina State, Nigeria. Methodology: The research utilized a pre-test, post-test, non-randomized control group quasi-experimental design involving 188 ECE pupils (105 males, 83 females) selected through multi-stage sampling from public primary schools in Dutsin-Ma Zonal Education Quality Assurance (ZEQA). The experimental group (n=96) received six weeks of literacy and numeracy instruction via a WhatsApp-mediated flipped classroom model, while the control group (n=92) was taught using conventional face-to-face instruction. Data were collected using the Adapted Motivational Strategies for Learning Questionnaire (AMSLQ) and analyzed using paired-sample t-tests, independent-sample t-tests, and Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) in SPSS at an α=.05 significance level. Findings: Findings revealed a statistically significant increase in pupils' motivation scores within the experimental group following the intervention (t(95)=-19.41,p<.001). Furthermore, ANCOVA results demonstrated that after controlling for pre-test motivation scores, pupils taught using the blended learning strategy exhibited significantly higher post-test motivation scores than those taught using conventional methods (F(1,185)=7.490,p=.007). Additionally, no statistically signi…

title: Stereodefect Strategy Enables Thermally Resilient, Rapidly Crystallizable, High-Performance Aliphatic Polyester Thermoplastic Elastomers
abstract: Abstract Stereoblock star aliphatic polyester thermoplastic elastomers (APTPEs) comprised of poly(d-lactide)-b-poly(l-lactide)-b-poly(γ-methyl-ε-caprolactone) ((DLM)4) rapidly crystallize to give strong, tough, and resilient APTPEs. However, the high melting temperature of the stereocomplex formed in these materials (Tm ≈ 220 °C) is close to the onset temperature for thermally induced mass loss (Td,1% ≈ 230 °C). This decomposition of the polyester is likely due to depolymerization from the ends of the polymer chain. Here, we report the synthesis of APTPE stars containing stereodefective poly(lactide) end diblocks, that is poly(l-lactide) covalently bonded to a poly(d-lactide) segment that is intentionally doped with a small percentage of l-lactide defects. Incorporating a low level of stereodefects leads to a modest reduction in Tm, while maintaining high levels of crystallinity and rapid stereoblock crystallization rates. The resultant materials have physical properties that are nearly identical to stereoblock star polymers without defects but allow melt processing below the temperature at which significant mass loss begins to occur. To prepare these star block polymers, we also conducted the synthesis in a one-pot, one-catalyst system, aligning the process with the principles of green chemistry.

title: Disney's Location Strategy in China: Balancing Global Brand Identity and Local Adaptation
abstract: Multinational companies face a persistent tension between maintaining a consistent global brand identity and adapting to local consumer preferences. Disney's long-term presence in China provides a useful observation sample for examining this issue. Since the opening of Shanghai Disneyland in 2016, Disney has accumulated substantial operational experience in the Chinese market. This article examines how Disney has adapted to the Chinese market while maintaining its core brand identity. The paper employs PESTEL analysis and the theory of global localization to examine the challenges. Disney has encountered in policy, culture and competition, and analyzes its responses, including incorporating Chinese elements into the park, creating new characters for Chinese audiences, and cooperating with local enterprises. Existing research suggests that Disney's performance in China is not simply the result of cultural export but reflects an approach based on global localization. This study further examines this localization strategy and provides theoretical insights and practical references for cultural enterprises seeking to enter the Chinese market.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Pathways to sustainable business model transformation: corporate governance, strategic leadership and business strategy
abstract: Purpose In today’s rapidly evolving business environment, firms face increasing pressure to adopt sustainable practices, with the circular economy (CE) model emerging as a transformative pathway toward environmental and economic resilience. This study aims to investigate the role of governance mechanisms, particularly board and chief executive officer (CEO) dynamics, in enhancing CE performance among manufacturing firms in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. In addition, it examines the moderating role of business strategy in the relationship between governance mechanisms and CE performance, with a focus on innovation, resource efficiency and operational sustainability. Design/methodology/approach The analysis uses panel data from 6,929 firm-year observations and applies dynamic panel estimation techniques, including the system generalized method of moments, to assess the effects of governance, leadership and strategy on CE performance. To strengthen causal inference and ensure robustness, this study incorporates lagged variables, two-stage least squares, propensity score matching and generalized least squares. Findings The results show that board interlock, independence, expertise, CEO foreign experience and external roles significantly enhance CE performance, while concentrated ownership and long CEO tenure constrain it. Business strategy acts as both a direct dri…

title: Porous Polyacrylamide Electrolytes with Improved Ionic Conductivity for Long-Cycle-Life and High-Power-Density Flexible Zinc–Air Batteries
abstract: Abstract Polyacrylamide (PAM) hydrogels are simple to prepare under readily controllable conditions, making them suitable for the large-scale production of high-quality electrolytes. However, when used in zinc–air batteries, continuous water evaporation through the semi-open battery structure causes electrolyte desiccation, reduced ionic conductivity, and increased interfacial contact resistance, ultimately limiting battery performance and cycle life. To address this issue, a porous NaHCO3/PAM hydrogel electrolyte was prepared using a establishes gas-foaming method. NaHCO3 was introduced as an additive and thermally decomposed to generate CO2, producing a highly uniform pore structure. The resulting hydrogel exhibited a more uniform internal pore structure and enhanced electrolyte absorption. Consequently, the resultant flexible zinc–air battery demonstrates a superior peak power density of 163.9 mW cm–2 and an extended cycle life of 81.7 h. This study not only provides establishes a paradigm for designing anti-desiccation hydrogel electrolytes but also paves the way for the development of durable flexible energy storage devices.

title: How power advantage and digital intelligence reconfigure green supply chain efficiency: a dynamic QCA approach
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how different dimensions of power advantage and digital intelligence combine to shape green supply chain (GSC) efficiency. Design/methodology/approach Using data from 140 Chinese listed manufacturing enterprises over the period 2015–2023, this study applies dynamic qualitative comparative analysis (QCA) to comprehensively examine the configurations associated with GSC efficiency. Findings Four configurations can lead to high GSC efficiency: market synergy management, organizational change leading, ecological network empowerment and professional authority allocation. The sufficiency of the four configurations exhibits limited temporal variation as policy and market conditions evolve. The first three configurations show greater empirical relevance among high-end equipment manufacturing enterprises, whereas the fourth configuration is more relevant among enterprises outside this industry and those located in non-key environmental protection cities. Additionally, configurations leading to low GSC efficiency result from mismatches and imbalances among antecedent conditions and are not symmetric with those leading to high GSC efficiency. Originality/value Drawing on power-dependence theory and complex systems theory, this study develops a configurational framework that treats market, technology and network power advantages, digital-intelligent equipmen…

title: Effects of plyometric vs. traditional resistance training on kick performance and anaerobic power in elite taekwondo athletes
abstract: Background Taekwondo requires high-velocity kicking actions and repeated explosive efforts, which depend heavily on lower-body power and stretch-shortening cycle function. Plyometric training may offer greater improvements in these demands than traditional heavy-resistance training, but direct evidence in elite taekwondo athletes is limited. Objective This study compared the effects of 8 weeks of plyometric training and traditional resistance training on roundhouse kick performance, lower-body maximal strength, and anaerobic power in elite male taekwondo athletes. Methods Twenty-four elite male taekwondo athletes (age 18–24 years, body mass 58–68 kg) were randomly assigned to either a plyometric training group ( n = 12) or a traditional resistance training group ( n = 12). Elite status was defined as holding a National First-Class Athlete certification and having won a provincial championship or placed in the top three at a national-level competition. Both groups trained twice per week for 8 weeks in addition to their regular taekwondo training. Before and after the intervention, participants were assessed for squat one-repetition maximum (1RM), roundhouse kick speed, kick power, 20-second continuous kick repetitions, countermovement jump (CMJ) height, reactive strength index (RSI), and Wingate peak and mean power. Data were analyzed using two-way repeated-measures ANOVA. Resul…
venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: How consumers transition between illicit and legal cannabis markets following the implementation of licensed recreational cannabis retail sales: evidence from a national panel with a recent policy shock
abstract: Abstract Introduction States across the US continue to legalize recreational cannabis to shift consumers from illicit to regulated markets. Yet evidence on whether the implementation of licensed recreational retail markets increases the share of cannabis obtained legally remains limited. This study examines how the implementation of recreational cannabis retail sales influences cannabis sourcing behavior using nationally representative panel data and recent policy variation. Methods We use three waves of panel survey data collected in June 2024 (pre-retail sales), January 2025, and August 2025. The analytic sample is a balanced panel of 578 adults (1,734 observations). We estimate difference-in-differences models of the proportion of cannabis obtained from legal sources, exploiting the implementation of recreational cannabis retail sales in Ohio in August 2024 within a multi-state context. Models controlled for baseline policy status, demographics, and survey wave fixed effects. Results Legal sourcing varies substantially across policy environments. Individuals residing in states with fully legal cannabis markets report significantly higher reliance on legal sources than those in fully illegal states (31.6 percentage points, p < 0.001). Exploiting the implementation of licensed recreational cannabis retail sales in Ohio, we find a 5.3 percentage-point increase in the share of c…

title: The Economic and Social Effects of Widely Adopted Technology-Driven Personalised Pricing
abstract: Digital technology enables firms to implement personalised pricing based on consumers' willingness to pay, which is widely recognised as a modern form of first-degree price discrimination. This study explores the multifaceted economic and social consequences of the large-scale adoption of personalised pricing. Adopting a cost-benefit analytical framework, the research conducts a cross-country comparison covering developed and emerging Asian economies, utilising macroeconomic indicators including gross domestic product, unemployment rates and Gini coefficients to analyse relevant market and distributional effects. The results demonstrate that widespread personalised pricing can improve static and dynamic market efficiency by eliminating deadweight loss and stimulating corporate innovation. Nevertheless, without effective regulatory constraints, algorithmic pricing practices may aggravate income inequality due to information asymmetry and inaccurate consumer profiling. In addition, unfair pricing perceptions erode consumer trust and may offset efficiency benefits. This paper concludes that personalised pricing presents an inherent trade-off between market efficiency and social equity. Its final socioeconomic outcomes hinge on robust competition regulatory systems that restrain exploitative pricing behaviour.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: The Impacts of Widespread Personalized Pricing in Digital Markets
abstract: Digital technologies can help platforms to develop a personalised pricing model, which involves gathering and analysing multidimensional data about consumers. This paper explores the economic, ethical and social implications of the implementation of personalised pricing in digital markets. The research is based on a number of examples of commercial platforms, including Ctrip, Amazon, Target and Pinduoduo, and recent empirical and theoretical research, to examine the theoretical efficiency gains from neoclassical economic concepts and the actual market outcomes. The analysis is carried out on four aspects: procedural unfairness because of price discrimination, risk of privacy violations because of the intensive monitoring of consumers' data, psychological manipulation of consumer preferences by algorithms, and allocative efficiency in theory versus reality. The results show that while in theory personalised pricing can remove the deadweight loss and enhance the allocation of resources, widespread information asymmetry and opaque algorithmic systems and mass data extraction reduce the potential benefits. The widespread adoption will further increase market inequality, reduce consumer privacy, affect consumer choice, and allow for further concentration of market power by large digital platforms. Finally, such pricing policies are at odds with the desire to promote general social w…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Monte Carlo Simulation for Pricing Asian Call Options: Evidence from Apple Inc.
abstract: This paper estimates the value of a 30-day fixed-strike arithmetic Asian call option on Apple Inc. (AAPL) using Monte Carlo simulation under a risk-neutral geometric Brownian motion framework (GBM). The AAPL contract is used as a case study and is not presented as an actual listed Asian option. The model uses a starting stock price of $333.26, a $335 strike, a 4.15% risk-free rate, a 0.3241% dividend yield, 30% annual volatility, 30 daily observations, and 250 simulated paths. The base-case arithmetic Asian call value is $5.7317, compared with $11.2107 for a matched European call. The results show that averaging reduces the effect of large movements near maturity and lowers the option value in this case. Sensitivity tests also show that both option values rise with volatility and fall as the strike increases, while the European call reacts more strongly to volatility. The paper also discusses simulation error and the limits of the constant-volatility GBM assumption.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Information Advantage, Differentiated Pricing and Consumer Surplus: Algorithm Driven Dynamic Pricing of Online Ride Hailing Platforms
abstract: With the development of digital platforms, algorithmic dynamic pricing has been gradually applied to ride‑hailing and other markets. Taking ride‑hailing platforms as the research object, this paper analyzes how platforms leverage consumer demand differences and information advantages to implement dynamic pricing based on third‑degree price discrimination, two‑sided market theory and game theory, and discusses its impacts on market equilibrium and consumer surplus. The differences in consumers' willingness to pay and price elasticity provide the basis for the platform to implement differentiated pricing, and the information advantage of the platform further enhances its price adjustment ability. In the strategic interaction, dynamic pricing can not only adjust the relationship between supply and demand, but also transfer some consumer surplus to the platform. There are differences in the impact on high- and low-elasticity consumers. Therefore, this paper believes that dynamic pricing itself has a certain role in resource allocation, but when the advantages of algorithmic information are used for excessive differentiated pricing, it may damage consumer welfare. In this regard, regulatory measures including price constraints and algorithm information disclosure can curb the excessive expansion of platform pricing power while preserving the efficiency of dynamic pricing.
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Optimization of an Explainable Machine Learning Model for Customer Churn Prediction and Business Retention Strategy
abstract: Customer churn forecasting is critical for companies that want to identify potential churn customers and develop more targeted customer maintenance strategies. This study explores whether Bayesian optimization can improve the performance of machine learning in customer churn prediction, and whether explainable model output can provide useful business insights. This research used Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) to analyze the IBM Telecom customer churn data set containing 7,043 customer records. We applied Bayesian hyperparameter optimization to XGBoost by using five-fold hierarchical cross-validation, and used SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to explain the optimized model. The optimized XGBoost model achieves the Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.8424 and the Precision-Recall Area Under the Curve (PR-AUC) of 0.6518, and the recall rate also increased from 0.6408 in the baseline XGBoost model to 0.7721. SHAP analysis shows that the type of contract, user duration and Internet services are the most influential predictors. Risk segmentation further shows that there are significant differences in the churn rates of different customer groups. Research results show that combining model optimization with interpretable analysis helps to make more transparent …
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: From ambiguity to ownership: a reflective practitioner inquiry into team coaching in a global experiential learning environment
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how team coaching supported a student team in learning to organise itself under conditions of ambiguity, enabling collective ownership and shared leadership to emerge. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a reflective practitioner inquiry to examine coaching practice within a single team participating in the Global Business Challenge (GBC). Reflection was informed by programme artefacts generated through routine educational practice, including coaching session transcripts, client interactions, student reflections and other contemporaneous materials. An iterative, interpretive analysis developed a five-phase process-oriented account of how collective ownership and shared leadership emerged as the team learnt to organise itself. Findings The findings reveal a developmental trajectory from initial ambiguity and dependence toward increasing collective ownership and shared leadership. Team coaching did not resolve ambiguity but sustained it as a condition for learning, prompting the team to develop its own ways of organising. Originality/value This paper develops a process-oriented, practice-based account of how coaching supported teams to organise themselves under conditions of ambiguity, enabling collective ownership and shared leadership to emerge.

title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning with Dynamic Cost-Sensitive Random Forest for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis of Diesel Engines
abstract: Reliable identification of incipient degradation is critical to the durability and functional integrity of diesel engines. However, diagnosis is challenged by scarce degradation labels, severe class imbalance, and heterogeneous multi-source monitoring data. This study proposes a selfsupervised contrastive learning with dynamic cost-sensitive random forest (SSCL-DCSRF) framework for intelligent fault diagnosis with a focus on wear- and lubrication-related degradation states. Rather than directly measuring surface morphology, roughness, residual stress, or wear loss, the proposed method identifies operating states associated with surface-related degradation from multi-source monitoring data. A physically consistent view-generation strategy preserves operating-condition semantics and cross-variable relationships, enabling robust representation learning from unlabeled data. A dynamic cost-sensitive random forest then integrates class frequency, feature-space dispersion, and prediction uncertainty to improve the recognition of minority and difficult-to-classify states. Experiments on a multi-source diesel-engine fault dataset demonstrate that SSCL-DCSRF outperforms representative machine-learning methods in class-balanced diagnostic performance, with enhanced sensitivity to early wear and lubrication-related degradation. The proposed framework provides an effective data-driven appro…

title: Learning from student-led interdisciplinary projects: a lesson study–informed practice-based inquiry into mentorship, failure and motivation
abstract: Purpose This study reports a practice-based inquiry into student-led interdisciplinary projects in secondary computer science education, using a lesson study (LS)–informed practitioner inquiry stance to examine how teacher mentoring sustains student agency and motivation when experimental outcomes are unsuccessful. Design/methodology/approach The study draws on a structured LS process conducted across one academic year by four subject teachers. Three cycles combined in-class diagnostic observation, joint observation of extracurricular project sessions and end-of-year synthesis. Five data streams were analysed through a three-pass iterative interpretive process with cross-source triangulation. Findings The focal case showed different patterns of student reasoning from the technically successful comparison case when mentoring reframed experimental failure as an epistemological resource. Motivation was sustained through autonomy, disciplinary relatedness and personal meaning rather than outcome validation. Competition outcomes provided external corroboration. After non-qualification for a national final, focal-case students independently diagnosed a robotics competence gap and developed a new project, providing evidence of self-directed learning agency following sustained LS-informed mentoring. Practical implications Four mentoring principles are proposed: agency-focused observati…
venue: International Journal for Lesson & Learning Studies

title: Integrated experimental and machine learning study on sustainable concrete incorporating fly ash and eco-sand
abstract: The construction industry faces increasing pressure to reduce carbon dioxide emissions and minimise dependence on conventional cement and natural fine aggregates, motivating the development of sustainable concretes incorporating industrial by-products. In this study, the combined use of fly ash (FA) and eco-sand (ES) as partial replacements for cement (0–25%) and fine aggregate (0–20%) was evaluated across 26 concrete mix designs. Experimental assessments included mechanical, durability and microstructural characterisation through tests for workability, strength, water absorption, porosity and acid resistance, along with scanning electron microscopy/energy-dispersive spectroscopy analysis. The results showed that the mix with 15% FA and 10% ES achieved the highest compressive strength of 39.1 MPa, representing a 10.8% improvement over the control mix. The mix with 20% FA and 15% ES exhibited enhanced durability with reduced porosity (6.5%), water absorption (1.42%) and acid-induced mass loss. To extend the experimental investigation and enable predictive performance assessment, machine learning models (including support vector regression with radial basis function (SVR-RBF), bagging SVR and Gaussian process regression) were developed using a 70:30 training–testing split and leave-one-out cross-validation. SVR-RBF achieved the highest predictive accuracy (coefficient of determin…

title: A Hybrid Temporal Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Depression Detection on Social Media
abstract: Depression is one of the most common mental health problems, as it influences mood, cognition, and quality of life. Social media offers an abundance of user-generated content that can be utilized to detect and track depressive tendencies at early stages. Conventional methods cannot always work to capture very complex temporal variations and other hidden contextual indicators within the unstructured social media data. To overcome these drawbacks, this research proposed the Neuro Thought Weave Mindstream Predictor (NTwMP), an atomistic hybrid temporal deep learning (DL) model that combines both long-term and short-term temporal modeling with a ThoughtWeave Attention mechanism. The NTwMP enables categorization of multi-level severity, abrupt deviation detection, and understandable predictions, which are useful in preventing mental health interventions. The model handles dynamic social media feeds in real-time with sliding time windows, which does not require retraining. Accuracy is 98.33%, which is considerably higher than that of existing DL methods. Other measures such as precision, recall, and F1-score also show excellent reliability and consistency. The main advantages are scalability, reproducibility, interpretability, and applicability in real-time, which makes it a strong and viable instrument to monitor depression trends and assist clinicians, caregivers, and automated sys…
venue: International Journal of Software Engineering and Knowledge Engineering

title: Neural Constrained Charge Equilibration for Extracting Charge Transport Parameters from Machine Learned Interatomic Potentials
abstract: Abstract Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) continue to gain popularity as efficient tools for predicting energies and forces for atomic structures at an accuracy comparable to quantum chemistry. However, there are limited trained MLIPs for certain important applications such as in charge transport. Accelerating and automating the determination of parameters for such applications can be of critical importance in the rapid discovery of materials such as organic electronics (e.g., OLEDs). This work develops and introduces neural constrained charge equilibriation (NcQEq) and applies the technique to AimNet2 and OrbMol-V2. The new method enables extracting information about the diabatic states and thereby charge transport parameters. The approach is demonstrated on model systems against constrained density functional theory charge transport and then tested on intramolecular hole transport properties for polyethylene. This work demonstrates that the NcQeq approach is compatible with the charge equilibration schemes for AimNet2 and the latent charge predictions of OrbMol-V2. After calibration to reference data, the method enables estimation of the electronic coupling, reorganization energy, and the free energy difference.

title: Free movement of dentists and life-long learning requirements within the countries of the European Economic Area: a scoping review of existing insights and future considerations
Professional learning communities as catalysts for writing teacher feedback literacy: a case study of two EFL secondary schools
abstract: Abstract Despite growing recognition of the importance of feedback literacy, limited attention has been paid to how teachers engage in professional learning to enhance their writing teacher feedback literacy (WTFL). To address this gap, this qualitative case study investigated the development of WTFL among teachers in two school-based professional learning communities (PLCs). Data were collected over one academic year from multiple sources, including interviews with four focal teachers, recordings of PLC meetings, classroom observations and documents, and student writing samples. Findings reveal that through participation in the PLCs, teachers expanded knowledge of feedback, reoriented values toward student agency, and strengthened abilities through practice innovation. Additionally, variations in WTFL development were shaped by individual, structural, and institutional factors. By uncovering the mechanisms through which PLCs foster WTFL and demonstrating their varied impact, this study advances understanding of the under-explored construct of WTFL, providing useful implications for classroom feedback practices and teacher education.
venue: International Review of Applied Linguistics in Language Teaching

title: Regenerative hospitality model using tourist municipalities using web scraping and unsupervised machine learning
abstract: Abstract Based on the research question: How can the regenerative hospitality actions undertaken by municipalities listed on the tourism map be classified? This study proposes a classification model for regenerative hospitality in Brazilian tourist municipalities. To achieve this aim, the study adopted a municipal-level adaptation of the regenerative dimensions proposed by Inversini et al. (2023), followed by the adapted model. Data were collected using natural language processing techniques, supported by a Python-based web‑scraping system that extracted text from municipal webpages listed on the National Confederation of Municipalities tourism map. The system gathered data, computed cosine similarity, vectorised the text, and compared the results against entries stored in a MySQL database, according to the dimensions of the regenerative hospitality model. The system obtained approximately 14,000 records and aggregated them by municipality, federative unit, and dimension. The dataset was then subjected to exploratory factor analysis using the principal components method with varimax rotation, which yielded two dimensions—socio‑environmental regeneration (X‑axis) and regenerative co‑creation (Y‑axis)—that explained 68% of the variance. K-means clustering was then applied, and the Elbow method indicated a three‑cluster solution: Cluster 1—Connectivity and Ideation, Cluster 2—Expa…

title: Technology-mediated feedback in instrumental music practice, performance, and learning: a systematic review of feedback architectures, performance outcomes, and effect-size feasibility
abstract: Introduction Technology-mediated feedback can support instrumental music performance during practice, but such gains do not necessarily indicate durable learning. This systematic review examined feedback architecture (information type, modality, timing, performance target, and function), performance outcomes, assessment conditions, and quantitative-synthesis feasibility. Methods Scopus, Répertoire International de Littérature Musicale (RILM) Abstracts of Music Literature, Web of Science Core Collection, APA PsycINFO, and ERIC were searched in May 2026 for empirical studies published since 2000 involving instrumental music learners across expertise levels. Quantitative and mixed-methods designs with learner-level performance data were eligible. Appraisal used the 2018 Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Findings were mapped and tabulated by design, comparator, feedback characteristics, and outcome domain, with reporting guided by Synthesis Without Meta-analysis. Results Of 1,689 records, 29 were retained in the record ledger; 27 formed the systematic-synthesis set and 26 the descriptive synthesis set. Learners ranged from novices to advanced musicians, principally in piano and bowed-string tasks. Among these 26 records, 21 included visual feedback and 18 delivered feedback concurrently. Movement, posture, or technique and rhythm or timing each accounted for 9 of 43 performance outcome…

title: Visual Attention Dynamics in Children with Special Needs During Eye-Tracking-Based Adaptive Learning Game Sessions in Pontianak, Indonesia
abstract: Background: Children with special needs (CSN), particularly those with attention disorders and autism spectrum conditions, may experience difficulty sustaining visual attention consistently. Eye-tracking technology allows visual attention to be measured objectively through eye-movement characteristics. Integrating eye tracking with an adaptive learning game has the potential to produce visual stimulation that is more responsive to individual user characteristics. Objective: This study aimed to analyze changes in visual-attention indicators of children with special needs across three measurement sessions using an eye-tracking-based adaptive learning game. Methods: This study used a quantitative approach with a one-group repeated-measures design. Sixteen children with special needs receiving services at the Disability Services and Assessment Center (LDAC) of Pontianak City served as subjects. Each participant underwent three measurement sessions on different days using an adaptive learning game system integrated with an eye tracker. The visual-attention indicators analyzed were mean fixation duration, saccade count, mean saccade distance, and gaze transition rate. Descriptive analysis was performed by calculating means and standard deviations. Differences across the three measurements were analyzed using the Friedman test, given the repeated-measures design on the same subjects. …

title: Instructional supervision and differentiated literacy learning for students with special needs in an inclusive school
abstract: Background-Principals in inclusive schools must supervise instruction for students with special needs (SEN), yet little is known about how supervision reaches differentiated literacy instruction where specialist staff are scarce. Objectives- This study analyzes how a principal, as supervisor and educator, manages the instructional program and oversees differentiated literacy learning for SEN students. Methods- An instrumental single-case study was conducted at SDN 8 Sintang, an inclusive elementary school in West Kalimantan, Indonesia. Participants included one principal, one classroom teacher, one special assistant teacher (SAT), and five SEN students. Interviews, observations, and documents were analyzed using NVivo 15. Results-Participants described scheduled supervision aimed at differentiation and a redefinition of literacy achievement as individual progress. Differentiation appeared divided between the classroom teacher (content) and the SAT (process and assessment), although observed collaboration was inconsistent and students' communication about reading content was limited. Reported barriers were structural: the SAT ratio, incomplete individualized education program documentation, and limited special-pedagogy training. Conclusions-Within this school, the principal's dual role was perceived to support differentiated literacy work; the findings are tentative given one in…

title: The Development of Micro Game-Based Learning Model on Intelligent Metaverse Learning Environment
abstract: This study aimed to synthesize, develop, and evaluate the Micro Game-Based Learning Model on Intelligent Metaverse Learning Environment. The study integrated Microlearning, Game-Based Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and Metaverse technologies to create a learning environment that provides short learning units, interactive game-based activities, and simulated communication situations. The research objectives were to (1) synthesize the learning process, (2) develop the learning model, and (3) evaluate the learning model. The evaluation panel consisted of three experts from various academic institutions. The experts were selected based on their experience at least 3 years in education, instructional design and development, particularly in teaching English for communication. The research instruments consisted of the learning model, learning platform, and an expert evaluation questionnaire based on a 5-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics according to the research objectives. The findings indicated that the appropriateness of the developed learning model was evaluated at a highest level (Mean = 4.93, SD = 0.24). The findings suggest that integrating Microlearning, Game-Based Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and an Intelligent Metaverse Learning Environment provides a feasible approach for developing technology-supported English com…

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Coordinated Emergency Building Sweeps
abstract: We develop a Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) framework for coordinating emergency responders during building sweeps. The problem is formulated as a Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (Dec-POMDP) that captures building topology, occupant vulnerability, dynamic hazards, and partial observability. In the six-room office baseline, MADDPG reaches a 134-second sweep time after 5,000 episodes, within 6.3% of the 126-second theoretical optimum and outperforming PPO and DQN. Extensions to a two-story school and a U-shaped warehouse achieve 120 seconds with five responders and 105 seconds with four responders, respectively, with diminishing returns beyond these staffing levels. Under communication failure, coverage remains about 98% while sweep time rises 15–20%; reduced staffing triggers workload redistribution, and dynamic hazards cause threatened areas to be prioritized. Occupancy sensing, mesh networks, and environmental sensing are projected to reduce sweep time by 35–50%. Sensitivity analysis confirms robust performance across realistic parameter ranges.

title: The profile of secondary education teachers in relation to the degree of utilization of digital learning objects in the educational process
abstract: The increasing demands in education, along with the use of technology tools, have changed the learning process for the benefit of students. The use of online educational material during lessons is constantly increasing. Digital learning objects (DLOs) are new educational resources that support instructional planning with the help of technology. Teachers plays an important role in this process, as they must manage and correctly use the new conditions by incorporating digital learning objects into teaching. The purpose of the present study was to portray the profile of secondary education teachers regarding the use of DLOs in teaching in relation to their demographic characteristics. Data were collected through a questionnaire used in the research of Tserola (2023). The analysis of the results showed that the specialty, teaching experience, teacher training and the school where they serve influenced the degree of utilization of DLOs in the classroom.

title: Research on Rock Physics and Seismic Inversion Methods for Deep- to Ultradeep- Strata Carbonate Reservoirs
abstract: Deep- to ultradeep-strata carbonate reservoirs are a crucial strategic area for increasing oil and gas reserves and production in my country. These reservoirs are characterized by their great depth, strong heterogeneity, and complex pore structure. The high-temperature and high-pressure environment makes the seismic response mechanism unclear, posing a severe challenge to traditional rock physics models and seismic inversion methods. This paper systematically reviews the recent research progress in rock physics and seismic inversion methods for deep-strata carbonate reservoirs. In rock physics, the paper focuses on the achievements in high-temperature and high-pressure experiments, pore structure characterization, and theoretical model improvements. In seismic inversion, the paper reviews the current development status of pre-stack inversion, multi-information constraints, and artificial intelligence-assisted methods. Based on this, the paper points out the shortcomings of current research in terms of theoretical foundation and prediction accuracy, and proposes development trends and key research directions of deep-strata integration, refinement, and intelligence.

title: MRD negativity by PBMCs and ctDNA confirms deep and durable responses after epcoritamab monotherapy in R/R FL
abstract: Abstract In EPCORE NHL-1, the CD3 × CD20 bispecific antibody epcoritamab demonstrated promising efficacy and manageable safety in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL) after ≥2 prior lines of therapy. Using the clonoSEQ assay, we evaluated minimal residual disease (MRD) status using peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and/or circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) at prespecified time points and investigated their correlation with clinical outcomes. Epcoritamab induced rapid conversion to MRD negativity, with most MRD-evaluable patients reaching MRD negativity by cycle 3 (C3) day 1 (D1) as measured by either analyte. MRD negativity at C3D1 landmark by either analyte correlated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; median not reached), irrespective of radiographic response status. PFS was comparable among patients with overall MRD negativity by PBMCs or ctDNA, regardless of challenging-to-treat disease features. By C3D1 and C5D1 landmarks, patients with complete or partial response, as assessed by positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT), who were MRD positive had a shorter PFS compared with those who were MRD negative. In multivariable analyses at week 12 and week 18 PET/CT landmarks, MRD-negative responders by PBMC assessment (week 12) and by both PBMC and ctDNA assessment (week 18) had significantly improved PFS when adjusted …

title: Efficient and Stable Fractionation of Pennisetum × sinese by Three-Stage Countercurrent Recycling of a Fermentation Compatible Deep Eutectic Solvent
abstract: Abstract Efficient fractionation of lignocellulosic biomass is essential for maximizing carbon utilization and enabling integrated biorefinery processes. We developed a three-stage countercurrent recycling process using a fermentation compatible deep eutectic solvent (DES) for Pennisetum × sinese. In this process, regenerated DES contacted the partially fractionated solids in the final stage, while the lignin-rich DES stream was used for the initial treatment of fresh biomass. This countercurrent arrangement improved the use of the remaining solvent capacity. Lignin and hemicellulose removals remained at approximately 90 and 95%, respectively, over 12 recycling cycles. The glucose yield remained at 34.28–37.26 g per 100 g of dry biomass, with fluctuations between cycles being smaller than those observed in conventional batch cycles. In addition, 10–14 g of low-molecular-weight lignin was recovered per 100 g of dry biomass, with limited structural variation during recycling. The DES recovered remained suitable for microbial fermentation and showed high glycerol utilization, demonstrating its potential for further biological conversion. Overall, the three-stage countercurrent recycling process provides a practical strategy for extending DES reuse and integrating biomass fractionation, fermentable-sugar production, lignin recovery, and further valorization of the solvent within a …

title: Uncertainty in surface topographic measurements
abstract: Abstract With the publication of the ISO 25 178 family of standards, a basis has been given for surface topography measurement, evaluation and interpretations. Also these standards contain all elements needed for an uncertainty evaluation of measured surface topography. Still, extensive uncertainty evaluations are rarely given when surface topography measurements are presented or reported. This review gives an overview of techniques and aspects of uncertainty evaluations as they are reported in the recent literature. The principles of the metrological characteristics and the various ways of their measurement and calibration is covered for the amplification coefficient, the non-linearity, flatness, noise, topographic spatial resolution and topographic fidelity, depending on the measurement configuration and detection principles. The detection principles comprise confocal and chromatic probe, contact stylus, coherence scanning and phase shifting interferometry, focus variation and confocal microscopy. It is shown how the metrological characteristics and aspects such as stitching and filter effects can be combined in an uncertainty evaluation. It is concluded that additional work is needed from instrument makers and metrology institutes in order to implement uncertainty evaluations as common practice.

title: Coping with news doubt: Exploring user-driven tactics to deal with uncertainty about the news
abstract: Abstract This study examines how news users cope with doubt—moments of uncertainty about the factuality or neutrality of news stories—in an increasingly overwhelming, algorithmically curated hybrid news environment. Drawing on 31 in-depth interviews in Belgium, we explore how participants, particularly young people, adopt energy-preserving tactics to manage doubt. These strategies range from dismissing doubt as fleeting to treating it as a constructive, self-protective stance, shaped by topic relevance and by whether doubt was experienced as burdensome or beneficial. Participants expressed doubt toward both editorial and algorithmic news selection and often relied on platforms to eventually surface clarifications, rather than actively verifying information. This approach challenges the notion of a rational, proactive news user and highlights a preference for low-effort coping tactics over verification, such as tolerating uncertainty or waiting for information to find them. The paper argues that media literacy and fact-checking interventions should acknowledge these tactics and embed verified content more broadly to increase incidental exposure and reduce cognitive load.

title: Strategic financing and sustainability decisions in dual-channel supply chains under demand uncertainty: a distribution-free game-theoretic perspective
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how financing structure and sustainability investment jointly influence pricing, service, and green decision-making in a dual-channel supply chain under demand uncertainty. It particularly examines how bank financing and trade credit shape firms' ability to improve environmental performance, strengthen channel competitiveness, and enhance customer value. Design/methodology/approach A Stackelberg game-theoretic model is developed involving a manufacturer and a retailer who operate through both online and offline channels. The manufacturer invests in green innovation financed through bank borrowing, while the retailer chooses between bank financing with a wholesale price discount or trade credit with deferred payment. Demand is uncertain and influenced by green investment and retail service. A distribution-free approach is employed to derive robust equilibrium strategies without assuming a specific demand distribution. Findings Results show that financing choices critically shape sustainability-oriented decisions and channel coordination. Trade credit encourages higher green investment and retail service when financing costs are high, whereas bank financing is more effective under lower borrowing rates and stronger discount incentives. Demand uncertainty substantially affects inventory and profitability, particularly under high-variance settings. T…

Quality optimization of inkjet-printed PVC cards via plasma corona, UV radiation and belt speed parameters
abstract: The production of inkjet-printed PVC cards often faces technical challenges such as ink smearing, low chemical resistance, and poor adhesion. This study aims to optimize the printing quality by analyzing the influence of three independent variables: Plasma Corona treatment, UV radiation, and belt speed variations. An experimental method was employed using eight variations of these parameters on an AMX-UVD-20 Drop on Demand (DOD) inkjet printing machine. The printing quality was comprehensively evaluated through immediate visual morphology observation and dimensional measurements on the day of printing, followed by delayed adhesion stability assessments and solvent resistance tests conducted one month post-printing. The immediate testing revealed that all variations strictly maintained dimensional stability within the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 standard, though samples processed at a lower belt speed of 25.5 cm/s combined with integrated Plasma Corona and active UV radiation yielded the sharpest ink morphology with zero smearing. Furthermore, the one-month post-printing evaluation indicated that while all samples eventually established strong physical adhesion due to long-term natural atmospheric curing, configurations omitting active UV radiation completely failed the solvent resistance tests (0 cycles). These findings suggest that while long-term ambient aging can eventually secure sup…

title: Two Scaling Conjugate Gradient Methods Using the Approximate Optimal Stepsizes for Unconstrained Optimization Problem
abstract: This paper proposes a new method, which combines the gradient method using the approximately optimal stepsizes with the Barzilai and Borwein scaling conjugate gradient method, and propose two scaling conjugate gradient methods for nonlinear unconstrained optimization problems. And then, the sufficient descent property and the global convergence are proved under some reasonable conditions and the standard Wolfe line search. We give some preliminary numerical results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Enzymatic optimization for enhancing earthworm peptide yields and biological activities on antioxidant, cytotoxic against HT-29 and HepG2 cancer cells, and antimigration
abstract: The purposes of this study were to investigate the antioxidant, cytotoxic against HT-29 and HepG2 cancer cells, and antimigratory activities of peptide fractions derived from Amynthas arenulus earthworm. Earthworm proteins were hydrolyzed with alcalase using response surface methodology. The optimal conditions resulted in a maximum degree of hydrolysis of 61.25% at an enzyme-to-substrate ratio of 1.5% (v/v) and a hydrolysis time of 2 h. Following simulated gastrointestinal digestion, gastric and intestinal recoveries of the peptides were 56.83% and 90.10%, respectively. The 10–30 kDa peptide fraction exhibited antioxidant activity, with estimated IC 50 values of 3.18 and 0.79 mg/mL for DPPH and ABTS assays, respectively. FRAP activity was also exhibited. The 10–30 kDa peptide fraction showed antiproliferative activity against HT-29 and HepG2 cells, with IC 50 values of 0.634 and 0.761 mg/mL, respectively, whereas it was not cytotoxic against non-cancerous cells of L929 fibroblast cells. This peptide fraction was trigger apoptosis-associated cellular changes observed using inverted light microscopy, AO/PI and DAPI staining, DNA fragmentation, and scanning electron microscopy. Relative cell migration values in HT-29 and HepG2 cells were 67.34% and 70.29%, respectively which compared to 100% of control. As resultants, this peptide fraction might be considered for applied in medica…

Numerical Simulation Study on Structure Optimization of a New Swirl Stable Combustion Low Nitrogen Burner Based on Computational Fluid Dynamics
abstract: Abstract In order to optimize the structure of the new swirl stable combustion low-nitrogen burner to reduce NOx emissions, this paper uses Fluent software to conduct numerical simulation research on the new swirl stable combustion low-nitrogen burner based on the computational fluid dynamics method. The effects of different swirl blade angles and different primary and secondary air ratios on the temperature field, velocity field and NOx concentration field during combustion are simulated. The results show that when the swirl blade angle is 40°, the burner performance is optimal. At this time, the average NOx mass fraction is as low as 24 ppm, the temperature peak is about 1800 K, the velocity distribution is uniform, and the flame anchoring effect is good; when the primary and secondary air ratio is 2:1, the average NOx mass fraction is also 24 ppm, there are few local high-temperature areas, the combustion is stable, and the thermal NOx generation can be effectively suppressed. The study shows that the swirl blade angle of 40° and the primary and secondary air ratio of 2:1 are the optimal parameter combination of the burner, which can achieve a balance between combustion efficiency and environmental protection performance, and provide a reference for the structural optimization of low-nitrogen burners.

title: Next-Generation Autocatalysis-Integrated Antibody-Bioorthogonal Catalyst Conjugates for Amplified Cell-Surface Antigen Imaging and Targeted In Situ Prodrug Activation
abstract: Abstract Immunoassays and antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) rely on specific antigen–antibody recognition for biomarker detection and targeted cancer therapy; however, their practical performance is often hampered by low antigen abundance, which yields weak readout signals or insufficient local drug concentrations. Autocatalytic bioorthogonal reactions offer an attractive route to achieve exponential signal amplification, but existing CuAAC-based autocatalytic systems suffer from slow multistep ligand assembly and fluorophore self-quenching that degrade signal-to-background ratios. Herein, we report a next-generation autocatalysis-integrated bioorthogonal catalyst-linked immunosorbent assay (BCLISA) employing bis(triazolylmethyl)aminopropyne (DTTA) as a key autocatalytic precursor. Unlike the prior tripropargylamine (TPA) system that demands three successive CuAAC events for ligand formation, DTTA assembles active tris(triazolylmethyl)amine ligands via only one single CuAAC reaction with 7-azidocoumarin (7AC), incorporating merely one coumarin moiety per ligand to mitigate fluorescence self-quenching. Benefiting from accelerated kinetics and suppressed self-quenching, DTTA-mediated autocatalysis enables sensitive in vitro detection of recombinant HER2 and BK polyomavirus VP1 antigens, outperforming commercial ELISA kits. Functionalized with n-octyl lipid tails, DTTA-C8 anchors au…

title: Expansion of Korea's Special Estimate Case System and changes in out-of-pocket expenditure: an interrupted time-series analysis
abstract: Background Since the 2000s, Korea has expanded its National Health Insurance coverage through the implementation and expansion of the Special Estimate Case System. This study examined changes in the proportion of out-of-pocket (OOP) expenditure associated with these policy changes. Methods We analyzed nationwide National Health Insurance Database data from 2002 to 2024. Interrupted time-series (ITS) analysis using monthly data was performed to examine changes in the proportion of OOP expenditure relative to total medical expenditure associated with the implementation (September 2005) and expansion (July 2009) of the Special Estimate Case System. An additional controlled interrupted time-series (CITS) analysis compared changes between care covered and not covered under the system following the 2009 expansion. Results The proportion of OOP expenditure decreased from 27.1% in 2005 to 25.3% in 2006 and from 25.4% in 2009 to 24.3% in 2010. The ITS analysis showed immediate reductions of 1.78 percentage points following implementation and 0.47 percentage points following expansion for total care. In the additional CITS analysis, the differential reduction following the 2009 expansion was 3.11 percentage points for total care, indicating a greater reduction in the OOP expenditure proportion for care covered under the system than for care not covered under the system. Conclusion The im…

title: An Application of Trigonometric Interpolation on Solving a Non-Linear ODE System with Constraints
abstract: In this paper, a trigonometric interpolation-based method is used to solve general non-linear ODE systems with certain constraints due to conservation laws in physics, biology, and engineering. In the case that a target solution of ODE is highly oscillated or rapid changed somewhere in its domain, the algorithm is expected to outperform significantly difference-based methods such as Runge-Kutta rules, which has been confirmed by several numerical experiments conducted in this paper.

High-quality remote sensing reflectance products over China and US coast
abstract: Remote sensing reflectance ( R rs ) is fundamental for deriving bio-optical properties of global surface waters. However, accurate atmospheric correction (AC) to derive R rs in coastal waters remains challenging due to strongly absorbing aerosols and complex water optics. To address this, we developed an improved processing framework that integrates flexible use of global gridded aerosol models better suited for coastal environments and incorporates tailored masking strategies. Based on this framework, we generated a high-quality R rs dataset from Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Aqua observations, spanning 2003–2022 for the coastal waters of China and the United States (US) – two regions where complex water optics and frequent anthropogenic aerosols have long impeded retrieval accuracy and valid data yield. Compared to the NASA standard MODIS Aqua R rs products, the improved framework achieved a significant reduction in systematic bias. Multiple validation metrics support this, with the restoration of the mean regression slope to unity (1.00 ± 0.08 vs. 0.90 ± 0.06) across eight bands being the most prominent. Performance gains are particularly pronounced in the 488–555 nm range, which is most relevant to water color applications. The new dataset also yields significantly more valid retrievals, with regional mean increases of 56 % in the Chinese coastal wat…

title: Tiltrotor Tricopter Dynamics and Control Using the Gibbs–Appell Formulation and Integrated Feedback Linearization with LQR-PD Control
abstract: The equations of motion of a flying robot composed of n rigid arms, each equipped with a motor at its end to provide controllability during complex three-dimensional maneuvers, were previously derived in [1]. The most significant outcome of that study was the demonstration that the robot can reach any point in space while simultaneously achieving an arbitrary desired orientation. It was shown that accomplishing this objective requires at least six actuators and, consequently, six propellers. However, increasing the number of actuators results in higher manufacturing costs, greater energy consumption, and increased overall weight. Therefore, the development and analysis of more efficient flying robot configurations become increasingly important. In the design proposed in this paper, a three-arm flying base is employed instead of a six-arm configuration, with a propeller mounted at the end of each arm. A distinctive feature of this design is that each propeller, in addition to rotating about its primary axis, can also rotate about a secondary axis. This capability enables the thrust vector generated by the main propeller motor to be reoriented by means of a smaller auxiliary motor, thereby allowing the robot to achieve arbitrary orientations in space. To facilitate the analysis, the flying robot is decomposed into several open-chain robotic structures. The equations of motion of …

title: Shadow of success: the temporal association between performance incentive system and research misconduct
Atypical presacral masses in Currarino syndrome: a case series
abstract: Abstract Introduction Currarino syndrome is a rare congenital disorder classically defined by the triad of sacral anomaly, anorectal malformation, and a presacral mass. While anterior meningoceles and teratomas are the most commonly reported lesions, an expanding body of literature suggests a broader spectrum of presacral pathology. We present three cases from our institution that expand the phenotypic range of presacral masses associated with Currarino syndrome, including lesions not previously well described in this population. Case presentation Three cases are presented. Final pathologic diagnoses included myxopapillary ependymoma, mature cystic teratoma, and neuroendocrine tumor arising within a teratoma. Conclusion These cases highlight the considerable heterogeneity of presacral lesions in Currarino syndrome and identify two underrecognized or previously unreported tumor types: myxopapillary ependymoma and neuroendocrine tumor. Surgical management must be individualized and often requires a multidisciplinary approach. Future studies will further clarify genotype–phenotype relationships and improve diagnostic and management strategies in this complex syndrome. Established facts Currarino syndrome is a rare congenital disorder classically defined by the triad of sacral anomaly, anorectal malformation, and a presacral mass. Presacral masses are most commonly anterior meningo…

title: Monte Carlo tree search for the multi-crane scheduling problem with temporal constraints
abstract: Abstract This study addresses the multi-crane scheduling problem with temporal constraints (MCSPTC) arising in steelmaking shops, where multiple rail-guided overhead cranes transport materials on shared tracks and must strictly avoid interference. The problem requires jointly determining task assignment and sequencing decisions while satisfying temporal constraints on task start times, including time windows and precedence relations. In practice, manufacturing execution system data are updated frequently, requiring high quality solutions to be generated repeatedly within short computation times. However, existing heuristics lack quality guarantees, while exact models do not scale to industrial-size instances within practical time limits. To tackle these challenges, we formulate the MCSPTC as a sequential decision process and propose a Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS)–based solution framework. The proposed approach performs look-ahead planning at each decision point using a schedule construction mechanism. To improve search efficiency, we develop a feasibility-based action pruning strategy that eliminates actions inevitably leading to infeasible schedules prior to node expansion. We further tailor the value backup and final action selection rules to account for the tight temporal feasibility and the varying size of the feasible action space induced by temporal constraints. Our num…

title: Hit-Guided Monocular 3D Shuttlecock Trajectory Reconstruction via 3D-Oriented Robust 2D Tracking and Multi-Constraint Modeling
abstract: Recovering the three-dimensional trajectory of a shuttlecock from fixed monocular match videos is important for landing-point judgment, net-clearance analysis, flight-curve modeling, and stroke-quality assessment. Existing monocular badminton 3D recovery pipelines usually integrate court geometry, player pose, 2D shuttle trajectories, hit events, and physical constraints, demonstrating the feasibility of this task; however, in real matches, the shuttlecock is small and fast, and long 2D gaps, local large deviations, and hit-event misjudgments may still be amplified during 3D modeling, while frame-wise 3D ground truth is also scarce. To address these problems, this paper proposes a hitguided monocular 3D shuttlecock trajectory reconstruction method. The method first builds a 3Doriented robust 2D trajectory processing framework, improving the continuity and reliability of 2D inputs through multi-source candidate evidence, conservative selection, and candidate-level calibration; it then uses hit-to-hit flight segments as the basic unit and recovers segment-wise continuous 3D shuttlecock flight curves by combining court-camera geometry, 2D reprojection, pose semantics, and gravity-drag physical constraints. The evaluation is organized according to the task pipeline: 2D trajectory annotations are used to assess the quality of the preceding observation stage, ShuttleSet/ShuttleSet22 …

title: Hasil Belajar Materi Perubahan Iklim dengan Media Pembelajaran Berbasis Android pada Siswa Kelas X
abstract: Penelitian ini menelaah hasil belajar kognitif siswa kelas X pada materi perubahan iklim setelah pembelajaran menggunakan media berbasis Android. Kajian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh keterbatasan variasi media pembelajaran di kelas dan oleh bukti terdahulu yang menunjukkan bahwa manfaat mobile learning dipengaruhi oleh desain pedagogis, konteks materi, dan cara implementasinya. Penelitian menggunakan kuasi eksperimen dengan desain nonequivalent pretest-posttest control group pada 70 siswa SMA Negeri 3 Mataram, masing-masing 35 siswa pada kelas eksperimen dan kontrol. Kelas eksperimen menggunakan media Android yang dikembangkan dengan Construct 2 selama empat pertemuan, sedangkan kelas kontrol mengikuti pembelajaran tanpa media tersebut. Hasil belajar diukur menggunakan 25 soal pilihan ganda. Secara deskriptif, rata-rata pretest kelas eksperimen dan kontrol masing-masing 54,85 dan 45,37, sedangkan rata-rata posttest masing-masing 91,78 dan 84,68. Namun, gain mentah kelas eksperimen (36,93) lebih kecil daripada kelas kontrol (39,31), sehingga perbedaan posttest tidak dapat langsung ditafsirkan sebagai efek perlakuan tanpa mengendalikan perbedaan awal. Oleh karena itu, analisis antar-kelompok perlu menggunakan ANCOVA dengan posttest sebagai luaran dan pretest sebagai kovariat serta melaporkan interval kepercayaan dan ukuran efek. title: Adaptive Confidence-Aware Multi-Antenna RFID Anti-Collision Method for Precision Livestock Monitoring
abstract: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) enables automatic livestock identification in precision agriculture, but simultaneous tag replies can cause collisions and increase reading delay. Earlier work combined multiple receiving antennas with Dynamic Frame Slotted ALOHA (DFSA) to improve bulk tag reading. This paper proposes a confidence-aware extension, called CA-MA-DFSA, that combines slot-outcome feedback, antenna-level response confidence, and a bounded frame-size update. The reader estimates the remaining tag population from idle, successful, and collided slots, then adjusts the next frame conservatively. Antenna observations are used to prioritize repeated interrogation of uncertain tags rather than assuming that every antenna independently identifies a new tag. A simulation plan is specified for comparison with conventional DFSA and multi-antenna DFSA. No experimental results are claimed in this draft; performance must be established through implementation and reproducible testing.

title: Multi-scale computational modeling of magnetoelectric nanoparticle-dispersed conductive nanofibers for peripheral nerve modulation
abstract: Introduction The electrical stimulation of peripheral nerves has shown the potential to restore impaired functions across a wide range of clinical scenarios. In most cases, though, the lack of selectivity of existing stimulation interfaces limits their applicability and can in some cases produce severe adverse effects. In addition, traditional stimulation requires physical connectors to a pulse generator that can add further biological and mechanical stress already linked to interfacing with physiological structures. This study focuses on the use of magnetoelectric nanoparticles (MENPs) embedded within conductive polymeric nanofibers as new wireless, highly selective, and minimally invasive interfaces for modulating peripheral nerves activity. Methods A step-by-step detailed characterization of the physical variables involved in this interaction, spanning from the nanometric single MENPs to micrometric multi-nanofibers structure with dispersed MENPs (poly-ME devices) and ending with the millimetric peripheral nerve, was proposed. MENPs concentration and distribution, device geometry, orientation, and size were systematically varied, and their effects on nerve fiber recruitment were quantified across myelinated and unmyelinated fiber types at different distances from the stimulating source. Results and discussion Our results evidenced how higher MENPs concentrations, higher stim…

title: Deciphering isonicotinylation and mast cell-associated pathogenic patterns in Duchenne muscular dystrophy: evidence from ensemble learning-driven multi-omics and in vitro validation
abstract: Background Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is dystrophin-deficiency skeletal and cardiac muscle disease. Protein post-translational modification (PTM) and aberrant immune cell activation play a key role in its pathogenesis. Objective Our study aims to investigate isonicotinylation (Kinic)-associated signature modulatory patterns in mast cells and DMD pathogenesis. Methods We first performed integrated bioinformatic methods, such as WGCNA, GSVA, and CIBERSORT to identify Kinic and mast cell (KM)-related differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in DMD patient muscle bulk profiles (GSE38417 and GSE109178). Next, consensus clustering and assembling machine learning pipeline identified KM-associated diagnostic model and molecular subgroups in training the DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE6011), and then, diagnostic model performance was examined in the independent DMD patient muscle bulk set (GSE32720). In addition, SHAP analysis decoded the main contributor in KM-associated diagnostic model construction, and contributor molecular and immune characters in DMD were estimated in GSE6011 and the DMD mouse muscle single-cell transcriptomic dataset (GSE213925) assisted by computational virtual cells. In addition, the deep learning framework and network pharmacology identified the drug synergy strategy for the treatment of DMD. Finally, the in vitro assay identified expression patterns of t…
