title: Feasibility and acceptability of a multilevel, family-based hypertension self-management intervention for African American primary care patients: a pilot trial protocol
abstract: Abstract Background Significant disparities in hypertension outcomes experienced by African Americans are only partially ameliorated by existing lifestyle interventions, which largely fail to leverage family level strengths or address family level stress. Given African Americans living with hypertension regularly report friends, family, or kin as key to their disease self-management efforts, family-based interventions that are integrated into usual primary care and also address environmental barriers to self-management may be a particularly culturally attuned approach that is accessible and efficacious. We aim to evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of Walk Together, a community-informed dyadic intervention to promote hypertension self-management among African American primary care patients with uncontrolled hypertension via a single-arm pilot trial. Methods We will recruit African American, English-speaking primary care patients (18–75 years) with an essential hypertension diagnosis and 2 past-year clinic-based blood pressure measurements of > 130/ > 80 mmHg ( n = 30). Patients with a diagnosed severe psychiatric condition, current suicidality, cognitive impairment, or prior engagement in an onsite hypertension clinic will be excluded. Patients will self-identify an English-speaking family support person (aged 18–75) who is involved in their daily care and helps them man…

title: Citizens' perceptions of AI-enabled public services: a thematic analysis of “Julia”, the chatbot of the Rome Municipality
abstract: Purpose This study investigates how citizens perceive and discuss artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled public services, focusing on “Julia,” the AI-based chatbot launched by the Municipality of Rome. It examines online discussions, revealing sociotechnical tensions and discussing their implications for institutional legitimacy and public value in the context of local government digital transformation (DT). Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative approach based on the analysis of 610 citizen comments posted across the social media platforms of the Municipality of Rome and the Mayor. A thematic analysis was conducted to identify recurring patterns in how citizens interpret and evaluate the chatbot's introduction. An engagement analysis contextualized public interactions with chatbot-related posts across platforms. Findings The findings show that citizens interpret the chatbot not merely as a technological tool but as a symbolic representation of the public entity. Four main thematic dimensions emerged: (1) trust and mistrust toward institutions, (2) digital innovation and AI, (3) evaluation of public services and urban management and (4) political, economic and symbolic evaluations of the administration. These dimensions reflect the sociotechnical tensions associated with AI-enabled public services discussed in the literature. Originality/value This study contr…
venue: International Journal of Public Sector Management

title: Encryption and Key Management of Personal Data in Cloud Computing: The Case of Amazon S3 and AWS KMS
abstract: Cloud computing has enabled individuals and organizations to store growing volumes of personal data efficiently, but it has also reduced users' direct control over storage infrastructure and increased exposure to unauthorized access. This paper examines the protection of cloud-based personal data through envelope encryption and key management, using Amazon S3 and AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) as a case study. It addresses the following research question: To what extent can the S3–KMS encryption mechanism reduce personal-data leakage risks, and what factors limit its practical effectiveness? Based on a review of academic literature and AWS technical documentation, the paper analyzes the roles of data encryption keys (DEKs), key encryption keys (KEKs), access permissions, key rotation, and audit logs. The analysis finds that SSE-KMS can reduce the risk that copied stored data will directly disclose personal information by separating encrypted objects from the key encryption keys (KEKs) needed to recover their data encryption keys (DEKs). However, encryption alone cannot prevent breaches caused by stolen credentials, excessive permissions, improper key deletion, or inadequate log monitoring. The paper concludes that effective cloud privacy protection requires a coordinated framework combining encryption, key lifecycle governance, least-privilege access control, and continuo…

title: Drivers of Tobacco Policy Priorities in the United States: A Best-Worst Scaling Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: The aim of this study was to bolster strategic guidance offered to state tobacco prevention and control programs by quantifying the relative importance of criteria used in policy prioritization and examining variation in importance across policy environments. Design: A best-worst scaling (BWS) experiment was embedded in a survey. We developed 11 criteria pertinent to decision making among state tobacco prevention and control programs using qualitative interviews, quantified the criteria's relative importance using BWS, and analyzed the data using conditional logit and latent class logit models. Setting: State tobacco control programs. Participants: Qualitative interviews to inform the development of the BWS were conducted with 12 managers of state tobacco prevention and control programs in 2023. The survey and BWS experiment included individuals working in state tobacco control programs and were conducted in 2024 (n = 114/372, 30.6%). Main Outcome Measure(s): Importance scores of decision-making criteria, on average and across latent classes. Results: The BWS included 11 criteria, encompassing data and evidence, logistics and process considerations, and expected policy support. The most important criteria were addressing needs in priority populations, the availability of existing evidence that a policy works, legislative support, and state data showing a gap…
venue: Journal of Public Health Management & Practice

title: The Bosadi-Salutogenic framework: culturally embedded identity as a personal resource for work engagement among Black South African women in middle management
abstract: The dominance of Euro-American frameworks in industrial and organizational psychology has rendered culturally embedded work experiences largely invisible. While foundational models such as the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) framework elegantly illuminate universal engagement mechanisms across diverse contexts, occupational health literature has traditionally paid less attention to how intersecting racialized and gendered identities shape occupational well-being in postcolonial settings. This conceptual paper addresses this contextual gap by examining the organizational position of Black women in South African middle management, a group navigating unique structural tensions rooted in historical exclusion and contemporary marginalization. Responding to calls for disciplinary decolonization, I propose an integrated Afrocentric framework that brings Bosadi theorization into conversation with salutogenic principles. Specifically, I argue that Bosadi identity functions are not merely as a demographic marker but as a culturally embedded personal resource that shapes how job demands are interpreted, managed, and made meaningful. By positioning identity as an analytic resource rather than a contextual variable, the framework extends the JD-R model’s explanatory power to account for culturally specific modes of resilience and meaning-making. The paper concludes by outlining theoretical con…

title: Internal Control over Financial Reporting in Lease Cycles under SOX 404
abstract: Background: IFRS 16 and its Indonesian adoption through PSAK 73 bring most leases onto the statement of financial position, increasing the importance of reliable contract data and timely control execution in capital-intensive entities. Objective: This study examines the design and operating effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting (ICoFR) in the lease transaction cycle of a dual-listed infrastructure enterprise during the post-remediation stabilization phase. Methods: A descriptive qualitative single instrumental case study design was applied using a top-down, risk-based approach derived from PCAOB AS 2201. Evidence was triangulated through semi-structured interviews with six functionally diverse informants, guided observation, and inspection of five key control working papers covering 2023–2026. Results: All five key controls were adequately designed. However, operating effectiveness testing identified a control deficiency involving delayed lease modification updates and inconsistent data input by field business units. The deficiency did not escalate to a significant deficiency or material weakness because the K-02 compensating control consistently detected and corrected potential misstatements before the financial statements were issued. Conclusion: Reliable ICoFR in a decentralized lease cycle depends on both sound control design and timely first-line risk …
venue: Journal of Business, Social and Technology

title: Visual trust signals in digital financial marketplaces: eye-tracking evidence from verification badges
abstract: Purpose This study examines when a platform-issued verification badge affects consumer choice in a high-uncertainty digital financial marketplace. Integrating signaling theory and attention-based choice research, it distinguishes signal assignment, item-card visual consideration, post-task self-reported badge noticing, and hypothetical selection. Design/methodology/approach A controlled eye-tracking experiment involved 60 participants. Each participant viewed 10 NFT listings, five randomly assigned a badge within the participant's choice set, and selected three listings for hypothetical purchase. Item-card fixation, time to first fixation, fixation count and selection were analyzed using participant and item fixed effects and a Cox model. Findings Badged item-cards were fixated in 83.3% of observations, compared with 35.7% for unbadged item-cards. Among cards with an observed first fixation, badge assignment was associated with an approximately 1.47-s earlier first fixation. Hypothetical selection rates were 42.3% for badged listings and 17.7% for unbadged listings. The estimated badge-selection relationship was substantially stronger among participants who reported clearly noticing the badge. The gaze measures concern the full item-card rather than direct badge-icon fixation, and noticing was not experimentally manipulated. Originality/value By combining randomized cue assignm…

title: Literary History in Fragments: The Transmission and Reception of Roman Republican Literature
abstract: This paper looks at the issue of how the fragments of Roman Republican literature have been transmitted (by isolated quotations in later ancient authors) and how this way of transmission has shaped the perception of this phase of Roman literature.

Audit committee diversity as a moderator of the relationship between financial crises and firm profitability: evidence from the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: Purpose This study examines the moderating role of audit committee diversity in the nexus between financial crises (the COVID-19 crisis) and profitability. Design/methodology/approach This study analyses Jordanian non-financial companies listed on the Amman Stock Exchange as a sample for the study from 2018 to 2022. The hypotheses were tested using panel-corrected standard errors (PCSE) regression analysis to address the issues of heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation. This study uses the system Generalised Method of Moments (GMM), along with fixed-effects and dynamic regression analyses to address endogeneity concerns. Findings This paper concluded that the COVID-19 crisis negatively impacted the profitability of companies. Gender diversity moderated this relationship, significantly mitigating the negative impact of the pandemic, whereas the results did not indicate that nationality diversity played a moderating role. Practical implications This investigation relies on the novel results concerning the moderating effects of audit committee diversity characteristics, offering guidance to regulators on incorporating these underrepresented traits into corporate governance codes in Jordan and similar developing countries. Originality/value The literature investigating diversity’s influence on corporate profitability during crises predominantly emphasizes board-level diversity, dir…

title: Preventing recurring material misstatements through behavioural sustainment: a 5S-based conceptual framework for financial reporting
abstract: Purpose This paper develops a conceptual framework to explain how behavioural discipline is sustained in routine financial reporting work and how such sustainment conditions the recurrence of material misstatements under conditions of reasonable assurance. Rather than treating reporting reliability as an outcome optimised through technical rules or ex post detection, the paper reconceptualises financial reporting as a behaviourally enacted process shaped by routines, accountability, and reinforcement over time. Design/methodology/approach The paper adopts a structured conceptual integration of accounting, management control and behavioural literature. The 5S principles – Sort, Set in Order, Shine, Standardise and Sustain – are reinterpreted as a behavioural process framework that explicates how reporting routines are enacted, coordinated, scrutinised and reinforced across reporting cycles. The approach is conceptual in nature and does not constitute a systematic review or a design science intervention. Findings The framework suggests that the recurrence of material misstatements is shaped less by the presence of additional procedures than by the extent to which disciplined reporting practices are behaviourally sustained over time. It explicates how 5S operates through behavioural mechanisms – such as selective attention to materiality, anticipatory coordination, anomaly questio…

title: Financial Resource Management Towards Public School Governance
abstract: In recent years, financial resource management in public schools has gained increasing attention due to the growing demand for transparency, accountability, and effective governance. This descriptive-correlational study aimed to determine the level of financial resource management in public secondary schools in Jamindan, Capiz. The respondents consisted of 102 teachers and 256 stakeholders, composed of alumni and parents. Data were collected using a researcher-made survey questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive statistics. The findings revealed that most teachers were in early to mid-career stage, predominantly female, married, and holders of bachelor’s degrees with some graduate units. Most alumni were young, single, and high school graduates, indicating that they were in the early stages of their personal and professional development. The parents were mostly in mid-adulthood, married, and had varied educational attainments, with many reaching the college level, while others had limited formal education. The parents also showed diverse socioeconomic backgrounds. In terms of financial resource management, teachers, alumni, and parents all rated it as very high, with emphasis on budget preparation and planning, transparency and accountability, stakeholder involvement, and governance effectiveness. The study also found that there were no significant differences in perception…

title: Compassionate leadership and job performance: the mediating role of supervisor support and financial anxiety in emerging economies
abstract: Purpose Drawing upon Social Exchange Theory and Organizational Support Theory, this study investigates how Compassionate Leadership (CFL) influences employee Job Performance (PERF) in an emerging Asian economy, focusing on the mediating role of Perceived Supervisor Support (PSS) and the stress-induced influence of Financial Anxiety (FIN_ANX). Design/methodology/approach Using a quantitative, cross-sectional design, data were collected from 250 employees in Vietnam facing a cost-of-living crisis. The hypothesized dual-pathway model was tested using structural equation modeling (SEM) and bias-corrected bootstrapping in Stata 17.0. Findings Results indicate that CFL significantly enhances PSS, which in turn positively drives Job Performance (a partial mediation effect). Concurrently, Financial Anxiety also positively impacted performance, revealing a dual-pathway mechanism where performance is driven by both reciprocal leadership support and survival-based economic stress. Research limitations/implications The reliance on cross-sectional, self-reported data restricts causal inferences. Future research should employ longitudinal designs and supervisor-rated performance metrics. Practical implications Cultivating compassionate leadership is a strategic imperative. Organizations are encouraged to train leaders in financial empathy to transition employees from a reactive scarcity mind…

Financial Development, Financial Globalization and Logistics Performance in Mediterranean Economies: Long-Run and Distributional Evidence
abstract: This paper investigates the relationship between logistics performance, financial development, and financial globalization in a sample of nineteen Mediterranean countries over the period 2007-2022. Logistics performance is measured by the World Bank Logistics Performance Index (LPI), while financial development and financial globalization are proxied by composite indices. Since the global logistics survey index is not observed on a yearly basis but only in irregular intervals, interpolation is used to construct an annual panel. The most probable case is that our panel captures the medium- and long-run dynamics between the benchmarks and not short-term annual variations. The empirical specification employs second-generation panel procedures, long-run estimators, Granger-causality tests, and distribution-sensitive approaches. Significant persistence, common stochastic components, and medium- to long-run co-movement are uncovered, providing evidence for the persistent long-term co-movement of logistics performance and financial conditions. Baseline estimates of FMOLS, DOLS, and PMG-ARDL reveal positive long-run relationships for both financial development and financial globalization. Yet, domestic financial development becomes statistically weaker under more flexible treatment of cross-sectional dependence, unobserved common factors, and slope heterogeneity, whereas financial glob…

title: Exploring How Audit Quality Bridges the Link between Board Audit Committee Financial Expertise and Financial Reporting Quality: Empirical Evidence from Kenyan Commercial Banks
abstract: Financial reporting quality (FRQ) within the banking industry is of particular interest due to the importance of transparency, market confidence and financial stability. Banks are particularly prone to FRQ issues due to the high level of estimation within the accounting process such as loan loss provisions (LLP). In addition, low FRQ may mask risk and pose a threat to financial stability. This study sought to establish the mediating effect of audit quality on the relationship between board audit committee financial expertise and financial reporting quality (FRQ) among banks in Kenya. Anchored on Agency Theory, Stakeholder Theory and Resource Dependence Theory, the study adopted a positivist philosophy and an explanatory longitudinal panel research design. Secondary data were obtained from audited financial statements, annual reports, external audit reports and Central Bank of Kenya publications covering 2015–2024, and all analyses were based on this full balanced panel of 330 observations. Financial reporting quality was measured using absolute discretionary loan-loss provisions derived from a bank-specific loan-loss-provision model, with lower values indicating less reporting discretion and higher financial reporting quality. Audit quality was proxied by external audit fees. Mediation was tested using the Sobel test. The mediation results demonstrated that audit quality mediat…

title: Monetary Policy Transmission in an Intangible Economy: Evidence from Firm Performance and Loan Markets
abstract: Growing importance of software, data, R&D, brands, and organizational capital might affect the monetary policy transmission channel because intangibles cannot be easily pledged and innovative expenditure can be prohibitively expensive to undo. This paper examines whether firms with high intangible intensity are more or less vulnerable to contractionary monetary policy shocks in the US. The dataset encompasses Compustat Global, annual monetary-policy shocks for firms from Jarociński and Karadi aggregated by firms' fiscal year, and DealScan syndicated loan data. The sample includes an unbalanced panel of international firm-year observations from 2001–2023. Models with interactions between firm- and year-fixed effects and annual policy shocks lagged one period and six other lagged firm control variables are estimated. Following contractionary shocks, high-intangible-intensity firms experience a comparatively low sales growth, which means they face a relatively higher risk of being more vulnerable. However, they show a relatively higher increase in R&D intensity, R&D share, and R&D expenditure, suggesting that R&D is preferred and comparatively resilient, but not necessarily increases in total R&D expenditure. Financing restrictions exacerbate the sales decrease. Results from the loan market indicate that syndicated loan spreads do not change differentially. Greater commitment volu…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Can ChatGPT be skeptical? A case-based evaluation of generative AI in financial statement auditing
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how effectively GenAI (ChatGPT) displays professional skepticism characteristics in external audit tasks, as insufficient skepticism may impair audit quality and heighten the risk of audit failure. Design/methodology/approach ChatGPT is evaluated using four audit tasks representing common judgment-oriented audit procedures. Three experienced external auditors independently assessed ChatGPT’s responses using a structured professional skepticism assessment. Findings ChatGPT appears to display varying levels of skepticism characteristics across audit tasks, with relatively higher levels in preliminary risk assessments and substantive analytical procedures and lower levels in going-concern evaluations. This suggests that it may be more effective in analytical tasks than in those requiring deeper professional judgment. Originality/value This study appears to be among the first to systematically assess whether a general-purpose reasoning GenAI tool can display characteristics associated with professional skepticism across different audit tasks. By applying an established skepticism framework, it provides a structured baseline for understanding where GenAI may support or fall short in audit judgment contexts.

title: Determinants of financial performance of Nepalese mutual funds: Evidence from fixed-effects panel analysis
abstract: This study examines the determinants of financial performance: Net Asset Value (NAV), Net Profit and Dividend Payout Ratio (DPR) of Nepalese close end-mutual funds. This study is based on 988 fund-month observations of 26 registered funds over 38 months. The fixed-effects panel regression is used and the Hausman test indicates it is the better than the random effects and Pooled OLS. The results show that fund size has the most positive effect on all three performance measures (p < 0.01); operating expense has a negative effect on NAV and Net Profit (p < 0.05); but not on DPR; fund age is statistically insignificant; and trade amount has a positive effect on NAV and Net Profit (p < 0.01) but not on DPR. DPR is primarily driven by Net Profit and fund size. The fund-level policy was the major driver of DPR as shown by the multilevel variance decomposition where ICCs were 0.546 (NAV), 0.336 (Net Profit) and 0.760 (DPR). The fit of the model is satisfactory (R2 = 0.521, 0.568 and 0.401, respectively; all p < 0.01). The practical contribution of the study is to provide the first causal, panel-based evidence on Nepalese mutual fund performance, thereby providing actionable guidance for investors (prefer large, low-expense, high-turnover funds), fund managers (cost control, active trading, transparent dividend policy) and regulators (minimum capital, expense caps, performance-based eva…
venue: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)

title: The Impact of BNPL on Adolescents' Financial Behavior and Perceptions in a Digital Credit Environment
abstract: Amid the rapid expansion of digital finance, "Buy Now, Pay Later" (BNPL), a new type of digital credit tool, has become increasingly embedded in mobile payment ecosystems and gained growing popularity among young consumers. At the same time, adolescents' financial literacy is still underdeveloped and their ability to identify risks is limited, making them more prone to irrational consumption behavior when using digital credit tools. Thus, it is necessary to explore the potential impact of BNPL on adolescents' financial behavior and cognitive structures. This paper investigates the mechanisms through which BNPL affects adolescents' consumption patterns and financial awareness, as well as the resulting outcomes. Moreover, it also examines how BNPL shapes consumption decisions, saving practices, and perceptions of credit, while further exploring its role in the accumulation of financial risks. Through the lenses of bounded rationality, the pain-of-payment effect, intertemporal choice, and mental accounting, this paper identifies the pathways through which BNPL influences consumption decisions and risk perceptions based on existing research on digital credit tools and youth consumption behavior. The results indicate that by diminishing the immediate pain of payment, delaying the sense of payment responsibility, and blurring the boundaries between credit and assets, BNPL induces ado…
venue: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences

title: Human Resource Competence as a Moderator of the Influence of State Property Administration on the Quality of Government Agencies' Financial Statements
abstract: Reliable government financial statements are essential for promoting transparency and accountability; however, weaknesses in state property administration and variations in employee competence may compromise financial reporting quality. This study examined the association between state property administration and financial statement quality and assessed human resource competence as both a direct predictor and a moderator within the Audit Board of the Republic of Indonesia. A quantitative survey design with purposive sampling was used to recruit 70 employees involved in state property management. Questionnaire data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with a two-stage higher-order construct approach and bootstrapping with 5,000 subsamples. State property administration, encompassing bookkeeping, inventory, and reporting, was positively and significantly associated with financial statement quality (B = 0.824, p < 0.001). Human resource competence showed neither a significant direct association with financial statement quality (B = 0.027, p = 0.716) nor a significant moderating effect on the relationship between state property administration and financial statement quality (B = 0.072, p = 0.315). The model explained 73.1% of the variance in financial statement quality. These findings highlighted the importance of consistent state propert…

title: “Less is less” or “Less is more”? Financial constraints and green innovation in a global context
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the theoretically ambiguous relationship between financial constraints and green innovation. The resource-based view holds that financial frictions impede green innovation by restricting investment in costly, risky technologies (“less is less”), whereas the induced innovation hypothesis argues that these constraints can spur creativity and adaptive problem solving, thereby enhancing green innovation (“less is more”). Design/methodology/approach This study uses the ordinary least squares (OLS) method to analyze 2,750 firms across 44 countries for the 2005–2021 period. In addition, propensity score matching, firm fixed effects, change regression and lead-dependent variable techniques are applied to address potential endogeneity concerns. Findings Results show that financial constraints reduce firms’ green innovation, supporting the “less is less” hypothesis. The effect is more pronounced among firms in countries with higher economic development, weak national governance and lax environmental policy enforcement. Reduced environmental expenditure and poor workforce wellbeing channel the effect. Institutional ownership and strong corporate governance reduce the adverse impact of financial constraints on green innovation. Practical implications This study suggests how financial constraints hinder green innovation. Specifically, the conditions un…

title: Research on Enterprise Financial Risk Intelligent Early-Warning Model Based on XGBoost
abstract: Against the background that the demand for risk prevention and control in the capital market is increasingly prominent, financial crises of listed companies occur frequently. Traditional linear early warning models find it difficult to depict the nonlinear associations of financial indicators, and also face practical problems such as sample imbalance and model black box. This paper selects A-share non-financial listed companies, constructs a multi-dimensional financial early warning indicator system, uses period t indicators to predict period t+1 financial risk, constructs a financial risk early warning model based on XGBoost, introduces SHAP to realize the interpretable analysis of the model, and conducts comparative empirical research with logistic regression and random forest. The results show that the XGBoost model has better overall accuracy and early warning precision, and profitability, cash flow, and solvency indicators are the core factors for identifying financial risk; SHAP can effectively solve the model black box problem, and realize global risk factor identification and single-enterprise risk tracing. The research can provide technical support and decision-making reference for enterprise management, investors, creditors, and regulatory agencies to carry out financial risk identification and risk control.

From silos to sharing: An Open Educational Resources-based framework for consumer financial education
abstract: Orientation: Consumer financial education (CFE) provision remains duplicated, fragmented and inconsistent in quality despite global and national mandates for coordinated action. CFE can be understood as a grand challenge requiring system-wide collaboration, supported by openness and shared value creation. Research purpose: To develop a framework for the coordinated, cooperative and collaborative (3C) development of CFE resources, with Open Educational Resources (OER) as the enabling mechanism. The framework moves ecosystem actors from aligning goals (coordination), to sharing purpose and effort (cooperation), to jointly producing openly licensed resources (collaboration). Motivation for the study: Transnational policy frameworks call for accessible, inclusive financial literacy education, yet practical mechanisms for jointly developing and sharing CFE content remain underdeveloped. Research design, approach and method: A conceptual design was adopted. Literature on systems thinking, the Quintuple Helix Innovation Model, collaboration theory and open educational practices was purposively synthesised through an abductive analytic process. Main findings: Duplication persists because collaboration, although mandated, is not operationalised. Open practices and OER, through open licensing, shared workflows and reuse, provide a viable mechanism for 3C resource development. The framewo…

title: Construction and content validation of an OBE-AI-CED integrated teaching framework for the liquor factory design course in local undergraduate universities: a modified Delphi study
abstract: The digital, intelligent and green transformation of the Chinese baijiu industry has introduced new competency demands for liquor engineering education. The Liquor Factory Design course is a comprehensive upper-level engineering design course for students in the liquor engineering program that combines knowledge of brewing technology, chemical engineering, engineering drawing, brewing equipment, energy-saving and environmental protection, and production management. However, the course in local undergraduate universities still has several problems, such as an unclear design task chain, a lack of authentic engineering contexts, ambiguous boundaries for the use of artificial intelligence, and an assessment approach that focuses too much on the final product rather than the learning process. The above problems may limit the all-round development of students’ engineering design abilities. Given the above problems, this paper builds an OBE-AI-CED integrated teaching system for the Liquor Factory Design course by integrating Outcome-Based Education, Artificial Intelligence and Complex Engineering Design. A modified Delphi method was employed to examine the content validity and refine the framework. Two rounds of expert consultations were conducted with university teachers, engineering technicians from Baijiu Enterprise, and experts from an engineering design institution. The first rou…

title: Compliant Structure Design for Improved Robot Motion Control Performance
abstract: This narrative review examines how compliant structural design redistributes motion control functions between mechanical bodies and computational controllers. It synthesizes theoretical, experimental, and co-design studies on passive dynamic walking, elastic coupling, self-stabilizing locomotion, soft robots, underactuated grasping, morphological computation, and morphology-control optimization. Across these systems, compliance can store and return energy, couple joint motion, shape attracting dynamics, adapt contact geometry, and transform inputs before feedback intervenes. These mechanisms can reduce the number of independently controlled variables and the demands on sensing, modeling, and feedback. Their benefits remain conditional: excessive or poorly located compliance can reduce positioning bandwidth, force capability, repeatability, and robustness outside the intended operating range. The reviewed evidence, therefore, supports allocating compliance to specific functions rather than minimizing stiffness globally. Mechanical self-regulation should be combined with sufficient sensing and actuation for disturbances beyond the passive region, while morphology and control should be optimized jointly with manufacturability, parameter variation, and transfer from simulation to hardware taken into account.

title: The ternary complex structure as a foundation for structure-guided molecular glue design
abstract: Abstract Molecular glues are opening up new therapeutic areas by turning previously undruggable and intractable proteins into tractable targets through the formation or stabilisation of a ternary complex between two proteins. The present review focuses on how such structures are obtained and leveraged to guide rational design. Ternary complexes can be classified by protein–protein interface architecture and degree of topological constraint, informing the design process towards a given biological outcome. As with conventional small-molecule drug discovery, structural information provides invaluable insights for rational optimisation of glues, but solving a ternary complex structure remains a significant challenge owing to the underlying three-body equilibrium. Biophysical characterisation of cooperativity and ternary complex half-life not only provides optimisation parameters but also provides a means for prioritising the most promising glues for ternary structural studies by X-ray crystallography or cryogenic electron microscopy. Once solved, a ternary structure enables conventional structure-based design, such as scaffold hopping and surface decoration, and increasingly informs computational methods, though these remain most powerful when grounded in experimental validation. Ternary complex structures for canonical glue systems are now available in relative abundance, providin…

title: Announce, brand, repeat: the illusion of Australian health reform
abstract: Health reform announcements can signal progress before improvements in care are demonstrated. Drawing on Baudrillard’s account of sign value, we examine how visible policy achievements can acquire authority independently of clinical benefit. My Health Record illustrates the distinction between implementation, use and outcomes. We connect established improvement principles to four questions about resource allocation, duplication, clinical work and public accountability. The aim is to make claims of reform answerable to evidence of improvement.

title: Socio-spatial inequality: the case of Indonesian railway's reform
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how accounting practices as tools of governance reproduce inequality by reshaping relational spaces which intersect with colonial legacies, local contexts and neoliberal logics. Design/methodology/approach This study investigates organisational reforms of PT Kereta Api Indonesia (Persero) (KAI) during 2009–2014. It focuses on the transformation of station areas where neoliberal imperatives of efficiency and customer orientation reshaped socially vibrant, informally sustained spaces into purified, commercially driven zones, displacing long-standing occupants and disrupting local economies. Employing 28 semi-structured interviews with employees, passengers, consultants and experts, complemented by annual reports and public documents, the study validates methodological triangulation. By situating stations as socially and historically constructed spaces, the analysis demonstrates how accounting and governance practices intersected with spatial restructuring to produce and legitimise socio-spatial inequalities. Findings The findings reveal that neoliberal reforms generate structural inequalities by redefining who and what is recognised within organisational spaces. Accounting functions as a powerful instrument in this process, shaping the criteria through which actors are rendered visible, accountable and authorised to occupy the contested spaces. …

title: Primary care reform and concurrent changes in the regional distribution and equity of the ministry of health family medicine workforce in Saudi Arabia: a descriptive longitudinal analysis, 2014–2022
abstract: Background Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, with family medicine positioned as the organising specialty of primary care. Whether this transformation has translated into a more equitable distribution of family medicine across the Kingdom remains under-examined. This study aimed to evaluate whether the primary-care reform altered the regional distribution and equity of the FP workforce across the fourteen health administrative units of the Kingdom. Methods A retrospective, longitudinal panel was constructed from Saudi Ministry of Health Statistical Yearbooks (2014–2022) across three reform phases: pre-reform (2014–2016), transformation (2017–2020), and post-reform (2021–2022). FM density per 10,000 population was the primary outcome. Inequality was assessed by the Gini coefficient, Theil index, and coefficient of variation, (bootstrap 95% Cis: 1,000 resamples). Phase comparisons used by Kruskal–Wallis with Bonferroni-adjusted Mann–Whitney pairwise tests; temporal trends by Mann–Kendall. Regional trajectories by Ward hierarchical clustering on z-standardised density paths. Because an administrative reclassification in 2021 depressed the national count, trend results are reported both for the full series and with 2021 excluded, and the artifact-adjusted estimates are treated as the primary ones. Only MOH-employed family physicians are covered; private, military and university providers …

title: Knowledge Dependency and Institutional Decoupling in Global Education Governance: A Case Study of Higher Education Reform in Kazakhstan
abstract: In the aftermath of World War II, higher education became a key focus of international development. International institutions such as the OECD have actively channeled educational resources to support global economic reconstruction, particularly in war-affected developing countries that lacked systematic educational infrastructure. While these efforts aim to establish universal educational standards, policy formulation often overlooks local conditions, generating unintended problems. Existing scholarship separately examines these potential outcomes in educational policy transfer yet overlooks their mutual circular feedback relationship. Focusing on the case of Kazakhstan, this paper uses a qualitative case study approach and argues that a subtle hegemony rooted in global educational programmes, may lead to knowledge dependency in developing countries and further result in institutional decoupling. Such decoupling can ultimately generate new rounds of knowledge dependency and impede educational development in developing countries like Kazakhstan. It also calls for developing countries' attention to the indigenous institutional autonomy in higher education.
venue: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media

title: Shadow Pricing in Transient Stability-Constrained Optimal Power Flow
abstract: Transient stability constraints alter the economic dispatch of power systems, while the resulting price signals and their implications for market settlement remain insufficiently characterized. Existing approaches identify stability-related components in locational marginal prices, without deriving shadow prices for individual assets, such as generators and loads, or analyzing the resulting settlement. To address this gap, this paper derives shadow prices from a transient stability-constrained optimal power flow in which the differential-algebraic equations governing the system dynamics are embedded through direct discretization. Each shadow price decomposes into a nodal energy component and a stability component, the latter formed by the dual variables of the dynamic equations in which the power of the asset appears. Shadow prices are therefore asset-specific: co-located generators and loads are assigned the same nodal energy component, but can be subject to different stability components when their transient behaviors differ. Case studies on the WECC 9-bus system and a modified IEEE 39-bus system show that settlement at the proposed shadow prices allocates the cost of the stability constraints among the assets without any side payment. An asset that reduces the stability margin is charged its stability component, whereas an asset that improves it is paid, and no generator is …

title: Impact of Data Center Load on Co-Optimized Generation and Transmission Expansion Planning with Embedded Unit Commitment
abstract: The rapid growth of hyperscale data centers challenges grid expansion planning, yet existing studies focus largely on operational flexibility rather than long-term investment decisions. This paper examines how large data center loads sited at multiple buses affect co-optimized Transmission Expansion Planning (TEP) and Generation Expansion Planning (GEP). The problem is formulated as a multi-year, Unit Commitment (UC)-embedded mixed-integer linear program on the modified IEEE 24-bus Reliability Test System (RTS-24) with Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT)-calibrated renewable energy profiles. A 500 MW data center load, about 17.5% of the base-year peak, is allocated across four buses by voltage level, generation headroom, renewable co-location, and network connectivity. Integrating this load raises the 15-year net present value of total system cost by 1,794 million USD (+61.6%) and the system-average locational marginal price (LMP) by 45.2%, with operating cost dominating capital investment (84.2% versus 15.8%). Renewable curtailment remains negligible: existing renewables are already near full utilization, so the added demand is served almost entirely by incremental thermal generation. Most notably, the load shifts the optimal plan from transmission-only to generation-only, replacing the base-case 230 kV reinforcement with a new 400 MW combined-cycle gas turbine and s…

title: Computation of Price Signals for Controlling Flexible Prosumers in Distribution Grids Incorporating Stochasticity and Fairness
abstract: This paper proposes a method for distribution system operators (DSOs) to design spatially fair dynamic price signals for flexible prosumers, accounting for both distribution grid constraints and the stochastic behavior of prosumers. Since locational pricing can introduce price unfairness when grid constraints are active, the proposed approach includes mechanisms to enforce price fairness across the network. The method involves the DSO solving a scenario-based optimal power flow (OPF) problem to derive, similarly to locational marginal prices in transmission systems, the Lagrange multipliers associated with grid constraints and to compute individualized price signals for each prosumer under various PV generation and demand scenarios. Subsequently, two methods are introduced to aggregate these individualized prices into a single fair price across prosumers. Their performance is evaluated through simulations on a model distribution grid, comparing prosumer revenues, grid constraint violations, and analyzing the impact of fairness on reducing cost variance among prosumers.

title: Stock Volatility and Market Valuation: Analyzing the Financial Impact of Subscription Transitions at Adobe and Autodesk
abstract: This study examines how switching from traditional software licenses to a recurring subscription model impacts a company’s financial performance and market valuation over time. For this comparative case study, this paper analyzes Adobe Inc. and Autodesk, Inc. by looking at their financial data from the pre-transition, active-transition and post-transition periods. The study focuses on the important financial metrics like total revenue, GAAP net income, operating margins, Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR), Enterprise Value-to-Sales (EV/Sales) multiples, Price-to-Earnings (P/E) multiples and stock price volatility. The findings show that both companies faced problems during their transitions, with temporary declines in metrics like revenue, profitability, and operating margins. On the other hand, ARR increased significantly as the subscription revenue became a larger part of each company’s business. The valuation multiples generally increased and stock price volatility fluctuated over time. These results show that declines in financial performance during a transition to a subscription model do not mean that the overall business is getting weaker, since some part of the decline can come from changes in when the revenue is actually recognized. Overall, the analysis shows that while moving to subscriptions can hurt financial performance in the short-term, a successful transition can cr…
venue: Student Journal of Business and Economics

title: Coimbatore Property Valuator: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Offline Market-Intelligence Framework for Property Valuation Real Estate Market and Trend Prediction Model
abstract: Determination of property value is complicated due to factors of locality, property type, area, accessibility, physical characteristics and market conditions. In this paper, a local framework for property valuation in Coimbatore, India is presented, namely, the Coimbatore Property Valuator (CPV). The system includes a data-acquisition and machine-learning module, and an offline evaluation and market-intelligence module. Property listings are automatically harvested from the web, cleaned, standardized, and enhanced with a locality knowledge base, which provides attributes and context on the locality's micro-market, zone, soil, connectivity, and appreciation. XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost are the algorithms used for separate training of Sale and Rent/Lease pipelines. They make predictions using a weighted log-space ensemble with weights of 0.40, 0.35 and 0.25, respectively. The models are based on area, BHK, market statistics, geographic attributes and property-category features. The mobile app also offers an offline valuation engine that uses processed data to compute locality market-rate baselines and uses transparent, rule-based adjustments. It calculates and compares the seller's asking price with a "fair value" range and categorizes the outcome as Great Deal, Fair Market Deal or Overpriced. It also provides locality connectivity and rule-based appreciation projections. The …
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science, Engineering and Technology

title: PERFORMANCE-МАРКЕТИНГ ЯК ЧИННИК СТАЛОГО ЕКОНОМІЧНОГО РОЗВИТКУ ПІДПРИЄМСТВ ЦИФРОВОЇ ЕКОНОМІКИ
abstract: The article examines the impact of performance marketing on the sustainable economic development of enterprises in the digital economy under conditions of digital transformation. The growing role of data-driven technologies, digital channels, and the necessity of improving marketing investment efficiency have significantly transformed approaches to marketing management. Under these conditions, performance marketing is considered not only as a set of digital promotion tools but also as an important managerial approach focused on measurable outcomes, continuous performance monitoring, and resource optimization. The study generalizes contemporary scientific approaches to performance marketing and identifies its role in improving enterprise performance. It is substantiated that the systematic use of marketing analytics, key performance indicators, and investment effectiveness evaluation creates an information basis for informed decision-making, enhances resource utilization efficiency, improves economic performance, and strengthens competitive positions in the digital economy. Particular attention is paid to the relationship between the stages of performance marketing implementation and the components of sustainable economic development. To systematize these relationships, a matrix framework is proposed, reflecting the contribution of individual implementation stages to information…

title: КОНЦЕПЦІЯ СТАЛОГО ТУРИЗМУ ЯК ІНСТРУМЕНТ ЗБАЛАНСОВАНОГО РОЗВИТКУ ПРИРОДНО-РЕКРЕАЦІЙНИХ СИСТЕМ
abstract: The article examines the role of the sustainable tourism concept as an instrument for the balanced development of natural and recreational systems in Ukraine in the context of reconciling economic, environmental, and social interests. It is substantiated that tourism activity directly depends on the condition of natural resources, which determine the recreational attractiveness of territories and the opportunities for the long-term functioning of the tourism industry. It is established that excessive intensity of tourist and recreational use may reduce the natural potential of territories; therefore, sustainability requires the regulation of recreational pressure, rational resource use, and the preservation of the capacity of natural complexes for self-recovery. It is determined that the economic effectiveness of sustainable tourism is associated with the optimization of natural, energy, and material resource use, ensuring the long-term profitability of tourism activities, and integrating tourism into the local economy. The dynamics of tax revenues from the tourism industry to the State Budget of Ukraine is analyzed, demonstrating the recovery and strengthening of the fiscal role of tourism following the decline in 2022. It is emphasized that the financial outcomes of tourism activities should be assessed in conjunction with the condition of the natural environment and the capa…

title: ІННОВАЦІЙНІ ІНСТРУМЕНТИ РОЗВИТКУ ФОНДОВОГО РИНКУ
abstract: The article is devoted to the study of modern innovative instruments of the stock market and their definition. The study determined the role of digital financial instruments in the transformation of the mechanisms of capital markets. The main trends in the development of financial technologies were considered. Their impact on increasing the efficiency of investment activities, optimizing asset management and ensuring the transparency of stock market transactions was analyzed. The advantages of using innovative instruments compared to traditional approaches to investment were determined. The main advantages are high speed of transactions, reduced transaction costs, expanded access to financial services, automation of decision-making processes and increased liquidity of capital markets. The article examines the features of the application of blockchain technologies, tokenization of financial assets, cryptocurrencies, exchange-traded funds for digital assets and digital currencies of central banks. Smart contracts, fintech platforms, open banking solutions and APIs are considered. Special attention is paid to Big Data technologies, artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotic process automation, algorithmic and high-frequency trading, robo-advisory as an innovative tool for managing investment portfolios. The global experience of using innovative stock market instruments is …

title: Beyond labour market entry: Gendered unpaid work and the double burden of women workers in India
abstract: Rising female labour force participation in India does not guarantee a fairer division of household work. This paper uses unit level data from the 2024 Time Use Survey to examine unpaid domestic and caregiving work among 179,585 workers aged 15 to 59, of whom 44,394 are women. Women workers spend 257.6 minutes a day on unpaid work against 44.3 minutes for men, and 138.9 fewer minutes in employment. Their combined paid and unpaid burden is therefore 74.4 minutes longer. Survey weighted regressions with demographic, geographic, employment status and diary day controls give an adjusted gender gap of 210.0 minutes in unpaid work and 88.7 minutes in combined burden. The gap in unpaid work is 145.2 minutes larger among currently married workers. It is smaller among regular salaried and urban workers, and it varies widely across States. A threefold Oaxaca Blinder decomposition attributes only 3.1 percent of the raw gap to observed characteristics. The results hold when unpaid family helpers are excluded and when the sample is restricted by diary day type and age. These are associations, not causal effects. Labour market entry and an equal distribution of total work are distinct outcomes, so policy on women's employment must address care and household time as well as access to jobs.
venue: International Journal of Business and Management (IJBM)

title: УПРАВЛІННЯ БРЕНДИНГОМ НА РИНКУ АВТЕНТИЧНИХ ТОВАРІВ З ВИКОРИСТАННЯМ ІНСТРУМЕНТІВ ЦИФРОВОГО МАРКЕТИНГУ
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and practical aspects of branding management in the market of authentic goods under the conditions of digital transformation. The study substantiates that branding has evolved from a traditional marketing instrument into a strategic intangible asset that enables enterprises to create sustainable competitive advantages, strengthen consumer trust, and enhance long-term market performance. Particular attention is paid to the specific features of branding authentic products, where the key determinants of success include verified product origin, cultural and historical heritage, quality, transparency, and emotional engagement with consumers. Based on the analysis of contemporary scientific approaches to branding and brand management, the paper proposes an integrated algorithm for branding management in the authentic goods market. The algorithm includes market analysis, identification of authentic product attributes, development of the brand platform, creation of brand identity, implementation of marketing communications, trust building, brand promotion, performance monitoring, and continuous brand development. It is argued that digital marketing plays a cross-functional role throughout all stages of the branding process and significantly enhances communication efficiency and customer engagement. The study also systematizes the most influential di…

title: ANALYSIS OF THE TRANSFORMATION OF THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC MECHANISM OF STATE SUPPORT FOR THE POPULATION OF UKRAINE UNDER WAR CONDITIONS
abstract: The article analyzes the transformation of the socio-economic mechanism of state support for the population of Ukraine under war conditions. It substantiates the need to shift from a predominantly compensatory model toward an adaptive, targeted and integrated system of state support. The main components of this mechanism are examined, including financial assistance, social services, housing support, medical and psychological rehabilitation, professional adaptation, employment and economic integration. Particular attention is paid to veterans, their family members, and the families of fallen Defenders and Defendresses of Ukraine. The main areas of their financial and socio-economic support are analyzed, including housing, rehabilitation, employment, professional adaptation and veteran entrepreneurship. The study emphasizes the importance of targeted financing, digitalization of social services, individualized case management and improved coordination between public authorities and local governments. Further transformation should be based on targeting, integration and adaptability to support human capital recovery and sustainable post-war recovery in Ukraine.

title: ІНСТИТУЦІЙНА ДЕЗІНТЕРМЕДІАЦІЯ ЯК ІНСТРУМЕНТ МІНІМІЗАЦІЇ ТРАНСАКЦІЙНИХ ВИТРАТ ЕКОНОМІКИ УКРАЇНИ В УМОВАХ ІНДУСТРІЇ 4.0
abstract: The article provides a comprehensive theoretical and methodological substantiation of the conceptual foundations for overcoming digital managerialism and algorithmic bureaucracy within Ukraine’s economy through institutional disintermediation under Industry 4.0. It is argued that the current neoliberal model of financial digitalization has created a severe structural mismatch, masquerading as transactional efficiency while driving the decoupling of fictitious capital from real-sector material reproduction. Under conditions of severe industrial degradation, this model fosters destructive economic gentrification, draining vital resources away from hard-tech enterprises, domestic manufacturers and the defense-industrial complex. The paper exposes the institutional nature of algorithmic bureaucracy, exemplified by supranational compliance and ESG standards, which operate as an implicit "tax on complexity" by shifting enterprise resources toward unproductive administrative functions. The research identifies critical macroeconomic risks stemming from these distortions: the "two-speed economy" effect, local inflation in service-oriented digital hubs, systemic vulnerability due to the volatility of symbolic capital and human capital loss through intellectual emigration. To address these challenges, the author conceptualizes the transition toward a decentralized production-integrated ec…

title: Impact of Quick Commerce on Grocery Buying Behaviour: Evidence from an Emerging Indian Urban Market
abstract: Purpose: Quick commerce platforms offering ultra-fast delivery have transformed grocery retail ecosystems. This study investigates their influence on grocery buying behaviour in an emerging Indian city context. Design/Methodology/Approach: Primary data were collected from 109 consumers in Nagpur city using a structured questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, chi-square testing, and regression analysis were employed to examine relationships among platform usage, customer satisfaction, demographic factors, and willingness to pay premium delivery charges. Findings: Results indicate that quick commerce complements rather than replaces traditional grocery shopping. Customer satisfaction does not significantly influence willingness to pay additional delivery charges, suggesting persistent price sensitivity. Age shows only marginal influence on adoption behaviour. Research Implications: The study extends omnichannel retail theory to quick commerce settings in emerging markets. Practical Implications: Quick commerce firms should emphasize convenience positioning while maintaining competitive pricing strategies. Originality/Value: Provides empirical evidence from a tier-II Indian city, a context underrepresented in quick commerce research.
venue: International Journal of Innovations & Research Analysis

title: ОРГАНІЗАЦІЙНО-УПРАВЛІНСЬКІ МЕХАНІЗМИ АНТИКРИЗОВОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ ПІДПРИЄМСТВОМ В УМОВАХ ВОЄННИХ ВИКЛИКІВ
abstract: The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of enterprise anti-crisis management under wartime challenges, high uncertainty, and transformation of the external environment. The necessity of shifting from predominantly reactive responses to crisis phenomena toward a continuous preventive system of strategic management integrated with risk management, scenario forecasting, digital transformation, and business continuity management is substantiated. Based on a critical analysis of contemporary scientific approaches, the content of the concept of “enterprise anti-crisis management” is clarified, the main factors determining its effectiveness are systematized, and the relationship between strategic and tactical objectives at different stages of crisis development is determined. The authors propose a methodology for implementing an enterprise anti-crisis strategic planning system, which involves a consistent sequence of setting goals and objectives, developing an information and analytical base, conducting comprehensive crisis diagnostics, assessing risks, identifying priorities for anti-crisis measures, scenario modelling, implementing management measures, monitoring, and adjusting managerial decisions. Unlike the traditional financial approach, the proposed methodology provides for a comprehensive assessment of the financial, production, human resources, log…

title: ОБЛІКОВО-АНАЛІТИЧНЕ ЗАБЕЗПЕЧЕННЯ ЗОВНІШНЬОЕКОНОМІЧНОЇ ДІЯЛЬНОСТІ: ІНТЕГРАЦІЯ ПОДАТКОВОГО ТА УПРАВЛІНСЬКОГО ОБЛІКУ
abstract: The relevance of the topic lies in the need to develop integrated accounting and analytical support for foreign economic activity, combining tax and management accounting to improve information quality, control tax implications, and ensure effective management decisions. The purpose of the article is to substantiate the theoretical and methodological foundations of accounting and analytical support for foreign economic activity through the integration of tax and management accounting. The objectives of the research article are to: reveal the essence of accounting and analytical support for foreign economic activity; define the role of tax accounting within the system of foreign economic activity; substantiate the importance of management accounting for control and decision-making; propose an approach to integrating tax and management accounting into a unified information system. The article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of accounting and analytical support for an enterprise’s foreign economic activity through the integration of tax and management accounting. It is substantiated that, under conditions of increasingly complex international business transactions, stronger tax regulation, and growing managerial risks, the formation of a unified information system becomes especially important, as it ensures the timely identification, systematization, and an…

title: ОСНОВНІ ТЕОРІЇ ОПОДАТКУВАННЯ ТА ЇХ РОЛЬ У ФОРМУВАННІ СУЧАСНОЇ ПОДАТКОВОЇ ПОЛІТИКИ
abstract: This article examines the evolution of theories of taxation and their impact on the formation of the state’s modern tax policy. It summarizes academic approaches to defining the nature and purpose of taxes, and explores the characteristics of classical tax theory, the benefit theory, the ability-to-pay theory, as well as Keynesian, monetarist, and institutional theories. It is demonstrated that modern tax policy is not based on the provisions of any single theory, but is shaped through the integration of various theoretical concepts, which ensures the fulfillment of the fiscal, regulatory, social, incentive, and control functions of taxes. A comparative analysis of the impact of major taxation theories on the formation of modern tax policy was conducted, and the specific features of their practical application in the context of the developing digital economy were identified. The interrelationship between the evolution of taxation theories, the principles of tax system design, tax policy instruments, and tax administration mechanisms was systematized. The authors propose a model for transforming tax theories into modern state tax policy, which reflects the sequence of the transition from scientific concepts to principles of taxation, the formulation of tax policy, the implementation of the tax mechanism, the conduct of tax administration, and the evaluation of the tax system’s p…

title: ESG-ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ БАНКІВСЬКОГО СЕКТОРУ УКРАЇНИ: СУЧАСНІ ТЕНДЕНЦІЇ, ІНСТРУМЕНТИ ТА ПЕРСПЕКТИВИ РОЗВИТКУ
abstract: The article examines the current state, key trends, and prospects of ESG transformation in Ukraine’s banking sector amid wartime challenges, economic instability, and deepening European integration. It is substantiated that the implementation of environmental, social, and governance principles is gradually shifting from a voluntary practice to an important element of banks’ strategic management, risk assessment, and long-term financial stability. The role of the National Bank of Ukraine in shaping the institutional environment for sustainable finance and integrating ESG factors into banking regulation and supervision is considered. The main instruments of ESG transformation are analyzed, including green finance, lending to sustainable development projects, ESG scoring, environmental and social risk assessment, non-financial reporting, responsible corporate governance, and digital technologies. The practical implementation of ESG approaches by leading Ukrainian banks is examined, and directions for their further development are outlined. It is established that the environmental component is developing most dynamically, particularly through the financing of energy efficiency, renewable energy, and economic recovery projects, while the social and governance components require further development. The main barriers to this process are identified, including insufficient regulatory c…

title: Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange
abstract: Unlocking Value Through Nonprofit Resource Sharing Nonprofit organizations often operate under tight budgets while idle equipment, unused space, and shareable skills and expertise are frequently underutilized, with existing resource exchanges in the nonprofit sector limited to bilateral barter or relatively homogeneous resources. In “Community-Oriented Market Design for Nonprofit Resource Exchange,” Huang et al. propose Sharing With a Purpose (SWAP), a resource-sharing system that enables nonprofits to exchange heterogeneous resources without monetary payments. SWAP combines an auction-based process, SWAPcredit valuation, and integer optimization to facilitate multilateral exchanges, allowing nonprofits to obtain needed resources by contributing resources of their own. The authors implement this market design through the SWAP Hub, a digital platform deployed with nonprofit communities in multiple regions. Through repeated exchange episodes, participating organizations have shared not only physical assets but also a wide range of skills, services, and expertise, including marketing, management, event planning, and organizational development. The study demonstrates how innovative market design can unlock latent value in community resources, alleviate resource constraints, and encourage new connections and collaboration among nonprofit organizations.

title: Capital Market Pricing of Audit Quality Attributes
abstract: Audit quality is widely regarded as a crucial external governance mechanism that impacts firms' capital costs. However, there is still limited evidence on the economic consequences of different audit quality attributes. Drawing on the information intermediary and signalling role of auditing, this study examines how audit quality attributes influence firms' cost of capital. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms between 2018 and 2023, this study employs a two-way fixed effects model to examine five audit quality attributes: auditor size, industry specialization, auditor change, audit tenure, and audit opinion. The results show that auditor size and industry specialists are associated with lower cost of capital, but their effects differ across financing markets. This study extends the literature on the economic consequences of audit quality and provides practical insights for firms and regulators in emerging markets.
venue: International Journal of Information Technologies and Systems Approach

title: Sociocultural Conditions and Health-Service Access Challenges in the Javaé Community of Boa Esperança Village, Tocantins, Brazil: A Qualitative Study for Local Diagnosis and Public Policy Implications
abstract: Aims: To analyse the social, cultural, educational and environmental conditions of the Javaé (Inỹ) community of Boa Esperança Village on Bananal Island, Tocantins, Brazil, and to identify locally reported challenges and assets relevant to public policy and community-led initiatives. Study Design: Descriptive qualitative field study with a structured village-level identification component. Place and Duration of Study: Boa Esperança Village, municipality of Lagoa da Confusão, state of Tocantins, Brazil, between August and September 2024, in articulation with the University of Gurupi (UnirG). Methodology: Data were produced through three analytic sources: a Village Identification Form recording 141 residents in 40 households, semi-structured interviews with three purposively selected community leaders (the chief, the deputy chief and a female elder), and participant observation recorded in a field diary. Analysis primarily involved deductive thematic content analysis across seven predefined axes, with multi-source comparison used to identify convergence and divergence. A community assembly supported collective authorisation and contextual confirmation of the broad priority domains but was not treated as a fourth independently coded dataset. Results: The village-level form recorded a young age structure, with 87 of 141 residents (61.7%) aged 0-14 years and 18 residents aged 60 year…
