Assessing primary health care facilities in six prioritized Nigerian states: Linking facility readiness with service availability
abstract: Background Nigeria’s poor health indicators have been linked to its dysfunctional Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities. Policy gaps remain in achieving sustainable and equitable provision of PHC for Nigerians. Therefore, this study examined the relationship between health facilities’ readiness and service provision in Nigeria. Methods This was a cross-sectional assessment of 204 PHC facilities enrolled under the Basic Health Care Provision Fund program, in six prioritized states in Nigeria. The facilities were assessed for the provision of ≥80% of the three levels of primary healthcare services—Tier 1, Tier 2, Tier 3—as the outcome variables. The three tiers represent the minimum, intermediate, and comprehensive levels of essential PHC services, respectively, defined under Nigeria’s Minimum Service Package. Health Facility (HF) readiness (explanatory variable) was assessed across six domains, with five of the domains disaggregated into 3 levels (poor, fair, and good). Data were analysed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and multivariable logistic regression model (alpha = 0.05). Results The majority (81.9%) of the HFs have a functional management committee, 54.4% have an updated BHCPF annual quality improvement plan, 81.9% have standard operating procedures. While 16.2% met the World Health Organization standard ≥2.3 Health Care Workers (HCWs)/1000 population, none met t…

title: Mathematical Anticipation and Representational Coordination Within Van Hiele Levels: Evidence From Pre‐Service Teachers Learning Linear Equations
abstract: ABSTRACT This research examines how pre‐service mathematics teachers coordinate algebraic and graphical representations when solving linear‐equation problems. Particular attention is given to mathematical anticipation, including predictions, intermediate results, and verification as participants move between representations. A qualitative interpretive design was used with 126 pre‐service mathematics teachers working in 15 heterogeneous groups. Each group included participants representing the five van Hiele levels of geometric thinking: visualization, analysis, informal deduction, deduction, and rigor. Written and graphical solution artifacts from all groups were examined, and retrospective interviews were used to clarify participants' reasoning. Three representative cases were selected to capture distinctive patterns in the artifacts. The analysis identified three patterns of reasoning: separation of algebraic and graphical representations, emerging but incomplete coordination, and integrated coordination supported by prediction and verification. Across the cases, mathematical anticipation ranged from limited expectations to predictions that guided subsequent actions and were checked against information from other representations. The results indicate that spatial reasoning in linear‐equation problem solving involves more than producing or interpreting graphs. It also involves…

title: The impact and value of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management of patients with cervical cancer with service evaluation audited against national evidence-based PET-CT guidelines
abstract: Purpose First, to assess the diagnostic value of fluorine-18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET-computed tomography ([ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT) compared with conventional MRI and/or CT. Second, to audit the clinical indications for referring patients with cervical cancer for [ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT against the 2022 guidelines published by the Royal College of Radiologists and the Royal College of Physicians. Finally, to evaluate the impact of [ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT on management plans. Methods A retrospective cohort study of 49 patients with histologically proven cervical cancer across the Sussex Cancer Network underwent 59 [ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT between 1 November 2020 and 31 October 2022. Scans were compared with the most recent CT and MRI scan conducted within 4 months of the [ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT. Scan indications were categorized as either ‘in accordance’ or ‘outside’ the guidelines. Those in accordance fell into one of four groups: staging, response assessment, suspected recurrence, or staging when considering exenterative surgery. A questionnaire investigating the impact of the [ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT on the management plan of each patient was answered by one clinical oncology consultant. Results [ 18 F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guide…

title: Molecular Detection and Codetection of Lower Genital Tract Microorganisms among Women Attending an STI Referral Service in the Brazilian Amazon
abstract: Among 133 women attending an STI referral service in the Brazilian Amazon, multiplex real-time PCR identified a heterogeneous microbiological profile, including STI pathogens, bacterial vaginosis-associated microorganisms, Candida species, and frequent codetection. Clinical and epidemiological characteristics showed variable associations, while self-reported vaginal discharge had limited ability to distinguish specific molecular findings.
authors: Maria das Graças Vale Barbosa Guerra

title: Legal Regulation of Forest Therapy in Healthcare: Implications for Professional Practice in Lithuania and the Republic of Korea
abstract: Background/Objectives: This article examines legal and professional challenges related to legal regulation of forest therapy. It explores the legal and institutional frameworks governing professional forest therapy and their implications for professional qualifications, access to practice, and the organization of professional activities in Lithuania and the Republic of Korea. It also illustrates regulatory models and examples of certification practices for forest therapy professionals in the European Union (EU) and third countries, provided by public and private bodies. This study identifies similarities and differences in professional forest therapy training and qualification requirements, and considers their potential implications for professional responsibility and protecting service users. Methods: A structured comparative legal analysis of legal and documentary sources was conducted, complemented by a structured analysis of scientific literature. Results: Forest therapy is regulated through diverse, often non-harmonized legal and professional frameworks. Differences exist in the legal definition of the practice, practitioner qualifications and training, and certification and accreditation procedures. These differences may affect access to professional practice, professional accountability, and safeguards for users, especially where professional forest therapy is provided i…

title: Regulation of Sugar Content and Glass Transition in Jujube Slices via CP-Assisted Pulsed Vacuum Drying: Effects on Physicochemical Properties and Blood Glucose Regulation
abstract: Although red dates (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) are rich in nutrients and have both edible and medicinal properties, during the drying process, due to their high sugar content, they often result in a lower glass transition temperature (Tg), enhanced hygroscopicity, surface agglomeration, and a decline in storage quality, severely limiting the shelf stability of the products and the improvement of the processing quality. Cold plasma (CP) can form cavities through surface etching, promoting water migration, thereby increasing the drying rate and diffusion coefficient. Vacuum pulsation drying (PVD) has a higher drying rate, stronger mass transfer ability, and better quality retention effect compared to ordinary drying methods. Based on these characteristics, we believe that CP and PVD have a synergistic enhancing effect in the drying of date slices. Therefore, in this study, CK-PVD (without plasma pre-treatment, direct vacuum pulsation drying) was used as the control group, and CP-PVD (after plasma pre-treatment, vacuum pulsation drying), A1, A2, and A3 (after plasma treatment, soaking in different concentrations of ethanol and then vacuum pulsation drying) were used as experimental groups to study the effects of CP pre-treatment combined with ethanol extraction on the sugar composition, glass transition temperature (Tg), physical stability, and reduce blood sugar activity of dried dat…

title: Establishment of an Efficient Softwood Cutting Propagation System for Prunus salicina Lindl. via Plant Growth Regulators and Agronomic Regulation
abstract: Plum is an economically important stone fruit crop worldwide, but its industrial production is limited by low propagation efficiency and disadvantages associated with conventional grafting. This study established a softwood cutting system for three elite Nai plum cultivars (‘Shibanwannai’, ‘Huangguanli’, and ‘Zaofurong’). Gradient concentrations of two plant growth regulators (PGRs), NAA and ABT, were tested in combination with integrated agronomic practices, including girdling pretreatment, a tested growing substrate formulation, and staged moisture management. The results showed that 100 mg·L−1 NAA and 150 mg·L−1 ABT yielded relatively high seedling survival rates (78% to 85%) and promoted the formation of well-developed mixed adventitious root systems. Distinct cultivar-specific differences in sensitivity to PGRs were detected among the three cultivars. This softwood cutting protocol shortens the nursery cycle to 3–4 months, compared with 18–24 months required by traditional grafting. The established high-efficiency cutting method supports standardized nursery production and may facilitate the sustainable development of the Nai plum industry.

Gain-Scheduled Internal Model Control of Full-Bridge CLLC Resonant Converters for Wide-Range CC/CV Regulation: A Simulation-Based Study
abstract: This paper proposes a gain-scheduled internal model control (GS-IMC) strategy for wide-range constant-voltage (CV) and constant-current (CC) regulation of a full-bridge CLLC resonant converter. The symmetric CLLC resonant network inherently enables zero-voltage switching (ZVS) of the primary-side switches; the contribution of this work lies in the control-oriented modeling and regulation of the converter under pulse-frequency modulation (PFM). Traditional first-harmonic approximation (FHA) models neglect the dominant pole formed by the output capacitance and load resistance and lose accuracy far from resonance, which limits their usefulness for closed-loop design. To overcome these limitations, the nonlinear voltage-gain and frequency-sensitivity characteristics of the converter are characterized over the full range of switching frequency and load using Piecewise Linear Electrical Circuit Simulation (PLECS). The resulting small-signal sensitivities are stored in two-dimensional (2D) lookup tables, from which the parameters of the internal plant model are scheduled according to the measured operating point, without online parameter estimation. The IMC controller is then derived from the scheduled model, so a single filter time constant sets the closed-loop response at all operating points. Simulation results on a 750-V/11-kW converter show that, for CV regulation from 330 V to 9…

title: Modeling finishing pig growth performance and carcass response to dietary net energy using ingredient nutrient values from four different databases
abstract: Abstract Data from 91 grow-finish pig experiments with diets differing in net energy (NE) and other nutrients were used in a meta-analysis to model growth performance and carcass characteristics based on the diet's NE, crude protein (CP), standardized ileal digestible (SID) Lys, neutral detergent fiber (NDF), and lysine to NE (Lys:NE) ratio. Energy and nutrient concentrations in all diets were determined using values from four different databases (NRC, 2012 [NRC]; CVB, 2022 [CVB]; INRA, 2024 [INRA]; Rostagno et al., 2024 [BR]). Stepwise selection using Akaike information criteria was used for model selection considering the linear, quadratic, and interactive effects of NE, SID Lys, CP, NDF, Lys:NE ratio, and body weight. Model variable predictors were generated using a linear mixed model. Selected models indicated that ADG and G:F increased as dietary NE increases in the four databases evaluated. However, the magnitude of response in G:F differed between ingredient databases at the early and late stages of the finishing period. The model using BR database appears to overestimate ADG when diets with concentrations of NDF are used. The 4 models predicted greater changes in ADG and G:F when the Lys:NE ratio was maintained compared to when a constant SID Lys level was used. title: Impact of Incremental Loading on Instrumentation Response in a Full-Scale Railroad Test Section Trafficked with a Heavy-Vehicle Simulator
abstract: Rail is a key infrastructure component for military asset movement, and the design and evaluation of these rail structures is important to ensure adequate support for military loading conditions. The current military design methodologies are outlined in U.S. Department of Defense Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-860-1 Railroad Design and Evaluation ; however, there is a need to advance current practices toward a more robust mechanistic-empirical design methodology. To support this effort, a full-scale test section was constructed to collect controlled instrumentation response data at applied loads ranging from 10 to 100 kips, primarily to assess the impact of a relatively stiff subgrade (10 California bearing ratio [CBR]) and a relatively weak subgrade (2 CBR) on track structural response. Instrumentation included earth pressure cells at various locations in the track structure, deflectometers in the subgrade, and strain gauges on the rail. The response data were analyzed and comparisons were made between the measured response values and the calculated response values from the existing military design methodologies. It was found that the subgrade support had a meaningful impact on measured stress, and that the measured stress was approximately 30% higher in the 10 CBR test item than in the 2 CBR test item. Deflection data indicated that plastic deformation occurred in the we…

title: The green paradox of on-demand adaptation: how digital delivery amplifies urban carbon and material burdens
abstract: Abstract With the rapid expansion of digital on-demand services, urban residents increasingly rely on platforms as a primary adaptation to extreme heat. However, the resource implications of this shift—specifically the "green paradox" where protective behavior accelerates material and energy consumption—remain poorly quantified. Drawing on transaction-level food-delivery records for 100 Chinese cities (2017–2019, 2023), we show that heat shocks trigger nonlinear surges in delivery demand, concentrated in midday peaks. By integrating these orders with a system-wide accounting of last-mile transport and packaging-related emissions, we quantify how behavioral responses propagate through urban metabolic systems. We find that delivery-related CO$_2$ emissions rise more than twice as fast as demand volume, reflecting the combined influence of last-mile transport and packaging-related emissions. This elasticity gap widens in digitally dense cities with carbon-intensive grids and inefficient packaging standards. We formalize this imbalance as the Urban Green Paradox: individual heat avoidance is achieved by shifting burdens to material-intensive infrastructures. These results reveal that digital adaptation amplifies urban resource intensity under current regimes. Targeted interventions, including enforcing reusable packaging and fleet electrification, offer pathways to realign digital …

This study examined the longitudinal development of sprint performance in youth soccer players across different stages of biological maturation. Forty male soccer players (ages 10–16) were categorized into pre-peak height velocity (PHV) and circa-PHV groups based on maturity offset values estimated using the Mirwald equation. Sprinting speed was assessed using a 30-m sprint test. A linear mixed model analysis revealed significant improvements in sprint performance over time ( p < 0.002, d = 0.78), with the circa-PHV group consistently outperforming the pre-PHV group ( p < 0.001, d = 0.43). There was no significant time × maturity interaction ( p = 0.722), indicating that the rate of change in sprint performance over the 12-month interval did not differ between pre- and circa-PHV players. These findings support the critical role of biological maturity in sprint progression, as more mature athletes demonstrated faster 30-m sprint performance. However, this study does not support the notion that sprinting develops at a significantly higher rate dur…

title: Evaluating automated pollen monitoring for thunderstorm asthma and public health forecasting: a comparative study in Melbourne, Australia
abstract: Abstract High-quality pollen measurements are essential for effective environmental monitoring and reliable public health forecasting. Automated pollen counters offer continuous, high-resolution observations that have the potential to reduce reliance on labour-intensive manual microscopy, but their performance must be evaluated against established methods. This study evaluates the performance of the SwisensPoleno Mars by comparing its daily and sub-daily pollen measurements of total pollen, and the two dominant airborne pollen types in Melbourne, grass and cypress, with those from a co-located Burkard Hirst-type spore trap at the University of Melbourne over the 92-day spring monitoring period in 2022. Data from the automated system showed a strong linear relationship with the co-located manual trap, with coefficients of determination ( R 2 ) of 0.92 for total daily pollen counts, 0.92 for grass pollen, and 0.86 for cypress pollen. Grass pollen measurements, which are central to epidemic thunderstorm asthma (ETSA) risk forecasting in Victoria, showed particularly high correspondence, including consistent classification into low, moderate, and high operational thresholds. The SwisensPoleno Mars also reproduced expected diurnal variation in pollen concentrations, demonstrating its ability to capture short-term changes in airborne pollen levels. These results indicate that automat…

title: Price Is a Feature of Person-Centered Abortion Care
abstract: Abstract Schroeder and colleagues contribute to the understanding of person-centered abortion care by examining preferences for telemedicine and facility-based medication abortion care. We argue that because cost was very or extremely important to three-quarters of participants, price should itself be treated as a feature of care, and studies of patient preferences should attend to the actual prices patients face across care options.

title: Namir Abdel Messeeh, dir. Life After Siham . 2025. 80 minutes. Arabic and French, with French subtitles. France and Egypt. Oweda Films and Les Films d’ici. Distributed by Météore Films. No price reported.
The just price: a market-process account
abstract: Abstract When is a price just? This paper develops a new theory of justice in pricing, grounded in the Austrian market process tradition. Prices, I argue, are not merely outcomes to be evaluated against an external standard of fairness. They are instruments through which the competitive process performs morally significant functions: communicating information, generating incentives and coordinating the plans of millions under pervasive ignorance. When this process is operating, the prices it produces carry a genuine presumption of justice. I establish this claim through two complementary arguments and demonstrate its power across cases from price gouging to wages to monopoly.

title: Toward a standard lexicon for ecological forecasting
abstract: Unprecedented environmental changes challenge our understanding of the natural world, yet critical environmental decisions are made every day. Ecological forecasting provides a mechanism to inform science‐based decision‐making amid accelerating environmental uncertainties by using foundational forecasting principles to anticipate ecological unknowns. However, as an emerging and interdisciplinary field, ecological forecasting lacks unified terminology, limiting cohesion and hindering communication across other forecasting subdisciplines. Here, we examined current use of common forecasting terms by surveying forecasting professionals ( n = 109) and synthesizing literature trends (Scopus; 1970–2025) and internet search queries (Google Trends; 2004–2024). Our results informed the development of standardized definitions for “forecast”, “prediction”, and “projection”, and illuminated a disconnect between the goal of aiding decision‐making and the inclusion of decision science in the forecasting process. This work promotes participation and growth in ecological forecasting, helping forecasters meet priority end goals by facilitating communication across forecasting disciplines and within forecasting processes.
venue: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment

title: ARGUS Survey of AI Driven Personal Finance Analytics and Budget Forecasting
abstract: Personal-finance software is useful only when it can move from records to decisions without hiding uncertainty. We reviewed 25 papers published in 2025 and 2026 and grouped their evidence into six connected activities: UNDERSTAND, ANTICIPATE, PERSONALIZE, ADVISE, EXPLAIN, and TRUST. For every paper, we recorded the study design, data, method, reported result, limitation, and relevance to ARGUS. The stated review window runs from 1 January 2025 to 30 September 2026, while the locked-corpus audit was completed on 22 September 2026. The study set contains 11 observational surveys, six human experiments, four audits of model output, two computational studies, and two reviews. This distribution matters because only P02 directly evaluates both personal transaction classification and budget prediction. The remaining evidence is strongest on advice, adoption, privacy, vulnerability, explanation, and trust. We therefore do not treat an adoption coefficient or a favorable user rating as proof that a budgeting model works. We also compare the literature with the inspected ARGUS implementation. The current project uses deterministic categorization, exact-money arithmetic, budget comparisons, and answers grounded in the user ledger; it does not contain a trained forecasting model. Archived project records report 205 passing automated tests, acceptable grounded responses for ten controlled q…

title: Class-Conditional Allocation of Forecasting Models for Retail Inventory Replenishment: Evidence from an ABC-Segmented Hardware Portfolio
abstract: Background: Retail inventories are heterogeneous, yet demand forecasting studies typically select one model for an entire portfolio, leaving open how forecasting effort should be allocated across inventory segments. Methods: Six models—ARIMA, SARIMA, ARIMAX, Random Forest, LightGBM and an LSTM network—were estimated on weekly demand for a Colombian hardware retailer (35,399 transactions, 1633 SKUs, January 2025–March 2026). Because 95.5% of items are intermittent or lumpy, models were fitted to three ABC-class-aggregated series of 60 observations, evaluated on a 12-week holdout and under a rolling-origin scheme, and compared against naive benchmarks using MASE and RMSSE. Results: The best model differs by class. In Class A a statistical specification wins, ARIMAX on the holdout (RMSE 843 units per week) but ARIMA under rolling origins, the two being statistically indistinguishable. Random Forest is best in Class B (255). In Class C no model improves on a last-value rule (75 against 66). Relative to that benchmark, error falls to 39.8% in Class A and 47.6% in Class B. Diebold–Mariano tests separate 16 of 45 pairs on the holdout and three of 30 under rolling origins. Conclusions: Allocating models by inventory class is operationally justified rather than statistically decisive, and the low-turnover class warrants no model at all.

title: Electricity Consumption, Human Development and Economic Growth Nexus in Nigeria: Evidence From the ARDL Approach
abstract: Electricity remains a critical driver of socioeconomic transformation, yet Nigeria continues to experience persistent electricity shortages despite abundant energy resources. This study examines the nexus between electricity consumption, human development and economic growth in Nigeria. Specifically, the study investigates the effects of Electricity Consumption Per Capita (ECPC), Gross Fixed Capital Formation (GFCF), Human Development Index (HDI), Total Primary Electricity Consumption (TPEC), and Government Capital Expenditure (GCE) on Real Gross Domestic Product (RGDP). Annual time-series data were analyzed using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) approach. The Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) and Phillips-Perron (PP) tests were employed to examine the stationarity properties of the variables, while the ARDL Bounds testing technique was applied to establish long-run relationships. The Error Correction Model (ECM), diagnostic tests and Granger causality analysis were also conducted. The findings revealed that Electricity Consumption Per Capita and Total Primary Electricity Consumption have negative and statistically insignificant relationships with economic growth in Nigeria. Human Development Index has a positive but insignificant relationship with economic growth, while Gross Fixed Capital Formation contributes positively but with limited immediate impact. The Error Corre…

title: FDMSNet: A frequency-decomposed multi-scale hybrid framework for renewable energy power forecasting
abstract: Accurate renewable energy power forecasting is of great significance for the safe operation, dispatch optimization, and efficient management of modern power systems. However, wind and photovoltaic power generation series usually exhibit significant non-stationarity, volatility, and multi-scale variation characteristics, posing great challenges to medium- and long-term forecasting. To address these issues, this paper proposes FDMSNet, a frequency-decomposed multi-scale hybrid network for renewable energy power forecasting. The model first divides the input sequence into non-stationary and stationary components through a frequency decomposition module. For the non-stationary component, a multilayer perceptron is adopted to extract global nonlinear variation features. For the stationary component, a multi-scale forecasting module is designed based on multi-branch downsampling and cross-scale prediction fusion. Subsequently, the forecasting results of different components are fused to generate the final power prediction. Experiments are conducted on real-world wind farm and photovoltaic power station datasets under multiple prediction horizons. MAE, MSE, and RSE are used as evaluation metrics, and FDMSNet is compared with different types of forecasting models. The experimental results show that FDMSNet achieves strong forecasting accuracy and stability in both wind and photovoltaic…

Actions of Pharmaceutical Lactones and Lactams on the Enzymes with Lactonase Activity: In Silico Prediction and In Vitro Study
abstract: Pharmaceutical pollutants that contain lactone or lactam rings in their structure are frequently detected in wastewater. Enzymes with lactonase activity, synthesized by the microorganisms in aerobic activated sludge, are expected to be able to participate in the hydrolysis of these pharmaceutical pollutants, but the actual activity of many lactonases towards such compounds remains poorly characterized. In this work, a systematic molecular docking study of 12 enzymes and 39 pharmaceutical pollutants (β-lactam antibiotics, macrolides, coumarins, statins) was undertaken. The binding affinity, active-site occupancy, total enzyme surface occupancy and geometric characteristics of the molecules (the distance from the catalytic nucleophile to the carbonyl carbon of the lactone ring, and the attack angle formed between the nucleophilic atom of the enzyme and the C–N/C–O bond of the substrate) were evaluated in silico for a set of hydrolases displaying lactonase activity (AidC, AaL, hexahistidine-tagged organophosphate hydrolase (His6-OPH), etc.) and metallo-β-lactamases (MβLs) (NDM-1, MIM-1, SAM-1). Lactamases exhibited favorable intermolecular interaction geometry for the majority of β-lactams. title: Prediction of Lindane-Induced Breast Cancer Toxicity Through Multi-Target Network Analysis and Mechanistic Investigation
abstract: This study aimed to identify potential molecular targets associated with Lindane-induced molecular alterations in breast cancer and elucidate its toxicological mechanisms using an integrated strategy combining network toxicology, machine learning, molecular simulation, and experimental validation. Lindane-related targets and breast cancer transcriptomic data were collected from public databases, and differentially expressed genes and WGCNA-derived hub genes were integrated to identify candidate targets. GO and KEGG analyses were performed to explore biological functions, while machine learning models and SHAP analysis were applied to screen potential biomarkers. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations were conducted to evaluate the interaction between Lindane and key proteins. Twenty-eight overlapping targets were identified and mainly enriched in lipid metabolism, sphingolipid signaling, and p53-related pathways. The LASSO-plsRglm model achieved the highest average AUC (0.996) and identified five candidate genes, including NR3C2, AR, TGM2, ATAD2, and P2RY2. NR3C2 exhibited strong discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.982) and was consistently downregulated in breast cancer tissues. Integrated Clinical, Respiratory and Biomarker Prediction of Mortality in Patients with Severe COVID-19 Pneumonia Treated with Convalescent Plasma: Development and Internal Validation of Prognostic Models
abstract: Background: Mortality risk among patients with severe COVID-19 is determined by interacting clinical, respiratory and systemic factors. This study evaluated whether routinely available respiratory and biomarker information could provide incremental prognostic information in a cohort of patients treated with convalescent plasma (CCP). Methods: A secondary prognostic modelling analysis was performed using data from 376 consecutive patients with severe COVID-19 pneumonia treated with CCP at ULSS 3 Serenissima, Italy. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Sequential multivariable models were developed using Firth penalised logistic regression. Two parallel severity pathways were evaluated: Berlin severity (Model 5A) and ventilatory support (Model 5B). Both pathways incorporated tachypnoea >30/min, PaO₂/FiO₂ <200, raised Cystatin C, BNP and hs-cTnI. Internal validation used 2,000 bootstrap resamples with optimism correction; calibration and decision-curve analysis were also assessed. Results: There were 97 deaths (25.8%). Tachypnoea and PaO₂/FiO₂ <200 provided strong incremental prognostic information. Cystatin C was the first biomarker retained, followed by BNP and hs-cTnI; galectin-3 did not add significant information after these biomarkers. Apparent AUCs were 0.9560 for Model 5A and 0.9656 for Model 5B; optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.9315 and 0.9457, respectively. …

title: Prediction of Air Pollutant Concentrations by Selected Neural Network Architectures
abstract: Air pollution currently represents a significant environmental challenge with a direct impact on both public health and ecosystems. One of the aims of this paper is to predict the concentration of particulate matter PM10 and CO2 in the air using machine learning methods, specifically by employing various types of neural networks, including feedforward, convolutional, and recurrent models. The aim is also to compare the performance of these architectures in processing univariate time series with different temporal resolutions (monthly, hourly). The study uses real data from the Slovak Hydrometeorological Institute (SHMÚ) and modelled emissions from the EDGAR database. The models were trained, optimized, and evaluated using standard error metrics. The results showed that Conv1D models achieved the highest accuracy on hourly data of PM10, while feedforward architectures performed best on monthly national data of CO2. The findings confirm the potential of artificial intelligence methods as a tool for environmental monitoring and decision support in air quality protection. Opportunities for extending the models with meteorological variables and applying them in real-time warning systems are also discussed.

title: Advancements of propulsion systems for zero-emission buses - approach for effective prediction of energy consumption
abstract: The article discusses selected advancements of propulsion systems for zero-emission buses focussing on their energy consumption under different climatic conditions. The special attention is paid on proposal of a method for analysis and prediction of the energy consumption of electric drive systems in public transport vehicles, developed in response to the rapid advancement of zero-emission technologies. Developed dedicated test bench enabling the replication of real operating conditions as well as the suitability of utilising telemetry data collected during vehicle operation for model validation and for identifying factors influencing energy efficiency are presented and discussed.

Design and Testing of an Autonomous Laser Weeding Robot with Cross-Modal Vibration Prediction for Cotton Fields
abstract: Laser weeding is a non-chemical, non-contact precision weeding method particularly suited for inter-row operations during the crop seedling stage. However, maintaining precise laser targeting on weed stems during dynamic field operation remains challenging. This task requires close coordination among perception, control, and actuation modules, while vehicle vibration from uneven terrain further degrades strike precision on the move. This paper presents a fully autonomous laser weeding robot for inter-row operation in cotton seedling fields, integrating weeding control, automatic mode switching, and autonomous navigation into a coordinated multi-process architecture. Vibration-induced strike deviation is mitigated by STCF-Net (Spatio-Temporal Cross-modal Fusion Network), a cross-modal prediction framework that fuses forward-looking depth maps with historical IMU signals to forecast vibration severity over a 3 s horizon. The prediction enables the control system to proactively adjust travel speed and weeding mode before encountering rough terrain, balancing precision and efficiency under dynamic field conditions. Field experiments validated weeding performance in static and dynamic scenarios and demonstrated that STCF-Net-guided predictive switching reduced operational time by 11.5% to 13.9% compared with a conservative baseline in two controlled experiments, with only a marginal…

title: Limited incremental value and cross-cohort transferability of CT radiomics for survival prediction after TACE in hepatocellular carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate whether pretreatment CT radiomics adds information for overall survival (OS) prediction among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated with transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), and assess frozen imaging-model performance in an independent cohort. Methods This retrospective study included 221 WAW-TACE and 98 HCC-TACE-SEG patients with pretreatment arterial and portal venous CT. Incremental value of a tumor-radiomics Random Survival Forest score (R1) beyond cohort-specific clinical Cox models (C0) was evaluated within each cohort using 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times. External validation was restricted to frozen WAW-trained R1 models (Top-K = 5, 10, 15) applied to HCC-TACE-SEG without refitting; the combined C0 + R1 model was not externally validated. Results WAW-TACE included 162 deaths and HCC-TACE-SEG 86 deaths. In WAW-TACE, C0, R1 Top-K = 15, and C0 + R1 achieved C-indices of 0.646 ± 0.043, 0.593 ± 0.049, and 0.639 ± 0.045, respectively. Corresponding HCC-TACE-SEG estimates were 0.496 ± 0.087, 0.530 ± 0.072, and 0.495 ± 0.094. Thus, R1 did not consistently improve cohort-specific clinical reference models. In frozen external application, Top-K = 5, 10, and 15 achieved C-indices of 0.463 (95% CI 0.397–0.532), 0.535 (0.468–0.608), and 0.528 (0.460–0.598), respectively. Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Cardiac Magnetic Resonance in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Diagnosis, Phenotypic Characterization, and Risk Prediction
abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a genetically and phenotypically heterogeneous myocardial disease associated with a broad spectrum of clinical outcomes, including heart failure, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) plays a central role in the comprehensive assessment of HCM by enabling integrated evaluation of myocardial morphology, ventricular and atrial function, tissue characterization, myocardial deformation, and longitudinal disease progression within a single comprehensive imaging modality. However, conventional CMR interpretation remains limited by manual post-processing, interobserver variability, sequence-dependent measurements, and reliance on a relatively restricted set of predefined imaging parameters. These limitations may hinder the full exploitation of the rich multidimensional information contained in CMR datasets. Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches, particularly machine learning and deep learning, together with radiomics-based quantitative image analysis, provide new opportunities to extend the diagnostic and prognostic value of CMR to extract high-dimensional and quantitative information from cine imaging, late gadolinium enhancement, parametric mapping, and feature-tracking-based deformation analysis. Emerging evidence suggests that AI-enhanced CMR may facilitate automated image ana…

title: Agent-Based Model for Surface Aerothermal Prediction Based on Ensemble Learning
abstract: This paper employs an ensemble learning algorithm to construct a surrogate model for predicting aerodynamic heat flux on hypersonic vehicle surfaces, based on the influence of flight state parameters on physical characteristic state parameters. First, an aerothermal dataset for the vehicle surface is obtained through computational fluid dynamics. Second, based on the strong nonlinear coupling relationship between flight state parameters and the physical characteristics of the flowfield, a set of physical characteristic state parameters was constructed as supplementary input features. Finally, the eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) ensemble learning algorithms are separately adopted to develop point-to-point aerothermal surrogate models denoted as physical characteristic state parameters. Validation using a hypersonic double-ellipsoid model demonstrates that the proposed model achieves mean absolute percentage errors below 10% for the full-surface heat flux prediction, with the relative error at the stagnation point kept within 3%. In addition, XGBoost outperforms LightGBM in full-surface heat flux prediction accuracy. Meanwhile, the prediction of a single flight condition takes only about 2 s. This model effectively shortens the aerodynamic heat calculation cycle while meeting the accuracy requirements for aerodynamic heat predict…

title: Lightweight CNT Fabric Current Collectors Enabling Silicon Anodes in High-Capacity Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Abstract Conventional lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) require metallic current collectors such as copper for anodes and aluminum for cathodes, adding significant weight without contributing to the capacity. This is especially problematic for Si-dominant anodes, with mass loadings lower than 2 mg cm–2. Here, copper is replaced with lightweight, non-woven carbon nanotube fabrics (CNTfs) combined with high-capacity Si/PPAN active material to form a self-standing composite anode. This lightweight electrode delivers a capacity of 1000 mAh g–1 (normalized with respect to the total Si/PPAN/CNTf anode weight) for over 700 cycles at a current density of 1 A g–1 and can potentially boost the cell-level energy density by ∼25% when paired with commercial cathodes. Cross-sectional SEM-EDX imaging and peel tests confirm excellent interfacial contact between the Si/PPAN layer and CNTf current collector. Furthermore, the effects of increasing CNTf thickness reveal more evident SEI formation in the CNTf layer, lowering the first-cycle Coulombic efficiency. These findings demonstrate the potential of using CNTfs in high-energy LIBs, while also reducing emissions associated with metal manufacturing.

title: Administrative state capacity and the effect of EU democracy assistance on levels of democracy: a time-series cross-sectional analysis, 2007–2021
abstract: Abstract The European Union (EU) is one of the world’s major donors of democracy assistance, which aims to foster democratisation. Its effects, however, depend on various conditional factors. This study explores the nexus between democracy assistance and administrative state capacity. Since democracy assistance seeks to strengthen —not substitute—the state and its institutions, we argue that administrative capacity is a crucial condition for the effectiveness of democracy assistance. To test our argument, we conduct a time-series cross-sectional analysis covering EU democracy assistance allocation from 2007 to 2021 across 23 countries in the EU’s neighbourhood. Our results indicate that assistance allocated to countries with higher state capacity has a more substantial effect on their levels of democracy than assistance allocated to countries with lower state capacity. With that, we address an important research gap and contribute to policy debates on the allocation of democracy assistance.

title: Eye movements reflect capacity-dependent organization of working memory
abstract: Human cognition is capacity-limited, requiring strategies to actively structure information. Eye movements offer a natural mechanism for sequential sampling, but whether such sequences reflect memory organization is unknown. We developed a working-memory task where color-frequency pairings created a latent ordinal structure to optimally reduce memory load. Across two experiments, gaze patterns spontaneously aligned with this structure. Participants sampled items following this sequence during encoding and revisited them during maintenance. Critically, the expression of this structure depended on cognitive demand. In a 3-item task, high performers showed robust sequential sampling during encoding, whereas lower performers compensated with replay-like revisitation during maintenance. Under higher demand (4 items), encoding-based organization was disrupted, and structured revisitation emerged primarily during maintenance. These findings suggest that eye movements provide an overt expression of an internally generated organizational process that flexibly adapts to cognitive demands, revealing a behavioral analogue to neural replay when encoding resources are strained.

title: AI Tutor, Online Course, or Both? A Randomized Experimental Pilot Study for Evaluation Capacity Building
abstract: Extension lacks literature comparing standalone generative artificial intelligence (AI) with structured professional development for capacity building. Guided by Social Cognitive Theory and Cognitive Load Theory, this study evaluated the effects of an asynchronous online course and a custom AI tutor on evaluation knowledge and self-efficacy among Cooperative Extension professionals. We conducted a randomized 2 × 2 factorial pilot study crossing access to an evaluation certificate course with access to a custom Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT). Of 144 registrants, 78 provided matched pre- and post-test data, with attrition differing across conditions. Data were analyzed using a three-way mixed factorial ANOVA. Course access and GPT access each increased objective knowledge, with post-test means around 91% across treatment groups. No statistically significant additive effect was detected for knowledge gain. However, given a possible ceiling effect and limited statistical power, this result is inconclusive. Course access and GPT access each increased self-efficacy, but the combined condition produced the smallest self-efficacy gain among treatment groups. Because these estimates are based on participants who completed the study, findings are preliminary. If replicated, results suggest that Extension should combine AI tutors and coursework only when each modality provides k…

title: MODIFIED PLANT-FIBER-REINFORCED FULLY BIODEGRADABLE WOOD-PLASTIC COMPOSITES FOR SUSTAINABLE LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURE: INTERFACE COMPATIBILITY AND AGING MECHANISM
abstract: The growing demand for sustainable materials in landscape architecture has highlighted the potential of polylactic acid/polybutylene adipate-terephthalate (PLA/PBAT)-based wood-plastic composites. However, poor interfacial compatibility between the hydrophilic plant fibers and the hydrophobic polyester matrices, coupled with susceptibility to hydrolytic degradation, limits their outdoor applications. This study presents a synergistic modification strategy for bamboo powder using a silane coupling agent (KH550) and nano-silica (Nano-SiO2), integrating all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with accelerated aging experiments to elucidate the enhancement mechanism of "chemical bridging–physical filling. " MD simulations revealed that the modification forms a dense "core-shell" barrier via covalent anchoring and a robust hydrogen-bond network, reducing the interfacial free volume to 14.1 % and lowering the water molecule self-diffusion coefficient from 4.58 × 10–7 to 0.42 × 10–7 cm2 s–1. This microscopic moisture barrier underpins the macroscopic aging resistance. Accelerated UV-condensation aging tests (1000 h) confirmed that the modified composites preserved the polyester backbone, with a weight-average molecular weight retention of 88.4 %, a tensile strength of 84.3 %, and an impact strength of 81.2 %. The surface color change was limited to E = 4.2, markedly outperformin…

title: Elucidating the Action Mechanism of the Carbon Substrate in Pt/C-Catalyzed Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution Reaction
abstract: Abstract In the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), loading Pt on a carbon substrate can markedly enhance its activity. Electrochemical tests show that the Tafel slopes of Pt/C and Pt mesh are 73 and 171 mV dec–1, respectively, which indicate the HER mechanisms on Pt/C and Pt are different. In alkaline media, the HER on Pt is limited by H2O dissociation. Therefore, in this paper, the effect of the carbon substrate on the H2O dissociation process on a Pt cluster was systematically studied by density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The results indicate that the electron redistribution of the Pt cluster caused by the carbon substrate can enhance the Lewis acidity of the active site, thereby accelerating H2O dissociation step on the Pt cluster. Therefore, promoting the H2O dissociation step on Pt by the carbon substrate is one of the prime reasons for the eminent activity of Pt/C in the alkaline HER.

An Enhanced Intelligent Transport Mechanism for Detecting and Recognizing Traffic Signs using Transformer with YOLOv9 Model
abstract: Traffic road sign detection and classification are essential technologies for developing an automated driver guidance system using computer-aided techniques. Accidents are increasing on a daily basis because of improper and irregular road signs. Many studies have already been reported on the identification, recognition, and classification of traffic signs on roads. These studies have limitations such as long recognition times, misidentification, fewer results, and the absence of image enhancement. To address these issues, this paper proposes an enhanced intelligent transport mechanism for detecting and recognizing traffic signs using a transformer and a YOLOv9 model. Initially, images are collected from publicly available datasets, and then geometric and photometric distortion approaches are used to augment the increasing number of images and reduce overfitting issues. The images are preprocessed using the bilateral filter to remove artifacts present in the images. The global feature modeling transformer-based encoder-decoder model is used to enhance images and remove unwanted artifacts. Lastly, a refined YOLOv9 model is proposed to identify and detect traffic signs in a variety of weather scenarios. Performance is improved and adjusted using the updated wild horse optimizer. On the Indian traffic sign dataset, German traffic sign recognition benchmark, and Belgian traffic sign…

Mineralization mechanism and pollutant immobilization characteristics of vaterite induced by Bacillus velezensis and Pseudomonas putida
abstract: Exploring strain-specific differences in bacterial vaterite biomineralization can supplement the basic theoretical research of biomineralization and reveal the biogeochemical linkages between microbially induced carbonate formation and in-situ pollutant sequestration in soil environments. In this study, Bacillus velezensis LB002 and Pseudomonas putida KT2440 were used as representative bacterial strains to compare strain-dependent vaterite formation and pollutant sequestration behavior. The biomineralization processes in the liquid medium were dynamically monitored, and the induced biominerals were characterized, with particular attention to their organic components. The differences in vaterite characteristics between both bacterial systems were evaluated, and their sequestration performance was assessed taking Cu 2+ and tetracycline as target pollutants. Both strains induced vaterite formation under identical culture conditions, while B. velezensis exhibited a stronger biomineralization capacity than P. putida . In a 100 mL culture system, the Ca 2+ mineralization percentage of B. velezensis reached 35.06%, and the dry weights of biomineral aggregates produced by B. velezensis and P. putida were 0.36 and 0.31 g, respectively. SEM observations revealed that the vaterite induced by B. velezensis had a loose and porous surface, whereas that induced by P. putida had a relatively s…

title: TE-CSA: trajectory entropy-aware cross-step aggregation for improving embedding capacity of distribution-preserving linguistic steganography
abstract: Abstract Existing diffusion-based linguistic steganography methods largely operate in a timestep-local manner, where embedding decisions are made independently within isolated denoising steps. Such a design fundamentally underutilizes the trajectory-level uncertainty naturally distributed across the diffusion process, causing a substantial gap between achievable embedding performance and the embedding opportunities available throughout the diffusion trajectory. In this paper, we propose TE-CSA, a Trajectory Entropy-aware Cross-Step Aggregation framework for high-capacity distribution-preserving linguistic steganography based on diffusion language models. First, departing from conventional timestep-local embedding paradigms, TE-CSA introduces a trajectory-level aggregation mechanism that jointly exploits embedding opportunities scattered across multiple denoising timesteps. By transforming isolated local candidates into globally coordinated embedding resources, the proposed framework significantly enlarges the effective embedding space and unlocks latent capacity hidden within diffusion trajectories. Second, from an information-theoretic perspective, not all candidate positions contribute equally to embedding. Low-entropy positions often behave as bottlenecks that consume embedding opportunities while providing little effective information gain. To alleviate this entropy bottlen…

Comparative Evaluation of Pressurized Liquid and Conventional Solvent Extraction of Agro-Industrial By-Products: Phenolic and Flavonoid Contents, Antioxidant Capacity and Cytotoxicity Assessment
abstract: In the present study, extracts obtained from four agro-industrial by-products, namely pomegranate peels (Punica granatum L.), turnip tops (Brassica rapa L.) residues, prickly pear (Opuntia ficus-indica L.) peels, and artichoke (Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus) stems and leaves, were produced by conventional solvent extraction (acidified methanol–water, 80:20, v/v) and water-based pressurized liquid extraction (PLE). The extracts were comparatively evaluated for total phenolic and flavonoid contents, chemical antioxidant capacity by ABTS and FRAP assays, and cytotoxicity toward Caco-2 cells. Conventional solvent extraction generally resulted in higher Folin–Ciocalteu-estimated total phenolic contents and ABTS activity, whereas flavonoid contents were comparable between the two extraction procedures. Pomegranate peel exhibited the highest values among the investigated matrices, with total phenolic contents of 141 and 193 mg GAE/g dry matter for PLE and conventional extraction, respectively and flavonoid content of approximately 100 mg QE/g dry matter for both procedures. Consistently, pomegranate peel showed the highest ABTS and FRAP responses, reaching 492 mg Trolox/g dry matter and 6032 μmoL Fe (II)/g dry matter for PLE and 618 mg Trolox/g dry matter and 8015 μmoL Fe (II)/g dry matter for conventional extraction, respectively. In contrast, PLE resulted in higher FRAP responses…

Engineering Carbon Nanotube Quantum Well Defects With Recognition Tripeptides for Optical Detection of Extracellular Vesicles in Plasma
abstract: ABSTRACT Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry surface proteins that reflect the molecular signatures of their originating cells. However, their low abundance and the modest sensitivity of current EV detection methods in complex biological environments limit access to EV surface biology in the native biological context. Here, we present a near‐infrared optical nanosensor comprising a quantum well defect functionalized carbon nanotube coupled with integrin‐recognition RGD tripeptide to detect surface integrins on EVs in a human plasma background. The nanosensor achieved sub‐picomolar detection of three integrin subunits (α5β1, αVβ1, and αVβ3) and quantified glioblastoma, ovarian cancer, and fibroblast‐derived EVs at concentrations as low as 10 4 EVs·mL −1 . Molecular dynamics simulations indicated that the RGD‐coupled quantum defect stably engages the canonical integrin‐binding pocket, localizing the binding event at the defect site and providing a structural basis for the selective response. Interestingly, the nanosensor detected comparable responses from fibroblast‐ and cancer‐derived EVs, and the finding was independently validated by surfaceome proteomics, which confirmed that RGD‐receptor integrins are present at comparable levels across all three EV populations. Our result indicates that RGD‐receptor integrins define a broadly distributed adhesion‐associated EV phenotype shar…

title: Digital Transformation, Carbon Disclosure, and Green Innovation in Energy Transition: Firm-Level Evidence from China’s Energy Sector
abstract: China’s dual-carbon goals have made understanding how digital transformation shapes corporate carbon performance a policy priority, and the rapid expansion of firm-reported emissions disclosure since 2020 now makes such inquiry feasible at scale. Drawing on CSMAR financial data and CNRDS digital-transformation keyword frequencies for 914 A-share energy firms over 2020–2025, we combine panel fixed-effects models, a placebo-validated triple-difference design, disclosure-choice models with a Heckman selection correction, and event studies of two policy milestones. We find that digital transformation robustly stimulates green-patent applications and significantly raises the likelihood of carbon disclosure in the cross section, identifying green-patenting and disclosure as the two margins on which digitalization is already measurable. The direct association with disclosed carbon intensity remains statistically insignificant in the selection-corrected model and on the directly disclosed subsample, indicating that emission reductions are not yet measurable at the firm level. A sharp but short-lived emission-reduction pulse among digitalized high-carbon firms in 2021 is consistent with but does not confirm a Porter-type mechanism. Investors nonetheless priced transition-regulatory exposure: ETS-covered firms earned significantly negative abnormal returns around both policy milestones. …

title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
abstract: ABSTRACT Accessing high‐energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near‐infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4‐chloro‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( CDFTM ) and tris(4‐bromo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl ( BDFTM ), based on tris(4‐halo‐2,6‐difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open‐shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6‐trichlorophenyl)methyl ( TTM ), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller‐like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital‐selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher‐energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof‐of‐concept applicability of these radicals…

title: Stock Exchange Trading Optimization Algorithm Improved Based on Information Technology Investment Analysis for Numerical Optimization and Practical Problems
abstract: Stock Exchange Trading Optimization (SETO) is a population-based metaheuristic with a compact market-inspired search framework, but its performance may be limited by uneven random initialization, coarse Relative Strength Index-based search-state identification, and excessive concentration of trading resources. To address these limitations, this study proposes an improved SETO, termed ISETO, by reformulating concepts from information technology investment analysis into population-search mechanisms. First, an IT investment portfolio screening initialization strategy jointly considers solution quality and spatial diversity to improve initial population coverage. Second, a discounted-return and downside-risk dual-state search strategy evaluates the magnitude, temporal relevance, and risk of historical improvements to adaptively coordinate exploration and exploitation. Third, an entropy-regularized real-option capital reallocation strategy redistributes search resources according to solution quality, capital efficiency, technical debt, and population diversity, while reinvesting abandoned candidates into underexplored regions to mitigate stagnation. The dominant computational complexity remains approximately O(TmaxND). ISETO is evaluated on 22 benchmark functions from the IEEE CEC2020 and CEC2022 suites under 10- and 20-dimensional settings and compared with nine representative meta…

title: Long-term trends of carbon monoxide over the North Pacific upper troposphere from in-situ airplane measurements 1991–2018
abstract: Carbon monoxide (CO) is not a greenhouse gas, but as the dominant sink of the hydroxyl radical it governs the oxidising capacity of the troposphere and so indirectly forces climate. Its trends in the North Pacific upper troposphere matter disproportionately: this is the principal outflow corridor for Asian anthropogenic emissions, the fastest-growing combustion source of the past half-century, yet it has almost no routine ground-based monitoring and satellite retrievals resolve it poorly. We therefore combine in-situ CO measurements from the In-service Aircraft for a Global Observing System (IAGOS; 2012–2018) with earlier in-situ data from NASA/NSF/NOAA campaigns (1991–2019), the Measurements of Pollution in the Troposphere (MOPITT) satellite record, and the Integrated Modelling System (IMS) global chemistry transport model. Trends are computed separately for the monthly maximum, percentile, minimum and mean statistics, using a 10,000-sample perturbation regression framework. Mean CO increases by 0.15 ppb month –1 (18.0 ppb decade –1 ; 95% CI: −0.02 to 0.32) over 150 ∘ E − 140 ∘ W , 45 ∘ N − 60 ∘ N and by 0.06 ppb month –1 (7.2 ppb decade –1 ; 95% CI: −0.04 to 0.16) over 25 ∘ N − 45 ∘ N ; both intervals include zero but lie predominantly positive. The monthly maximum rises significantly over 25 ∘ N − 45 ∘ N , by 0.31 ppb month –1 (37.2 ppb decade –1 ; 95% CI: 0.06 to 0.57), whi…

title: Synergistic Porosity and Defect Engineering to Construct S-Scheme Porous Carbon-Modified CeO 2 /Graphitic Carbon Nitride Heterojunctions for Enhanced Photocatalytic Degradation of Ciprofloxacin
abstract: Abstract Although CeO2/graphite-like carbon nitride (CeO2/CN) heterojunctions exhibit good photocatalytic potential, the low specific surface area and poor interfacial contact of conventional CeO2 substrates limit the charge separation efficiency of the system. To this end, this study proposes a strategy combining substrate premodification with interface optimization: first, a porous, carbon-modified CeO2 substrate (PC-CeO2) was prepared via a polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP)-assisted hydrothermal calcination process; this was then combined with g-C3N4 to successfully construct a PC-CeO2/CN S-Scheme heterojunction. Characterization results indicate that the in situ pyrolysis of PVP effectively suppressed the agglomeration of CeO2 nanoparticles, endowing the substrate with a high specific surface area (114.25 m2/g) and inducing initial oxygen vacancy on the surface. Following composite formation with g-C3N4, the concentration of oxygen vacancies in the system increased further; this porous defect structure facilitated close interfacial contact for the assembly of the two phases. Combined spectroscopic and photoelectrochemical analyses indicate that charge transfer in the PC-Ce/CN composite system follows an S-Scheme mechanism. The optimized porous interface reduces interfacial charge transfer resistance, while oxygen vacancies act as effective charge capture centers; the synergistic e…

Effects of Mepiquat Chloride Application Timing and Concentration on Soybean Plant Architecture and Stem Mechanical Properties
abstract: Soybean plant architecture and stem mechanical properties are important determinants of lodging-resistance potential. To clarify the regulatory effects of mepiquat chloride (MC) applied at different growth stages and concentrations on soybean stem traits, two cultivars, Heinong 44 (HN44) and Heinong 65 (HN65), were used. Water-sprayed plants served as the control (MCK), and MC was applied foliarly at 50, 100, 200, or 400 mg/L at the V3 and R1 stages. Plant height, stem diameter, stem mechanical traits, and cell-wall components were measured. The effects of MC were strongly dependent on application timing, concentration, and cultivar. Following V3 application, 400 mg/L MC reduced the plant height of HN44 by 21.85% at R1; 200 mg/L MC increased basal stem diameter by 15.01% at R3 and fifth-internode diameter by 17.94% at R4. In HN65, 400 mg/L MC increased bending deflection by 27.01% at R1, whereas 100 mg/L MC increased cellulose content by 36.50%. In HN44, 100 mg/L MC increased lignin content by 77.39% at R2. Following R1 application, 400 mg/L MC increased bending deflection of HN44 by 29.40% at R2; 50 mg/L MC increased basal stem diameter by 20.85% at R6; and 400 mg/L MC increased stem breaking force by 36.23% at R4. In HN65, 200 mg/L MC increased hemicellulose content by 42.62% at R6. Correlation analysis showed a significant positive correlation between hemicellulose and ligni…

title: Effect of Fatty Acid Saturation and Side-Chain Length on the Thermal Behavior and Morphology of Plant Oil-Based Acrylic Polymers
abstract: In this work, saturated plant oil-based acrylic monomers (POBMs) derived from coconut oil (CCM), babassu oil (BBM), and fully hydrogenated soybean oil (HG SBM) were investigated as building blocks for semicrystalline biobased polymers. The effects of fatty acid saturation and side chain length on free radical polymerization, copolymerization, and polymer morphology were evaluated. Increasing fatty acid saturation suppressed allylic chain transfer reactions, resulting in lower chain transfer constants and higher polymer molecular weights than those of POBMs with higher degrees of unsaturation. Copolymerization of CCM with styrene yielded reactivity ratios of rCCM = 0.44 and rSt = 0.96 and Alfrey–Price parameters of Q = 0.49 and e = 0.03, demonstrating favorable reactivity of saturated POBMs toward conventional vinyl comonomers in chain copolymerization. Thermal and structural analyses revealed a pronounced dependence of polymer morphology on fatty acid side chain structure. Polymers containing predominantly C12 side chains exhibited limited molecular ordering, whereas highly saturated C16–C18 side chains produced pronounced melting transitions and substantially increased crystallinity. Specifically, semicrystalline morphologies were observed in HG SBM-based (co)polymers with degrees of unsaturation of approximately 4 mol% or lower. Poly(HG SBM) exhibited an enthalpy of fusion of…

S ‑glutathionylation of MaWRKY44 orchestrates a MaZFP139‐MaWRKY44‐MaGSTU07 cascade to enhance banana cold tolerance
abstract: ABSTRACT Chilling injury caused by low temperatures severely reduces the postharvest quality and marketability of banana fruit. Although glutathione S ‑transferase (GST)‐mediated reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging constitutes a core antioxidant defense against cold oxidative stress, the transcriptional and post‑translational mechanisms governing this process remain largely elusive. Here, we discovered that S ‑glutathionylation of the WRKY transcription factor MaWRKY44 functions as a previously unknown redox switch that orchestrates a hierarchical transcriptional cascade to enhance cold tolerance. LC‑MS/MS identified Cys45 and Cys199 as conserved S ‑glutathionylation sites of MaWRKY44. Biochemical and molecular analyses revealed a biphasic redox switch: Mild ROS triggers reversible glutathionylation to stabilize MaWRKY44 and enhance its DNA‑binding capacity, whereas sustained oxidative stress drives irreversible cysteine over‑oxidation that abolishes its transcriptional function. Mechanistically, we identified a C2H2 zinc finger transcription factor, MaZFP139, as a direct upstream activator of MaWRKY44, which in turn specifically binds to the W‑box motifs of the MaGSTU07 promoter to drive its transcription. Transient gain‑ and loss‑of‑function assays in banana, together with stable heterologous transformation in tomato, demonstrated that the MaZFP139‐MaWRKY44‐MaGSTU07 casc…

title: Role of AI in Thermal Control for Power Plants: Techniques, Challenges and Opportunities
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Power plants require efficient thermal control to reduce operational costs and improve energy performance. Conventional methods may have limited adaptability to changing operating and environmental conditions. AI-based techniques offer a promising solution for improving thermal efficiency and predictive maintenance. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to develop an AI-based framework for optimizing power plant thermal control, improving energy efficiency, and predicting equipment failures using Reinforcement Learning (RL) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). METHODS: The Coal Fired Power Plant Thermal Performance Dataset is used to train the proposed models. RL is applied to optimize boiler temperature and turbine pressure, while ANNs are employed for failure prediction. The Multiverse Optimizer is used to optimize model hyperparameters and improve performance. RESULTS: The proposed framework achieves an R² of 0.9528, MAE of 0.0216, RMSE of 0.0237, and MAPE of 0.023%, demonstrating high prediction accuracy and improved thermal efficiency compared with conventional approaches. CONCLUSION: The proposed AI-driven framework provides an adaptive and efficient approach to power plant thermal management. The integration of RL, ANN, and the Multiverse Optimizer enhances thermal optimization and predictive maintenance, supporting more reliable and efficient power plant operation…

title: International housing finance projects and mortgage-market development in Central Asia with implications for housing affordability
abstract: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractHousing affordability and mortgage-market development remain important challenges in Central Asia, where long-term housing finance is constrained by differences in financial-system development, borrowing costs, household incomes, and institutional capacity. This study examines the relationship between international housing-finance interventions and mortgage-market development in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and the Kyrgyz Republic over 2020–2025. Using 18 country-year observations, the analysis combines the Mortgage-to-GDP ratio and outstanding mortgage portfolios with two indicators of international financial activity: IFI Finance and IFI Projects. Real interest rates, inflation, and real GDP growth are included as macro-financial controls, while Price-to-Income and Mortgage Burden provide supplementary measures of housing affordability. The empirical analysis employs descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations, pooled OLS regressions with lagged and contemporaneous IFI variables, diagnostic tests, and HC3 heteroskedasticity-consistent inference. The results do not provide stable evidence of a significant association between IFI-supported activity and Mortgage-to-GDP. Lagged IFI Projects are significant only in one specification and lose significance under HC3 estimation, while neither contemporaneous IFI variable is significant. In con…

title: Climate disclosure and risk premium in the European bond market
abstract: Abstract Stringent climate regulations are necessary to achieve robust mitigation targets, putting carbon-intensive activities under pressure and increasing the risk perceived in financial markets. This paper empirically investigates how transition risk is priced into European firms' risk and creditworthiness, using five-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads and Merton's Distance to Default (DtD). The sample comprises European listed companies covered by the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS). Evidence suggests that the ETS carbon price and verified emissions increase credit risk, whereas disclosing emissions reduces it. We find heterogeneous effects across the two indicators, which could indicate different ways in which transition risk is channelled to bond markets. Furthermore, the divergent effects between voluntary and compliance-based measurement of environmental performance could indicate underpricing of emissions relocated outside regulated jurisdictions.

Facet-Dependent Plating/Stripping Behavior and Crystallographic Evolution during Cycling on Zn Metal Anodes
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and low-cost option for scalable energy storage; however, their practical reversibility is limited by nonuniform Zn plating/stripping and dendritic growth. Here, Zn single-crystal electrodes exposing well-defined (002), (100), and (101) crystalline facets were used to isolate the role of crystallography in Zn metal cycling. Zn deposition is strongly facet-dependent, forming hexagonal, rectangular/prismatic, and corner-defined morphologies on (002), (100), and (101) facets, respectively. Time-dependent SEM further reveals that Zn growth proceeds via discrete edge- or corner-initiated crystallographic units rather than uniform terrace coverage. During stripping, Zn metal is removed via facet-preserved mesoscopic dissolution domains, leaving geometry-defined pits rather than random corrosion-like features. However, these pits are not preferentially refilled during subsequent plating. Repeated cycling redirects Zn growth to protrusions and roughened regions, causing mossy/dendritic accumulation, mixed-texture evolution, and loss of epitaxial reversibility. These findings highlight the need to control both oriented deposition and poststripping surface reconstruction.

title: Atomistic Origin of the High Supercooling of Erythritol for Seasonal Thermal Energy Storage: Decoupling Thermodynamic and Kinetic Barriers for Crystallization
abstract: Abstract Crystallization from supercooled liquids is a scientific challenge across diverse disciplines. For seasonal thermal energy storage (TES), erythritol is a promising phase change material (PCM) due to its high natural degree of supercooling. However, successfully suppressing its spontaneous crystallization under extreme climates requires a fundamental understanding of the underlying nucleation and crystal growth mechanisms of such PCMs. Here, the thermodynamic and kinetic barriers governing the supercooled state of erythritol are systematically decoupled at the atomic scale. It is revealed that the suppression of crystallization relies on a highly synergistic “dual-locking” mechanism, characterized by a decoupling gap of ∼70 K between the maximum crystal growth rate and the maximum steady-state nucleation rate. Specifically, at low degrees of supercooling, spontaneous nucleation is thermodynamically suppressed by a massive solid–liquid interfacial entropy penalty, which induces an insurmountable critical nucleation barrier. Liquid molecules must sacrifice substantial conformational degrees of freedom to match the crystal lattice, quantified by a significant conformational entropy gap of approximately 9–10 J/(mol·K). In contrast, at high degrees of supercooling, while the critical nucleation barrier sharply diminishes to theoretically facilitate nucleation, the stabilizat…

title: Pharmaceutical Residues in Human Urine from Patients Under Antiretroviral Regimens and Self-Reported Healthy Individuals Before and After Three Months’ Storage: Implication for Agricultural Reuse in Pretoria, South Africa
abstract: Background/Objectives: Pharmaceutical residues in human urine have raised serious concerns about the safe reuse of urine in agriculture. The current study investigates and compares the concentrations of pharmaceuticals in urine samples collected from male patients undergoing active antiretroviral regimens and self-reported “healthy individuals” at a government hospital in Pretoria, South Africa, and determines how the residues changed during three months of ambient storage, which is the usual recommendation before use in agriculture. Methods: The urine samples were collected in a plastic bottle to prevent fecal contamination, and 15 targeted compounds were analyzed using solid-phase extraction and liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry. The linearity ranged from 0.9910 to 0.9999, 75.5% to 99.1% for recovery, and intra-day and inter-day precision were below 6%. The urine from each group was collected into one pooled sample and then analyzed both pre- and post-storage. Results: Thirteen pharmaceuticals were detected in urine from patients on regular medication before storage; in “healthy individuals”, detections rose from eight to twelve after storage. Concentrations in the composite samples after storage were higher for some of the compounds but lower for others, including caffeine, nevirapine, prednisolone and 17α-ethinylestradiol. Metformin was highest overall at 1186.25 µg/L…

title: Effects of raw material (chilled/defrosted) and long-term frozen storage on volatile compounds and quality markers of mechanically separated common carp (Cyprinus carpio)
abstract: Abstract This study evaluated the impact of raw material thermal history (chilled vs. defrosted) and 12-month frozen storage (-18 °C) on the quality of mechanically separated common carp (Cyprinus carpio). Between months 6 and 12, a significant increase in volatile concentrations – primarily hexanal - and thiobarbituric acid reactive substances (TBARS) was observed, alongside a decrease in total volatile basic nitrogen (TVBN). Microbiological quality remained stable throughout the period and none of the monitored pathogenic species (E. coli, C. perfringens and Salmonella spp.) were detected. Histamine was the dominant biogenic amine, but its levels (7-34 mg/kg) were well below the safety limits. These results suggest that chilled and defrosted raw materials provide mechanically separated fish of similar quality, and the product is shelf-stable for at least six months.
