Geologically informed machine learning for neutron porosity reconstruction from legacy well logs: implications for high-temperature reservoir thermal energy storage
abstract: Abstract High-temperature thermal energy storage in subsurface reservoirs (HT-RTES) can help balance seasonal heat demand and supply by storing excess thermal energy in subsurface reservoirs. Mature hydrocarbon fields are promising storage targets because their reservoir properties are relatively well constrained; however, many legacy fields lack modern petrophysical data. In the Leopoldshafen oil field (northern Upper Rhine Graben), complete log coverage is limited to legacy self-potential (SP) and short-normal (SN) resistivity logs, whereas neutron porosity (NPHI) logs are available only in two wells (LH-5 A and Stutensee-1). Here, we present an integrated workflow to reconstruct NPHI in legacy wells using machine-learning methods. SP and SN logs from 24 boreholes were digitized, standardized, and cleaned to remove acquisition artefacts. Lithological classes were derived from SP–SN cross-plot clustering and used as a rock-physics-guided lithology flag. Five supervised algorithms were tested using two input configurations: Model 1, based on scaled SP and SN logs, and Model 2, which additionally included the lithology flag. Random Forest with Model 2 yielded the best performance in the training well Stutensee-1 and generalized well to the independent validation well LH-5 A. The main prediction errors occurred in gas-bearing intervals, but a lithology-specific post-processing co…

title: Breaking the Graphite Trilemma: An Isotropic Core–Shell Anode for High-Energy and Fast-Charging Li-Ion Batteries
abstract: High-energy-density Li-ion batteries demand highly graphitized graphite anodes, yet elevated graphitization inevitably amplifies structural anisotropy, obstructing Li+ intercalation and compromising rate capability. To resolve this trilemma, we establish a precursor–structure–performance framework for pitch-based artificial graphites, revealing that this performance trade-off is governed by impurity content, ordered domains, and micropores: low-impurity precursors facilitate crystallite growth along the c-axis to realize high graphitization; ordered domains promote in-plane crystallite growth; and intrinsic micropores restrain excessive in-plane crystallite enlargement, lowering the orientation index and maintaining structural isotropy. Purified coal-based needle coke emerges as the optimal matrix, featuring a high graphitization degree of 94.89% alongside a moderate orientation index of 10.25. A resin-derived hard-carbon coating, with markedly higher disorder than its pitch-derived counterpart, is applied to construct an isotropic core–shell architecture (AG-R). The disordered surface layer acts as a Li+ transfer station, preserving low-rate capacity while boosting the Li+ diffusion coefficient by ~2.2-fold. In 2.5 Ah 18,650 full cells, AG-R achieves an energy density exceeding 430 Wh kg−1 (based on the total active material mass), retains 92.3% capacity at 10 C discharge and …

title: Predictive Tires for Electric and Autonomous Vehicles: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: The role of tires in vehicle dynamics has evolved from passive support elements to active sources of information. This paper provides a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in wheel–road interaction, structural optimization, and intelligent sensing, toward the emerging concept of the predictive tire. Fundamental phenomena, including slip-induced energy losses, aquaplaning thresholds, and radial stiffness variation, are analyzed for their impact on safety, ride comfort, and energy efficiency. Structural developments, including multi-objective optimizations and advanced composite materials targeting rolling-resistance reduction and NVH (Noise, Vibration, Harshness) improvement, are important for electric-vehicle applications. At the same time, progress is being made in the integration of sensors, such as polyvinylidene fluoride piezoelectric films (PVDF), distributed strain sensors, embedded accelerometers, and hybrid tire pressure monitoring systems (h-TPMSs), along with advanced data-driven methods such as fuzzy logic, hybrid Kalman filters, and Transformer neural networks for estimating friction coefficients and contact forces. The integration of these directions supports the tire’s transition toward a predictive multifunctional platform supplying real-time variables for the anti-lock braking system (ABS), electronic stability control (ESC), torque vectoring, and advance…

title: Research on Trajectory Tracking Control of Distributed Drive Electric Vehicles With Four‐Wheel Steering Based on Iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator
abstract: ABSTRACT Four‐wheel‐steering distributed‐drive electric vehicles (4WS‐DDEVs) provide multiple control degrees of freedom for improving path‐tracking and lateral‐motion performance. However, the coupling among front‐axle steering, rear‐axle steering, additional yaw moment, and nonlinear vehicle dynamics increases the difficulty of coordinated control. To address this issue, this study develops a coordinated path‐tracking framework based on an iterative linear quadratic regulator with particle swarm optimization–gray wolf optimization (PSO‐GWO‐ILQR). At the upper level, an online receding‐horizon ILQR controller determines the front‐axle steering angle, rear‐axle steering angle, and additional yaw moment. While retaining the conventional ILQR recursion, a differentiable hyperbolic‐cosine penalty is incorporated into the running cost to regulate excessive variations in these control commands. The state and control weighting parameters are calibrated offline using an update‐level PSO‐GWO mechanism that combines the multi‐leader guidance of GWO with the historical velocity information of PSO. A tracking‐ and stability‐oriented fitness function incorporating lateral error, heading angle error, sideslip angle, and yaw rate error is used to evaluate candidate weighting configurations. At the lower level, the axle‐level steering commands are converted into four individual wheel angles, …

title: SH APSA control strategy for improved power quality of grid-connected SPV systems
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a simplified hybrid affine projection sign algorithm based adaptive control strategy for grid-connected solar photovoltaic systems under abnormal grid conditions. The proposed method combines the robustness of sign-based adaptation with the fast convergence capability of affine projection techniques to achieve accurate current estimation and improved dynamic response. A simplified structure is developed to reduce computational complexity and enable efficient real-time implementation. The controller is evaluated under varying irradiance and unbalanced nonlinear load conditions. Simulation results demonstrate improved convergence speed, reduced oscillations, enhanced harmonic compensation, and stable DC-link voltage regulation compared with conventional adaptive algorithms.

Cambios en indicadores de inseguridad alimentaria y estrategias de afrontamiento del hogar, antes y después de la estrategia de bono alimentario en Medellín, Colombia (2024)
abstract: Introduction: Food insecurity refers to the difficulty individuals face in accessing safe food in sufficient quantity and quality to meet their nutritional requirements, in accordance with their tastes and preferences, thereby enabling a healthy and active life. In the District of Medellín, food assistance strategies to ensure access to food among vulnerable groups through the distribution of food packages and vouchers. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of the periodic delivery of vouchers redeemable for food on households' perceptions of food security and coping strategies using questionnaires administered before and after participation in the project. Methodology: A secondary-source, longitudinal observational study was conducted with a sample of 317 households benefiting from the food voucher program during 2024. The results of the measurements taken before and after the intervention were analyzed using the food insecurity perception and coping strategies questionnaires, comparing the changes observed at both times. Results: The provision of food vouchers had a positive effect on reducing the classification of perceived food insecurity reflected in decreased median score from 12 to 5 points and the changes in RCSI scores from 21 to 10 points, indicating more than half following the intervention. Conclusions: Although the periodic distribution of food vou…

title: Device Design Implications on RON×QOSS FOM in p-GaN Power HEMTs: A Simulation Study
abstract: In this paper, we analyze by means of numerical simulations the device design implications on the RON×QOSS Figure of Merit (FOM) in p-GaN power HEMTs to be employed in soft-switching converters. During switching, p-GaN power HEMTs experience dynamic RON increase but also dynamic QOSS reduction, effectively establishing a trade-off between the two device parameters. This trade-off stems from the physical mechanism of hole redistribution within the C-doped buffer. Device design choices such as field plate length, channel and buffer thickness as well as C-doping concentration influence both parameters; however, the relative variation of the two parameters is not necessarily symmetric. Simulations are therefore carried out to identify the best device design choices depending on the target trade-off between RON and QOSS.

title: Continuous Pathway Reinforced Polyurethane-Based Thermal Interface Materials for High-Power Density Chips
abstract: Thermal interface materials (TIMs) are indispensable in electronic thermal management, as they mitigate interfacial thermal resistance and improve heat transport efficiency between adjacent components. A major factor hindering the thermal performance of conventional TIMs is the substantial interfacial thermal resistance arising at the interfaces between non-continuous fillers and the polymer matrix. To overcome this limitation, this study develops a continuously oriented TIM using a monolithic pyrolytic graphite film (PGF) combined with film-coating and hot-pressing processes. A polyurethane layer is coated onto PGF films, which are stacked and hot-pressed into a dense composite block. Sectioning the block perpendicular to the pressing direction yields a PGF/PU TIM. The material delivers a thermal conductivity of 118.5 W/(m·K) and demonstrates superior heat dissipation behavior under practical testing conditions. Through the establishment of continuous heat transfer pathways, this strategy alleviates interfacial resistance at filler–matrix interfaces and provides both theoretical basis and technical routes for high-power-density electronic packaging applications.

title: Venetoclax combined with olverembatinib and prednisone as a frontline therapeutic strategy for Philadelphia chromosome-positive mixed-phenotype acute leukemia
Halal Tourism Development Strategy in Pontianak City: Potentials, Disparities, and Urban Islamic Tourism
abstract: Halal tourism studies in Indonesia have largely focused on Sharia-compliant services, such as halal food, worship facilities, and religious tourism, while the development of urban Islamic tourism remains relatively limited. This study analyzes the development of halal tourism through an urban Islamic tourism approach in Pontianak City. Using a qualitative interpretive design, data was collected through interviews, observations, and documentation involving eight informants from academic, government, and community backgrounds, including tourism-related institutions at the provincial and city levels. Data was analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke. The findings show that Pontianak has substantial potential for urban Islamic tourism through the Kapuas River, Pontianak Sultanate Palace, historic mosques, the Equator Monument, and Malay-Islamic cultural heritage. However, further integration is needed across regulation, destination management, promotion, human resources, and public understanding of halal tourism. The study proposes urban Islamic tourism as a framework that extends halal tourism beyond Sharia-compliant services toward the integration of cultural identity, urban space, creative economy, and social cohesion in a multicultural city.

Hybrid Governance and Feminist Strategy: Navigating Multiple Centres of Authority in South Sudan
abstract: This article examines how South Sudanese women's movements operate within a hybrid governance order in which authority is distributed across formal state institutions, customary and religious leaders, civil society networks, international organisations and conflict-era political actors. Drawing on the dissertation's mixed-methods study of 314 completed engagements across Juba, Wau and Malakal, the analysis focuses on alliance architecture and multi-actor strategy. The source reports 47 active partnerships with government institutions, 156 with civil society organisations, 89 with international organisations, 234 with traditional and religious leaders, 23 with private-sector entities and 18 with academic institutions. Civil-society alliances received the highest effectiveness rating at 4.2/5.0, while traditional and religious leader engagements were the most numerous and provided cultural legitimacy and community access. Government partnerships offered policy access but were constrained by bureaucratic weakness and political dynamics. International partnerships supplied funding, technical assistance and diplomatic leverage but introduced dependency and agenda-alignment risks. The dissertation's hybrid-governance framework explains why no single arena is sufficient: women’s movements must lobby parliamentarians in Juba, work with chiefs and elders in Wau, engage international and…

title: How Circular Economy Practices Drive Sustainable Performance: A Dual‐Moderator Model of Green Culture and Environmental Dynamism in the Hotel Industry
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how circular economy practices (CEP) influence sustainable performance (SP) in the hospitality industry. It explores the mediating role of green supply chain management (GSCM) and investigates how green organizational culture (GOC) and environmental dynamism (ED) moderate the CEP–SP relationship. Data were collected from 425 employees of four‐ and five‐star eco‐friendly hotels in Türkiye using judgmental sampling. Data were analyzed using PLS‐SEM to test the measurement and structural models, including mediation and moderation. CEP did not directly improve sustainable performance. However, GSCM fully mediated the CEP–SP relationship, indicating that circular practices must be operationalized through supply chain processes to create sustainability outcomes. Furthermore, GOC strengthened the positive effect of CEP on SP, highlighting the importance of supportive internal culture. ED also amplified the CEP–SP link, suggesting that dynamic external conditions enhance the effectiveness of circular initiatives.

title: Advancing Industrial Symbiosis: The Dynamic Role of Public Organisations
abstract: ABSTRACT Industrial symbiosis is a key circular economy strategy that relies on collaboration among diverse actors to turn residual streams into new value. Although prior research acknowledges supportive public‐sector involvement, there is a lack of understanding of how public organisations' roles evolve over time as industrial symbiosis initiatives develop. This study addresses this gap through a qualitative case study of a regional industrial ecosystem in northern Sweden. Drawing on 25 interviews with public organisations, support actors and producers, five distinct public‐sector roles are identified (policymaker, facilitator, knowledge broker/data provider, participant and financier). The study shows that roles shift across industrial symbiosis development phases, and a framework is developed that links role configurations to phase‐specific barriers. The study contributes by conceptualising public organisations as dynamic ecosystem actors and by offering a practical framework that helps public organisations to align roles with evolving ecosystem needs to support long‐term circular economy transformation.

Dual‐Audit Governance and Sustainability Reporting for Environmental Innovation: International Evidence
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how external sustainability assurance (EA) and internal audit reporting (IA) relate to sustainability reporting (SR) and environmental innovation (GI). Using 10,092 firm‐year observations from 1937 firms across 18 countries over 2010–2024, we employ LASSO‐guided two‐way fixed‐effects models supplemented by fixed‐effects instrumental‐variable estimation, clustered bootstrap path analysis, interaction tests, multiway clustering, and propensity‐score methods. Results show that EA and IA are positively associated with SR, while SR is positively associated with GI. Both contemporaneous indirect associations are also positive and remain stable across alternative control sets and richer fixed‐effects structures. However, the preferred within‐firm interaction is insignificant, instrumental‐variable estimates do not support causal interpretation, and entry into a positive external assurance score predicts stronger reporting but not subsequent innovation. The findings position external assurance and internal audit as additive governance mechanisms linked to reporting within observed firms, rather than evidence of causal mediation, substitution, complementarity, or hierarchical dominance.

title: Clinical experience with ventriculovesical shunting as a salvage or bridging strategy in children with hydrocephalus when peritoneal diversion was considered unsuitable: a retrospective case series
abstract: Objective Ventriculoperitoneal (VP) shunting remains a standard cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) diversion procedure for pediatric hydrocephalus. However, peritoneal diversion may be considered unsuitable in selected children because of abdominal infection, severe peritoneal pathology, refractory CSF ascites, or persistent CSF abnormalities. The objective of this study was to describe our institutional experience with ventriculovesical shunting (VVS) as a selective salvage or bridging CSF diversion strategy in such patients. Materials and methods We retrospectively reviewed 36 children with hydrocephalus who underwent VVS at our center between September 2014 and January 2022. The decision to use VVS was individualized according to the clinical circumstances and the treating team's assessment that peritoneal diversion was undesirable or not feasible at that time. Available reasons to avoid peritoneal diversion, postoperative complications and conversion to subsequent VP shunting were reviewed. Results All 36 VVS procedures were technically completed. Follow-up ranged from 6 to 24 months (mean, 13.44 ± 8.21 months). At the most recent available follow-up, radiological improvement of hydrocephalus was reported in 27 patients, while seven remained clinically stable; two patients discontinued treatment and were lost to follow-up. title: Towards a Better Definition of Patient-Centered Therapeutic Strategy of Parkinson’s Disease: An Opinion Paper
Disaster Governance as Strategic Infrastructure and Non‑Traditional Security in the Indo‑Pacific: Insights from South Asia for Canada’s Indo-Pacific Strategy
abstract: Disasters are becoming more intense and frequent, causing destruction, deaths, and community asset devastation in South Asian communities, highlighting the importance of disaster governance as a key factor in regional and global stability within non-traditional security frameworks. Drawing on empirical evidence from Nepal’s 2015 earthquakes and recurrent cyclones in eastern India, this article emphasizes that regional cooperation and community resilience foster a shared responsibility among policymakers and security officials for effective disaster governance within the Indo-Pacific security architecture. Keywords: Disaster governance, regional stability, community resilience
venue: Journal of Military and Strategic Studies

title: From Optimization to Subversion : Sociotechnical Expressions of Agency in Platform Labor in Indonesia and the Philippines
abstract: This paper examines how ride-hailing and delivery workers in Indonesia and the Philippines, as active technology actors, navigate and contest digital infrastructures that govern their labor. In contexts marked by platform dependency and labor insecurity, we move beyond discrete accounts of compliance and resistance to argue that worker agency lies in the capacity to move fluidly along a continuum of optimization and subversion practices. Drawing on 142 worker interviews, we find that these practices are embedded in the shifting dynamics of permissibility on platforms, workers’ familiarity with their apps, and the everyday ethical positioning of workers who continually balance the need to maintain access to the platform with efforts to improve pay and conditions. This dynamic exposes a paradox: platforms rely on workers’ ingenuity to patch systemic gaps and sustain operations even as they attempt to constrain it. By allowing oscillation between optimization and subversion, platforms defuse frustration, manage precarity, and secure their own endurance. Ultimately, this paper demonstrates how survival-driven adaptations both express worker agency and coshape platform capitalism from below—showing that platform arrangements are engineered from above yet are continually sustained, challenged, and reshaped through workers’ everyday practice.

title: Implementation of Right to Information Act in Cooperatives of Birendranagar Municipality, Surkhet
abstract: Cooperatives are volunteer and member- controlled organization, which are based on principles of autonomy, equality and democracy. The main objective of this study was to analyze the implementation of Right to Information (RTI) in various cooperatives in the Birendranagar Municipality, Surkhet. The study was of qualitative and quantitative nature. A total of 104 member from various cooperatives were selected through non proportional stratified random sampling and 15 representatives of the cooperatives were selected through purposive sampling. In addition, two focus group discussions and non-participatory observation of the cooperatives were done. The study was mainly focused on the awareness of the members of RTI, availability of information, attitude of the staff, modes of access, voluntary compliance, monitoring, behavior of the members, and information and satisfaction of the members. Of the total 104 members, 96.1% had general knowledge about RTI. Of the total members, 73.1% had made a request for information, 32.7% of the total members had made repeated request for information and 29.8% of the total members had received the requested information. The overall average of the implementation of the RTI was found to be 44%, which was interpreted as very poor. The average of monitoring was found to be 27.5% which was very poor. Geopolitical Risk in the Financial Sector: A Systematic Bibliometric Review
abstract: Geopolitical risk (GPR) is increasingly recognized as a central concern for financial stability, yet its transmission to the financial sector remains relatively underexplored. To address this gap, a Bibliometric–Systematic Literature Review combining PRISMA-guided screening with bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping (Bibliometrix 5.4.0, VOSviewer 1.6.21) was carried out. A total of 604 journal articles were retrieved from Scopus on the broader GPR and finance literature, including a subsample of 78 documents addressing banking (67), insurance (10), and both sectors jointly (1). Results of the analysis show that scientific production accelerates sharply from 2018, with growth in the banking- and insurance-focused subsample outpacing growth in the field overall. Our co-citation analysis of cited references and authors finds that the field’s intellectual core is organized around Caldara and Iacoviello’s foundational GPR index, alongside clusters extending towards commodity and energy market applications and spillover-index methodology, with four distinct author-centered citation clusters identified; the co-authorship analysis further identified China as the dominant contributor to international research collaboration. Our analysis adds to the growing body of bibliometric reviews on GPR to provide a structured research agenda for future investigations, particularly …

title: Transfer Optimization in Professional Football: A Total Cost of Ownership Decision Framework Adapted from Industrial Procurement
abstract: Despite record revenues across European professional football, many clubs consistently report negative annual results. Player transfers represent the single largest controllable cost driver, yet investment decisions are rarely evaluated through a rigorous economic lens: the headline transfer fee dominates deliberation while salary obligations, injury exposure, and player-attributable revenue contributions receive little systematic attention. This paper proposes a holistic investment decision framework for professional football by adapting the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) concept from industrial procurement. The framework treats players as capital assets and integrates further financially relevant dimensions into a net economic metric assessed over the contract period and discounted to present value. We illustrate the framework using the 2025 transfer of Florian Wirtz from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool FC (initial fee approximately EUR 118 million, £100 million), which also draws on age-based market value forecasting and probabilistic injury risk assessment among its inputs. The analysis highlights economic dimensions beyond market-price-based evaluation. By applying the framework, total costs in the base case are approximately 1.6 times the headline fee in present-value terms, and the illustrative scenario range spans approximately EUR 80 million. Institutional Quality and the Financial Returns of Social Supply Chain Practices
abstract: ABSTRACT Social supply chain practices (SSCP) have become increasingly relevant as firms seek to support sustainable development and respond to stakeholder expectations. This study examines the association between SSCP and corporate financial performance (CFP) and investigates the moderating role of country‐level institutional quality. Drawing on resource dependence, legitimacy, and institutional theories, we constructed a composite SSCP index based on 11 binary indicators and applied fixed‐effects panel regressions to global firm‐level data from 2018 to 2023. The results show that SSCP is negatively associated with return on assets (ROA) and Tobin's Q , while their association with market capitalization is not statistically significant. The interaction between SSCP and country‐level institutional quality is positive and significant across all three CFP measures, indicating that the estimated SSCP–CFP association becomes more favorable as institutional quality increases. However, the conditional pattern differs across the three CFP measures. For market capitalization, the association becomes positive and statistically significant at high levels of institutional quality, whereas for ROA and Tobin's Q , it becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero and does not become significantly positive within the observed range. title: Optimal Control Strategies for Financial Literacy and Loan Repayment Dynamics among MSMEs in Kenya
abstract: Financial instability and weak loan repayment performance remain major constraints on the growth and sus tainability of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Kenya. Low levels of financial literacy and digital-finance integration, inflexible debt conditions, inadequate buffers to liquidity and operational stress reduce the stability of cash flows and increase vulnerability to default. In this study, a five-control optimal control model is developed for financial interventions to enhance the financial literacy and loan repayment dynamics of MSMEs. A system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations represents the interactions among financial literacy, financial health, loan burden, cash reserves, and operational stress. Bounded controls are financial literacy training, FinTech support, loan restructuring flexibility, emergency liquidity injection and business mentorship. The application of Pontryagin’s maximum principle leads to the derivation of the Hamiltonian, adjoint equations, transversality conditions, and optimal control characterisations. The resulting optimality system is solved numerically using a forward–backward sweep method with a fourth- order Runge-Kutta scheme. The simulations indicate that FinTech support has the most significant individual impact as it directly boosts the capacity of repayments, while literacy training and mentorship improve financia…

title: Ecological Commodification and Capital Accumulation in R. K. Narayan’s The Financial Expert
abstract: This study explores how land, agrarian labour and social relations are transformed into abstraction of financial value within the fictional world of Malgudi in R. K. Narayan’s The Financial Expert (1952), focusing especially on the relationship between the ecological resources and the new formations of capital accumulation. The study aims to examine the ideological and material processes that transform communal and ecological forms of value into exchange, credit and collateral and to expand the novel’s interpretive scope beyond its traditional reading as social comedy or character study. The research is based on a close reading of the text, using a qualitative, theory-based approach that draws on Marx’s (1990) theories of capital accumulation and primitive accumulation and Huggan and Tiffin’s (2010) postcolonial ecocriticism, with an emphasis on the banyan tree, the Co-operative Land Mortgage Bank, the moneylending economy, and Margayya’s domestic sphere as interdependent spaces that redefine relationships between nature, labour, and economic value. The analysis shows that financial accumulation in the novel depends upon the abstraction of value from the ecological and social conditions that sustain material life. The novel’s comic and cyclical structure, moreover, reveals the recurrent tensions produced by this process. The study therefore argues that The Financial Expert (195…

title: Public Service Decline and Support for the Populist Right: Evidence from England’s National Health Service
abstract: The rise of populist right parties is well studied, but relatively little attention has been given to how public service performance influences voter support. Given that public services are often the primary means through which citizens interact with the state, we argue that declining public services can create grievances that increase the appeal of populist right parties. Focusing on England’s National Health Service, we combine administrative data on local health facility closures with panel data on public preferences and voting intentions. Using a staggered difference-in-differences design, we find that closures reduce satisfaction with public services and increase support for populist right parties. These effects are moderated by migrant registrations at local health practices, highlighting the interaction between public service performance and immigration concerns in fueling populist right support. Our findings underscore the role of public service decline as a driver of support for populist parties, especially in areas undergoing demographic change.

title: Early colony-level transmission of juvenile hormone analog baits alters task-related behavior in workers of the red imported fire ant, Solenopsis invicta
Out-of-pocket health expenditures as a barrier to healthcare access, financial protection, and progress toward universal health coverage: a narrative review from Somalia
abstract: Universal health coverage (UHC) requires both access to needed services and protection from financial hardship, yet Somalia's health system depends heavily on out-of-pocket (OOP) payments. This narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on the magnitude, drivers, and consequences of OOP spending in Somalia and identifies policy options to strengthen financial protection. OOP payments account for 44.9% of total health expenditure, far above the global (18.6%) and sub-Saharan African (35.7%) averages, while government financing and insurance coverage of about 3.5% remain minimal. Weak public financing, a dominant and largely unregulated private sector, and fragmented donor aid sustain this reliance. Roughly 24% of households experience catastrophic health expenditure, commonly resorting to borrowing, asset sales, and reduced consumption, and many forgo care altogether. These burdens fall disproportionately on the poor, women, rural populations, and internally displaced persons, leaving Somalia with the lowest UHC index among 120 countries at 33.5. Experiences from Rwanda, Ghana, and Ethiopia show that reducing OOP reliance depends on increased public financing, pooled prepayment, and pro-poor subsidies rather than insurance laws alone, supporting a phased, subsidy-backed reform agenda.

title: Pengaruh Good Corporate Governance, Sistem Pengendalian Internal, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap Financial Statement Fraud pada Perusahaan Consumer Good di BEI 2020-2025
abstract: The incongruity of prior findings concerning the role of Good Corporate Governance and the firm-specific attributes of companies in the consumer goods industry during the 2020–2025 period provides the impetus for investigating the determinants of Financial Statement Fraud. This study examines consumer goods companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange to ascertain the association of Good Corporate Governance, Internal Control Systems, and Firm Size with Financial Statement Fraud. The dataset comprises annual reports, audited financial statements, and Good Corporate Governance reports from 15 companies selected through purposive sampling, yielding 90 observations over a six-year observation period. Financial Statement Fraud is proxied by the Dechow F-Score, while GCG is operationalized through independent commissioners, audit committees, and institutional ownership; Internal Control Systems are measured through disclosed internal control components; and Firm Size is gauged by the natural logarithm of total assets. Statistical evidence of a significant association with Financial Statement Fraud emerges solely for Firm Size, which exhibits a negative relationship with a significance value of 0.012, whereas GCG and Internal Control Systems demonstrate no statistically significant effects, with respective significance values of 0.912 and 0.637. title: MOLIYAVIY STRATEGIYANI SHAKLLANTIRISHDA KRAUDFANDING MEXANIZMLARIDAN FOYDALANISHNING XORIJIY TAJRIBASI
abstract: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of crowdfunding technologies widely used in the digital economy, one of the key areas of modern economic development, and examines their role in the formulation and implementation of financial strategies. It explores the role and significance of crowdfunding in contemporary economic processes, its main types, major crowdfunding platforms operating in foreign countries, market capitalization, and development trends. Furthermore, the article examines the potential of crowdfunding to attract financial resources, diversify funding sources, and enhance the effectiveness of financial strategies, as well as the prospects for its application in Uzbekistan

title: Financial Architecture, Government Effectiveness and Carbon Emission Risk in Foreign Capital Mobilization in Sub-Saharan Africa
abstract: Background Sub-Saharan Africa faces a persistent external-finance constraint that limits investment, employment, technology transfer and progress toward sustainable development. Rather than treating the regressors as separate determinant questions, this study investigates a broader empirical phenomenon: whether foreign capital systematically responds to domestic financial architecture, institutional credibility and environmental conditions in heterogeneous Sub-Saharan African economies. Methods Annual data for 44 Sub-Saharan African economies from 2004 to 2022 were analysed using a sequential panel design. Cross-sectional-dependence and slope-heterogeneity diagnostics motivate second-generation CIPS unit-root testing, Westerlund cointegration and heterogeneous estimation. CS-ARDL serves as the baseline estimator; CCEMG and AMG assess estimator robustness, System GMM addresses dynamic endogeneity concerns, panel quantile regression examines distributional heterogeneity and Dumitrescu-Hurlin tests assess Granger-predictive direction. Results Financial inclusion, the domestic-credit proxy interpreted conservatively as financial intermediation capacity, and government effectiveness are positively associated with both FDI and remittance inflows in the long run. title: Liquidity Management Strategies and Financial Performance of Listed Manufacturing Companies in Nigeria
abstract: This study examined the effect of liquidity management strategies on the financial performance of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria. Specifically, it assessed the effects of cash management, inventory management, and accounts receivable management on net profit margin. The study adopted an ex post facto research design and used secondary data obtained from the annual reports and audited financial statements of 19 listed manufacturing companies over the period 2016–2025, yielding 190 firm-year observations. Panel data regression techniques were employed, with descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and diagnostic tests conducted to ensure the reliability of the estimates. The findings revealed that cash management had a positive and significant effect on net profit margin (β = 6.234, p = 0.016), while inventory management also had a positive and significant effect (β = 1.234, p = 0.001). In contrast, accounts receivable management had a negative and significant effect on net profit margin (β = −0.038, p = 0.001). The study concludes that effective management of liquidity resources is essential for enhancing the profitability of listed manufacturing companies in Nigeria. It recommends that firms maintain adequate cash reserves, improve inventory control, and strengthen credit and collection practices to optimize liquidity and financial performance.
venue: JOURNAL OF ACCOUNTING AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT

title: Learning From the Field: Reflections on the Use of Theory, Mixed Methods and Case Study Design to Explore Implementation and Experience in Mental Health Crisis Services for Children and Young People
abstract: This article arises from a theory-informed, sequential, mixed methods project which combined a survey and multiple nested case studies to examine implementation and experience in the context of mental health crisis services for children and young people in England and Wales. Its primary contribution to mixed methods research is to show how theory, mixed methods and case studies can be practicably brought together to improve understanding of complex interventions introduced into complex systems. It makes a further contribution through a reflective exploration of the implementation of mixed methods research in sensitive fields involving vulnerable groups, by specifically exploring: participation and engagement; and fieldwork flexibility, power and control.

title: Cultural Differences and Quality Trust in Sustainable Cross-Border Closed-Loop Photovoltaic Supply Chain Network Design
abstract: Green manufacturing of photovoltaic (PV) modules and the rapid evolution of cross-border production models have given rise to prominent environmental issues and severe cultural differences. Therefore, incorporating sustainability and cultural differences into supply chain network design is particularly necessary. First, this study considers the carbon tax price, the consumer quality trust index (QTI) for recycled and remanufactured products, and the cultural differences faced by cross-border manufacturers. A mixed-integer programming model is constructed for the optimal design of a cross-border PV module supply chain network, incorporating three objectives: economic cost, environmental, and social benefit. The model aims to minimize economic cost and carbon emissions while maximizing social benefit. Second, a triangular fuzzy function is introduced to handle uncertain parameters in the model, and a non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm is used to solve the model and obtain the optimal solution. Finally, a sensitivity analysis of the carbon tax price and cultural differences is conducted, and the effects of different QTI levels on the supply chain network are discussed. The results indicate that these factors have a significant impact on the designed sustainable supply chain network. title: Teaching Earthquake-Resistant Design Through a Serious Game and an Interactive Environment
abstract: Serious games and interactive multimedia are widely used in instruction, yet two questions remain comparatively under-answered: whether the learning gains they produce endure beyond immediate post-testing and how they perform on technical, spatial subject matter. This study designed and evaluated an integrated digital learning package pairing an interactive multimedia environment, which delivers theory, with a purpose-built three-dimensional serious game, in which learners assemble the load-bearing system of a building so that abstract structural principles become spatial decisions. Both components were grounded in the Revised Bloom Taxonomy and the Werbach and Hunter gamification framework, and their usability was appraised by expert panels before deployment. The package was tested against conventional instruction in a pre-test, post-test, and retention control-group experiment with forty third-year architecture students in Türkiye, randomly assigned to the two conditions and matched on content, contact time, and instructor. Knowledge of earthquake-resistant design was measured with a twenty-five-item expert-validated test before instruction, one week after, and eight weeks later. The groups were equivalent at baseline. The experimental group scored substantially higher at post-test (62.2 versus 49.6; Cohen’s d = 1.41), an advantage confirmed by an analysis of covariance (ANCO…

title: An instructional workflow for interdisciplinary prototype design in biology and engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Interdisciplinary collaboration between biology and engineering students can be difficult to implement within traditional undergraduate coursework, despite increasing demand for students to develop collaborative technical skills. To address this challenge, we developed an instructional workflow that connected introductory biology and engineering students through the design, fabrication, and testing of field-delivery prototypes inspired by agricultural research relevant to the local community. Directly linking the project to a regional issue and to interactions with collaborating scientists strengthened student engagement and investment in the work. Coordinating the initial interactions between the groups of students was supported by implementing an onboarding activity designed to identify disciplinary perspectives, knowledge gaps, and collaborative challenges prior to prototype development. Students were also introduced to the importance of developing simple, minimum viable prototypes that allowed for more rapid design and testing iterations. Reciprocal peer instruction throughout the workflow required students to share their discipline-specific knowledge to overcome challenges related to biological constraints, field application considerations, microscopy, computer-aided design, and 3D printing. Accountability measures gauged student progress and included weekly progr…

title: Acting on the Corridors: A Minilateral Coalition Design for Southeast Asia's Scam-Compound Crisis
abstract: Southeast Asia’s scam-compound networks expose a persistent gap in regional security governance: the institutions required to dismantle transnational criminal economies are, in some jurisdictions, compromised by the networks they are expected to regulate. Although scholarship on minilateralism demonstrates the capacity of small coalitions to act beyond consensus-bound institutions, its application has focused predominantly on great-power competition. Research on transnational crime in Southeast Asia has examined how ASEAN’s non-interference norm and consensus-based decision-making constrain collective enforcement, but has paid less attention to coalition-building when state capture undermines the reliability of potential partners. This paper bridges these literatures by examining how minilateralism can be adapted to counter transnational criminal networks operating across compromised jurisdictions. It argues that a coalition anchored by six willing ASEAN members—Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam—with support from Canada and other middle powers offers a viable framework for sustained counter-criminal governance. Rather than relying on enforcement within captured jurisdictions, this model prioritizes financial chokepoints and human-trafficking corridors that traverse non-captured jurisdictions, enabling coordinated intervention while reducing …

title: Serum Uric Acid and Spot Urinary Calcium–Creatinine Ratio in Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Comparative Study
abstract: Background: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are major contributors to maternal and perinatal morbidity. Serum uric acid and spot urinary calcium/creatinine ratio are simple biochemical parameters that may help in assessment of these disorders. Aim: To determine serum uric acid and urinary calcium/creatinine ratio in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and in normal pregnant women. Methods: This hospital-based comparative cross-sectional study was conducted among 50 pregnant women, including 25 women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and 25 normotensive pregnant women. Demographic, obstetric and clinical details were recorded. Blood pressure and proteinuria status were documented. Venous blood was collected for serum uric acid estimation, and clean-catch midstream spot urine was collected for urinary calcium and creatinine estimation. Urinary calcium/creatinine ratio was calculated. Results: Serum uric acid was significantly higher in the hypertensive group compared with controls. Urinary calcium and urinary calcium/creatinine ratio were significantly lower among women with hypertensive disorders. Urinary creatinine showed no significant difference between the groups. Conclusion: Serum uric acid and spot urinary calcium/creatinine ratio may serve as simple supportive biochemical markers in the evaluation of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. title: Technological Trends and Forecasts of the Global Collaborative Robots Market
abstract: The relevance of this study is driven by the rapid growth of collaborative robotics adoption across various industries and the need to understand long-term trends for developing an effective technological development strategy. The aim of this study is to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the current state and development prospects of the global and Russian collaborative robotics markets, identifying key growth drivers, technological trends, adoption barriers, and assessing their impact on the transformation of industrial automation. To achieve this goal, the paper addresses the following objectives: assess the current size and structure of the global cobot market; analyze market development forecasts by region and application industry; systematize the barriers and limitations to collaborative robotics development; identify key technological trends and innovations in collaborative robotics; compare global market development forecasts; analyze, evaluate the potential and specifics of the Russian collaborative robotics market. The methodological framework of the study comprises general scientific methods of synthesis and analysis, statistical data processing, content analysis of open sources and peer-reviewed scientific publications. The object of the study is the global and Russian collaborative robotics markets operating under industrial digital transformation. The subject of …

title: Curvularia lunata as a versatile pathogen causing leaf spot diseases in diverse plant species and its management strategies
Climate stress, energy shocks and carbon-market connectedness in the European emissions trading system
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine state-dependent connectedness in the climate-energy uncertainty-carbon system surrounding the European Union Emissions Trading System. It asks whether average connectedness differs from carbon-market stress states and extreme-heat states. Design/methodology/approach This study constructs a monthly data set for 2011–2024 covering heat anomalies, geopolitical risk, energy transportation uncertainty, crude oil returns, European gas returns and carbon allowance returns. It combines correlation and tail-dependence evidence, partial-correlation networks and generalized forecast error variance decomposition to compare contemporaneous dependence and directional spillovers across average and stressed states. Findings The average monthly system is only modestly connected, with carbon allowances mainly receiving shocks. Connectedness rises in both lower- and upper-tail carbon-return states and during extreme-heat months, indicating that stressed conditions reveal stronger energy-carbon-uncertainty transmission than full-sample averages suggest. Under upper carbon-return states, carbon allowances also become more active in transmitting shocks. Originality/value This study integrates physical climate stress, energy shocks and uncertainty indicators into a state-dependent connectedness framework for the European carbon market. The evidence shows that averag…

title: Dried blood spot IP-10 as a biomarker of tuberculosis severity and treatment responses: results from a phase IIb trial of adjunctive acetylsalicylic acid and ibuprofen
abstract: Background Host-directed therapies may improve tuberculosis (TB) outcomes by modulating immune responses and attenuating hyperinflammation, yet accessible biomarkers remain limited. We hypothesized that interferon-γ–inducible protein 10 (IP-10/CXCL10) measured in dried blood spot (DBS), a low-threshold and field-adapted sampling method, has potential as a biomarker for treatment response in pulmonary TB. Accordingly, we assessed IP-10 levels in patients receiving adjunctive acetylsalicylic acid (ASA) or ibuprofen (IBU) alongside TB standard therapy. Methods IP-10 levels were quantified longitudinally in DBS from 120 pulmonary TB patients enrolled in the SMA-TB clinical trial (NCT04575519) at two sites in South Africa. Samples collected at baseline, week 2, week 8, and week 24 were analyzed by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Associations with disease severity and treatment response were assessed, and the predictive value of IP-10 for microbiological, clinical, and radiological outcomes was evaluated. Results IP-10 levels correlated with TB disease severity, with higher concentrations observed in patients with elevated clinical and radiological scores and positive sputum acid-fast-bacilli staining. This association was reflected in treatment response, as patients with good clinical outcomes exhibited an earlier decline in IP-10 (week 8, p=0.0005), whereas those wit…

title: Determinants of rice farmers' market participation and marketing channel choice in Côte d'Ivoire: evidence from a Multinomial Conditional Logit Model
abstract: Purpose This study identifies the determinants of rice farmers' market participation and the choice of paddy rice marketing channels in Côte d'Ivoire. Design/methodology/approach A two-stage sampling method was used to randomly select 588 rice farmers from seven rice-growing areas. Unlike previous studies, we consider the characteristics related to the use of various marketing channels by using a Multinomial Conditional Logit Model. Findings Results show that rice-farmer-specific variables, such as age, education, paddy yield, rice farming system, membership in farmer-based organizations, access to credit, and off-farm income, are crucial determinants of rice farmers' participation in the paddy market. Marketing channel-specific characteristics, such as cash payment, contractual arrangements, access to information, price per kilogram of paddy, and distance, are key determinants of marketing channel choice. Research limitations/implications Future research could be extended to other food crops and could make use of panel data. Originality/value The study demonstrates the importance of considering the characteristics of rice farmers and marketing channels together to enhance rice farmers' integration into the paddy rice market in Côte d’Ivoire. It enriches the existing literature on the integration of smallholder farmers into food crop markets in developing countries.

Cross-Subsidization as a Mechanism to Discipline Market Power: An Airport Pricing Model
abstract: The article examines cross-subsidization in airports as an incentive to refrain from the exercise of market power and avoid setting excessive airport charges. The study is relevant as the traditional treatment of airports as natural monopolies presumes that an airport operator has incentives to increase airport charges, meanwhile commercialization and growing importance of non-aeronautical services provide incentives to reduce charges for aeronautical services and not to exploit market power. The study develops a stylized airport profit-maximization model using a vertical-structural approach that distinguishes rent and platform pricing logics and derives threshold conditions under which aeronautical services are cross-subsidized by revenues from non-aeronautical services. The results show that the optimal level of an airport charge decreases as non-aeronautical revenue per passenger increases. The paper also systematizes the factors determining the profitability of non-aeronautical services. In addition, the article adds to the debate widely represented in the airport economics literature on whether the disciplining effect of commercialization is sufficient to argue against ex ante economic regulation. The article also provides the practical application of the model in a counterfactual setting: using financial statements for 5 Russian airports, the study assesses threshold valu…

title: Post-market safety signals of energy-based surgical devices: a cross-specialty disproportionality analysis of the FDA MAUDE database with robotic-platform validation and regulatory triangulation, 2015–2025
False Advertising, Market Competition, and Consumer Protection
abstract: Abstract We examine a model in which firms produce goods that are both vertically and horizontally differentiated. While firms know the quality of their product, either high or low, it is unobservable to consumers. Firms signal quality to consumers, and we investigate how market rivalry and public enforcement influence their incentives to misrepresent quality, as well as the implications for consumer welfare. Our analysis reveals that stronger enforcement, by curbing false advertising, can drive a low-quality signaling firm out of the market. This strengthens the market power of a high-quality signaling firm, leading to higher prices and ultimately harming consumers.

title: Integrating Weather and Potato Price Market Data into AI-Driven Hybrid Models for Climate-Smart Agricultural Forecasting
Servant leadership effects on service climate and employee engagement: a multi-level analysis
abstract: Purpose This study examined the multi-level relationships between servant leadership, service climate, and employee engagement. It investigated how store manager servant leadership cultivated group trust at the store level, consequently affecting service climate and influenced employee engagement through perceived supervisor support. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a multi-level design to investigate the relationships. Data were collected in two waves from a total of 1,409 restaurant employees in Thailand, with usable responses obtained from 801 individuals across 120 restaurants who completed both waves of the survey in full. On average, teams had 6.68 members. A multi-level structural equation modeling approach was employed to account for the nested structure of employees within restaurant, enabling simultaneous testing of individual-level and store-level relationships. Findings Store manager servant leadership indirectly influenced employee engagement through perceived supervisor support. Additionally, servant leadership cultivated group trust at the store level, which, in turn, positively impacted service climate. Practical implications Organizations can significantly improve employee engagement by fostering leaders who value empathy, humility, and the well-being of their teams. Additionally, by prioritizing employee growth and creating a supportive environm…

title: AI is not for luxury: balancing Chronos efficiency and Kairos experience
abstract: Purpose This study aims to theorise how AI-driven acceleration reconfigures firms’ temporal assets, creating efficiency gains while destroying relational time (trust, loyalty, premium value), a hidden cost invisible to managerial accounting but acutely felt by customers. Design/methodology/approach A mixed-method dual-coding design combining qualitative coding of 2,000 reviews (from a 1.2 M Google Maps corpus across 10 luxury chains) with an automated Gemini natural language processing extraction. The comparative design developed temporal categories and validated brand-level friction patterns while proving human interpretation essential to detect Kairos deficits and distinguish intentional deceleration from service failure. Findings Systematic temporal fractures where AI acceleration destroys relational value. Five Strategic Temporal Archetypes (Decelerator, Bifurcator, Autonomy Provider, Fragmentor, Automator) represent distinct competitive positions on the efficiency-experience frontier. Research limitations/implications This study extends AI, service and organisational temporality research by conceptualising AI as a temporal agent and introducing Kairos deficit, temporal extraction and temporal co-destruction. It also demonstrates the value of dual-coding methodologies combining computational scale with qualitative interpretation. Future research should test Strategic Tempor…

title: Gait-parameterized RL for locomotion across morphologies and scales without reward retuning
A Novel Framework for Smart Service Failure and Recovery
abstract: Abstract While conventional approaches to Service Failure and Recovery (SFR) predominantly rely on basic surveys and scenario-based experiments, recent advancements in failure recovery found in related fields like Industry 4.0, AI-enabled decision support and digital service systems have presented intriguing possibilities (Wang et al., 2024; Zhang, 2024). Against this backdrop, this study proposes a novel methodology that leverages the rapidly evolving domain of smart maintenance and knowledge-based capability to establish a fresh framework for SFR. The suggested framework consists of seven distinct modules, namely Monitoring, Predictive and Preventive, Service Failure Detection, Failure Report, Diagnosis, Prognosis, and Healing Support. This investigation delineates the key functions and activities associated with each module, elucidates the information flows between them, and outlines their interface with service providers, customers, suppliers, and clients. Additionally, it delves into the considerations and implications arising from the proposed framework.

When recovery goes beyond the focal customer: service recovery in customer-companion contexts
abstract: Purpose Firms often must decide how to allocate recovery compensation when service failures occur in customer-companion service encounters. While prior research has examined service recovery directed at individual customers or within larger group settings, less is known about recovery decisions within a customer-companion pair. This study aims to test the companion effect in service recovery by exploring how customer responses vary with companion presence during consumption and companion inclusion in recovery. Design/methodology/approach Across three experiments, this study examines loyalty program customers’ responses to service recovery in social consumption settings. Studies 1 and 2 compare companion-accompanied with solo consumption contexts, using shared and individually allocated compensation, respectively. Study 3 holds companion presence constant and compares companion-inclusive with companion-exclusive recovery, while testing the moderating roles of loyalty status and compensation amount alongside the psychological mechanisms. Findings Customers responded more favorably to recovery in companion-accompanied than in solo consumption contexts. When companion presence was held constant, companion-inclusive recovery proved particularly effective for low-tier customers when compensation was small and for high-tier customers when compensation was large. Recovery satisfaction …

title: Population Administration Service Policy Innovation Through E-SPASI in the City of Bandung
abstract: This research is motivated by the ongoing problem of queues in population administration services even though the E-SPASI (Electronic Queue Registration System Via SMS) program has been implemented by the Population and Civil Registration Office of the City of Bandung since 2016. The research gap was identified because previous studies on similar digital innovations in population administration generally only examined one stakeholder perspective and rarely integrated the perspectives of policy makers, technical implementers, system managers, and service users at the same time. This study aims to analyze the implementation of E-SPASI using the theory of Rogers Innovation Diffusion (2003), including relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability, and observability. The method used is qualitative descriptive, with data obtained through in-depth interviews with the Head of Service, service staff, system managers, and the service user community, supported by observation and documentation. The results of the study show that E-SPASI provides real benefits in the form of ease of registration, efficiency of waiting times, and service effectiveness, and has adapted to technological developments through the switch from SMS to WhatsApp. However, its implementation still faces dependence on third-party technical infrastructure, limited access for digitally vulnerable groups, li…

Foster mothers’ attachment styles and children’s attachment security in middle childhood: a mixed-methods study of the Turkish foster family service model
abstract: Attachment theory predicts that a caregiver’s own attachment organization shapes the security of the child in their care, but the evidence comes almost entirely from biological parent–infant dyads. Whether it extends to a caregiving relationship with no shared genetic history, no shared infancy, and a competing attachment figure still present is largely untested, particularly in middle childhood, when children can report on the relationship themselves. This study examined whether the attachment security of children aged 9–12 in foster care is associated with their foster mother’s attachment style, with the age at which they entered protection, and with the frequency of contact with their birth family, and explored how foster mothers and children describe those relationships. In this explanatory sequential mixed-methods study, 314 foster mother–child dyads across eight Turkish provinces, 13.2% of the eligible national population, completed the Relationship Scales Questionnaire and the Kerns Security Scale. In-depth interviews with 10 foster mothers sampled across all four attachment classifications, and their 10 children, were analysed thematically. Children’s security differed by foster mother attachment style, F (3, 310) = 13.16, p < 0.001, η 2 = 0.113, 90% CI [0.058, 0.164]; children of securely attached foster mothers scored higher than children of fearful (d = 0.83), pre…

title: Fare sensitivity at point zero: How fare-free transit riders react to fare reinstatement and service changes?
abstract: Abstract Transit users are considered insensitive to fare changes. Therefore, reducing fares is often viewed as ineffective for increasing ridership. However, removing fares has led to markedly different outcomes in practice. Fare-free transit (FFT) policies have resulted in substantial increases in ridership among the agencies that implemented them. This contrast between expected behavior and actual FFT outcomes suggests a gap between theoretical fare elasticities and the actual sensitivity of transit users in the FFT context. This study examines sensitivity to fare and service changes among FFT users, using 2024 survey data from five U.S. transit agencies. Four cumulative linked mixed models are applied, one for each of fare, in-vehicle time, waiting time, and walking time. Results reveal that riders are far more responsive to fare reinstatement than previously thought, with a 7.6 times greater likelihood of decreasing ridership per dollar increased in fare. Riders also respond more strongly to fare reinstatement than to travel time increases: a $1 reinstated fare was perceived equally as a ~ 20-min increase in travel time, while a $2 fare was perceived on par with an additional 35-min travel time. This research also examines the potential impacts of reinstating fares after operating fare-free for a while, and indicates that it could cause sharp ridership declines: 50% of new…

title: Human–AI collaborative patterns in GenAI-supported instructional design among pre-service teachers: an analysis of interaction sequences and cognitive load
abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence is profoundly reshaping the paradigm of instructional design. However, the micro-level process patterns of human-AI collaboration in generative AI-enabled instructional design for pre-service teachers still require in-depth analysis. This study aims to uncover the behavioral patterns and cognitive load characteristics of pre-service teachers when collaborating with generative AI to complete instructional design tasks and to explore the patterns of efficient human-AI collaboration. A total of 67 pre-service teachers completed instructional design tasks with AI assistance. A systematic instructional plan quality evaluation rubric was developed based on relevant theories, and participants were assigned to the high-quality and low-quality groups using a median split of their lesson-plan quality scores. The study employed lag sequential analysis to compare the behavioral sequence patterns between the two groups and measured their multidimensional cognitive load. The results indicate that the high-quality group exhibited a significant evaluation-revision bidirectional cycle and a revision self-loop, with a clear progressive sequence of “planning → decision-making → generation → evaluation → revision → re-evaluation” in their behavioral flow. In contrast, the low-quality group was mired in ineffective cycles, with fr…

title: The Effect of Digital Government Service Integration on Public Trust through Public Service Quality: A Study on Digital Government Service Users in Indonesia
abstract: Fragmented digital government services can undermine service quality and public trust through inconsistent information, repeated data entry, and disconnected administrative processes. This study examined the relationship between digital government service integration and public trust, with public service quality as a mediating variable in the Indonesian context. An explanatory quantitative design was employed to analyze data from 100 respondents using 15 reflective indicators measured on a five-point Likert scale. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was performed using SmartPLS 4, with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples to assess the measurement model, structural relationships, and mediation effects. The measurement model demonstrated adequate internal consistency reliability, convergent validity, and discriminant validity. Digital government service integration was positively associated with public service quality (B = 0.574) and public trust (B = 0.293), while public service quality was positively associated with public trust (B = 0.515). The indirect effect of digital government service integration on public trust through public service quality was significant (B = 0.296), indicating complementary partial mediation; all structural relationships were statistically significant at p < 0.001. The model explained 32.9% of the variance in public service quality an…

title: BODIPY-Based Fluorescent Probes for Selected Hazardous Chemicals: Multilevel Regulation of Sensing Performance
abstract: Abstract The rapid and reliable detection of hazardous chemicals in complex environments remains an important challenge in fluorescence sensing. BODIPY dyes and related boron-difluoride fluorophores have attracted considerable attention because of their excellent photophysical properties and highly tunable molecular structures. However, sensing performance depends not only on analyte recognition but also on excited-state processes, intermolecular interactions, aggregation behavior, analyte transport, and practical signal readout. This review examines BODIPY-based fluorescent sensing of selected hazardous chemicals at the molecular level, supramolecular and aggregated-state level, and sensing material and device level, focusing on how regulation at different levels addresses different performance limitations. At the molecular level, recognition unit design, conformational regulation, and boron-center transformation regulate analyte recognition and signal transduction. At the supramolecular and aggregated-state level, noncovalent interactions, aggregation-state regulation, and molecular packing influence emission behavior and signal stability. At the sensing material and device level, interfacial and transport regulation, sensing material construction, and device integration and signal readout improve analyte accessibility and practical detection performance. This review provides…

title: Low-frequency passive mechanical stimulation produces antidepressant-like effects in rats involving gut–brain axis modulation
abstract: Introduction Depression is associated with dysregulation of neuroendocrine, immune, and gut -brain axis pathways. Exercise is an effective non-pharmacological intervention; however, poor motivation and fatigue limit adherence in patients with depression. Methods We investigated a novel passive exercise modality, low-frequency passive vertical oscillation assisted by elastic ropes (LF-PVO-ER), in a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) rat model. Results LF-PVO-ER significantly improved depressive-like behaviors, including anhedonia and behavioral despair. Alongside these behavioral improvements, increases were observed in serum serotonin and brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), along with reductions in serum corticosterone, inflammatory markers (IL-6, TNF), and lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Histological analysis revealed attenuation of hippocampal and colonic injury. 16S rRNA sequencing showed partial restoration of CUMS-induced gut microbiota dysbiosis, as reflected by increased diversity and enrichment of short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-associated genera. Untargeted metabolomics revealed changes in amino acid, lipid, and bile acid metabolism. Integrated analyses indicated coordinated associations among gut microbiota, metabolites, and neuroimmune markers. Conclusion These findings suggest that LF-PVO-ER may exert antidepressant-like effects through multiple pathways involvi…

title: Extracellular vesicles in colorectal cancer: M2 polarization, bidirectional regulation of CAFs, metastasis, and treatment
abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), as key mediators of intercellular communication, play a critical regulatory role in the pathogenesis and treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). By carrying diverse bioactive molecules—including miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs, and DNA—EVs influence multiple components of the tumor microenvironment (TME), such as promoting macrophage M2 polarization, reducing T and B Cell activity and proliferation, enabling evasion of natural killer (NK) cell surveillance, and regulating bidirectional fibroblast interactions in CRC. Furthermore, CRC-derived EVs can promote CRC metastasis by stimulating angiogenesis in endothelial cells, facilitating epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and promoting the formation of pre-metastatic niches. Through an analysis of the role of EVs in the pathogenesis of CRC, numerous studies have found that EVs can augment the efficacy of immunotherapy. At the same time, both mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs and engineered EVs (such as plant-derived and microorganism-derived EVs) can play significant roles in the treatment of CRC. However, most current research remains in the in vitro and in vivo trial stages. Due to difficulties in purification and engineering, as well as inherent heterogeneity, clinical translation remains challenging; consequently, no related products have yet been brought to market. title: When absence becomes functional: lysine deserts in protein regulation and evolution
abstract: Lysine deserts–extended, continuous protein regions containing no lysine residues–occur across diverse proteomes, yet their definition, evolutionary origins and biological significance remain incompletely understood. In this Review, I examine the evidence linking local lysine depletion to protein regulation, with particular emphasis on ubiquitin- and proteasome-dependent pathways. Studies of toxin catalytic subunits and endogenous components of the ubiquitin-proteasome system show that introducing lysines at selected positions can alter ubiquitylation, protein turnover or function. These findings support a context-dependent model in which lysine deserts can limit the availability of ubiquitin acceptor sites within particular structural and enzymatic environments, rather than generally protecting entire proteins from modification or degradation. I discuss how lysine position, solvent accessibility, E3 ligase geometry and protein conformation determine the consequences of lysine introduction, and how N-terminal or non-lysine ubiquitylation as well as ubiquitin-independent proteolysis can bypass lysine depletion. I also consider the reported enrichment of lysine deserts in selected Actinobacteria and Mycobacterium phages, highlighting a testable Pup-proteasome adaptation hypothesis. Finally, I discuss potential functions beyond ubiquitylation and the methodological challenges of d…

title: Comparative Analysis of Pricing Regulation Models in Fuel Markets: Lessons for Russia
abstract: In recent years, Russia has seen many changes in its fuel market regulations, including the introduction of a large tax maneuver and a damping mechanism, as well as quasi-directive control over retail prices. These changes have placed an increased burden on the federal budget and increased uncertainty for oil companies. The purpose of this study was to identify patterns and consequences of different pricing regulation models in fuel markets to improve the Russian regulatory framework. The study analyzed structural options for regulating fuel markets in 149 countries and classified pricing models. Based on this analysis, optimal tools were identified for improving Russia's current model. It was found that direct forms of price regulation are typical in developing countries, used as a means of maintaining social stability. However, this can lead to fiscal risks for government budgets. The Russian model is not immune to these risks. Comparison with the experience of countries with similar institutional characteristics supports the effectiveness of more liberalized pricing models. These models increase the adaptability of the economic system and maintain a balance between social stability and economic benefits for businesses. The transition to a more liberalized form of pricing regulation can be achieved through a gradual process of removing the damping mechanism. This can be done …

title: Correction: A novel Mamba model based on frequency domain enhancement and visual state space for high-precision lithology classification
Frequency and factors associated with flare-ups in lupus patients with lupus nephritis in French Guiana
abstract: Background French Guiana ranks among the French overseas territories with the highest prevalence of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). However, local data on lupus flares and renal involvement remain limited. This study aimed to determine the frequency of lupus flares and identify associated factors among patients with lupus nephritis (LN) compared with those without renal involvement. Methods We conducted an observational historical cohort study using data from the West Guyanese lupus cohort between January 2018 and December 2022. Patients with confirmed SLE were consecutively included and classified according to the presence or absence of LN. Clinical, biological, and immunological data were extracted from medical records. Lupus flare was defined as documented disease worsening requiring therapeutic intensification. Factors associated with flares were assessed using multivariable logistic regression. Results Sixty-two patients were included, of whom 45 (72.6%) had LN. Overall, 53% experienced at least one flare. Flares occurred more frequently in patients with LN than in those without LN (62.2% vs. 29.4%). Higher anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith antibody levels, higher SLEDAI scores, fever, pleural effusion, and cutaneous manifestations were significantly associated with flares. In multivariable analysis, LN (OR 3.64; 95% CI 1.00–13.23; p=0.049) and higher anti-dsDNA antibody level…
