Exploring the feasibility of restorative justice as an alternative response to cybercrime victimization in Malaysia
abstract: Purpose The increasing prevalence of cybercrime has created complex forms of victimization involving financial loss, emotional distress and psychological harm. While the conventional criminal justice system primarily emphasizes investigation, prosecution and punishment, it may not fully address victims’ needs for acknowledgement, accountability and restoration. Hence, this study aims to explore the feasibility of implementing Restorative Justice (RJ) as an alternative response to cybercrime victimization in Malaysia. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted an exploratory qualitative research design to examine the perspectives of criminal justice stakeholders regarding the potential implementation of RJ in cybercrime cases. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 participants comprising deputy public prosecutors, judges and police officers from Johor, Sarawak and Selangor. The data were analyzed using a thematic analysis approach to identify key themes related to the feasibility for RJ implementation. Findings The findings indicate that RJ is perceived as a potentially feasible approach within Malaysia’s criminal justice system, particularly as a complementary mechanism rather than a replacement for conventional prosecution. Participants highlighted that RJ may be suitable for selected cybercrime cases involving minor offences, first-time offenders, identifiable…

SCD1 inhibition promotes lipid peroxidation and enhances anti-PD-1 response in triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Background Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a heterogeneous disease that often exhibits a relatively immunologically “cold” tumor microenvironment, which can limit the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). Alterations in lipid metabolism and lipid peroxidation may influence tumor–immune interactions and represent potential determinants of response to immune checkpoint blockade. Methods Human TNBC cell lines (MDA-MB-231, BT-549) were treated with ferroptosis inducers (FINs), including RSL3 and SCD1 inhibitor (SCD1i), and cell death was assessed. Proteomic profiling of cell lysates and conditioned media was performed, and IL-8 and MIF secretion was quantified by ELISA. Splenocytes were incubated with conditioned media to assess immune activation via flow cytometry. In vivo efficacy of SCD1i, PD-1 blockade, and their combination was evaluated using the E0771 murine TNBC model. Results SCD1i and RSL3 treatment induced the release of inflammatory mediators, including IL-8 and MIF, as confirmed by ELISA. Conditioned media from treated TNBC cells enhanced immune activation in splenocytes, characterized by increased effector CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell populations and altered expression of immune checkpoint receptors. In vivo , SCD1 inhibition increased CD8+ T cell infiltration into the tumor microenvironment and increased PD-1 and LAG-3 expression in both CD4+ and CD8 + T…

title: A longitudinal Bayesian framework for estimating causal dose-response relationships
abstract: Abstract Existing causal methods for time-varying exposure and time-varying confounding focus on estimating the average causal effect of a time-varying binary treatment on an end-of-study outcome, offering limited tools for characterizing marginal causal dose-response relationships under continuous exposures. We propose a scalable, nonparametric Bayesian framework for estimating marginal longitudinal causal dose-response functions with repeated outcome measurements. Our approach targets the average potential outcome at any fixed dose level and accommodates time-varying confounding through the generalized propensity score. The proposed approach embeds a Dirichlet process specification within a generalized estimating equations structure, capturing temporal correlation while making minimal assumptions about the functional form of the continuous exposure. We apply the proposed methods to monthly metro ridership and COVID-19 case data from major international cities, identifying causal relationships and the dose-response patterns between higher ridership and increased case counts.

title: Demand-weighted edge betweenness centrality for identifying critical pipes in water distribution networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphical abstract summarising the DWEBC workflow: a WDN is converted to a weighted graph; EPANET hydraulic outputs and demand data are used to compute DWEBC; and high-ranking pipes support resilience screening, maintenance prioritisation, and digital-twin decision-making. Water distribution networks (WDNs) support urban resilience by delivering potable water under highly variable demands and hydraulic conditions. Traditional graph-theoretic centrality measures identify critical pipes based solely on topology, overlooking the spatial heterogeneity of nodal demands that drives service loss priorities. This study proposes demand-weighted edge betweenness centrality (DWEBC), a hydraulically informed extension of EBC in which pipe length, head loss, and target-node demand are embedded into the edge-weight function, thereby aligning shortest-path computations with the hydraulic relevance of the paths. Three weighting schemes – global constant, time-varying nodal, and time-varying nodal and pipe-specific scaling – are formulated. The algorithm is demonstrated on a small laboratory-scale Kaina network, Exnet, d-town, and d-town benchmark networks and validated on Net3, where DWEBC, in particular the time-varying nodal and pipe-specific variant, distinctly ranks pipes that serve major demand corridors. This offers a rapid screening tool for maintenance prioritisation, emergenc…
venue: AQUA — Water Infrastructure, Ecosystems and Society

title: Non-monotonic response of net dust deposition kinetics to low wind speeds
abstract: Dry deposition is a major sink for mineral dust, yet its behavior under weak winds remains poorly constrained and is often parameterized monotonically with wind speed. Here we quantify size-resolved dust net accumulation kinetics in a closed-circuit recirculating wind tunnel using a two-stage protocol (brief high-wind loading followed by low-wind deposition at 0, 2, 4, and 6 m s −1 ). Cumulative retained-mass time series were measured with an array of collection trays, with the initial suspended dust loading recorded by an online concentration monitor. Particle sizes were characterized by laser diffraction and grouped into six diameter-threshold classes (PM 2.5 –PM 63 ). A first-order kinetic model described the temporal accumulation dynamics and yielded a fitted asymptotic retained mass ( a ), effective net-accumulation rate coefficient ( k ), characteristic time scale (τ=1/k), and initial net accumulation flux ( J 0 = a k ). The observed J 0 was highest at 2 m s −1 for PM 2.5 –PM 30 , and 4 m s −1 for PM 40 and PM 63 , while J 0 declined markedly at 6 m s −1 for the lower diameter thresholds. Quadratic fits across the four wind-speed levels suggest a potential maximum near 2–3 m s −1 for PM 2.5 –PM 40 . These measurements quantify the size-dependent response of effective surface retention to low wind speeds and provide benchmark behavior for coupled deposition, retention, and…

title: Genome-wide analysis of the GATA gene family in Castanea mollissima reveals key regulators involved in salt stress response
abstract: The GATA gene family comprises important transcription factors (TFs) that affect plant ontogeny and abiotic/biotic stress tolerance. Castanea mollissima is a significant economic and food-producing tree species in the Northern Hemisphere, known for its strong wind resistance and soil stabilization capabilities. Nevertheless, existing studies have not explored the characteristics and functions of the GATA family in C. mollissima . The study identified 21 CmGATA genes from the N11–1 reference genome assembly of C. mollissima , which were dispersed among 12 chromosomes. Phylogenetic analysis helped to categorize these genes into four distinct subfamilies, with genes belonging to the same subfamily exhibiting considerable similarities in terms of structural characteristics and conserved motif composition. Collinear analysis further revealed that the major driver of CmGATA gene family expansion was segmental duplication, followed by evolutionary pressure predominantly shaped by purifying selection. Phenotypic indicators, such as antioxidant enzyme activity, exhibited significant alterations, and transcriptomic analysis revealed increasingly more differentially expressed genes (DEGs) as salt stress treatment continued. Notably, transcriptome analysis demonstrated the expression patterns of CmGATA genes under salt stress, and combined with their correlation with phenotype indicators a…

title: Long-term structural response of three-layer tunnel linings in fault fracture zones
abstract: Fault fracture zones can markedly affect deep water-conveyance tunnels, but their influence on long-term behaviour of three-layer composite linings remains unclear. A three-dimensional finite-element model of the LG6 section of the Pearl River Delta Water Resources Allocation Project was developed, and its structural modelling strategy was evaluated against in situ loading-test and operational-monitoring data. Faulted and fault-free conditions were compared, and 60-year behaviour was assessed by updating key material properties. Under an internal pressure of 1.3 MPa, the fault increased the maximum radial deformation of the steel tube and self-compacting concrete (SCC) from 0.85 mm and 0.84 mm to 0.93 mm and 0.92 mm, respectively, caused a peak SCC circumferential strain of 263 με near the B1–L1 joint and produced a more uneven bolt-stress distribution. Long-term degradation increased maximum radial deformation by 12.4–13.1% and progressively transferred load from the steel tube and SCC to the segmental lining. These findings demonstrate that geo-interfaces, including the faulted ground–lining contact and the multi-layer interlayer interfaces, play a governing role in mediating long-term load redistribution and deformation localisation. The proposed framework provides a basis for geo-interface-aware service assessment of composite water-conveyance tunnels in fault-affected grou…
venue: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Geotechnical Engineering

title: Baseline anti-PLA2R antibody titer predicts treatment response and renal outcomes in rituximab-treated membranous nephropathy
abstract: Abstract Introduction As rituximab (RTX) has become a first-line therapy for idiopathic membranous nephropathy (IMN), identifying baseline predictors of treatment response is crucial for personalized management. This study was conducted to evaluate whether baseline anti-PLA2R titer could predict treatment response and renal outcomes following RTX therapy. Methods A single-center retrospective cohort study was conducted on 69 patients with PLA2R-associated membranous nephropathy treated with RTX. The primary outcome was partial/complete remission. Secondary outcomes included rapid renal function decline (eGFR decrease ≥3 mL/min/1.73m 2 /year) and renal composite endpoint (≥ 30% eGFR decline or end-stage kidney disease). Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess associations between log-transformed baseline anti-PLA2R levels and clinical outcomes. Results Over a median follow-up of 25.1 months, remission was achieved in 78.3% of patients with a median time of 6.8 months. Higher baseline log(anti-PLA2R) levels were significantly associated with a lower probability of remission (adjusted HR per 1-log increment: 0.71, 95% CI 0.58–0.87) and a higher risk of rapid renal function decline (adjusted HR per 1-log increment: 1.47, 95% CI 1.04–2.07). Patients with anti-PLA2R ≥402 RU/mL exhibited a 6.0-fold higher risk of rapid renal function decline (95% CI 1.88–19.15). Conclusion…

title: Shared mediators, divergent networks: a tissue-response hypothesis for discordant phenotypes in chronic spontaneous urticaria and atopic dermatitis
abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) and atopic dermatitis (AD) are pruritic inflammatory skin diseases that share partly overlapping mast-cell-related pathways, including IgE/FcεRI signaling, type 2 inflammation, neuroimmune signaling, and lipid mediator pathways. Yet they usually produce distinct phenotypes: transient wheals and angioedema in CSU and persistent eczematous lesions with inflammation in AD. Whether disease activity in the two conditions fluctuates concordantly or independently within the same patient has not been directly tested. This Perspective proposes that phenotypic divergence reflects the tissue-response network in which mast cell activation is embedded rather than mediator identity alone. In CSU, autoimmune and autoallergic FcεRI-dependent activation, MRGPRX2-related neuropeptide pathways, coagulation/fibrinolysis-C5a signaling, and platelet-activating factor (PAF)/lipid mediators may preferentially converge on mast cells and basophils poised for rapid degranulation within the dermal vascular/perivascular unit. This network favors histamine bursts, endothelial hyperpermeability, neurovascular itch, and feedback-limited wheal formation. In AD, mast cells are embedded in a barrier-disrupted, alarmin-rich neuroepidermal niche, producing a multicellular inflammatory network involving keratinocyte activation, cytokine and chemokine production, neuronal sensitiz…

title: Response to Govindaraju et al.
The response of multinational and international organisations to resilience and sustainability in Latin America and the Caribbean: future directions
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the theoretical foundations of resilience and sustainability in relation to multinational enterprises and international organisations operating in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). It provides an understanding of how resilience and sustainability can be developed in the context of multinational enterprises and international organisations in LAC. Design/methodology/approach Using the PRISMA methodology, 61 academic articles were analysed using a mixed-methods approach that combined quantitative and qualitative techniques. The study identifies and analyses the Sustainable Development Goals addressed in the literature. Findings The study provides a structured synthesis of how multinational enterprises and international organisations address resilience and sustainability in LAC, highlighting gaps in contextual analysis and database coverage. It identifies the principal research themes and reveals four thematic clusters. The findings emphasise the need to broaden the scope of future research and highlight implications for policy and practice. Opportunities for cross-sector collaboration among academia, businesses, policymakers and international organisations are also discussed. Originality/value To the best of the author’s knowledge, this study is among the first to provide a comprehensive synthesis of research on resilience and sustainability…

title: Does chronic occupational demand alter EEG stress biomarkers during cognitive challenge? a study of emergency physicians
Inter-particle lubrication model for ballast bed response at medium moisture contents
abstract: For railway lines in rainy regions, ballast beds may remain at medium moisture contents for prolonged periods because of their good drainage, and surface water on ballast particles can lubricate inter-particle contacts. Existing research mainly focuses on the dynamic responses of the ballast bed under field capacity (i.e. low moisture content) or saturation conditions. This study proposes an inter-particle lubrication contact model for ballast at medium moisture contents, in which lubrication force, friction coefficient and capillary force vary with the thickness of the surface water film. A minimum contact distance, defined from ballast surface asperity and water-film thickness using previous laboratory results, is introduced into the model. The model is implemented in the EDEM software program through a user subroutine and used to reproduce a full-scale half-sleeper test under simulated rainfall. The discrete-element model results show that, macroscopically, sub-ballast stress fluctuates with moisture content whereas dynamic stiffness remains nearly stable. Microscopically, moisture content changes inter-particle contact behaviour and significantly affects particle angular acceleration, with clear spatial differences across the ballast bed. The simulated macro- and microscopic trends agree well with previous laboratory observations, confirming the applicability of the propose…

title: Re: “A machine learning-based framework for predicting ovarian response and OHSS risk in GnRH antagonist IVF/ICSI cycles: a multiobjective optimization approach” (Mao et al., Middle East Fertility Society Journal, 2026)
Preparedness and institutional drivers of AI adoption in records management: perspectives of archives and records management professionals in Nigeria
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the preparedness of archives and records management (ARM) professionals in Nigeria for the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies. It also examines the influence of institutional drivers on AI integration efforts. The research addresses a critical gap in localized understanding of how individual and organizational readiness intersect to shape AI adoption in the Nigerian records management sector. Design/methodology/approach The study employed a cross-sectional survey design targeting ARM professionals registered with the Society of Nigerian Archivists. A structured questionnaire was administered via an online platform. Data from 217 respondents were analysed using descriptive statistics, t-tests and Pearson correlation to assess levels of awareness, preparedness, institutional support and perceived barriers. Findings The findings reveal individual preparedness, positive perceptions of AI benefits and strong willingness to adopt AI if trained. However, institutional support was weak, particularly in leadership engagement, strategic planning and funding. A significant positive correlation was found between institutional drivers and AI preparedness, while no gender-based differences in readiness were observed. Research limitations/implications The study emphasizes the importance of institutional reform in driving AI readiness. It sugg…

title: Does public attention effectively reduce climate risk vulnerability? Evidence from 30 Chinese Provinces from 2012 to 2022
abstract: Purpose In the context of intensifying global climate risks and increasingly frequent extreme weather events, enhancing climate adaptation capacity and strengthening risk management have become urgent tasks for governments and the public. The purpose of this study is to examine the effect of public climate attention on provincial climate vulnerability across Chinese provinces. Members of the public are key social actors in climate policy: their awareness and risk perception can prompt action that reduces vulnerability to climate risks. Design/methodology/approach China is a geographically diverse country and faces both coastal risks, such as sea-level rise, and inland challenges, such as droughts and extreme weather. Using provincial panel data in China from 2012 to 2022, this paper measures public climate attention through Baidu search volumes of climate-related keywords and constructs a climate risk vulnerability index based on exposure, sensitivity and resilience. A two-way fixed-effects model is used to examine the relationship between public climate attention and climate risk vulnerability, as well as its underlying mechanisms. Findings The findings show that climate risk vulnerability in China follows a spatial pattern, being low in the southeast and high in the northwest, with an overall declining trend over time. Public climate attention significantly reduces climate ri…

title: Use of methylene blue in the management of refractory shock in pediatric intensive care units: a nationwide assessment of clinical practice in Türkiye
DEVELOPMENT AND EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH OF A POWER SUPPLY SYSTEM FOR A AUTOTRACTOR DIESEL ENGINE FOR OPERATION IN GAS-DIESEL MODE ON LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GAS
abstract: Modernization and conversion of agricultural machinery to alternative fuels is a key tool for improv-ing its environmental and economic performance. The use of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) in dual-fuel systems allows for a significant reduction in emissions of harmful substances (CO2, CO, NOx), however, the successful conversion of serial tractor diesel engines with the provision of stable operational characteristics at all load modes remains an unsolved scientific and practical prob-lem. The purpose of the work is to develop methods and techniques for experimental research of a diesel engine in a gasodiesel cycle, which ensures its stable operation at various load-speed modes with different fuel mixture compositions. To implement the tasks set, an original schematic diagram of the gas-diesel engine power supply system with a mechanical device for manual adjustment of the position of the high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) rail of the UTN-5 type was developed, which made it possible to eliminate the instabil-ity of the standard all-mode regulator. Experimental studies were carried out on a KI-5542 brake running-in stand based on a four-cylinder diesel engine 4F11.0/12.5, additionally equipped with gas cylinder equipment, a panel rotameter LZM-15ZT-4 and an electronic gas flow weight control sys-tem. The tests were performed according to the “loading - unloading” cycle. The least sq…

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION MANAGEMENT IN ISLAMIC EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS: ADAPTATION STRATEGIES FOR THE ERA OF THE INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION 4.0 AND 5.0
abstract: Digital transformation is both a challenge and an opportunity for Islamic educational institutions in facing the dynamics of the Industrial Revolution 4.0 and Society 5.0. This study aims to analyze the digital transformation management strategies implemented by Islamic educational institutions in improving the effectiveness of governance and learning quality. The research method used is a qualitative approach with the library research method, which is by examining various literature and the latest research results that are relevant to the topic of digital transformation and Islamic education management. The results of the study show that the success of digital transformation is determined by three main aspects, namely visionary leadership based on Islamic values, strengthening the digital literacy of educators and education personnel, and integrating information technology systems in the management of educational institutions. In addition, it was found that Islamic educational institutions that are able to adapt strategically to technological changes have higher competitiveness in creating an effective, innovative, and characterful learning ecosystem. The conclusion of this study emphasizes the importance of synergy between spiritual values and technological innovation in realizing globally competitive Islamic education in the digital era.

title: Effectiveness of digital health education interventions for chronic disease self-management in community-dwelling older adults: an umbrella review and evidence classification
abstract: Background Digital health education interventions are widely promoted to support chronic disease self-management. However, existing umbrella reviews pool evidence across all ages and have not assessed community-dwelling older adults, who face barriers to digital access. This umbrella review aimed to determine whether current evidence supports the effectiveness of digital health education interventions for chronic disease self-management in community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older. Methods We conducted an umbrella review of systematic reviews evaluating digital health education interventions for chronic disease self-management in community-dwelling adults aged 60 years or older. Six databases were searched for systematic reviews published between 2015 and 2026. Meta-analytic outcomes were re-estimated using random-effects models, evidence was graded according to the Ioannidis criteria, methodological quality was assessed with AMSTAR 2, and primary-study overlap was quantified using the corrected covered area (CCA). Results Of the 1,272 records identified, 11 met the eligibility criteria, and 10 contributed 44 meta-analytic outcomes derived from 199 primary randomized controlled trials (RCTs) across five chronic disease clusters. The evidence base showed minimal overlap among primary studies (overall CCA was 0.76%). None of the outcomes met the criteria for convincing (Cl…

title: Entrepreneurship and creative destruction: the enduring relevance of Schumpeter in the age of artificial intelligence
abstract: Purpose This study aims to reexamine Schumpeter’s framework of entrepreneurship and creative destruction to assess its explanatory power in artificial intelligence (AI)-intensive capitalism, where algorithmic technologies reshape the structural conditions under which entrepreneurial agency and innovation unfold. Design/methodology/approach This study adopted a conceptual reinterpretation approach grounded in a close reading of Schumpeter’s principal texts, placing this reconstruction in dialogue with contemporary literature on AI and entrepreneurship, as well as with post-Schumpeterian patterns, including Schumpeter Mark I, Mark II and intellectual monopoly dynamics. Findings Moreover, AI confirmed the Schumpeterian conceptual core, radicalised its dynamics through temporal compression and ecosystemic displacement and necessitated a partial reformulation. Entrepreneurial judgement under radical uncertainty remained irreducible, although agency became distributed across hybrid human-algorithmic configurations where formative creativity grows increasingly automatable, while transformative creativity was dependent on human judgement. Creative destruction shifts towards platform-governed ecosystemic architectures and the prevailing Schumpeterian pattern depends on each sector’s appropriability and governance conditions, rather than on the technology itself. Where intellectual monop…

title: Refugees as economic factors or subjects of solidarity? A qualitative analysis of German corporations’ political advocacy during two migration crises
abstract: Purpose The 2015 and 2022 European refugee crises sparked vivid societal debates about how to deal with migration. While Germany played a central role as a main host state, German companies have only slowly started to enter the issue arena on migration. This study investigates how DAX-listed companies framed refugees during both crises by analyzing public statements by CEOs and board members, and examining the alignment between these positions and corresponding CSR initiatives to see whether they walked their talk. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative framing analysis identified the corporate framing of refugees. The sample included 124 statements from corporate influencers, i.e. CEOs and board members, drawn from direct quotes in traditional and social media in 2015 and 2022. CSR activities were identified through refugee-related initiatives reported in annual and sustainability reports (N = 50). Findings The findings reveal a shift and increase in framing between the two crises: in 2015, refugees were primarily discussed in the context of economic considerations, whereas in 2022, more corporate voices entered the debate, expressing greater empathy. The study also uncovers that corporations largely walked their talk, as corporate actions were adapted to match communication strategies in each period. Originality/value This research contributes to communication management r…

title: Global financial stability and exchange rate turbulence: a multiscale wavelet–quantile analysis of BRICS-T currencies
abstract: Purpose Concerns about the vulnerability of emerging-market currencies have intensified amid recurrent episodes of global financial volatility over the past 2 decades. This vulnerability is particularly pronounced among the BRICS-T economies (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and Turkey), which have become increasingly integrated into global financial markets. Although the general exposure of emerging market exchange rates to global financial shocks is widely recognised, the complex, frequency-dependent and state-dependent pathways of these spillovers remain less understood. This study contributes to this literature by offering a targeted empirical assessment of BRICS-T currency responses to global financial volatility. By applying a wavelet-quantile framework, we evaluate how global common asset volatility (COVOL) propagates across distinct return distributions and short-, medium- and long-run horizons. Design/methodology/approach The study employs daily data spanning from September 15 2005, to February 7 2025. Global financial stability is proxied by the Global Common Volatility Index (COVOL). To capture nonlinear, asymmetric and frequency-dependent dynamics, the analysis applies wavelet quantile-on-quantile regression (WQQR) and wavelet quantile regression (WQR), allowing exchange rate responses to vary across return distributions and short-, medium- and long-run ho…
venue: European Journal of Management and Business Economics

title: Factors Influencing Self-Management Behavior Among Patients with End-Stage Renal Disease Receiving Hemodialysis: A Cross-sectional Study
abstract: Hemodialysis is a critical life-sustaining treatment for individuals with end-stage renal disease. Despite advances in hemodialysis care, many of these individuals continue to demonstrate suboptimal self-management behaviors. Understanding the factors influencing self-management behaviors is essential for developing nursing interventions that effectively address people's needs. This study developed and examined a structural model of self-management behaviors among people with end-stage renal disease undergoing hemodialysis in Thailand. A cross-sectional design was employed. A total of 550 participants were recruited from 11 hemodialysis units using cluster and purposive sampling techniques. Data were collected between March and August 2024 utilizing the Demographic Questionnaire, Family State and Functioning Assessment Scale, Hemodialysis Knowledge Questionnaire, Patient Health Questionnaire, Social Support Questionnaire, Hemodialysis Self-Management Self-Efficacy Questionnaire, 14-item Health Literacy Scale, and the Hemodialysis Self-Management Instrument. Descriptive statistics and structural equation modeling were used for data analysis. The structural model demonstrated a good fit with the empirical data. It revealed that health literacy, hemodialysis-related knowledge, social support, and depression exerted direct positive effects on self-management behaviors. Family funct…
venue: Pacific Rim International Journal of Nursing Research

title: Effects of green certification and price premiums on consumer willingness to pay for recycled products from construction and demolition waste
abstract: Purpose Understanding consumers' willingness to pay (WTP) for construction and demolition waste (CDW)-recycled products is crucial for advancing the circular economy. While prior studies have separately examined consumers' responses to green products and price premiums, a neurocognitive gap remains in integrating the dual factors (green certification as a sustainability cue and price premium as a cost cue), especially for CDW-recycled products. This study aims to investigate how green certification tiers and price premiums influence consumers' WTP and the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms. Design/methodology/approach An event-related potential (ERP) experiment with a 3 (green certification tier: one-star, two-star, and three-star) × 3 (price premium level: 5%, 20%, and 35%) within-subjects factorial design was conducted. Forty participants completed a behavioral choice task (WTP assessment) while EEG data were recorded. Findings Key results revealed that behaviorally, WTP increased with increasing certification tiers and decreased with increasing premium levels, showing a significant synergistic interaction. The combination of two-star and 20% premium products elicited the longest response time, consistent with diagnostic ambiguity, while three-star and 5% premium products showed the shortest response time, consistent with cue consistency. Neurophysiologically, P200 amplitud…

title: Project governance, inclusive leadership and knowledge integration: an analysis of employee mental health in multi-project environments
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how project governance and inclusive leadership influence the mental health of project team members engaged in multiple simultaneous projects. It also investigates the mediating role of knowledge integration and the moderating role of project assignment in shaping these relationships. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through a questionnaire survey distributed to 400 employees (project managers, team leaders and team members) working in telecom organizations in Pakistan, with 150 valid responses obtained. Findings Results confirm that project governance and inclusive leadership positively affect the mental health of project team members. Knowledge integration mediates the inclusive leadership path, highlighting its role as a critical mechanism in multi-project settings. Moreover, project assignment moderates the governance path, with stronger governance benefits observed under high-assignment conditions. Originality/value This study extends the project integration and organizational behavior literature by integrating governance, leadership and knowledge integration perspectives to explain team members’ mental health in multi-project contexts. It addresses a critical research gap by linking organizational and team-level factors with employee well-being in high-pressure project environments.
venue: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems

title: Warehouse logistics and task switching theory revisited: asymmetric height switching costs in order picking systems
abstract: Purpose This study investigates the impact of pick location height switching on task performance time in manual order picking systems. Drawing on task switching theory, we examine whether switching between ground- and chest-level pick locations increases task performance time, whether switching costs are asymmetric, and whether item weight strengthens possible differences between ground-to-chest and chest-to-ground switches. Design/methodology/approach We adopt a two-stage approach that combines internal validity and operational generalizability. First, a controlled eye-tracking experiment simulates a simplified order picking scenario to explore the cognitive mechanisms underlying visual search when repeating versus switching pick location heights. Second, we analyze 3,537,973 pick location visits from a German grocery retail warehouse to test the effects of pick location height switching in a real-world operational environment with professional order pickers. Findings The eye-tracking experiment provides mechanism-oriented evidence that switching between pick location heights increases visual search time and reorientation demands under controlled conditions. The archival field study complements these behavioral insights by showing that height switching is associated with longer task performance time. It further shows that switching costs depend on direction, with ground-to-che…
venue: International Journal of Physical Distribution & Logistics Management

title: The final count-down: estimating the total value of all the world's natural resources and an estimate of how long they may last
abstract: Introduction We have attempted a final count-down of all resources available to human society in future and converted this to monetary value for 2026. Methods Simulations using the WORLD7 Integrated Assessment Model explore how long the available resources will support wealth and value creation in the global society. Results The estimates made suggests that about 75% of the world's value creation has its origin in natural resources, and about 2 / 3 of the value creation has its origin in finite, fossil natural resources, fossil energy, fossil metals, and fossil materials. Our results suggests that a system reconfiguration, including thorium-based technologies, would be required for making society last more than 1,000 generations. The most valuable resources in analysis are the energy resources, but these are partly dependent on the availability of technology metals and materials. Thorium appears to be the single most valuable energy resource on the list, provided thorium-based power plants are adopted, and based on the energy price. The gross revenue from resource extraction and the profit value of the annual production was estimated. The recoverable resource stocks of natural resources and the annual extraction rates were estimated. Discussion Our estimates were combined with earlier estimates of the value of the ecosystems on the Earth and estimates of the value of the geo- a…

title: Towards Automation and Elimination of Subjectivity in Industrial Risk Management Based on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Risk management is one of the fundamental components of a company's success, whatever its sector of activity. This paper reviews the work done in the field of risk management, both traditionally and by integrating Artificial Intelligence. It highlights the way in which risk management was solved in the traditional way, discussing methods and approaches and citing the limitations of traditional risk management. It also outlines research into the integration of Artificial Intelligence into risk management in the various phases of the risk management process. Based on the open literature published in the various journals in the field of risk management, the stages of the risk management process are the result of human judgment, which may identify risks or, for psychological or/and social reasons, may not, so human subjectivity influences the risk identification phase and all phases of the risk management process. To reduce this subjectivity and to reduce human contact in this phase, our article proposes a model based on Artificial Intelligence that attempts to identify risks and treat them in order to reduce or eliminate existing risks.
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: SpeciNet-IDS: A False-Alarm-Aware Intrusion Detection System for Reliable Network Security
abstract: In practice, false alarms still plague the ability of deployed intrusion detection systems to be effective. If models are primarily tuned for accuracy, with unbalanced traffic, they're overly tolerant of benign misclassifications; analysts become overwhelmed by a rising number of false alarms, and real threats go unnoticed. We suggest a new hybrid network (CNN-Dense) called SpeciNet, which is trained with specificity, rather than accuracy. There are 4 mechanisms that function together. A parallel Conv1D branch learns local statistical patterns, and a Dense Residual branch learns multi-feature global interactions that are important for rare attack classes. The training is based on a focal loss (γ=2, αₜ=0.75) which pulls towards flows that are borderline benign behind the majority of false alarms. The operating threshold is selected based on the far target calibration process, which is a threshold that is as high as possible and does not exceed the 2% validation far threshold. The gains are confirmed by a SHAP-based attribution gate (not used after configuration is selected), but during configuration selection. We evaluate on CICIDS2017 as the primary benchmark and NSL-KDD for corroboration. SpeciNet-IDS reaches binary false alarm rates of 0.01% and 2.71%, with specificity of 99.99% and 97.29%. On CICIDS2017, only 16 false alarms occur across 318,547 benign test instances - a 13-…
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: Reinforcement-Learning based Self-Healing Banking Transaction System against Malware Attacks in IoT Networks
abstract: The IoT technology that was at the height of popularity in the banking industry has resulted, improved real-time transaction processing, enhancing the availability of smart financial products and services, and the automated payment systems are more feasible than the traditional banking IoT security models. However, these implementations often fail to detect newly developed "zero-day” malware applications. In contrast, the proposed design for this research is based on developing a Reinforcement Learning (RL) system for banking IoT networks. As compared to traditional Intrusion Detection Systems, which send an alert and/or block the offending actions, the RL-based systems described herein treat the network as a continuous agent-environment dynamic loop that autonomously configures the network, including real-time/configurable routing protocol and resource allocation, in order to preserve transaction integrity during active malware propagation. The proposed research presents a banking transaction processing system that employs RL technology to identify, mitigate, and recover from malware-related events and intrusions in IoT-enab led financial networks by using real-time virus/abnormality detection via a deep Reinforcement Learning (RL) controller. The deep RL controller models the overall context of network security in accordance with the principles of Markov Decision Processes (M…
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology

title: Enhanced power quality compensation using an improved third-order sinusoidal integrator for a single-phase distribution system
Unlocking wind energy potential in data-scarce regions: a deep learning framework for strategic climate action in Vietnam’s Central Highlands
abstract: Purpose As Vietnam accelerates its transition toward a sustainable energy future under ambitious national strategies like the Power Development Plan VIII (PDP8), a critical barrier persists: the lack of high-fidelity resource maps for strategic planning. This is particularly acute in data-scarce regions with high potential, such as Vietnam’s Central Highlands. This study aims to address this strategic gap by developing and validating a robust deep learning framework to produce an enhanced and detailed high-resolution wind energy map for this region, providing a conservative proof-of-concept for regional energy planning. Design/methodology/approach The framework integrates coarse-resolution daily wind speed data from an ensemble of 11 global climate models with long-term observational records (1985–2023) from a sparse network of meteorological stations. To preserve synoptic extremes critical for wind power, the downscaling was conducted at a daily temporal resolution. A suite of advanced machine learning and deep learning models were systematically trained. To address the limitations of spatial interpolation in complex terrain, the downscaled 10 m wind speeds were extrapolated to a 149 m commercial hub-height using a terrain-aware power law, integrating high-resolution surface roughness data. A technical potential map (GWh/km²/year) was then generated by combining the turbine po…

title: Do government subsidy policies promote the energy transition resilience of enterprises? Empirical evidence from China
abstract: Purpose Energy transition resilience (ETR) captures enterprises’ capacity to maintain sustainability during low-carbon transitions. This paper aims to construct a comprehensive ETR evaluation index system and examines how government subsidies affect enterprises’ ETR. Design/methodology/approach This study uses panel data from 2013 to 2023 on small and medium-sized enterprises listed on China’s A-share SME and ChiNext boards to construct a comprehensive ETR evaluation index system. Econometric models are used to empirically test the impact of government subsidies on enterprises’ ETR, while further analysing the mediating role of financing constraints, the threshold moderating effect of environmental regulations and heterogeneity across ownership, region and industry. Findings The results indicate that: government subsidies significantly enhance enterprises’ ETR; the resource-based and signalling functions of government subsidies improve ETR by easing financing constraints; environmental regulations exert a countervailing moderating effect on the relationship between government subsidies and ETR, displaying a single threshold; and government subsidies have a stronger positive effect on ETR among non-state-owned enterprises, eastern enterprises and manufacturing enterprises. Practical implications The findings offer empirical support for governments to optimise subsidy policies an…

title: Lessons learned from the management of unusual scrofuloderma extending to the chest wall in an adolescent male: case report
abstract: Abstract Background Cutaneous tuberculosis is a rare manifestation of extrapulmonary tuberculosis in children. Scrofuloderma is the most common manifestation of cutaneous tuberculosis in developing countries. It results from the direct extension of tuberculosis infection from an underlying infected structure, such as lymph nodes, bones, or joints, to the overlying skin. We report a remarkable case of scrofuloderma extending to the chest wall in an adolescent male. Case presentation A 16-year-old Indonesian male who had received six months of inadequate-dose tuberculosis treatment presented to our Pediatric Respirology Clinic with a complaint of a new cervical nodule. He had a prior history of bilateral cervical nodules and a mass on the right chest wall. The patient had previously received inadequate dose of antituberculosis therapy. Fine-needle aspiration biopsy of the cervical nodules confirmed tuberculous lymphadenitis. A thoracic CT scan revealed an abscess, and thoracotomy with aspiration was performed. Histopathological examination confirmed tuberculous inflammation of the chest wall. He was restarted on adult fixed-dose combination antituberculosis therapy at an adequate dose for 12 months. As a result, the nodules resolved, skin lesions healed, and significant weight gain occurred. Conclusion In high TB-burden settings, clinicians should recognize the varied manifestati…

title: A critical review of cross-cultural adaptation and psychometric validation studies of the principal instructional management rating scale (PIMRS)
abstract: Purpose Despite the widespread international use of the Principal Instructional Management Rating Scale (PIMRS), limited contemporary attention has focused on its adaptation across cultural contexts and the breadth of validation evidence supporting those adaptations. Design/methodology/approach This integrative review examined 12 formal PIMRS adaptation and validation studies conducted across nine countries. The included studies were classified as validation-only, adaptation and validation, or reconstruction and validation, and critically examined for model retention or modification, contextual adaptation, sampling characteristics, and psychometric evidence. Findings Consistent retention of the three-dimensional PIMRS framework across the 12 reviewed studies offers preliminary evidence of conceptual stability alongside localized modification across cultural and institutional settings. Selective modification or removal of functions such as Curriculum Coordination, Principal Visibility, and Incentives for Learning highlights the need for contextual sensitivity in adapting the instrument. Validation practices were uneven, relying heavily on internal consistency estimates and confirmatory factor analysis fit indices. Evidence concerning response processes, criterion-related validity, and measurement invariance was limited, as was attention to sampling adequacy and the nested struct…

title: Textbook outcome–based performance assessment during transition to the da Vinci SP system in reduced-port robotic gastrectomy
Comprehensive Formulation of Power Balance and Exergy Analysis for the Assessment of Highly Integrated Transport Aircraft
abstract: Abstract In the context of future transport aircraft, advanced concepts of propulsion-airframe integration feature Boundary Layer Ingestion (BLI), Distributed Propulsion (DP), together with advanced propulsion technologies such as Open Rotor, and Ultra High Bypass Ratio (UHBR) engine configurations. These concepts have the potential for reducing overall aerodynamic drag but also introduce a strong coupling between thrust and drag, necessitating the use of comprehensive performance assessment methods like Exergy Analysis and Power Balance. The key advantage is that both methods eliminate the need to explicitly determine aerodynamic forces acting on the body and are applicable to steady-state compressible flows. A unified nomenclature has been developed in the present paper to enable meaningful comparisons between Exergy Analysis and Power Balance methods, and to clarify the types of physical phenomena each method can investigate. It is also shown that the terms in the Power Balance method can be deduced from Exergy Analysis by omitting the terms associated with heat transfer and associated entropy generation. Despite their differing capabilities in identifying specific loss mechanisms, both approaches provide complementary insight into system losses and remain valuable tools for uncovering opportunities to improve aircraft system efficiency.

title: Social Capital as a Tool of Recovering the Competitiveness in Tea Plantation Sector in Sri Lanka
abstract: This study examines how social capital contributes to improving the competitiveness of Sri Lanka’s tea plantation sector. Adopting a mixed method approach, qualitative data were collected through interviews and observations, while quantitative data were obtained from 200 employees across 100 profit centers. The findings reveal that managerial employees perceive social capital as a strategic resource, whereas non-managerial employees view it as a naturally embedded social phenomenon. Empirical results confirm that social capital has a significant positive impact on firm competitiveness, with knowledge sharing acting as a partial mediator. The study contributes to the literature by providing empirical evidence from an agricultural sector context and offers policy recommendations to enhance industry competitiveness. Future research should consider larger samples and advanced analytical techniques.

title: Machine Learning-based forecasting of PM2.5 levels in Byrnihat, Meghalaya: Northeast India’s most polluted city
Reservoir eutrophication prediction with explainable framework integrating temporal convolutional networks and bidirectional sequence modeling
abstract: Abstract Accurate prediction of total nitrogen (TN) concentration in dam reservoirs is recognized as one of the significant challenges in water resources management. In this regard, the present study, to develop an intelligent and robust modeling framework, introduced the integrated model, which consists of the combination of the improved variational mode decomposition algorithm (IVMD), the attention mechanism-based temporal convolutional neural network (AttTCN), the bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and the grasshopper optimization algorithm (GOA), which is used to predict the total nitrogen of Mahabad Dam. The results of this study suggest that the proposed framework has a significant advantage over conventional models, as the analysis of the indices indicated that, with each layer of complexity added to the model, prediction accuracy improved significantly. The 80% reduction in the mean absolute error value from the basic BiGRU model to the final IVMD-GOA-AttTCN-BiGRU model, along with the improvement of Willmott’s index of agreement from 0.75 to 0.99, confirms the superiority of the proposed integrated approach. This significant improvement in accuracy demonstrated that the intelligent combination of data preprocessing, an attention mechanism, and hyperparameter optimization can yield models with greater reliability in water quality prediction. The use of interact…

title: A hybrid deep Kronecker and BN-eLU-AlexNet framework for early prediction of learner outcomes in e-learning platforms
abstract: Introduction Early prediction of learner outcomes in online learning environments can support timely academic intervention and learner support. Methods This study proposes DKBNE-AlexNet, a hybrid architecture combining a Deep Kronecker Network branch, a feature-token batch-normalized eLU AlexNet-inspired branch, gated residual fusion, and a wide linear residual path. Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, 24,153 enrolments from 22 module presentations and 22,234 learners were analyzed. Eighty-four predictors were constructed from learner characteristics, course design, and engagement during the first 25% of each presentation. The target was the weighted mean of tutor-marked and computer-marked assessment scores. Models were evaluated using five-fold cross-validation grouped by module presentation and repeated three times. Results DKBNE-AlexNet achieved an MAE of 11.424 (95% group-bootstrap CI 10.389-12.560), RMSE of 14.843, and R 2 of 0.117. Random Forest and LightGBM achieved slightly lower MAEs of 10.916 and 10.918, respectively, but the presentation-level difference between DKBNE-AlexNet and Random Forest was not statistically significant (Wilcoxon p = 0.388; Holm-adjusted p = 1.000). Distinct learning materials accessed and active learning days were among the strongest predictive contributors. Discussion DKBNE-AlexNet provides a competitive and stable framewo…

Explainable machine learning integrating CT-derived intratumoral heterogeneity for histological subtype prediction in pure ground-glass lung adenocarcinoma: multicenter validation and transcriptomic characterization
abstract: Background Preoperative differentiation of lepidic-predominant adenocarcinoma from other histological subtypes in lung adenocarcinoma presenting as pure ground-glass nodules remains challenging. We evaluated whether a CT-derived intratumoral heterogeneity score provides complementary predictive and biological information beyond routine clinical and CT features. Methods This retrospective multicenter study included 533 patients, divided into a training cohort (n = 373) and a held-out validation cohort (n = 160). Twelve supervised algorithms were compared exclusively within the training cohort using stratified five-fold cross-validation and grid-search optimization; predictors, hyperparameters, and the decision threshold were locked before the held-out cohort was evaluated once. Incremental value of the ITH score and leave-one-center-out internal–external validation were additionally assessed. Segmentation reproducibility was evaluated in 100 lesions. An independent radiogenomic cohort of 43 pathological Tis/T1 lung adenocarcinomas was analyzed by differential-expression and Hallmark gene-set enrichment analyses after median ITH-score stratification. Results XGBoost achieved the highest training-set cross-validation AUC (0.908 ± 0.021) and was selected before held-out evaluation. In the validation cohort, the AUC was 0.919 (95% CI, 0.870–0.968), with accuracy 0.850, precision 0.8…

High performance white blood cell classification using ensemble CNNs with Monte Carlo dropout and conformal prediction for clinical uncertainty quantification
abstract: Automated classification of white blood cell (WBC) images may support cell-morphology workflows, but high accuracy alone does not establish clinical readiness. We developed an Uncertainty-Guided Deep Ensemble (UGDE) combining MobileNetV3-Large, EfficientNet-B0, and ShuffleNetV2 with Monte Carlo dropout, temperature scaling, split conformal prediction, and Grad-CAM. The primary dataset contained 16,027 single-cell images from 78 patients (33 with leukemia and 45 without leukemia). All stated development partitions were grouped by patient, and augmentation was restricted to the proper training subset. On the held-out internal test set (3,205 images from 16 patients), UGDE achieved approximately 99% image-level accuracy and macro-F1 of 0.99. Expected calibration error was 2.3% before and 0.8% after temperature scaling. Internal empirical conformal coverage was 94.2%, 89.7%, and 79.7% at nominal coverage levels of 95%, 90%, and 80%, respectively; these slight shortfalls are reported without claiming that the targets were met. External evaluation used 2000 Raabin-WBC images after mapping the nine model outputs to five shared leukocyte categories and yielded 94% descriptive accuracy. Grad-CAM examples were used as post-hoc visualizations and were not interpreted as causal explanations. These retrospective results support further evaluation of uncertainty-aware WBC image classificatio…

title: Sustainable by All-Biobased Design: Recyclable Flax Fiber/Silk Matrix Composites with Machine Learning-Assisted Mechanical Performance Prediction
abstract: Abstract Fiber-reinforced polymer composites are indispensable structural materials, yet their sustainability is limited by two key issues: the environmental impact of manufacturing and the difficulty of recycling at the end of life. Here, we develop fully biobased composites by combining flax fibers with a regenerated silk fibroin matrix to overcome both obstacles. Owing to the room-temperature self-assembly capability of the silk matrix, chemical additives such as crosslinkers, curing agents, and catalysts are completely avoided during fabrication. The resulting composite achieves a tensile strength and modulus of up to ∼70 MPa and 2.4 GPa, comparable to conventional petroleum-based counterparts, while the silk matrix can be dissolved to non-destructively recover flax fibers for repeated reuse. To complement this all-biobased material design, we further construct a machine learning model trained on experimental datasets for predicting the mechanical properties of fiber-reinforced silk matrix composites. By narrowing the experimental formulation search space and identifying a promising fiber-content range for subsequent experimental validation, this data-driven approach serves as a low-resource design aid that reduces trial-and-error experimentation. Collectively, the combination of fully biobased composite design with machine learning-guided formulation offers a promising pat…

title: Risk factors associated with colorectal adenomas and the formulation of prediction models
abstract: Importance Colorectal adenomas (CRAs) are the primary precancerous lesions in the development of colorectal cancer; establishing a simple, cost-effective and non-invasive tool for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy is of great significance for risk stratification. Objective To investigate the association between peripheral blood metabolic and inflammatory markers and the risk of colorectal adenomas, and to develop a personalised risk prediction model for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy. Design, setting, and participants This study was a single-centre retrospective case-control study conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong Second Medical University. The study included 2,437 patients with colorectal polyps who underwent endoscopic resection between January 2020 and December 2025. Exposures Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors and peripheral blood biochemical markers, with a particular focus on the triglyceride-to-glucose (TyG) ratio and markers of systemic inflammation. Main outcomes and measure Patients with colorectal adenomas confirmed by histopathology. title: An Enhanced Bi-LSTM for Shield Tunnelling Parameter Prediction Coupled with Transfer and Incremental Learning
Dynamic dopamine signaling, prediction error, and microcircuit mechanisms in stress-induced depression-like behaviors
abstract: Chronic stress contributes to major depressive disorder (MDD) phenotypes by disrupting coordinated neuromodulatory systems and their corresponding computational frameworks. In this review, we explore how the dynamic interplay of ventral tegmental area dopamine (DA) signaling, microcircuit gating, and prediction error mechanics orchestrates stress-induced depressive behaviors, such as anhedonia and amotivation. Rather than acting as the sole driver of depression, pathway-specific neuroadaptations across mesolimbic ( VTA → NAc ) and mesocortical ( VTA → PFC ) dopaminergic projections operate within a broader multi-transmitter landscape, interacting with serotonergic, noradrenergic, cholinergic, and glutamatergic/GABAergic systems. These signaling anomalies often translate into computational deficits in reinforcement learning, manifesting as blunted striatal reward prediction error (RPE) signals that scale directly with anhedonia severity. Chronic stress also disrupts cortical microcircuit gating governed by dopamine D 1 and D 2 receptors, inducing cellular senescence and collapsing ensemble synchrony within the prefrontal cortex and interconnected networks. Furthermore, specialized subcortical loops, including inputs from the nucleus accumbens (NAc), ventral hippocampus (vHIPP), lateral habenula (LHb), and locus coeruleus (LC), recalibrate overall susceptibility versus resilience…

LACO-GAI: A Laplace Copula Generative AI Network Model for Accurate Stroke Disease Prediction
abstract: Stroke is major wellbeing condition which creates serious hazard to human health and cause of bereavement and disability universal. Several risk factors contribute to its development, including hypertension, diabetes, tobacco use, raised cholesterol levels, and obesity. Conventional methods have been used to predict stroke, however it frequently face demands in achieving enhanced accuracy as well as minimizing errors. To overcome the demands mentioned above, a new model named the Laplace Copula Generative Artificial Intelligence (LACO-GAI) is introduced to deliver precise stroke predictive outcomes with minimal time and error rate. Initially, patient data samples are gathered from relevant datasets during the data acquisition stage. Input information is first transferred to input level, then forwarded to first hidden layer, where pre-processing takes place. This includes handling missing values through Multiple Imputations by Chained Equations (MICE) technique and removing anomalies or outliers using High Contrast Subspace method to compromise model performance. In second hidden level, is executed by Laplace Copula Multivariate feature ranking method, which identifies and retains the most relevant features. Subsequently, the third hidden layer handles the stroke prediction phase by employing Logistic Regression as a binary classification model to accurately forecast the presenc…

title: A 2-year prognostic assessment of patients with coronary borderline lesions based on three-vessel quantitative flow ratio and the development and internal validation of a risk prediction nomogram
abstract: Objective To investigate the prognostic value of three-vessel quantitative flow ratio (3V-QFR) in patients with borderline coronary lesions (QFR 0.75–0.80) over a 2-year period; to identify key variables using LASSO regression; and to construct and internally validate a personalized nomogram model for predicting major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) over 2 years. Methods This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with coronary artery disease who were treated at Ordos Central Hospital from January 2021 to December 2024, underwent coronary angiography revealing at least one borderline lesion in a major coronary artery, and received a QFR assessment. Patients were followed for up to 24 months after discharge through outpatient visits, telephone follow-up, and electronic medical-record review. The primary endpoint was defined as the occurrence of MACE during the 2-year follow-up period. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was used to explore the nonlinear relationship between 3V-QFR and the risk of MACE. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) penalized regression evaluated 19 prespecified candidate predictors using 10-fold cross-validation and the one-standard-error rule. A nomogram was constructed based on the selected factors, and the model’s discriminatory power, consistency, and clinical net benefit were evaluated using receiver ope…

title: Monitoring centerless grinding processes for workpiece roundness prediction using internal machine sensors and Bayesian sparse regression models
Scientific Machine Learning: Prediction of Freeform Microlens Shapes
abstract: The electrical deformation of liquid polymer droplets offers a promising approach for the fabrication of customized freeform microlenses. This work investigates Scientific Machine Learning models for predicting the resulting lens shapes before UV curing. Three different neural network architectures are compared: a pointwise Multilayer Perceptron, a sequence-wise 1D convolutional U-Net and a self-attention-based Transformer Encoder for sequence regression. Prior knowledge of the geometric microlens boundaries is embedded either as a soft penalty term in the loss function or as a hard boundary constraint through a trial function layer. The sequence-wise architectures show improved prediction accuracy compared with pointwise regression. The best root mean squared error is obtained with the hard-constrained 1D U-Net (3.1 μm), followed closely by the hard-constrained Transformer (3.3 μm). The results show that the imposed boundary constraints improve physical consistency locally, while future work will include global constraints to further enhance the overall robustness of the predicted shapes.

Latent class analysis of intrinsic capacity and its association with quality of life in hospitalized older people with stroke: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Objective This study aimed to identify latent classes of intrinsic capacity among hospitalized older people with stroke and to examine the associations of these classes with stroke-specific quality of life. Methods A cross-sectional design was used, and 314 hospitalized older people with stroke were consecutively recruited. Stroke severity was assessed using the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), comorbidity burden using the Age-adjusted Charlson Comorbidity Index (ACCI), perceived social support using the Perceived Social Support Scale (PSSS), intrinsic capacity across five domains using the Intrinsic Capacity Assessment Tool, and stroke-specific quality of life using the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life Scale (SS-QOL). Latent class analysis identified intrinsic-capacity profiles, and multivariable logistic regression was used to examine factors associated with latent-class membership, and ANOVA was used to compare SS-QOL scores across the identified classes. Results LCA identified three latent classes of intrinsic capacity among hospitalized older people with stroke: the low motor–low vitality group (27.70%), the low cognitive–moderate vitality, psychological, and sensory group (17.20%), and the function maintenance group (55.10%). Multinomial logistic regression showed that age, stroke severity, sleep duration, and social support were associated with membersh…

title: Capacity strengthening for community health workers in trachoma prevention and referrals: a mixed-methods study in Al Sabra district, Ibb governorate, Yemen
abstract: Trachoma remains a preventable cause of blindness in fragile and conflict-affected settings, where community-level prevention is often weak. This study examined short-term changes in community health worker capacity for trachoma prevention and referral practices, and community-reported behaviors following a capacity-strengthening intervention in Al Sabra district, Ibb, Yemen. A mixed-methods pre–post implementation design was used around an intervention delivered from 7 May to 9 July 2025. Quantitative data included CHW knowledge surveys and routine facility records of reported eye infections as a proxy indicator. Qualitative data were collected through in-depth interviews, community dialogues, and focus group discussions. Fifteen CHWs participated alongside supervisors, health staff, and community members. At endline, CHWs demonstrated high knowledge of trachoma transmission, prevention, and referral, alongside high self-reported confidence in case identification, referral, and community education. Because the baseline survey included CHWs and supervisors, whereas the endline survey included CHWs only, these findings were interpreted descriptively rather than as a direct paired comparison. Qualitative findings suggested greater awareness, less reported reliance on traditional remedies, and wider use of facial cleanliness and hygiene practices, particularly among mothers and ch…

title: Building sustainable QI capacity through a regional QI education programme: lessons from 8 years of experience with London paediatric resident doctors
abstract: Introduction Since 2018, the NHS London Specialty School of Paediatrics has collaborated with QIClearn (an independent organisation) to design and deliver a structured Quality Improvement (QI) education programme for postgraduate resident doctors in the region to build QI capacity. The programme (QI Change Champions) has been designed not only to equip resident doctors with core improvement skills but, uniquely, to secure its own future through a novel, scalable approach to faculty and mentor development. This paper outlines the experience and learning from this programme, discusses transferable lessons and the potential contribution to the wider field of QI education. Method We believe we have developed an innovative and sustainable model for embedding essential QI capability into postgraduate training for resident doctors in a region. We have observed QI in practice by constantly reflecting, learning and adapting our approach. Although this is not a formal programme evaluation, we have described our work in practice and the themes captured from mentor and learner feedback used to continually improve the programme. The analysis was designed to mitigate bias, in view of the fact that QIClearn was receiving payment as a company, and the faculty who co-designed the programme were educators for the London Specialty School of Paediatrics and not employed by QIClearn. Results We hav…

title: Mechanical Properties and Volatile Pollutants Absorbing Capacity of Mortar Composites with Addition of Coconut Shell Activated Carbon and Gamal Wood Chips Aggregates
abstract: The use of biomass has the potential to improve the mechanical characteristics of cement-based composites. Activated carbon is considered competitive in absorbing hazardous pollutants in the air, is able to reduce cracking and increase the mechanical strength of cement-based composites. The addition of gamal wood chips also has the potential to increase flexibility in mortar composites. The purpose of this study was to analyze the characteristics of the mechanical properties and pollutant absorption capacity of mortar composites with the addition of activated carbon and gamal wood chips. In this study, activated carbon is used as a fine aggregate (filler) with an addition of 1-5% to the weight of cement. Gamal wood chips are used as much as 1.5% of the total weight. Composite brick testing includes density, compressive strength, modulus of elasticity (MOE), modulus of rupture (MOR), adsorption capacity for ammonia, benzene, chloroform, and formaldehyde and thermal analysis of Field Emission Electron Microscopes (FE-SEM) and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). The density of composite mortar with the addition of activated carbon and gamal wood chips ranges from 1950.36±19.54-2137.24±45.09 kg/m3, compressive strength 8.48±0.76-9.71±1.68 MPa, MOE 421.74±69.59 -645.58±57.51 MPa, MOR 2.14±0.27-2.75±0.20 MPa. Mechanism-Guided Triple Defense of Solid Deposition Enabling Durable Electrochemical Cement Clinker Precursor Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrifying cement production offers a viable pathway to decarbonize one of the world’s most CO2-intensive industries. Electrochemical synthesis of cement clinker precursors enables low-temperature manufacturing but is constrained by solid deposition, reactor blockage, and voltage instability that limit durability. Here, we identify the dominant deposition-induced degradation pathway in a three-chamber electrochemical reactor and develop mechanism-guided mitigation strategies. The voltage rise is governed by ohmic loss from Ca(OH)2 accumulation in the middle chamber, while coupled experiments and simulations reveal that hydrodynamic heterogeneity creates low-velocity zones that promote particle retention. Guided by these insights, a synergistic triple-defense strategy integrating flow-field redesign, electrolyte regulation, and surface wettability control suppresses deposition at multiple origins. As a consequence, these coordinated interventions extend continuous reactor operation from ∼1 to ∼9 h without sacrificing Faradaic efficiency. Furthermore, the strategy was validated in a scaled-up reactor with an effective electrode area of 100 cm2, achieving stable operation for 100 h at 5 A (50 mA cm–2). This work elucidates deposition-driven degradation mechanisms and establishes general design principles for durable electrochemical reactors for industrial decarbonizatio…

Analysis of stability influencing factors and failure mechanism of anti-dip rock slope under strong earthquake
abstract: Anti-dip rock slope is a common layered rock slope, and the failure mechanism of it under strong earthquake is not well studied. In order to analyze the stability and failure mode of anti-dip rock slope under strong earthquake, this paper investigates 60 typical failure cases of anti-dip rock slope, analyzes the effect of factors on slope stability, and summarizes the failure mode. Taking the Hongshiyan slope as an example, the dynamic response law of the slope under earthquake action was summarized, and the failure mechanism of the slope was studied. Finally, the sensitivity of each influencing factor was analyzed through orthogonal experiments. The results show that the failure mode of the anti-dip rock slope with hard rocks upper and soft rocks lower is the shear slip of the soft rock at the bottom and the tensile cracking and topplingfailure of the hard rock at the top. The influencing factors ranked in descending order of sensitivity are as follows: slope angle, seismic wave frequency, inclination, seismic wave amplitude, slope shape coefficient, and slope height. It is of great significance to study the failure mode of anti-dip rock slope under strong earthquake and evaluate its stability for slope disaster prevention and control in infrastructure engineering.

Numerical study of load bearing behavior and load sharing mechanism of anchored MSE walls
abstract: As key components in the design of anchored MSE walls with constrained reinforced fill zones, anchors and geosynthetic reinforcement have an important influence on the load bearing behavior and deformation characteristics of the wall system. This paper presents a numerical study on the behavior of three wall configurations, including unanchored MSE wall, anchored MSE wall, and anchored wall without geosynthetic reinforcement, to quantitatively assess the influence of anchors and geosynthetic reinforcement and clarify the load sharing mechanism. In this study, a finite-difference model was developed and validated against instrumented reduced-scale unanchored and anchored MSE wall tests. The simulated results were in reasonable agreement with the measurements, including facing displacements and reinforcement tensile strains. The results indicate that the combined restraint provided by anchors and geosynthetic reinforcement is more effective in reducing facing displacement. Settlement response transitions from an anchor-dominated mode at low stress levels to a coupled anchor-reinforcement mode at higher applied vertical stresses. In addition, the inclusion of anchors restrains outward wall movement and reduces lateral stress release behind facing, resulting in greater lateral soil thrust. title: Exploring the protective mechanism of Huangqishengmaiyin against anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in breast cancer with concomitant gut microbiota modulation
abstract: Objective To elucidate the bioactive compounds and cardioprotective mechanism of Huangqishengmaiyin (HQSMY) against anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity (AIC) in breast cancer with concomitant gut microbiota modulation. Methods Myocardial fibrosis was quantified using Masson's trichrome staining. Hematoxylin and eosin staining was used for general histopathological evaluation. Ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-Q Exactive HFX) was employed to comprehensively identify blood components in HQSMY. The regulatory effect of HQSMY on the gut microbiota of AIC mice was assessed by 16S rRNA microbial sequencing. Network pharmacology and molecular docking mapped the compound-target-pathway network. Western blot was performed to detect key proteins in the predicted pathways, including JAK1, STAT3, and HIF-1 α . Results HQSMY reduced myocardial fibrosis rates, enhanced gut microbiota diversity, abundance and health indices. Meanwhile, HQSMY increased the abundance of anti-inflammatory bacteria like Bacteroidetes and restored normal metabolic pathways in multiple gut microbes, including glycolysis. 42 blood components were identified, exhibiting antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and gut microbiota-regulating activities. Network pharmacology analysis revealed that the JAK-STAT and HIF-1 signaling pathways are key mechanisms. Enrichment analysis focused…

Evolution mechanism of damage locations in drift region of SiC MOSFETs under heavy ion irradiation
abstract: This paper investigates the evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations in the drift region of the SiC MOSFETs under different applied drain voltages (VDS(irra)) during heavy ion irradiation using 587 MeV 36Kr ions. It is interesting to find from the post-irradiation blocking I–V curves that the drain–source leakage current increases significantly at about 500 V for the case under relatively low VDS(irra) (175–300 V) and increases rapidly at low voltage for the case under relatively high VDS(irra) (350 V). To explain this phenomenon, a local damage-related lifetime-model along the ion track is proposed and validated by technology computer-aided design simulations. The model indicates that thermal damage will develop near the p-base/n-drift junction once the damage near the n-drift/n-sub junction along the ion track becomes sufficiently serious with increasing VDS(irra). The proposed evolution mechanism of severe thermal damage locations can help analyze mechanisms of single-event leakage current and single-event burnout in SiC devices and guide radiation-hardening designs for SiC devices.
