Improving energy efficiency and carbon balance through conservation and precision agriculture with respect to conventional agriculture: a methodological approach
abstract: Introduction Conservation Agriculture (CA) is based on three core principles that, at farm scale, imply minimizing soil disturbance through tillage, maintaining a permanent soil cover with residues and diversifying the species in crop rotations. Precision Agriculture (PA) envisages a more efficient use of inputs by reducing the overlaps between machine passes. The combination of both contributes to a more sustainable agricultural system. Methods A four-season study was carried out to assess the energy consumption and carbon balance of a combined CA and PA system. No-tillage (NT) with residue retention and tractor guidance assistance (GA) was compared with conventional tillage (CT) in three annual crops: wheat, sunflower and legumes. To analyse the data obtained, a simple methodological approach was developed to facilitate energy and carbon balance calculations. Results No significant differences were found in yield between systems. NT with GA reduced fuel consumption by around 50%, and the energy parameters studied improved compared with CT. Across crops, energy efficiency relative to CT ranked as follows: sunflower > wheat > legumes. A similar pattern was observed for carbon use efficiency and carbon use productivity. Conclusions The results show the suitability of jointly using CA and PA techniques, such as tractor guidance under NT soil management.

title: Atomically Dispersed Copper Sites on Nitrogen-Doped Mesoporous Carbon for Efficient Ammoxidation of Aromatic Alcohols to Nitriles
abstract: Abstract Catalytic ammoxidation of alcohols has emerged as a preeminent technology for nitrile synthesis, distinguished by its utilization of low-cost, readily accessible alcohols and the circumvention of highly toxic cyanide-based reagents. Herein, we report for the first time a nitrogen-doped mesoporous carbon-supported Cu-based single-atom catalyst that enables the efficient conversion of alcohols and aqueous ammonia to nitriles in the aqueous phase with molecular oxygen as the oxidant. This catalytic system exhibits a wide range of substrates, including various benzylic, allylic, and heterocyclic alcohols. Most substrates can be efficiently converted into the corresponding nitriles in moderate to excellent yields under mild conditions. Furthermore, the catalyst features robust stability, enabling 13 consecutive catalytic cycles with no notable attenuation in catalytic activity. Gram-scale experiments validate the excellent practical feasibility of the catalyst. XPS, aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM, and XAFS characterizations verified the existence of atomically dispersed Cu sites coordinated with nitrogen atoms. The potassium thiocyanate poisoning experiment, DFT calculations, as well as the comparison of the performance of Cu or CuO nanoparticle-based catalysts, suggested that Cu-Nx sites are the main contributors to the ammoxidation of alcohols to nitriles. Mechanism inve…

title: Optimization of span distance in photoelectrothermal-based curved-type hydrophilic carbon fabric evaporators for seawater desalination
The enhanced capabilities of mid-infrared limb emission sounding to observe stratospheric aerosol injection geoengineering
abstract: Using a model-based pseudo-reality (PR) future scenario and realistic pseudo-observations (POs) representative for a proposed satellite mission concept (CAIRT – the Changing-Atmosphere Infra-Red Tomography explorer), we analyse the capabilities of a high-spectral-resolution limb-emission sounding technique to detect and quantitatively monitor very weak stratospheric aerosol injections (SAI) geoengineering deployments, in terms of the injected sulphur dioxide (SO 2 ) and its evolution into sulphate aerosols (SA). Our results suggest that this technique would detect SO 2 injections, at the horizontal and vertical scale, within hours to a few days since the SAI deployment. This concept would quantify the SO 2 injected mass, even for injections of the order of magnitude of a few hundreds of tonnes of SO 2 per day, characteristic of “near-term” to “mid-term” experiments feasible even unilaterally, or in the context of small-scale outdoor experiments, with presently existing technology and at relatively low cost. In addition, our results suggest that this concept would be able to track the temporal evolution of the subsequently formed SA, as it spreads zonally and then toward higher latitudes through meridional dispersion, and to monitor changes in its vertical distribution over time through processes like self-lofting of the resulting SA plume. Existing satellite instruments, e.g. b…

title: Advancements in Diamond-Like Carbon (DLC) Coatings for Dental Applications: A Narrative Review
abstract: Dental implants have revolutionized restorative dentistry, yet long-term success can be compromised by biological and mechanical complications, primarily peri-implantitis. The implant abutment, as the transmucosal component, plays a critical role in establishing a stable soft-tissue seal and preventing bacterial colonization. In the field of dentistry, surface modification of abutments is a key strategy to enhance their performance. Examples of such modifications include laser microtexturing, anodic oxidation and bioactive molecule coatings. Among various materials, Diamond-Like Carbon (DLC) coatings have emerged as a highly promising candidate due to their unique combination of mechanical, chemical and biological properties. This review critically evaluates the application of DLC coatings on dental abutments, with a specific focus on their advantages and disadvantages. Key advantages include superior biocompatibility, reduced bacterial adhesion, excellent wear resistance and a low coefficient of friction, which collectively contribute to improved soft-tissue integration and reduced risk of peri-implant disease. However, significant challenges hinder their widespread clinical adoption. These disadvantages include concerns regarding the long-term adhesion of the coating to the abutment substrate (delamination), potential degradation in the oral environment, the high cost and com…
venue: Journal of Dental Health and Oral Research

title: Shrub expansion increases particulate organic carbon accumulation through reduced shoot litter decomposition rates
abstract: Abstract Shrub expansion is a widespread phenomenon in global grasslands, yet its impact on soil organic carbon (SOC) content remains inconsistent. Investigating litter input and decomposition rates can clarify the dynamics and mechanisms driving SOC formation during grassland shrubification. This study investigated the impacts of shrub-induced changes in litter input and decomposition on SOC and its composition within the 0–20 and 20–40 cm soil layers on the Tibetan Plateau. We found that shrubs produced higher aboveground and root litter inputs compared to grasses. However, shrub shoot litter decomposed much more slowly than grass shoots and roots due to its high lignin and low nitrogen (N) contents. Shrub expansion did not increase the total SOC content in either soil layer. Instead, it fundamentally altered SOC composition: particulate organic carbon (POC) under shrubs was 27.9 % and 28.6 % higher in the 0–20 cm and 20–40 cm layers, respectively, compared to grasses. This increase in POC was not significantly correlated with root litter input in either soil layer; rather, it was primarily driven by the lower decomposition rates of shrub shoot litter. Concurrently, while shrub expansion increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) across both soil depths and stimulated surface phospholipid fatty acids (PLFA), subsoil mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC) significantly decreas…

title: Light curve spectral energy distribution fitting of 13 carbon-rich Mira variable stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud
abstract: Carbon-rich Mira variables are highly dynamic stars characterized by large-amplitude radial pulsations and intense mass-loss. The standard spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting often relies on time-averaged observations, which flatten the intrinsic variability and provide only an approximation of the stellar and circumstellar parameters. We aim to overcome the limitations of static SED modeling by dynamically tracing the physical parameters of a selected sample of 13 carbon-rich Mira variables in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) throughout their entire pulsation cycle. We combined time-series photometry from , WISE, VMC, 2MASS, and OGLE to reconstruct simultaneous multiband light curves. We extract independent SEDs at 14 distinct phases across the pulsation cycle and model them using the ATHENA-C grid. Gaia Our phase-resolved approach allows us to coherently trace the cyclic variations of effective temperature (T_̊m eff), optical depth (τ_0.55), and bolometric luminosity. We found peak-to-peak T_̊m eff variations ranging from ∼ 100 K to over 1000 K. A strong anti-correlation between τ_0.55 and bolometric luminosity is observed, consistent with the dust condensation zone being pushed outward at maximum brightness, thereby making the star's circumstellar environment optically thinner. Additionally, we recovered the classical period-luminosity relation and derived the amplitu…

title: Development trends and driving mechanisms of coordination in the Digitalization–Urban development–low-carbon transition system
abstract: Against the backdrop of sustainable development and China’s Dual Carbon Goals, Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition continuously interact to shape urban sustainable development. However, the long-term coordination of the Digitalization–Urban Development–Low-carbon Transition (DUL) system and its underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently understood. To address this research gap, using panel data for 289 prefecture-level and above cities in China from 2010 to 2024, this study constructs the DUL system and applies the CRITIC-Entropy Weight Method to evaluate the development levels of the three subsystems and the overall DUL system. The Local and Tele-coupling Coordination Degree (LTCCD) is employed to characterize long-term coordination, while the Dagum Gini coefficient and GeoDetector are used to examine regional disparities and driving mechanisms. Based on this analytical framework, the results show that: (1) the development levels of Digitalization, Urban Development, and Low-carbon Transition all improved continuously, but their evolutionary trajectories differed, resulting in asynchronous development of the DUL system; (2) LTCCD exhibited a sustained upward trend, with coordination gradually evolving from imbalance to coordination, although eastern China consistently outperformed the central and western regions; (3) regional disparities in LTCCD gene…

title: The effects of co-application of organic fertilizer and limestone powder on soil organic carbon and its fractions in rubber plantations: associations with microbial necromass carbon and Fe/Al oxides
abstract: Introduction Rubber plantations serve as significant carbon reservoirs within China’s terrestrial ecosystems. To provide a scientific foundation for improving soil fertility management, this study investigated the response of soil organic carbon and its components in rubber plantations to different soil amendments. Methods Soil samples were collected from the 0–20 cm horizon of acidic soils in second-generation rubber plantations in Jinghong City, Yunnan Province. A laboratory incubation experiment was then conducted with four treatments: an unamended control (CK), organic fertilizer alone (T1), limestone powder alone (T2), and a combined organic fertilizer and limestone powder treatment (T3). The effects of these amendments on soil organic carbon and its fractions, iron and aluminum oxides, and microbial necromass carbon were systematically evaluated. Results The results demonstrated that under T3, Organic carbon (SOC) increased significantly by 12.80%, relative to CK ( p < 0.05). Treatments T2 and T3 significantly enhanced microbial necromass carbon (by 6.92–10.90%), fungal necromass carbon (by 6.60–11.32%), and bacterial necromass carbon (by 7.79–9.74%) compared to CK ( p < 0.05). T3 also significantly increased amorphous (Fe o , Al o ) and complexed (Fe p , Al p ) iron and aluminum oxides (p < 0.05). Two-way ANOVA revealed a significant interaction between organic …

title: Rational design of biochar for carbon dioxide capture and catalytic conversion
abstract: The continuous increase in carbon dioxide (CO<sub>2</sub>) emissions has intensified the need for efficient carbon capture and utilization (CCU) technologies. Biochar has emerged as a promising, cost-effective, and sustainable platform for CCU. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the rational design of biochar for CO<sub>2</sub> capture and subsequent catalytic conversion. We first discuss various synthesis methods and activation strategies for tailoring the physicochemical properties of biochar. We then elucidate the mechanisms of CO<sub>2</sub> capture, highlighting the roles of pore modification and heteroatom functionalities in enhancing both physisorption and chemisorption. Furthermore, the roles of biochar in thermocatalytic, electrocatalytic, and photocatalytic CO<sub>2</sub> conversion are critically examined, with particular emphasis on its function as a multifunctional support for metal nanoparticles, molecular catalysts, single atoms, and nanoclusters. Finally, we outline key challenges and future directions for the rational development of next-generation biochar toward practical carbon-neutral technologies. Accordingly, this review establishes a rational design framework based on application demand, key performance parameters, and targeted synthesis strategies, thereby linking practical CCU requirements with the controlled engineering of biochar porosit…

title: Land carbon sinks in the European Union are not keeping pace with carbon neutrality expectations
abstract: Abstract The European Union has substantially reduced greenhouse-gas emissions since 1990, yet the land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF) sink has not strengthened in parallel. The EU-27 LULUCF balance was approximately −231 MtCO₂e in 2024, while the latest Member State projections indicate a remaining gap of 40–55 MtCO₂e to the binding −310 MtCO₂e target for 2030. Here, we synthesise recent assessments to examine the drivers of this weakening in the land carbon sink and their implications for the effectiveness of climate mitigation policy. Declining forest growth, increased harvesting, climate-driven disturbances, and rising biomass demand reduce net carbon uptake, with one 2040 GLOBIOM sensitivity analysis indicating an approximately 100 MtCO₂e reduction in the LULUCF sink under an additional 20 Mtoe of woody-biomass demand. Concurrently, the EU inventory reported 52.7% uncertainty in the 2022 LULUCF level and 29.4% uncertainty in its trend, while important soil-carbon dynamics remain incompletely represented. These findings indicate that current climate policy frameworks implicitly assume stable, scalable, and rapidly deliverable land-based removals, whereas land carbon sinks are dynamic, disturbance-sensitive, and constrained by biophysical limits. Addressing this mismatch requires land-removal plans to be evaluated through dependable removal capacity, combining ex…

title: Phonon transport in layered NaMnO2: Roles of interlayer electrostatic coupling and Jahn–Teller distortions
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries offer a sustainable alternative to lithium-based systems, but their safety and performance can be affected by inadequate thermal management during high-rate operation. Here, we present a first-principles investigation of lattice thermal transport in representative layered NaxMnO2 structural models, including the fully desodiated δ-MnO2 limit (x=0), an intermediate-composition O3′-Na0.5MnO2 model (x=0.5), and fully sodiated O3′-NaMnO2 and P2′-NaMnO2 polymorphs (x=1). Using the Boltzmann transport equation combined with the Wigner transport formalism, we reveal pronounced variations in both the magnitude and anisotropy of lattice thermal conductivity among these structural models. Relative to desodiated δ-MnO2, Na+ insertion redistributes charge and strengthens electrostatic interactions between the inserted Na+ layer and adjacent oxygen layers, thereby enhancing out-of-plane phonon transport. Meanwhile, the Mn3+-associated Jahn–Teller distortion softens selected in-plane Mn–O linkages and suppresses the corresponding in-plane thermal transport. These structural changes modify phonon dispersions, group velocities, and mean free paths, resulting in a substantial reduction in thermal conductivity anisotropy in the sodiated models. Our results clarify how Na content, interlayer interactions, and Jahn–Teller distortions jointly regulate anisotropic phonon transpo…

title: Geometry-driven plexcitonic coupling in plasmonic nanoparticles: full 3D Maxwell–Bloch study
Coupling dynamics of topological states in an acoustic glide-dislocation lattice
abstract: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupling dynamics between two topological states in an acoustic glide-dislocation lattice. By mapping the lattice structure to a two-waveguide model based on coupled-mode theory, we establish a quantitative link between macroscopic coupling behaviors and microscopic geometric parameters. Then, we demonstrate topological Bloch oscillation and topological supermode propagation under single-state excitation and eigenstate-matched excitation, respectively. The topological Bloch oscillation exhibits strong robustness against structural perturbations, whereas the topological supermode propagation undergoes moderate amplitude and phase fluctuations under the same perturbations. This work lays a solid foundation for exploiting coupled topological states in acoustic wave manipulation and may inspire future applications in integrated acoustic devices.

title: Coupling the Spin State Switching and CO2 Adsorption Operating at Different Temperatures in a Breathing Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Gas-responsive magnetic response arising from spin-crossover (SCO) phenomena is rare yet highly attractive for molecular sensing and spintronics. However, it remains unclear how gas uptake influences SCO behaviour when the two phenomena occur in separate temperature regimes. Herein, we report a strong influence of CO2 adsorption on the SCO behaviour of a Hofmann clathrate, [FeII(epac)2(PtII(CN)4)]·nEtOH (1·nEtOH, n ≤ 2), despite the two effects occurring at different temperatures. Complex (1·2EtOH) exhibits highly cooperative SCO with a hysteresis width ∼65 K and preserves the framework topology upon desolvation (1). However, hysteresis reduces to 30 K in the guest-free phase (1), underscoring the critical role of lattice solvent in mediating cooperativity. Complex (1) selectively adsorbs CO2 through a gate-opening mechanism at temperatures substantially higher than the SCO region. Despite this mismatch in operating temperatures, increasing CO2 loading progressively stabilizes the low-spin state and shifts the transition temperature (Teq) by ∼20 K. These findings support a delayed guest-mediated coupling mechanism where CO2 first enters the framework at elevated temperatures and subsequently modifies spin-state energetics only after immobilization within the host lattice at lower temperatures. This study establishes that gas adsorption and SCO need not occur within ove…

SUBSTANTIATION OF PARAMETERS OF A MOBILE CHARGING STATION FOR ELECTRIFIED MACHINERY UNDER AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION CONDITIONS
abstract: The article considers the substantiation and selection of the main parameters of a mobile charging station intended to support the operation of electrified machinery under agricultural production conditions. The relevance of the study is determined by the gradual expansion of electric and hybrid machinery in modern agriculture, including compact electric tractors, robotic platforms, unmanned aerial vehicles, battery-powered tools and various types of auxiliary electrical equipment. For agricultural enterprises, an important issue is not only the availability of reliable charging infrastructure, but also the possibility of transporting it directly to fields, farms and other locations where technological operations are performed. A calculation scheme of a mobile charging station is proposed, which includes a battery energy storage unit, photovoltaic modules, an inverter-charger, a charge controller and the possibility of backup connection to the electrical grid or a diesel generator. Such a combined configuration increases the autonomy and flexibility of the charging system and makes it possible to use renewable energy directly at the place of operation. Based on the accepted daily energy demand of electrified agricultural machinery, the required capacity of the battery unit, the installed power of the photovoltaic system, the power of the charging equipment and the expected redu…

title: 3D-printed circular TPMS lattices: advancing energy absorption through novel geometric design
Sub-minute fatigue monitoring for enhanced lifetime assessment of wind turbines
abstract: Accurate fatigue-damage estimation is a critical step for managing and extending the life of wind turbine fleets and the basis on which operators decide whether an ageing asset can be kept in service beyond the end of design life. The most accurate estimation relies on continuous high-frequency strain measurements processed with rainflow cycle counting. However, only a small subset of turbines within a fleet are typically instrumented with strain sensors, and even for these, the data volumes, computational complexity, and cost of continuously processing high-frequency strain data via rainflow counting over long-term operation make this approach impractical to sustain at scale. For this reason, industry practice has long relied on stress data aggregated over 10 min windows already used by supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, which are available across the full fleet. This choice is convenient but, when combined with conventional window-based rainflow counting, tends to underestimate fatigue damage generated by cycles whose period exceeds the window length, driven by factors such as slow variations in wind speed and direction, operational transitions, control actions, and seasonal or daily temperature variation, as well as, for offshore turbines, changes in wave parameters. Residual-preserving approaches, most notably low-frequency fatigue dynamics (LFFD), ad…

title: JUSTIFICATION OF THE OPTIMAL SPEED REGIME FOR A TRACTOR-IMPLEMENT UNIT BASED ON TRACTION-ENERGY AND TECHNOLOGICAL PERFORMANCE INDICATORS
abstract: The article provides a theoretical substantiation of the rational operating speed of a machine-tractor unit based on a comprehensive consideration of traction, energy, and technological performance indicators. The influence of operating speed on draft resistance, required drawbar power, field capacity, wheel slip, traction efficiency, hourly and specific fuel consumption, and specific energy consumption is determined. A generalized mathematical model of the draft resistance of an agricultural machine is proposed, in which the total resistance is divided into static and dynamic components while accounting for operating speed, working width, and tillage depth. The dynamic component of draft resistance is represented by a power-law dependence on operating speed, which makes it possible to describe the nonlinear increase in energy demand as the travel speed of the unit increases. Analytical relationships are obtained for determining drawbar power, theoretical and actual field capacity, wheel slip coefficient, traction efficiency, fuel consumption, and specific energy consumption. Numerical simulation demonstrates that an increase in operating speed improves field capacity only up to a certain limit, beyond which the increasing dynamic component of draft resistance, wheel slip, and power demand leads to deterioration in energy performance. The existence of a rational speed range is …

title: GRAPHO-ANALYTICAL ANALYSIS OF THE CHARACTERISTICS OF OBLIQUE CUTTING OF STOCHASTIC SOIL STRUCTURE BY THE FLEXIBLE WIRE OF A SOIL-DEEPENING TOOL
abstract: The design features of most modern tillage implements determine a characteristic aspect of their operating processes associated with the oblique-angle cutting regime applied to the heterogeneous and stochastic structure of the soil. Therefore, a detailed study of soil deformation and failure under oblique cutting conditions is important for substantiating and optimizing the structural and operational parameters of innovative tillage machinery at the stages of development, design and further practical application. The paper presents the results of a graphical-analytical investigation of the oblique cutting characteristics of a “flexible wire” subsoiler intended for loosening over-compacted sub-arable soil layers and eliminating the negative effects of a plow pan. Based on the obtained research results, the structural layout of the proposed subsoiler was substantiated. Its design incorporates a double-acting mechanical damper installed within the “flexible string” circuit. The application of this element makes it possible to significantly reduce the draft resistance of the subsoiler by promoting soil failure mainly through a system of longitudinal and transverse shear cracks propagating toward the open surface of the soil half-space. This operating principle reduces unnecessary compaction and improves the energy efficiency of deep soil loosening. The installation of the mechanica…

title: RESEARCH INTO DEWATERING PROCESSES OF WET DISPERSED MATERIALS UNDER VIBRATORY AND VIBROIMPACT LOADING
abstract: The paper presents a comprehensive theoretical and comparative analysis of the mechanical dewatering processes of wet dispersed materials, including food-production wastes such as distillery stillage, brewery spent grain, sugar beet pulp and coffee slurry, under static, vibratory and vibroimpact loading conditions. Particular attention is paid to the physical and mechanical mechanisms governing moisture removal and to the possibilities of increasing the energy efficiency of dewatering equipment. The forms of moisture binding in colloidal capillary-porous bodies are systematised according to their binding energy, with a clear distinction between mechanically removable moisture and more strongly bound adsorption and chemically bound fractions. The rheological behaviour of wet dispersed materials is described using phenomenological models based on combinations of Hooke, Newton and Saint-Venant elements, including elastoviscoplastic and inertial components. The theoretical principles of static pressing are analysed considering capillary, neutral and effective pressure components, as well as moisture filtration according to Darcy’s law. The conditions governing transitions to pseudofluidisation and vibroboiling are examined, taking into account particle size, initial moisture content, excitation acceleration, vibration parameters and static punch pressure. Governing equations descri…

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A TECHNICAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL SOLUTION FOR THE SUPPLY AND MIXING OF A FOUR-COMPONENT TWO-PHASE MIXTURE IN AN ENGINE COMBUSTION CHAMBER
abstract: The article considers the issue of developing a technical and technological solution to ensure stable supply, dosing and effective mixing of a four-component two-phase mixture directly in the engine combustion chamber. The relevance of the study is due to the need to increase the completeness of fuel combustion, improve the energy and environmental performance of the engine, as well as ensure controlled formation of the fuel-air mixture under variable operating conditions. The functional structure of the component supply system is substantiated, the requirements for dosing, mixing and spraying elements are determined, as well as for coordinating the flow rates, pressure, temperature and phase state of the components. A basic scheme for forming a two-phase flow is proposed, which involves the phased introduction of the mixture components, preliminary dispersion of the liquid phase and subsequent intensification of mixing in the injection zone. Particular attention is paid to ensuring the homogeneity of the mixture, flame stability, reducing the size of the drops and increasing the rate of mass and heat transfer. The methodological basis of the work is the analysis of the mixture formation processes, structural and functional modeling of the system and evaluation of the main operating parameters. The influence of the design parameters of the mixing unit, the geometry of the chann…

title: Controlled sol-gel nanoassembly of Au25(SR)18 nanoclusters for structural and functional integration
abstract: Structural assembly of nanomaterials imparts new and enhanced properties to individual components. The “Sol-gel” approach has been a traditional technique to connect diverse types of materials. Here, 3-mercaptopropyl (trimethoxysilane) (MPTS), a dual-functional ligand, has been employed to assemble one of the popular members of atomically precise nanoclusters–Au 25 − and connect individual nanoclusters via the formation of the Si(OR) 4 “sol-gel” network during the purification process. Depending on the purification procedure, a particle or film of Au 25 -SiO 2 was achieved and characterized using different techniques. The obtained superstructures of nanomaterials were utilized as a catalyst for the nitrophenol hydrogenation reaction, revealing a 2.5 times faster reaction rate of Au 25 -SiO 2 -film relative to the particle.

title: CALCULATED ASSESSMENT OF THE EFFECT OF INJECTOR HOLE CLOGGING ON FUEL DELIVERY
abstract: This article examines changes in fuel delivery caused by partial blockage of the nozzle holes of the 171.1112010-50 injector equipped with the 6А1-20с2-50 nozzle for MTZ tractors. The study aims to assess the effect of a reduction in the unobstructed cross-sectional area of nozzle holes on fuel flow rate and to compare uniform and non-uniform clogging. The orifice flow equation and a geometric model of a uniform annular deposit layer are applied. The geometric parameters of the nozzle are taken from the manufacturer's data, while the pressure difference, fuel density, discharge coefficient and deposit thickness are specified as calculation inputs. This approach allows the effect of geometric blockage to be assessed at constant fuel properties, including those of a blend containing biofuel. For a nozzle with five holes having an initial diameter of 0.32 mm, a uniform deposit layer 2–10 μm thick was found to reduce the unobstructed cross-sectional area of each hole by 2.48–12.11%. At a constant pressure difference, fuel density and discharge coefficient, the volumetric fuel flow rate decreases by the same percentages. At a pressure difference of 40 MPa, a density of 850 kg/m³ and a discharge coefficient of 0.75, the formation of a 10 μm deposit layer reduces the calculated mass of fuel flowing through all holes over 1 ms from 78.65 to 69.12 mg. Three clogging scenarios with a tot…

title: Interpenetrating Elastomers for High-Fidelity Shape Recovery and Broad Temperature Energy Dissipation
abstract: Abstract The design of elastomers integrating high-fidelity shape memory behavior with broad-temperature energy dissipation remains a fundamental challenge due to the intrinsic trade-off between network rigidity and segmental mobility. Here, an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) strategy is developed to fabricate polyurethane (PU)/brominated butyl rubber (BIIR) IPNs via a two-step process. The resulting IPN elastomers exhibit a sea–island morphology, with PU as dispersed rigid domains and BIIR as the continuous phase. Physical entanglements and internetwork confinement within the interpenetrated architecture contribute to effective shape memory behavior, resulting in shape fixity and recovery ratios of 94.0% and 90.2%, respectively, at 20 phr BIIR content. The large mismatch in glass transition temperatures and confined interfacial friction induces hierarchical segmental relaxation, leading to a broad damping temperature window (tanδ ≥ 0.3) of 154.8 °C. The IPNs further demonstrate repeatable energy dissipation over the tested cycles, a characteristic impact-force decay time of less than 0.1 s in the falling-ball test, and a 91% energy-loss fraction derived from the pendulum rebound test. The IPNs also exhibit effective acoustic insulation, reducing the transmitted acoustic amplitude to 20.6 mV. This work provides a general strategy for overcoming the trade-off between shap…

title: Nanocrystalline SrTi1-x Fex O3-δ perovskites as high-performance electrodes for intermediate-temperature symmetric SOFCs
abstract: Nanocrystalline SrTi 1 − x Fe x O 3 − δ perovskites (x = 0.20–0.50) represent a compositionally tunable platform for cobalt-free symmetric electrodes in intermediate-temperature solid oxide fuel cells. Synthesized via a gel-combustion route, all as-prepared compositions form single-phase cubic perovskites with nanometric domains, while the Fe/Ti ratio governs lattice contraction, mixed Fe + 3 / F e + 4 surface chemistry, and redox responsiveness. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals that Fe-rich materials (x = 0.35 and x = 0.50) exhibit markedly lower polarization resistances than the x = 0.20 composition under both oxidizing and reducing atmospheres. Distribution of relaxation times analysis reveals that Fe incorporation markedly attenuates the polarization contributions across the intermediate- and high-frequency ranges, confirming accelerated charge-transfer and surface-reaction kinetics under both oxidizing and reducing conditions. Under reducing conditions, STF50 undergoes adaptive structural evolution, including Fe exsolution and the emergence of Ruddlesden–Popper-type domains, highlighting a dynamic interplay between high electrochemical activity and redox-induced restructuring. Preliminary button-cell tests confirm the functional viability of STF50 as a symmetric electrode within the intermediate-temperature range. Overall, nanocrystalline SrTi 1 − x Fe x O 3 …

title: From Urban–Rural Antagonism to Urban–Rural Integration: A Contemporary Interpretation of Marx’s Theory of Urban–Rural Relations
abstract: Urban–rural connectivity can deepen while the relations of subordination embedded in it persist. This article explains that divergence through a contemporary reconstruction of Marx’s account of town–country antagonism. Reading selected primary texts alongside scholarship on spatial justice, capabilities, and digital inequality, it distinguishes productive integration, understood as stronger economic coordination, from substantive integration, assessed through usable access, reciprocal benefit, and collective agency. Its contribution is a synthesis that connects group-specific outcomes to the institutional organization of interdependence. Property arrangements allocate assets and surplus; entitlement rules govern eligibility; fiscal systems distribute the costs of social reproduction; organizational rules shape bargaining alternatives. A bounded territorial comparison shows how service eligibility and financing can alter access under equivalent productive connections. A separate organizational proposition explains how restrictions on switching reduce credible alternatives and weaken participants’ ability to negotiate returns. These mechanisms specify why aggregate gains can coexist with exclusion and identify conditions that can interrupt it. The resulting framework treats integration as a political transformation of cooperation: its substantive direction depends on who can use …

title: A multi-dimensional performance framework for industry 5.0 manufacturing: integration of lean six sigma with human-centric, sustainability and resilience metrics
abstract: Purpose This study examines how Lean Six Sigma (LSS) can support the implementation of Industry 5.0 and its three pillars to improve progress toward Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It seeks to clarify the overlaps between LSS and Industry 5.0, develop an integrated conceptual model connecting both frameworks to SDGs 8, 9, 12 and 13, and demonstrate its practical use through a Define-Measure-Analyze-Improve-Control (DMAIC)-based case study in manufacturing. Design/methodology/approach A structured conceptual literature review was conducted to synthesize and critically analyze existing studies on LSS, Industry 5.0, and SDGs. The review was used to identify conceptual synergies and research gaps that informed the development of the proposed human-centric, sustainable, and resilient enhancement (H-SURE) framework. The proposed framework was subsequently illustrated through a DMAIC-based single-company case study to demonstrate its practical implementation within an Industry 5.0 manufacturing environment. Findings The analysis shows that LSS and Industry 5.0 strongly align in strategic orientation, waste reduction, human engagement and continuous improvement, while differing in regulatory readiness and technological integration. The conceptual H-SURE framework indicates that LSS offers a structured pathway to operationalize Industry 5.0 and advance SDGs 8, 9, 12 and 13. The ca…

title: Accelerating Ghana’s sustainable transport transition: the role of electric vehicles in achieving SDG 7 and SDG 13
abstract: Introduction Urban transport in Ghana relies heavily on imported fuel and contributes significantly to emissions. Electric vehicles have been proposed as an alternative, but we still know little about what shapes drivers’ willingness to adopt them in major city corridors. Methods We used Social Cognitive Theory to assess how two factors - tax incentives and environmental awareness - relate to three self-reported outcomes: intention to adopt EVs, sustainable energy consumption, and beliefs about greenhouse gas emissions. We did not measure actual emissions. The survey covered 800 commercial drivers and private car owners recruited from transport union hubs in Accra, Tema, Kumasi, and Takoradi, and we analyzed the data with PLS-SEM, including tests for moderation. Results Drivers who reported higher tax incentives and greater environmental awareness also reported stronger EV adoption intentions and more sustainable energy use, and lower perceived emissions. Environmental awareness moderated these links: it amplified the link between tax incentives and adoption intentions but dampened the links between tax incentives and both energy consumption and perceived emissions. Discussion Among unionized operators in these four urban corridors, tax incentives and environmental awareness are linked to intentions and perceptions, not to verified behavior or emission cuts. title: IMPROVEMENT OF THE DESIGN OF A HIGH-SPEED SHEEP SHEARING MACHINE
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive substantiation of the rational design parameters of the pressure mechanism, lever system, and eccentric drive of a high-speed sheep shearing machine. The analysis was performed considering the kinematic, dynamic, and operational characteristics of shearing devices operating under increased oscillatory and impact loads. Particular attention was paid to optimizing the geometric parameters and relative arrangement of the mechanism components to improve reliability, reduce vibration, and ensure the stability of the sheep shearing process. The kinematic analysis of the working elements made it possible to establish the relationships between the parameters of the eccentric mechanism, the oscillation amplitude of the cutter block, and the magnitude of the contact forces in the cutting zone. Rational relationships between the geometric and force parameters were determined to reduce energy losses, minimize component wear, and improve wool cutting efficiency. It was established that deviations of the oscillation centers of the pressure rod and the lever from their optimal positions lead to additional dynamic loads, misalignment of the cutter assembly, and non-uniform distribution of contact pressure. These factors adversely affect shearing quality and reduce the service life of the machine components. To eliminate these drawbacks, it is proposed to imp…

title: Design and performance analysis of a six-state QKD over FSO and optical fiber utilizing switch-controlled polarization generation for secure optical communications
abstract: Abstract Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a process that utilizes the principles of quantum mechanics to securely share a secret key between two parties, ensuring unconditional security. Diverse QKD protocols are established to guarantee the security and integrity of information against any attempts by an eavesdropper monitoring the transferred photons. One of these protocols is the six-state protocol. This work employs OptiSystem 21.1 simulation software to design and emulate the six-state protocol, wherein polarization states are produced through random switching control rather than optical modulators. The protocol’s performance, indicated by quantum bit error rate and secure key rate, is analytically examined for both free space optical (FSO) channel and optical fiber channel, incorporating parameters from two types of commercial single-photon detectors to enhance realism. The maximum secure key rate attains 5.439 Mbps at 10 km of optical fiber, in contrast to 1.674 Mbps at 0.2 km under clear weather conditions in the FSO quantum channel utilizing ID 281 single-photon detector modules across both channels. The maximum distance that guarantees secure key rate with ID 281 for FSO channel is 2 km with 1760 bps with heavy haze compared to 100 km optical fiber with secure key rate of 15,000 bps.

title: Mikro Mekânların Yapay Zekâ ile Yeniden Tasarımı: Farklı Yapay Zekâ Araçları Üzerinden Karşılaştırmalı Bir Değerlendirme
abstract: Bu çalışma, kentsel yaşamda artan alan kısıtlılığı bağlamında mikro mekân tasarımında yapay zekâ (YZ) araçlarının sunduğu olanakları ve tasarım performansını incelemektedir. Araştırmada ölçek, ergonomi, esneklik, erişilebilirlik ve mekânsal verimlilik ilkeleri doğrultusunda YZ’nin mimari tasarım sürecindeki üretim ve optimizasyon potansiyeli ele alınmıştır.Uygulama aşamasında, önceden tanımlanan bir mikro mekân senaryosu farklı YZ araçları kullanılarak yeniden tasarlanmış ve elde edilen planlar ayrıntılı ve sistematik biçimde karşılaştırmalı olarak analiz edilmiştir. Değerlendirmede mekân organizasyonu, alan kullanımı, ergonomi, mahremiyet, estetik bütünlük ve uygulanabilirlik ölçütleri dikkate alınmıştır. Üretilen tasarımların teknik ve uygulamaya yönelik doğruluğu, yapısal uygulanabilirliği ve ilgili mimari standartlara uygunluğunun değerlendirilmesi amacıyla araştırma yöntemi, genel kullanıcı deneyimi analizinden deneyimli uzman mimar ve iç mimarlardan oluşan odak grup görüşmesi modeline dönüştürülmüştür. Bu yöntemsel revizyon, tasarımların mesleki ve teknik bilgi ve deneyim çerçevesinde değerlendirilmesine ve teknik açıdan daha nitelikli ve kapsamlı veriler elde edilmesine olanak sağlamıştır.Bulgular, YZ’nin özellikle ergonomik optimizasyon ve fonksiyonel verimlilik açısından mikro mekân tasarımına önemli ve işlevsel katkılar sunduğunu göstermektedir. Latent variable or achievement-tailored composite?: The home resources for learning (HRL) index in TIMSS and PIRLS
abstract: Abstract Background variables in international large-scale assessments are often combined into indices for statistical analyses. Using the Home Resources for Learning (HRL) index as an example, we draw from the Cowan et al. (2012) report on socio-economic status (SES) to consider parallel ways of defining HRL composites, and show how the choice among alternatives has the potential to affect estimation of cross-country HRL–achievement relationships. Prior studies have emphasized HRL indicator variables as reflective indicators of a latent HRL construct, and address cross-country measurement differences through latent variable partial-invariance models [e.g., Wendt et al. (2017); Jusufi et al. (2026)]. However, the latent variable logic commonly applied to constructs like HRL and the accompanying perspectives of measurement invariance that ensure can be questioned (Welzel and Inglehart, 2016). In this paper, rather than adopting a strong stand regarding which approach is best, we explore empirically the implications of adopting latent variable weights as opposed to achievement-tailored weights as a basis for improving cross-country comparability in HRL. Our empirical analyses using structural equation modeling demonstrate disproportionality between latent variable HRL indicator loadings and the corresponding predictive effects of the HRL indicator variables on achievement, sugges…

title: Kurum, Bağlam ve Tasarımcı Arakesitinde Türk Ticaret Bankası (TTB) İzmir Şubesi Örneği
abstract: Bu çalışma,1951 yılında mimari tasarım yarışması ile projesi elde edilen ve halen ayakta olan Türk Ticaret Bankası İzmir Şubesi Binası’na odaklanmaktadır. 2023 yılında yeniden aktif çalışmaya başlaması gündeme gelen Türk Ticaret Bankası (TTB), son 20 yılı pasif olsa da 110 yıllık bir özel teşebbüstür. Türkiye’nin ilk özel bankası unvanına sahiptir. Kurumun özellikle 1950-1960 yılları arası mimari üretimi ve Türkiye mimarlık ortamı ile ilişkisi tartışmaya değerdir. Bu bağlamda, İzmir şube binasının özgün değeri, ilişkili ama ayrı üç düzlemde tartışılmaktadır. Tartışma düzlemlerinden ilki, yapının parçası olduğu kuruma ve kurumun 1950-1960 yılları arası mimari üretimine odaklanmaktadır. İkinci tartışma düzleminde, yarışma süreci ve katılımcı projeler ele alınmakta, özellikle binanın yer ile kurduğu ilişki üzerinde durulmaktadır. İzmir'de 17. yüzyıldan bu yana ticari yapı yoğunluğu olan bölgede konumlanan proje alanı ve mevcut yapılı çevre ile ilişkisi tartışılmaktadır. Proje müelliflerinden biri olan Enver Tokay ve ortaya konan tasarım yaklaşımı ise, çalışmanın üçüncü tartışma düzelemini oluşturmaktadır. Çalışmanın sonuç bölümünde, üç düzlemde yürütülen tartışma ilişkilendirilerek çıkarımlar ortaya konmaktadır.

title: Design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of pyrimidine linked fused thiazole–isoxazole conjugates as dual cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Abstract Alzheimer’s disease (AD) affects over 55 million individuals worldwide, yet approved pharmacotherapies remain limited to symptomatic relief. Dual inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE) offers a validated approach to restoring cholinergic tone. However, structurally differentiated inhibitors with favorable selectivity profiles are critically needed. Here, we report a series of pyrimidine clubbed thiazolo[4,5-c]isoxazole framework that functions as potent dual cholinesterase inhibitors with low-micromolar activity against both AChE and BuChE. Lead compound- 1 demonstrated IC 50 values of 6.19 ± 0.60 μM (AChE) and 8.64 ± 0.91 μM (BuChE) showing promising performance over the reference donepezil (AChE IC 50 = 19.38 ± 0.98 μM, BuChE IC 50 = 27.54 ± 1.34 μM). Furthermore, structure–activity relationship analysis identified electron-withdrawing ( p -CF 3 , p -F, o,p -Cl, p -NO 2 ) and electron-donating (–OH) aryl substituents as principal modulators of inhibitory potency. Moreover, molecular docking against human AChE and BuChE crystal structures revealed dual engagement of the catalytic anionic site and peripheral anionic site through hydrogen-bonding and π–π stacking interactions. In silico ADMET profiling confirmed electronic reactivity and drug-likeness of lead compounds. These findings establish pyrimidine-clubbed thiazolo[4,5-c]isoxa…

title: Nesne Yönelimli Ontoloji Perspektifinden Chichu Sanat Müzesi’nin Ontolojik Analizi
abstract: Bu çalışma, Nesne Yönelimli Ontoloji (NYO) kuramı temelinde, mimari nesneyi insan merkezli temsil ve deneyim odaklı yaklaşımların ötesinde konumlandıran ontolojik bir analiz yöntemi geliştirmeyi amaçlamaktadır.Tadao Ando’nun Chichu Sanat Müzesi (CSO) NYO kuramından hareketle geliştirilen beş kavramsal analiz parametresi (Ontolojik Otonomi, Maddenin Ontolojisi, Negatif Boşluklar, Eş-Düzlemli Gerilimler, Zaman-Dışı Derinlik) ışığında kavramsal olarak incelenmiştir. Analizler, mimari nesnelerin yalnızca biçimsel ya da işlevsel değil, kendi başlarına özerk bir varlık olarak anlam üretebildiğini ortaya koymaktadır. Işık, boşluk, malzeme ve yüzeymimari ögeler olarak, insan dışı aktörler olarak yapıların ontolojik derinliğini belirler. Bu bağlamda çalışma, mimarlık eleştirisine nesnelerin içkin potansiyelleri üzerinden yeni bir bakış sunmakta ve mimari nesneleri temsilin ötesinde, kendi varlık kiplerinde değerlendirmeyi önermektedir. Elde edilen bulgular, NYO’nun mimari düşünceyi dönüştürme potansiyelini ortaya koyarken, gelecekte farklı bağlamlara uygulanabilecek çoğul bir analiz zemini oluşturur.

title: Arkeolojik Alanda Ahşap Strüktür Seçimini Yönlendiren Tasarım Ölçütlerinin Etkinlik Düzeyinin DEMATEL Analiz ile Belirlenmesi
abstract: Arkeolojik alanlarda inşa edilen koruma yapıları, kalıntıların çevresel koşullardan zarar görmesini önlemenin yanı sıra, ziyaretçi deneyimini yönlendirme ve alanın temsil gücünü artırma gibi çoklu hedefler doğrultusunda tasarlanmaktadır. Bu bağlamda, ahşap malzemenin hafifliği, montaj kolaylığı ve modüler yapısı sebebiyle koruyucu yapılarda kullanımı tercih edilmektedir. Çalışma kapsamında, ahşap strüktürlü koruma yapılarında, malzemenin tasarım sürecinde yönlendirici bir tasarım girdisi olarak üstlendiği stratejik rolü görünür kılmak, mimari ve yapısal kararların birbirini nasıl etkilediğini çok katmanlı bir analizle irdelemek amaçlanmaktadır. Bu doğrultuda, Türkiye’de ve uluslararası bağlamda seçilen on farklı arkeolojik alan örneği, taşıyıcı sistem, zeminle temas, form, geçirgenlik, cephe, yönlendirme ve benzeri on temel tasarım etkeni açısından değerlendirilmiştir. Karar hiyerarşisi ve ölçütler arası etkileşim, çok girdili karar verme yöntemlerinden biri olan DEMATEL analiz tekniği ile incelenmiştir. Bu yöntem, bu tür karmaşık ilişki düzenlerinde kriterler arasındaki nedensel yapıyı görselleştirmeye ve karar hiyerarşisini ortaya koymaya olanak tanıması bakımından çalışmanın amacıyla örtüşmektedir. Elde edilen çıkarımlar doğrultusunda karar üretim sürecindeki yönlendirici ve bağımlı değişkenler belirlenmiştir. Bulgular, bazı ölçütlerin yüksek nedensellik değerleriyle öne çık…

title: Beyoğlu kiliselerinin gizli dili: Üç farklı mezhepteki renk ve ışıkla şekillenen mekânsal algı ve kimlik
abstract: Bu çalışma, farklı Hristiyan mezheplerine ait ibadet mekânlarında renk ve ışık kullanımının mekân algısı ve dini kimlik üzerindeki etkilerini incelemektedir. Araştırma kapsamında İstanbul’un Beyoğlu ilçesinde yer alan Ayia Triada Rum Ortodoks Kilisesi, Saint Anthony Katolik Kilisesi ve Alman Protestan Kilisesi (Kreuzkirche) örnek olarak seçilmiştir. Araştırma sorusu, bu üç farklı mezhebe ait yapılarda renk ve ışık kullanım biçimlerinin mekân algısı ve kimliğini hangi yönlerden farklılaştırdığıdır. Hipotez, her mezhebin teolojik ve kültürel yaklaşımına göre bu unsurları özgün biçimde yorumladığı ve bunun kilise kimliğini doğrudan etkilediğidir. Yöntem olarak literatür taraması, belge incelemesi, fotoğraf ve gözleme dayalı görsel analiz kullanılmıştır. Çalışmanın özgünlüğü, aynı kentsel bağlam içinde yer alan farklı mezheplere ait ibadet mekânlarının karşılaştırmalı olarak analiz edilmesiyle, mezhep farklılıklarının mimari estetik üzerindeki etkilerini ortaya koymasıdır. Bulgular, renk ve ışığın yalnızca estetik değil mekânsal algının ve mekân kimliğinin oluşumunda belirleyici bir rol oynadığını ortaya koymaktadır. Çalışma, tasarımcı ve araştırmacılara mekân kimliği odaklı yaklaşımlar geliştirme konusunda katkı sunmaktadır.

title: Tailoring soy protein isolate–alginate double emulsion composite gel microcapsules for cheese-like texture and probiotic protection in plant-based cheese analogues
abstract: While the market for plant-based dairy alternatives is expanding rapidly, most products mainly focus on the sensory attributes of traditional dairy items and lack functional fortification, such as the incorporation of probiotic bacteria. The objective of this study was to develop and characterize novel water-in-oil-in-water (W/O/W) double emulsion-based gelled microcapsules for Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LRGG) using a soy protein isolate (SPI) (3.0%–6.0% w/w) and sodium alginate (SA) (0.5%–2.0% w/w) composite with Ca 2+ cross-linking, aiming to tailor and customize the microcapsules for cheese-like textural characteristics from spread to semi-hard types, while preserving probiotic viability for incorporation into plant-based cheese analogues. Using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) under a 3 2 full factorial design with center-point replication, the complex interactions between the wall materials and their effects on physical, textural, and functional properties were systematically evaluated. The results revealed that SA concentration strongly enhanced bulk firmness and particle size ( D 50 ) through robust calcium cross-linking. In contrast, SPI played a crucial role in providing protection against simulated gastrointestinal fluids during digestion testing. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that the SPI-SA system bridges the gap between macroscopic structural integrity and…

Integrated structural, computational, and genetic analyses link KASII-AL263F to increased palmitic acid composition and highlight its potential in soybean oil breeding
abstract: Soybean seed oil quality is governed by the relative proportions of five major fatty acids. Most genetic studies of soybean fatty acid mutants have evaluated allelic effects primarily on fatty acid composition, rather than quantifying their corresponding contents. Because fatty acid composition is expressed as relative percentage of total fatty acids, an increase in the proportion of one fatty acid is necessarily accompanied by a relative decrease in others, making it difficult to distinguish compositional shifts from changes in the actual amount accumulated per unit seed mass. In this study, we characterized PE1604, an EMS-induced mutant derived from the Korean soybean cultivar Pungsannamul and evaluated fatty acid phenotypes using both composition and contents. Sequence analysis identified a C to T transition in KASII - A (Glyma.17G047000) that resulted in an L263F amino acid substitution at a leucine residue conserved among KASII-A homologs from 11 species of the family Fabaceae. AlphaFold2 models superposed on the Escherichia coli ( E . coli ) FabF complex with crypto - 1b-AcpP (C16-AcpP) placed Leu263 within the buried hydrophobic core of KASII-A, distant from the catalytic residues Cys240, H380, and H416 in the active site. title: Correction to: KH2PO4 and salicylic acid synergistically promote the germination of rapeseed, Brassica napus, under aluminum stress
Multi-source temporal fusion and multi-station learning for early warning of diamondback moth infestation in Brassica crops
abstract: Introduction Meteorological variability influences diamondback moth (DBM; Plutella xylostella ) infestation and the resulting damage to Brassica crops. Accurate multi-horizon forecasting requires models that preserve short-lived meteorological exposures while integrating thermal timing, spatial dependence, and recent infestation dynamics within a transparent framework. Methods The Temporal–Geospatial Pest Network (TG-PestNet) forecasts the weekly percentage of inspected plants classified as DBM-infested 1 to 4 weeks ahead at four Guangdong stations, from origin-time information only. It preserves hourly exposure, encodes lookback weeks on a thermal-time axis, couples stations through a wind-informed graph, and protects infestation history in a gated anchor. Evaluation used 344 synchronized weeks, 66 later test origins, 13 history-only comparators, retraining ablations, matched-width controls, and input-matched generic encoders. Results and discussion TG-PestNet achieved the lowest observed root-mean-square error, mean absolute error, and mean absolute percentage error in all 12 station–metric combinations, with mean reductions of 5.9%–13.0%. Year-ahead forecasts outperformed persistence in all four test years. Removing the history anchor increased error by 14.3% and remained significant after multiplicity correction, demonstrating its central contribution to forecast accuracy. …

title: Patient perspectives on virtual consultations for type 2 diabetes in the United Kingdom: use, associated factors, and perceived quality of care
abstract: Introduction Although virtual consultations (VCs) have become a routine component of type 2 diabetes (T2D) care, evidence regarding patient experiences remains limited. We investigated VC use among UK adults with T2D, factors associated with both current and intended use, and perceived quality of care. Methods A weighted national cross-sectional survey of 373 UK adults with self-reported T2D was conducted via the YouGov panel. The questionnaire included digital adoption factors based on the UTAUT2 framework, and perceived impacts of virtual consultations across IOM quality domains. Weighted logistic regression identified predictors of use and satisfaction. Results About one in three respondents (31.0%) had used virtual consultations, almost always by telephone (91.3%) and infrequently. After adjustment, younger age (18–44 vs. ≥65: OR 7.76, 95% CI 2.22–27.16) and a bachelor's undergraduate education (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.06–3.96) were the only independent factors associated with use, and the same profile predicted intention to use. In the acceptance framework UTAUT2, effort expectancy and facilitating conditions were the strongest constructs and social influence the weakest. Across the full sample, efficiency was perceived as the quality domain most positively impacted by virtual consultations (62.4%), whereas patient-centredness was rated least favourably (34.5%). title: Diffusible signals from Azospirillum brasilense promote rice growth and induce distinct gene expression changes in plant roots
abstract: Plants form associations with diverse beneficial microbes, including arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi, rhizobia, and plant growth-promoting bacteria (PGPB). Research on legume-rhizobia symbiosis (LRS) and AM symbiosis has demonstrated that molecular communication between symbiotic partners is essential for initiating these interactions. Genetic and biochemical studies have further identified both plant and microbial signals, as well as host genetic pathways, that regulate these interactions. However, most studies on plant-PGPB interactions have focused on direct application of PGPB to plant roots, leaving the early signaling mechanisms underlying these interactions poorly understood. In this study, we report that diffusible signals from A. brasilense can promote rice growth without direct contact between bacteria and plant roots, 7 days post-treatment (dpt). Using RNA sequencing, we identified 2,516 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in rice roots in response to diffusible signals from A. brasilense at 1 dpt. We identified differential expression of genes involved in flavonoid synthesis, defense responses, receptor activity, transcription factors, and hormone pathways. Comparative transcriptomic analysis of rice roots with or without contact with A. brasilense revealed both shared and unique gene expression patterns. We observed upregulation of certain defense-response gene…

title: Peer power over hierarchy: why knowledge sharing outperforms transformational leadership in gamification adoption in education
abstract: Purpose Despite gamification's potential to catalyze student engagement, faculty adoption remains stagnant at 11.3%. This study investigates the impact of transformational leadership (TL) and knowledge sharing (KS) on instructors' intentions to adopt gamified pedagogy in Vietnamese higher education through the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM). Design/methodology/approach Using a quantitative, time-lagged design (N = 204), validated scales for TL, KS, and TAM were analyzed via hierarchical regression and Hayes' PROCESS Model 80 to test serial mediation through perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEOU), and attitude. Findings Knowledge sharing emerged as a robust direct predictor of intentions, operating through both PU and PEOU pathways. Transformational leadership demonstrated no significant direct effect in the parsimonious model but exerted significant indirect influence via the PU to attitude path. These results reveal that “peer power”, collaborative knowledge exchange, is a more potent driver of innovation than hierarchical mandates in autonomous academic environments. Originality/value Addressing a lacuna, where only 9% of research examines adoption antecedents, this study provides a theoretically grounded framework for understanding faculty decision-making. title: Analysis of Students' Mathematical Thinking Skills in Trigonometry Learning through a Digital Worksheet Assisted by Virtual Reality
abstract: Mathematical thinking skills are skills that students need to master, particularly in trigonometry. This study aims to analyze and describe students’ mathematical thinking skills in trigonometry learning through Digital Worksheet assisted by Virtual Reality. The method used was qualitative descriptive. The research subjects consisted of 32 tenth-grade students at SMA N 1 Belitang. The research procedure consisted of three stages: preparation, implementation, and the final stage. Data were collected through Digital Worksheet assisted by Virtual Reality, written tests, and interviews. Data analysis was conducted in three stages: data reduction, grouping the data based on four indicators of mathematical thinking skills, and presenting the data based on the Digital Worksheet assisted by Virtual Reality, written tests, and interviews, followed by drawing conclusions. The results of using a Digital Worksheet assisted by Virtual Reality in the specializing activity showed that students were able to identify and explain known and requested information. In the generalizing activity, students were able to transform contextual situations into right triangles. In the conjecturing activity, students were able to make conjectures about the appropriate trigonometric ratios to solve problems. In the convincing activity, students were able to prove their conjectures through calculations and dra…

abstract: Perubahan iklim global, yang ditandai oleh kenaikan suhu 1,55°C di atas level pra-industri dan emisi gas rumah kaca yang terus meningkat, turut memperburuk kerentanan masyarakat pesisir Indonesia yang sangat bergantung pada sumber daya laut untuk penghidupan namun memiliki keterbatasan modal, teknologi, dan infrastruktur. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif studi kasus melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi lapangan, dan studi dokumentasi. title: Effects of eccentric training on athletes’ explosive power: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Background Eccentric training is frequently used to improve explosive performance in athletes; however, findings across different performance dimensions (e.g., jumping and sprinting) remain inconsistent, and intervention heterogeneity is substantial. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the effects of eccentric training on explosive performance in athletes. Methods Web of Science, PubMed, CNKI, Wanfang, Scopus, and SPORTDiscus were systematically searched. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were included according to the PICOS framework (healthy athletes; explicitly labeled eccentric training; conventional training as control; outcomes related to explosive performance, including countermovement jump (CMJ) and linear sprint performance over 10 m, 20 m, and 30 m). Only studies explicitly labeled as eccentric training were included; Nordic hamstring exercise and other interventions not explicitly labeled as eccentric training were excluded. Methodological quality was assessed using the Physiotherapy Evidence Database (PEDro) scale, and meta-analyses were performed using a random-effects model. Results Eleven RCTs (n = 348; 11–25 years; 6–24 weeks) were included. Pooled results showed that eccentric training significantly improved CMJ performance (MD = 2.92 cm, p = 0.0006). However, no significant improvements were observed for short-distance sprint performance: 10-m and 20…

title: PlantDefender: a unified deep learning approach for maize disease and pest detection
abstract: Introduction Maize crops face severe threats from various diseases and pests, significantly affecting crop quality and yield. Prompt and accurate diagnosis is essential to minimize agricultural losses. Existing models have demonstrated limitations in handling complex backgrounds, inter- and intra-class variations, and inefficient feature extraction, which complicate the recognition of maize diseases and pests. Methods This study proposes a unified deep learning model, termed PlantDefender, for the simultaneous recognition of maize diseases and pests. PlantDefender employs an improved Faster R-CNN architecture with a refined InceptionResNet-V2 as its backbone. The conventional InceptionResNet-V2 is modified by replacing the ReLU activation function with Swish to enhance feature extraction. The extracted features are subsequently processed through the Region Proposal Network (RPN), ROI Align, regression, and classification modules for accurate detection and recognition. The model is evaluated using the IP102 dataset for maize pest recognition and the CD&S dataset for maize leaf disease recognition. Results PlantDefender achieves an accuracy of 78.67% on the IP102 dataset and 98.44% on the CD&S dataset. The results demonstrate effective localization and classification performance across both maize pest and disease recognition tasks. Discussion The experimental results indi…

title: Coordination of photosynthetic performance and leaf N:P stoichiometry under fluctuating coastal environmental conditions in Bolboschoenoplectus mariqueter
abstract: Introduction The population of Bolboschoenoplectus mariqueter has substantially declined because of habitat modification and competition. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize the photosynthetic and stoichiometric traits of B. mariqueter and their environmental regulation in a natural tidal-flat population to facilitate successful conservation. Methods Light- and CO 2 -response characteristics, diurnal and seasonal dynamics of leaf gas exchange, daily carbon assimilation and transpiration, chlorophyll characteristics, and leaf nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry in a natural were investigated in a × B. mariqueter population in Hangzhou Bay, China. Random forest, variation partitioning, and redundancy analyses were used to evaluate the relationships among photosynthetic performance, leaf nutrient stoichiometry, and microenvironmental factors. Results The net photosynthetic rate (Pn), transpiration rate (Tr), and water-use efficiency (WUE) varied substantially among months. Pn and Tr showed generally coordinated diurnal dynamics, whereas daily carbon assimilation and transpiration followed partially divergent seasonal trajectories after July. Leaf N and P concentrations and N:P ratios exhibited pronounced and asynchronous seasonal variations. The random forest model explained 65%, 69%, and 42% of the variations in Pn, Tr, and WUE, respectively. Leaf P and N:P were…

title: Thermal effects of die-attach void fraction and position in high-power LED packages: a three-dimensional finite-element study
abstract: Purpose This study aims to quantify the effects of die-attach void fraction and in-plane position on heat flow in a high-power phosphor-converted LED package. Design/methodology/approach The model was run in MATLAB R2025b with the Partial Differential Equation Toolbox. Nineteen configurations covered six void fractions and three positions, plus the void-free case. Mesh, energy-balance, transient, material, convection, source-partition, shape and aspect-ratio checks were completed. The 18 voided cases were examined as a 6 × 3 fraction–position grid. Findings The 30% corner-directed void raised junction temperature by 5.50 °C and package resistance by 39.37%. It also made the chip-top field strongly non-uniform. The corner penalty remained 5.39–5.61 °C over the conversion-layer heat sweep. Heat was redirected laterally, and the position penalty grew with void fraction. Practical implications A limit based only on total void area can miss a large defect located near the edge or corner of the bond. Originality/value Moving a void while keeping its projected area unchanged produced different temperature and resistance values. The heat-flux maps relate this position effect to the loss of the direct through-thickness path and increased lateral flow through the remaining bonded area.

title: Phenotypic and genetic characterization of an unexplored yam (Dioscorea spp.) collection from Togo and development of a core collection
A study on the identification of wheat powdery mildew using chlorophyll fluorescence imaging
abstract: Introduction Wheat powdery mildew poses a serious threat to global wheat production, and its accurate identification is key to smart agriculture. Methods This study combines chlorophyll fluorescence imaging with deep learning algorithms to investigate the temporal dynamics of key fluorescence parameters (such as maximum photochemical efficiency, QYmax) during the progression of powderymildew. A QYmax-based chlorophyll fluorescence image dataset for wheat powdery mildew was constructed. Building on this, the LCRNet model was proposed, which effectively processes fluorescence image data through a collaborative mechanism integrating the Large Selective Adaptive Fusion (LSAF) and Coordinated Attention (CA) modules. Results On an independent test set, the model achieved an accuracy of 94% and an F1 score of 94.1%, outperforming comparison models. Discussion This study proposes a method for classifying the severity of powdery mildew in wheat that reduces the computational cost of fluorescence data processing, providing important methodological support and technical insights for advancing the intelligent, precise, and green transformation of crop disease prevention and control systems.

title: MICROPROCESSOR SYSTEM FOR DIGITAL CONTROL OF ELECTRIC DRIVES OF WORKING ELEMENTS OF GRAIN CLEANING MACHINES
abstract: This paper addresses the development and experimental validation of a digital control system for the electric drives of grain-cleaning machine working units based on the SAKO SKI780 frequency converter, the Arduino Uno microcontroller platform and the Modbus RTU communication protocol. The proposed system is intended to improve the accuracy, flexibility and reliability of electric-drive control during grain-cleaning operations. The general architecture of the control system, the principles of interaction between its main hardware components, the control algorithm for generating and transmitting commands through the RS-485 interface, and the corresponding software implementation of the microprocessor-based control system are presented. Particular attention is paid to ensuring stable and reliable data exchange between the microcontroller and the frequency converter, as well as to the correct formation of control commands for regulating rotational speed and other operating parameters of the electric drive. The developed software makes it possible to set the required operating modes, transmit control signals, process feedback data and coordinate the operation of individual machine units. Experimental studies confirmed the stable operation of the proposed control system and its ability to accurately reproduce specified speed modes under varying load conditions. The obtained results …

title: EVALUATION OF SPRAY CHARACTERISTICS AND PESTICIDE DISTRIBUTION USING CENTRIFUGAL NOZZLES UNDER LABORATORY CONDITIONS
abstract: This scientific paper presents a comprehensive experimental study on the formation of the spray plume and the distribution of the working fluid by centrifugal nozzles under stationary laboratory bench conditions. The relevance of this study is driven by the strict requirements of modern agricultural production to increase the efficiency of plant protection product application while simultaneously minimizing environmental impact. Traditional field tests are often complicated by a number of uncontrolled meteorological factors (wind speed and direction, fluctuations in air temperature and humidity), which significantly reduces the reliability of determining the true performance characteristics of individual nozzles. To solve this problem, the authors applied a laboratory testing methodology using a specialized hydraulic bench manufactured in accordance with current standards, which made it possible to isolate and evaluate the influence of key technological parameters with high precision. The object of the study is the processes of hydraulic liquid spraying by AM.03.SB and Ej.03 centrifugal nozzles. The subject of the study is defined as the regularities of changes in the coefficient of variation of the transverse distribution of the working fluid depending on the pressure in the pressure manifold and the height of the sprayer boom. During the experimental studies, the working pres…

title: RESULTS OF EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH ON THE QUALITY OF CLEANING CARROT ROOTS WITH A SPIRAL CLEANER
abstract: The article presents the results of a study of the influence of controlled factors on the quality of cleaning a pile of carrots from soil impurities and plant residues, as well as on the level of damage to root crops during the operation of the cleaner. To establish the nature and strength of the influence of the studied parameters, regression equations were developed that allow assessing the dependence of the main indicators of the cleaning process on the mass of carrot roots (m, g), the angular speed of rotation of the cleaner shafts (ω, rad∙s⁻¹) and the angle of inclination of the cleaning bed to the horizon (α, deg.). Experimental studies and statistical processing of the obtained results were performed using the Statistica 13.0 package of applied statistical programs. Based on the obtained data, three-dimensional spatial response surfaces were constructed that characterize the dependence of the amount of separated and adhered soil on the studied factors. The analysis was carried out for two variants of the root crop entering the cleaning bed, which made it possible to determine the features of the technological process depending on the initial position of the carrot. The obtained graphical relationships provide a visual representation of the results of laboratory experiments and allow to assess both the individual influence of factors and the nature of their interaction. T…

title: XPERIMENTAL INVESTIGATION OF THE PARAMETERS OF A WORKING TOOL FOR REMOVING THE DISTURBED SOIL LAYER FROM THE CENTER OF A CRATER
abstract: The article presents the results of theoretical and experimental studies of the process of removing a damaged soil layer inside a crater by means of a specially developed working tool. The structural scheme and the general configuration of the working tool are described in detail. For performing the technological operation, the tool was mounted on the boom of an excavator, which provided the required positioning, movement trajectory and interaction with the treated soil surface. The design of the working tool includes the use of channel flanges and angle-section elements that ensure gradual layer-by-layer cutting, separation and removal of the damaged soil from the inner surface of the crater. Such a design makes it possible to control the depth of soil removal and to reduce excessive disturbance of the underlying undamaged layers. To determine the soil cutting force and to evaluate the nature of the mechanical loading during dynamic experimental studies, an electronic dynamometer equipped with an SBA interface was used. The dynamometer strain-gauge sensor was installed directly on the brackets of the working tool, which ensured continuous and reliable registration of force parameters during the cutting process. The obtained experimental data made it possible to assess the actual loading conditions of the tool and to compare them with the values predicted by the theoretical mod…

title: Health behavior, loneliness and social participation among students in a higher education institution: a community case study providing insights into health psychology
abstract: Background Higher education institutions can be conceptualized as community settings that may facilitate individuals’ health and well-being (in terms of low loneliness), health behavior, and general social participation. However, facilitating factors in individuals, their social network, and contextual factors were not researched building on the Evolutionary Theory of Loneliness and the Compensatory Carry-Over Action Model . Objective In a community case study, students’ health behavior, loneliness, and social participation were investigated to determine interrelations and factors that help students maintain a healthy lifestyle, reduce loneliness, and increase social participation. Method We analyzed an online survey of 373 students using descriptive statistics, group comparisons, regression models, and exploratory curve estimation. Results Of 293 students with available loneliness data, the mean loneliness was M = 2.76 (SD = 1.06; range 1–4), and 122 (41.6%) were classified as lonely. Loneliness was reflected in private relationships and study-related contacts, whereas no significant association was found with studying/working from home, χ 2 (1) = 0.11; p = 0.74. Lonely students differed from not-lonely students across 10 behavioral domains, including talking to a doctor, watching films, spending time in nature, interacting with others online, listening to music, drinking alco…
