Resolving the LiFePO4 Battery State beyond Voltage-Based Diagnostics Using Surface-Scan MRI
abstract: Abstract Reliable assessment of state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH) in commercial batteries remains a major challenge because their closed architecture obscures the underlying electrochemical, structural, and thermal processes, while existing diagnostic methods often provide only indirect, spatially averaged, voltage-based information about battery operation and degradation. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) is among the most widely deployed cathode materials due to its low cost, long cycle life, and high thermal stability; however, its characteristically flat voltage profile fundamentally limits the information content of conventional diagnostics. In this work, we exploit the large magnetic-susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases and the lithiation-dependent evolution of their phase fractions for accurate and time-efficient determination of SoC in commercial pouch cells and battery packs. Surface-scan magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides new SoC and SoH metrics through quantitative inside-out measurements of battery-induced magnetic field perturbations. LFP is a cathode material particularly well suited to this approach because its biphasic FP/LFP regime spans a large fraction of the usable SoC window while generating substantial magnetic susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases. Under the biphasic approximation, the average magnetic susc…

title: Efficient Extraction of Tea Polyphenols and Their Bioactive Preservation Using Magnetic-Induced Electric Field
abstract: Abstract Tea polyphenols (TPs) are valuable bioactive compounds derived from tea with diverse health-promoting effects. However, efficient extraction of TP with preserved bioactivity remains a challenge. This study evaluated magnetic-induced electric field (MIEF) technology for efficient TP extraction. Under optimized conditions (solid-liquid ratio 1:30, conductivity 1000 μS/cm, voltage 800 V, frequency 70 kHz, 60 min, and 30 °C), MIEF achieved a TP yield of 223 mg/g, exceeding those of water bath extraction (WE, 194.05 mg/g) and ultrasound-assisted extraction (UE, 201.97 mg/g) by 14.91% and 10.41%, respectively. Catechin composition and other fundamental chemical components were also enhanced, with notably higher dissolution of ester-type catechins (epigallocatechin gallate and epicatechin gallate) by 21.2% and 10.4% over WE. MIEF treatment induced a honeycomb-like porous structure (20–80 nm) in tea residues with a 7.1-fold increase in specific surface areas (3.24 m2/g) relative to untreated control. MIEF extract solutions contained uniformly dispersed nanoparticles (140–160 nm) with a higher negative charge (ζMIEF-30 ≈ –60 mV), compared with WE (ζWE ≈ –20 mV) and UE (ζUE ≈ –40 mV). Moreover, MIEF extracts exhibited brighter yellow hues than the dull reddish tones observed for WE and UE extracts, suggesting reduced TP oxidation and polymerization during low-temperature MIEF ex…

title: Research on entry guidance and test methods for reusable launch vehicle
abstract: Abstract The purpose of the re-entry phase is to reduce excessive speed and altitude to meet the initialisation conditions of the Terminal Area Energy Management (TAEM) phase for a reusable launch vehicle (RLV). The key to re-entry guidance research lies in designing the lateral bank angle profile and the longitudinal angle-of-attack profile. The bank angle profile must be designed to ensure achievement of the total re-entry range, while the angle-of-attack profile should primarily minimise the aerodynamic heating load of the vehicle. In this paper, a guidance law design method based on the drag-energy profile is presented, and the profile is obtained using an optimisation method. A linear control law is derived to track the drag reference; the angle-of-attack and bank angle profiles are developed, and a re-entry flight guidance and control system is established based on a specific vehicle model. Flight simulation results show that the control system works effectively: the RLV can fly to the start of the TAEM phase with a range error of less than 0.2 km, a maximum overload of 1.6 g (meeting the constraint requirement of 2.5 g) and a maximum dynamic pressure of 13 kPa (below the allowable limit of 17 kPa); the trajectory azimuth angle error is limited to within ±18°, which fully verifies the accuracy, safety and feasibility of the proposed guidance method.

title: Optimal placement of shared autonomous electric vehicles waypoints using open-source GIS data: a case study of suburban Lille, France
Endogenous strategy spaces in sequential- and simultaneous-move duopoly games
abstract: Abstract Duopoly markets are widely discussed in industrial economics under the assumptions of quantity and price competition in sequential- and simultaneous-move duopoly games with differentiated goods. We compare Nash and Stackelberg equilibria in which the firms endogenously choose to behave as a price or quantity setter. Using the utility function introduced by Dixit (1979), we generalize the model of Boyer and Moreaux (1987) by allowing different market sizes and show that it is always more profitable to strategically set the price (quantity) if the goods are complements (substitutes). For every degree of product differentiation, consumer surplus and total welfare are highest under the standard Bertrand equilibrium, followed by the price Stackelberg, the quantity Stackelberg, and the Cournot equilibrium. In a generalized framework of Boyer and Moreaux (1987), we show that there is no unique ranking of prices, quantities, and profits of the leader and follower depending on the degree of product differentiation and the type of competition. Furthermore, we show that the price (quantity) Stackelberg equilibrium is bounded by the Bertrand and the mixed Nash equilibrium in which Firm 1 sets the price (quantity) and Firm 2 the quantity (price).

title: A GIS-based multi-objective optimization strategy for urban automated external defibrillator deployment
abstract: Abstract Background Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains a critical urban health challenge due to persistently low survival rates and uneven access to automated external defibrillators (AEDs). Existing deployment strategies often rely on heuristic decisions, limiting their ability to address spatial disparities in emergency response. This study aims to develop a spatially informed, data-driven framework to optimize AED placement and improve urban emergency response capacity. Methods Using Qinhuai District in Nanjing as a case study, we applied Geodetector to identify the spatial determinants of OHCA risk. High-risk population density and its interaction with resident density emerged as dominant factors, informing the construction of a high-resolution AED Demand Index for candidate site selection. We then formulated a multi-objective optimization model to balance service coverage, perceived accessibility, and cost-effectiveness. The model was solved using an enhanced NSGA-II algorithm incorporating tabu search and 2-opt mutation. Results The optimized layouts demonstrated substantial improvements over existing AED configurations. The maximum service distance decreased by 55.3%, and overall satisfaction reached a near-optimal level of 0.997. The enhanced algorithm also achieved notable computational gains compared with standard approaches. Conclusions The proposed GIS-ba…

title: Data governance, business strategy, and sustainability practices: exploratory employee-perception evidence from a single pulp and paper corporate group
abstract: Purpose This study examines how data governance (DG) contributes to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) integration by strengthening data accountability, the reliability of ESG-related information, and strategic alignment. Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV), it investigates the relationships among DG, Business Strategy (BS), and sustainability practices and principles (SPP) within a single pulp and paper organisation. Design/methodology/approach This study adopts a bounded single-organisation employee survey design based on non-probabilistic convenience sampling. Survey data were collected from 103 valid respondents within one pulp and paper corporate group and analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling to examine perceived associations among DG, BS, and SPP. The analysis was complemented by contextual information on the organisation's DG model and its integration with operational excellence to support ESG objectives. Findings Within the studied organisation, the results suggest positive direct and indirect associations among DG, BS, and SPP. The indirect association through BS is statistically significant and consistent with partial mediation, suggesting that BS may play an alignment role between DG and SPP. The findings provide exploratory, context-specific evidence that respondents perceive DG as associated with the organisational embed…

title: Stent retriever angioplasty with the Tigertriever as a bailout strategy for intracranial atherosclerotic disease–related large-vessel occlusion: illustrative cases
abstract: BACKGROUND Intracranial atherosclerotic disease–related large-vessel occlusion (ICAD-LVO) is associated with residual stenosis and early reocclusion following mechanical thrombectomy (MT), particularly in Asian populations. Conventional stent retrievers (SRs) are optimized for embolus removal and may not provide sufficient mechanical dilation. The Tigertriever is a radially adjustable SR with operator-controlled expansion and manual constriction, enabling stentoplasty and safe retrieval. OBSERVATIONS This study retrospectively analyzed the data of 3 consecutive patients with ICAD-LVO who were treated using a sequential algorithm that included initial conventional MT, followed by Tigertriever-assisted stentoplasty and loading doses of DAPT. Durable recanalization was performed in 2 cases involving the middle cerebral artery and internal carotid artery, respectively, with 1 patient showing significant functional improvement, from a modified Rankin Scale score of 5 to 1 on day 7. The third case involved the vertebral artery and showed temporary recanalization despite eventual recurrent occlusion, with neurological preservation reflecting collateral adaptation. LESSONS Tigertriever-assisted stentoplasty combined with DAPT is a promising sequential bridge strategy for refractory ICAD-LVO identified during thrombectomy. By achieving direct mechanical vessel dilation similar to balloo…

title: Multi-strategy Engineering of a Glycosyltransferase for More Sustainable and Efficient Biosynthesis of Mogroside IE
abstract: Abstract Mogroside IE is a valuable natural sweetener precursor, but its industrial production is hampered by inefficient plant extraction and nongreen chemical synthesis. Herein, we report a computational-experimental engineering strategy that transformed a putative glycosyltransferase, UGTX1, with negligible initial activity (2.4% conversion) into a highly efficient biocatalyst. This was achieved by synergistically combining machine learning (ESM-2) for zero-shot prediction, dynamic cross-correlation network analysis (DCCNA) for allosteric control, and structure-guided tunnel engineering to rationally design a focused mutant library. Screening identified beneficial single-point mutations, which were mapped onto the enzyme structure to define three functional zones (core, tunnel, and shell). Guided by this spatial insight, a focused rational iterative site-specific mutagenesis (FRISM)-based combinatorial assembly yielded the quintuple mutant UGTX1-M5, which exhibits a 54-fold increase in catalytic efficiency (kcat/Km = 1.13 × 104 M–1 s–1). The engineered enzyme enabled the scalable synthesis of mogroside IE in a simple, green aqueous-phase system, achieving >98.5% conversion of 1.5 mM mogrol within 14 h at 35 °C without exogenous metal ions. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the mutations collectively stabilize a catalytically competent conformation, enlarge the …

title: STRATEGY FOR OVERCOMING THE COMMUNITY'S NEGATIVE IMAGE TOWARD ISLAMIC BOARDING SCHOOLS
abstract: Islamic boarding schools (pesantren), as traditional Islamic educational institutions in Indonesia, often face a negative public image portraying them as closed, rigid, and less adaptive to modern challenges such as radicalism, narcotics, and bullying. The background of this issue stems from stereotypes reinforced by mass and social media, which highlight cases of isolation without contextualizing positive aspects, as well as from the public's limited understanding of moderate Islamic values such as tolerance and empathy. This condition hinders the role of pesantren as agents of social change and as institutions shaping the character of the younger generation. This study employs both qualitative and quantitative methods, including surveys, in-depth interviews with pesantren leaders, alumni, and community members, as well as literature reviews to identify the factors contributing to stigma and strategies for its mitigation. This approach is grounded in philosophical, sociological, and juridical foundations, such as Law Number 18 of 2019 on Pesantren, which emphasizes adaptability and innovation. The findings indicate that effective strategies include curriculum modernization through the integration of general sciences and technology, social media campaigns to build positive narratives, anti-bullying programs through counseling and conflict resolution skills training, and partner…

title: Osmoconditioning Using Polyethylene Glycol (PEG) 6000 as a Strategy to Enhance Seed Viability and Vigor
abstract: Background: High-quality seeds are essential for crop establishment, but seed deterioration can reduce seed viability and vigor. Since controlled water uptake is fundamental to seed priming, osmoconditioning with polyethylene glycol (PEG) 6000 has been investigated to regulate seed hydration. Objective: This narrative review aimed to critically synthesize evidence on the physiological mechanisms of osmoconditioning with PEG 6000, its reported effects on seed viability and vigor, factors contributing to variation in seed responses, and current research gaps. Methods: A narrative review supported by a structured literature search was conducted using publications from 2016 to 2026. Evidence was comparatively synthesized according to physiological mechanisms, PEG concentration or osmotic potential, priming duration, plant species, and responses related to seed viability and vigor. Results: Osmoconditioning with PEG 6000 was associated with favorable responses in germination percentage, uniformity, seedling length, and other seed viability and vigor parameters, although responses varied among plant species and treatment conditions. Physiologically, PEG 6000 lowers external water potential, enabling controlled hydration and pre-germinative processes while limiting premature radicle protrusion. Increasing PEG 6000 concentration or extending priming duration did not consistently produc…

title: Sediment management strategy prioritization in hydropower reservoirs under data scarcity
abstract: Introduction Sedimentation in hydropower reservoirs is a major challenge for sustainable energy production. It reduces storage capacity, increases turbine abrasion, and raises operational costs, while also causing environmental impacts and operational management difficulties. Therefore, the identification of appropriate sediment management strategies is essential for maintaining reservoir sustainability and operational performance. However, many reservoirs have limited hydrological and sediment monitoring data, which restricts the application of conventional process-based methods. Methods This study proposes a multi-criteria decision-making framework that integrates the Best-Worst Method (BWM) and the Combined Compromise for Ideal Solution (CoCoFISo) method to prioritize sediment management strategies under data-scarce conditions. Ten management strategies were evaluated using four dimensions: economic, environmental, technical, and social. Criterion weights were determined using BWM, an optimization-based method for deriving weights from expert judgments. The CoCoFISo method was used to rank the strategies by combining additive and multiplicative aggregation mechanisms to handle complex decision problems. Results The results show that the technical dimension received the highest weight (0.365), while the social dimension received the lowest weight (0.089). At the criterion lev…

Real-time visual feedback on dynamic postural stability modulates performance and strategy
abstract: Lower limb injuries are prevalent in sports and frequently recur, with impaired dynamic postural stability identified as an important risk factor. Real-time visual feedback has shown potential to improve postural stability, yet the relative effectiveness of different feedback types remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of four types of real-time visual feedback on dynamic postural stability during a single-leg perturbation task using a between-subject design. Eighty-nine healthy participants performed 192 mediolateral perturbations, to evoke and then measure balance responses, divided across a warming-up, feedback, and retention condition. Participants were assigned to one of five groups, receiving feedback on center of pressure speed (CoPS), time-to-stability (TTS), vertical force deviation (FYdev), trunk angular velocity (TAV), or no feedback (control). Outcome measures were these four measures and the angular velocities of the arms (AAV) and swing leg (SAV). For each outcome, ANCOVAs with warming-up performance as covariate were followed by pairwise comparisons with the control group. FYdev and TAV feedback improved their targeted outcome measure (both p < 0.01), whereas CoPS and TTS feedback did not. All four feedback types reduced SAV ( p < 0.05), FYdev feedback additionally reduced CoPS and TTS ( p < 0.05), and CoPS and TAV feedback both reduced TA…

title: Implementation of the Structured Debate Learning Model to Improve Learning Outcomes in Pancasila Education on the Topic of "the Territory of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia" at UPT SMP Negeri 3 Semanding
abstract: Low initial learning mastery highlighted the need for more active instruction in Pancasila Education at UPT SMP Negeri 3 Semanding. This study examined changes in learning outcomes following the implementation of structured debate on the territory of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia (NKRI), with students divided into affirmative and opposing groups. A mixed-methods classroom action research design was conducted over two cycles involving 26 seventh-grade students in Class VII-C. Data were collected through observations, questionnaires/tests, and interviews and analyzed descriptively using quantitative and qualitative techniques. At baseline, two students (8%) met the minimum mastery criterion (KKM = 70), and the class mean score was 55. In Cycle I, mastery increased to 16 students (62%), with a mean score of 71. In Cycle II, mastery remained at 16 students (62%), while the mean score was 69. Qualitative findings indicated a progression from basic conceptual understanding toward analysis involving higher-order thinking skills, accompanied by greater self-confidence and stronger argumentation skills. These findings indicate that mastery gains relative to baseline were maintained across the two cycles, alongside qualitative improvements in students’ thinking and participation. The study provides contextual evidence for constructivist, debate-based civic pedagogy and p…

title: Training Methods in Higher Education and the Workplace: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Abstract The growing use of technology-supported training has increased the need to examine training methods in higher education and workplace settings more thoroughly. Although the literature includes many studies that report a growing use of technology-supported training, such as simulation-based and immersive approaches, it still presents important gaps because it remains fragmented. Many studies focus on isolated training methods, specific sectors, or single outcomes, which limits a broader understanding of how training has been designed, evaluated, and measured across different contexts. To address this gap, this systematic literature review analyzes research published between 2019 and 2024 on training methods in higher education and the workplace. Following the PRISMA framework, this review of the literature analyzes 36 articles to examine how training methods, learning theories, and evaluation practices are reported and combined in both higher education and workplace settings. The analysis suggests that constructivist, cognitivist, and behaviorist perspectives have commonly guided training design approaches, with limited hybridization across them, while assessment practices have varied across contexts and include different research methods and structured evaluation models. In addition, outcome measures have mainly focused on learning, performance, and skill development, …

title: Faktor-Faktor yang Memengaruhi Niat Siswa Mengadopsi Game-Based Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Game-Based Learning (GBL) adalah pendekatan pembelajaran berbasis permainan yang menghibur dan melibatkan peserta didik sekolah menengah. Namun, adopsi GBL masih diperdebatkan secara akademis dan memerlukan penyelidikan lebih lanjut. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis faktor-faktor yang memengaruhi niat siswa untuk mengadopsi GBL. Studi ini menggunakan Systematic Literature Review (SLR) dengan panduan PRISMA terhadap 20 artikel ilmiah terkemuka dari Google Scholar dan Scopus yang diterbitkan pada rentang tahun 2021 hingga 2026. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa faktor utama yang memengaruhi niat adopsi GBL dan keterlibatan siswa meliputi persepsi kegunaan dan kemudahan penggunaan (Technology Acceptance Model), penurunan kecemasan belajar (Learning Anxiety), interaksi guru-siswa, serta dukungan teknis dan kesiapan institusional sekolah. Temuan ini memberi panduan bagi pendidik untuk membangun ekosistem GBL yang inklusif dan berkelanjutan, serta menjadi acuan sekolah dalam mengadopsi teknologi pendidikan baru. Untuk penelitian yang akan datang, direkomendasikan penggunaan pendekatan longitudinal guna menguji retensi pengetahuan jangka panjang dan daya ingat siswa terhadap mekanika game. Selain itu, penelitian selanjutnya perlu memperluas pengujian model adopsi ini pada konteks sekolah dengan keterbatasan sarana infrastruktur serta penerapannya pada kurikulum digital lai…

Development of the Baamboozle Game-Based Interactive Learning Module on Acids and Bases
abstract: This study was motivated by the need for more interactive teaching materials to help students understand acid-base concepts. The aim of this research is to produce an interactive learning module based on the Baamboozle game on acid-base material. This study employed a research and development (R&D) methodology based on the ADDIE model, with implementation limited to the development stage. Data were collected through a teacher needs analysis questionnaire, validation forms for subject matter experts and media experts, and response questionnaires for teachers and students. The needs analysis questionnaire used the Guttman scale, while the validation forms and response questionnaires used the Likert scale. The data were analyzed using quantitative descriptive methods by calculating the percentage of scores to determine the product’s level of suitability and practicality. The results of the study indicate that the developed module received a feasibility rating of 89.17% from media experts and 87.03% from content experts, both categorized as “highly feasible.” The practicality test results showed a rating of 89.3% from teachers and 93.2% from students, categorized as “highly practical.” Thus, the Baamboozle game-based interactive learning module on acid-base material is deemed highly feasible and highly practical for use in chemistry instruction. The novelty of this research lies in…

title: Facilitating Deep Learning Characteristics through Problem-Based Learning and PhET Simulation in Molecular Geometry
abstract: Chemistry concepts related to molecular structure are challenging to learn due to their abstract nature, the necessity for multiple representations, and the demand for three-dimensional spatial visualization skills. This study examines the implementation of Problem-Based Learning (PBL) supported by PhET Simulation, an interactive virtual tool that enables students to visualize and explore molecular structures and chemical concepts. The objective is to promote deep learning through meaningful, joyful, and mindful learning experiences. An embedded mixed-methods approach with a one-group pretest–posttest design was utilized. The sample consisted of 36 grade X students from SMA Negeri 3 Palopo, selected via random sampling. Research instruments included a conceptual understanding test, a joyful learning questionnaire, an observation sheet, and a PBL-based Student Worksheet (LKPD). Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively using N-Gain, with hypothesis testing conducted via the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test for meaningful learning and a paired-samples t-test for joyful learning. Qualitative data from student observations and reflections were analyzed thematically. The results showed a significant increase in meaningful learning (N-Gain = 0.554, moderate category) and joyful learning (N-Gain = 0.576, moderate category). Observations and thematic analysis further indicated that mindfu…

title: NeuroEarlyAI: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework with EarlyDetectNet for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection and Classification using MRI Scans
abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is an ageing and progressive neurodegenerative disease, and one of the most prevalent dementias that affects millions of patients worldwide, including millions of people in Europe, and is a public health priority. Early and right diagnosis is of paramount importance for early therapeutic intervention as well as retardation of the disease. The visual search for small changes in the brain is rather time-consuming and subjective. For comparison, we chose two traditional diagnostic procedures: clinical evaluation and manual MRI analysis, where the clinical evaluation is more appropriate for the intended user in healthcare centres. The automatic detection of AD using recent advancements in deep learning are yet to lack a few drawbacks, such as class imbalance, overfitting and generalisation issue on external datasets, low transparency in the decision-making of the deep learning model, which makes it difficult for clinical applications. To fill this gap, in this paper, we propose NeuroEarlyAI, an end-to-end learning framework with EarlyDetectNet, a new model for early and interpretable detection of AD from the structural MRI scans. The framework also consists of sophisticated pre-processing strategies (denoising, data augmentation and skull stripping) to enhance the quality and diversity of the data. EarlyDetectNet has an attention mechanism which highlights …

title: Editorial: Learning on the edge: EdTech in conflict-affected and fragile regions
Predicting student success in open and distance learning: a comparative evaluation of machine learning models
abstract: Purpose This study compares Logistic Regression, linear Support Vector Machine, Random Forest and Histogram Gradient Boosting for predicting four student outcomes in open and distance learning (ODL) from the first four weeks of study. Design/methodology/approach Using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, the analysis included 27,535 registrations from 24,841 students. Day-28 predictors comprised static characteristics, raw virtual learning environment (VLE) activity and engagement-focused behavioral features. Class-weighted models were evaluated using nested stratified group cross-validation, with student records grouped across partitions. The macro-averaged F1 score (macro-F1) was the primary metric. Findings With engagement-focused features, the linear support vector machine yielded the highest macro-F1 (0.406) and 47.6% accuracy, followed closely by Random Forest (0.404) and Histogram Gradient Boosting (0.402). Engineered behavioral features improved macro-F1 by 0.014 over raw VLE activity, with a 95% confidence interval of [0.009, 0.019]. A secondary assessment-informed model reached a macro-F1 of 0.434, whereas excluding sensitive demographic attributes did not clearly reduce performance. Originality/value This research contributes to ODL through a fixed early window, student-grouped validation and theory-aligned behavioral feature engineering. It supports timel…

title: Exploring nursing students’ experiences of using generative AI for emotional intelligence learning: a qualitative study
abstract: Background Emotional intelligence is a core competency for nursing students; however, traditional nursing education faces challenges in fostering emotional intelligence, including curricular imbalances, limited teaching methods, and delayed assessment and feedback. The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers new possibilities for addressing the above issues; however, existing research has not yet thoroughly explored how nursing students learn emotional intelligence through GenAI or their experiences in this process. Objective Based on the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) and the Teaching Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, and using Goleman’s five-dimensional model of emotional intelligence as a reference, this study explores the experiences of undergraduate nursing students in using generative artificial intelligence for emotional intelligence learning, as well as the factors that facilitate this process. Method This study employed a qualitative descriptive research design and Reflexive Thematic Analysis (RTA). Using purposive sampling, 19 undergraduate nursing students (from freshman to senior year) were selected for one-on-one semi-structured in-depth interviews. All participants had experience using GenAI tools (such as DeepSeek and Doubao) for communication practice, case discussions, or sentiment analys…

title: From literacy to action: econometric and machine learning evidence on digital financial behaviour in India
abstract: Purpose This study examines the impact of digital financial literacy (DFL) on digital financial practices (DFP) in India by combining causal inference and machine learning approaches. It investigates whether higher DFL translates into greater engagement with digital financial services and whether this effect varies by gender. Design/methodology/approach Using primary survey data from 1,215 adults, the study applies covariate-adjusted ordinary least squares (OLS), propensity score matching (PSM) and overlap weighting to estimate the effect of DFL on DFP. Gender heterogeneity is analysed through interaction models and stratified matching. A Random Forest model is used to assess predictive importance. Findings Results consistently show that higher DFL is associated with significantly greater DFP across all estimators, with effect sizes ranging from 0.86 to 1.41 (p < 0.001). The effect is stronger among women, indicating a potential equalising role of literacy in digital finance adoption. Machine learning results further identify DFL as the most important predictor of DFP, explaining a substantial share of variation in outcomes. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation, and findings are specific to the Indian context. Future research can extend this work using longitudinal data and comparative frameworks. Practical implications Th…

title: Beyond Technocentrism in AI-Supported Special Education: The PAISEN Model of Teacher-Mediated Inclusive Learning
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) offers new possibilities for inclusive teaching and learning for students with special educational needs (SEN), yet AI-in-SEN research remains largely technocentric, often describing system capabilities without explaining how outputs become pedagogically meaningful. This conceptual paper develops the PAISEN Model (Pedagogical Artificial Intelligence for Special Education Needs) through an integrative synthesis of AI in education, inclusive pedagogy, Universal Design for Learning (UDL), and assistive technology. The model proposes a non-deterministic sequence in which AI Teaching Support Systems provide data and adaptive affordances, Teacher Pedagogical Mediation interprets and contextualises them, and an Inclusive Learning Environment translates decisions into accessible participation opportunities. SEN learning outcomes are treated as proposed consequences rather than established effects. Teacher AI competency, institutional support, digital infrastructure, and learner characteristics function as boundary conditions, while an adaptive feedback loop links learner evidence to teacher reflection and instructional adjustment. The novelty of PAISEN lies in making teacher judgement the central explanatory mechanism and separating technology, pedagogical processes, learning conditions and moderators. Theoretically, it bridges AIED and inclusive education;…

title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair
abstract: Background Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR. Methods A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. Results LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regressio…

title: The Hidden Curriculum of Generative AI: Institutional AI Policies and the Potential for Student Inequality
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, prompting institutions to develop policies governing its use in teaching, learning, and assessment. Although existing discussions have emphasized academic integrity, assessment practices, and technological access, less attention has been given to the knowledge and competencies students may need to interpret and comply with institutional AI policies. This study examines how institutional GenAI policies establish explicit and implicit expectations for students and identifies potential pathways through which policy-navigation demands may contribute to educational inequality. Using comparative qualitative content analysis, publicly available policies and guidance documents from 20 purposively selected higher education institutions across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, and South Africa were examined. The analysis considered policy permissiveness, disclosure requirements, instructor discretion, student responsibilities, AI-literacy guidance, accessibility, equity, and implicit navigation demands. Findings indicate that acceptable AI use is frequently determined at the course, instructor, or assessment level, requiring students to interpret context-specific rules, understand disclosure requirements, verify AI-generated outputs, and reconcile varying instructor expectatio…

Deep Contextual Feature Fusion with CFF-Net for Tamil and Malayalam Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Sentiment analysis of the Dravidian languages, such as Tamil and Malayalam, is necessary in most cases to decipher the perception and sentiments expressed in social media, which is normally rich in code-mixed, informal, and vague text. The issue of noisy, skewed and context-variable data in the context of accurate classification is a problem in these languages. The proposed solution to these challenges is a new sentiment classification model that incorporates Contextual Feature Fusion Network (CFF-Net) with Adaptive Gradient-Weighted Optimization (AGWO) to overcome these challenges. The aim is to enhance accuracy in classifications, address the issue of class imbalance and provide strong detection of positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. The framework identifies context-sensitive features of the text in the form of hierarchical levels of attention and semantic interaction, and focuses on informative tokens, but rejects irrelevant information. AGWO automatically selects the learning rates of each modality, which converges faster and more steadily. Tests were run on complete datasets of Tamil and Malayalam, and performance was measured in terms of Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and AUC. The findings indicate that the proposed CFF-Net with AGWO is superior to the current models in all metrics, with an accuracy of 97.14% on Tamil and 96.67% on Malay…

title: Facing uncertainty in primary care: perceptions, strategies and educational needs – a qualitative explorative study with German general practice trainees
abstract: Abstract Background Uncertainty is an inherent aspect of everyday practice in primary care with a context of low-prevalence conditions. Dealing with diagnostic ambiguity and therapeutic uncertainty constitutes a central challenge within postgraduate medical training in general practice (GP). This study aimed to explore how GP trainees perceive and manage uncertainty and their educational needs to tailor specific measures. Materials and methods In 2025, GP trainees of the Competence Centre Baden-Württemberg (KWBW) were recruited by purposive sampling to participate in an interview-study. A semi-structured interview guide was specifically developed. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and subsequently analysed using a content-analytical approach by three researchers. Results 22 interviews with mean duration of 46 min (min. 36 min, max. 70 min) were performed. GP trainees experienced uncertainty regarding themselves (intrapersonal), their patients (interpersonal) and the primary care context (systemic). Common strategies to manage included watchful waiting, seeking collegial advice, consulting external sources and relying on experience and intuition. Uncertainty was more perceived in outpatient than in inpatient settings and was linked to various emotions. The interviewees recommend early and longitudinal integration of uncertainty management into training, as it represents a…

title: Reliability-Based Assessment of Slopes Stability Considering Seismic and Soil Uncertainty
abstract: In slope instability hazard assessment, it is essential to account for uncertainties associated with both soil heterogeneity (the mechanical and physical properties of the soil) and environmental conditions, such as hydraulic boundary conditions, external loads, and seismic actions. This study investigates the reliability of slope stability by integrating both the intrinsic and spatial variability of soil properties together with hydro-mechanical and seismic loading effects. Two representative case studies are analysed: a natural slope and a zoned earth dam. A combined deterministic–probabilistic framework is employed, in which the Bishop limit equilibrium method is used to calculate the factor of safety, while probabilistic methods including Monte Carlo simulation, the First-Order Reliability Method (FORM), and random field modeling, are applied to estimate the probability of failure. Sensitivity analyses are also conducted to identify the most influential parameters affecting slope stability. The results indicate that groundwater level rise, seismic acceleration, and soil heterogeneity significantly increase the probability of failure. Further more, kriging-based random field models demonstrate that spatial variability of soil shear strength parameters has a decisive effect on reliability estimates. The study demonstrates that neglecting either spatial variability or seismic …

title: Do large language models keep the hedge? Uncertainty preservation when large language models summarize aviation and maritime incident reports
abstract: Safety-incident reports are written with deliberate epistemic caution: A reporter marks what was seen, what was inferred, and what remains unsure, and a dropped hedge can turn a tentative observation into an apparent cause. As large language models take over summarizing such reports for triage, indexing, and search, whether they preserve that caution becomes a property of the safety record itself. This study asks whether models keep a reporter's expressed uncertainty when they summarize, testing two hypotheses fixed before any summary was generated: that models systematically harden uncertainty by default and that an explicit instruction to preserve it overcorrects into softening. Six open-weight models summarized 42 real incident reports, 30 from the United States Aviation Safety Reporting System and 12 from the United Kingdom Marine Accident Investigation Branch, under a plain prompt, a preserve prompt, and a paraphrase of it. Uncertainty change was measured two ways: at the passage level, by a deterministic epistemic-marker lexicon, and at the claim level, by aligning those markers between source and summary, each validated against manual annotation and cross-checked against two independent language-model judges. Under plain summarization, all six models hardened the reporter's uncertainty (claim-level hardening 0.59–0.85), dropping explicit hedges almost entirely (retention…

title: Living With Known Unknowns: Prognostic Uncertainty in Congenital Cytomegalovirus Following Diagnosis
abstract: OBJECTIVE To examine how parents experience and navigate prognostic uncertainty following a diagnosis of congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) and identify implications for clinical communication and newborn screening. METHODS We conducted in-depth qualitative interviews with 41 birth parents of children with cCMV. Interviews explored diagnosis, communication with health care practitioners, health care navigation, and perceptions of child development. Transcripts were analyzed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS Prognostic uncertainty emerged as a central and enduring feature of parents’ experiences. Five themes characterized how families navigated uncertainty: (1) families live with the burden of an unpredictable future, (2) families struggle to make meaning from incomplete and inconsistent information, (3) families become drivers of the diagnostic journey to gain clarity and control, (4) knowledge provides families direction even when certainty is impossible, and (5) families value early diagnosis because it makes uncertainty more manageable. Uncertainty contributed to anxiety, information seeking, and ongoing monitoring. However, parents consistently valued early diagnosis because it provided direction, facilitated treatment and developmental surveillance, supported access to intervention, and informed decision-making. Rather than eliminating uncertainty, diagno…

title: Business Cycle Effects of Firms’ Uncertainty Under Low and High Uncertainty
abstract: Abstract Non-linearities in the uncertainty-output relationship may help to explain pronounced business cycle fluctuations. We suggest that the level of uncertainty itself influences the reaction of real activity to a surprise increase in uncertainty. We base our analysis on a measure of business uncertainty of firms’ decision makers, which is derived from a large survey panel covering the time-span 1980–2018. To study differences in the response to an increase in uncertainty, we use an interacted VAR model, where coefficients depend on the level of uncertainty, and uncertainty enters as an endogenous variable. Surprise increases in uncertainty have particularly adverse effects when the level of uncertainty is low compared to periods in which firms are already highly uncertain. This non-linear effect occurs during recession and non-recession phases.

title: Quantifying the contribution of vegetation layer uncertainty to simulated forest fuels treatment placement
abstract: Background Western US forests face rising high-severity fire risk motivating increased investment in forest management. The high cost of treatments and vast areas needing work require efficient resource allocation. Forest landscape models can help scale up analysis and support management, but underlying uncertainties can limit their utility. Aims We examined uncertainty in the initial forest input layer, quantifying the error and determining how much field data are needed to produce outputs suitable for informing management. Methods We created eight initial forest layers using various sample sizes and selection methods, ran 50-year simulations and compared outputs. We also resampled model outputs from 100 to 500 m resolution and evaluated the effects. Key results Stratified sampling stabilized errors and allowed using smaller sample sizes relative to random sampling, and coarser resolution resampling reduced errors while retaining key information. Combining these strategies produced similar outputs using all and only 25% of the data. Conclusions Combining stratified sampling with output coarsening reduces data demands while maintaining analytical rigor, enabling more actionable guidance for management planning. Implications This work advances the operational use of landscape models as a decision-support tool, allowing managers to scale up planning by integrating model outputs w…

title: A bio-inspired model for cluster optimization in software-defined networks
Integrated Optimization of Fresnel Lens–PMMA Optical Fiber Daylighting Systems Using a MATLAB-Based Platform
abstract: Daylighting technologies offer an energy-efficient solution for indoor lighting by harnessing and transmitting natural sunlight through optical fibers. However, their large-scale deployment remains limited due to design complexity, coupling inefficiencies, and performance instability under real climatic and mechanical conditions. This study proposes an optimised sunlight concentration and transmission system based on PMMA optical fibers, developed through an integrated MATLAB App Designer platform that unifies optical, thermal, and lighting analyses within a single engineering environment. The system combines Fresnel lenses for solar concentration, PMMA optical fibers for light transmission, and an interferential thermal filter designed using OpenFilters to mitigate infrared absorption and prevent fiber overheating. The performance of the system was evaluated in two Moroccan cities, Errachidia (maximum DNI of 789 W/m 2 ) and Nador (612 W/m 2 ), representing high and moderate solar resource regions in North Africa. Three Fresnel lenses with diameters of 317.5 mm (Lens 1), 139.7 mm (Lens 2), and 63.5 mm (Lens 3) were investigated. A novel fiber bundle configuration allowing a controlled overlap beyond the focal spot is introduced, improving packing efficiency while ensuring stable optical transmission under vibration and alignment deviations, an issue largely neglected in previou…

title: Reducing antibiotic burden in gram-negative bacteraemia: duration optimization and early oral transition
abstract: Purpose of review Gram-negative bloodstream infections have traditionally been managed with prolonged and intravenous antibiotic therapy. This review aims to summarize the evidence supporting strategies to reduce antibiotic burden through shorter treatment durations and/or oral step-down therapy. Recent findings Recent randomized controlled trials, target trial emulations, and large observational studies demonstrate that in patients with uncomplicated Gram-negative bloodstream infections an early oral step-down therapy and/or reduced antibiotic courses achieve clinical outcomes comparable to prolonged intravenous therapy and longer treatment durations. Fluoroquinolones and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remain the preferred oral agents because of their high bioavailability. Appropriately dosed oral β-lactams appear to provide comparable outcomes, highlighting the importance of exposure optimization rather than antibiotic class alone. The evidence is expanding also for special populations, but important knowledge gaps remain for patients with severe immunosuppression and multidrug-resistant pathogens. Summary Current evidence supports reducing antibiotic exposure in selected patients with Gram-negative bloodstream infections by combining shorter treatment durations and early oral step-down therapy. Future studies should address remaining evidence gaps, particularly in frail patie…

Delivery Accuracy, Robotics, and Logistics Information System Integration in Operational Performance Through Sorting Optimization
abstract: Background: Logistics transformation at Sentral Pengolahan Pos (SPP) Jakarta, a high-volume mail-processing hub within PT Pos Indonesia (Persero), is taking place amid rising shipment volumes and persistent challenges in national logistics performance. Objective: This study examines the relationships between delivery accuracy, robotic technology implementation, and logistics information system integration and logistics operational performance, with sorting process optimization tested as a mediating variable. Method: The study employed a quantitative explanatory, cross-sectional design using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. Primary data were collected through a 5-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered to 80 employees and operators at SPP Jakarta using total sampling (census). Results: All ten hypothesized structural paths were statistically supported. Delivery accuracy, robotic technology implementation, and logistics information system integration were positively and significantly associated with sorting process optimization and logistics operational performance. Robotic technology implementation showed the largest path coefficient for sorting process optimization (0.471), while logistics information system integration showed the largest direct path coefficient for logistics operational performance (0.434). Sorting process opt…

title: THEORETICAL PRINCIPLES OF GROUNDING AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE PARAMETERS OF SOIL PROCESSING MACHINE UNITS
abstract: The publication highlights the theoretical principles of substantiation and optimization of the parameters of tillage machine-tractor units as one of the key factors in increasing the efficiency, productivity and energy performance of forestry production. The research is based on a systematic methodology that integrates the fundamental principles of theoretical mechanics, soil mechanics, traction theory and the general theory of machine-tractor units for the development and operation of high-performance aggregates. A comprehensive analysis of the main factors determining productivity, energy efficiency, reliability and quality of technological operations during primary tillage was carried out. Particular attention is paid to the complex interrelationships between the structural and technological parameters of tillage machines, the traction and energy characteristics of power units, soil properties and specific operating conditions. Considerable attention is focused on the problem of reducing energy losses and improving the utilization of the traction capabilities of tractors. Modern approaches to mathematical modeling and optimization of operating parameters using traction-balance models, energy indicators and analysis of the time structure of technological operations are considered. The proposed methodology makes it possible to take into account actual operating conditions, ch…

title: Integrated metabolomic and single-cell analyses reveal crotonylation-related epithelial remodeling and SDC4 dysregulation in adenomyosis
abstract: Background Adenomyosis (AM) is characterized by ectopic endometrial invasion and myometrial fibrosis, yet the molecular links between local metabolic remodeling, lysine crotonylation (Kcr), and epithelial dysfunction remain poorly understood. We investigated the metabolic and crotonylation-related landscape of AM and sought to identify epithelial molecular features associated with these alterations. Methods Clinical metabolic profiles, public and newly generated tissue metabolomic data, crotonyl-CoA measurements, and tissue crotonylation assays were integrated with single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses. Kcr-related transcriptional patterns were characterized using multiple gene-set scoring approaches and co-expression analysis, followed by multi-algorithm feature prioritization. SDC4-associated epithelial states were further examined using trajectory inference, cell-cell communication analysis, transcription-factor prediction, and in silico perturbation. Results Adjusted clinical analyses showed no robust differences in circulating lipid profiles, whereas tissue-level metabolomic analyses revealed alterations in lipid- and lysine-related metabolites in AM. Crotonyl-CoA estimates were higher in AM tissue, accompanied by increased H3K18cr. A higher p65-associated Kcr signal was also observed in a single IP comparison; given that only one IP measurement was available per gr…

title: Unidirectional integrated optical elements for secure communication systems in multimode optical fibers
abstract: Abstract In bidirectional transmission, existing optical communication systems suffer from propagation loss, crosstalk, delay in transmission, back-reflection, signal leakage, noise accumulation, and physical-layer security vulnerability. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a secure unidirectional optical communication system over multimode optical fiber. A proposed system includes optical isolators, one-way transmission, and mode-selective filtering to minimize intermodal interference. Unidirectional transmission: suppresses crosstalk and enhances signal integrity by controlling the propagation of the signal based on the dominant transmission mode. The system was tested using simulations with realistic channel conditions, such as attenuation, dispersion, and noise. The performance was evaluated in terms of signal to noise ratio (SNR), bit error rate (BER), and suppression of crosstalk. The proposed model gave a BER of 2 × 10 −4 at SNR of 10 dB compared to 5 × 10 −4 without optical isolator and 8 × 10 −4 without mode-selective filter. The proposed model reduced the BER by 80 % and intermodal crosstalk by 40–60 % compared to the baseline. The BER decrease from 5 × 10 −4 to 2 × 10 −4 was observed as an SNR gain of 1.2–1.8 dB. The results show performance enhanced propagation efficiency, channel reliability, and physical-layer security, which is suitable for the syst…

title: Estimates of transition burden, geographic distribution, and risk-stratified care for adolescent and young adult cancer survivors: A multi-centre analysis from a low- and middle-income country
abstract: Background Improved survival in low- and middle-income countries is generating a rapidly expanding population of childhood cancer survivors (CCS) who will transition to adult care. In India, the capacity and geographic distribution of long-term survivorship care remain poorly characterized. Methods We synthesized survivorship data from three tertiary pediatric oncology centres in North India. Transition-eligible survivors were those diagnosed before age 18 years, who completed cancer-directed therapy between January 2016 and December 2025 and had attained age >18 years by December 2025. We quantified the transition-eligible cohort, projected the transition burden through 2030, mapped adolescent and young adult (AYA) survivors by geographic distance from their treating centre, and risk-stratified survivors for survivorship care planning as per published diagnosis and exposure based criteria. Results Among 3,060 survivors, 398 (13.0%) were transition-eligible; 288 (72.4%) were male. Lymphomas (34.1%), solid tumors (29.1%), and acute lymphoblastic leukemia (27.8%) were the predominant diagnoses. The transition-eligible cohort is projected to increase to 1,071 by 2030 (+169.1%). Approximately 58% lived >50 km from their treating centre. Overall, 387 (97.2%) were classified as moderate (44.9%) or high risk (52.3%). Transition processes were absent (56%) or informal (33%); barr…

title: Etnobotani Aren (Arenga pinnata) pada Masyarakat Minangkabau di Lima Puluh Kota, Sumatera Barat
abstract: Aren (Arenga pinnata (Wurmb) Merr.) merupakan palma multiguna yang penting bagi rumah tangga pedesaan, tetapi variasi pengetahuan pemanfaatannya pada masyarakat Minangkabau di Kabupaten Lima Puluh Kota belum terdokumentasi secara komparatif. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi bagian aren yang dimanfaatkan, mendeskripsikan bentuk dan cara pengolahannya, serta membandingkan frekuensi penyebutan pemanfaatan pada tiga kecamatan. Survei etnobotani deskriptif dengan komponen kualitatif dan kuantitatif dilaksanakan pada Desember 2025-Maret 2026 di Kecamatan Gunuang Omeh, Lareh Sago Halaban, dan Mungka. Sebanyak 90 responden berusia ≥40 tahun (30 responden per kecamatan) diwawancarai menggunakan pertanyaan terbuka. Data dianalisis sebagai ragam bentuk pemanfaatan dan frekuensi sitasi responden, disajikan sebagai n (%). Hasil menunjukkan 10 bagian/material aren dengan 28 bentuk pemanfaatan dalam lima kelompok utama, yaitu pangan, kerajinan, bahan bangunan/energi, pengobatan tradisional, dan kebutuhan budaya. Berdasarkan daftar pemanfaatan yang terdokumentasi, Gunuang Omeh memiliki 21 bentuk pemanfaatan, Lareh Sago Halaban 15, dan Mungka 18. Sapu ijuk paling sering disebut di Gunuang Omeh (28/30; 93,3%), sedangkan gula aren dan sapu lidi masing-masing disebut oleh 23/30 responden (76,7%) di Mungka. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pengetahuan pemanfaatan aren tidak seragam antarlokasi…

title: How digital recruitment shapes recruitment performance: A stage-level analysis
abstract: Orientation: Digital transformation has integrated technology across recruitment stages, yet research treats digital recruitment as a single concept, overlooking its multistage nature and varied performance effects. Research purpose: This study examines how digitalisation across recruitment stages - sourcing, screening, interviewing, selection, offer and closing, and onboarding – affects outcomes including cost and time efficiency, quality of hire, sourcing effectiveness, and first-year retention. Motivation for the study: Empirical evidence on stage-specific digitalisation performance impact remains limited, leaving organisations without clear guidance on where digital investment yields the greatest returns. Research approach/design and method: A quantitative design using survey data from 454 STEM HR professionals was employed. Multiple regression analyses assessed digitalisation’s unique effects on performance outcomes, while a Multivariate General Linear Model evaluated multivariate impact. The study draws on the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory. Main findings: Stage-level digitalisation showed differential associations with recruitment performance. Interviewing was the most consistent predictor. Offer and closing showed the strongest and broadest effects. Screening showed a small negative association with cost efficiency and a positive association with fi…

title: Treating a systemic disease as a local one: failure points of current pancreatic cancer management and a multimodal, biology-guided framework for redesign
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remains among the most lethal solid tumors, with 5-year survival near 13% despite decades of incremental change, and current management continues to be organized around anatomic resectability and a chemotherapy backbone applied largely without regard to tumor biology. This article advances the thesis that the dominant paradigm underperforms because it treats a systemic, molecularly convergent, multi-compartment disease as though it were a local one. We first summarize the real advances of the past decade—in surgery, systemic therapy, molecular profiling, and immunotherapy—and then identify five interlocking failure points that persist despite them: (i) selection by vessel anatomy, judged on imaging criteria that are read inconsistently and that classify inaccurately even where read consistently, and applied to splanchnic veins without accounting for their baseline variability and tumor-associated thrombosis; (ii) occult metastasis and the resulting limits of local cure for the systemic majority, evidenced by the gap between complete resection and durable survival and by early distant recurrence; (iii) the addition of radiotherapy, which improves local control without extending survival; (iv) chemotherapy chosen without reference to a validated prognostic classical/basal-like distinction, although prospective subtype-directed regimen selection ha…

title: Industry 4.0 and the premises for organizational decision-making: a multi-layer analysis
abstract: Purpose The article approaches Industry 4.0 through the lens of social systems theory. It studies the impact of Industry 4.0 as a strategic initiative on organizational programs setting the premises for decision communication. Design/methodology/approach The study proceeds interpretively on seminal publications on Industry 4.0 and a collection of documents on application. Using hermeneutic analysis, it identifies criteria for correct decision-making on four layers of organization in society that are addressed in literature. Findings Different criteria are identified for the manufacturing sector as a whole, national industrial complexes, single companies and their systemic substructures. All of them are relatable to the idea of keeping the respective organizations in charge of the ongoing digital transformation by demonstrating innovativeness. Originality/value The study draws attention to the role of Industry 4.0 in communication constituting organization through decisions. It enables a discussion of strengths and weaknesses from a new perspective, giving a more nuanced account of Industry 4.0 as a strategic initiative.

title: Fetal right to life at the intersection of ethics, law, and health: a qualitative study of parents’ and health clinicians’ perspectives
abstract: Abstract Background The right to life is recognized as a fundamental human right and a basis for the enjoyment of other rights. However, how this right applies to the fetus remains ethically and legally contested and has important implications for reproductive and prenatal health care. Previous studies have examined the moral and legal status of the fetus, abortion, and maternal–fetal conflicts, but less is known about how the concept of fetal right to life is understood by those directly involved in prenatal care and how ethical, legal, and health considerations interact in this understanding. This study aimed to explore how parents and health clinicians conceptualize the fetal right to life, identify its perceived dimensions and challenges, and examine possible strategies for its protection at the intersection of ethics, law, and health. Methods This conventional qualitative content analysis study was conducted in Saveh, Iran, from April 2025 to March 2026, based on an interpretative epistemological orientation. Data were collected using 16 semi-structured, face-to-face interviews, with 21 participants: 10 parents (five couples) and 11 clinicians involved in fetal health care, such as gynecologists, neonatologists, embryologists, medical ethicists, forensic medicine experts, and midwives/nurses. The participants were selected using purposive and maximum variation sampling tec…

title: What if Crossan is right? The origin and the future of the Catholic Eucharist
abstract: This study examined John Dominic Crossan’s theory regarding the historical origins of the Eucharistic rite. According to the American historian and exegete, the primary source of the Eucharist is the practice of the Jesus movement, which involved open table fellowship. Crossan also believes that the connection between the early Eucharist and the Paschal Mystery is not historically primary, and in any case, should not be the only dimension in interpreting the meaning of this ritual. The current article analyses Crossan’s views and, based on them, raises questions about Catholic Eucharistic practice. The research indicates that Crossan’s reconstruction is credible, at least to some extent, and accepting his conclusions allows us to determine which aspects of the Eucharist should be appreciated today so that the Church may be more faithful to the historical origins of this rite. The Eucharist of the early Christians was, above all, a horizontal, communal Eucharist, and precisely on that level, it was a way of experiencing God’s presence. This article sets out, in this key, proposals for experiencing the Eucharist with a greater appreciation of the communal dimension – a dimension that is, after all, present in Catholic doctrine and practice. Intradisciplinary and/or interdisciplinary implications: The study demonstrates the importance of historical research on the origins of Chris…

title: Too Hot, Too Cold, or Just Right? The Effects of Temperature on Sleep
abstract: Sleep is necessary for optimal functioning and for overall health and wellbeing. You might have heard advice on how to improve your sleep, such as reducing intense activities close to bedtime or keeping a regular sleep-and-wake schedule. As many countries experience climate change, it is also important to be aware of how sleep may be affected when the temperature changes. Sleep may be delayed or disturbed in a cold environment or a hot and humid one, and poor sleep can make it difficult to function well, especially if it happens often. It is important to create a good sleep environment, keeping in mind that the temperature and humidity of the room, the air circulation, as well as the bedding and clothes worn to bed, play a role in a person’s ability to get the most out of the time spent in bed.

title: Financial Recordkeeping as a Condition of the Relationship between Digital Payment Use and Hotel Credit Access
abstract: This conceptual conference paper proposes that financial recordkeeping may condition the relationship between digital payment use and hotel credit access. Its focus is the conversion of traceable receipts into interpretable evidence about business activity and repayment capacity. It distinguishes payment adoption, record quality and lenders’ actual use of information, and outlines an application-level study in Uzbekistan. The proposed contribution is a testable moderation framework supported by a practical measurement strategy. No hotel survey or lending experiment has yet been conducted, and no empirical effects are claimed.

title: ELEKTRON TIJORAT SHAROITIDA POCHTA BIZNES JARAYONLARINI TAKOMILLASHTIRISH VA MOLIYAVIY SAMARADORLIKNI BAHOLASH
abstract: This article examines postal business process improvement and financial performance assessment in the context of e-commerce. The methods include a systems approach, functional process analysis, horizontal analysis and financial ratios for 2023–2024. Revenue increased by 58.02%, gross profit by 37.01% and net profit by 4.21%, while the net profit margin declined from 0.212% to 0.140%. A proposed monitoring model links information transparency, logistics, digitalization, customer segmentation and additional services. Research on electronic payments, artificial intelligence and innovation performance is applied to postal service management. The findings support assessing service volume alongside costs, service quality and profitability

title: РАЗВИТИЕ ФИНАНСОВЫХ МАРКЕТПЛЕЙСОВ В УСЛОВИЯХ ФОРМИРОВАНИЯ ЦИФРОВОЙ ЭКОНОМИКИ УЗБЕКИСТАНА
abstract: The article investigates the essence of the financial marketplace, the specifics of its functioning, and the relevance of incorporating these digital platforms into the modern financial system. The paper characterizes the structure of the financial marketplace alongside its key participants and provides a comprehensive analysis of the financial marketplace industry in the Republic of Uzbekistan. Furthermore, the study outlines the core advantages of utilizing financial platforms while examining the existing constraints and barriers that impede the full-scale development of such solutions within the country. In conclusion, it is argued that the subsequent evolution and popularization of financial marketplaces will substantially streamline the acquisition of financial products and services for consumers

title: Severe Congenital Pneumonia Associated With Probable Vertical Transmission of Mycoplasma pneumoniae During a UK Epidemic Surge
abstract: Congenital Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MP) is rare. During the United Kingdom’s 2023/2024 MP epidemic, we encountered a fatal case of probable vertically transmitted MP in a preterm infant. This report highlights the need to consider MP during incidence surges, reviews existing literature, and examines whether congenital MP cases cluster around epidemic peaks.

Driving sustainable banking performance: the roles of digital transformation, FinTech adoption, and financial inclusion under regulatory environment moderation
abstract: Purpose With sustainability becoming a global priority, financial institutions increasingly use FinTech to support sustainable performance within evolving regulatory environments. This study investigates how digital innovation, specifically FinTech Adoption and financial inclusion, is associated with firms' sustainable performance while examining the moderating role of the regulatory environment in shaping these relationships. It also offers insights into how regulatory frameworks can support the use of digital tools to promote a more sustainable financial future. Design/methodology/approach This study employed a survey methodology to collect data from bank employees in Saudi Arabia. From a total of 402 survey responses, 385 were considered valid and used for analysis. The proposed relationships were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings The study revealed that digital transformation was significantly linked to sustainable performance, FinTech Adoption, and financial inclusion. Fintech Adoption was positively related to financial inclusion and sustainable performance. The moderation analysis showed that the regulatory environment strengthens the association between financial inclusion and sustainable performance. title: The psychology of digital credit: the association of financial anxiety and impulsive traits with “buy now, pay later” delinquency
abstract: Introduction Digital credit structures, exemplified by the “Buy Now, Pay Later” (BNPL) model, combine frictionless transactional accessibility with the underlying psychological vulnerabilities of users. This cross-sectional investigation maps the statistical covariation between perceived financial anxiety and distinct digital credit usage dimensions. Methods Utilizing a dataset of 890 respondents (708 of whom are active BNPL users), regression and mediation analyses was conducted. The study evaluated subjective financial anxiety, BNPL usage (frequency, dependence, hedonic preference, and delinquency), impulsive buying tendency, and objective financial literacy. Results Analyses reveal an absence of significant correlation linking financial anxiety to operational usage frequency or overarching bill dependence. However, a robust positive covariation emerges between heightened financial anxiety and both the allocation of credit toward non-essential hedonic consumption and the propensity for debt delinquency. Impulsive buying tendency acts as a stable trait that shows a statistical indirect association in this cross-sectional relationship, and objective financial literacy does not significantly moderate this association. title: Behavioral differentiation during the AIGC image generation waiting period: effects on creativity in conceptual design
abstract: Introduction: Artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) offers new ways to generate inspiration for conceptual design, yet limited attention has been paid to the waiting period between prompt submission and AI image output. This study examined behavioral differentiation during this interval and investigated how the task relevance and cognitive load of waiting-period behaviors affect creativity in conceptual design. Methods Three experiments were conducted with design students. Experiment 1 identified and classified core waiting-period behaviors ( N = 30); Experiment 2 measured the cognitive load of representative behaviors using the NASA-TLX ( N = 24); and Experiment 3 employed a behavior-based 2 × 2 conceptual framework ( N = 60), in which four representative waiting-period behaviors were selected to represent different combinations of task relevance (high/low) and relative workload (higher/lower), and their creative performance was compared. Results The results showed that the AIGC generation waiting period was not a passive interval but involved multiple identifiable behavioral patterns. Creative performance differed across the four representative behavioral conditions. title: Soft Skills and Hard Skills Training Design for Sustainable Economic Empowerment of Transit Apartment Residents
abstract: Background: Economic empowerment of social housing residents is essential for sustaining housing programs for low-income communities. Objectives: This study aims to analyze the implementation of existing training programs, identify residents’ needs and barriers, and formulate a soft skills and hard skills training design for Transit Apartment residents in West Java Province. Methods: A descriptive qualitative approach was applied at the Batujajar and Rancaekek Transit Apartments, involving 31 residents, 2 apartment managers, and 2 community empowerment staff members selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through observation, in-depth interviews, and documentation, and analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. Results: The implemented training improved residents’ knowledge, skills, and entrepreneurial motivation but had not yet produced sustainable economic independence because of limited business capital, market access, post-training mentoring, and uneven participation. This study formulates the Penta Participatory Apatrans model, which is built on a participatory needs assessment and integrates five main components: soft skills strengthening, hard skills development, continuous mentoring, business network strengthening, and pentahelix collaboration among government, academia, business, community, and media. Conclusion: The model pr…

title: The emancipation of technology as a subject: teachers’ views of technology content in secondary education
abstract: Abstract The roles of technology and engineering within STEM education have evolved from a focus on technology as a product to a broader vision encompassing the processes involved in its creation, closely linked to engineering. As the newest disciplines in STEM education, technology and engineering lack a well-defined identity, leading to uncertainty among educators about what and how to teach these subjects in K–12 education. This study proposes a comprehensive framework integrating multiple perspectives on essential knowledge in technology and engineering education, ranging from hands-on skills to theoretical, epistemological understanding, in order to characterize pre-service and in-service teachers’ perception about technology as a content for secondary education. Our findings reveal that teachers’ views represent a mosaic of complementary perspectives rather than a unified vision, reflecting ongoing identity challenges in these fields. Notably, both novice and experienced teachers display diverse conceptions, highlighting gaps potentially rooted in limited training and the shift from traditional technical to design-oriented learning outcomes. Additionally, teachers tend to emphasize practical knowledge over theoretical aspects and often perceive engineering design as a linear, procedural process rather than an epistemic activity. title: Kentsel Yeşil Alanların Farklı Tematik Yaklaşımlar Açısından İşlevleri ve Stratejik Önemi
abstract: Günümüzde kentler, hızla artan nüfus, kontrolsüz ve plansız gelişmenin yanı sıra iklim değişikliği ve afet risklerinin yarattığı çok boyutlu kırılganlıklarla da mücadele etmek zorunda kalmaktadır Bu çalışma, kentsel yeşil alanları geleneksel "sosyal altyapı" tanımı ve işlevinin ötesine taşıyarak; bu alanları şehircilik, iklim değişikliği ve afet yönetimi perspektiflerinden tematik ve bütüncül bir işlevsel çerçevede ele almayı amaçlamaktadır. Araştırma kapsamında kentsel yeşil alanlar; küçük, orta ve büyük ölçekli (sokak, mahalle, kent ve bölge) tipolojiler üzerinden genel özellikleri ve işlevlerine göre sistematik bir matrisle sınıflandırılmıştır. Literatür taraması ve mevzuat analizi yöntemlerinin kullanıldığı çalışmada, mevcut imar mevzuatının yeşil alanları afet ve iklim dirençliliği bağlamında ikincil konumda bıraktığı tespit edilmiştir. Çalışma, yeşil alanların yer seçimi ve mekânsal organizasyonunda salt sayısal standartların yanı sıra kentsel morfoloji ile bütünleşik ve çok işlevli tasarım stratejileri, ilkeleri ve araçlarının benimsenmesi gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır. Elde edilen bulgular, yerel yönetimler ve politika yapıcılar için afetlere karşı dirençli ve sürdürülebilir kentlerin inşasında ve kentlerdeki yaşam kalitesinin arttırılmasında stratejik bir rehber niteliği taşımaktadır.
