title: Estimating the Heritability of Intelligence with a Nuclear Twin Family Design
abstract: Abstract Intelligence, and the favorable life outcomes with which it is associated, are not shared equally between individuals or groups. In an endeavor to better understand the inequality, behavioral genetics (BG) have employed the classical twin design (CTD) to apportion the variability in the intelligence quotient (IQ) to genetic and environmental sources. Recent research has revealed that such parameter estimates are subject to bias: underestimating the influence of assortative mating, and nonadditive genetic effects. These biases are somewhat mitigated by the nuclear twin family design (NTFD). To date no published studies have applied the NTFD to IQ. This study addresses this limitation utilizing a meta-analysis of data comprising IQ measures from 660,365 twin, parent-child, and spousal pairs collected over more than 50 years from more than 15 countries. In a comparison of parameter estimates obtained under the CTD and NTFD, this study confirmed that the NTFD more accurately estimated the heritability of IQ. These findings will inform and guide future research, gene-mapping efforts, and public policy aimed at correcting the inequality in educational and life outcomes that are significantly associated with IQ.

title: Mimar Sinan Parkı Selçuklu Yapıları Yeniden Kullanım Projelerinin Özgünlük Kavramı Üzerinden Değerlendirilmesi
abstract: Bu çalışma, kültürel mirasın korunmasında özgünlük kavramını temel alarak Kayseri Mimar Sinan Parkı’nda yer alan Gevher Nesibe Tıp Kompleksi ile Avgunlu Medresesi’nin yeniden kullanım süreçlerini özgünlük bağlamında karşılaştırmalı olarak incelemektedir. Araştırma, Nara Özgünlük Belgesi’nin (1994) ortaya koyduğu tasarım, malzeme, yapım tekniği, işlev, konum ve çevre gibi ölçütlerini değerlendirme çerçevesi olarak benimsemektedir. Araştırma kapsamında, tarihî arşiv belgelerinden elde edilen veriler güncel mimari özelliklerle karşılaştırılmış; yapıların özgünlüğü, uzman görüşleri ve güncel kavramsal tartışmalarla nitel yöntemle değerlendirilmiştir. Bu amaçla, Nara Belgesi’nin çok boyutlu özgünlük yaklaşımını temel alan ve 0–4 arasında derecelendirilen beşli bir değerlendirme ölçeği geliştirilmiştir. Ölçek, yapılan müdahalelerin kapsamını, geri döndürülebilirliğini ve yapının fiziksel ile anlatımsal kimliğine etkisini dikkate alarak farklı yeniden kullanım uygulamalarının karşılaştırılmasına olanak sağlamaktadır. Gevher Nesibe Tıp Kompleksi’nin müze, Avgunlu Medresesi’nin ise kitabevi–kafe olarak yeniden işlevlendirilmesi bu çerçevede incelenmiştir. Bulgular, her iki yapının da konumsal sürekliliğini korumasına karşın çevresel dönüşümlerin bağlamsal özgünlüğünü zayıflattığını, müdahalelerin niteliğinin ise özgünlük düzeyleri üzerinde belirleyici olduğunu göstermektedir. title: Morphological analysis of Traditional Odunpazarı houses: A study on periods
abstract: Traditional Turkish House, studied by numerous researchers throughout history, constitutes a significant component of cultural heritage with its architectural, social, and spatial characteristics. This study examines the morphological and spatial changes occurring in the floor plans of Traditional Turkish Houses in Odunpazarı, Eskişehir. Aiming to address the lack of comprehensive and comparative research in the literature, the study selected a total of 30 houses, 15 from each of two distinct construction periods. The selected structures were documented using LIDAR-SLAM technology, and the data obtained were numerically interpreted using spatial syntax methods, analyzing connections, visual integration, and the number of doors. The analysis results show that the garden areas, which have a fundamental socio-spatial function, and the central sofa (living/accommodation room) layout have narrowed over time. The findings reveal that the houses in Odunpazarı have evolved from a socially oriented and holistic housing arrangement to a more compact, inward-facing, and fragmented spatial organization.

title: Impact of Atrium Design on Lighting in Shopping Malls: Prestige Mall, Istanbul
abstract: Shopping spaces, serving not only as centers of commerce but also as key areas promoting social interaction, are environments where users spend significant amounts of time. In such spaces, the limited capacity of buildings to utilize natural daylight poses challenges in terms of energy efficiency and design. To address this issue, atrium designs, which effectively bring daylight into interiors, are increasingly favored in large-scale structures like shopping malls. Atriums enhance visual comfort and reduce energy consumption by allowing natural light to penetrate deeply into interior spaces.This study analyzes the impact of the atrium design of the Prestige Mall shopping center in Istanbul on energy consumption for both natural and electric lighting, using the DIALux Evo software. In this context, variations in indoor illuminance levels during summer and winter periods were compared. The research tests the hypothesis that an efficiently designed atrium can minimize electric lighting demand and improve overall energy performance. The influence of daylight on lighting consumption during the summer period was calculated, while both daylight and electric lighting effects were evaluated during the winter period. The findings reveal that a well-designed atrium has the potential to significantly reduce energy consumption. Consequently, the study highlights the potential of atrium desi…

title: İzmir Ege Mahallesi; Kentin İçinde/Dışında Bir Mahalle
abstract: Ege Mahallesi, Roman sakinlerin kent ve barınma hakkına erişimde yaşadıkları güçlükler, sosyal dışlanma ve yoksulluk sebebiyle kentin hem içinde hem de dışında olma halinin belirsizliğiyle bir “gri alan” olarak değerlendirilebilir. Bu çalışma, Ege Mahallesi örneğinde kentsel dönüşüm süreçlerinin Roman topluluğunun kent hakkı, barınma hakkı ve sosyal adalete erişimi üzerindeki etkilerini incelemeyi ve bu etkileri mekânsal analizlerle destekleyerek tartışmayı amaçlamaktadır. Araştırma kapsamında Ege Mahallesi hakkında detaylı ikincil veri analizi, mekânsal karşılaştırmalar ve space syntax değerlendirmeleri yöntem olarak kullanılmıştır. Space syntax, fiziksel dokunun (plan kurgusu ve ara sokaklar) sosyal kullanım biçimleriyle ilişkisini görünür kılarak çalışmaya katkı sunmaktadır. Mekânsal analizler projelerin fiziksel yapı özelliklerini ortaya koymak üzere destekleyici veri sunarken, çalışmanın esas odağı bu mekânsal dönüşümlerin sosyal kullanım biçimleri ve mahalle kimliği üzerindeki etkileridir. Çalışma, Ege Mahallesi’nin kentsel dönüşüm sürecini yalnızca fiziksel yapıların dönüşümü olarak değil, aynı zamanda toplumsal ilişkilerin ve kültürel kimliklerin yeniden şekillenmesi bağlamında ele almakta; bu nedenle daha kapsayıcı ve adil kentsel stratejilerin geliştirilmesi gerekliliğini vurgulamaktadır.

title: Counter Legal Draft-KHI (CLD-KHI) and The Reform of Islamic Family Law In Indonesia: Between A Humanistic-Prophetic Paradigm And Its Political-Legal Limits
abstract: The Compilation of Islamic Law (KHI), issued through Presidential Instruction No. 1 of 1991, remains the main substantive source for Indonesian Religious Courts, yet several of its provisions conflict with contemporary standards of gender equality and human rights. The Counter Legal Draft (CLD-KHI) offered an alternative in 2004 but was never enacted. This article asks which contested KHI provisions can be reformed on Islamic grounds and why the CLD-KHI failed to become law. Using qualitative library research, it classifies provisions in eight domains of family law with Abdullah Saeed's hierarchy of values and tests how far they may be revised through Muhammad Shahrūr's ḥudūd theory. The contested rules in seven domains are implementational rather than obligatory and open to revision within God's boundaries, whereas the 2:1 inheritance ratio is the most contestable reform because its numerical share is stated in the text. The draft's failure reflects elite advocacy, weak institutional legitimacy, and the symbolic authority of classical fiqh, not conservative resistance alone. The article offers a text-sensitive framework for evaluating Islamic family law reform in Indonesia.

title: Labeling Non-Conformity in EU Consumer Protection Enforcement: A Five-Country Assessment of How Market Surveillance Results Are Reported, with a Romanian County Case
abstract: Accurate product information underpins consumer choice and the circular economy instruments of the Green Deal, yet the comparability of the evidence that national authorities publish on labeling non-conformity has rarely been examined. This study assesses publicly reported enforcement results from five EU Member States covering three levels of economic development (Romania, Germany, Poland, Croatia and Bulgaria), with a county-level case for Alba County, Romania. Each reported figure was coded by the unit inspected, denominator, product category, and design of the enforcement action. The reported values (67%, 23.9%, 19.8%, approximately 8.6%, 26.4% and 7.7 acts per 100 inspections) measure at least four different indicators and mostly come from targeted actions; expressed on a common basis, they do not support a convergent cross-country rate. None of the five data sets reported all elements of a proposed minimum reporting set (scores 1.5–3.5 of 5). The main finding is therefore that national systems report labeling non-conformity in non-comparable formats. Alba County ranked fifth of 42 county-level units by number of sanctions in 2025, but in the absence of inspection counts, no inference about enforcement intensity can be drawn. The paper proposes the reporting set and a literature-informed matrix linking non-conformity types to detection methods, and discusses, as an implica…

title: Impactos da COVID-19 no mercado de energia solar no Brasil: desafios e perspectivas para o setor fotovoltaico
abstract: The emergence of COVID-19 in late 2019 triggered an unprecedented global crisis, reaching Brazil in February 2020 and generating profound impacts not only on public health but also on the entire national economic structure. In the electricity sector, the distributed photovoltaic generation market faced significant challenges during the pandemic period from 2020 to 2022, due to its dependence on direct sales models and in-person commercial proposals, which were rendered unfeasible by isolation measures. In addition to operational difficulties, the sector dealt with the destabilization of supply chains and the high costs of imported inputs. To mitigate these negative effects, companies in the sector needed to adopt new digital marketing and relationship management strategies to ensure their survival in the market. This work analyzes the transformations that occurred during this two-year period, comparing the sector's growth before and during the pandemic crisis. The results demonstrate that, despite the initial downturn and logistical obstacles, the implementation of effective market strategies and the resilience of demand for clean energy allowed the photovoltaic sector to consolidate itself as a strategic driver in the Brazilian economic recovery.

title: МАРКЕТИНГОВА АДАПТАЦІЯ УКРАЇНСЬКИХ ІТ-КОМПАНІЙ ДО ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЙ МІЖНАРОДНОГО РИНКОВОГО СЕРЕДОВИЩА В УМОВАХ ВІЙНИ
abstract: This article examines the marketing adaptation of Ukrainian IT companies to changes in the international market environment in the context of the war. The aim of the study is to substantiate the marketing principles underpinning such adaptation, based on an analysis of changes in companies’ market behaviour between 2020 and 2026, and to systematise priority areas aimed at maintaining market stability and strengthening competitive positions in international markets. The study employs methods of comparative, structural and dynamic analysis, as well as the generalisation and systematisation of data on the export of computer services, business models, the geographical structure of export revenues and the international presence of Ukrainian technology companies. The results showed that, following a decline in computer services exports in 2023–2024, positive growth resumed in 2025, whilst data for the first half of 2026 indicate further stabilisation. A significant structural change was the growing role of hybrid service-and-product models, which combine the delivery of client projects with the development of proprietary products and technological solutions. The analysis also revealed a redistribution of the geographical structure of exports, whilst revenue remained highly concentrated in key markets, as well as a growing importance of local presence abroad. title: ТРАНСФОРМАЦІЯ РИНКУ РЕКЛАМНИХ ПОСЛУГ В ЕКОСИСТЕМІ ЕЛЕКТРОННОГО БІЗНЕСУ ПІД ВПЛИВОМ ФРАГМЕНТАЦІЇ СВІТОВОЇ ЕКОНОМІКИ ТА ІМПЕРАТИВІВ СТАЛОГО РОЗВИТКУ
abstract: The article examines the transformation of the advertising services market within the e-business ecosystem, emphasizing the contradictory influence of global economic fragmentation and sustainable development imperatives. It is shown that the digitalization of advertising, the platformization of e-business, the diffusion of algorithmic technologies and artificial intelligence are reshaping interactions among advertisers, digital platforms and e-consumers and changing the mechanisms of creating, distributing and evaluating advertising value. The study argues that the technological globalization of advertising increasingly coexists with institutional, regulatory, technological and data fragmentation of the digital environment. This combination creates a fundamentally new configuration of the global advertising market, in which the growing technological interconnectedness of market participants is accompanied by increasing differentiation of regulatory regimes, digital ecosystems and conditions for accessing consumer data. Particular attention is paid to the growing concentration of platforms and investment resources, the regional differentiation of data governance rules, and the increasing role of AI-driven advertising, retail media and programmatic technologies. It is emphasized that these processes strengthen the role of data, algorithms and digital infrastructure as strategic …

title: МЕХАНІЗМ АДАПТАЦІЇ ТОРГОВЕЛЬНОЇ ПОЛІТИКИ ДО ВИМОГ СТРУКТУРНОЇ МОДЕРНІЗАЦІЇ ВНУТРІШНЬОГО РИНКУ СПОЖИВЧИХ ТОВАРІВ І ПОСЛУГ
abstract: The article examines the structural modernization of Ukraine’s domestic market for consumer goods and services and substantiates a mechanism for adapting trade policy to its requirements. Based on the generalization of statistical data and research findings, the key structural imbalances of the domestic market are identified: consumer, spatial, sectoral-performance, and intra-industry imbalances. Their manifestations are found to be associated with the specific structure of consumer demand, uneven territorial development of trade infrastructure, a mismatch between the scale of trade activity and its contribution to value added, as well as divergent dynamics across individual trade segments. The concept of “structural modernization of the domestic market for consumer goods and services” is further developed and defined as a purposeful, managed, and consistent process of qualitative and quantitative changes in the key structural proportions of the market, aimed at gradually reducing the identified imbalances, improving the performance of trade activities, and ensuring the balanced development of individual segments of the domestic market. A mechanism for adapting trade policy to the requirements of structural modernization of the domestic market is developed. Its functional structure comprises three interrelated groups of instruments: institutional, economic, and organizational. …

title: Digitalization and Occupational Polarization in Indonesia: Evidence from the Labor Market
abstract: Rapid digitalization is reshaping labor markets, yet its effects on occupational polarization remain underexplored in emerging economies. This study investigates how internet use and digital technology adoption influence occupational outcomes across low-, middle-, and high-skilled workers in Indonesia while accounting for generational differences. Using nationally representative microdata from the 2024 Indonesian National Labor Force Survey (SAKERNAS) covering 382,920 working-age individuals, this study employs a multinomial logit model with average marginal effects to estimate occupational attainment. The results reveal a clear occupational hollowing-out pattern: digitalization reduces the likelihood of low- and middle-skilled employment while increasing the probability of high-skilled occupations. These effects are more pronounced among Millennials and Generation Z, indicating greater adaptability to digital transformation than older generations. Education, work experience, and job training further promote occupational upgrading, whereas gender disparities and spatial inequalities continue to constrain labor market opportunities. By providing micro-level evidence from an emerging economy, this study extends the literature on digitalization and occupational polarization and highlights the importance of inclusive policies that strengthen digital skills, lifelong learning, and e…

Do AI and Lexicon-Based ESG Scores Converge? Evidence from IPO Prospectuses in an Emerging Market
abstract: The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate Environmental, Social, Governance (ESG) scoring from corporate disclosures raises questions about alignment with conventional lexicon-based scores. Such alignment can be problematic as a lexicon-based approach quantifies the textual density using an ESG dictionary, while LLM-based scores are able to assess the thematic coverage of ESG themes. It remains unclear whether the two approaches produce comparable or distinct results when applied to the same corporate information. This paper examines the construct alignment between LLM-generated and lexicon-based ESG scores using 625 Indian IPO prospectuses issued between 2018 and 2024. A rebalanced dictionary of 630 terms measures disclosure intensity, while contextual scores are obtained by prompting a generative AI model. Both sets of scores are harmonised into quantile categories and compared using confusion matrices, correlation analysis, and chance-corrected agreement. The methods converge for the environmental dimension (EMR = 46.1%; weighted κ = 0.56) but diverge for social (28.2%) and governance (23.0%) disclosure, with only limited alignment overall (31.7%). The findings suggest the two approaches operationalise ESG differently, with implications for construct validity and transparency in ESG analytics.

title: Cryptocurrency volatility and market response: A GARCH-based analysis of trading volumes in financial firms
abstract: This research aims to investigate the connection between trading volume and volatility in cryptocurrency prices on leading exchanges, namely Bitfinex, Coinbase, and Kraken. It explores the application of regression and correlation analysis and whether volatility has a significant impact on trading activity, based on 60 observations. The trading volumes and price volatilities of the three exchanges showed positive correlation with each other, with coefficients of 0.6408, 0.6372, and 0.6452, respectively, and this implies that when price volatility is high, the trading volume is high on all three exchanges. Volatility on a single exchange has an impact on trading activity, but not as much as trading activity on the cryptocurrency exchange as a whole. Regression analysis also shows that volatility on each individual exchange does contribute to the overall fluctuations in trading activity. Based on the results, volatility seems to be a systemic behavior exhibited by investors and market liquidity in cryptocurrency markets. The study's conclusions help investors create risk management plans, financial institutions enhance their volatility forecasting instruments, and regulators keep an eye on the systemic risks associated with digital assets. The results emphasize the need for flexible approaches to navigating the turbulent cryptocurrency landscape.

title: Energy Consumer Model Estimation Using Machine Learning
abstract: A novel utility model of the daily electricity consumption patterns of any residential unit is proposed. The model is semi-parametric—its internal parameters are tractable to straightforward interpretations from the standpoints of microeconomics as well as game theory. The model considers fixed and shiftable loads. A modified Cobb–Douglas preference function is applied to incorporate utility tradeoffs in operating shiftable loads at different hours of the day based on the consumer’s intrinsic preference and time-of-use pricing. Model parameter estimation is formulated as a quadratic optimization problem with inequality constraints. The existence of a global optimum that is unique except under a very specific circumstance is theoretically established. A dual-gradient-ascent learning algorithm was developed to train the parameters that best fit real time-series load data. For units with single-point monitoring, an optional unsupervised learning algorithm for partial load disaggregation was developed. As a case study, the proposed model was trained with load profiles of two real-world residential units. The trained model is able to faithfully reproduce typical electricity consumption characteristics. Model interpretability was demonstrated by numerically evaluating the utility and cost functions with varying loads. These results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodo…

title: Silencing without clearing: pharmacological modulation of the SASP in aging and disease
abstract: The global rise in life expectancy has led to an increasing prevalence of age-related diseases, including neurodegenerative disorders, cancer, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and cardiovascular conditions, placing substantial societal and economic burdens on healthcare systems worldwide. A key mechanism underlying both aging and these pathologies is cellular senescence (CS), now recognized as one of the 12 hallmarks of aging. Senescent cells exert their effects largely through the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), a complex pro-inflammatory secretome that disrupts tissue homeostasis in neighbouring cells and actively promotes disease progression. This review first describes the biology of CS and the SASP in the context of aging and age-related pathologies, with emphasis on key regulatory pathways. We then provide a comprehensive overview of current senomorphic agents, i.e., compounds that modulate the SASP without eliminating senescent cells, covering their mechanisms of action, the signaling pathways they target, and the translational challenges they face. A particular focus is placed on the context-dependent dual role of the SASP. While its proinflammatory components drive tissue damage in chronic disease, SASP factors also contribute to wound healing, immune surveillance, and embryonic development. This duality has important implications for therapeutic design. Alt…

title: Clearing the way for optical mapping of the brain with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy
abstract: Abstract Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) has emerged as a powerful optical imaging technique for studying complex biological systems, particularly in neuroscience. By selectively illuminating a thin optical plane and combining it with camera-based widefield detection, LSFM enables rapid volumetric imaging with reduced photobleaching and phototoxicity compared to point-scanning approaches, such as confocal and multiphoton microscopy. Originally developed for imaging small, transparent organisms, LSFM has evolved into a versatile platform capable of probing large specimens, including whole mouse brains and human tissue samples, through the integration of advanced optical clearing techniques and sophisticated data-analysis tools. This review is focused on the optical principles underlying LSFM, the recent technological developments in light-sheet generation and system configurations, and their impact on imaging performances in highly-scattering tissues. It also discusses practical considerations related to the multiple optical clearing methodologies developed in recent decades and highlights representative applications in brain structural mapping. Finally, it outlines current challenges in data handling and imaging artifacts, and briefly considers future directions for integrating LSFM with complementary imaging modalities.

title: Seasonal Prior-Guided Dynamic Forecasting of Nonstationary Gridded PM2.5 Concentrations in China
abstract: Accurate and timely short-term forecasting of gridded PM2.5 concentrations is essential for air-quality management and public health protection, especially for the growing elderly population who are particularly vulnerable to air pollution. Advances in multi-source environmental data and deep learning have substantially improved the spatiotemporal prediction of PM2.5 concentrations. However, existing studies have mainly focused on developing increasingly sophisticated model architectures and optimization strategies while insufficiently considering the temporal nonstationarity of PM2.5 pollution and the recurrent characteristics associated with similar seasonal environmental regimes. Changes in natural environmental conditions and anthropogenic emissions can continuously alter the relationships governing PM2.5 concentrations, challenging the stability of continuous short-term forecasting; meanwhile, historically recurring seasonal pollution characteristics provide potentially valuable prior information for model adaptation. To address this problem, we propose a Seasonal Prior-guided Elastic Weight Consolidation (Seasonal EWC) framework for dynamic forecasting of nonstationary gridded PM2.5 concentrations in China. The framework derives season-specific parameter anchors and Fisher-based parameter importance from historical seasonal conditions and uses this prior knowledge to guid…

title: Short-term photovoltaic power forecasting under complex weather conditions using optimized signal decomposition and attention-based learning
abstract: Abstract Photovoltaic (PV) power sequences exhibit significant intermittency and strong non-stationarity under complex weather conditions, particularly during rapid cloud movements that intensify short-term fluctuations, posing substantial challenges for short-term forecasting. To address this, this study proposes a hybrid deep learning forecasting model. First, the Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) is employed to adaptively optimize key parameters of Variational Modal Decomposition (VMD), enabling the decomposition of the original power sequences into sub-modes with distinct frequency characteristics. Subsequently, a hybrid forecasting architecture is constructed by serially integrating a Temporal Convolutional Network with an Efficient Channel Attention (TCN-ECA) mechanism and a lightweight Transformer, enabling collaborative modeling of local high-frequency fluctuations and global long-term dependencies. Experimental results from the DKASC photovoltaic power station in Australia demonstrate that the proposed method reduces RMSE and MAE by 31.8% and 21.6%, respectively, compared to suboptimal models on an annual basis. It maintains high prediction accuracy even under cloudy conditions and during summer periods with strong meteorological fluctuations. Further integration with a physically constrained weather classification method based on the clear-sky index and scattering fracti…

title: Pork Price Fluctuations in China: Epidemic Associations, Storage and Release Operations, and Forecasting
abstract: Pork remains a cornerstone of many food systems, and fluctuations in its price are a critical concern for the economic sustainability of agricultural supply chains. This study connects epidemic associations, reserve-operation case studies and forecasting to examine pork price fluctuations in China using average retail prices in 36 major cities. Linear and nonlinear regressions examine epidemic conditions, while reserve cases compare price changes and pig-to-grain ratios. Chronological out-of-sample forecasts compare seven models at one-, three- and six-week horizons, with ordinary least squares as the principal benchmark. Direct-price and cumulative-change approaches are evaluated on the original price scale. The epidemic index exhibits a nonlinear association in the five-knot specification with year controls despite limited linear explanatory power. Reserve episodes show differing adjustment paths, and higher pig-to-grain ratios are not consistently accompanied by lower dispersion. Univariate autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) achieves the lowest root mean squared error in most comparisons, while market indicators improve selected forecasts. Support vector regression using price history and slaughter profits under the cumulative-change approach yields the lowest three-week errors among the evaluated main-sample configurations. These findings inform market monitor…

title: Forecasting a Democratic Resurgence? Partisan Accountability in the 2026 U.S. Midterm Elections
The Strategy of Decentralization
abstract: The enactment of the Electricity Act 2023 represents a transformative shift in Nigeria's electricity governance, transitioning from a centralized federal system to a decentralized, multi-tiered electricity market. This research examines the strategic implications of electricity sector decentralization on regional development in Nigeria, analyzing constitutional and legislative foundations, implementation progress, and developmental outcomes across states. Through qualitative analysis of policy documents, regulatory frameworks, and implementation data from pioneering states including Enugu, Ekiti, Ondo, Edo, Imo, and Oyo, the study reveals that decentralization has created unprecedented opportunities for state-driven innovation, private sector participation, and renewable energy integration. Key challenges include regulatory coordination complexities, infrastructural constraints, capacity gaps, and the risk of market fragmentation. Successful implementation requires robust intergovernmental coordination mechanisms, substantial capital investment in transmission infrastructure, comprehensive capacity building for state regulatory institutions, and harmonized frameworks balancing state autonomy with national grid stability.

title: Advances in Predictive Financial Risk Assessment Using Python- Based Forecasting Systems
abstract: Predictive financial risk assessment has evolved significantly with the adoption of programmingbased forecasting systems, particularly those leveraging Python. This study examines the advances in financial risk modeling, focusing on Python-based tools and techniques that enhance predictive accuracy, operational efficiency, and decision-making in financial institutions. Using a comprehensive literature review and analysis of existing forecasting frameworks, the paper identifies key algorithms, system architectures, and data processing methodologies. The study further explores challenges, best practices, and the impact of Python’s versatility in integrating machine learning, statistical modeling, and visualization for financial risk assessment. The findings provide practical insights for financial analysts, risk managers, and policymakers seeking to implement predictive systems.

From Linear Regression to Temporal Fusion Transformers: Benchmarking Electricity Price Forecasting Models in Markets with Different Renewable Energy Shares
abstract: Rising renewable penetration increases wholesale price volatility and challenges traditional forecasting approaches. This paper benchmarks three methods—adaptive linear regression, Random Forest (RF), and the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)—on hourly day-ahead prices in four European markets with contrasting generation mixes: Slovakia (nuclear-dominated), Spain (solar-rich), Denmark (wind-dominated), and Germany (mixed). Using Energy-Charts data for 2015–2025, all the models are evaluated under one day-ahead protocol on a common 12-month hold-out against naive 24-h persistence. With price-history features, the RF significantly outperforms persistence in three of four markets. A single cross-market five-seed TFT ensemble attains the lowest MAE everywhere, cutting the persistence error by 55.6% in Germany (to 12.88 €/MWh) and 21.7% in Slovakia. The improvement is generally larger in markets with higher variable-renewable penetration, though not strictly monotonic. Replacing the realized fundamentals with TSO day-ahead forecasts changes the MAE by at most 0.22 €/MWh: the day-ahead price is itself formed from those forecasts. Multivariate Diebold–Mariano tests confirm both advantages everywhere on absolute errors. Quantile averaging yields pinball losses of 3.87–6.53 €/MWh, but the 80% intervals cover only 71–78%. Variable importance ties the leading driver to each mix: wind in D…

title: Waste to Electricity Generation
abstract: The increasing generation of solid waste has created significant challenges related to waste disposal, environmental pollution and energy demand. Waste-to-energy technology provides an approach in which the thermal energy available from combustible waste can be converted into useful electrical energy. This paper presents the design and development of a small-scale waste-to-electricity prototype based on thermal energy recovery. The proposed system consists of a waste-burning chamber, heat-collecting element, electrical conversion circuit, diode, capacitor, battery-storage unit, heat-sensing element and LED load. When suitable waste material is heated inside the combustion chamber, the resulting thermal energy is transferred to the heat conversion element. The generated electrical output is conditioned through the electronic circuit and stored in a rechargeable battery. The stored energy can subsequently be supplied to a low-power LED load. A sensing arrangement is incorporated to control the output according to the availability of generated energy. The prototype demonstrates the basic principle of recovering useful electrical energy from waste heat at a small scale. The work also highlights the importance of waste segregation, controlled combustion and appropriate pollution-control measures for practical implementation. The proposed concept can serve as an educational and exper…

Does Electricity Marketization Reform Promote Green Electricity Generation? A Quasi-Natural Experiment of China’s Electricity Spot Market Pilot
abstract: Persistent supply–demand mismatches pose major obstacles to deploying green electricity. As a critical marketization reform instrument, the electricity spot market (ESM) is expected to optimize power resource allocation. This paper examines whether ESM pilots contribute to the growth of green electricity generation, and further tests their moderating role in the relationships between urbanization, industrial structure, and green electricity generation. To this end, we treat the ESM pilot as a quasi-natural experiment and employ a difference-in-differences (DID) model to empirically assess the impact of the ESM on green electricity generation, using provincial data from 1998 to 2021. The results show that establishing the ESM significantly promotes green electricity generation. This positive impact remains robust across a series of robustness checks, including parallel trend tests, alternative regression approaches, variable re-measurement, and placebo tests. Further mechanism analysis confirms that the ESM enhances green electricity generation by reducing government intervention and reshaping the energy consumption structure. Additionally, our analysis of moderating effects reveals that the ESM helps mitigate the negative impacts of urbanization and the expansion of secondary industries. These findings provide empirical implications for emerging and developing economies on usin…

title: Phase Spirals across Galactic Disks. II. Using Large-scale “Macrospirals” in Phase-spiral Amplitude to Derive Perturbation Times
abstract: Abstract Phase-space spirals in the Milky Way disk are a key observable remnant of recent perturbations to the Galaxy. They provide insight into the disk’s potential, dynamical evolution, past interactions, and even substructure. However, the complex dynamics of phase-spiral formation and evolution have made clear interpretations challenging. For example, recent work has shown that the “winding time”—measured from how tightly wound a phase spiral is—is a biased estimate of the true time since the inciting perturbation due to the complex effects of self-gravity. In this paper series, we present an alternative approach by looking at correlations in phase-spiral morphology across galactic disks. Here, we show that following a localized perturbative event, the ridge line connecting the largest amplitude phase spiral at each radius winds up into a “macrospiral” at the rate expected for differential rotation. This means the macrospiral can (1) be unwound to constrain the origin—time and location—of correlated phase-spiral properties and (2) indicate the delay in individual phase-spiral winding as a novel diagnostic of disk dynamical properties. Applying these ideas to the Milky Way’s phase spirals, we estimate a perturbation time of ≃1 Gyr ago, consistent with the penultimate passage of the Sagittarius dwarf galaxy through the disk, and delay times of up to 800 Myr for phase spirals …

title: Numerical Investigation of Crack Driving Force and Ultimate Bearing Capacity of D1,422 mm X80 Pipelines with Composite Groove Girth Weld
abstract: Existing prediction models for the ultimate bearing capacity of circumferential welds are primarily limited to manual or combined automatic welding with single V-grooves, failing to address full-automatic welding with composite grooves, and that is a critical technical gap for large-diameter, thick-walled X80 steel pipelines using automatic welding processes. To fill this gap, this study focused on cracked circumferential welds with composite grooves in full-automatic welded X80 pipelines, establishing a nonlinear finite element model that accurately accounts for the composite groove’s geometric characteristics, three material zones, and canoe-type crack simulation. Spider-web mesh refinement was applied at crack tips to ensure precision, and the model was validated using full-scale wide-plate tensile tests. Using J-integral as the crack driving force parameter, this study systematically analyzed the effects of nine key factors: load parameters, material properties, geometric parameters, and crack dimensions. The results revealed that residual stress had negligible impact on bearing capacity, while internal pressure (0→12 MPa) reduced capacity by 44.726%, misalignment (0→3 mm) by 52.982%, and crack depth (1→3 mm) by 47.451%. abstract: The article develops conceptual foundations for forming a tactical planning mechanism for corporate social responsibility (CSR) under the transformation of the external environment. The research problem arises from the gap between long-term sustainability strategies and the daily implementation of social, environmental and ethical commitments. Rapid regulatory changes, economic volatility, technological renewal, labour-market shifts, climate risks, security threats and growing stakeholder expectations require enterprises to revise CSR priorities more frequently and to connect them with budgets, responsibilities and measurable outcomes. The purpose of the study is to design a management mechanism that translates strategic CSR goals into coordinated actions for a three-to-twelve-month planning horizon. Systems, process, stakeholder and portfolio approaches are used. The proposed mechanism is organised as a recurring cycle that includes monitoring of the external environment, updating the stakeholder map, identifying material issues, setting tactical priorities, forming a balanced portfolio of CSR initiatives, allocating resources and responsibility, implementation, communication, control and corrective managerial learning. Tactical initiatives are divided into four groups: mandatory compliance measures, risk-reduction measures, stakeholder-value projects and development-oriented …

title: Insecticidal Activity and Mechanism of 7-Methylcoumarin Against Diaphorina citri Reveal the Role of Chemosensory Genes in Defense Response
abstract: The Asian citrus psyllid (Diaphorina citri) is a major vector of Huanglongbing (HLB), a devastating citrus disease worldwide. In addition to vectoring HLB, D. citri is a significant economic pest in its own right, causing direct damage to citrus by feeding on tender shoots, leading to leaf distortion, shoot dieback, and sooty mold infestation. Chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing D. citri populations, but heavy reliance on insecticides has led to insecticide resistance. Coumarin and its derivatives, as a natural product, are widely recognized for their insecticidal activities against various agricultural pests. In this study, the insecticidal activity of 11 coumarin compounds against D. citri nymphs was evaluated by bioassay, among which 7-methylcoumarin exhibited the most substantial efficacy. Moreover, the insecticidal mechanism of 7-methylcoumarin was assessed by a comparative transcriptome analysis, and 294 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, including 165 up-regulated and 129 down-regulated genes. GO enrichment analysis showed that DEGs were mainly involved in extracellular region/space, (chitin-based) cuticle development, and structural constituent of (chitin-based) cuticle terms, especially down-regulated genes related to cuticle proteins, chemosensory proteins and odorant-binding proteins, which were further verified by qPCR. Amo…

title: Topological Reconfiguration in Sheared Granular Assemblies: Non-Dissipative Mechanism and Its Irreversible Characteristics
abstract: Granular materials exhibit pronounced macroscopic irreversible deformations during shearing, which mainly contributes to frictional sliding dissipation in the conventional thermodynamic frameworks. This study aims to investigate the non-dissipative microscopic mechanisms governing macroscopic irreversibility of granular materials. Using DEM, a series of biaxial shear and reverse loading simulations are conducted on dense granular assemblies with different friction coefficients. The results show that continuous topological reconfiguration occurs through the transformation from lower-order to higher-order meso-loops, eventually reaching a statistical steady state at the critical state. Accompanying this topological evolution, elastic energy at contact level is continuously stored and released, providing a persistent non-dissipative energy exchange that sustains continuous shear alongside primary frictional dissipation. Based on the reverse loading analysis, topological reconfiguration is intrinsically irrecoverable, causing part of the free energy to remain locked within the reconfigured contact network as irrecoverable free energy. Meanwhile, another portion of the recoverable free energy is irreversibly dissipated through friction during unloading. Together, these two components constitute the irreversible free energy. The evolution of irreversible free energy with interparticl…

title: A Quantum Mechanism-Centered Review of Carbon Dot-Based Theranostics
abstract: Despite advances in drug discovery, effective delivery and precise imaging still pose significant obstacles. Scientists have turned to zero-dimensional nanomaterials like carbon dots (CDs) to enable precision drug delivery. Due to their multidisciplinary appeal, there is extensive research on both the physical properties and biological applications of CDs, yet the fields rarely complement each other. This review applies a quantum-mechanistic framework to better understand CDs and unify the relationship between electronic structure, photophysical behavior, and theranostic performance. We first highlight the theranostic advantages of CDs over quantum dots, then discuss the quantum mechanisms behind a CD’s imaging capabilities, including surface states, excitation-dependent photoluminescence, and the electronic origins of photostability. Through this physical lens, we then evaluate the effect of different precursors and doping strategies during synthesis on electronic structure and how dots are engineered to load, release, and track therapeutic cargo. Photodynamic therapy and surface functionalization strategies are also evaluated. Finally, we address the significance of renal clearance and translational bottlenecks such as heterogeneity.

title: Thermal Oxidation Increases Dissolved Carbon Leaching through Altered Microplastic Structural Chemistry and Accelerated Release Kinetics
abstract: Abstract We assessed the leaching potential of dissolved carbon (DC) from polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) microplastics (MPs), selected for their differing polymeric structure and response to thermal oxidation. Although thermal oxidation alters the chemical structure and reactivity of MPs, the mechanisms influencing DC leaching remain poorly understood. We quantified physicochemical changes resulting from thermal oxidation at 100 and 250 °C followed by leachate kinetic modeling. Thermal oxidation decreased chlorine (Cl) concentration by 96% in PVC, increased carbonyl index from 0.397 to 0.504 in PET, and increased oxidation index from 0.151 to 0.506 in PVC. No significant DC leaching occurred in PET; however, leaching increased 15-fold in PVC 250 °C compared to nonoxidized PVC. Leaching kinetics for all PVC oxidation conditions were best fit to the biphasic model, although goodness of fit decreased with thermal oxidation, with adjusted R2 values decreasing from 0.95 in nonoxidized PVC to 0.85 to 0.82 in PVC exposed to 100 and 250 °C, respectively. These findings highlight the distinct chemical fingerprint and unique leaching behavior of thermally oxidized MPs, providing new insights about their release of DC at burn sites or following wildland-urban interface fire events.

One major components of the state revenue was derived from the appropriation of taxes that was compulsorily contributions levied on individuals or corporations by the state government. The necessity for taxation emanateds from the need for government to provide for financial sustainability within its system. Now the tax to GDP ratio had remained very very low. The objective of the study was to examine the effect of Non-PAYE tax revenue on Fiscal sustainability of all states in Nigeria. Data were collected through secondary sources obtained from the Public Finance Database of the Nigeria Governors Forum (NGF), annual fiscal reports published by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), Joint Tax revenue generation through taxation and allocations received from the federation account. The data were analysed using the panel regression technique. Finding revealed that Non-PAYE tax revenue had no significant effect on the fiscal sustainability of states in Nigeria. In conclusion, the potential challenges in the collection and management of other forms of taxation, such as taxes on goods and services, property taxes, or business taxes might be the reason for such a situation. title: Study on marketing dynamics on sales of electric vehicles and SWOT analysis
Enhanced Electron Charging Induces Positive Aging of QD-LEDs: An Electrically Excited Transient Absorption Study
abstract: Abstract Quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QD-LEDs) require encapsulation to extend their storage and operational lifetime. However, acidic encapsulants commonly used usually induce an anomalous positive aging phenomenon─the device performance improves rather than decreases in the initial days. These uncontrollable gains hinder the commercialization of QD-LEDs, yet no study to date has directly probed the in situ evolution of charge carriers during this process. Here, we employ electrically excited transient absorption (EETA) spectroscopy to investigate how encapsulants influence charge carrier dynamics in QD-LEDs. Taking red QD-LEDs as a model system, we demonstrate that positive aging is accompanied by enhanced electron charging in the quantum dot (QD) layer and accelerated electron injection into the emissive layer. Furthermore, we show that acid-induced progressive passivation of surface defects on ZnMgO nanoparticles improves electron injection efficiency. This work reveals that enhanced electron charging induces positive aging in QD-LEDs.

title: EfaSim - A Prototype for a SUMO-Driven Emergency Vehicle Driving Simulator
abstract: EfaSim (German: "Einsatzfahrt-Simulator", English: "Emergency Driving Simulator") is a prototype for an emergency vehicle driving simulator which uses the microscopic traffic simulation SUMO (Simulation of Urban Mobility) to simulate the behavior of other traffic participants. Unreal Engine provides rendering power to visualize the environment, traffic, and the user interface. In the game engine, the user steers an emergency vehicle equipped with a toggleable blue light. This device influences the reaction of the other vehicles to the emergency vehicle within the designated radius. Communication between Unreal and Sumo is established using a dynamic linked library and the C++ implementation, Libsumo. Our goal is to create an efficient prototype that can simulate and render the game environment with a large number of simultaneously active vehicles while achieving an optimal frame rate of 60 frames per second (fps). In addition, we use a completely free-to-use pipeline for creating the environment and running the simulation. We benchmark our implementation to test its efficiency and further compare our implementation with an additional TraCI implementation. The results show that both simulations operate on similar fps; however, the DLL achieves a measurable increase in information flow efficiency. We conclude that our architecture performs satisfactorily for our requirements, bei…

title: Scalable Gaussian Process for Learning Non‐Ergodic Ground Motion Model From Physics‐Based Simulations With Application to Power Infrastructure Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents the development and application of a scalable non‐ergodic ground motion model (NGMM) for the Los Angeles area. The NGMM is trained and validated on physics‐based simulated ground‐motion data from a recent Statewide California Earthquake Center (SCEC) CyberShake study. The NGMM is formulated as a Gaussian Process (GP) regression model, where the prior median is defined as the ASK14 ergodic ground‐motion model and the posterior median is obtained by learning the non‐ergodic effects embedded in the training data. These non‐ergodic effects include systematic site and path effects, which are represented in the GP using Matérn and specialized covariance kernels that explicitly characterize path vectors. Implementing the NGMM requires hyperparameter tuning and inference on large datasets (on the order of one million data points or more), posing significant computational challenges for conventional GP approaches. To address this scalability issue, this paper presents a suite of computational strategies, including sparse Cholesky inversion, parallel computing, and GPU acceleration. Despite these advances, the full CyberShake dataset (on the order of hundreds of millions of data points) remains computationally prohibitive. Therefore, the aleatory variability introduced by the stochastic rupture generator is modeled separately using a mixed‐effects formulation…

title: Non-Orthogonal DF Relaying for SWIPT over Fading Channels with Power Adaptation
abstract: This paper investigates two-phase non-orthogonal decode-and-forward (DF) relaying for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) over fading channels. The source transmits in both phases, while the relay forwards the decoded information in the second phase and the destination employs power splitting in both phases. We jointly optimize the source-power allocation between the two phases and the power-splitting ratios to maximize the ergodic end-to-end achievable rate subject to a minimum average harvested-energy requirement. By exploiting the time-sharing property, the original nonconvex problem is solved using Lagrangian duality. Numerical results under Rayleigh fading show that the proposed adaptive scheme achieves a higher ergodic achievable rate and supports a wider range of feasible harvested-energy requirements than a conventional scheme employing a fixed power-splitting ratio, with the performance advantage becoming more pronounced under stringent harvested-energy requirements.

title: Putting place first: towards a new vision for UK industrial strategy
Modular soft robot docking strategy and reliability
abstract: Modular soft robots rely on reliable docking to achieve configuration reorganization and task switching, but the stability of flexible interfaces is affected by posture, load, and environmental conditions. This article compares four types of autonomous docking strategies: magnetic coupling, fluid interlocking, microstructure adhesion or electro adsorption, and shape memory locking. It analyzes their alignment tolerance, locking and releasing, cyclic use, and system synergy conditions. Comparison shows that various interfaces have trade-offs between initial tolerance, load-bearing capacity, release capability, and environmental adaptability, and cannot be simply compared without considering module size, load direction, and cycling conditions. Pose errors, material fatigue, state confirmation, and fault recovery in unstructured environments still affect system reliability. Subsequent research should report the success rate of docking, load-bearing capacity, release performance, and cycling results under clear experimental conditions. The review also discusses the requirements for autonomous alignment, connection-state sensing, multi-module coordination, and safe recovery mechanisms needed to support repeatable reconfiguration under realistic operating conditions.

title: From Linear Regression to Temporal Fusion Transformers: Benchmarking Electricity Price Forecasting Models in Markets with Different Renewable Energy Shares
abstract: Rising renewable penetration increases wholesale price volatility and challenges traditional forecasting approaches. This paper benchmarks three methods—adaptive linear regression, Random Forest (RF), and the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT)—on hourly day-ahead prices in four European markets with contrasting generation mixes: Slovakia (nuclear-dominated), Spain (solar-rich), Denmark (wind-dominated), and Germany (mixed). Using Energy-Charts data for 2015–2025, all the models are evaluated under one day-ahead protocol on a common 12-month hold-out against naive 24-h persistence. With price-history features, the RF significantly outperforms persistence in three of four markets. A single cross-market five-seed TFT ensemble attains the lowest MAE everywhere, cutting the persistence error by 55.6% in Germany (to 12.88 €/MWh) and 21.7% in Slovakia. The improvement is generally larger in markets with higher variable-renewable penetration, though not strictly monotonic. Replacing the realized fundamentals with TSO day-ahead forecasts changes the MAE by at most 0.22 €/MWh: the day-ahead price is itself formed from those forecasts. Multivariate Diebold–Mariano tests confirm both advantages everywhere on absolute errors. Quantile averaging yields pinball losses of 3.87–6.53 €/MWh, but the 80% intervals cover only 71–78%. title: AI-Enabled Interoperability in Intelligent Digital Systems: A Socio-Technical Framework for Secure, Scalable, and Privacy-Preserving Integration
abstract: The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), biometric recognition, intelligent transportation systems, distributed energy platforms, and connected vehicles has resulted in increasingly heterogeneous digital infrastructures. Although these systems generate substantial quantities of data and provide sophisticated analytical capabilities, their effectiveness is frequently constrained by fragmented architectures, incompatible data representations, isolated databases, security vulnerabilities, and inadequate mechanisms for trusted information exchange. Interoperability has therefore emerged as a fundamental requirement for the development of intelligent digital ecosystems. However, interoperability cannot be treated exclusively as a technical problem because data integration also involves organizational, semantic, institutional, privacy, security, and governance considerations. This paper investigates the relationship between AI and interoperability and develops a conceptual socio-technical framework for integrating heterogeneous intelligent systems. The study synthesizes research concerning machine-learning-based face recognition, electronic toll collection, peer-to-peer energy trading, human-bot discrimination, federated intrusion detection, low-code/no-code intelligent automation, and secure computing. title: A Two-way Interactive Secure Communication Model for Electric Energy Metering Data
abstract: INTRODUCTION: As power market reforms deepen, traditional unidirectional protocols (e.g., IEC 102) fail to meet the secure, real-time, and bidirectional data exchange requirements of modern power grids, leaving systems vulnerable to eavesdropping and tampering.OBJECTIVES: To ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and reliability of power data transmission by overcoming the pattern leakage vulnerabilities of traditional encryption, while satisfying the strict real-time and high-frequency demands of large-scale power systems.METHODS: Two schemes are designed: a pure SM4 symmetric encryption scheme for high-frequency data, and an SM2-SM4 hybrid scheme for advanced authentication. To enhance security, a novel ECB-CBC hybrid encryption mode is introduced for SM4. RESULTS: The proposed ECB-CBC hybrid mode effectively eliminates plaintext redundancy. Its Shannon entropy stabilizes at ~7.99 bits/byte (nearly touching the 8.0 theoretical ideal, vastly improving upon standard ECB's ~3.5 bits/byte). It also achieves an optimal inter-block avalanche effect of ~64 bits per block. The SM2-SM4 hybrid scheme's encryption time is only 15%-20% higher than that of pure SM4. Across 1-16 thread tests, the throughput of both SM4-based schemes grows linearly, outperforming RSA and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) by several orders of magnitude.CONCLUSION: The proposed ECB-CBC hybrid architecture ov…

title: “Migrant labour regimes and the regulation of temporary labour migration in Europe”
abstract: This special issue develops the concept of “migrant labour regime” (MLRs), to analyse the regulatory infrastructure of labour migration. MLRs involve complex networks of actors, institutions, norms, and expectations, that facilitate migration, and regulate the labour processes in migrants’ workplaces, and migrants’ interactions with labour markets. MLRs arise out of employers’ demands and employer requirements for control of the labour process in specific production activities. Other actors, such as migrants, unions, and the state shape them at various points. MLRs are influenced by employer efforts to avoid norms, regulations and institutions of worker protection. The empirical contributions to this special issue analyse particular MLRs, teasing out their characteristics, which are focused on placing migrants at a labour market disadvantaged vis-a-vis employers and other workers. These include the presence of labour market intermediaries, dualized labour markets, restrictive status regimes, sector specificity, expansive dynamics, limited state capacity for enforcement, and an emphasis on social isolation of migrants. Both eastern and western European countries receive migrant labour through MLRs, although each MLR's characteristics are specific to its context.

title: AgroNLP-SimAssist: a multilingual transformer-based decision support simulator for crop disease diagnosis, advisory generation, and market intelligence
abstract: Abstract There are three major shortcomings of agricultural NLP and need addressing, regardless of the recent developments in the field: (i) use of proprietary or small-scale datasets that affect reproducibility; (ii) one-task models that only focus on intent recognition but lack integration for crop disease diagnosis, advice, and market information; and (iii) the absence of simulators for evaluating the system’s performance during actual deployment. The application of precision agriculture is constrained by limitations in diverse farming environments. The study introduces AgroNLP-SimAssist, which represents a unified multilingual transformer architecture augmented by an easily deployable agricultural decision support simulator, as the proposed solution to overcome the challenges. The five major components constituting the proposed framework are: (1) domain-specific multilingual transformer embedding; (2) data collection and cleaning from publicly available agricultural datasets; (3) multiple prediction tasks including trend price estimation, crop disease detection, and advisory recommendation; (4) SHAP value explainability for expert validation; and (5) advisory simulation engine for evaluating latency and scalability. Factors associated with health service utilisation in rural Victoria: a multilevel analysis informed by Andersen’s behavioral model
abstract: Abstract Background Access to health services in rural areas can be hampered by a variety of factors contributing to reduced utilisation and poorer health outcomes. Andersen’s behavioral model was developed to understand how people utilise health services by assessing associations with predisposing factors, needs factors and enabling factors. The aims of this study were to determine the relative contribution of these factors to utilisation of general practice, medical specialists and dental services in a rural area and also to identify the nature of barriers to health service access. Methods A cross-sectional survey design was used. Households were randomly selected from local government lists. Respondents were asked about their health, use of health services, barriers to health service access and demographic details by trained research assistants. Multilevel regression analysis informed by the Andersen model was used to identify factors associated with health service utilisation, and impact of access barriers on utilisation as per Yeatt’s expansion. Results Household respondents ( n = 2680) provided data about their health and service utilisation. General practice utilisation was lower for males than females (OR 0.57 [0.40, 0.8]). title: Dampak E-Service Quality Terhadap Kepuasan dan Loyalitas Nasabah pada Bank Negara Indonesia Cabang Sengkang
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh e-service quality terhadap kepuasan dan loyalitas nasabah pada Bank Negara Indonesia Cabang Sengkang, serta menguji peran kepuasan nasabah sebagai variabel intervening. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data yang dikumpulkan dari 96 responden, yaitu nasabah yang menggunakan layanan digital banking. Data dianalisis menggunakan analisis jalur (path analysis) dan uji Sobel untuk menguji efek mediasi. Hasil uji instrumen menunjukkan bahwa seluruh item pernyataan valid dan reliabel, serta model regresi memenuhi asumsi klasik. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa e-service quality berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap kepuasan nasabah (β = 0,677; p = 0,000) dan terhadap loyalitas nasabah (β = 0,223; p = 0,018). Kepuasan nasabah juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap loyalitas nasabah (β = 0,585; p = 0,000). Selain itu, kepuasan nasabah terbukti memediasi pengaruh e-service quality terhadap loyalitas nasabah, dengan pengaruh tidak langsung sebesar 39,6%, lebih besar daripada pengaruh langsungnya sebesar 22,3% (uji Sobel = 4,379; p = 0,000). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa peningkatan kualitas layanan elektronik yang cepat, aman, dan mudah digunakan perlu diikuti dengan upaya menciptakan kepuasan nasabah, karena kepuasan merupakan jalur utama dalam membentuk loyalitas

title: Assessing E-Governance Service Responsiveness and Challenges in Khulna City Corporation: Insights from Service Providers and Citizens
abstract: Effective e-governance is essential to providing citizens with accessible, timely, transparent, and citizen-focused public services, little empirical research exists on service providers' and citizens' experiences with municipal digital services in Bangladesh. This study examines responsiveness, effectiveness, and implementation challenges in e-governance services in Khulna City Corporation, considering institutional perceptions and citizens' actual service experiences. The survey included 425 purposively selected respondents, 400 service recipients and 25 e-governance service providers, and used a quantitative cross-sectional design. The data have been analyzed using frequencies, percentages, mean scores, Spearman rank correlation, chi-square tests, and Kruskal–Wallis tests. The results show a gap between providers' positive perceptions and citizens' experiences. 88% of providers rated the response as good, 66% of citizens reported slow service, 57.8% rated the response speed as slow or very slow, and 55.3% reported technical problems. However, 82.5% said e-governance enhanced access to government information, and 64.5% said they were willing to recommend e-governance services. Perceived response speed, timely updates, and information clarity were highly correlated with citizen satisfaction, while service delay was significantly correlated with intention to recommend. title: Changes in higher vocational nursing programme sites in China and their alignment with regional health service demand: implications for nursing workforce planning
abstract: Abstract Background To explore the changes in higher vocational nursing programme sites in China in 2013–2025 and analyze their distribution between regional health service demand, to provide evidence on optimizing the layout of nursing vocational education and to provide information for nursing workforce planning. Methods Data of the higher vocational nursing programme sites in each province-level region in China between 2013 and 2025 were retrieved from publicly available information from the National Platform for Vocational College Specialty Setting Management and Public Information Services and other official sources. These data were merged with official 2024 data on the population of the country, population of 65 years old and above, and the regional gross domestic product to describe the changes at the national, regional, and provincial levels of the country of the programme sites. To create a regional health service demand index and relative higher vocational nursing education supply index, indicators of regional health service demand and relative higher vocational nursing education supply were standardized. The relative supply index was operationalised as the population-adjusted number of programme sites. Demand–supply alignment was then evaluated by quadrant analysis across provinces, and sensitivity analysis was performed to investigate the stability of results. Resul…

title: AcWRKY75 and AcMYB108 mediated ABA-GA antagonism in the regulation of pineapple internal browning
abstract: Abstract Gibberellic acid (GA) and abscisic acid (ABA) antagonistically regulate various biological processes, but whether they antagonistically regulate tissue browning remains unclear. Here, we showed that ABA reduced pineapple internal browning (IB) by inhibiting phenolic biosynthesis via downregulating AcWRKY75 and AcMYB108, while GA 3 had the opposite effects. Biochemical evidences showed AcWRKY75 and AcMYB108 directly bound to and activated the phenolic biosynthetic gene Ac4CL5 . Interestingly, AcMYB108 directly bound to AcWRKY75 promoter and activated its transcription, indicating that AcMYB108 functions upstream of AcWRKY75. Arabidopsis overexpressing AcWRKY75 , AcMYB108 or Ac4CL5 displayed promoted phenolic biosynthesis. AcWRKY75 transient overexpression in pineapple reduced, while its transient silencing enhanced IB and phenolic accumulation. Transcriptomic profiling of pineapples transiently overexpressing and silencing AcWRKY75 revealed that plant hormone signal transduction and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis were among the most significantly enriched KEGG pathways, suggesting the role of AcWRKY75 in regulating phenolic biosynthesis involves plant hormones. ABA suppressed and GA 3 enhanced enzyme activity of GUS transiently expressed in tobacco driven by promoter of AcWRKY75 , AcMYB108 or Ac4CL5 . Legal Regulation of Homoeopathy in India: A Critical Analysis of the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020
abstract: Homoeopathy is one of the most widely practised systems of traditional medicine in India and plays an important role within the AYUSH healthcare framework. The enactment of the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020 marked a significant shift from the earlier regulatory regime under the Homoeopathy Central Council Act, 1973 by introducing a governance model focused on transparency, accountability, quality medical education and professional ethics. India currently has more than three lakh registered homoeopathic practitioners and hundreds of recognised teaching institutions, which highlights the need for an effective and uniform regulatory framework. This paper critically examines the legal framework established under the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, analyses its institutional mechanisms governing education, registration, ethics and professional standards, and evaluates the reforms introduced to strengthen homoeopathic regulation in India. The study adopts a doctrinal research methodology based on an analytical examination of the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, relevant rules and regulations, constitutional provisions, parliamentary materials, judicial decisions, government reports and scholarly literature. The paper analyses the evolution of homoeopathy regulation in India, the establishment and functions of the National Commission, the r…

title: Psychological resilience and the athlete mental health continuum: serial indirect associations through emotion regulation and sport anxiety
abstract: Abstract Background Psychological resilience has been consistently associated with athletes’ mental health and psychological well-being. However, the emotional and anxiety-related processes involved in the association between psychological resilience and the Athlete Mental Health Continuum remain insufficiently understood. Emotion regulation and sport anxiety may represent interrelated psychological variables associated with this relationship in competitive sport settings. Objective This study aimed to examine the associations among psychological resilience, emotion regulation, sport anxiety, and the Athlete Mental Health Continuum and to evaluate a theory-informed serial indirect-association model involving emotion regulation and sport anxiety. Methods A cross-sectional research design was employed. The study included 850 athletes actively engaged in individual and team sports in Türkiye. Data were collected using the Psychological Resilience Scale, Emotion Regulation Scale, Sport Anxiety Scale, and Athlete Mental Health Continuum Scale. A serial mediation analysis was conducted using the PROCESS Macro Model 6 with 5,000 bootstrap resamples. Because the data were cross-sectional, the model was interpreted as a theory-informed pattern of direct and indirect associations rather than evidence of temporal or causal relationships. Prediction of early radiological response in esophageal cancer using CT radiomics and clinical factors: a single-center proof-of-concept study in an elderly cohort
abstract: Abstract Background To develop, as a proof-of-concept analysis, a machine learning model predicting early radiological treatment response in an elderly, single-center esophageal cancer (EC) cohort, and to test whether adding clinical factors to CT radiomics improves prediction. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 189 patients with EC treated with definitive radiotherapy. Radiomic features were extracted from baseline contrast-enhanced CT. Following TRIPOD recommendations, a LASSO-penalized logistic regression (LASSO-LR) on the radiomic feature set was pre-specified as the primary model, with the number of predictors capped at five (events per variable [EPV] ≥ 10; 50 events). Performance was estimated by 5 × 5 nested cross-validation and in an independent test set (8:2 split; 151 training, 38 test), with out-of-fold calibration; a sensitivity analysis repeating the full pipeline within each outer fold and a 200-resample feature-stability analysis were also performed. Five classifiers across clinical-only, radiomics-only and multimodal feature sets, including support vector machines (SVM), were exploratory comparisons only; incremental value was tested by bootstrap paired comparison (5,000 resamples). title: From perception to practice: Faculty-led assessment redesign in response to generative AI in higher education
abstract: The rapid diffusion of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT into higher education has unsettled long standing assumptions about the validity, reliability, and authenticity of conventional assessment methods. Existing research has predominantly examined perceptions, ethical concerns, and technology acceptance, leaving the actual pedagogical redesign work of faculty, and its relationship to established principles of assessment quality, comparatively underexplored. Drawing on constructive alignment theory, this study examines how faculty are reshaping assessment design under conditions of AI disruption and whether their adaptation strategies address or fail to address core dimensions of assessment validity. A sequential explanatory mixed methods design was used across two phases: a survey of 180 faculty members across STEM and non STEM disciplines at a private institution in India, followed by semi structured interviews and assessment artefact analysis with a purposively selected subset of participants. The results show a marked shift away from unsupervised, product based assessment toward process oriented, reflective, and authentic formats, including oral examinations, project based tasks, in class problem solving, and reflective journals, an implicit faculty led re alignment of assessment with intended learning outcomes. title: Macro‑mesoscopic mechanical response of deformation‑induced disasters in deep coal‑rock structures
abstract: Abstract Deep large-section coal-rock chambers are prone to deformation and instability disasters induced by composite structural effects. To reveal the surrounding-rock deformation-failure mechanism of deep coal-rock chambers, this paper performs a dual-scale comparative study of laboratory specimens and chamber surrounding rock with a refined 10 mm coal thickness gradient. Combining mechanical tests, digital image correlation (DIC) strain monitoring, acoustic emission (AE) monitoring and numerical simulation, this work clarifies the stress evolution, deformation characteristics and failure laws of ternary coal-rock composite structures at dual scales, and reveals the synergistic failure mechanism of coal thickness and bedding planes. The test results show that with increasing coal thickness, composite specimens present an obvious brittle-to-ductile transition, the uniaxial compressive strength undergoes three-stage nonlinear attenuation, and the failure modes evolve sequentially from tensile failure of rock mass, tensile-shear composite failure of coal and rock, X-shaped shear failure of coal mass to multi-surface shear failure of whole coal specimens. The deformation and AE responses are dominated by the coupling effect of coal thickness and bedding planes. title: Dose‒response relationship between tooth loss and cognitive impairment in older adults
abstract: Abstract Background In recent years, associations between oral health factors, including tooth loss, and cognitive function have received increasing attention. However, the dose-response association between tooth loss and cognitive impairment remains incompletely understood. Objective To examine the association and dose–response relationship between the number of remaining natural teeth and cognitive impairment among older adults. Methods The cross-sectional study included 6,997 participants aged 60 years and older from the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), and the number of remaining natural teeth was self-reported. Multivariate logistic regression and restricted cubic spline analyses were performed to examine the association and dose–response pattern between tooth loss and cognitive impairment. Subgroup and multiplicative interaction analyses were further conducted to explore potential heterogeneity, and modified Poisson regression with robust variance was used to assess the joint association and additive interaction between tooth loss and denture use. Results Fewer remaining natural teeth were associated with higher odds of cognitive impairment.
