Integrating radiomic features and clinical variables from cervical lymph node CT to predict treatment response in advanced-stage nasopharyngeal carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Purpose To develop a combined radiomic and clinical model based on pretreatment contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) images of metastatic cervical lymph nodes(CLNs) for predicting complete response (CR) versus non-CR in patients with N2–N3M0 nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). Methods This retrospective study included 493 patients with N2–N3M0 NPC, who were stratified by treatment response and divided into a development cohort ( n = 345) and a held-out validation cohort ( n = 148). Radiomic features were extracted from manually delineated metastatic CLNs on pretreatment CECT images. The clinical model was constructed using ridge logistic regression. Following reproducibility assessment and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator–based(LASSO) feature selection, six radiomics classifiers were compared. The combined model integrated clinical and radiomics predictions using logistic stacking. Model development and hyperparameter tuning were conducted using nested stratified five-fold cross-validation. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), bootstrap confidence intervals, and DeLong tests. Results Gaussian naive Bayes was selected as the radiomics classifier based on the development nested out-of-fold AUC. In the held-out validation cohort, the clinical, radiomics, and combined models achieved AUCs of 0.…

title: The Influence of Profitability, Asset Management, and Firm Size on Firm Value
abstract: This study aims to examine the influence of profitability, asset management, and firm size on firm value in the property and real estate sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2021–2023 period. A quantitative approach with multiple linear regression analysis was employed. The sample was selected using purposive sampling, resulting in 36 companies with a total of 108 observations. The findings indicate that profitability has no significant effect on firm value, asset management also shows no significant influence, while firm size has a significantly positive effect on firm value. These results suggest that larger firms, as measured by total assets, play an important role in enhancing firm value. Conversely, high profitability and efficient asset management do not necessarily reflect a higher firm value from the perspective of investors.

title: An efficient and versatile reverse genetics system for bovine coronavirus facilitates antiviral evaluation
abstract: Abstract Bovine coronavirus (BCoV), a primary etiological agent of calf diarrhea, exhibits dual tropism for the respiratory and enteric tracts. However, research on BCoV gene function and pathogenesis has been limited by the lack of convenient and flexible reverse genetics tools. Herein, we report a robust reverse genetics system for BCoV based on an optimized circular polymerase extension reaction (CPER) methodology. We successfully rescued recombinant BCoV (rBCoV) in HRT-18G cells and engineered recombinant BCoV expressing ZsGreen fluorescent protein (rBCoV/Zs-T2A-ns2). Phenotypic analysis demonstrated that both unmodified rBCoV and rBCoV/Zs-T2A-ns2 maintained growth kinetics comparable to the wild-type BCoV. Importantly, the reporter virus demonstrated remarkable genetic stability for over ten passages, identifying the ns2 locus as a suitable insertion site for stable foreign gene expression without compromising viral fitness or sequence integrity. As a proof-of-concept application, the rBCoV/Zs-T2A-ns2 was employed for antiviral compound evaluation, successfully identifying four compounds—camostat, nafamostat, niclosamide, and nelfinavir—capable of effectively inhibiting BCoV replication. Further time-of-addition assays revealed that nelfinavir and niclosamide targeted the BCoV replication stage, while camostat and nafamostat interfered with BCoV internalization. This versa…

title: Beyond awareness: How perceived benefits, risk and trust shape Indian investors' preference and intention toward green investments
abstract: Sustainable finance has expanded rapidly in India, yet retail uptake of green investments remains uneven, and little is known about the behavioural factors that shape preference for green over conventional options. This study examines how awareness, perceived benefits, perceived risk and trust influence investment preference, and how that preference translates into behavioural intention to invest in green financial products. Drawing on behavioural finance and ESG literature, a structured questionnaire was administered online to a convenience sample of 250 individual investors, and the proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling in SmartPLS. The measurement model met reliability and validity criteria, and model fit was acceptable (SRMR of 0.062 for the saturated model and 0.074 for the estimated model). Perceived benefits (β = 0.329) and trust (β = 0.269) increased investment preference, while perceived risk reduced it (β = 0.244, negative). Awareness had no significant direct effect (β = 0.107, p = 0.128). Investment preference strongly predicted behavioural intention (β = 0.624), consistent with a mediating role for preference, and the model explained 40.8% of the variance in preference and 38.7% in intention. title: Cardiovascular health in transgender and gender diverse individuals: an expert opinion on gender-affirming hormone therapy, risk assessment and clinical management
abstract: Abstract Transgender and gender diverse (TGD) individuals represent a growing population with specific cardiovascular health needs. Current cardiovascular prevention strategies are largely derived from cisgender populations and may not adequately account for the combined effects of gender-affirming hormone therapy (GAHT) and other determinants. This expert opinion summarizes current evidence regarding cardiovascular health in TGD individuals, focusing on the cardiovascular effects of GAHT, population-specific cardiovascular risk factors, practical approaches to cardiovascular risk assessment, and future research priorities. Available evidence indicates that GAHT is associated with changes in cardiometabolic risk factors, haemostasis, vascular function, and cardiac physiology. Feminizing GAHT is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, whereas masculinizing GAHT is associated with adverse lipid changes, erythrocytosis, and a potentially increased risk of major cardiovascular events. However, causal inference is limited by the predominance of observational studies, relatively young study populations, heterogeneous GAHT regimens, short follow-up, and the absence of randomized study evidence. title: A $$3\times 3$$ linear q-difference system with $$E_8^{(1)}$$-symmetry
abstract: Abstract We present a linear q -difference equation of rank 3, which admits the affine Weyl group symmetry of type $$E_8^{(1)}$$ E 8 ( 1 ) . This equation has essentially 8 parameters and 2 accessory parameters. We characterize this equation by the spectral type of q -difference system which is introduced by Sakai–Yamaguchi. We further compare this equation with Moriyama–Yamada’s quantum curve which has $$W(E_8^{(1)})$$ W ( E 8 ( 1 ) ) -symmetry. We show that our equation can be regarded as an extension of Moriyama–Yamada’s curve. We introduce the point configuration of a higher-order scalar q -difference equation to characterize our equation and clarify the corresponding between our equation and the curve. The symmetry of our equation is provided by the q -middle convolution, defined by Sakai–Yamaguchi and reformulated by Arai–Takemura. In this paper, we provide a reconstruction of the q -middle convolution via a q -Okubo-type equation. This construction is a natural q -analog of the middle convolution of Fuchsian differential equation. Several properties for our q -middle convolution are also discussed.

title: MACROINVERTEBRATE-BASED BIOMONITORING AND PHYSICO-CHEMICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF WATER QUALITY IN A TROPICAL RIVER SYSTEM: A CASE STUDY OF OLORI RIVER, SOUTHWESTERN NIGERIA
abstract: Assessment of freshwater ecosystems using biological indicators provides valuable insights into their ecological integrity and pollution status. This study evaluated the water quality and macroinvertebrate assemblages of Olori River, Oke-Igbo, Southwestern Nigeria, to determine the ecological condition of the river. Water and macroinvertebrate samples were collected bi-monthly from six sampling stations between December 2023 and October 2024. Physico-chemical parameters including temperature, dissolved oxygen (DO), pH, total dissolved solids (TDS), electrical conductivity (EC), and biological oxygen demand (BOD) were measured using standard methods. Macroinvertebrates were sampled using a D-frame net and direct hand-picking technique and preserved in 70% ethanol for identification. The results showed that most physico-chemical parameters did not vary significantly among sampling stations (p > 0.05), except for temperature. A total of 2,002 macroinvertebrate specimens belonging to 12 orders, 31 families, and 51 genera were recorded. Melanoides sp. was the most dominant species, while Philaccolus sp. was the least abundant. Station 1 exhibited the highest taxa richness and diversity indices, whereas the lowest diversity was observed in Station 6. title: Trading privacy for personalisation: Ethical trust and high school students’ intention to use AI in education
abstract: Educational AI tools personalise learning by drawing on sensitive student data, yet the privacy calculus assumes that people can freely weigh benefits against risks and decline when risks dominate. This assumption is doubtful for adolescents, who have limited ability to scrutinise institutional data practices and little scope to opt out when AI is embedded in schooling. This study examines how perceived personalisation benefits, perceived data sensitivity and privacy concerns relate to high school students’ intention to use AI, and tests whether ethical trust, defined as confidence that an AI system will handle personal data responsibly, transparently and in the user’s interest, links privacy concerns to intention. Survey data from 323 students across IB, A Level, CBSE, American and other curriculums were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. Perceived benefits strongly predicted ethical trust (β = .605, p < .001) and intention to use AI directly (β = .454, p < .001). Perceived data sensitivity raised privacy concerns (β = .563, p < .001), and privacy concerns modestly reduced ethical trust (β of negative .185, p = .002). Ethical trust in turn predicted intention to use AI (β = .453, p < .001), whereas the direct effect of privacy concerns on intention was negligible (β = .023, p = .507). Evaluating the accuracy of the judging support system in artistic gymnastics compared to the 3D motion analysis system
abstract: Abstract In this study, the measurement accuracy of split angle data obtained using the Judging Support System (JSS), a markerless motion analysis system used in artistic gymnastics, was evaluated in comparison with a gold-standard optical motion capture system (VICON). Nine female collegiate artistic gymnasts executed split leap trials recorded simultaneously using both systems. We defined the split angle as the angle between the left and right leg vectors, each extending from the hip joint center to the toe center, and compared time-series waveforms and maximum split angles between systems. Agreement in maximum split angle was assessed using Bland–Altman analysis and the concordance correlation coefficient, and similarity in time-series movement patterns was evaluated using dynamic time warping. The JSS showed slightly larger maximum split angles than VICON, with a mean difference of − 1.1°, and no significant proportional bias was observed. Nevertheless, the concordance correlation coefficient was high across trials, and the time-series waveforms showed similar patterns during the aerial phase, including the maximum split angle. Temporal discrepancies were mainly observed during take-off and landing. title: Consensus-based perspectives on integrating IPX203 into Parkinson’s disease management
abstract: Abstract Motor fluctuations are a common and burdensome complication of Parkinson’s disease (PD) when the disease progresses, largely driven by the short half-life and variable absorption of immediate-release (IR) levodopa. IPX203 is a next-generation modified-release levodopa/carbidopa formulation that delivers rapid onset and sustained plasma levodopa concentrations through IR granules and extended-release pellets. Clinical studies have shown that IPX203 increases Good ON time (ON time without dyskinesia plus ON time with non-troublesome dyskinesia, equivalent to ON time without troublesome dyskinesia), reduces OFF time and improves motor symptom control compared with IR levodopa/carbidopa. In anticipation of the introduction of IPX203 in Europe, nine PD specialists convened to develop consensus recommendations for its use in clinical practice. Through a structured process incorporating predefined statements, voting and moderated discussion, the group reached high levels of agreement (88.9% to 100%) across seven topics. These included defining motor symptoms control, identifying patients most likely to benefit from IPX203, positioning of IPX203 within the treatment pathway, practical considerations for switching to IPX203 from current regimens and recommendations for monitoring and follow-up. The experts emphasised that IPX203 should be considered for patients with motor fluc…

Beyond Acknowledgement: The Legal Gap in Protecting the Family Rights of Transgender Persons in India – Constitutional and Personal Law Aspects
abstract: The Supreme Court of India’s landmark judgments in NALSA v. Union of India (2014) and Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018) have paved the way for broader legal recognition of transgender persons in India. However, basic rights such as the right to marry, to form a family, to adopt and to inherit remain largely unrecognised in law. This article examines the intersection of the rights of transgender persons with the statutory and personal laws of the Indian legal framework. The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 and the Special Marriage Act, 1954 continue to use heteronormative terms such as “bride” and “bridegroom”, creating impediments for transgender couples. Likewise, adoption under the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 is confined to a “male” or “female” Hindu, leaving transgender persons in a grey zone. The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 is also framed in gendered terms, giving rise to disputes over self-identified gender. Marriage (nikah) under Muslim personal law is traditionally a contract between a man and a woman, leaving little, and uncertain, space for transgender persons. Beyond kafala (guardianship), adoption is not recognised under Muslim personal law, and inheritance rights under Muslim law are tied to the distribution of property between binary gender categories. The article argues that these exclusions in the personal laws conflict with the fundamental rights …

title: The Influence Of The Audit Committee, Leverage, Profitability On Tax Aggressiveness With Independent Commissioners As A Moderating Variable
abstract: Tax aggressiveness is an action taken by a company to reduce its cost in fulfilling its tax obligations. Companies that engage in tax aggressiveness to save on tax payments will generate higher profits in the future. The purpose of this research is to examine and explain the influence of the audit committee, leverage, profitability, and independent commissioners on the value of manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. The sample size in this study consisted of 107 manufacturing companies from 2021-2023, with 49 outlier data points and a total of 272 companies in the research. Data collection used the non-participant observation method. The data analysis technique used is moderation regression analysis. The analysis results show that the audit committee has a positive and significant effect on tax aggressiveness, leverage has a negative and significant effect on tax aggressiveness, profitability has a positive effect on tax aggressiveness, independent commissioners weaken the influence of the audit committee on tax aggressiveness, independent commissioners weaken the influence of leverage on tax aggressiveness, and independent commissioners strengthen the influence of profitability on tax aggressiveness. The theoretical implication of this research is to provide knowledge and strengthen the theory of corporate agency value related to the audit committee, l…

title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in sustainable FMCG purchasing among Generation Z: An integrated innovation resistance theory and intention–behavior gap framework
abstract: Fast moving consumer goods (FMCG) firms contribute substantially to packaging waste and emissions, and Generation Z consumers express strong environmental concern, yet their sustainable purchases lag behind their stated intentions. This paper reviews research on the intention behaviour gap in green purchasing and integrates it with innovation resistance theory to explain why green intentions often fail to become purchases among Gen Z consumers in India. Following PRISMA reporting guidance, the review synthesises 70 studies identified through database searches covering 2016 to 2026. The synthesis indicates that environmental consciousness, sustainability knowledge and social media exposure shape green purchase intention, whereas functional barriers (perceived risk, price and inconvenience) and psychological barriers (greenwashing, image concerns and low trust) weaken the conversion of intention into purchase. Green trust, credible sustainability communication and peer validation appear to reduce resistance and to support repeat purchase and electronic word of mouth. Building on these themes, the paper proposes a conceptual framework in which barriers link intention to behaviour and trust and peer validation act as moderating conditions. Most of the available evidence comes from intention based surveys and from settings outside India, so the framework offers propositions for test…

Self help group bank linkage as a social innovation for poverty reduction: A qualitative analysis using the McKinsey 7S framework
abstract: The Self Help Group Bank Linkage Programme (SHG BLP) is widely regarded as a social innovation that extends formal finance to low income, collateral constrained households in India, especially women. This study asks how the features of SHG BLP align with the elements of the McKinsey 7S framework: shared values, structure, systems, staff, skills, style and strategy. Using a qualitative design, we conducted a hermeneutic reading and open, focused and theoretical coding of about ten publicly available sources, including microfinance advertisements, documentaries and interview accounts from SHG members and promoting institution leaders. The analysis suggests that group functioning is framed around a social contract, peer monitoring, and routine practices of regular meetings, savings, bookkeeping and internal lending. Intermediation by NGOs and self help promoting institutions, support from the National Rural Livelihood Mission, livelihood and financial literacy training, and community leadership are presented as complementary elements. Narratives of microfinance stress, including high interest rates, over indebtedness and coercive recovery, also show the limits of credit alone. The findings point to microfinance as a targeted, embedded intervention rather than a one shot solution to multidimensional poverty. Because the sources are promotional and anecdotal, the results are interpr…

Collective Bargaining and Industrial Disputes: A Comprehensive Study on the Maintenance of Industrial Peace
abstract: Collective bargaining is the main institutional mechanism through which employers and workers negotiate working conditions, resolve grievances and regulate employment relations. Its effectiveness can be weakened by representational weakness, trust and communication gaps, structural and economic pressures, and political and managerial resistance. This study examines how these four barriers relate to industrial disputes and how industrial disputes, in turn, relate to industrial peace. A descriptive and analytical research design was used, based on a structured questionnaire of 32 five-point Likert items administered to 153 respondents. The analysis comprised frequency and percentage analysis, descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson correlation, multiple regression, one-way ANOVA and regression-based bootstrap mediation analysis. Internal consistency was acceptable for all six constructs (alpha = 0.755 to 0.845), and construct means were close to the scale midpoint (2.94 to 3.06). The four barrier dimensions together explained 19.3% of the variance in industrial disputes (R² = 0.193, p < .001); representational weakness (B = 0.189, p = .008) and trust/communication gaps (B = 0.203, p = .003) were significant predictors, while structural/economic pressures and political/managerial resistance were not. title: The sustainable development goals and Aldo Leopold’s land ethic: A philosophical analysis of ecological sustainability, human well-being, and environmental ethics
abstract: Aldo Leopold’s Land Ethic is one of the seminal works in environmental ethics because he brought the consideration of ethics from human interests to the biotic community. The idea of ecological integrity, stability and beauty, however, suggests a philosophical question about the relationship between ecological responsibilities and human health, justice and democratic choice. This article looks at how the norms of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) can be applied to Leopold’s Land Ethic in a constructive way. The study collates Leopold’s original formulation, philosophical understandings of ecological holism, and sustainable development, human rights and environmental justice literature with the use of structured secondary-literature review and reported with reference to the PRISMA 2020 framework. The analysis in particular emphasizes SDG 15 (Life on Land), SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 10 (Reduced Inequalities) and SDG 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions). The article suggests that the Land Ethic and SDGs can be engaged productively when ecological integrity becomes a state of human long-term flourishing, not an excuse to ignore social justice or human dignity. The SDG framework brings in practical elements such as poverty alleviation, equality, participation, institutional accountability an…

TAMIS repair within a structured multimodal management pathway for colorectal anastomotic leaks: surgical technique and outcomes
abstract: Abstract Aim We describe the transanal minimally invasive surgerical (TAMIS) procedure for the elective repair of colorectal anastomotic leaks (AL) within a structured management pathway based on early leak detection and selective adjunctive therapy. We also report the clinical outcomes of this multimodal approach, along with an operative video illustrating the surgical technique step by step. Method Data on patients who underwent TAMIS for AL at our centre were collected. The operative video demonstrates each step of the technique, highlighting its advantages and feasibility. Results Thirteen patients underwent the TAMIS approach to treat colorectal AL between 2016 and 2024, with a median age of 55 (range: 14–84) years. Anastomosis was repaired and rescued in 12 (92.31%) patients. The median length of hospital stay was 20 (14–38) days. All but one patient (92.31%) with long-term anastomotic healing achieved closed ileostomies. Conclusions Within a structured multimodal management pathway, TAMIS is a safe and feasible option for selected patients with colorectal anastomotic leaks. Limitations This is a single-centre study with a small sample size.

title: From Dignity to Dispossession: The Constitutional Backlash Against Queer Self-Determination in India
abstract: The journey towards the constitutional recognition of LGBTQIA+ rights in India has been shaped by judicial interpretations focused on dignity, equality, privacy and personal autonomy, but recent constitutional developments have left some doubt about the realisation of queer self-determination. The purpose of this study is to analyse critically the constitutional reaction to queer self-determination in India and its repercussions for marriage equality, family recognition and substantive equality. The study focuses in particular on the constitutional basis of queer self-determination and on the implications of the recent rulings for the protection of LGBTQIA+ rights. A qualitative doctrinal research method is used, with analytical and interpretative analysis of constitutional provisions, judicial precedents, statutes and current legal literature, principally published between 2015 and 2026. The results show that, while the Indian Constitution has made a strong case for dignity and equal citizenship for queer citizens, judicial restraint and legislative apathy continue to hamper the attainment of substantive equality and family rights. The study finds a need for holistic legislative restructuring and for radical fundamental constitutional change in order to realise meaningful queer self-determination and constitutional justice in India.

abstract: Abstract Viscosity is a fundamental property of polymer materials and solutions that strongly influences their flow behavior, processing, and performance in various industrial and engineering applications. Polymer materials and polymer solutions are vital components in many industrial and engineering processes, in which viscosity is an important characteristic determining their flow behavior and performance. This paper presents predictive modeling of logarithmic viscosity (LV) of polymer solutions using Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). 420 samples were collected through a public Kaggle database. Logarithm Shear Rate (LS), Polymer Concentration (PC), NaCl Concentration (NA) and Temperature (TE) are considered as input variables. The collected dataset is randomly divided into training (70%), validation (15%) and test set (15%). From the results, the error histogram revealed that the majority of the prediction errors are centred around −21.35, while the ANN model performed optimally during validation with MSE of 67,522.49 at epoch 20. A representative ANFIS prediction yielded an LV value of 11.7 cP for an input combination of LS of 55.8 s −1 , PC of 0.175 wt%, NA of 2.05 wt%, and TE of 57.5 °C. ANFIS was found to perform exceptionally well compared to ANN, based on an RMSE of 31.50, an MAE of 6.49, and an R2 value of 0.9846. In ad…

title: A deep hybrid feature extraction model based on MobileNet and vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia prediction
abstract: Abstract Early and accurate identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from peripheral blood smear images can support microscopic screening, but reliable evaluation requires both discriminative feature learning and transparent reporting of the experimental protocol. This study presents MoViTHAFX-Net, a hybrid MobileNet–Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) and Grad-CAM++ visualization for binary classification of ALL blasts and healthy hematogones (HEM) using the 10,661 labelled cell images in the training component of the C-NMC 2019 dataset. MobileNet extracts local morphological information, whereas ViT models long-range contextual relationships. HAF first refines the two branches and then adaptively combines three learnable morphology-guided feature projections before binary classification. The reported experiment uses an image-level stratified partition containing 7462 training images, 1600 validation images, and 1599 held-out test images; augmentation is restricted to the training partition. On the held-out test partition, the model correctly classified 1583 of 1599 images, corresponding to 99.00% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 0.990 and an AUC of 0.99. Ablation results within the same experimental setting indicate an incremental advantage of HAF over direct CNN–ViT concatenation. Grad-CAM+…

title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

Forest carbon certification under climate and mortality uncertainty: ecological and economic trade-offs of management scenarios in Freiburg, Germany
abstract: Abstract Background Forest carbon certification could help finance the transformation of climate-sensitive stands, but early interventions may reduce biomass and timber revenue before carbon and ecological benefits emerge. Evidence that jointly evaluates forest growth, hydrological co-benefits, timber economics, carbon accounting, and uncertainty remains limited. We compared no management, business-as-usual management, a conventional certification scenario, and a transformative certification scenario across five spruce-dominated plots in Freiburg, Germany. Forest development was simulated from 2020 to 2080 using 3-PG-Hydro under three climate models, two emissions pathways, and four mortality assumptions, resulting in 480 stand-level simulations. Timber-based net present value was assessed at discount rates of 1%, 2%, and 4%, and indicative carbon-credit potential was estimated relative to business as usual. Results Management, mortality severity, and initial stand structure generally had greater effects on biomass than differences among climate models or emissions pathways. No management retained the highest biomass under no and low mortality, but this advantage declined under stronger mortality assumptions. Business as usual produced the greatest harvest volumes and pronounced harvest-related biomass fluctuations. The transformative scenario generally produced among the highe…

title: Swietenia mahogani Fruit Shell-Based Carbon as a Filter Medium for Domestic Liquid Waste: A Preliminary Evaluation
abstract: Domestic wastewater generated from daily household activities can degrade environmental water quality if discharged without adequate treatment. Filtration is one of the most widely applied preliminary treatment methods due to its simplicity and effectiveness in increasing water quality. Activated wood carbon (AWC) is widely used as an adsorbent in filtration systems. However, commercially produced AWC can be expensive, prompting interest in developing carbon from lignocellulosic waste such as mahogany fruit shells. In this study, mahogany shell carbon was prepared in both activated (AMC) and non-activated (NMC) forms, with activation performed using KOH, and evaluated alongside other common filtration media. The effectiveness of each filter configuration was assessed based on improvements in physical water quality parameters. The results showed that filters using zeolite, sand, and NMC provided balanced performance, achieving reductions in color, turbidity, and TDS while maintaining an adequate filtration rate. In contrast, the filter containing AMC exhibited extremely low permeability due to its fine particle size, resulting in poor filtration efficiency. These findings highlight the potential of NMC as a cost-effective filtration material for household-scale wastewater pretreatment.

Coupling between stellar and HI lopsidedness in Milky Way--type galaxies from the Auriga Superstars cosmological simulations
abstract: Lopsidedness is a common feature in disk galaxies, but its origin and evolution remain poorly understood. Previous works have generally focused on stellar or gas lopsidedness separately. However, a combined analysis can help identify the mechanisms driving lopsidedness and constrain recent galactic evolution and environmental interactions. We study lopsidedness in the density and kinematics of the stellar and atomic hydrogen (HI) components of nine Milky Way-type galaxies from the Auriga Superstars cosmological zoom-in simulations. The high stellar mass resolution (mathrm m_ * =800, M_⊙ ) of the simulations improves the visibility of features in the stellar disk and halo, reduces the effect of noise on the measurement of lopsidedness, and provides a refined sampling of the gravitational potential. We quantified morphological and kinematical lopsidedness through the amplitude of the first Fourier mode (m=1) of the face-on projected mass distribution and radial velocity maps consistently for stars and gas and over 0.5-1, opt , where R_ opt is the stellar optical radius. At z=0, the morphological lopsidedness of the old stellar component ($>0.5$ Gyr old) strongly correlates with that of HI, tracing distortions in the global gravitational potential, while the young stellar population ($<0.5$ Gyr old) primarily traces asymmetric star formation along strong spiral arms. Safe host integration in islet tissue engineering for Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: emerging technologies and a constraint-guided hybrid islet framework
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) results from autoimmune destruction of pancreatic β cells and requires lifelong insulin replacement. Islet transplantation can restore endogenous insulin secretion, but donor scarcity, immune rejection, early graft loss, inadequate oxygen delivery, and fibrosis limit its application. This review examines conventional and emerging islet tissue-engineering approaches and proposes a conceptual hybrid bio-artificial islet system (HBAIS). A heuristic constraint-exchange framework compares the functions gained from successive technological additions with their associated risks, overlapping benefits, and operational dependencies. The analysis identifies hypoimmune stem cell-derived β cells within a retrievable, transport-permissive interface, supplemented by temporary oxygen generation, as a provisional core configuration. Optogenetic amplification and synthetic protocell-mediated vascular support remain conditional additions when intrinsic insulin responsiveness or host vascular integration is inadequate. The review also proposes auxiliary donor-antigen-matched decoys, including lymph-node grafts, retrievable implants, and intraportal islets, as potential means of relocating immune interactions away from the principal graft. Their ability to intercept immune effectors or promote donor-specific regulation, rather than amplify sensitization, requires exp…

Energy-dependent underwater abrasion behavior of sustainable lightweight concrete incorporating agro-waste aggregates and natural fibers under rotational hydraulic conditions
abstract: Abstract Lightweight aggregate concrete has become a popular material in hydraulic engineering and coastal and offshore engineering, and understanding its durability under underwater rotational abrasion is critical. Comparative studies on the abrasion resistance of several agricultural waste aggregates under high-energy underwater conditions have been conducted for the production of sustainable concrete; however, such studies are still scarce, especially considering the combined effects of rotational speed, abrasion time, aggregate properties, and properties of the interfacial transition zone between the aggregate and cement matrix. This study aims to fill this research gap by comparing conventional concrete with lightweight aggregate concrete using coconut shell, expanded clay aggregate, oil palm shell, and areca nut shell aggregates with natural fibers (hemp, jute, and coir) under underwater rotational abrasion. Abrasion tests were conducted at 1200 rpm and 1600 rpm to investigate the influence of exposure time, abrasion energy, and aggregate nature on the abrasion resistance. Findings indicated that the Abrasion loss increased linearly with exposure time, confirming cumulative mechanical erosion. After 6 h at 1600 rpm, weight loss increased from 461.93 g for conventional concrete to 549.44–698.91 g for lightweight concretes. Wear rate ranged from 23.35–38.80 g/h (1200 rpm) a…

Depression, anxiety, stress and coping strategies among undergraduates in a public and a private university in Osun State Nigeria using a comparative cross-sectional design
abstract: Abstract This study compared depression, anxiety and stress symptoms and examined their associated factors among undergraduates in a public university and private university in Osun State, Nigeria. A comparative cross-sectional design was used. Of 387 questionnaires distributed, 340 were returned (87.9%), while 322 sufficiently completed questionnaires were analysed, comprising 161 students from each institution. Data were collected using the Depression, Anxiety and Stress Scale-21 and an adapted 15-item Brief COPE questionnaire. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, chi-square/Fisher–Freeman–Halton tests, Spearman correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and pooled binary logistic regression. Moderate-or-higher depression occurred among 19.3% of public and 36.0% of private university students. Depression severity differed significantly between institutions, χ² (4) = 19.60, p<0.001, while private university students had higher adjusted odds of depression (AOR = 1.94, 95% CI: 1.08–3.50). Moderate-or-higher anxiety occurred in 49.7% of students in both institutions, with no significant institutional difference (p = 0.298). Moderate-or-higher stress occurred among 9.9% and 19.3%, respectively, with no significant severity difference (p = 0.106). Denial and Self-Critical Disengagement Coping was positively associated with depression, anxiety and stress in both ins…

Optimasi Formula Sediaan Lotion dari Ekstrak Daun Nangka (Artocarpus heterophyllus Lam.) sebagai Antioksidan dengan Simplex Lattice Design
abstract: Pada tahun 2022 WHO mencatat prevalensi melanoma maligna mencapai 331.722 kasus diseluruh dunia dengan 25.033 kasus di Asia dan 1.716 kasus di Indonesia. Radikal bebas akibat paparan lingkungan terhadap kerusakan kulit sehingga diperlukan pengembangan sediaan topikal berbahan alam dengan aktivitas antioksidan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengevaluasi aktivitas antioksidan ekstrak daun nangka, karakteristik fisik lotion, dan menentukan formula optimum menggunakan Simplex Lattice Design. Penelitian merupakan eksperimental laboratorium dengan populasi daun nangka dari Kabupaten Grobogan, Jawa Tengah dan sampel sebanyak 5 kg. Ekstrak dibuat dengan maserasi menggunakan etanol 96%. Instrumen meliputi spektrofotometer UV-Vis, viskometer, moisture analyzer, rotary evaporator, dan Design Expert versi 13. Data dianalisis melalui evaluasi fisik, ANOVA, Simplex Lattice Design, dan penentuan IC₅₀ menggunakan metode DPPH. Ekstrak menghasilkan IC₅₀ 9,58 ppm, sedangkan lotion formula optimum sebesar 22,48 ppm, keduanya termasuk kategori sangat kuat. Formula optimum terdiri atas asam stearat 80% dan TEA 20% dengan desirability 1. Kesimpulan: Ekstrak daun nangka memiliki aktivitas antioksidan sangat kuat dan dapat diformulasikan menjadi lotion dengan karakteristik fisik yang memenuhi kriteria serta formula optimum yang dapat diprediksi menggunakan Simplex Lattice Design.

Exploring transcriptomic and genomic latent variable correction approaches in differential expression analysis
abstract: Abstract Differential expression analysis is a central tool for studying the biological processes altered in human diseases via transcriptomic signatures. However, transcriptomic datasets are systematically confounded by latent variables from two distinct sources: unmeasured technical and biological heterogeneity within the expression data, and expression differences driven by population stratification. Correction using expression-based surrogate variables (SVs) and genotype-based principal components (PCs) addresses these sources independently, yet no study has directly evaluated their combined use against either method alone within a differential expression framework. In this study we hypothesised that simultaneously including both correction layers would produce more biologically valid and reproducible results than either approach alone, and tested this in two independent post-mortem RNA-seq datasets of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) cases and controls with paired genotype data. Four nested differential expression models (corrected for PC-only, SV-only, both SV and PC, and neither PCs nor SVs) were evaluated across the KCLBB (96 cases and 52 controls) and ALS Consortium (272 cases and 35 controls) datasets. Models were evaluated on cross-dataset effect size concordance, cross-dataset replicability quantified by the Jaccard Similarity Index, and biological recall against…

title: Hierarchical generative modeling for the design of multi-component systems
abstract: Abstract The functionality of catalysts, enzymes, and supramolecular assemblies emerges not from individual molecules alone, but from the subtle interplay between multiple components arranged in complex systems. Designing such systems is a grand challenge: the combinatorial explosion of possible chemical compositions and spatial arrangements makes brute-force exploration infeasible, while many current generative approaches remain limited to isolated molecules. In this work, we introduce a hierarchical generative optimization framework that overcomes this barrier by coupling a genetic algorithm for configurational search with a generative model for molecular design. This closed-loop approach enables simultaneous refinement of geometry and composition, efficiently steering discovery toward systems with targeted functionality. As a proof of concept, we design catalytic environments for the Claisen rearrangement of p-tolyl ether by optimizing surrounding components around a fixed reference transition-state geometry. Despite this constraint during the search phase, post-hoc validation via Climbing-Image Nudged Elastic Band calculations, with the environment held fixed, indicates a reduction of the activation barrier by about 30%. Seeing through others’ eyes in immersive VR: insights from a user study
abstract: Abstract Despite the increasing usage of collaborative Virtual Reality in classrooms, teachers often struggle to ascertain whether the participants are adequately sharing the same viewpoint and are seeing the same information during lectures. Virtual Reality offers numerous advantages, including immersive experiences that enhance traditional classroom instruction and foster active and cooperative learning. A relevant part of the teaching process involves pointing to concrete regions or points of the virtual scene, and describing them. At this point, it is important that the pupils are able to see the same that is being seen by the instructor. In this paper we analyze viewpoint sharing methods commonly used in the literature, like teleport, 2D views with or without continuous streaming, and propose a novel method, dubbed Model Movement (MM). Our application layout is structured around a central 3D model that acts as the primary focal point at the collaborative session and the experiments were performed using 3D anatomical models. We conducted a user study with 32 participants (local and nominally remote) where participants were asked multiple times to swap to the instructor’s viewpoint and tracked their response times and their movement in the scene, among other variables. abstract: Mobile and application-derived artefacts are becoming more central to digital forensic investigations; however, they can be a diverse set of evidence in a UFDR which are hard to prioritize manually. Mobile and application derived-artifacts are becoming more important to digital forensic investigations, and can be a diverse set of evidence in a UFDR that is difficult to manually prioritize. In the paper, the authors propose an Artificial Intelligence-based UFDR report analysis and intelligent digital forensic investigation assistant to transform the extracted report information into a structured and explainable analysis flow. The prototype now supports reading reports in JSON, XML, CSV and ZIP formats, validates the uploaded report, calculates an integrity checksum (SHA-256), and stores proof of the integrity in SQLite. Twenty behavioral features are created in communication, temporal, browser, application, and file activity. The trained Random Forest (RF) classifier enables three-way classification, and a trained Isolation Forest (Anomaly scoring) is used. A suspicious detector based on the 4 parameters is set, and activates when late-night activity is detected, or when suspicious incoming/outgoing communication, suspicious text indicators or high anomaly scores are detected. title: An intersection of machine learning and advanced econometric techniques to analyse sustainable development in Europe through resource efficiency, institutional quality, and ICT
abstract: Abstract Sustainable development is a critical challenge as well as an opportunity for modern economies, especially for European countries, where technological and institutional frameworks are increasingly evolving and reshaping. This prospective study investigates the role of resource efficiency, institutional quality and information and communication technologies (ICT) to promote sustainable development in 26 European countries for 2000–2023. The study uses a comprehensive methodology, including econometric methodologies such as the Three-Stage Least Squares (3SLS), Generalized Method of Moments (GMM), and Full Information Maximum Likelihood (FIML), along with machine learning models, so that the results are accurate and have predictive depth. Based on the results, there are significant factors that promote sustainability in Europe countries such as better resource utilization, improved institutional quality and advanced ICT infrastructure. All these effects are positive and statistically significant, with institutional quality (coefficient = 0.023–0.030), ICT (0.011–0.025) and resource efficiency (≈ 0.008–0.016) being the most influential drivers, while CO₂ emissions have a significant negative effect. An adaptive federated deep learning approach for efficient DDoS detection in IoT edge networks
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has expanded the attack surface of modern networks, motivating the need for accurate detection of DDoS and botnet activity in resource-constrained settings. Centralised intrusion detection systems (IDS) face privacy, scalability, and heterogeneity challenges that limit their suitability for IoT. This study suggests a Federated Learning-based Intrusion Detection System (FL-IDS) for IoT edge networks in order to get around these restrictions. Each client trains a hybrid CNN-LSTM model locally, and a central server aggregates client updates with Federated Averaging (FedAvg). An adaptive global decision-threshold optimisation is used post-training to the pooled predictions of the global model on the held-out test partition in order to address class imbalance. The system is evaluated on the N-BaIoT benchmark together with preliminary validation on a recent public healthcare IoT dataset, with the nine N-BaIoT devices treated as independent federated clients during the primary federated evaluation. The global model achieves an accuracy of 0.9238, precision of 0.9265, recall of 0.9963, F1-score of 0.9601, ROC-AUC of 0.8133, and PR-AUC of 0.969 at the optimal operating point $$\tau = 0.15$$ . SHAP-based post-hoc analysis identifies the traffic features that most influence model decisions.

Multiobjective optimization of foamed concrete for sustainable construction using statistical and artificial intelligence approaches
abstract: Abstract Foamed concrete is lightweight and insulating, but its mix design is a headache. Strength, durability, and carbon footprint all fight each other. This review looks at how researchers have tried to optimize these trade-offs using methods like RSM, Taguchi, ANN, and genetic algorithms. RSM is easy to interpret but struggles with nonlinear foam behavior. AI models handle nonlinearity better but need lots of data and tell you nothing about why they work. The best path forward seems to be hybrid approaches. On the environmental side, cement drives most of the carbon. Replacing it with SCMs can cut GWP by 20–50%. We put together a conceptual Pareto front showing the sweet spot: 900–1200 kg/m³ density, 8–15 MPa strength, and 350–500 kg CO₂-eq/m³. Big gaps remain. No standard testing protocols. Pore-scale physics is missing from models. Almost nobody has coupled LCA with real optimization. Field validation is rare. We end with a research roadmap: hybrid frameworks, open databases, and proper microstructural inputs.

Stochastic gradient with least-squares control variates
abstract: The stochastic gradient descent (SGD) method is a widely used approach for solving stochastic optimization problems, but its convergence is typically slow. Existing variance reduction techniques, such as SAGA, improve convergence by leveraging stored gradient information; however, they are restricted to settings where the objective functional is a finite sum, and their performance degrades when the number of terms in the sum is large. In this work, we propose a novel approach which is well suited when the objective is given by an expectation over random variables with a continuous probability distribution. Our method constructs a control variate by fitting a linear model to past gradient evaluations using weighted discrete least-squares, effectively reducing variance while preserving computational efficiency. We establish theoretical sublinear convergence guarantees and demonstrate the method's effectiveness through numerical experiments on random PDE-constrained optimization problems.

Integrated Assessment of Climate and Land Use/Land Cover Change Effects on Hydrological Responses in the Hare River Watershed, Southern Ethiopia
abstract: This study assesses the integrated impacts of land use/land cover (LULC) change and climate change on hydrological responses in the Hare watershed, Southern Ethiopia, using the SWAT model. Historical climate trends, LULC dynamics, and future climate projections based on CMIP6 scenarios were analyzed. The model was calibrated and validated using observed stream flow data. Results indicate that LULC change and climate variability significantly influence surface runoff, evapotranspiration, base flow, and water yield. Combined scenarios showed stronger hydrological responses compared to individual impacts. The findings provide useful insights for sustainable watershed management under changing climate and land-use conditions.

Sustainable bacterial cellulose-based delivery system for probiotic stabilization in functional beverages
abstract: Abstract The growing demand for functional foods has driven innovation in probiotic delivery systems that ensure microbial stability and targeted release. Probiotics, defined as live microorganisms conferring health benefits, often face challenges related to survival during processing, storage, and gastrointestinal transit. This study investigates bacterial cellulose (BC), a biopolymer produced by acetic acid bacteria, as a natural and sustainable encapsulating material for improving the stability and delivery of Enterococcus faecalis RITBM S15-3 in a functional beverage. Freeze-dried BC was characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and probiotic cells were encapsulated within a pectin/BC composite matrix before incorporation into a mango-based functional beverage. The viability of encapsulated probiotics was assessed under simulated gastrointestinal conditions, during 16 days of ambient storage, and by monitoring beverage physicochemical properties and antioxidant activity. The viable cell count decreased from 9.25 to 8.18 log CFU/ml after exposure to simulated gastric fluid and further to 6.39 log CFU/ml following simulated intestinal conditions, demonstrating substantial protection of encapsulated cells during gastrointestinal transit. title: A Computer Vision-Based Driver Drowsiness Detection System Using Facial Landmarks and Temporal Eye Analysis
abstract: Driver drowsiness is an important traffic safety problem, as reduced alertness is known to affect visual attention, decision making and reaction time thereby increasing the risk of unsafe driving. Continuous monitoring of driver behavior can help identify visual signals that are associated with drowsiness and provide feedback to the driver in a timely manner. In this paper, we present a web CV driver monitoring system that focuses on drowsiness detection based on facial landmarks and temporal eye behavior. We detect the driver face and obtain 68 facial landmark points to inspect eye part by this method. The EAR (Eye Aspect Ratio) is a common ratio we can calculate from the eye landmakrs to find out how open are the eyes. Since any isolated frame displaying decreased eye openness may only reflect natural blinking or transient saccadic eye movement, the system applies exponential moving average (EMA) smoothing and temporal decision logic to assess shifts between contiguous observations. Finally the last setting maintains a 0.283 EAR threshold and a 0.16 EMA smoothing coefficient. The broader monitoring framework further provides auxiliary capabilities for head-pose and gaze detection, road-scene processing, and safety-oriented monitoring. title: Multimedia Utilization and Instructional Effectiveness in Social Studies
abstract: This study examined the relationship between multimedia utilization and instructional effectiveness among Social Studies teachers at the University of Cebu Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue Campus during the academic year 2026-2027. Anchored in the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) Framework and Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning, the study employed a descriptive-correlational research design involving 50 Social Studies teachers selected through complete enumeration. Data were gathered using an adapted and researcher-modified questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics and Pearson's correlation coefficient. Findings revealed a generally low level of multimedia utilization (M = 2.48), with educational videos being the most frequently used resource. Instructional effectiveness was generally rated effective (M = 2.55), particularly in attaining learning objectives, while student engagement remained comparatively less effective. Time constraints emerged as the primary challenge, followed by technical skills and resource availability. Correlation analyses revealed no statistically significant relationships between multimedia utilization and instructional effectiveness (r = 0.216, p = 0.132) or between multimedia-related challenges and instructional effectiveness (r = -0.123, p = 0.397). title: The Malnutrition-Infection Cycle in Children Under Five: A Systematic Review and the GROW-WELL Integrated Nutrition and WASH Model
abstract: Malnutrition and infection are closely interrelated in children under five, with inadequate nutrition increasing susceptibility to infection and illness further compromising nutritional status. Water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) conditions can intensify this cycle, yet nutrition and WASH interventions are often implemented separately. This review examines the evidence on the relationship between malnutrition and infection and the potential value of integrated approaches. A systematic review was conducted using searches of PubMed, ScienceDirect, Dimensions AI, and the World Health Organization repository. The review included 16 publications: 11 empirical studies and five policy documents. Two reviewers independently screened records, and methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT, 2018) for empirical studies and the Appraisal of Guidelines for Research and Evaluation II (AGREE II) instrument for policy documents. Findings were synthesized narratively. The included literature highlighted interconnected relationships among nutritional status, infectious disease, and environmental conditions, including inadequate water, sanitation, and hygiene. Nutrition-specific interventions and WASH measures addressed complementary pathways, although findings on the effectiveness of combined interventions were heterogeneous. abstract: This study examined teachers’ perceptions of elementary learners’ reading proficiency, associated literacy factors, and challenges in literacy monitoring and evaluation at Banawa Elementary School, Cebu City, during School Year 2025–2026. Anchored in Chall’s Stages of Reading Development, Bandura’s Social Learning Theory, and Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, the study employed a descriptive quantitative research design guided by the Input–Process–Output (IPO) framework. Thirty-six Grades 1–6 teachers were selected through purposive sampling, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics and correlation analysis were used to examine the findings. Results revealed a High overall perceived reading proficiency (M = 3.87), with vocabulary skills receiving the highest rating (M = 4.02), followed by reading comprehension (M = 3.93) and word recognition (M = 3.66). Factors associated with reading proficiency were also rated High (M = 3.96), particularly reading habits, motivation, and access to reading materials. Consensual Rape? The Aftermath of Failed Relationships
abstract: The expression “consensual rape” presents a legal contradiction, yet it captures a recurring controversy in Indian criminal jurisprudence: whether sexual relations voluntarily established between adults can later become the subject of a rape prosecution after the relationship deteriorates or ends. This paper examines the boundary between consensual sexual intimacy, sexual intercourse obtained through deception, and rape committed after consent has been withdrawn. It analyses the transition from the Indian Penal Code, 1860, to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, with particular emphasis on sections 63 and 69. The study adopts a doctrinal and interdisciplinary methodology, examining statutory provisions, landmark Supreme Court judgments, selected High Court decisions, research papers, scholarly articles, legal commentaries and committee reports. It argues that the subsequent failure of a relationship cannot retrospectively transform earlier consensual intercourse into rape. At the same time, a prior romantic or sexual relationship cannot protect an accused where a later sexual act occurs through force, coercion, deception or after consent has been withdrawn. The paper distinguishes a promise of marriage that was false from its inception from a genuine promise that was subsequently broken. It further examines whether section 69 BNS creates an independent offence of deceitful sexual…

title: Protecting Workers' Right to Mental Health in Digital Work Environments: Legal Challenges and Reform Directions in Vietnam
abstract: Digital work technologies increasingly determine when, how, and at what intensity work is performed. Continuous connectivity, electronic monitoring, algorithmic management, and technology-enabled harassment can generate psychosocial risks that are not adequately addressed by legal rules designed mainly for physical workplaces. This article asks whether Vietnamese labour and occupational safety and health law provides a coherent preventive framework for protecting workers’ mental health in digital work environments and which comparative models can guide reform. It uses doctrinal analysis, interdisciplinary literature synthesis, and functional comparison with international standards and selected approaches in the European Union, France, and Australia. The analysis finds that Vietnamese law contains relevant constitutional, working-time, occupational safety and health, dignity, anti-harassment, and personal-data safeguards, but these rules remain fragmented. In particular, psychosocial risks are not expressly defined or systematically assessed; workers have no statutory right to disconnect; electronic monitoring and algorithmic management are not regulated as working-condition issues; and protection for platform and remote workers remains incomplete. Avoiding Secondary Hemodilution During Planned Temporary Right Ventricular Assist Device Implantation: An Autologous Priming Technique
abstract: Background: Temporary right ventricular assist device (RVAD) support is used during selected high-risk cardiac operations, including durable left ventricular assist device implantation, orthotopic heart transplantation, and procedures complicated by anticipated right ventricular failure. When RVAD implantation is planned during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB), the RVAD circuit is commonly primed with crystalloid solution. Although 500-600 mL may appear modest in many adult patients, this secondary circuit prime may produce clinically meaningful hemodilution in patients who are frequently anemic, volume loaded, and near transfusion thresholds, where relatively small changes in hematocrit may alter clinical management. Technique: This report describes an autologous priming technique that uses patient blood available during CPB to displace crystalloid from the RVAD circuit before completion of the outflow connection. The technique requires no change to the conventional RVAD circuit, adds minimal time, and can be discontinued at any point if patient conditions do not safely permit further displacement. Discussion: This technique applies established autologous priming principles to a secondary extracorporeal circuit introduced after CPB has already been established. abstract:

abstract: Abstract Procurement effectiveness remains a persistent challenge in development partners funded development projects, despite growing investments in procurement reforms and market intelligence systems. Drawing on transaction cost economics (TCE) and dynamic capabilities theory (DCT), this study investigates the relationship between tender negotiation (TN) and project procurement performance (PPP), and examines how supply market intelligence (SMI) moderates this relationship in World Bank financed projects in Tanzania. Using a quantitative cross sectional design, data were collected through structured questionnaires from 181 project implementation units (PIUs) based in Dodoma and Dar es Salaam. Purposive sampling was employed to select completed projects where tender negotiation process are commonly involved and respondents involved in the process. The hypothesised relationships were tested using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Findings indicate that tender negotiation significantly associates with project procurement performance. However, supply market intelligence exhibits a negative moderating association, implying that excessive or misaligned intelligence gathering corresponds to elevation of transaction and information processing costs, thereby constraining the performance benefits of negotiation. THE RISE OF ASPIRATIONAL CONSUMPTION IN ASIA: EXPLORING CONSUMER MOTIVATION, MARKET FORCES AND BRAND EQUITY DYNAMICS
abstract: Aspirational consumption has emerged as one of the most prominent features of contemporary consumer markets across Asia. Rapid economic development, urbanisation, digital connectivity, and the expansion of the middle class have transformed consumption from a functional activity into a means of expressing identity, social mobility, and personal success. Consumers increasingly seek products and brands that symbolise achievement and prestige while remaining financially attainable. This shift has fuelled the remarkable growth of masstige and affordable premium brands across sectors such as fashion, electronics, automobiles, cosmetics, and lifestyle products. Although aspirational consumption has attracted growing scholarly attention, existing research remains fragmented, with limited integration of the psychological, socio-cultural, and brand-related factors that collectively shape this phenomenon across Asian markets. The proposed study seeks to develop a comprehensive theoretical framework explaining the growth trajectory of aspirational consumption in Asia by integrating insights on consumer psychology and branding from emerging market literature. Particular emphasis was placed on understanding how intrinsic consumer motivations, such as the need for uniqueness, hedonism, and extended self, drive the purchase intention of customers of masstige products. “So, yeah, that’s a blind spot”: Exploring gender awareness in cultural entrepreneurship education at art and design higher education institutions in the Netherlands
abstract: This study investigates how educators understand and address gender within cultural entrepreneurship education (CEE) in art and design higher education in the Netherlands. CEE has become central to preparing students for increasingly precarious cultural labour markets and, in Europe, is informed by fields long criticised by feminist scholars for privileging traditionally masculine-coded norms such as competitiveness and risk-taking. Despite this, gender has received virtually no explicit attention in CEE policy and research. Drawing on interviews with 18 CEE educators and (co-)heads of Fine Art programmes across all eight state-funded institutions in the Netherlands, the study identifies a disconnect between educators’ awareness of gender inequality and its largely ad hoc integration into teaching. Despite their awareness, educators reinforce this disconnect through gender blindness and non-performativity. Their accounts sustain the belief in CEE’s neutrality, potentially disadvantaging women despite their majority presence in Fine Art higher education.

title: BHunter: Generating Blind-Spot Driving Scenarios for Robustness Testing of Perception Systems
abstract: For widespread deployment of autonomous driving systems (ADS), perception robustness plays a fundamental role. However, maintaining robust perception performance remains a significant challenge, especially under occlusion-rich conditions, known as blind-spot driving scenarios. In these scenarios, traffic participants are temporarily occluded by surrounding objects, making detection and tracking significantly more difficult. However, existing datasets lack sufficient coverage of such scenarios, hindering comprehensive evaluation and improvement of perception capabilities under such conditions. In light of this, we systematically model blind-spot scenarios for the first time and develop a corresponding framework, BHunter , for generating perception test cases. Specifically, this framework enables controllable synthesis of sensor data corresponding to these scenarios, such as generating data with specified occlusion levels, to effectively test perception models. With the help of BHunter , we construct a dataset of 2,000 blind-spot driving scenarios, covering five occlusion levels with a balanced distribution. Each scenario includes synchronized multimodal sensor data, accurate 3D annotations, and temporally consistent frames, and can be directly used for training and evaluating state-of-the-art perception models. Early Observations From the Adoption of Robotic Cholecystectomy by an Acute Care Surgery Service
abstract: Background Laparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is the standard procedure for gallbladder disease. Robotic cholecystectomy (RC) has been increasingly adopted; its role within Acute Care Surgery (ACS) services remains undefined. We evaluated early outcomes following the adoption of RC by an ACS service at a Level I trauma center and compared perioperative outcomes with LC. Methods A retrospective study revealed all adult patients undergoing LC or RC, emergently or electively, by ACS surgeons at a verified Level I trauma center between January 2024 and 2025. Demographic characteristics, operative indications, body mass index (BMI), operative duration, conversion to open surgery, length of stay (LOS), complications, and 30-day readmission were collected. Categorical variables used Fisher’s exact test and continuous variables utilized Welch’s t-test. Results 416 cholecystectomies were performed, including 305 LC (73.3%) and 111 RC (26.7%). Mean patient age was 50.3 years and 33.4% were male, with no demographic differences between groups. Robotic cholecystectomy patients had a higher mean BMI (36.0 vs 32.1 kg/m 2 ; P = 0.002). Operative duration, conversion to open surgery (4.1%), and overall complication rates (10.8%) were similar between LC and RC. Self-Regulated Learning Strategies in English Language Learning Among Pre-Service Teachers
abstract: This study examined the self-regulated learning (SRL) strategies employed by pre-service teachers in English language learning within a private higher education institution. Specifically, it; assessed their use of SRL strategies across the dimensions of self-efficacy, planning, self-monitoring, effort, evaluation, and reflection; identified the perceived benefits and challenges associated with these strategies; and determined whether significant differences existed when students were grouped according to selected demographic variables. A quantitative descriptive–comparative research design was employed involving 100 pre-service teachers selected through quota sampling during the Academic Year 2025–2026. Data were collected using a structured online questionnaire consisting of a researcher-developed demographic section, an adopted SRL–English Language Learning (SRL-ELL) scale, and researcher-developed items measuring perceived benefits and challenges. Results indicated that students demonstrated a generally high level of engagement in self-regulated learning strategies. title: Crystallographic Regulation of LIPSS Formation on Metal Surface Under Randomly Polarized Nanosecond Laser Irradiation
abstract: ABSTRACT Laser‐induced periodic surface structures (LIPSS) provide a mask‐free route for fabricating periodic micro/nanostructures. However, the directional energy modulation imposed by linear polarization can often mask crystallography‐dependent material responses, leaving the role of crystallographic characteristics in LIPSS formation insufficiently understood. Here, a randomly polarized nanosecond laser (1064 nm, 7 ns, 700 kHz) is employed with line‐by‐line scanning to weaken the fixed polarization constraint and reveal crystallographic contributions across FCC FeCoCrNiMn high‐entropy alloy, laser‐induced FCC+BCC 310L stainless steel, BCC 430 stainless steel, and Ni‐P amorphous alloy. The crystalline systems exhibit pronounced grain‐selective LIPSS formation, with the formation probability varying strongly with crystallographic orientation. Correlative electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) analysis further shows that LIPSS orientations preferentially align with projected crystallographic slip traces, indicating that crystallographic slip geometry is closely associated with the directional selection and subsequent development of LIPSS. The FCC, FCC+BCC, and BCC systems exhibit comparable LIPSS spatial periods but progressively reduced continuity and ordering, while grain refinement decreases continuity through increased grain‐boundary (GB)‐related discontinuities. title: Epigenetic Silencing of CYYR1 Promotes Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression Through TRIM21‐Dependent Regulation of HMMR Stability
abstract: ABSTRACT Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains a leading cause of cancer‐related mortality. Integrative multi‐omics and machine‐learning analyses across independent cohorts identified CYYR1 as a frequently downregulated transmembrane protein in LUAD, with low expression associated with poor prognosis and promoter hypermethylation. CYYR1 restoration suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor growth, and metastasis. Mechanistically, CYYR1 facilitated TRIM21‐dependent ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of HMMR, thereby reducing CDC20‐associated oncogenic signaling. Biochemical and cellular analyses supported this CYYR1–TRIM21–HMMR regulatory relationship, while a patient‐derived LUAD organoid model provided proof‐of‐concept evidence that CYYR1 restoration inhibited organoid growth and reduced HMMR, CDC20, and Ki67 expression. CYYR1 restoration also increased cisplatin sensitivity. Genistein treatment was associated with CDC20 modulation and enhanced cisplatin response, and cellular thermal shift assays provided evidence consistent with CDC20 engagement, although CDC20 dependence of the Genistein response remains unproven. Collectively, these findings identify CYYR1 as an epigenetically dysregulated tumor‐suppressive factor that regulates HMMR stability through a TRIM21‐dependent mechanism and reveal a potential therapeutic vulnerability in CYYR1‐deficient …

title: An ATP7A‐Mediated Endogenous Regulation Bio‐Clay Enzyme Enables Self‐Amplified Copper Accumulation for Immunogenic Pyrop
abstract: ABSTRACT Tumor cells maintain abnormal metabolism to support their rapid proliferation, which often compromises the therapeutic outcomes, including pyroptosis. Inhibiting the copper transporter ATPase (ATP7A) effectively disrupts this metabolic balance, yet current exogenous ATP7A inhibition strategies suffer from poor delivery efficiency and low tumor selectivity. Herein, we developed an endogenous regulation strategy to downregulate ATP7A levels using a self‐amplifying bio‐clay enzyme (Bio‐Clayzyme), cupriferous Prussian blue/montmorillonite (CuPB/Mt). Upon tumor cell internalization, CuPB/Mt induces a robust reactive oxygen species (ROS) storm, accompanied by antioxidant depletion, mitochondrial dysfunction, and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) exhaustion. These metabolic disturbances are associated with reduced ATP7A expression, which may subsequently impair ATP7A‐mediated copper efflux. The resulting intracellular copper accumulation may further promote ROS amplification, supporting a positive feedback loop among ROS production, ATP7A downregulation, and copper retention. Specifically, the introduction of Mt optimizes the Cu d‐band center and strengthens tumor cell adhesion, thereby boosting the multi‐enzyme‐like catalytic activity and enabling efficient utilization of short‐lived ROS. title: Simulation‐Guided Tracer Optimization for Magnetic Particle Spectroscopy: Interplay of Core, Shell and Anisotropy Across Physiological‐Range Viscosities for Single‐ and Dual‐Frequency Excitation
abstract: ABSTRACT Detection of magnetic nanoparticles (MNP) relies on their nonlinear magnetic response, changing with the local environment in vivo. Employing an effective viscosity model within stochastic coupled Néel–Brownian simulations, we quantify how viscosity (0.8–50 000 mPa·s) affects signal intensity of single‐frequency magnetic particle spectroscopy (MPS, 25 kHz) and frequency‐mixing MPS (FM‐MPS; f H = 40.5 kHz, f L = 0.063 kHz). We investigate single‐core, non‐interacting MNP with various core sizes (12–28 nm), hydrodynamic shell thicknesses (5–100 nm), and anisotropy (4–200 kJ m − 3 ), using dominant readouts (MPS: third‐harmonic; FM‐MPS: f H + 2 f L mixing‐term). Increasing viscosity progressively suppresses Brownian rotation, with thicker shells affected at lower viscosities, and drives signals toward an immobilization plateau. Under the simulated conditions, MNP appear distinguishable in blood‐associated viscosities using MPS, whereas distinguishability is pronounced in cellular/tissue‐like viscosities with FM‐MPS. Moderate anisotropy (∼20–40 kJ m − 3 ) enhances signals by ∼10%, whereas higher anisotropies suppress relaxation, finally collapsing the signal. While large cores maximize the signal at fixed particle number, dosage‐normalized conditions suggest favorable performance for intermediate cores (∼15–18 nm). title: Wanted Dead or Alive: Anticipatory Regulation of Digital Immortality Platforms
abstract: The loss of a loved one is a painful and unique experience. To address that loss, technology companies are exploring the potential of digital immortality platforms, preserving individuals through artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on digital data generated in life. These datasets can be collected from scraping social media profiles and text conversations postmortem or intentionally recording videos and conversations with a person prior to their death for training AI models. In the face of any novel technology, the potential risks and benefits should guide the responsible development and deployment of every product. However, the liminal regulatory space that digital immortality technologies occupy makes this type of evaluation a difficult undertaking. One such approach would be to examine analogous sectors to the novel technology as a first step in developing regulations in that space. In this paper, we identify several ethical risks presented by digital immortality technologies and propose four analogies to contextualize possible regulation: psychology/grief counseling, death care/remains management, social media platforms, and AI companion services. We examine the parallels between digital immortality and each of these analogies in a proactive effort to prevent harms before the widespread public adoption of this technology. The contributions of this paper are a prelim…
