title: Synergistic Regulation of High Dielectric Constant and H‐Aggregation for Efficient and Thickness‐Tolerant Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD‐6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8‐BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8‐BO) and H‐aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8‐BO:BMD‐6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high‐efficiency, thickness‐tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.

title: MS ‐ FSSM : A Multi‐Scale Frequency‐Sensitive State Space Model for Brain Tumor Segmentation in Multi‐Modal MRI
abstract: Accurate automatic segmentation of brain tumors is clinically essential, yet remains challenging due to their irregular morphology, ill‐defined boundaries, and weak contrast in enhancing regions. To alleviate these challenges, we propose MS‐FSSM (Multi‐Scale Frequency‐Sensitive State Space Model). The architecture features three decoupled, parallel encoding streams—convolutional neural network (CNN), vision transformer (ViT), and state space model (SSM)—designed respectively to capture local texture, global semantic context, and diffuse long‐range structural dependencies. Following multi‐scale feature fusion, a frequency‐aware enhancement module is introduced to recover high‐frequency boundary details. In the decoding stage, semantic‐gated skip connections suppress background interference, while a state‐space refinement module integrated at the mid‐resolution level helps improve segmentation completeness and boundary continuity of tumor regions. Evaluated on two public benchmarks—the Medical Segmentation Decathlon (MSD) Task01 and BraTS 2025 Task02—MS‐FSSM achieves 0.87 Dice on enhancing tumor (ET) in both glioma (MSD) and meningioma (BraTS), with Surface Dice of 0.91 in MSD. Meanwhile, it only requires 11.36 M parameters and 2.06 GFLOPs. Experimental results indicate that our method achieves a favorable trade‐off between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency, offe…

title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF DISASTER EMERGENCY RESPONSE TRAINING ON FAMILY FIRST AID SKILLS IN EMERGENCY SITUATIONS IN AN EARTHQUAKE-PRONE COMMUNITY
abstract: Earthquakes can create emergency situations requiring rapid and accurate first aid. Families act as initial responders before healthcare professionals arrive; therefore, first aid skills need to be strengthened through structured training. This study aimed to analyze the effectiveness of disaster emergency response training on the first aid skills of families in the earthquake-prone area of ​​Mesjid Raya District. A pre-experimental design with a one-group pretest-posttest approach was employed. Thirty-five respondents from Perumnas Neuheun, Ujung Batee Village, were selected using consecutive sampling. The intervention comprised education, demonstrations, and emergency response simulations. Data were collected using a first aid skills questionnaire and analyzed using the Wilcoxon Signed Rank test. Prior to the intervention, 37.1% of respondents possessed moderate-level skills, while 62.9% possessed good-level skills. Following the intervention, all respondents (100%) achieved the "good" category. The mean skill score increased from 26.80 to 29.71. The Wilcoxon test results indicated a significant improvement (Z = -4.253; p < 0.001). Disaster emergency response training is effective in enhancing family first aid skills. Training programs incorporating education, demonstrations, and simulations can be implemented to strengthen family preparedness in earthquake-prone regions.

title: The Influence of the Fed Rate and the Dow Jones Index on the Movement of the Composite Stock Price Index (IHSG) for the 2016-2025 Period
abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of the Fed Rate and the Dow Jones Index on the movement of the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) for the 2016-2025 period. This study uses a quantitative method with a saturated sampling technique, encompassing 10 years of reporting data on the Fed Rate, the Dow Jones Index, and the JCI. Data analysis techniques included classical assumption tests, regression analysis, correlation coefficients, coefficients of determination, and hypothesis testing. The results show that partially, the Fed Rate has a significant positive effect on the JCI with a coefficient of determination of 65.4% and a t-count of 2,442 > t-table 2,262. The Dow Jones Index also has a significant positive effect on the JCI with a coefficient of determination of 84.3% and a t-count of 4.425 > t-table 2.262. Simultaneously, the Fed Rate and the Dow Jones Index have a significant positive effect on the movement of the JCI with the regression equation $Y = 4051.111 + 127.109X_1 + 0.071X_2$. The simultaneous coefficient of determination is 76%, while the remaining 24% is influenced by other factors not examined in this study. The hypothesis test obtained an F-count > F-table (11,078 > 4,737). In conclusion, there is a significant effect of the Fed Rate and the Dow Jones Index on the movement of the Jakarta Composite Index.

title: Volatility Forecasting: A Fused Filter Algorithm
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a fused filter algorithm (FFA) for volatility forecasting. The FFA extracts latent volatility by solving a penalized optimization problem, a formulation related to the HP filter and Whittaker–Henderson smoothing. To investigate the empirical performance of the FFA, we apply it to 10 major stock indices and compare its performance, both in‐sample and out‐of‐sample, against different benchmarks. The results show that FFA significantly dominates the benchmark models across different loss functions and horizons, and this dominance mainly concentrates in normal and low‐volatility regimes. A volatility timing strategy is used to evaluate the economic value of the FFA, and the results also confirm its competitiveness in comparison with the benchmark models. In summary, the FFA provides a computationally efficient alternative tool for market volatility filtering and forecasting.

PrOMet: Accurate and Robust Metal‐Binding Site and Type Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal binding to proteins is crucial for many biological functions, yet the prediction of metal‐binding sites and metal types remains underexplored compared to other biomolecular interactions. Despite advances in deep learning, computational methods have achieved limited success in this area; even the best‐reported approaches reach only moderate localization accuracy on high‐resolution crystal structures, and even worse when applied to medium‐resolution data. We hypothesize that the main challenge lies in the nature of metal binding. While the putative sites span the entire protein surface, actual binding requires the atomic‐level coordination geometry. We present a structure‐based metal binding site and type predictor, PrOMet, in this work, which leverages a Prune‐and‐Optimization strategy built upon two hierarchically connected machine learning architectures. This strategy allows the method to effectively narrow the search space while maintaining robustness to AlphaFold models and medium‐resolution cryo‐EM structures. PrOMet outperforms existing methods, including structure‐based and language model‐based predictors, achieving a PR‐AUC of 0.739 for metal ion localization and an average F1‐score of 0.743 for metal type classification—Zn, Ca, Mg, Mn, Fe, Cu, respectively. PrOMet can be an effective tool for allocating uncertain metal positions and types within protein s…

title: DSCrisk: A dual-view and substructure aware based method for drug-drug interaction risk-level prediction enhanced by contrastive learning
From Prediction Markets To Capability Markets: Epistemic Extractivism In Generative AI
abstract: Some Generative AI (GenAI) platforms are introducing advertising into their conversational interfaces, others have committed not to. We use this divergence as a starting point, and argue that it obscures a deeper convergence: all major GenAI platform operators instrument the interfaces through which users interact with GenAI models, and all are positioned to develop and monetise AI capability products from the records this instrumentation produces. Drawing on analysis of the infrastructure that standardises and structures the recording of GenAI interactions, alongside industry documentation, research, and reporting, this paper surfaces interaction telemetry data as a distinct data object in the political economy of GenAI: a record of the cognitive processes materialised at the GenAI interface. We identify two forms of extraction co-constituted with this data object. Behavioural extraction, continuous with surveillance capitalism, captures user states for the prediction and shaping of user behaviour. Cognitive extraction, in contrast, captures teleological labour -- the labour through which users cajole GenAI platforms into doing what they want -- and refines this into AI capability products. In this context we draw on Grosfoguel's account of the appropriation of knowledge from marginalised communities to argue that cognitive extraction is an example of epistemic extractivism, a…

title: Algorithmic Gender Prediction Is Illegitimate, but Gender Imputation Can Yield Valid Measurements
abstract: Machine learning ethics researchers, critical HCI scholars, and interdisciplinary academics have argued that algorithmically predicting gender is wrong. At the same time, others in the same research communities rely on predicted gender labels to study gender disparities and develop algorithmic fairness techniques. Taking both of these perspectives in good faith pushes us to believe that algorithmic gender prediction simultaneously cannot be trusted and at the same time can identify genuine gender disparities. How do we reconcile these two seemingly contradictory intuitions? We draw a distinction between two questions: whether algorithmic gender prediction is wrong, being illegitimate and thereby contributing to harm; and whether algorithmic gender prediction is wrong, being invalid and thereby producing unusable measurements. Our analysis translates different arguments against gender prediction into these terms of legitimacy and validity and shows how gender imputation applied for fairness purposes can be both illegitimate and still yield valid disparity measurements. We clarify this bind by drawing upon transfeminist literature to distinguish two forms of sexism: sexism that targets women and femininity, and sexism that targets transgender and nonbinary people. While gender imputation can produce valid measurements for the former, it is illegitimate and harmful for the latter.…

title: GRAVIDRO: deep sea underwater gravity battery parks scalable toward TWh energy storage capacity
abstract: Energy reservoirs are an ongoing challenge for renewable/green energy production system based on non- programmable sources, like wind or solar energy. Several solutions are being studied and implemented, from hydro-reservoirs to mechanical energy storages, from hydrogen to electrical batteries. Gravity batteries are also being tested: here we present a conceptual study of an underwater gravity battery park in deep sea waters, that we name Gravidro, which appears well suitable to be scalable towards very large energy levels, that is the TWh scale (a few Petajoules). Gravidro involves well established technologies and negligible ecological impact, joined to no usage of land and extremely low accident relevance even in case of severe faults. At the TWh energy storage level, for a mid-size developed country consuming routinely about 40 GW of electrical power, besides maintaining the available energy continuity on a day by day basis as well as the seasonal energy coverage, Gravidro could guarantee a stored energy sufficient to run for a day even in case of a severe electrical black-out. Gravidro parks would make intermittent energy generation systems (solar, wind) the most favorable source of green/renewable energy, aiming to strongly reduce the usage of fossil sources or nuclear fuel.

title: When AI Does the Work, What Is Learning For? Post-Instrumental Learning and the Risk of Capacity Dissolution
abstract: As AI systems become capable of producing the essays, code, reports, summaries, plans, and decisions through which institutions usually recognize competence, a familiar question becomes harder to answer: what is learning for? Existing AI ethics rightly emphasizes present failures—bias, opacity, hallucination, labor extraction, privacy risk, and weak accountability. But if the case for learning rests only on those failures, then each technical improvement appears to weaken it. This article develops a different answer. Using the idealization of AI that executes specified tasks flawlessly while lacking authority over purposes, legitimacy, and responsibility, we argue for post-instrumental learning: learning that preserves the capacities people and institutions need when many useful outputs can be delegated. We analyze five such capacities—end-setting, reason-giving, contestability, refusal/revision, and participation—and name their erosion capacity dissolution. The central case is assessment under generative AI. When a polished artifact no longer reliably evidences understanding, institutions must assess the learner's accountable relation to AI-mediated work rather than the artifact alone. The takeaway is practical: AI governance should evaluate not only whether systems perform well, but also whether their deployment leaves people able to understand, challenge, revise, and share r…

Scenario-based optimisation of steel production technologies: A comparative assessment for Mobarakeh Steel Group's capacity enhancement
abstract: This study proposes a systematic framework for selecting optimal ironmaking technologies to enhance the sustainable production capacity of Mobarakeh Steel Company (MSC) in Isfahan, Iran. Five commercial technologies – Midrex, Corex, Finex, SL/RN, and ITmk3 – were evaluated across nine scenarios with varying shares of scrap, DRI, and hot metal, emphasising low-grade haematite utilisation. A multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) approach assessed energy use, CO 2 emissions, water consumption, and capital and operating costs. Scenarios were optimised for raw material flexibility, environmental compliance, and a target 6 Mt/year capacity increase. Results show that a mix of 25% scrap and 75% hot metal, using COREX or a hybrid COREX–FINEX/ITmk3 system, is the most favourable, reducing CO 2 emissions by 18%, energy use by 22%, and raw material costs by 30% compared with conventional BF–BOF routes. The findings offer practical guidance for integrated steel plants pursuing sustainable and cost-effective production, especially in regions rich in low-grade iron ores under carbon pricing policies.

title: Valorization of Waste Eggshells through Pyrolysis: Functional Screening of the Liquid Fraction for Antioxidant Capacity and Antibacterial Potential
abstract: The conversion of food-processing by-products into functional materials has gained increasing attention within sustainable waste management strategies. In the present work, waste chicken eggshells were thermochemically converted into a liquid pyrolysis fraction under solvent-free conditions, and its antioxidant-related characteristics together with antibacterial activity were investigated. Pyrolysis was conducted in a fixed-bed reactor using 500 g of powdered eggshell under a continuous nitrogen flow. The temperature was increased at a rate of 10 °C/min until reaching 400 ± 3 °C and maintained for 360 min. The obtained liquid fraction contained 15.34 ± 0.83 mg GAE/g of total phenolic equivalents and 3.51 ± 0.02 mg QE/g of total flavonoid equivalents. Antioxidant evaluation revealed a total antioxidant capacity of 10.54 ± 0.35 mg TE/L. Radical scavenging experiments demonstrated a negligible response toward DPPH radicals (0.32 ± 0.09% inhibition), while a substantially greater activity was detected in the ABTS•⁺ assay, reaching 42.35 ± 0.96% inhibition. Furthermore, the cupric ion reducing capacity was determined as 20.70 ± 2.25 mg TE/L, indicating the presence of compounds capable of electron donation despite the mineral-rich nature of the raw material. The antibacterial assessment showed that the pyrolysis liquid failed to generate inhibition zones against the tested reference…

title: Bearing capacity and safety factors of ring foundations in spatially variable soils: a hybrid FELA-machine learning approach
abstract: Abstract Ring foundations efficiently support axisymmetric structures like silos, storage tanks, chimneys, and cooling towers with reduced concrete volume compared to solid circular foundations. Their ultimate bearing capacity is strongly affected by asymmetric loading and spatial variability in soil properties. This study presents a hybrid machine learning framework to predict normalized bearing capacity factors and safety factors for ring foundations in spatially variable cohesive-frictional (c-φ) soils. Datasets were generated via finite element limit analysis (FELA) in OptumG2, incorporating random field modeling of effective cohesion (c’) (lognormal, depth-linear mean: µ c’ = 10 kPa, k = 1 kPa/m, COV = 0.3) and friction angle (φ’ up to 40°). Four loading configurations (complete, internal half, middle half, external half), inner-to-outer radius ratios of 0–0.9, rough/smooth interfaces, and nine anisotropic scale-of-fluctuation cases (horizontal: 10–60 m; vertical: 2–8 m) were analyzed. A Convolutional Neural Network processed random field images and parameters, achieving R² > 0.95 and relative errors < 3%. External half and complete loading gave highest capacities; internal half reduced them by up to 40%. Spatial variability in c’ and φ’ contracted failure envelopes by 10–25%, emphasizing reliability-based design. The framework dramatically reduces computational cost versu…

Mechanism‐based kinetic modeling of standard NH 3 ‐ SCR over Cu‐ SSZ ‐13 catalysts using experimentally determined parameters
abstract: Abstract Cu‐SSZ‐13 is a key catalyst for NH 3 ‐SCR in mobile aftertreatment systems, yet reliable kinetic modeling remains challenging due to the complex interplay among Cu speciation, NH 3 solvation, and oxidation side reactions. In this work, NO oxidation, NH 3 oxidation, and standard SCR over Cu‐SSZ‐13 catalysts with varying Cu loadings were systematically investigated, and a mechanism‐informed kinetic model was developed using experimentally derived kinetic parameters. The results show that NO oxidation and NH 3 oxidation are primarily associated with multinuclear Cu species, whereas standard SCR mainly proceeds on exchanged Cu ions through Cu II /Cu I redox cycling. Both NH 3 oxidation and standard SCR exhibit distinct low‐ and high‐temperature kinetic regimes associated with NH 3 ‐solvated mobile Cu species and framework‐bound immobile Cu species, respectively. The model successfully reproduces experimental reaction behavior across various Cu loadings and temperatures, demonstrating the effectiveness of experimentally constrained kinetic modeling for SCR reactor simulation and aftertreatment system optimization.

title: An Efficient Graph Neural Network‐Based Routing Optimization Mechanism for Congestion‐Aware Software‐Defined Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT Software‐Defined Networking (SDN) has developed as a suitable solution for complex networks with a flexible and programmable networking paradigm. SDN infrastructure is facing critical challenges in efficient routing under dynamic and congestion‐prone conditions. This research paper proposes an efficient Improved Graph Neural Network (IGNN)‐based routing optimization mechanism designed for achieving congestion‐aware traffic management in SDN environments. The proposed model uses the inherent graph structure of network topology by representing switches as nodes and communication links as edges, and this mode is utilizing real‐time network metrics such as bandwidth, delay, queue length, and packet loss as feature inputs. A deep GNN framework is used for learning topology‐aware node by incorporating through message passing, and this will enable accurate prediction of optimal routing paths under varying traffic conditions. Unlike conventional GNN‐based routing approaches that primarily learn topology‐aware node representations through graph message passing, the proposed IGNN integrates topology representation with congestion prediction and multi‐objective routing optimization considering throughput, packet delay, packet loss, and congestion utilization, enabling congestion‐aware adaptive path selection. The suggested model makes use of congestion‐aware cost functions for lo…

title: Efficient and Polarized Emission From Cs 3 Cu 2 Br 5 Nanorods via Dithiol Ligand Exchange
abstract: ABSTRACT Ternary copper halides, such as Cs 3 Cu 2 X 5 (X = Cl, Br, or I), are a new class of lead‐free nanocrystals with exceptional optical properties, making them promising for photo‐down‐conversion display applications. However, recent studies on blue‐emitting ternary copper halide nanorods (NRs) have reported low photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQY), rendering them inadequate for displays. Using a dithiol ligand‐assisted growth method, here we have synthesized Cs 3 Cu 2 Br 5 NRs with a uniform rod morphology that exhibit an improved PLQY of 63% and a photoluminescence excitation (PLE) anisotropy of 0.201. We used transient absorption spectroscopy to explore the exciton recombination mechanisms and provide insights into the optical performance differences between 1,2‐ethanedithiol (EDT) and 1,6‐hexanedithiol (HDT)‐treated NRs. Density functional theory calculations are conducted to evaluate ligand binding modes, binding energies, and lattice distortion. Our findings indicate that short‐chain dithiols (EDT/HDT) enable bidentate ligand‐assisted shape control of Cs 3 Cu 2 Br 5 NRs by displacing long‐chain oleate ligands and forming Cu–S − bonds orthogonal to the preferential growth direction. Control experiments with monothiol ligands show that these ligands demonstrate effective surface passivation but do not promote nanorod elongation. These findings offer new perspective…

title: Carbon Markets and Natural Climate Solutions in Brazil: Institutional Coherence Across Biodiversity, Land‐Use and Territorial Governance
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how natural climate solutions (NCS) are institutionalised through carbon market governance in tropical contexts, focusing on Brazil's emerging Emissions Trading System (SBCE). It contributes to debates on the effectiveness, equity and governance of nature‐based climate action by analysing how carbon market instruments interact with biodiversity governance, land‐use regulation and socio‐ecological systems characterised by territorial diversity and inequality in Brazil. Using a qualitative multi‐method design combining statutory and document analysis, legislative process tracing, and computationally assisted text analysis, the study evaluates horizontal, vertical and functional coherence across climate, biodiversity, land‐use and territorial governance domains. The findings show that the SBCE represents a significant regulatory innovation, supported by a technically advanced architecture, particularly in monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) systems and registries. However, institutional coherence remains partial and uneven, with stronger integration in financial and technical domains than across biodiversity, land‐use and territorial governance systems. Stakeholder patterns are also uneven: governmental and financial actors have greater procedural visibility, while territorial, Indigenous and environmental actors are more strongly concentrate…

title: Effect of Aronia (Aronia melanocarpa) Pomace Powder on the Physicochemical, Bioactive, and Microbiological Properties of Buffalo Yogurt during Refrigerated Storage
abstract: Aronia (Aronia melanocarpa) pomace is a fruit-processing by-product rich in bioactive compounds with potential for valorization as a functional food ingredient. This work evaluated buffalo yogurt enriched with solar collector-dried aronia pomace powder (APP) at 1% (APP1), 2% (APP2), and 3% (APP3), focusing on changes in physicochemical, microbial, color, and bioactive attributes over 21 days at refrigerated conditions. APP supplementation significantly increased dry matter content from 15.67% in the control to 18.51% in APP3 (p<0.05). Although the treatments had comparable pH values initially, increasing APP levels were generally accompanied by greater titratable acidity. Compared with the control, higher APP levels increased syneresis and reduced water-holding capacity, although syneresis decreased and water-holding capacity increased during storage. Viable lactic acid bacteria exceeded 7 log CFU g⁻¹ throughout the experiment, and by day 21 their counts were significantly greater in APP2 and APP3 than in the control (p<0.05). No yeast or mold growth was detected at any sampling point. Increasing APP concentration produced a progressively darker and redder yogurt with greater color saturation. A dose-dependent enrichment in anthocyanins and phenolics was evident, and APP3 consistently contained the greatest amounts during storage. APP3 also generally exhibited the strongest DPP…

title: V─O─Ti Bridge‐Bond Polarity Boosts Na + Migration in V‐Based Fluorophosphates for Fast Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐based fluorophosphates are promising high‐energy‐density cathodes for next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, the pronounced degradation of Na + diffusion at high voltage hinders their fast‐charging capability. Herein, a Ti 4+ ‐doping‐induced bridge‐bond‐polarity‐driven strategy is proposed to reshape the V electronic structure for facilitating V─O electron exchange. Correspondingly, voltage hysteresis, polarization, and structural distortion at high voltage are suppressed, accompanied by enhanced electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, the polar V─O─Ti bridge bonds expand the dominant one‐ and two‐dimensional Na + transport channels by inducing bridging‐O displacement, further boosting Na + migration capability. Therefore, Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 with V─O─Ti delivers high capacities of 121.8 and 62.1 mA h g −1 at 0.1C and 50C, respectively, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Additionally, the 0.92‐Ah Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 //HC pouch cell exhibits 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1C. At the 9 Ah scale, the pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 154 Wh kg −1 . This synergistic reinforcement strategy driven by bridge‐bond polarity paves the way for sustainable high‐power polyanionic SIBs.

Design Approaches for Oxygen Reduction Systems for Warehouse Storage Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxygen reduction systems (ORS) are protection systems, with a design protection objective to limit fire spread beyond the point of ignition. Research has shown that the prescriptive design methods, in VdS 3527, EN 16750, and ISO 20338, are not appropriate as prescriptive design methods as they result in insufficient protection levels. In this paper, two design approaches for ORS for warehouse applications have been developed to address the lack of robust design methods. One design approach was aimed at creating a robust prescriptive method for determination of design oxygen concentrations for ORS. Such a method needs to cover a vast majority of storage configurations and ignition sources. The need to consider intentional fires is also discussed in this paper, as these fires are common in warehouses. The prescriptive method is based on the limiting oxygen concentration for fire propagation (LOC FP ) determined by large‐scale testing performed by Factory Mutual Insurance Company (FM) complemented with a procedure using the Controlled Atmosphere Cone Calorimeter (CACC). The second design approach was aimed at creating a performance‐based design framework for specific applications. The framework is based on an in‐depth analysis of the stored goods, storage configuration, and possible ignition sources. If the specific application is comparable to the large‐scale test setup,…

title: Architecting Anisotropic Force‐Responsive Bidirectional High‐Contrast Three‐Color Fluorescence Switches via Effective Molecular Modulation for High‐Security Information Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Although bidirectional three‐color fluorescent molecular switches triggered by anisotropic force are promising for enhancing the security of information storage, the engineering and development of such force‐responsive smart emissive materials face significant challenges, rendering them extremely rare. Here, 13 uncommon tricolored mechanofluorochromic luminogens were obtained through efficient molecular engineering strategies synergistically integrating substituent variation and positional isomeric approaches, three of which exhibited exceedingly scarce force‐induced hypsochromic and bathochromic bidirectional fluorescence responses. More specifically, employing dibenzofulvene as the core scaffold, a family of 20 fluorene‐based fluorogenic compounds was elaborately constructed by incorporating pyrene, tetraphenylethene, and three isomeric carbazole moieties at the conjugated extension sites, with phenyl and regioisomeric trifluoromethylphenyl groups respectively attached to the two flanking positions. Next, a three‐step high‐efficiency screening protocol was devised for these luminogens: first assessing mechanoresponsive fluorescence behaviors, then evaluating the three‐color mechanofluorochromic capabilities, and finally determining whether the selected force‐responsive tricolored fluorescence switches could realize bidirectional three‐color fluorescence switching aft…

title: Quantifying Dynamic Changes in Stem Storage‐Water Use and Rehydration in Mature Trees: A Study on Pinus sylvestris Trees Exposed to Increased Atmospheric and Soil Drought
abstract: ABSTRACT Forests increasingly experience hot droughts, characterized by rising vapour pressure deficits (VPD) and declining soil moisture, highlighting the need to better understand water fluxes within trees. While stomatal conductance and transpiration are well studied, upstream fluxes such as internal stem water storage use and rehydration dynamics remain poorly quantified, despite their importance for maintaining tissue hydration and growth. Here, we quantify storage‐water use and rehydration dynamics by combining high‐resolution sap flow and dendrometer measurements in mature Pinus sylvestris at the VPDrought experiment of the Pfynwald research platform, where rain‐water input and VPD are independently manipulated. Fluxes were analyzed over the 2024 growing season in relation to VPD and soil water potential ( ψ soil ). The relative contribution of internal stem water storage to daily transpiration increased with drought, rising from about 10% under well‐watered conditions to up to 55% under dry conditions, mainly caused by reduced transpiration while storage water use is sustained. Notably, under mild soil drought, high nighttime VPD substantially constrained nighttime tissue rehydration fluxes. Overall, our novel framework highlights the dynamic role of stem water storage in modulating water potentials during drought and demonstrates the importance of explicitly considerin…

title: Bromine Retention Versus Electrochemical Accessibility in a Ferri‐/Ferrocyanide–Bromine Flow Battery
abstract: Bromine retention in aqueous redox flow batteries can be improved by complexation, but the resulting gain in stability is often accompanied by losses in electrochemical accessibility and transport. Here, we investigate a ferri‐/ferrocyanide–bromine flow battery based on soluble ferri‐/ferrocyanide and bromine/bromide redox electrolytes. Three bromine/bromide positive‐electrolyte conditions were compared: a pristine bromide electrolyte, an electrolyte containing the bromine‐complexing agent (BCA) N ‐ethyl‐ N ‐methylpyrrolidinium bromide ([EMPyrr]Br), and the same electrolyte after nitrogen presparging. Charge–capacity retention after 70 cycles increased from 23.4% for the pristine electrolyte to 34.9% with [EMPyrr]Br and 66.0% with [EMPyrr]Br and nitrogen presparging. Because neither a nitrogen‐pre‐sparged BCA‐free control nor an alternative inert‐gas control was examined, the higher retention cannot be attributed uniquely to nitrogen; deaeration and sparging‐induced redistribution of bromine‐rich phases may also contribute. Improved retention was accompanied by increased polarization, higher ex situ electrolyte impedance, and an initial voltage rise associated with bromine‐rich phase formation. Postcycling cyclic voltammetry provides qualitative evidence of bromine crossover, while Raman spectroscopy shows condition‐dependent bromine‐related signatures in the sampled liquid pha…

title: Stabilization of sesame oil during storage: mechanisms of endogenous phenolics in modulating oxidation kinetics and volatile retention
abstract: Abstract BACKGROUND Sesame oil is a high‐value edible oil with unique flavor and nutritional properties, but oxidative deterioration during storage compromises its quality and flavor stability. Endogenous phenolic compounds, particularly lignans, exhibit antioxidant activity and may regulate oxidation processes and volatile compound preservation. This study investigated the effects of endogenous phenolics on oxidative kinetics and flavor stability of sesame oil during storage. RESULTS Sesame oil models with different phenolic levels (SEO, SEO+P, and SEO++P) were stored at 45 °C for 40 days. Sesamin degradation followed zero‐order kinetics, showing good fitting performance in phenol‐enriched samples ( R 2 > 0.94), suggesting its potential as a marker for oxidative stability evaluation. Phenolic enrichment significantly ( P < 0.05) delayed increases in acid value, peroxide value and carbonyl compounds, at the same time as mitigating the decline of cis ‐CC bonds. Moreover, phenolics enhanced the retention of desirable heterocyclic aroma compounds, reducing pyrazine loss from 33.39% in SEO to 22.02% in SEO++P. Meanwhile, the formation of undesirable aldehydes decreased from 48.29% to 26.34%. Correlation analysis revealed positive associations between lignans and heterocyclic compounds ( r = 0.597–0.773), but negative correlations with carbonyl compounds ( r = −0.538 to −0.790). Vo…

title: Real-time decentralized multi-actuator chassis control strategy for vehicle lateral stability based on nonlinear MPC
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Decentralized Multi-Actuator Chassis Control (DMCC) strategy for vehicle lateral stability, utilizing real-time Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC). The proposed hierarchical framework decomposes integrated chassis control into a vehicle-level lateral dynamics control and multiple structurally identical wheel-level control for tire force realization. This modular design offers exceptional configurability, adapting seamlessly to diverse electric vehicle chassis configurations ranging from basic chassis configuration to fully actuated platforms featuring four-wheel independent drive, steering, and braking. To ensure microsecond-level deterministic computation, the vehicle-level controller employs a linearized model within an analytical quadratic programming formulation. At the wheel level, a Piecewise Affine (PWA) tire model with precomputed region-specific Jacobians facilitates efficient real-time linearization. Furthermore, a modified Hildreth’s active-set solver, augmented with Cholesky factorization and physics-informed warm-start strategies, is implemented to exploit spatiotemporal correlations, thereby achieving rapid convergence. High-fidelity CarSim co-simulations of high-speed double lane change maneuvers under varying friction conditions validate the approach. Results demonstrate substantial improvements in yaw rate tracking and sidesli…

title: Active vibration suppression of electric vehicle drive systems based on flux-linkage-current inverse mapping
abstract: Electric drive systems (EDSs) often exhibit complex coupled vibrations caused by interactions between electromagnetic nonlinearities and mechanical excitations. To characterize these interactions and develop an effective vibration-suppression method, this study establishes a multi-physics coupled model of an EDS that accounts for temperature-dependent electromagnetic parameters, magnetic-field harmonics, and time-varying mesh stiffness. The model accuracy is verified using test-bench measurements. Based on this, the coupled vibration behavior of the EDS is analyzed, and an active control method based on flux-linkage-current inverse mapping is proposed. The results show that nonlinear mechanical excitations generate sideband current components associated with the gear-meshing frequency, whereas electromagnetic harmonics intensify dynamic fluctuations in the gear drivetrain, indicating evident cross-domain coupling in the EDS. The vector-control system compensates for the temperature-induced decrease in magnetic flux density by increasing the fundamental component of the stator current. After harmonic-current injection, the maximum fluctuation amplitude of the electromagnetic torque is reduced by 43.89%, and the amplitudes of the 6 f e and 12 f e torque harmonics decrease by 46.17% and 80.38%, respectively. The proposed strategy also attenuates the corresponding harmonic componen…

title: The operation of electric buses by considering changes to the energy production structure in Poland.
abstract: This article provides a discussion on the results of the author’s in-house study on the greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions generated over the life cycle of the electric buses (BEV) used in Poland’s public transport services. The life cycle assessment (LCA) method was employed to evaluate the greenhouse gas emissions. The relevant changes to the energy mix, assumed in line with the electricity generation projections for Poland by 2040, have caused a drop in the average greenhouse gas emissions from electric buses in the consecutive years. For the energy mix envisaged for the years 2025, 2030, 2035, and 2040, being the source of the electricity consumed to charge batteries of electric buses, a decline in the mean emissions by 5%, 13.5%, 30%, and 39%, respectively, can be observed in comparison with the 2022 energy mix. Additionally, the article describes an original model for assessing the greenhouse gas emissions from electric buses which enables the GHG emissions to be studied with reference to various sources of electric energy.

title: Enhanced High‐Voltage Fast‐Charging Capability for Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes via Multifunctional Biphasic Interfacial Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐capacity Li‐rich Mn‐based oxide cathodes exhibit exceptional specific capacity density; however, their utilization encounters challenges pertaining to sluggish Li + ion transport kinetics and severe interfacial issues in high‐voltage lithium‐ion batteries, especially under the working condition of fast charging. Here, a protective biphasic shell layer coupled with B/Al co‐doping in the near‐surface bulk phase region is designed on Li 1.2 Mn 0.54 Ni 0.13 Co 0.13 O 2 cathode by means of feasible and facile chemical surface reconstruction engineering to solve performance degradation and structural collapse. The biphasic layer that is in situ fabricated consists of an amorphous Li 2 B 4 O 7 coating as the outermost layer and a spinel phase structure as the inner layer, respectively. Structural analysis confirms that the engineered interface assisted by surface co‐doping enhances interfacial stability by promoting the fast transfer of Li + ion and mitigating surface side reactions. As a consequence, the engineered batteries are demonstrated to achieve remarkable performance, delivering 138 mAh g −1 at 5 C, along with enhanced cycling stability, retaining 90.07% of their initial capacity after 300 cycles within a voltage range of 2.0–4.8 V compared to their layered oxide counterparts. This work provides an interface/surface modification strategy that simultaneously addr…

title: Securing Autonomous Vehicle Movement: GPS Spoofing Detection and Correction Using a Variationally Mimetic Operator Network for Improved Operational Integrity
abstract: ABSTRACT The Global Positioning System (GPS) enables accurate vehicle positioning by processing signals transmitted from navigation satellites. Nevertheless, GPS spoofing attacks, which send counterfeit satellite signals to deceive GPS receivers, pose a significant threat to autonomous vehicle navigation by causing incorrect position estimation, route deviations, potential collisions, and violations of traffic regulations. In this manuscript, an Autonomous Vehicle Movement for GPS Spoofing Detection and Correction utilizing a Variationally Mimetic Operator Network (AVM‐GPS‐SDC‐VMON) framework is proposed to secure autonomous vehicles by accurately detecting and correcting GPS spoofing attacks. The input data created from the Car Learning to Act (CARLA) simulator is used in this study. These data are fed to VMON for detecting and classifying the GPS signals as either authentic or spoofed. The Elk Herd Optimization Algorithm (EHOA) is introduced to optimize detection factors for better precision and flexibility. The proposed approach was implemented in Python, and experiments were analyzed utilizing well‐established statistical and computational metrics to ensure reliability, robustness, and efficiency. The proposed AVM‐GPS‐SDC‐VMON achieved 99.36% accuracy, 99.6% precision, 98% detection rate (DR), and 0.02% false alarm rate (FAR) with a reduced computational time of 1.2 s compa…

title: Circular Transformation in the Silk Sector: A Fuzzy Delphi–DEMATEL Analysis of Critical Factors
abstract: ABSTRACT The circular transformation in the silk industry is crucial for enhancing resource efficiency and minimizing waste. Despite growing interest in circularity within the textile sector, the silk industry remains underexplored. This study addresses this gap by systematically assessing the barriers and enablers influencing circular economy adoption in silk. A two‐stage methodology was applied. First, a comprehensive literature review combined with expert input identified key factors, which were then validated using the fuzzy Delphi method (FDM) with 16 experts from industry and academia, resulting in nine barriers and 12 enablers. Next, the Decision‐Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL) technique examined the prominence and causal relationships among these factors. Results indicate that lack of policy support from fashion brands, ineffective planning, and inadequate communication are the most significant barriers, while limited consumer awareness and high technology costs strongly influence other barriers. Key enablers include upcycling business models, rediscovery of silk knowledge, and waste material recovery. Resource efficiency culture, design for longevity, and traditional expertise act as causal drivers. The study provides actionable guidance for managers, policymakers, and researchers, offering practical and theoretical insights to advance circularity in s…

title: When does piecewise tire degradation modeling outperform linear models in Formula 1 race strategy? An empirical study across seven circuits using OpenF1 2023 telemetry with cross-validated model selection
abstract: Tire degradation modeling underpins pit-stop timing decisions in Formula 1 (F1) race strategy, yet the published literature has predominantly assumed a linear relationship between tire age and lap-time loss. This study tests that assumption against a physically constrained piecewise model with automated structural-break (“cliff”) detection, using 2023-season OpenF1 telemetry across seven circuits, yielding 14 compound–circuit combinations that meet a minimum sample threshold. A constraint requiring the post-break degradation rate to strictly exceed the pre-break rate excluded one physically implausible detection identified during the analysis. In-sample model comparison used the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), assigning the piecewise model five parameters to conservatively account for the degrees of freedom associated with grid-searching the break location. BIC did not favor the piecewise model for any of the 14 combinations; the closest case, Monaco Hard, showed ΔBIC = +3.0, favoring the linear model once the full search cost was accounted for. Five-fold cross-validation, applied independently across ten random seeds to assess stability, nonetheless revealed two combinations with a seed-stable out-of-sample improvement despite BIC favoring the linear model in both: Monaco Hard (10/10 seeds; 3.0% mean absolute error (MAE) improvement) and Singapore Hard (9/10 seeds; 0.9% …

title: The Search for a Universal ESG–FDI Relationship: Why Development and Investment Context Matter
abstract: ABSTRACT The empirical literature has not established a consistent relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and foreign direct investment (FDI). One reason may be that the association varies with countries' level of development and the structure of their investment flows. This study examines this possibility using a balanced panel of 10 upper‐middle‐income and 10 high‐income economies over the period 2002–2023. The baseline estimates are obtained from country fixed‐effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and are supplemented by lagged and dynamic specifications, pillar‐level analyses, nonlinear models, income–group interactions, and country‐level sensitivity checks. The results point to a negative and statistically significant association between ESG performance and FDI inflows in upper‐middle‐income economies, and this finding is relatively stable across alternative specifications. For high‐income economies, however, the estimates are considerably more sensitive to the composition of the sample. The ESG dimensions also exhibit distinct patterns across the two income groups, suggesting that the aggregate ESG measure masks important underlying heterogeneity. The interaction estimates provide further evidence of differences in the ESG–FDI slope across income groups, although both the magnitude and direction of this difference are sen…

title: The WOOP Strategy and Other Self-Regulation Strategies: A Critical Approach to Efficacy and Structural Limitations
abstract: This study reveals the theoretical and applied positioning of the WOOP strategy within the field of self-regulation, conceptualizing it as a hybrid model that integrates cognitive motivation with executive planning. The strategy has demonstrated a level of effectiveness ranging from moderate to high in translating intentions into actual behavior. This effectiveness derives from its composite structure, which combines mental contrasting with implementation intentions, thereby strengthening the linkage between mental representations and behavioral contingencies. However, this strength is not without structural limitations; the strategy’s efficiency declines when dealing with complex or long-term goals, reflecting an implicit limitation in its capacity for temporal sustainability. Furthermore, its reliance on a high level of self-awareness and executive competence renders it less effective among individuals with low self-regulation or in high-pressure environments. At the theoretical level, the study affirms that the distinctive value of WOOP lies in its emphasis on internal obstacles as a regulatory anchor, which enhances cognitive realism and reduces motivational illusions. From a comparative perspective, its uniqueness is evident in its deep integration of motivation and planning, in contrast to other strategies that tend to separate these two dimensions. Culturally, the need e…

title: Design and development of transmission gate-PFAL-based FIR filter utilizing efficient hybrid adders for low-power VLSI systems
The Benchmark Trap: Structures of Power and Injustice in AI Evaluations
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) benchmarks are not neutral tools of evaluation but socio-technical artefacts that shape competition, power, and research priorities within AI. Benchmarks standardise the assessment of systems and facilitate the creation of leaderboards that reward state-of-the-art performance with prestige, citations, trust, and institutional influence. As the costs of developing competitive AI systems rise, these rewards increasingly concentrate among powerful, industry-funded labs. This paper situates these concerns within Iris Marion Young's theories of oppression and structural injustice. It argues that current benchmarking practices may perpetuate systematic harms affecting various actors in AI research, aligning with four of Young’s "faces of oppression". Benchmarking culture is further framed as a source of structural injustice, as these harms emerge from normalised, individually defensible practices and network effects, even without explicit wrongdoing. By reinforcing existing power structures and narrowing possible research trajectories, benchmarking may in fact prevent the field from advancing in epistemically robust and socially beneficial ways.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society

title: Power With Confounders in Clinical Trials Using External Controls
abstract: ABSTRACT When the number of patients is limited in clinical trials for rare diseases and pediatric developments, enrolling sufficient participants for confirmatory randomized clinical trials is difficult. Alternative trial designs using external controls have been proposed: augmented randomized clinical trials (ARCTs) and supplemented single‐arm trials (SSATs). In order to assess the favorable situations in which to implement each trial design, we propose to specify the sensitivity analysis for confounding at the planning phase, and call it “pre‐sensitivity analysis.” In addition, we assessed the probability that the pre‐sensitivity analysis would show a treatment effect, which we define as “power with confounders.” A simulation was carried out across multiple cases, which considered the number of participants from external control data sources and the randomization ratio in an ARCT. The simulation indicated that allocating relatively more participants to the control arm in an ARCT could be considered when the available historical data are equal to or less than the number of concurrent trial participants. Conversely, when the available historical data are sufficient, allocating more participants to the test arm in an SSAT or ARCT could be considered.

title: The US$8.5 billion power play: How JioHotstar reshaped India’s video streaming industry
abstract: JioHotstar was formed through a US$8.5 billion joint venture between Reliance Industries Limited and The Walt Disney Company. Within a year of its launch, it reshaped the Indian digital entertainment industry and emerged as India’s largest digital entertainment platform. The case traces how the Reliance–Disney joint venture led to the formation of JioHotstar and highlights the strategic moves and technological innovations that contributed to the platform’s success. It examines how JioHotstar built a technology-enabled digital entertainment ecosystem by integrating premium content, live sports, artificial intelligence, advanced streaming technologies, and diversified monetization strategies. It also highlights how JioHotstar is changing sports broadcasting and competing with traditional broadcasters. The case further assesses JioHotstar’s competitive position against global and domestic over-the-top (OTT) platforms. By examining JioHotstar’s rapid growth and the key factors that contributed to its market leadership, the case offers insights into the changing dynamics of India’s digital entertainment industry. It also examines the challenges of sustaining this leadership, highlighting the need to balance continued innovation, consumer engagement, and profitable growth.

title: When Crises Entrench Gendered Power: Male Elite Adaptation in the Ugandan Parliament
abstract: ABSTRACT Recent scholarship argues that crises can create opportunities for women's political leadership. Yet crises also create opportunities for male political elites to adapt strategically to preserve their power. We develop and test a theory of crisis‐induced adaptation, whereby male political elites respond by shifting political attention toward crisis dimensions that reinforce their authority. We examine this theory using the Ugandan Parliament's response to COVID‐19, a health crisis in a policy domain traditionally associated with women. Using the complete corpus of parliamentary debates from 1998 to 2022 and text‐as‐data analyses, we find no evidence that COVID‐19 reduced gender inequalities in legislative speech. Instead, the pandemic widened them. Men's dominance in legislative speech grew as they increasingly framed the pandemic through traditionally masculine policy domains—the economy and national security—rather than public health. Rather than opening space for women, crises can provide men with new opportunities to entrench political dominance.

title: Ultra-short-term power prediction of photovoltaic power systems based on multi-climatic environments
abstract: Ultra-short-term power prediction of photovoltaic (PV) power generation system is an important basis for grid scheduling and energy management. In order to adapt to the complex and changing climatic conditions, this paper proposes an MHSA-LSTM ultra-short-term power prediction model for PV power generation system that integrally considers all kinds of climatic factors. In this study, the raw data of a PV power plant is processed by multiple interpolation, and four key climate environment variables, namely, temperature, irradiance, relative humidity and atmospheric pressure, which affect the power generation, are extracted from them. The time series data containing the influencing variables are used as samples, and the MHSA module is utilized to filter the importance of the data at different historical moments, and the strong and weak weights of each environmental variable are adaptively assigned to the LSTM network to obtain the prediction results. The results show that climatic factors such as solar irradiance, temperature, relative humidity and atmospheric pressure can affect the PV power, with irradiance having the most significant effect.The MHSA-LSTM model is oriented to the climatic conditions of different seasons and weather, and the predicted ultrashort-term power is closer to the actual power value. Taking spring conditions as an example, the MAPE\RMSE of the MHSA-LSTM…

title: AI Literacy: An Exercise in Power-Knowledge
abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes one of the most significant systems of knowledge production in our society today, questions relating to who can access and shape that production grow increasingly important in our discourse. This paper argues that the existing frameworks for AI literacy, which are dominated by technical competency and responsible use principles, are insufficient be-cause they enforce a “consumer” orientation toward AI rather than fostering genuine epistemic agency. Based upon Foucault's concept of power-knowledge, Freire's pedagogy of critical consciousness, and scholarship of digital literacy, this paper proposes a reconceptualization of AI literacy as a critical practice that equips individuals not just to use AI systems, but to critically evaluate them, resist their structuring assumptions, and participate in their governance. The paper further argues that unequal access to AI tools in society recapitulates longstanding epistemic injustices, and that a literacy framework oriented toward empowerment must account for these structural inequities. A three-part framework of AI literacy based on the notions of contextual use, critical interrogation, and participatory governance, frame this literacy as a cultivation of epistemic “agents” rather than the training of competent consumer of AI-generated information.

title: Impact of climate change on the photovoltaic power potential in Sweden across 21st century
abstract: Abstract Solar photovoltaic generation strongly relies on weather conditions, which will be affected by future climate change. Traditional methods for estimating photovoltaic generation potential often overlook detailed installation factors and snow impacts, leading to inaccuracies in high-latitude areas. We assess future photovoltaic system performance in Sweden using a validated photovoltaic installation model that incorporates air temperature, radiation and snow conditions. Applying this model to four Swedish cities under low- and high-emission climate change scenarios and three climate simulations, we project an approximate 5% increase in photovoltaic generation relative to the historical period with optimal installation angle. The combined effects of air temperature and snowfall are as crucial as solar radiation for photovoltaic generation in Sweden, so the photovoltaic generation change will be relatively limited by 2100. Optimized tilt angles are obtained for all the four cities, which could increase photovoltaic generation by 3-6% compared to the commercial angle. The findings also provide valuable insights into photovoltaic potential in a changing climate.

title: Enabling the 1:1 Promise: AI Enabled Fairness for Indonesia’s Retail IPO Allocation
abstract: Indonesia’s OJK Circular, effective November 2025, requires that half of every IPO’s pooled allocation go to retail investors. Uniquely amongst major capital markets, the regulation places all non-institutional participants, regardless of wealth, into a single competing pool rather than separating them by monetary thresholds. The rule is structurally sound; enforcement and measuring effectiveness require measures beyond rule-based detection alone. Well-resourced participants operating within the retail pool can distribute bids across networks of synthetic retail accounts, each individually compliant, to capture the retail quota undetected by standard concentration heuristics. Without a mechanism to detect such networks before allotment closes, the statutory guarantee of equal access becomes procedurally hollow: the quota is formally reserved for retail households whilst the economic benefit flows elsewhere. We present a framework identifying such nominee networks using eleven statutory fields already collected by Indonesia’s e-IPO infrastructure, requiring no new surveillance powers or personal data. The framework maps account connections to identify hidden networks (Louvain), learns behavioural patterns signalling coordination by mining association rules (Apriori), and scores each network’s likelihood of being a coordinated evasion ring (Random Forest). Evaluated on synthetic …

Pricing RMB Policy Risk: Evidence From Onshore and Offshore FX Option Markets
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines how onshore and offshore RMB option markets price potential shifts in China's RMB exchange rate regime. We calibrate a regime‐switching option pricing model to USD/CNY and USD/CNH options to recover daily risk‐neutral parameters summarizing the pricing of regime‐switching risk, including the risk‐neutral switching probability, the size of a possible RMB realignment, and exchange‐rate volatility under a possible new regime. This allows us to quantify and compare policy‐related tail‐risk pricing embedded in option prices over the past decade. The results show that CNH options price larger potential RMB devaluations and higher exchange‐rate volatility under a possible new regime than CNY options, especially during stress periods, whereas CNY options imply higher risk‐neutral switching probabilities. An event study around the introduction of the countercyclical factor further shows that CNY and CNH option‐implied risk‐neutral distributions evolved differently before and after the policy announcement. These findings point to segmented risk‐neutral pricing of RMB policy‐related risk across onshore and offshore option markets.

title: Force disguised as law enforcement in Venezuela: The 2026 capture of Maduro, hybrid justification and the erosion of article 2(4) of the UN charter
abstract: On 3 January 2026, United States forces struck targets in and around Caracas, seized Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores, and flew them to New York to stand trial on narco-terrorism charges. Washington presented the raid not as a use of force against Venezuela but as a law enforcement operation facilitated by the military. This article examines two linked questions: whether that framing has any footing in the jus ad bellum, and whether the reaction of other states was strong enough to protect the prohibition of force laid down in Article 2(4) of the UN Charter. Doctrinal analysis of the five justificatory strands advanced by the United States (law enforcement, implicit self-defence, non-recognition of Maduro, the Noriega analogy and the narco-terrorism designation) shows that none satisfies a recognised exception and that their combination functions to avoid any single, testable legal claim. The original contribution of the article is the Normative Response Index (NRI), a five-point coding scale (from -2, explicit legal condemnation, to +2, explicit endorsement) applied to all 27 states that addressed the Se- curity Council at its 10085th meeting on 5 January 2026. The mean NRI is -1.00 (SD = 1.18); only 11 of 27 states (40.7%) characterised the operation as unlawful, 13 (48.1%) voiced concern or equivocated, and 3 (11.1%) welcomed it. No Western Europ…

title: Co‐Creating Circular Pathways in the Fashion Industry: A Participatory System Dynamics Perspective
abstract: ABSTRACT Circular economy transitions in the fashion industry are frequently constrained not by a lack of reinforcing drivers but by endogenous feedback structures that limit growth as systems expand. Focusing on the Brazil context, this study identifies the dominant feedback archetypes governing circular transitions across four distinct socio‐technical contexts, namely, fashion brands, consumers, micro‐businesses, and digital circular platforms and offers an explanation, grounded in a participatory system dynamics approach, for why circular initiatives stall or progress. A participatory approach was adopted, combining co‐created causal loop diagrams, group model building, and backcasting workshops targeting a shared 2030 circular economy scenario, actively engaging 20 heterogeneous stakeholders including fashion brands, waste picker cooperatives, local government officials, and academics. Four causal loop diagrams were developed and validated through recorded and transcribed stakeholder interviews. The results identify a dominant limits to growth archetype across all four contexts, each driven by a distinct limiting mechanism: margin erosion in fashion brands, price‐mediated adoption constraints in consumer markets, infrastructure and workforce deficits in micro‐business recycling systems, and a dual operational and financial constraint in digital circular platforms. By struct…

title: Pricing Sustainability Without Backlash: Why One Line on the Receipt Can Make or Break Consumer Trust
Resolving the Sensitivity–Specificity Trade‐Off in Fluorescent Probes via a Tandem‐Activatable Shielding Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT For precise tumor diagnosis, the intrinsic trade‐off between sensitivity and specificity in fluorescent probes remains a longstanding bottleneck, underscoring an urgent need for strategies to break this fundamental constraint. To address the specificity limitation, we exploited a highly polarity‐sensitive fluorescent scaffold to construct a tandem‐activatable probe, enabling sequential activation by the acidic tumor microenvironment and the angiogenic marker aminopeptidase N. Whereas the single‐locked counterpart is prone to premature activation in circulation, the tandem‐locked probe remains inactive owing to a maleamic acid‐based shielding unit and is activated only upon encountering these two tumor hallmarks. Furthermore, this shielding strategy increases probe hydrophobicity, enhancing tumor uptake and driving accumulation of released fluorophores in low‐polarity lipid droplets, where fluorescence is markedly amplified to improve imaging sensitivity. The probe exhibits rapid and specific activation across various solid tumors with minimal toxicity, thus effectively resolving the sensitivity‐specificity trade‐off in probe design for in vivo applications.

title: Direct Enantioselective α-Alkoxylation of β-Keto Esters Enabled by Umpolung Strategy
abstract: Abstract Chiral ethers adjacent to a carbonyl group represent a valuable class of motifs; however, their catalytic asymmetric synthesis from readily available carbonyl compounds remains underexplored. Here, we present a catalytic asymmetric umpolung C–O bond-forming reaction of β-keto esters with alkyl hydroperoxides. This protocol employs in situ activation of alkyl hydroperoxides with trichloroacetonitrile, enabling the enantioselective alkoxy transfer to β-keto esters under catalysis by a chiral bifunctional organocatalyst, thereby allowing access to a broad range of highly functionalized, enantioenriched ethers bearing quaternary stereocenters.

title: Belief-based Risk-Aware Anticipatory Navigation: Modeling Intention and Position Uncertainty for Safe and Efficient Robot Navigation
abstract: The increasing deployment of Automated Mobile Vehicles (AMVs) in warehouses requires efficient navigation in dynamic environments shared with human workers. Traditional safety strategies, such as stopping or slowing down, often reduce efficiency and do not account for human-robot interaction. To address this, interaction-aware methods have been developed. However, traditional interaction models assume fixed parameters, rely on a single forecast, or use intent labels that are not updated during the interaction, and thus do not explicitly represent intention uncertainty, that is, variability in how people react to robots. When combined with position uncertainty introduced by sensing noise, this unmodeled intention uncertainty can make motion prediction and navigation decisions unreliable, leading to conservative behavior, inefficiency, or collisions in human–robot interactions. To bridge this gap, we propose Belief-based Risk-Aware Anticipatory Navigation (BRAN), a framework that jointly models intention and position uncertainty. BRAN maintains probabilistic beliefs over an agent's position and intention to explicitly represent uncertainty in both quantities. Position uncertainty is represented via sampled observations, and the intent belief is updated online through Bayesian inference so that predictions evolve with the interaction. These beliefs are propagated through the Socia…

title: Untangling Trust, Transparency, and Uncertainty in AI Literature and Policy
abstract: Trust, transparency, and uncertainty-awareness are widely cited as prerequisites for responsible and accountable machine learning (ML), yet their meanings and relationships remain inconsistent across research and policy. We present the first systematic review to examine how these concepts are defined and operationalized together across ML research, human–computer interaction, applied domains, AI policy, and technical standards. Analyzing 118 research papers, eight surveys of AI policy documents, and multiple national and international standards, we synthesize discussions on each concept and their relationships. We find that trust, transparency, and uncertainty are rarely defined explicitly in literature, limiting the transfer of meaning and findings between studies. In policy and standards, definitions are frequently circular or conflicting, creating ambiguous compliance expectations. Untangling the relationships between each concept, we argue that trust, transparency, and uncertainty are co-produced in ML, and show how this framing can improve conceptual clarity. Based on our findings, we provide recommendations to improve how we conceptualize, study, and implement ML systems in regard to each concept.

title: Uncertainty-guided optimization of spectral bands for two-color thermometry using laser-induced defect fluorescence in fused silica
Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left atrial (LA) stiffening augments the LA V wave, pressurizing the pulmonary artery (PA) out of proportion to left ventricular end-diastolic pressure. We characterized the pathophysiologic, diagnostic, and clinical implications of LA stiffening, as defined by prominent V waves, in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and less than moderate mitral regurgitation at rest underwent invasive hemodynamic exercise testing. Patients with heightened operant LA stiffening were defined by the PA wedge pressure (PAWP) V wave exceeding mean PAWP by ≥10 mm Hg. A previously used formula for V wave–corrected PAWP was validated against the PAWP waveform pressure-time-area to explore impact of the V wave on transpulmonary pressure gradients. Clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and outcome data were compared for patients with and without prominent V waves. RESULTS: Compared with patients without prominent V waves (n=844, 79%), those with prominent V waves (n=225, 21%) were older and more likely to be women, with more severe LA myopathy, evidenced by greater LA volume index (42.2±15.0 versus 32.5±13.0 mL/m 2 , P <0.001), lower LA reservoir strain (16.4±7.5% versus 23.2±8.3%, P <0.001), more atrial fibrillation (61.3% versus 22.9%, P <0.001), and increased operant…

title: Experimentalist Governance in Food Democracy: Monitoring and the Right to Food in Selected Chinese and European Cities
abstract: ABSTRACT Cities have become the level at which the right to food is either operationalized or left abstract, yet we have little comparative vocabulary for describing how they do it. This article examines local food observatories and monitoring mechanisms in four cities, namely, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Milan, and Berlin. It reads them against the four constitutive elements of experimentalist governance and finds that neither pair of cities completes the experimentalist cycle. The Chinese cases experiment extensively with means though their framework goals remain fixed and centrally set. The European cases deliberate openly over goals but show little evidence of the peer comparison and recursive revision that distinguish experimentalist governance from participatory consultation. The two sets of arrangements are therefore truncated at opposite ends of the same cycle, and the label administrative experimentalism and participatory experimentalism are used here to mark where each truncation falls. The article then asks what each arrangement makes claimable. Monitoring in Shanghai and Shenzhen produces data that flows upward and supports the evaluation of officials by their superiors. Monitoring in Milan and Berlin produces data that flow outward and support civil society scrutiny. Neither converts monitoring into a resource for individual rights claims. The study is exploratory and its …

title: Explainable AI for the EU Right to Explanation: A Systematic Review of the Law-XAI Translation Gap
abstract: When algorithms make or influence consequential decisions—about loan eligibility, hiring, or healthcare—EU law grants affected individuals a Right to Explanation. Yet whether (and how) Explainable AI (XAI) can satisfy this right in practice remains poorly understood, with direct implications for individuals' ability to contest automated decisions that affect their lives. This paper presents a systematic literature review of XAI in the context of the EU Right to Explanation, with particular focus on Art. 15(1)(h) GDPR, Art. 86 AI Act (AIA), and Art. 18(8)(a) Consumer Credit Directive (CCD). We consider papers published from 2024 onwards, as the final version of the AIA was published in July 2024—with Art. 86 being added late. From 2643 initial records identified by a deliberately broad search, we review 57 full texts, of which only 19 papers demonstrate substantive integration of both legal and technical perspectives, showing gaps in the interdisciplinary synthesis of the current regulatory framework. We document three problematic patterns across the corpus: Most misidentify the GDPR legal basis; few engage with the CJEU's Dun & Bradstreet judgment (likely due to publication timing); and the distinction between explanation form (governed by addressee) and content (governed by legal purpose) is often conflated. We conceptualize this as the Addressee/Purpose Framework, propose a f…

title: The quiet struggle: How vulnerable youth succeed with the right support
abstract: Abstract Educational inequality remains a pervasive and deeply entrenched global issue, with youth from vulnerable and marginalised backgrounds disproportionately affected. Despite the significant challenges that hinder the academic progress of many young people, often reinforcing cycles of social exclusion and economic vulnerability, some students demonstrate the capacity to excel academically, effectively defying the odds. This study seeks to examine the key structural and interpersonal factors that enable such students to achieve positive educational trajectories. Adopting a qualitative narrative research design, the research draws on two sets of semi‐structured interviews with both young people from vulnerable backgrounds and adults who played a role in their educational success ( n = 16). Findings identify four broad categories of factors shaping student success: (1) personal attributes such as resilience, intrinsic motivation, clear goals and a strong sense of purpose; (2) parental expectations and support; (3) teachers' emotional support, involvement and constructive feedback and (4) peer support. Of these, two factors emerged as consistently significant across all cases. First, parental expectations, underpinned by trust in their child's abilities and a high valuation of education, proved essential. Second, the depth and longevity of student–teacher relationships were c…

title: From Public Order to Public Convenience? Reasonable Restrictions on the Right to Peaceful Assembly under Article 19(1)(b)
abstract: Article 19(1)(b) of the Constitution of India guarantees citizens the right to assemble peaceably and without arms, a right that may be restricted only in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India or public order. This article asks whether the standard now used to restrict protest has shifted from “public order” to “public convenience”, a change that would bear on the constitutionality of such restrictions and on the safety of those who protest. It traces the development of the doctrine from Romesh Thappar and the Ram Manohar Lohia cases to Himat Lal Shah, Madhu Limaye and Ramlila Maidan, and examines how protests have been dealt with in practice, with reference to the Ramlila Maidan incident of 2011, the Thoothukudi firing of 2018 and the events at Jantar Mantar in 2026. Applying the proportionality test laid down in Anuradha Bhasin, it argues that although the formal wording of the doctrine has not changed, administrative practice has moved away from its principles, drawing on the rulings against the prolonged occupation of public places, particularly highways. It also recognises the interest of the State in ensuring public safety at large gatherings, and considers how life and property can be safeguarded through fair management of protest. Finally, it proposes four reforms: narrowly framed restrictions on assemblies, a formal notification system for protests, l…

title: Capability of the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology Approaches on Covid-19 Towards Policy Framework for Prevention and Control of Transmission
abstract: The study assessed the capability of the Las Piñas City Jail Male Dormitory in implementing COVID-19 prevention and control measures and developed a policy framework to strengthen institutional preparedness and response. Specifically, it examined the profile of implementing personnel (job assignment and level of knowledge of COVID-19 prevention and control), the capability level of prevention and control approaches as expected and as practiced, the moderating effect of job assignment on prevention and control indicators, and the overall extent of capability attained. A descriptive-correlational design was employed using a total-enumeration census of 64 Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP) personnel assigned to the Las Piñas City Jail Male Dormitory, consisting of 50 personnel on lockdown and 14 response team members. A researcher-developed Response Capability Questionnaire covering three prevention sub-areas and five control sub-areas was used, with content validity established through a three-member expert panel and reliability confirmed through Cronbach’s alpha on a pilot sample of five non-sample respondents. Paired-samples t-tests and one-way ANOVA were used for data analysis. Overall, COVID-19 prevention and control approaches were rated at a very high extent, both as expected and as practiced. However, statistically significant differences were found across most …

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Firms Value of Non-Financial Listed Firms Listed in Nigeria
abstract: This study assessed the effect of Corporate Social Responsibility on Firms Value of listed non-financial firms in Nigeria using ICT, Oil and Gas firms as evidence of study for a ten-year period spanning from 2013 to 2024. The specific objectives of this study are to determine the effect of corporate social responsibility on share price, price earnings, market capitalization of quoted ICT, Oil and Gas firms in Nigeria. Ex-post facto research design was employed. The population of this study consist of 29 (Twenty-nine) ICT, Oil and Gas firms quoted on the Nigeria Exchange Group as at 2024, out of which ten (10) of the ICT, Oil and Gas firms were selected using purposive sampling. Secondary data were extracted from annual reports and financial statements gotten from the Nigeria Exchange Group (NGX). The study employed descriptive statistics and inferential statistics using Pearson correlation, Panel pooled Least Square (PLS) regression analysis, normality test for the study.
