title: Cultivating Youth Financial Well-Being: A Perspective on Activity Theory in Digital Financial Services
abstract: Digital financial services (DFS) are reshaping how individuals manage money by embedding real-time tracking, personalised nudges, and frictionless transactions into everyday life. However, research remains largely focused on adoption and current-oriented practices such as short‑term usage and immediate convenience, offering limited insight into how DFS can foster users’ future financial lives and financial well-being, especially for young people who are digitally adept but financially precarious. Financial well‑being, understood as a sense of security and freedom in meeting present and future financial needs, includes both hedonic, and eudaimonic, toward meaningful goals. It is particularly challenging in youth-focused DFS. Drawing on activity theory, we conceptualise financial well-being as an evolving, practice-based activity rather than a static outcome state and investigate how DFS can be effectively leveraged to cultivate young users’ financial well-being. We conducted a qualitative case study of Enrich, a youth-focused DFS offered by a Taiwanese commercial bank. It repositioned from transactional convenience towards future-oriented tools that support financial responses and practices. We propose a pendulum-like framework of activity systems that captures young users’ oscillation between hedonic and eudaimonic orientations in DFS‑mediated practices and helps DFS researcher…

title: Electoral Reform and the Continuity of Local Government in Indonesia: The Constitutional Implications of Ruling No. 135/PUU-XXII/2024 on the Separation of National and Local Elections
abstract: This study addresses a gap in the literature concerning the implications of changes to electoral cycles for central and regional governance following Constitutional Court Decision No. 135/PUU-XXII/2024. It focuses on the misalignment between the terms of office of regional heads and members of Regional People's Representative Councils (DPRD) arising from the 2024 General Election. This misalignment has raised public and scholarly concerns about potential legal vacuums and deficits in democratic legitimacy. The study proposes constitutional engineering as a transitional mechanism to ensure legal certainty and maintain the continuity of regional governance. Using a normative legal research method, it adopts statutory, conceptual, and case-law approaches to examine primary legal sources through descriptive analysis. The findings indicate that Constitutional Court Decision No. 135/PUU-XXII/2024 necessitates legislative reform to harmonise the legal framework governing general elections and regional head elections and prevent a legal vacuum. The separation of electoral schedules may create a gap in the terms of office of regional heads and DPRD members elected in 2024. Without clear transitional provisions, this situation could undermine the continuity, legitimacy, and effectiveness of regional governance. The legal implications include the need for explicit transitional arrangement…

title: A mathematical model of HPAI transmission between dairy cattle and wild birds with environmental effects
abstract: High pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), particularly H5N1, poses an increasing threat at the wildlife–livestock–environment interface, with recent detections in dairy cattle motivating multi-host transmission models. We develop and analyze a deterministic compartmental model for HPAI transmission among cattle, wild birds and a shared contaminated environment. The model combines an SEIR structure for cattle with an SIR framework for wild birds and includes environmentally mediated transmission. We establish positivity and boundedness, characterize the disease-free and endemic equilibria, and derive the basic reproduction number [Formula: see text] as the spectral radius of a reduced next-generation matrix representing coupled transmission pathways. We also establish threshold and global stability properties of the equilibria. Numerical simulations illustrate extinction, persistence and parameter-dependent disease dynamics. Global sensitivity analysis identifies cattle recovery, cattle-to-cattle transmission, environmental viral decay and environmental transmission as the principal determinants of [Formula: see text] within the parameter ranges considered. title: From The Job Market To Poverty: An Analysis of Economic Growth Determinants In Java
abstract: Economic growth is one of the important indicators in describing the performance of regional development, especially in the Java Island region which has a large contribution to the Indonesian economy. However, differences in labor market conditions, price stability, quality of human resources, investment, government spending, and poverty can cause variations in economic growth between regions. This study aims to analyze the influence of the Open Unemployment Rate, inflation, investment, Human Development Index, local government capital expenditure, and the number of poor people on economic growth in six provinces on the island of Java during the period 2015–2025. The research uses panel data analyzed using the Fixed Effect Model (FEM). The results of the study show that the Open Unemployment Rate, Inflation and the Number of the Poor have a negative and significant effect on economic growth, respectively. The Human Development Index has a positive and significant effect. The number of poor people has a negative and significant effect. Meanwhile, investment and capital expenditure do not show a significant influence. In addition, all independent variables in this study simultaneously had a significant effect on economic growth from the R2 value, it was shown that the independent variable was able to explain 65.9% of the variation in economic growth. title: Interrupted time series analysis of inpatient C. difficile treatment in response to the 2017 and 2021 SHEA/IDSA updates using Oracle EHR Real-World Data
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine the prescribing patterns of metronidazole, vancomycin, and fidaxomicin for inpatients with Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) in response to the 2021 Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA)/Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) update. Methods We evaluated metronidazole, vancomycin, and fidaxomicin use utilizing Oracle EHR Real-World Data (2014-2024). Utilization data were measured by treatment courses, defined as 10 or more days of use or use on the last day of hospitalization. To determine if there was a statistically significant change in the use of each drug by CDI severity before versus after the SHEA/IDSA guideline updates, interrupted time-series analyses were conducted using multinomial logistic regression to model the probability of being assigned specific treatment and evaluate prescribing patterns over time, with vancomycin designated as the reference. Covariates included a continuous time variable, intervention indicators for both the 2017 and 2021 updates, and time by intervention interactions for both updates. Results A total of 70,200 CDI treatment courses were included (38,357 for nonsevere and 31,843 for severe disease). Metronidazole use dropped precipitously after 2017 for nonsevere and severe CDI. Eco Doxology: An Interfaith Response to the Ecological Crisis
abstract: Objective: To critically examine eco-short-termism as an ethical dimension of the ecological crisis and to develop eco-doxology as an interfaith framework oriented toward long-term environmental responsibility. Methodology: A qualitative, documentary, and theoretical-interpretive study was conducted using philosophical and conceptual analysis. The core corpus consisted of 40 academic articles indexed in Scopus, complemented by foundational works and the primary source required for the development of the concept of eco-doxology. The search prioritized studies on environmental short-termism, intergenerational ethics, religion and climate change, interfaith environmentalism, Indigenous ecological knowledge, environmental pragmatism, and ecological degradation. Results: The analysis identified six themes: ecological limits, short-term decision-making, intergenerational responsibility, religious environmental ethics, Indigenous ecological knowledge, and eco-doxology. The literature indicates that environmental costs generated by decisions focused on immediate benefits may persist far longer than those benefits. It also shows that different religious and Indigenous traditions contain principles of responsibility, restraint, interdependence, and care for nature that can support environmental cooperation. Conclusion: Eco-doxology is proposed as a complementary ethical framework, rather…

title: Design and Implementation of a lightweight evasion-aware brute-force detection and response system for SMEs
abstract: Authentication endpoints are a primary target for brute-force and credential-stuffing attacks, and attackers evade per-IP thresholds by pacing requests and rotating across many source addresses, while deep learning detectors need infrastructure that Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) rarely have. This paper presents a lightweight detection and response gateway built with FastAPI and Redis. Each request is scored with a time-decaying Reputation Score and an Evasion Score combining IP diversity, username diversity and timing regularity over failed attempts. Because per-source scoring cannot see attacks spread across rotating IPs, two target-keyed signals are added: Account Pressure, raised when many sources fail against one account, and Global Pressure, raised when failures dominate traffic from IPs with no login history. Both respond with a server-verified CAPTCHA rather than a lockout, and IPs that previously authenticated to an account are exempt. In a controlled evaluation of three seeds of about 860 labelled requests, covering six attack and six benign traffic families, the system detected all 60 attack campaigns, including every rotating-IP campaign, with 95.0% per-request recall and 2.3% of benign requests denied. On identical traffic, Fail2Ban reached 50.0% recall and missed all rotating-IP and honeypot campaigns, while per-account lockout denied 74.4% of benign requests…

abstract: Digital labour platforms have transformed work by enabling firms and consumers to access labour on demand while offering workers varying degrees of flexibility. However, this model frequently transfers economic risk, developmental responsibility and uncertainty onto workers. This conceptual paper examines how sustainable human capital management can address these tensions and strengthen workforce engagement and retention in the gig economy. An integrative review of peer-reviewed literature on sustainable human resource management, platform work, algorithmic management, work engagement, psychological contracts, career sustainability and worker retention provides the analytical foundation. The synthesis indicates that fair rewards, algorithmic transparency, meaningful autonomy, worker voice, capability development, relational support and well-being protection function as strategic resources rather than discretionary benefits. title: Effects of Ethyl Acetate Fraction of Dialium guineense Willd Leaves on the Stomach Architecture of Indomethacin-Intoxicated Albino Wistar Rats: Implication in Ulcer Management
abstract: Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is prevalent in many developing countries like Nigeria mainly due to abuse of alcoholic beverages and excessive use of pain killer drugs. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of ethyl acetate fraction of Dialium guineense (DG) leaves on the stomach architecture of indomethacin intoxicated Wistar rats. Methanol extract of the leaves was eluted with ethyl acetate to obtain the ethylacetate fraction (EAF). The fraction was subjected to phytochemical analysis. Thirty six adult Wistar rats were divided into 6 groups of 6 rats per group. Group 1 was normal control, while groups 2 - 6 received indomethacin (40 mg/kg via oral gavage). Group 2 animals were indomethacin control, Group 3 received omeprazole (20 mg/kg), while Groups 4 to 6 received 100, 200 and 400 mg/kg of ethyl acetate fraction respectively. The animals were treated for 14 days after indomethacin administration. On the 15th day blood samples were taken and the animals were sacrificed by cervical dislocation and their stomach isolated for histopathology. Free acidity, total acidity and pH were estimated. Anitoxidant activity was investigated using gluthathione (GSH), superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase (CAT), and malondialdehyde (MDA) activity. title: Foreign Exchange Risk Management and Financial Performance of Manufacturing Firms in Kenya
abstract: Foreign exchange risk management is an important consideration for manufacturing firms operating in an increasingly globalised business environment. Exchange rate fluctuations can affect the cost of imported raw materials, machinery, fuel, and other production inputs, thereby influencing profitability, liquidity, cash-flow stability, and overall financial performance. This study examines the effect of foreign exchange risk management on the financial performance of manufacturing firms in Kenya through a review of theoretical and empirical literature. The theoretical review is anchored on the International Fisher Effect theory, the Theory of Rational Expectations, and the Purchasing Power Parity theory, which explain the factors influencing exchange rate movements and firms’ responses to currency-related uncertainties. The literature review methodology involved examining relevant scholarly publications, including empirical studies conducted in Kenya and other international contexts. The reviewed literature focuses on financial hedging practices, including forward contracts and currency swaps, as well as operational strategies, such as exposure netting and natural hedging, and non-financial approaches, including pricing adjustments and supplier negotiations. The reviewed studies generally indicate that foreign exchange risk management practices are associated with improved financ…

title: Synchronous Scheduling and Vehicle Optimization of In-Plant Parts Transport Under Bidirectional Loading-Unloading
abstract: Aiming at the bidirectional closed-loop transport scenario between the auto parts logistics center and the complete vehicle factory in the in-plant logistics of automobile original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), this paper constructs a synchronous scheduling optimization model for tractors and trailers with hard time windows, to address the problems of long vehicle waiting time, low utilization rate and high operating cost in the traditional integrated transport mode. The model takes the completion of daily transport tasks as the hard constraint, takes the minimization of the total daily operating cost of tractors and trailers as the optimization objective, and fully considers the decoupling operation characteristics of tractors and trailers in bidirectional loading and unloading operations. Aiming at the NP-hard property of the model, a Tabu Search algorithm adapted to the two-point bidirectional scenario is designed. The feasibility verification of the solution is implemented through event-driven simulation based on greedy strategy, and global optimization is realized by combining neighborhood search rules, tabu list and aspiration criterion. Finally, a numerical example analysis is carried out with the actual operation data of an automobile OEM. The results show that, under the scenario with a daily transport demand of 50 vehicle trips and an effective working time of 480 m…

title: Establishment of an efficient hairy root transformation system and functional analysis of GsCGTa in Grona styracifolia
abstract: Abstract Grona styracifolia is a medicinal herb rich in bioactive compounds, including schaftoside, from the Lingnan region. However, functional genomic analyses of Grona styracifolia have been limited by the lack of a stable and highly efficient genetic transformation system. In this study, key parameters affecting Rhizobium rhizogenes -mediated hairy root transformation, including the explant type and seedling age, inoculation conditions, duration of cocultivation, stage of acetosyringone (AS) application, and cefotaxime (Cef) concentration, were systematically optimized. Optimal transformation was achieved by inoculating 10-d-old cotyledonary nodes as explants for 20 min with an MMA (MES‑MgCl 2 ‑AS) resuspension solution (OD 600 = 0.6), followed by a 3‑d co‑cultivation period and subsequent culture on 1/2 MS solid medium supplemented with 300 mg/L Cef. Through the integrated optimization, the transformation efficiency significantly increased from 35.56% to 71.11%. On the basis of this system, GsCGTa , a key structural gene in the schaftoside biosynthetic pathway, was functionally characterized. A transcriptome analysis revealed that C -glycosyltransferase a ( GsCGTa ) overexpression induced selective transcriptional reprogramming of pathway-related structural genes. title: Modeling Nutrient Concentrations in a Greenhouse Cascade Soilless System
abstract: A dynamic simulation model was developed and calibrated to predict nutrient concentrations in a three-level cascade hydroponic system (CasH). The performance of the model was evaluated across donor/primary (tomato) and receiver secondary (mint, peppermint), and tertiary (sea fennel, lemon balm) crops. An independent dataset was available for both calibration and evaluation of the primary tomato crop, whereas data for the secondary and tertiary stages were used exclusively for model calibration. Following model evaluation, three distinct operational scenarios were simulated, ranging from a baseline monoculture to a comprehensive three-stage cascade system. The simulations forecasted the progressive nutrient accumulation across stages, identifying the operational point at which critical sodium and salinity thresholds are approached. The proposed model shows potential as a foundational component for digital twins of hydroponic systems, complementing rather than replacing physical sensors by providing dynamic hourly simulations of nutrient dynamics. The model serves as an effective tool for optimizing resource efficiency and mitigating salinity risks in sustainable, closed-loop horticultural systems. These findings confirm the feasibility of nutrient-specific tracking in closed-loop horticulture, though independent evaluation was restricted to the primary stage, and the empirical c…

title: Nutritional Status of Soils Under Cassava Cultivation Using the Diagnosis and Recommendation System (DRIS) in the Savanna Zone of the Central African Republic
abstract: Cassava is an important crop that ensures food security for the population in the Central African Republic (CAR). It also significantly contributes to improving farmers' incomes. Unfortunately, there is no specific data on soil nutrient status that would allow for informed management of the crop’s nutritional condition and yield improvement, despite existing potential. The Diagnosis and Recommendation Integrated System (DRIS) is an approach used to interpret plant tissue analysis results and helps assess the nutritional status of crops. It focuses on comparing paired nutrient ratios and concentrations of nutrients in leaf tissues with norms developed from high-yielding crop populations. The objective of this study is to apply the DRIS model to determine the nutritional status of cassava cropping systems in the savanna forest zone of CAR. In total, 126 leaf samples were collected from cassava fields in the region. Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P), Potassium (K), Calcium (Ca), Magnesium (Mg), and Zinc (Zn) contents were analyzed. Root yields were also recorded. Significant differences (p = 0.001) were observed between the root yields of the low and high-yielding sub-populations. Based on the Nutritional Balance Index, nutrient requirements for cassava in this savanna zone were ranked as: Ca > Mg > N > K > P > Zn. The study recommends the implementation of Integrated Soil Fertility Ma…

Design and Development of A Web-Based Accounting Information System for D’Kriuk Fried Chicken Semarang
abstract: D’Kriuk Fried Chicken Semarang is a microenterprise in the ready-to-eat food industry that currently relies on manual record-keeping for its business processes. This practice results in errors in recording purchase and sales transactions, difficulties in monitoring the inflow and outflow of raw materials required for production, challenges in managing the transfer of finished-goods inventory to sales, delays in reporting, and a high risk of data manipulation in sales transactions. These challenges also affect the preparation of financial statements, particularly in terms of recording accuracy and data-processing efficiency. Therefore, this study aims to develop a web-based accounting information system to improve the efficiency and accuracy of business processes at D’Kriuk Fried Chicken Semarang. The system was developed using the prototyping method, designed using Unified Modeling Language (UML), and implemented using the CodeIgniter 4 framework, PHP, and a MySQL database. System testing was conducted using Black-Box Testing and User Acceptance Testing (UAT). The test results indicate that the developed system functions in accordance with the established business processes and user requirements and effectively integrates the business processes of D’Kriuk Fried Chicken Semarang.

title: Legal Certainty of the Position of Justice Collaborator in the Criminal Justice System as a Party Cooperating with Law Enforcement
abstract: This study is purposed to analyse the legal certainty regarding the status of a justice collaborator within the criminal justice system, the nature of the cooperation between the justice collaborator and law enforcement in uncovering criminal offenses, and the resulting legal consequences for the justice collaborator. The research employs a normative-juridical method—a form of legal research that examines and analyzes applicable legal norms relevant to the issue at hand, utilizing data gathered through a literature review. The findings indicate that enacting specific legislation (lex specialis) concerning justice collaborators is crucial for ensuring legal certainty and providing maximum protection for them. Such specific regulation would facilitate the determination of status and protection schemes, as well as the granting of sentence reductions. The cooperation of a justice collaborator begins with a commitment to assist law enforcement in exposing complex, organized crimes that are otherwise difficult to uncover. Consequently, the justice collaborator is required to provide honest and consistent testimony to help identify other principal perpetrators. Given the significant risk of intimidation and threats directed at them and their families, justice collaborators are entitled to comprehensive and maximum safety protection.

abstract: In this study, it is aimed to determine the mediating effect of conflict management (CAS) on the effect of strategic planning awareness (SPA) on problem solving (PS) of the Medical representatives (MR) working in pharmaceutical companies and to contribute the results to the strategic decision-making process of pharmaceutical company managers. In the study, it was aimed to determine the path analysis between variables with structural equation modeling. The sample of the study consists of 379 MRs between the ages of 24-50 working in pharmaceutical companies in Turkiye. The questionnaire, which includes the CAS, PS, SPA Scales and socio-demographic characteristics in the international literature. In the path analysis model with the variables observed in this study, it was determined that the effect of the Perception dimension, one of the sub-dimensions of SPA, on the Compromise and Confrontational sub-dimensions of CAS sub-dimensions was not significant, while all other direct effects were significant. In mediating effects; Knowledge variable affects PS variable negatively through Avoidant and Coercive variables, while it affects it positively through Facilitative and Confrontational variables. abstract: According to the 2015 Komnas Perempuan report, the mass media in Indonesia, especially online media, are still unable to comply with the Journalistic Code of Ethics (KEJ) in reporting on sexual harassment issues. The quality of news, in this case objectivity, is an important principle that journalists and media need to have as information centers for the public. This study analyzes 30 news stories with sexual harassment issues on Kompas.com and 30 news stories on Tribunnews.com in the time span between June 2021 - July 2021. This study uses a quantitative content analysis method and uses the concept of Objectivity dimension impartiality by Westerstahl which has been detailed by McQuail as a research measuring tool, as well as a scoring technique for each indicator in all analyzed news. The results of the study found that there were differences in the level of objectivity between Kompas.com and Tribunnews.com. title: Total Quality Management in Higher Education Leraning: A Qualitative Student Competency Development at the University of Darussalam Gontor
abstract: This research seeks to investigate the application of Total Quality Management in learning process in higher education and its role in developing student competencies in University of Darussalam Gontor. Qualitative descriptive research design was utilized to analyze how the principle of TQM had been implemented and experienced by the students during the learning process. Data were collected using semi-structured interviews, observations, and documentation conducted among the students, lecturers, and academic manager. Data analysis process involved data condensation, coding, categorization, thematization, and interpretation. Source and technique triangulation were also utilized to increase the credibility of data findings. Three main themes were found; which are total involvement, competency development, and quality culture. Students’ involvement in discussion, observation, presentation, cooperation, and feedback provided an opportunity for the students to improve their critical thinking skills, communication skills, cooperation skills, and problem solving skills. Evaluation, feedback, and recognition provided an opportunity to create a culture of quality learning.

title: Localising human resource management paradoxes: Developmental maturity and the maturation tree of inclusive shared value
abstract: Human resource management (HRM) systems are expected to deliver flexibility and consistency, efficiency and fairness, and short-term productivity and long-term capability simultaneously. Paradox theory explains why such contradictory yet interdependent demands persist, but emphasises the pervasiveness of tension rather than its distribution, offering little guidance on where tension becomes acute enough to warrant scarce attention. Contingency theory and strategic fit address location, but have modelled fit as a condition assessed at a single moment; recent dynamic-alignment and HR-ecosystem work relaxes that assumption without specifying where tension concentrates. This conceptual paper generalises to HRM the Maturation Tree of Inclusive Shared Value (MTISV), which joins contingency and paradox reasoning to locate developmental discontinuities in producer-centred systems. Transferred to the employment relationship, it yields a paradox localisation: HRM paradoxes become salient at interfaces where interdependent practices have developed to divergent levels of maturity. Developmental maturity (the state of a practice, not of the people it governs) is proposed as a dynamic contingency governing whether a contradiction remains latent or becomes salient. title: PandemIQ system in Poland: The hybrid approach to early detection of pandemic waves using interpretable AI models and GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS)
abstract: Humans live surrounded by a variety of threats. These threats can be diverse: natural, chemical, technological, psychological, social, ecological, global, biological, and health-related. The latter, namely biological and health threats, are the most pressing and dangerous from a human perspective as they affect living organisms’ health. Examples include infectious diseases caused by viruses, bacteria, or parasites (e.g., influenza, COVID-19, Lyme disease). In Poland, epidemic cases of the acute infectious respiratory disease COVID-19, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, were first reported on March 4, 2020. The pandemic lasted three years. This scientific article attempts to present the architecture and functionality of the PandemIQ system. The system was designed for the early detection and forecasting of the regional risk of pandemic waves. The system is based on a hybrid artificial intelligence model that combines predictions based on epidemiological, mobility, and transportation data with interpretability (attention) mechanisms enabling visualization and decision justification. This paper provides a detailed discussion of the structure of decision reports for authorities, GIS-based operational dashboards (ArcGIS), and alternative solutions using the Apache ECharts library. It also presents validation procedures, data security aspects, and compliance with legal regulations (GDPR…

title: Development of Three-Dimensional Worksheets Using Canva on The Human Digestive System for the 5th-Grade Natural Sciences Course Jepun Public Elementary School 1 Tulungagung Regency 2025/2026 School Year
abstract: This study was motivated by the lack of varied teaching materials used in IPAS lessons on the human digestive system for 5th-grade students at State Elementary School 1 Jepun, Tulungagung Regency. This study aims to: (1) describe the process of developing three-dimensional worksheets using Canva for the topic of the human digestive system, (2) determine the validity level of the three-dimensional worksheets using Canva, and (3) determine the practicality level of the three-dimensional worksheets using Canva in the IPAS subject for fifth-grade students at SDN 1 Jepun, Tulungagung Regency. This study employed a Research and Development (R&D) method using the ADDIE development model, which includes the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation stages. Data analysis utilized quantitative descriptive analysis with a Likert scale to determine the validity and practicality of the product. The research results show that the three-dimensional worksheets created using Canva received a validity score of 92% from subject matter expert 1, classified as “highly valid”; 100% from subject matter expert 2; 98% from media expert 1; and 92% from media expert 2, all of which were classified as “highly valid.” The results of the practicality test showed a response rate of 96% from teachers, 96.4% from small-group student respondents, and 96.5% from field test student respondents…

title: The Social Service Activities for Coastal Communities Affected by Coastal Erosion in Karawang Regency
abstract: Some coastal areas of Karawang Regency are affected by severe coastal erosion. This condition worsens the socio-economic life of coastal communities in Karawang Regency, particularly those in remote areas, amidst their relatively poor conditions. For this reason, Universitas Singaperbangsa Karawang and other universities held community service activities in the form of social service involving students. The social service was held on Saturday, October 12, 2024. This activity employs an observational socialization method to arouse students' concern to pay attention to the lives of remote coastal communities in Karawang Regency. As a result, this activity was successful due to the support of the Pasirjaya Village Government apparatus and local community leaders.

title: Analisis Efektivitas Telemarketing dalam Memperkuat Hubungan dengan Pelanggan Loyal untuk Meningkatkan Booking Service di Auto2000 Basuki Rahmat
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effectiveness of telemarketing in strengthening relationships with loyal customers and increasing service bookings at Auto2000 Basuki Rahmat Surabaya. Telemarketing plays a key role in maintaining customer communication through service reminders, follow-ups, and the dissemination of information regarding services and promotions. The study employs a descriptive approach, gathering data through observations of telemarketing activities, customer service, the service booking process, and inter-departmental coordination related to customer service. The analysis reveals that telemarketing contributes to maintaining customer relationships and encouraging customers to make service bookings. However, its implementation remains suboptimal; the average customer handling time is 17 minutes, whereas the established target is 7 minutes. This situation is attributed to a lack of integrated communication systems, staff reliance on other departments for information, limited access to customer data, and insufficient knowledge regarding products and services. Consequently, improvements are needed, including the development of an integrated digital system, enhanced telemarketing staff competence, optimized communication channels, and better customer database management. These measures are expected to boost telemarketing effectiveness, service quality, customer loyalt…

title: Integrative multi-omics analyses reveal transcriptional, metabolic, and hormonal regulation of vernalization-induced flowering in Wucai (Brassica rapa)
abstract: Abstract Vernalization, a low-temperature-induced transition from vegetative to reproductive growth, is essential for flowering in many Brassica crops, including Wucai ( Brassica rapa ssp. chinensis var. rosularis ). To elucidate the molecular basis of vernalization in Wucai, we performed an integrative multi-omics analysis of shoot apices from cold-treated plants. Twenty-eight vernalization pathway-related genes, including homologs of FLC , FLM , VIN3 , VRN , SOC1 , SVP , and VIL2 , exhibited conserved cold-responsive expression patterns. Transcription factors from the MYB, bHLH, bZIP, and NAC families showed dynamic regulation, implicating key members such as MYB57 , bHLH3 , and ABF4 in flowering control and hormonal signaling. Metabolomic profiling revealed significant enrichment of carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism, with increased levels of sucrose, glucose, galactose, glycine, serine, proline, and arginine, suggesting enhanced mobilization of energy and nitrogen during vernalization. Proline accumulation, together with upregulation of P5CS , indicates a potential role in floral transition. Hormonal analysis showed elevated auxin, kinetin, jasmonic acids, and brassinosteroids, with cold-induced BcDET2 expression correlating with increased brassinosteroid levels and early flowering. Exogenous brassinolide further promoted flowering by activating FT and SOC1 while repres…

title: FlexENN: A Graph Neural Network for Binding Energy Prediction of Globular and Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
abstract: Abstract Intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) drive a large fraction of cellular signaling, transcription, and assembly through interfaces that often lack a defined geometry, making the prediction of their binding energies challenging for methods developed primarily for folded complexes. Here, we introduce FlexENN, an interface-focused message-passing graph neural network framework comprising two independently trained models: FlexENN-F for folded protein complexes and FlexENN-I for complexes containing a disordered partner. The FlexENN architecture constructs a local interface graph in which each residue node integrates the relative geometry, flexibility-related structural descriptors, and sequence information, allowing the network to learn structure-affinity relationships from a single resolved bound conformation. We also construct an IDP-containing dataset for training the FlexENN-I model. Benchmarked across folded complexes and IDP-containing systems, including tubulin–tubulin interfaces within microtubules (MTs) and MTs in complex with microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs), with reference binding affinity values extracted from our experiments, the models reproduce physically reasonable energetic profiles, including the stronger interdimer relative to the lateral MT interactions, while feature-ablation analyses reveal system-dependent contributions of selected descripto…

title: Study on mechanical, corrosion and fractured surface of n-Mn modified Al5052 alloy: an ANOVA and ANN prediction of wear rate
abstract: Aluminum (Al) 5052 alloys are extensively utilized in marine environments, pressure vessels, and automotive parts due to their better strength and low density. However, more investigation is required to comprehend how the nanoscale manganese (n-Mn) element affects their mechanical, tribological, corrosion, and machinability. The development of Al5052 alloy modified with n-Mn by increasing the weight percentage in 0.25% increments from 0 to 1% through stir casting is the main focus of this study. The nano-composite showed notable improvements in hardness (23.72%), tensile strength (11.01%), and corrosion resistance (57.69%). However, increasing the n-Mn content also led to a 77.35% increase in machining force and a 69.23% increase in surface roughness (Ra). Taguchi and ANOVA approaches were used to analyze the effects of n-Mn (wt. %), sample temperature (ºC), and sliding distance (m) on wear loss (g). The improved alloy's wear rate was largely influenced by its n-Mn concentration. Wear rate confirmation tests showed that maximum errors for the n-Mn modified Al5052 alloy were within permissible bounds. Additionally, the wear loss was successfully predicted using the proposed 3-4-1 Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. For the wear attributes taken into consideration, the predicted performance metrics produced mean squared errors (MSE) of 4.925*10-5 and R-squared values (R2) of 0…

title: Monte Carlo and Neural Network-based Prediction of Base Shear Force in Airport Tunnels using the Pushover Method Considering Both Soil-Structure Interaction and Non-Interaction across Different Soil Types
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are powerful nonlinear function approximators that can learn complicated relationships from data. They offer increasing value in civil, seismic, and geotechnical engineering applications. Recent findings indicate that ANNs can also be applied to structural health monitoring, material behaviour prediction and the evaluation of deep buried structures, whereas their application to airport tunnels remains largely unexplored. This study expands the Monte Carlo framework developed for the seismic assessment of an airport tunnel. It integrates the principles of a neural network. 200 samples are generated for each scenario by incorporating uncertainties of peak ground acceleration and material strength into Monte Carlo simulations. The findings indicate a significant variation in the structure’s roof displacement and base shear and larger dispersion of these parameters is observed as the ground acceleration increases. In the case without SSI, the roof displacement varies between 1.40 and 3.44 cm while the base shear varies from 690.0 to 1,845.1 kN; these are the minimum and maximum values obtained over the 200 Monte Carlo samples and correspond exactly to the figures reported in Table 4. title: Evolution of Phenolic Compounds and Antioxidant Capacity of Olive Leaf (Olea europaea L.) Remaining on Branches After Pruning
abstract: Olive leaves (Olea europaea L.) are an important by-product of olive pruning and oil production and a rich source of phenolic compounds with antioxidant properties. However, their post-pruning biochemical evolution when leaves remain attached to branches is poorly understood. This study evaluated the changes in phenolic composition and antioxidant capacity of Cornicabra olive leaves attached to the branches during five months after pruning under intensive and super-intensive cultivation systems. Phenolic compounds were analyzed by HPLC-DAD and antioxidant capacity was assessed using DPPH and ORAC assays. Oleuropein was the main compound, followed by verbascoside and hydroxytyrosol derivatives. Both phenolic content and antioxidant capacity showed a clear temporal decline after pruning, with maximum values occurring within the first 6–24 days. The super-intensive system consistently showed higher levels than the intensive one. Antioxidant capacity closely followed phenolic behavior, with strong positive correlations, particularly for oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol compounds. Overall, olive leaves maintain high biochemical activity shortly after pruning, and the first 2–3 weeks represent the optimal period for their valorization. These results support improved management strategies and the use of olive leaves as a sustainable source of bioactive compounds.

title: Education and Capacity Building for Adolescents and Their Social Environment in Early Childhood Marriage Prevention Efforts in Ranokomea Village, Poleang Barat District, Bombana Regency
abstract: Early marriage is a social issue that can affect the continuity of education, psychological readiness, reproductive health, and the family's ability to carry out parenting functions. Therefore, educational efforts that involve teenagers and the social environment comprehensively are needed. This community service activity aims to increase the knowledge, understanding, and awareness of teenagers and the social environment about preventing early marriage in Ranokomea Village, West Poleang District, Bombana Regency. The activity implementation methods include observation and coordination with the village government, delivering material by two resource persons, interactive discussions, and evaluation through a Focus Group Discussion (FGD). The first resource person from the Poleang Barat District Office of Religious Affairs (KUA) provided education on laws, age limits, and marriage purposes based on regulations. The second speaker, an officer from the Poleang Barat District Family Planning (KB) office, gave a talk about couple’s mental readiness, women’s reproductive health, preparedness for parenthood, parenting, and preventing stunting in toddlers. The activity results showed that participants had a better understanding of the consequences of early marriage and the importance of being ready before starting a family. Participants also showed enthusiasm by actively joining in discu…

title: Eco-mechanical performance of fly ash-modified concrete blocks: strength development and CO<sub>2</sub> emission assessment
abstract: Fly ash is a waste product from coal combustion and can be used as a partial substitute for cement, thereby aiding in the production of lower-carbon-footprint concrete. Most studies have focused only on mechanical or environmental performance, and fewer studies are available that integrate properties of fly ash concrete in terms of mechanical performance, water absorption and CO2 emissions at low replacement rates (£20%). Accordingly, this study aims to meet this need by developing an integrated eco-mechanical evaluation to identify a practical replacement criterion based on three indicators. Five mixtures with varying amounts of fly ash (0%, 5%, 10%, 15% and 20%) were developed. The compressive strength, splitting tensile strength and water absorption after 28 days were tested in the laboratory, while the cradle-to-gate CO2 emission was calculated by calculating the CO2 emission from every constituent of the concrete. These results indicate that the 5% fly ash was able to achieve about 94.3% compressive strength of the control mixture, while also reducing CO2 emissions by 4.71%, yielding the best strength–carbon balance of the mixtures. Increased replacement levels resulted in higher emission reduction, up to 18.85% at 20% fly ash, while producing more significant strength reductions. The findings serve as the basis for policy and specific specifications that would be associat…

title: Enantioconvergent Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of α-Aryl Ketones via Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Photochemical enantioselective nickel catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing stereogenic C(sp3)–C(sp2) bonds in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel-catalyzed enantioconvergent decarboxylative cross-coupling of α-aryl carboxylic acid derivatives with aliphatic carboxylic acids, providing efficient access to enantioenriched α-aryl ketones. The reaction selectively engages two structurally distinct carboxylic acid-derived coupling partners while suppressing competing protodecarboxylation and homocoupling pathways. This protocol features broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee), providing a modular and practical approach to chiral α-aryl ketones from readily accessible carboxylic acid feedstocks.

title: Energía eólica y aerogeneradores: la revolución verde impulsada por el viento
abstract: El uso de combustibles fósiles, como el carbón y el gas natural, para la generación de electricidad produce grandes cantidades de gases de efecto invernadero, principalmente dióxido de carbono (CO₂), que contribuyen al calentamiento global, un fenómeno que impulsa el cambio climático. Una forma de mitigar el impacto ambiental del sector eléctrico es impulsar una transición energética hacia fuentes renovables, entre las que destaca la energía eólica. Esta fuente energética ha acompañado a la humanidad desde hace más de tres mil años: los antiguos egipcios ya aprovechaban la fuerza del viento para impulsar embarcaciones, y en la Edad Media se utilizaba para accionar molinos. Sin embargo, no fue sino hasta 1887 cuando el viento se empleó por primera vez para generar electricidad, mediante la construcción del primer aerogenerador. La energía eólica aprovecha la energía cinética del viento para producir electricidad por medio de aerogeneradores, dispositivos diseñados para transformar el movimiento del aire en energía eléctrica. Aunque existen diferentes tipos, todos comparten cuatro componentes fundamentales: el rotor, el sistema de transmisión, el generador eléctrico y el sistema de control. Los aerogeneradores se clasifican según diversos criterios: a) por la orientación de su eje, pueden ser de eje horizontal o de eje vertical; b) por su potencia, se dividen en microeólicos, min…

title: DIGITAL MARKETING AND CONSUMER KNOWLEDGE : RESIDENTIAL SOLAR ENERGY ADOPTION INTENTION THROUGH PERCEIVED SUSTAINABLE PRODUCT INNOVATION
abstract: This study examines the influence of digital marketing and consumer knowledge on residential solar energy adoption intention, with perceived sustainable product innovation serving as a mediating variable. A quantitative survey approach was employed using data collected from 223 respondents in Indonesia and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings demonstrate that digital marketing and consumer knowledge positively and significantly influence perceived sustainable product innovation and residential solar energy adoption intention. Perceived sustainable product innovation also significantly strengthens adoption intention and partially mediates the effects of both digital marketing and consumer knowledge. These findings indicate that consumers are more likely to consider adopting residential solar energy when they receive relevant and credible digital information, possess sufficient knowledge about solar technology, and perceive solar energy as an innovative and sustainable solution. The study contributes to the renewable energy adoption literature by integrating external marketing communication, internal consumer knowledge, and perceived sustainable innovation within a single consumer-level framework. It also highlights perceived sustainable product innovation as an important mechanism through which digital marketing and consumer…

title: From Solvency to Dignity: Artificial Intelligence, Energy, and a New Social Pact
abstract: Artificial intelligence requires systematic reflection on the relationship between technological progress, collective responsibility and the dignity of the person, making a new social pact necessary. The article links dependence on fossil fuels to geopolitical imbalances, inflationary pressures and the ability of authoritarian regimes to support power policies, proposing international coordination, including at the UN, that reconciles energy security, climate protection and the transition to renewable sources and, in perspective, nuclear fusion. This analysis is accompanied by the criticism of an economy based exclusively on solvency, which excludes needs without adequate purchasing power from the production and distribution of essential goods. To combat poverty, inequality and vulnerability to war, an international agency capable of promoting socially useful work and coordinating the production and distribution of fundamental resources is envisaged. In this framework, artificial intelligence and robotics could contribute to the analysis of needs, the organization of work, agriculture, assistance and scientific research, as long as they remain subordinate to democratic decision-making and criteria of transparency, human control and non-discrimination. Finally, the technological comparison between the United States, China and Europe shows the need, especially for Europe, to stre…

title: An Improved Workflow for Shale Resource Assessment: Demonstrated Using Triassic Chang 73 Shale
abstract: Abstract In the context of energy structure transition, fossil fuels will continue to play a crucial role in the near- to medium-term future. Globally widespread shale deposits possess significant resource potential and have become key targets for energy exploration, amid growing challenges posed by the supply-demand imbalance of conventional petroleum and continuously rising energy consumption. Accurate assessment of shale oil potential, vital for informed exploration and decision-making, is still hampered by issues in hydrocarbon loss correction and resource classification criteria. This study addresses these core issues by proposing an innovative evaluation workflow that integrates geological data and optimization algorithms, using lacustrine shale samples from the third submember of the seventh member of the Triassic Yanchang Formation as an illustrative example for method validation. Our findings indicate that hydrocarbon loss significantly impacts the quality assessment of shale reservoirs. As thermal maturity increases, resource boundaries and oil retention threshold gradually decrease. This implies that shale reservoirs with high thermal maturity may demonstrate superior resource quality at similar levels of TOC and oil contents, making them favorable targets for exploration. Compared to existing classification schemes, the proposed method offers two major advantages. F…

title: Behaviour Intervention Plans in Special Education: Design Versus Delivery
abstract: Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) occupy a central position in the institutional practice of special education. Anchored in the logic of functional assessment and the ethics of positive behaviour support, the BIP is the document that translates the functional analysis of a learner’s challenging behaviour into a programme of antecedent modifications, skill instruction, reinforcement contingencies, and response procedures. This narrative review synthesises the conceptual and evidentiary literature on BIPs across three interlocking domains: functional behaviour assessment as the epistemic foundation of the plan, positive reinforcement as the primary engine of behavioural change, and de-escalation as the ethical and safety perimeter within which the plan operates. The review traces the emergence of the BIP from the applied behaviour analytic tradition, documents the statutory and regulatory frameworks within which BIPs are generated, examines the quality indicators proposed in the methodological literature, and identifies recurring points at which the implemented BIP diverges from the plan as written. Particular attention is given to the paraprofessional workforce that most frequently implements BIPs in classroom settings, to the challenges of generalisation and maintenance across settings, and to the tensions between fidelity to the plan and clinical responsiveness to the learner…

Classroom Sensory Accommodations: Integrating Tools into Instructional Design
abstract: Sensory processing differences are now recognised as a defining feature of the experience of a substantial proportion of learners with autism spectrum disorder and are independently documented in learners with a range of developmental, behavioural, and mental-health conditions. Classrooms that were designed around the assumption of typical sensory regulation impose, on these learners, an environmental load that substantially interferes with their capacity to attend, engage, and learn. Sensory regulation strategies have entered routine classroom practice in response to this recognition, and three categories of tools have emerged as particularly prevalent: weighted items (blankets, vests, lap pads), quiet spaces (sensory rooms, break corners, regulatory retreats), and fidget aids (tactile objects, stress balls, resistance bands). Each category is supported by practitioner-oriented guidance, by a developing empirical literature, and by competing theoretical accounts. This paper proposes a conceptual framework that integrates the three categories into a coherent classroom-level approach to sensory regulation, grounded in the theoretical vocabulary of sensory integration and the Model of Human Occupation, and informed by the implementation realities of contemporary inclusive and specialist classrooms. The framework specifies the regulatory logic of each tool category, the conditions…

title: Design of π-Conjugated Donor-Bridge-Acceptor Radicals for Molecular Qudit Applications
abstract: Abstract Organic radicals with spin-polarized excited-state manifolds are attractive molecular platforms for quantum information technologies. A central challenge lies in the understanding of how emissive doublet states can communicate with higher-spin quartet states while maintaining efficient luminescence. In this context, we propose here a series of donor-bridge-acceptor radicals based on anthracene or naphthalene donors coupled to the tris(trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM•) radical acceptor. By combining excited-state electronic-structure analysis with interpolated coordinate pathways, we reveal how the locally excited (LE) states and charge-transfer (CT) states govern the accessibility of quartet manifolds and enable radical-enhanced reverse intersystem crossing (ERISC). Structural variations, including steric hindrance and donor–acceptor spatial separation, are shown to modulate the CT-state characteristics and reshape the LE-CT energy landscape. Our results identify the electronic-structure requirements and molecular design strategies for achieving both optically addressable emission and manipulation of quartet states, two key ingredients for molecular qudit architectures.

title: Transition to Destination: Semiotic Design Strategies for Thematic Pedestrian Bridges in Jakarta
abstract: This study reveals that the infrastructure of Jakarta experienced a paradigm shift towards place-making/destination design strategies from bridges for functional pedestrian use. From an architectural semiotic perspective, this study identifies a design strategy that uses visual form, elements, and signifiers (space) to convey the signified meaning (conceptual) related to iconic public spaces. This shift is investigated utilizing three case studies of pedestrian bridge infrastructure in Jakarta, which are recognized as Jembatan Penyebrangan Orang: Tebet Ecopark (the Link JPO), the Gelora JPO in Sudirman, and Phinisi JPO in Karet. These issues were chosen due to the robust characteristics of their design, which are capable of representing public behavior through intentional visitation from transit. Utilizing a qualitative approach, the study generates a formal evaluation of elements of semiotic architecture across visual, formal, and spatial dimensions. The research uncovers specific strategies of semiotics in every issue: the metaphor of the ship for Phinisi JPO, the Gelora JPO lighting dynamics, and the Ecopark JPO organic connectivity. The discussion illustrates that effective design strategies of semiotics transcend the infrastructure's technical functions, functioning as design narratives and a communication medium while building the identity from functionality. abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly informs consequential enterprise decisions, yet prevailing governance approaches tend to assess ethical principles, model properties, regulatory conformity or audit activities in isolation. This conceptual paper argues that trustworthy AI governance should focus on the organizational decision supported by AI rather than on the model alone. It develops Decision Assurance by Design, a capability framework that embeds assurance requirements across the AI lifecycle and connects trustworthy AI principles to organizational capabilities, operational controls, assurance evidence and explicit decision authorization. A structured integrative review synthesizes research on responsible AI governance, algorithmic auditing, organizational capability, sociotechnical systems and assurance reasoning. title: Design, synthesis, and structural characterization of novel 4-aminoantipyrine derivatives: Experimental and computational insights via DFT and molecular docking
abstract: 4-Aminoantipyrine (4-AAP) derivatives are of significant interest in medicinal chemistry because of their diverse therapeutic potentials. In this study, we report the synthesis of five novel 4-aminoantipyrine derivatives ( P1–P5 ). The synthetic approach involved the initial preparation of enaminone ( I1 ) via a solvent-free reaction of 4-aminoantipyrine with acetylacetone, followed by condensation with various primary amines or hydrazides in refluxing ethanol solution. The chemical structures of the prepared compounds were characterized using mass spectrometry, FT-IR, and NMR ( 1 H and 13 C) spectroscopy. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed at the B3LYP/6-311++G (d,p) level to optimize the molecular geometries and evaluate the global reactivity properties. Computational analysis revealed that the planarity of the molecules was highly dependent on the substituents of the imine moiety, with compounds P1 , P4 , and P5 exhibiting near-planar geometries. Furthermore, molecular docking simulations were conducted against Human DNA Topoisomerase I (PDB: 1T8I) to assess the binding affinity and potential anticancer mechanisms of the derivatives. These results were complemented by ADMET and toxicity predictions using the Swiss ADME and ProTox-3.0 platforms to evaluate their pharmacokinetic profiles and drug-like properties. title: Parametric Analysis of Thermal and Electrical Performance of Photovoltaic Thermal Systems Using Nano-Graphene Coolants and Enhanced Fin Design
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive three-dimensional numerical simulation to assess the performance of a photovoltaic thermal (PVT) system utilizing nanofluids (NFs) and enhanced fin configurations. The system integrates a copper flat plate collector, where nanofluids circulate within heat absorber tubes, and rectangular fins are strategically arrayed to augment heat dissipation. The effects of fin dimensions, count, nanofluid concentration, flow rate, and solar intensity on the PVT's thermal and electrical performance are examined. Key findings illustrate that fin configuration, particularly the number of fins, significantly dictates the system’s thermal management, with minimal impact from fin thickness. Optimal thermal behavior was observed with 0.5 wt% graphene nanoplatelet nanofluid at a mass flow rate of 0.1 kg/s, employing 400 fins. Analysis reveals that increasing the number of fins from 10 to 400 could enhance the thermal efficiency by approximately 18%, while reducing the overall system temperature by up to 7°C under peak solar conditions. Furthermore, the study indicates that an increase in solar radiation intensity from 800 to 1000 W/m2 reduces the electrical efficiency by about 2%, even though the electrical power output increases by 5%.

title: Design Quality Analysis of the Whispering Butterfly Robe as a Bridal Preparation Product
abstract: This study aims to analyze the design quality of the Whispering Butterfly Robe as a bridal preparation product. The robe was designed by adapting the characteristics of butterflies as the main source of inspiration, expressed through the application of organza floral appliqués and three-dimensional (3D) butterfly embellishments to create a feminine and elegant visual appearance. This study employed a descriptive quantitative method with an evaluative approach. The design quality assessment was conducted through expert judgment involving five fashion experts, including professors, educators, alumni, and fashion designers. The research instrument consisted of a validation sheet covering six evaluation aspects: design, sizing, sewing techniques, aesthetics, garment performance, and product uniqueness. The collected data were analyzed using descriptive statistics in the form of percentages. The results indicate that the Whispering Butterfly Robe achieved an average suitability score of 91.93%, categorized as “highly suitable.” The aesthetic aspect received the highest score (99.33%), followed by sizing (96.67%), garment performance (96.00%), and both design and sewing techniques (90.00%). Product uniqueness obtained a score of 79.33% and was categorized as “acceptable.” Overall, the findings demonstrate that the robe possesses high design quality and successfully integrates aesthet…

title: Franks & Farquhar (2007) and beyond: The influence of guard and subsidiary cell bio-mechanics on stomatal function
abstract: Abstract Stomata are the gatekeepers to leaf gas exchange and as such are essential for CO2 uptake for photosynthesis, water loss for evaporative cooling and ultimately plant growth and productivity. Research has long focused on understanding the mechanisms that govern stomatal aperture adjustments, in particular how changes in turgor pressure in GCs are achieved and how these cause the reversible cell shape distortion that leads to pore opening and closing. Here we discuss the immense impact the paper by Franks and Farquar (2007) has had on this research field, both in the past and more recently, by stimulating new angles of exploration of stomatal mechanics. As new techniques have emerged, the impact of the mechanical advantage of epidermal/subsidiary cells and how this is overcome by GCs has inspired novel studies into the importance of subsidiary to stomatal function, the effect of different cell shapes (dumbbell vs kidney shaped) on stomatal kinetics, the significance of cell geometries and cell complexes, as well as the underlying biochemical cell wall composition responsible for GC deformation. Whilst many questions remain unanswered, we summarize the take-home messages from the key literature on stomatal biomechanics.

title: Pengendalian Kelelahan Kerja sebagai Upaya Menjaga Keselamatan Pekerja Batching Plant di PT X
abstract: Work-related fatigue is one of the occupational safety and health problems that can affect workers’ concentration, performance, and safety. This community service activity aimed to identify workers’ physical fatigue conditions and determine fatigue control efforts in the work area with the highest fatigue level. The activity was conducted at PT. X, Balikpapan, involving 18 workers from QC and Lab, Workshop, and Batching Plant areas. The activity began with hazard identification using Hazard Identification, Risk Assessment, and Determining Control (HIRADC), followed by physical fatigue measurement using the Three-Dimensional Work Fatigue Inventory (3D-WFI). The results showed that the highest level of physical fatigue was found among Batching Plant workers. Based on these findings, a Fatigue Management SOP was developed covering work and rest schedules, short breaks, hydration, worker condition monitoring, fatigue handling, and recovery. The SOP is expected to increase workers’ awareness and support more structured and consistent fatigue control. Further evaluation is needed to determine the effectiveness of SOP implementation in controlling workers’ fatigue.

title: INVESTIGATION OF THE EFFECT OF PH VALUES ON THE PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF COPPER OXIDE NANOSTRUCTURES BY GREEN ASSISTED METHOD USING Origanum vulgar PLANT EXTRACTS
abstract: Copper oxide (CuO) nanoparticles were synthesized using the green method. The extract of the Origanum vulgare (O. vulgare) leaves has been used as a capping and reducing agent of CuO nanoparticles. The influence of pH values in the green growth solution (7.5–10.5) on nanoparticle properties was investigated using various characterization techniques. The obtained results from both optical properties and FTIR analysis confirmed that the O. vulgare plant extract is a highly efficient reducing and stabilizing agent. The UV-Visible spectrum of the O. Vulgare plant extract shows two distinct absorption peaks at 287.439 nm and 324.15 nm at ambient temperature. The FESEM results revealed that the pH of the growth solution significantly affects the morphology, shape, dimensions, and orientation of CuO nanoparticles. The sphere and rod-like nanoparticles were produced as the pH value changed from 7.5 to 10.5, with an average diameter in the range of (16.89-28.50) nm. The obtained results of XRD analysis confirmed that the fabricated CuO nanoparticles have a monoclinic crystal structure with crystalline size in the range of (10.7-17.81) nm. UV–Visible spectra of CuO nanoparticles at different pH values show strong UV absorbance < 300 nm and have band-gap energies in the range of (1.82-1.98) eV. The FTIR analysis of nanoparticles confirmed their purity and suggested that nanoparticles synt…
venue: Science Journal of University of Zakho

title: Performance Evaluation of Modular UPS Technology for Mission-Critical Applications: A Case Study of Centiel Stratus Power UPS
abstract: Mission-critical facilities require continuous, stable and high-quality electrical power. Modular uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems can provide incremental scalability, internal redundancy, rapid module replacement and improved capacity utilisation, but these outcomes depend on architecture, loading, fault isolation and maintenance. This conceptual paper evaluates Centiel StratusPower as an illustrative case through an integrative review grounded in reliability engineering, modularity, fault tolerance and power-quality perspectives. The synthesis links reported technological capabilities—including decentralised control, online double conversion, N+1 redundancy, adaptive module management and monitoring—to technical and operational outcomes. StratusPower is architecturally aligned with mission-critical requirements, although manufacturer-reported efficiency and availability claims require independent laboratory and field validation. The resulting framework and five propositions provide a basis for comparative testing and technology-selection decisions.
venue: Journal of Business Practice and Academic Research

title: Apports de la modélisation pour analyser les interactions entre plantes et définir les composantes des prairies multi-espèces – l’exemple de Virtual GrassLand
abstract: Face aux défis du changement climatique et à la nécessité de réduire les intrants, les prairies multi-espèces apparaissent comme un levier majeur pour renforcer la résilience et la durabilité des systèmes fourragers. Leur succès agronomique est reconnu, mais la meilleure façon de les adapter face à ces enjeux reste à définir. Les modèles individu-centrés, tels que Virtual GrassLand, permettent de simuler les interactions plante-plante et les dynamiques des communautés prairiales, offrant un laboratoire virtuel pour tester des compositions d’espèces, déterminer les traits d’intérêt et des pratiques culturales (e.g. mélanges de variétés) favorisant différents services. Ils ont par exemple permis de montrer par simulation que des objectifs de surproduction et de stabilité dans le temps des associations graminées-légumineuses étaient bien possibles dans des environnements bas intrants. Augmenter la diversité intraspécifique favoriserait la stabilité des communautés, mais n’augmenterait pas systématiquement la production. Ces approches ouvrent la voie à la conception de prairies multi-espèces adaptées à différents pédoclimats et à la définition d’idéotypes variétaux raisonnés pour leur usage en association avec d’autres espèces.

title: Why Do Older Adults Commence, Re-Commence and Continue Volunteering? Prioritising Enablers and Barriers to Participation
abstract: Volunteering is recommended as a way for older adults to age healthily due to a variety of biopsychosocial health benefits. The literature has previously identified a wide range of modifiable enablers and barriers to older adult volunteering participation, for example, supervisory support structures, program flexibility, and training quality; however, these have not yet been prioritised. Policymakers may benefit from knowing which strategies are likely to have the greatest immediate impact on recruitment and retention. This study aimed to prioritise enablers and barriers to volunteering and to compare priorities across four participant groups: Volunteer Program Representatives, Current volunteers, Former volunteers and Never volunteers. Participants (n = 681) were older adults in Australia aged 60 years and over or volunteer programme representatives aged 18 years and over. They were predominantly current volunteers based in Victoria. Participants completed an online survey scoring enablers and barriers to volunteering using Likert scale responses to indicate the importance of each item to commencement and continuation in volunteering. Data were analysed descriptively for responses to each item for each participant group, and simple pairwise comparisons were conducted between groups. Feeling welcome scored the highest for all participant groups (Participant Group (Median, IQR):…

title: From representation to equitable participation: An overview of multicultural education research published in 2025
abstract: Multicultural education research has expanded rapidly, but its definitions remain varied and the distinction between representation and equitable participation remains unresolved. This thematic-bibliometric review of one publication year examines 210 English-language articles published in 2025 and classified in the field of Social Sciences in Scopus, the sole database. The articles span 135 sources and 56 affiliation countries. The single-year design offers a concentrated view of contemporary conceptual patterns without estimating change over time. Bibliometric analysis examined publication, authorship, affiliation-country, keyword, bibliographic coupling, and cited reference patterns. Hybrid codebook thematic analysis examined how titles, author keywords, and abstracts framed multicultural education, without appraising complete articles. Keyword and co-citation patterns connected educator learning with diversity, equity, culturally responsive teaching, intercultural competence, policy, and a shared knowledge foundation in culturally relevant, responsive, and sustaining pedagogy. Six themes addressed recognition, culturally grounded pedagogy, institutional enactment, power and formal inclusion, learner development and access, and conceptual and evidential gaps. Through the theoretical framework, the themes inform a provisional educational ecology specific to this corpus. Within…
venue: Journal of Multicultural Education and Engagement

title: Liturgical Sonic Order in the Catholic Mass: Music, Participation, and the German-Language Gotteslob
abstract: Die musikalische Partizipation in der nachkonziliaren römischen Messe nimmt durch öffentlich zugewiesene Aufgaben sowie deren textuelle und zeitliche Organisation Gestalt an. Dieser theoretische Aufsatz entwickelt die liturgische Klangordnung als Verfahren zur Rekonstruktion und zum Vergleich musikalischer Rollenbeziehungen. Er verbindet liturgische Normen mit institutionellen Kommentaren und Repertoirezuordnungen zum Gloria GL 166, Sanctus GL 200 und Kehrvers GL 37,1 mit Psalm 23 im deutschsprachigen Gotteslob. Der Vergleich untersucht Textbewegung und zeitliche Rollenorganisation. Die Wiederöffnung desselben Textauftrags wird aus der geordneten Text-Rollen-Folge abgeleitet und erfasst dessen Rückkehr nach einer dazwischenliegenden Phase, die einer anderen öffentlichen Rolle zugewiesen ist. Der Gloria-Kommentar beschreibt die Verteilung der Textabschnitte und ihren motivischen Zusammenhang. Der Sanctus-Vergleich unterscheidet eine interne Wiederaufnahme im gemeinsamen Vollzug von der Rückkehr des Gemeindeauftrags mit dem Hosanna während der Einführung. Die Psalmkonfiguration ordnet die wiederkehrende Antwort nach dem Versvortrag. Normative Gloria-Varianten halten die liturgische Funktion konstant; zwei Gedankenexperimente verdeutlichen Beziehungen im Gesamtverlauf und an lokalen Übergängen. Das Verfahren zeigt, welche Quellenangaben eine strukturelle Deutung verändern, und prä…

title: Parental Participation Management for Improving School Quality in Elementary Schools with Limited Students Enrollment
abstract: This study aims to describe and analyze the management of parental participation in improving school quality in schools with limited student enrollment in Pugung District, Tanggamus Regency. The research focuses on the planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling (POAC) aspects of parental participation, supporting and inhibiting factors, and the school’s efforts to enhance sustainable parental involvement. A qualitative approach with a descriptive design was employed. Research participants included principals, teachers, school committee members, and parents. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, and analyzed using data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing techniques. The findings indicate that parental participation management has not been systematically implemented. In the planning stage, parental involvement remains limited to specific activities. The study highlights the necessity of structured and sustainable participation management to support quality improvement in schools with limited student enrollment. Keywords: Parental Participation Management, School Quality, Limited Student Enrollment, Educational Management, Primary School

Improving Students’ Mastery of Sequence Words in Recount Text through Creative Dance Strategy
abstract: Writing recount texts can be challenging for junior high school students, particularly when they need to generate ideas and use sequence words appropriately. This study aimed to improve students’ mastery of sequence words in recount texts through the implementation of Creative Dance Strategy, with particular attention to students’ ability to generate ideas for writing. The study employed Classroom Action Research based on the Kemmis and McTaggart model, consisting of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The research was conducted in Class VIII-A of SMP Negeri 1 Hiliduho during the second semester of the 2025/2026 academic year and involved 29 students. Data were collected through a preliminary writing test, writing tests at the end of each cycle, observation sheets, field notes, and documentation. Quantitative data were analyzed using mean scores and the percentage of students achieving the Kriteria Ketercapaian Tujuan Pembelajaran (KKTP), while qualitative data were analyzed descriptively. The results showed an improvement in students’ writing achievement, with the mean score increasing from 53.31 in the preliminary test to 64.66 in Cycle I and 83.45 in Cycle II. The percentage of students achieving the KKTP score of 75 also increased from 13.79% in Cycle I to 100% in Cycle II. The findings indicate that Creative Dance Strategy supported students in generating ideas …
