title: Diksi dan Eufemisme dalam Komunikasi Pejabat Publik: Implikasi bagi Pembelajaran Bahasa Indonesia
abstract: Bahasa pejabat publik tidak hanya berfungsi sebagai sarana penyampaian informasi dan kebijakan, tetapi juga menjadi sumber daya strategis untuk membangun makna, mengelola persepsi publik, dan merespons tekanan sosial. Dalam konteks tersebut, pilihan diksi dan penggunaan eufemisme menjadi penting, terutama ketika pejabat menyampaikan isu sensitif seperti kontroversi kebijakan, kritik, kesalahan, dan keresahan masyarakat. Penelitian mengenai eufemisme dalam wacana politik telah menunjukkan bahwa bentuk bahasa tidak langsung dapat digunakan sebagai strategi retoris untuk memperhalus makna, membangun citra positif, dan mengelola respons publik. Namun, pemanfaatan komunikasi pejabat publik sebagai sumber pembelajaran bahasa Indonesia, khususnya untuk pengembangan literasi kritis, masih perlu dikaji lebih lanjut. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis bentuk, penggunaan kontekstual, dan fungsi komunikatif diksi serta eufemisme dalam komunikasi pejabat publik serta mengidentifikasi implikasinya bagi pembelajaran bahasa Indonesia. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan deskriptif kualitatif dengan analisis wacana berbasis korpus. Data berupa 40 pernyataan pejabat publik yang dikumpulkan dari konferensi pers, pidato resmi, dan komunikasi melalui media sosial resmi selama tahun 2026. Data didokumentasikan, diverifikasi berdasarkan sumber yang tersedia, kemudian dikodekan, dikategorikan, dan di…
venue: Journal Of Education And Teaching Learning (JETL)

title: Comparative Machine Learning Approaches to Landslide Susceptibility in Southeastern Türkiye
abstract: Landslides are among the most destructive natural hazards in mountainous regions, causing severe economic losses and infrastructure damage. Reliable susceptibility mapping is essential for hazard mitigation and sustainable land-use planning, particularly in tectonically active areas such as southeastern Türkiye. This study aims to compare the predictive performance and spatial consistency of six widely used machine learning algorithms—Support Vector Machine (SVM), Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Naïve Bayes (NB), and Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt)—together with an Ensemble model, under identical geomorphological and environmental conditions. A GIS-based framework was applied using eleven conditioning factors derived from topographic, geological, hydrological, and land-cover datasets. A landslide inventory verified by field observations was used for model training and validation. Model performance was assessed using Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) analysis and the Area Under the Curve (AUC). All models achieved high predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.877–0.959). The NB model performed best (AUC = 0.959), while the Ensemble model produced the most spatially consistent susceptibility patterns. High- and very high-susceptibility zones were consistently associated with steep slopes and weak lithological units. Comparative machine learning a…

title: The Effect of Learning Motivation on Junior High School Students’ Mathematical Representation Ability
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of learning motivation on junior high school students’ mathematical representation ability. This research employed a quantitative approach using a survey method. The population of this study consisted of all seventh-grade students at SMP Negeri 13 Semarang in the 2025/2026 academic year, with a sample of 30 students selected through cluster random sampling. The research instruments included a mathematical representation ability test and a learning motivation questionnaire. The data were analyzed using normality and linearity tests, followed by a simple linear regression test. The results showed that learning motivation has a positive and significant effect on students’ mathematical representation ability, as indicated by a significance value of 0.000 (< 0.05). The coefficient of determination (R²) was 0.486, meaning that learning motivation contributes 48.6% to students’ mathematical representation ability. This finding suggests that students with higher learning motivation tend to have better ability in representing mathematical ideas through various forms of representation. In conclusion, learning motivation plays an important role in improving students’ mathematical representation ability. Therefore, teachers are encouraged to enhance students’ motivation in order to support better mathematics learning outcomes.

title: Does Educational Background Matter? The Role of Competency Alignment in Learning Outcomes among Fashion Education Students
abstract: Students entering vocational higher education often have different secondary educational backgrounds, which are commonly assumed to influence their academic achievement. This study examined whether educational background affects learning outcomes when students learn competencies that are relatively new to all learners. A quantitative causal-comparative (ex post facto) design was employed involving 83 undergraduate students enrolled in the Fashion Education Study Program who had completed the Fabric Construction Techniques course. Participants were classified into graduates of SMK Fashion (n = 32) and graduates of senior high schools (SMA) or non-fashion vocational high schools (n = 51). Learning outcomes were analysed using descriptive statistics and an independent-samples t-test. Students from SMK Fashion achieved a slightly higher mean score than the comparison group (83.47 vs. 82.45), but the difference was not statistically significant, t(81) = 0.793, p = .430, with a small effect size (d = 0.18). These findings indicate that secondary educational background explained little variation in learning outcomes. The study suggests that academic performance in vocational higher education depends less on school type than on the alignment between prior learning experiences and university competencies. The findings highlight competency alignment as an important explanation of learnin…

title: Transforming Organizational Culture Through Leadership and Learning: A Framework for Employee Engagement, Innovation, and Sustainable Performance
abstract: Organizations face continuous pressure to adapt to technological change, evolving workforce expectations, competitive intensity, and rising demands for sustainable performance, yet leadership development, learning, culture change, engagement, innovation, and sustainability are typically designed and evaluated as separate initiatives. This conceptual article develops an integrative framework explaining how transformational leadership and organizational learning jointly drive organizational culture transformation, and how a transformed culture supports sustainable performance through the complementary pathways of employee engagement and organizational innovation. The study adopts an integrative literature review and theory synthesis design, drawing on four complementary lenses: Transformational Leadership Theory, Organizational Learning Theory, Social Exchange Theory, and the Dynamic Capabilities perspective. Peer reviewed evidence is synthesized into four research questions and eight theoretically g
venue: Journal of Business Practice and Academic Research

title: Development of Google Sites-Based Learning Media Integrated with Wizer.me Using CBL-STEM Approach for Relations and Functions
abstract: Advances in digital technology call for innovative, interactive mathematics learning media to facilitate the understanding of abstract concepts, such as relations and functions. This research and development study aims to describe the design process, the level of technical feasibility, and the effectiveness of using Google Sites-based learning media integrated with Wizer.me interactive digital worksheets. Using a descriptive method in a limited-scale pilot study, the study subjects included 32 eighth-grade students from Class VIII-F at SMP Negeri 15 Semarang and a mathematics teacher serving as an expert validator. Data were collected through validation sheets, classroom observation, post-instructional interviews, student reflections, and learning outcome assessments. The results indicate that the learning medium met the criteria for “highly suitable,” with a validation score of 86.76% from the subject teacher; the implementation process was effective, with an average class assessment score of 76.16; and the majority of students provided positive feedback, although internet infrastructure constraints remained the primary technical challenge in the field. These results conclude that the integration of Google Sites and Wizer.me has great potential to serve as an alternative platform to support digital mathematics learning in schools.
venue_publisher: Jurusan Ilmu Komputer Universitas Negeri Semarang

title: Analysis of Students’ Numeracy Literacy in Terms of Self-Efficacy through Problem-Based Learning (PBL) Supported by Flipbooks with an Ethnomathematics Approach
abstract: Students’ numeracy skills in Indonesia remain relatively low due to a lack of attention to the aspect of self-efficacy. In addition, there is a need for instructional models and media capable of improving numeracy skills. This study aims to analyze students’ numeracy skills in terms of self-efficacy following the implementation of an ethnomathematics-based Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model aided by a flipbook. This study employed a mixed-methods approach with an explanatory sequential design, involving 32 eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 13 Semarang during the 2025/2026 academic year. Instruction focused on the topic of function relationships, integrating the ethnomathematics of Semarang City. The research instrument consisted of a numeracy literacy test that met validity criteria (a significance value of for each item) and was deemed reliable based on a Cronbach’s Alpha coefficient of 0,640. The data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics through normality tests, individual achievement tests, class achievement tests, simple linear regression tests in the experimental class, and descriptive analysis based on self-efficacy categories. The results of the study indicate that there was an increase in numeracy literacy skills in the class taught using Problem-Based Learning with an ethnomathematics approach aided by a flipbook ( to ), and that self-efficacy h…

title: The Effectiveness of the Timeline Method on Student Learning Outcomes in Islamic Cultural History Class 4 MI PAS Baitu-l-Quran Gontor
abstract: This study explores the efficacy of the Timeline method on the academic performance of fourth-grade students in Islamic Cultural History at MI PAS Baitul Quran Gontor. The Timeline method presents events chronologically to help students better understand historical sequences. A quantitative experimental approach with a Pretest-Posttest Control Group Design was used. Forty students were selected through Simple Random Sampling, with 20 in both experimental and control groups. Data was analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test with SPSS software. The results indicate a significant difference between the experimental class, which used the Timeline method, and the control class. The experimental class's post-test average was 85.25 compared to the control class’s 71, supported by a Mann-Whitney significance value of Sig. (2-tailed) 0.000 < 0.05. This shows the Timeline method's effectiveness in improving learning outcomes in Islamic Cultural History. Recommendations include encouraging students to enhance motivation and understanding, supporting educators in using innovative teaching methods, and urging institutions to foster creativity in the learning process.

title: Exploring Students' Pictorial Representation of Reading Texts Through Gallery-Based Summarizing in a Basic Reading Course
abstract: Reading comprehension requires students not only to identify information but also to construct, organize, and retain meaning. This study examines how undergraduate students create pictorial representations of reading texts through a Gallery-Based Summarizing activity in a Basic Reading course. Using a qualitative approach, the study analyzed semi-structured interviews with seven undergraduate students at a university in West Java, Indonesia, supplemented by observational notes collected during the creation of pictorial summaries and the subsequent gallery walk. The analysis revealed four themes. Students used deliberate comprehension strategies before drawing, particularly rereading texts and marking keywords. The drawing process involved initial planning, chronological organization of ideas, and deliberate selection of symbols to represent textual information. Students also experienced difficulties in visualizing abstract concepts and selecting information within limited visual space. Despite these challenges, participants reported greater engagement with the texts, increased attention to previously overlooked details, and support for information retention. All seven participants achieved the highest performance category, with a mean score of 14.29 out of 16. Overall, the findings suggest that Gallery-Based Summarizing offers a multimodal approach to reading that connects text…

title: The Analysis of Bilingualism Use in Teaching English at the Eighth Graders of SMP Negeri 2 Manderehe Barat
abstract: Bilingualism is commonly used in English language teaching to facilitate students’ understanding of instructional materials and classroom communication. In English learning, the use of English and Indonesian may help teachers accommodate students with different levels of English proficiency. This study aimed to analyze the types of bilingualism used in teaching English to eighth-grade students at SMP Negeri 2 Mandrehe Barat. This research employed a qualitative descriptive design. The participants were one English teacher and 18 eighth-grade students. Data were collected through non-participant classroom observation, semi-structured interviews, and documentation. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings showed that three types of bilingualism were found in English teaching: coordinate bilingualism, subordinate bilingualism, and compound bilingualism. Coordinate bilingualism occurred most frequently at 34.9%, followed by subordinate bilingualism at 33.3% and compound bilingualism at 31.7%. The teacher used bilingualism to help students understand learning materials, classroom instructions, vocabulary, grammar, and speaking activities. Students also responded positively because bilingual use helped them understand explanations, participate in classroom activities, and feel more confident. The study con…
venue: Journal Of Education And Teaching Learning (JETL)

title: Development of Wedang Ronde Ethnomathematics Teaching Materials in a Problem-Based Learning Model for Social Arithmetic
abstract: This study aims to develop ethnomathematics-based teaching materials integrated with the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model on Social Arithmetic using the traditional culinary context of wedang ronde. This research is motivated by the low mathematical problem-solving ability of students due to mathematics learning that is still abstract and less contextual.1 The research method used is Research and Development (R&D) with the ADDIE development model which includes the stages of analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation.2 The developed product was validated by material experts, media experts, and mathematics learning experts. Data collection techniques were carried out through observation, validation sheets, student response questionnaires, and formative assessments. The validation results showed that the teaching materials were in the very feasible category with scores between 73 and 100 out of a maximum score of 100. A limited trial of 25 seventh grade students showed that the teaching materials were easy to understand, visually appealing, and able to support student involvement in understanding the concept of Social Arithmetic. The integration of local cultural context and PBL syntax encourages students to think critically, collaborate actively, and connect mathematical concepts to real-life situations. Research findings indicate that ethnomathematics-based…

title: Constructing an Adaptive Learning Framework Integrating STEAM–Gamification for Numeracy and Computational Thinking in Remote Indonesian Elementary Schools
abstract: This study aimed to construct and validate the design of an adaptive learning framework that integrates STEAM–gamification principles with Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)–Item Response Theory (IRT) to simultaneously develop numeracy literacy and computational thinking among elementary school students in Indonesia’s 3T (remote, frontier, underdeveloped) regions. A mixed-methods sequential exploratory design integrated with Design-Based Research (DBR) was applied over eight months in Pinrang Regency, South Sulawesi, across 10 schools in the qualitative phase and 20 schools in the quantitative phase. Qualitative data were drawn from interviews and focus group discussions with 30 teachers, 10 principals, 30 students, and 20 stakeholders, alongside 30 classroom observations; quantitative data were collected from 300 Grade IV–V students and 60 teachers using structured surveys, IRT-calibrated diagnostic tests (3PL; α = .83), and an ICT infrastructure audit. The framework synthesized qualitative and quantitative findings into four integrated layers: Pedagogical (STEAM), Motivational (gamification), Adaptive (ZPD–IRT), and Assessment (computational thinking + numeracy). Expert design validation employed LORI, Aiken’s V, and Fleiss’ Kappa with eight domain specialists. The needs analysis showed that 85% of teachers relied exclusively on conventional instruction, 78% identified a stro…

title: Effect Of the Edutainment Learning Model Assisted by Monopoly Game Media on The Learning Outcomes of Grade V Students in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) at SDn 067246 Medan Tuntungan, Academic Year 2026/2027
abstract: This study was motivated by the low learning outcomes of fifth-grade students in the Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) subject at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan. This condition was reflected in the lack of students’ attention and participation during the learning process, as well as the monotonous classroom atmosphere. The study aimed to determine the effect of the Edutainment learning model assisted by Monopoly game media on students’ learning outcomes in the IPAS topic “Indonesia Kaya Raya” among fifth-grade students at SDN 067246 Medan Tuntungan in the 2026/2027 Academic Year. This research employed a quantitative approach using a pre-experimental method with a One Group Pretest-Posttest Design. The sample consisted of 25 fifth-grade students. Data were collected through tests, observations, questionnaires, and documentation. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive statistics, normality testing, correlation analysis, coefficient of determination analysis, and hypothesis testing. The results showed that the average pretest score was 50.88, while the average posttest score increased to 84.80. The correlation test yielded a coefficient of 0.951, indicating a very strong relationship, while the coefficient of determination was 90.44%. The hypothesis test produced a significance value of 0.000 < 0.05, resulting in the rejection of H₀ and acceptance of Hₐ. Therefore, it can be …

title: Collaborative Learning in Inclusive Education: Constructing Tolerant Attitudes of Students at Pondok Modern Darussalam Gontor
abstract: Learning strategies that are focused not just on academic success but also on the development of social attitudes—particularly tolerance in the setting of a heterogeneous society—are required by inclusive education. The purpose of this study is to examine how collaborative learning in inclusive education helps students at the Pondok Modern Darussalam Gontordevelop attitudes of tolerance. This study combined a case study design with a qualitative methodology. Students, instructors, and caregivers at Islamic boarding schools participated in semi-structured interviews, participant observation, and documentation to gather data. Thematic analysis approaches were used to analyze the data. The study's findings show that regular use of collaborative learning techniques fosters an inclusive and engaging environment for social interaction in both the Islamic boarding school's formal and informal learning activities. Through processes of positive interdependence within groups, open discourse, collaborative reflection, and institutional support for the inclusion concept, students develop tolerance attitudes. Students can observe firsthand how to manage conflict, appreciate diversity, and develop empathy in the Islamic boarding school's communal life through collaborative learning. By supporting collaborative learning as an educational approach that contributes to the development of emotive…

title: Innovation Practice as a Mediator between Organizational Learning and Organizational Performance in Case of Flower Firms in Ethiopia
abstract: Organizational learning (OL) and innovation practices (IP) have an impact on firm performance. To enhance their performance and persist in running, firms must learn, share knowledge and create new ideas. These practices can also benefit the environment in the floriculture industry through waste reduction, better utilization of resources and the introduction of new technologies. Organizational performance (OP) was selected as the outcome variable and the mediating variable was IP in the mediation role in nexus of OL on OP among floriculture firms in Ethiopia. The data collection method used was quantitative with descriptive and explanatory research designs. 415 questionnaires were sent out, with 391 of those being returned. The proposed nexus and mediation were tested using SEM. Outcomes observed that OL meaningful influences IP. IP also has a positive influence on OP, but significant. But OL has not a significant direct impact on OP. It also indicates that the nexus in OL and OP is completely mediated by the presence of IP. The study recommends to floriculture companies to increase the strength of OL and IP to enhance OP. Innovation, improved resource utilization and sustainable growth are possible with effective knowledge sharing and the use of new technologies.
venue: Journal of Organisational Studies and Innovation

title: PENGARUH TRANSFORMATIONAL LEADERSHIP, EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT DAN ORGANIZATIONAL LEARNING TERHADAP ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE DIMEDIASI ORGANIZATIONAL RESILIENCE
abstract: Studi ini dirancang untuk menyelidiki dampak kepemimpinan transformasional, partisipasi pegawai, serta proses belajar di lingkungan perusahaan terhadap hasil kerja keseluruhan organisasi. Pengumpulan informasi dilakukan melalui kuesioner yang disebarkan kepada staf, dengan menggunakan teknik analisis numerik melalui model penelitian berbasis survei. Data diperoleh dari 350 responden yang merupakan karyawan pada perusahaan ekspedisi di Batam. Pengolahan data dilaksanakan memakai SmartPLS guna menguji kaitan antara beberapa variabel. Hasil pengamatan memperlihatkan bahwa proses belajar organisasi, partisipasi pegawai, dan gaya kepemimpinan transformasional mempunyai dampak berarti dan baik terhadap performa organisasi.Selain itu, terbukti bahwa ketahanan organisasi berperan sebagai variabel mediasi yang memperkuat hubungan terhadap kinerja organisasi. Hal ini memungkinkan organisasi dengan tingkat ketahanan tinggi untuk mampu beradaptasi, bangkit kembali dari krisis, serta meningkatkan kinerja secara berkelanjutan. Penelitian ini juga memberikan saran bagi manajemen perusahaan agar meningkatkan ketahanan organisasi melalui kepemimpinan, keterlibatan karyawan, dan pembelajaran berkelanjutan. title: The Application of Interactive PowerPoint to Improve Learning Concentration in Pancasila Education Learning for Class XI of SMA Negeri 6 Semarang
abstract: Student concentration during Grade XI Pancasila Education lessons at SMA Negeri 6 Semarang was not optimal. Preliminary observations revealed that a number of students failed to pay attention to the teacher's explanations, engaged in conversations with peers, or busied themselves with activities unrelated to the lesson, thereby hindering the effective reception of instructional information. This study aimed to improve the learning concentration of Grade XI students through the implementation of interactive PowerPoint media. A classroom action research design was employed, conducted over two cycles; each cycle comprised the stages of planning, action implementation, observation, and reflection. Data were collected via observation sheets, questionnaires, and documentation, then analyzed both quantitatively and qualitatively, with a success criterion set at a minimum of 80% of students achieving a "good" category rating. The results demonstrated consistent improvement across stages: the initial condition showed an average score of 56.46 with a class mastery rate of 5.56%; this rose to an average of 61.91 with 61.11% mastery in the first cycle and reached an average of 72.57 with 100% mastery in the second cycle. Thus, the use of interactive PowerPoint media proved effective in enhancing student concentration during Pancasila Education lessons; it is therefore recommended as an alt…

abstract: This study aims to analyze the increase in teachers' teaching activities in Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS). The research uses the Classroom Action Research (PTK) approach with the Kemmis and McTaggart spiral design which includes the stages of planning, action, observation, and reflection. The data collection technique is carried out through observation and documentation with the instrument of the teacher's activity observation sheet. The data was analyzed descriptively quantitatively based on the teacher's activity score in each cycle. The results of the study showed an increase in teacher activity in each cycle, namely from a score of 50 with a good category in cycle I, increased to 70 with a good category in cycle II, and reached a score of 73 with a very good category in cycle III. These findings show that the gradual implementation of the cooperative learning model can improve the quality of teachers' teaching activities and create more interactive, collaborative, and student-centered learning. Enhancing Boiler Operational Economy via Data-Driven Collaborative Combustion Optimization
abstract: Abstract The growing need for flexible operation and reliable steam supply challenges coal-fired boilers to maintain an operating economy through fixed or single-variable combustion adjustments. This study develops a condition-aware, data-driven framework for coordinated combustion optimization. Historical stable-operation samples from the boiler were first classified according to the main steam flow rate and apparent fuel-related operating state. For each operating category, an MSE-constrained RF-NGBoost surrogate model was developed to predict the coal fan variable operating cost. The trained surrogate models then served as the offline response environment for a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) agent, which searched for coordinated target set points of flue-gas oxygen content, bed temperature, and bed pressure drop under operating constraints. The RF-NGBoost models achieved R2 values of 0.967–0.982, RMSE values of 0.387–0.483 CNY/t, and mean absolute error values of 0.255–0.396 CNY/t across the six operating categories. For representative low-, medium-, and high-load conditions, the offline TD3 optimization identified condition-specific target set points associated with predicted coal-electricity operating cost reductions of 0.36–1.07% within the historical feasible domain. Rethinking Leadership Decision Quality in AI-Augmented Strategic Business Environments: Toward an Integrated Multidisciplinary Framework
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in strategic business decision-making through predictive analytics, pattern recognition, forecasting, generative AI, and decision support systems. These capabilities expand organisational analytical capacity, but analytical capacity does not by itself constitute strategic decision quality; strategic decisions also require contextual interpretation, leadership judgment, appropriate reliance on AI, accountability, and adaptation under uncertainty. This conceptual study addresses a mechanism gap in the literature by developing an integrated framework explaining how AI-generated analytical capability can be converted into strategically meaningful managerial decisions through Human–AI Decision Integration. The framework integrates Upper Echelons Theory, Behavioral Decision Theory and bounded rationality, and Sociotechnical Systems Theory. title: Dignity-Preserving Personal Care in Special Education: An Integrated Framework
abstract: Personal care, including toileting and hygiene routines, occupies a distinctive place in the educational lives of learners with complex support needs. The work is simultaneously instructional, relational, and ethical, and its execution substantially shapes the learner's daily experience, her trajectory toward greater independence, and her sense of herself as a valued person whose body is treated with respect. Despite the consequential nature of the work, the professional literature on personal care in special education has developed unevenly, with substantial methodological and clinical development in behavioral protocols but with comparatively limited theoretical attention to the relational and ethical dimensions of personal care as an educational practice. This paper synthesises four strands of literature that bear on personal care in special education: the behavioral lavatory-training tradition descending from the classic protocols of Azrin and Foxx; the contemporary research on lavatory for learners with autism and intellectual disability; the broader literature on functional life skills instruction, systematic instruction, and partial participation; and the ethical and relational literature on dignity, privacy, and self-determination as these apply to the bodily life of learners with disabilities. The paper argues that these four strands must be held together in the design…

abstract: Abstract Background To evaluate the associations of the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and related adiposity-integrated indices with incident glaucoma and explore potential causal evidence using Mendelian randomization (MR). Methods This prospective cohort study included 396,213 participants without glaucoma of European ancestry from the UK. The TyG index and four related indices, including TyG-body mass index (TyG-BMI), TyG-waist circumference (TyG-WC), TyG-waist-to-height ratio (TyG-WHtR), and TyG-waist-to-hip ratio (TyG-WHR), were assessed. Multivariate Cox models and restricted cubic splines were used to examine the association with incident glaucoma. Associations between the corneal-compensated intraocular pressure (IOPcc) and retinal structures were assessed using regression analyses. The predictive performance was evaluated using extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Two-sample MR was conducted to assess the genetic association between the TyG index and glaucoma. Inclusive Self-Efficacy and Paraprofessional Collaboration: An Integrated Framework
abstract: Teacher self-efficacy, the educator's belief in her capacity to organise and execute the courses of action required to produce specified instructional attainments, has emerged as one of the most generative constructs in the educational psychology of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. When applied to inclusive classrooms serving learners with disabilities, the construct both illuminates and complicates the relationship between belief and practice. Inclusive selfefficacy is structured by the educator's perceived competence across instructional, behavioural, and collaborative domains, and the collaborative domain has become increasingly salient as paraprofessional staff has assumed a central role in the daily implementation of inclusive education. This paper synthesises the conceptual and empirical literature on teacher self-efficacy for inclusive practice with the emerging literature on paraprofessional-teacher collaboration, with a view to specifying how the two bodies of work can inform one another. The paper traces the genealogy of the self-efficacy construct within social cognitive theory, examines its specialisation as inclusive self-efficacy, identifies the principal correlates and antecedents documented in the empirical literature, and articulates the role of the paraprofessional workforce in the efficacypractice relationship. title: Dominant crack selection in multi-crack stress corrosion cracking of AISI 316L stainless steel under sustained loading in flowing HCl
abstract: Stress corrosion cracking (SCC) in structural components often involves the simultaneous development of multiple cracks; however, the mechanism by which a dominant crack emerges under sustained loading remains insufficiently resolved. This exploratory study investigates competitive multi-crack SCC behavior in AISI 316L stainless steel under sustained tensile loading in flowing 1 M HCl. Five naturally nucleated surface cracks formed around a central hole were monitored using repeated in situ optical imaging. Interval-based crack growth rates (Δa/Δt) were calculated from five discrete inspection times. Post-test fracture paths were analyzed, supported by SEM fractography and SEM–EDS to assess localized degradation. Fracture-path analysis showed that Cracks 3 and 4 controlled the final trajectory. Interval-based descriptors identified Crack 4 as kinetically dominant within the tested specimen, exhibiting the highest mean and maximum growth rates and the largest cumulative extension. SEM–EDS revealed localized degradation, secondary branching, higher oxygen content, and a detectable chlorine signal in the Crack 4 region. Within the tested multi-crack configuration, dominant-crack behavior could be distinguished using interval-based growth descriptors from discrete observations. abstract: Face aux aléas climatiques et à la réduction des fertilisants minéraux, les prairies multi-espèces incluant des légumineuses apparaissent comme une solution durable, alliant production fourragère équilibrée, résilience et services écosystémiques. Cependant, la multiplicité des mélanges possibles fait que le choix reste complexe pour les éleveurs qui manquent d’informations adaptées à leur contexte. Des Focus Groups réunissant éleveurs, conseillers, distributeurs, obtenteurs et chercheurs ont permis de recenser des attentes vis-à-vis des « idéotypes variétaux ». title: De la plante à la communauté et vice et versa : stratégies et connaissances pour concevoir des prairies multi-espèces
abstract: En France, de plus en plus de prairies sont semées en mélange d’espèces. Ces mélanges répondent à la demande des éleveurs souhaitant des prairies plus pérennes, plus productives en conditions de faibles intrants et mieux équilibrées en termes de valeur nutritive pour les animaux que les cultures pures. Proposer de tels mélanges n’est pas aisé dans un dispositif sociotechnique hérité de la révolution fourragère, encore empreint du modèle de la monoculture et de sa gestion par les intrants. Composer, sélectionner, produire, gérer des mélanges fourragers nécessitent encore de lever des verrous cognitifs, techniques et organisationnels. title: A Disease-Memory Guided Framework for Radiology Report Generation from Multi-View Chest X-rays
abstract: Chest X-rays are widely used, low-cost diagnostic tools. Writing chest X-ray reports manually is a time-consuming and tedious task. The increasing number of X-rays burdens radiologists, creating a need for a clinically accurate, fast and automated report generation system. To solve this challenge, we propose a new disease-memory-guided vision-language framework for radiology report generation. Frontal and lateral chest X-rays (multi-view) are encoded using a Swin-Transformer. These encoded visual features are then passed through a multi-label classification head that predicts disease probabilities, from which the top three labels are converted into learnable disease-memory embeddings. These are concatenated with projected visual tokens and fixed task instruction embeddings to form a multimodal prompt which is fed into a frozen decoder. A LLaMA-2-7B model adapted to the radiology domain using LoRA fine-tuning on the train-only MIMIC-CXR subset is used as an autoregressive decoder. The disease-memory embeddings serve as disease guidance during report generation. An extensive experimental analysis of different experimental variants is conducted on the benchmark Indiana University Chest X-ray dataset using three aspects: 1) statistical n-gram overlap, 2) semantic similarity, and 3) clinical label-based metrics. title: Rethinking School Readiness: Developmental, Ecological, and Pedagogical Perspectives
abstract: School readiness has shifted, over the past several decades, from a narrowly cognitive construct centred on pre-academic skill to a broadly developmental construct encompassing the child's cognitive, linguistic, social-emotional, motor, and regulatory capacities in relation to the expectations of the settings into which the child will transition. The shift has been particularly consequential for young children with developmental differences, for whom readiness is not a property of the child in isolation but a property of the child-setting fit and of the supports available to bridge the gap between current capacity and setting demand. This paper synthesises three traditions that have shaped contemporary understanding of early childhood readiness for diverse learners: developmental psychology, with its attention to the sequenced emergence of capacity; ecological and bioecological theory, with its attention to the nested systems within which development proceeds; and developmentally appropriate practice, with its attention to the pedagogical implications of developmental understanding. The paper argues that these three traditions are complementary rather than competing, that each supplies a distinctive perspective on readiness for young children with developmental differences, and that their integration offers a principled foundation for early childhood special education. title: Social Competence in Special Education: Skills, Reciprocity, and Cooperative Play
abstract: Social competence is now widely recognised as a central outcome of special education, with implications that extend across the academic, emotional, and occupational trajectories of learners with disabilities. The pedagogical infrastructure through which social competence is cultivated includes a diverse set of practices that address discrete social skills, reciprocal interaction routines, and cooperative play arrangements. This paper synthesises the conceptual and empirical literature on three interlocking strands of the social competence curriculum: the teaching of social skills through explicit instruction and structured practice; the development of turn-taking as a foundational reciprocal competence; and the promotion of cooperative play as the most developmentally rich context within which social skills are consolidated and generalised. The paper traces the theoretical foundations of the social competence construct, examines the methodological traditions that have produced the contemporary evidence base, articulates the pedagogical logic of each of the three strands, and considers the conditions under which integration across the strands is most likely to produce generalised and durable gains. Attention is given to the role of peer models, to the distinctive considerations of autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability, and to the ecological conditions that support…

title: Groundwater recharge potential mapping using GIS-AHP for sustainable water management in the Chohal and Damsal Dam command areas, Punjab, India
abstract: ABSTRACT Groundwater is a vital resource in the Shivalik foothills of Punjab, where seasonal rainfall variability, steep slopes, and limited natural storage restrict water availability. This study delineated groundwater recharge potential zones in the command areas of the Chohal and Damsal dams, Hoshiarpur district, Punjab, India, using geospatial techniques integrated with the analytical hierarchy process (AHP). Eight thematic layers, namely, geology, geomorphology, slope, soil, land use/land cover, rainfall, drainage density, and lineament density, were generated from satellite data, field maps, and secondary sources and integrated through weighted overlay analysis in ArcGIS. AHP-based pairwise comparisons identified geology, geomorphology, and rainfall as the dominant factors influencing recharge, followed by soil and slope. The consistency ratio (CR = 0.0113) indicated satisfactory reliability of the assigned weights. Recharge potential was categorized into five classes: very poor, poor, moderate, good, and very good. In the Chohal command area, good and very good zones covered 37.79 and 26.78% of the area, respectively, while in Damsal, these classes occupied 39.77 and 31.12%. Poor and very poor zones together accounted for less than 11% of both areas. Gender, Norms, and Informal Labor: Negotiating Daily Wage Inequality in Rural Bangladesh
abstract: Gender-based wage inequality remains persistent in informal labor markets, where wage-setting is shaped by customary practices, social norms, and unequal bargaining power rather than transparent standards. This qualitative study examines how wage inequality is experienced, justified, and reproduced among women daily laborers in Nageswari Upazila, Kurigram District, Bangladesh. Drawing on 30 in-depth interviews with women daily laborers, 30 with men, four focus group discussions (32 participants), and eight key informant interviews, thematic analysis identified five interconnected mechanisms: gendered wage-setting, occupational segregation, contractor-controlled recruitment, unequal bargaining power, and normalization of gender norms. Participants reported daily wage differences of BDT 100–250 between women and men performing comparable work. The evidence indicates these gaps stem from gender norms, limited mobility, unpaid care, contractor dependence, and weak governance rather than productivity differences alone. Addressing equal remuneration requires going beyond formal legal commitments to reform informal recruitment, occupational access, collective bargaining, and local labor governance.

The Effect of Financial Anxiety on Psychological Distress in Contract Teachers with Social Support as Moderator
abstract: Background: Psychological distress is one of the psychological problems that contract teachers are vulnerable to experiencing, particularly when facing financial limitations and uncertainty regarding employment conditions. Financial anxiety can increase psychological pressure through concerns about financial conditions and security, but its impact may differ for everyone. Social support is thought to play a role in reducing this vulnerability by providing psychological and emotional resources for coping with financial stress. Objective: This study aims to examine the effect of financial anxiety on psychological distress and the role of social support as a moderator among contract teachers. Methods: The study employed a quantitative approach with a correlational design involving 100 contract teachers selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K10), Financial Anxiety Scale (FAS), and Interpersonal Support Evaluation List (ISEL). Data analysis used Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). Results: The results demonstrated that social support significantly moderated the relationship between financial anxiety and psychological distress (β = -0,164; p = 0,018). title: Financial Technology, Digital Transformation and Higher Education Outcomes: Evidence from Saudi Arabia in Comparative Perspective (2019–2023)
abstract: Using comparative data for Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States over 2019–2023, this study examines conditional associations between Financial Technology (FinTech), digital infrastructure, and higher-education outcomes. The empirical unit is the country-year, yielding 25 observations (5 countries × 5 years). The empirical strategy combines descriptive cross-national benchmarking with parsimonious two-way fixed-effects panel models. The baseline models use the FinTech Penetration Index (FPI) internet penetration, Gross Domestic Product GDP per capita, and public education spending, with country and year fixed effects. The estimates show mixed conditional associations across enrollment, graduation, and administrative cost per student and are interpreted cautiously because only five countries are observed. Financial inclusion is treated as a theoretical mechanism that is not directly measured in the present panel. The study therefore provides a transparent comparative Financial Educational Technology (FinEdTech) framework while emphasizing the limits of inference from a small national panel.

abstract: Aim. title: Strengthening Educational Financial Governance through the Implementation of the adminara.id Digital Platform at SMA Muhammadiyah 2 Semarang
abstract: SMA Muhammadiyah 2 Semarang still manages education payments manually using a cash book and handwritten receipts, which is prone to recording errors, slow to recapitulate, and low in transparency. This community service program aimed to strengthen school financial governance through the implementation of, and training on, the adminara.id digital payment platform. The program ran in five stages from May to September 2026 and involved school leaders, administrative staff, teachers, and parents. Data were collected through an initial survey, a parent survey, observation, and a post-training evaluation questionnaire, and were analyzed descriptively and qualitatively. The initial survey showed low effectiveness of the existing system (1 of 5) and high urgency of digitalization (5 of 5), with most parental complaints concerning unclear payment status and proof of payment. After a socialization session for about 50 parents and hands-on training for teachers and operators, all evaluation aspects were rated high (4.50–4.90 on a 5-point scale), with usefulness the highest. All respondents, none of whom had used a digital financial application before, found the platform easy to operate, although continued assistance is still needed. Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Financial Market Volatility Classification
abstract: Financial market forecasting remains difficult because asset prices are strongly affected by randomness, noise, and limited short-term predictive information. Methods that aim to estimate precise future returns therefore often struggle to achieve consistently reliable results. To address this issue, this study reformulates the prediction task as a classification problem that distinguishes between different levels of market volatility, taking advantage of the persistence and clustering commonly observed in volatility dynamics. Ten machine learning methods are evaluated under a unified experimental framework, covering linear classifiers, support vector machines, instance-based approaches, decision trees, and ensemble techniques. The empirical results show that all tested models achieve classification accuracies above 80\%, indicating that future volatility states can be identified with relatively consistent performance across different model families. These findings suggest that volatility classification provides a comparatively stable and practically useful machine learning formulation for supporting financial decision-making.

title: Investment Timing and Electricity Decarbonization in Romania Under Stylized Emissions Constraints
abstract: This study compares long term generation/investment patterns in a simplified representation of Romania’s electricity sector between 2025 and 2050. A deterministic OSeMOSYS/MUIO model is used to examine a reference emissions ceiling, a terminal zero emissions target and an accelerated emissions pathway. The scenarios are conditional model experiments that share exogenous demand and technology assumptions. The model includes Romania’s main electricity generation technologies: coal, natural gas, hydropower, nuclear power, wind, and solar photovoltaics, and minimizes the total discounted system cost subject to technical, economic, and environmental constraints. Three likely scenarios are analyzed in the paper: first, a business-as-usual scenario without emission limits, a gradual decarbonization scenario, and finally an accelerated decarbonization scenario. Earlier emissions constraints shift investment toward low emission technologies and reduce modeled cumulative emissions, but they also increase the archived discounted objective under the stated assumptions. The model contains one aggregated node and eight time slices and does not represent explicit storage, electricity imports or exports, curtailment, network congestion, unit commitment or chronological dispatch. abstract: La transición de profesionistas mujeres provenientes de las áreas de Humanidades, Ciencias, Tecnologías e Innovación (HCTI) hacia el mercado laboral, el emprendimiento o los posgrados, en el contexto de la era digital, es en nuestros días un reto estructural complejo en el que convergen tensiones de género, tradiciones institucionales androcéntricas y una de las transformaciones tecnológicas más relevantes que ha impactado el mundo profesional. Esta investigación plantea una conceptualización participativa de esta transición, soportada en el diálogo con mujeres especialistas de los campos HCTI mediante entrevistas semiestructuradas, articuladas con una revisión documental sobre barreras de género en ecosistemas de las industrias y los posgrados iberoamericanos vinculados a tales áreas. title: أثر تقلبات الإيرادات النفطية في مؤشري القيمة السوقية وعدد الأسهم في سوق العراق للأوراق المالية للمدة (2005-2023)
abstract: The research aims to know the impact of oil revenue volatility on the market value and number of shares indices in the Iraq Stock Exchange for the period (2005-2023) by analyzing Iraqi oil revenues, as well as analyzing some market indicators represented by the market value and number of shares indices. To achieve the study objective, the descriptive and quantitative approach was used to analyze and measure the impact of oil revenues on the performance of the Iraq Stock Exchange indices using the (EVIEWS 13) program. The research concluded that crude oil prices are important for countries whose economies depend on oil revenues resulting from the production and export of crude oil, and this applies to Iraq. This dependency has imposed a state of instability and volatility towards the shocks witnessed by oil revenues associated with oil prices in global markets. The research reached that the official authorities in the country must have a real will to change the situation of the Iraqi economy in order to achieve balance and reduce complete dependence on the oil resource .

title: Moving “The Mark of a Criminal Record”: Consumer Preferences and Market Opportunities for Personal Trainers with Criminal Records
abstract: Abstract Sports and physical activities are common behind bars and may be linked to health benefits and positive behavioral changes. As many people with criminal records carry on their training after release and start sport-related small businesses, it is important to examine what may influence potential consumers’ choices. Drawing on existing research on prison sport and recent interest in entrepreneurship among people with criminal records, we administered a novel survey with an embedded conjoint experiment to a national sample of 1,100 U.S. adults in 2025 to determine what factors shape choices for personal trainers and whether factors driving overall preferences—such as trainer credentials and references, mode of instruction (in-person vs. online), session price, and trainer race—operate differently when the trainer is presented as having a prison record. Consistent with prior research on reentry, employment, and prison stigma, respondents preferred trainers with other workout backgrounds (as an after-work gym member, former college athlete, or member of the military) over those who began their training in prison. Respondents also generally preferred Black trainers and training sessions that were less expensive, in-person, and from qualified trainers. However, when assessing trainers with criminal records, the positive effects of in-person classes and cheaper instruction we…

title: ESG SUSTAINABILITY DISCLOSURES AND MARKET-BASED VALUATION IN AN EMERGING ECONOMY: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED NIGERIAN OIL AND GAS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
abstract: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) sustainability disclosure on share price of listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria over ten-year period covering 2016 to 2025. The research employed three dimensions of sustainability disclosures, Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) while share price form the Proxy of the dependent variable (Market performance Valuation). The research used an ex-post factor research design, with population consisting of all the eleven (11) listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria as of 31st December 2025. Judgmental Sampling technique was used in selecting only (7) seven oil firms whose report are up to the study reporting date. Data was sourced from secondary sources, since this is a quantitative research grounded on the positivist paradigm. The analysis was conducted using the two-step system GMM estimation technique, which addressed the dynamic nature of firm performance and controlled for potential endogeneity. However, the findings of the GMM analysis revealed that only environmental and social sustainability had a statistically significant impact on market-based performance, as measured by share price. While Governance disclosure were not statistically significant on share price of listed oil and gas firms. Although the coefficients for the indicators of the variables (Governance Sustainability) were havin…

Redesigned Electricity Institutions with Micro-Nodal Competitive Markets Reduce Electricity Costs Substantially and Induce Dynamic Energy Innovation
abstract: The electricity grid is a collective good that tends toward monopoly. It links private electricity generation to private electricity use. Its institutions converged near-globally at the end of the 20th century. Large-scale producers have separated ownership from transmission system operators. Quasi-markets link them. New challenges and opportunities render that design obsolete. Solar and wind energy are low-cost but intermittent. Decentralized secondary electricity is also becoming low-cost. Fast switches enable real-time adjustments in electricity production and use. Low-cost High-Voltage-Direct-Current lines centralize while also enabling decentralized frequency control. These centralizing and decentralizing options do not fit the currently fragmented markets-and-grids. Their integrated redesign is due, globally. Design elements include: a multi-layered meshed grid; multiple independent grid nodes; market rules that prohibit ownership of multiple linked nodes; real-time nodal pricing; equal prices for all purchasers at a node; and automatic equilibrium across nodes and the entire grid. The new driving mechanisms improve the electricity system’s efficiency and resilience, contributing to several SDGs. They include a single real-time integrated market, car batteries replacing in-grid batteries, and system expansion linked to low-cost renewables. Cost-reduction estimates are hig…

title: State Labor Market Policies and Health
abstract: Policy Points Starting in the 2000s, state governments began adopting labor market policies, including minimum wage laws, earned income tax credits, paid family and medical leave programs, paid sick leave mandates, and scheduling laws. Evidence suggests that labor market policies can improve earnings and job quality, and some are associated with improved worker health. States interested in evidence‐based policies for improving worker health should consider generous, refundable earned income tax credits; higher minimum wages tied to inflation; greater local government discretion to adopt labor market policies; and paid leave programs or mandates. Context State governments have begun to adopt labor market policies, including minimum wage laws, earned income tax credits, paid family and medical leave programs, paid sick leave mandates, and scheduling laws. The presence (or absence) of these laws can affect the health and well‐being of workers. Methods A review of the existing literature. Findings Emerging evidence indicates that state government actions to increase earnings for those in low‐wage jobs and to improve their job quality can lead to better health. Conclusions Encouraging findings in the literature strongly suggest that policymakers should continue to advance state‐level labor market policies to improve the health outcomes of workers, as well as support efforts by resea…

title: A Century and a Quarter of Stock Market Liquidity and Trading Costs
abstract: ABSTRACT A widely cited working paper from the 2000s, now published (Jones, 2026), documents a substantial decline in trading costs and a positive relation between bid–ask spreads and excess returns from 1900 to 2000. We update the analysis and find that over the next quarter century, turnover surges, spreads decline sharply and subsequently cluster near zero, and excess returns become negatively related to spreads. Additional analysis attributes the reversal of the excess returns relation to distortions in the time‐series analysis created by the sudden reduction and clustering of spreads. We find similar distortions using the Amihud illiquidity measure and in simple cross‐sectional analyses, which suggest the effects we highlight might be pervasive.

title: Energy–Carbon Synergy in Data Center-Based Energy Hub: Optimal Trading Decision in Coupled Electricity–Heat Markets Under Ladder-Type Carbon Trading
abstract: Data centers are becoming flexible prosumers in integrated electricity–heat systems (IEHSs) because of their large energy demand, workload flexibility, and waste-heat recovery potential. Coordinating these resources can improve energy utilization and carbon performance while supporting sustainable operation without curtailing computing services. This paper develops a trading decision-making approach for a data center-based energy hub (DCEH) participating in coupled electricity, heat, and carbon markets while accounting for independently operated power and district heating networks. The DCEH strategically bids electricity and heat prices and quantities and acts as a price taker in a ladder-type carbon market. A detailed DCEH model coordinates workload shifting, server operating states, thermal dynamics, waste-heat recovery, combined heat and power, a gas turbine, and energy storage. A bilevel model is then formulated in which the DCEH optimizes its bids and operation at the upper level, while the lower level clears the electricity and heat markets subject to network constraints. The bilevel problem is reformulated as a single-level mixed-integer linear program using KKT conditions, big-M linearization, and binary expansion. Case studies on a PDN33-DCEH-DHN32 system show that coupled energy–carbon trading improves the DCEH’s private financial outcome and reduces emissions, althou…

title: The unseen pain of the Vietnam War: long-term effects of Agent Orange on labor market outcomes
abstract: Abstract We examine the long-term labor market consequences of exposure to Agent Orange during the Vietnam War, focusing on cohorts whose childhoods overlapped the spraying period. Exploiting district-level variation in herbicide exposure intensity, we find exposed individuals attain lower levels of schooling and reduce their labor supply by 7% relative to the mean. Among individuals who remain in their birth provinces, labor income is reduced by 26.7%. We show that cognitive and physical health impairments do not fully explain the effects. Exposure also reduced household income and pushed individuals toward primary industries, away from wage employment. We further document intergenerational effects, as children of exposed parents exhibit lower educational attainment and reduced labor supply. These findings highlight the lasting and multigenerational economic costs of wartime chemical exposure.

title: Cross-cultural relationship management in the context of an emerging market: A social exchange approach
abstract: The purpose of this study is to enrich the understanding of cross-cultural relationship management from an emerging economy perspective. Drawing on social exchange theory, the study examines the case of Savico, a firm operating in Vietnam. The central themes under investigation include the factors that determine cross-cultural relationships with international partners, opportunities and challenges in these relationships, and how they evolve. Semi-structured face-to-face and online interviews were conducted with company representatives in leadership positions. The analysis reveals that while ethical principles, including trust, permeate such interactions, opportunities are heavily influenced by one-sided or nonconcrete rewards. The primary factors undermining relationships with international stakeholders include in-house and unmanageable inadequacies. In turn, their evolution is viewed primarily through the reinforcement of skills and values that are nurtured and embodied by the company’s leaders. Emerging from the analysis, the developed conceptual dimensions enabled a theoretical framework, highlighting various theoretical and practical implications.

title: Carbon Footprints and Indonesia Market Dynamics: The Risk-Mitigation Role of Artificial Intelligence Innovation
abstract: Climate transition has increased investors' concerns about carbon risk, yet evidence remains limited on how firms' technological capabilities shape market responses, particularly in emerging markets. This study examines the effect of carbon risk on stock performance and the moderating role of AI innovation among non financial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2016 - 2024. Drawing on Asset Pricing Theory, Signaling Theory, and Stakeholder Theory, this study argues that AI innovation reduces investors' uncertainty by enhancing firms' environmental management and signaling stronger technological capability. Indonesia provides a relevant setting because its carbon regulation, sustainability reporting, and AI adoption are still evolving. The results show that carbon risk is marginally associated with lower stock returns and increases stock volatility, while AI innovation significantly weakens the positive effect of carbon risk on stock volatility but has no direct effect on stock returns. This study contributes to the climate finance literature by providing evidence from an emerging market and demonstrating that AI innovation serves as a strategic mechanism for mitigating the financial impact of carbon-transition risk. The findings offer implications for managers, investors, and policymakers in supporting a more resilient low-carbon transition

title: Genetic Response of Some Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) Genotypes to Severity of Early and Late Leaf Spot (Cercospora spp) Diseases in Southern Guinea Savannah of Nigeria
abstract: A field experiment was conducted during the 2015 and 2016 cropping seasons to assess the genetic response of groundnut genotypes to the severity of early and late leaf spot diseases at the Teaching and Research Farm of the Federal University of Agriculture, Makurdi, Benue State, Nigeria. Thirteen treatments (groundnut genotypes) used in the disease assessment were Campalla, Samnut-10, Aloshi, Tisha-1, Benue AGR, Ijiwanda, Samnut-22, Borno Brown, Borno Red, Dan-Bomboyo, Samnut-21, Shar-nya, and Ex-Dakar. The treatments were laid out in a randomised complete block design (RCBD) and replicated four times on a 40 x 17 m area containing 52 subplots; each subplot measured 3 x 2 m. Two seeds were sown per hole on each of four ridges, and no synthetic chemical was used. The results revealed significant (P ≤ 0.05) differences among the groundnut genotypes in establishment count, disease severity, combined disease severity, leaf defoliation, fresh leaf yield (kg/ha), fresh pod yield, and 1000-seed weight in both cropping seasons. All treatments expressed different levels of early leaf spot disease severity from 50 to 57 DAS and late leaf spot disease severity from 64 to 71 DAS in both seasons. Combined disease severity showed that Borno Brown, Campalla, Samnut-10, Samnut-21, Samnut-22, and Tisha-1 were resistant (R) to early leaf spot disease; Ijiwanda was moderately susceptible (MS), wh…

title: Organizational Learning as a Mediating Mechanism: Transformational Leadership, IT-Business Alignment, and Service Innovation in Indonesian Healthcare
abstract: The digital health transformation in Indonesia presents a critical challenge for healthcare institutions, where digital maturity often lags behind national integration mandates. This study addresses this research gap by examining the roles of transformational leadership and IT-business alignment in driving service innovation performance. While numerous studies have examined the impact of digital transformation on broader organizational performance, considerably less attention has been directed toward understanding how organizational learning serves as the underlying mechanism through which leadership and technology alignment translate specifically into service innovation outcomes within healthcare settings. Using a quantitative causal methodology, data were obtained from 117 employees at hospitals and community health centers through purposive sampling. Data analysis was performed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS software. The findings demonstrate that IT-business alignment has a favorable and significant effect on service innovation performance. While transformational leadership does not directly influence innovation performance, it serves as a significant driver of organizational learning. These results highlight the necessity for healthcare management to prioritize synergy between digital strategies and business goals while fos…

Reconstructing the Public Service Paradigm for Business Actors: From Policy Objects to Strategic Government Partners in Economic Development
abstract: Public services connected with business activity in Indonesia have been progressively digitized and reorganized, yet legal and administrative friction remains visible when requirements, data, and operational instructions are not synchronized across institutions. Such friction can place business actors in the position of carrying documents between government bodies, repeating information already held by the state, or attempting to satisfy a requirement that another agency is not legally or technically able to issue. This article examines the legal position of business actors within the public-service framework and develops a normative reconstruction that treats them as strategic partners in economic development without weakening the regulatory and supervisory authority of the state. The study uses doctrinal legal research with statutory and conceptual approaches. Primary legal materials include the Public Service Law, the Government Administration Law, the Job Creation Law, Government Regulation Number 28 of 2025 on Risk-Based Business Licensing, regulations on One Data Indonesia and Electronic-Based Government Systems, and the Personal Data Protection Law. Secondary materials consist of public-administration and legal scholarship on public service, licensing, interoperability, and collaborative governance. The analysis finds that the central difficulty is not simply the number …

title: Regional Digitalization and Food-Service Industry Productivity: Evidence from Russian Regions
abstract: This study examines how different dimensions of the regional digital environment are associated with productivity in the food-service sector across Russian regions. Using regional panel data, the study distinguishes among digital infrastructure, digital platform adoption, online consumption, and advanced digital technologies to examine whether these associations vary across regions with different levels of sectoral productivity. Digital infrastructure is consistently associated with higher food-service productivity, with stronger associations observed in lower-productivity regions, suggesting that digital connectivity may be particularly relevant to regional disparities in service-sector development. Digital platform adoption also demonstrates generally positive associations with productivity across the productivity distribution, highlighting the growing importance of digitally enabled service delivery and platform-based business models in food services. In contrast, online consumption has limited contemporaneous associations with productivity but shows a stronger positive association in higher-productivity regions, suggesting that the relationship between digital consumer demand and productivity may depend on existing regional capabilities. Advanced digitalization, captured through a PCA-based index of AI, IoT, big data, and cloud technologies, is negatively associated with pr…

title: Natural Products in Diabetes Mellitus: A Narrative Review of Mechanistic Insights into Metabolic Regulation and Therapeutic Potential
abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a complex metabolic disease characterized by persistent hyperglycemia resulting from impaired insulin secretion, insulin action, or both. In addition to disturbances in glucose metabolism, the disease is accompanied by abnormalities in mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, lipid and protein metabolism, and chronic inflammation that contribute to progressive tissue injury and the development of vascular complications. Although current pharmacological therapies effectively improve glycemic control, many patients continue to experience disease progression and diabetes-associated complications, highlighting the need for complementary therapeutic strategies that target multiple pathogenic mechanisms. Growing evidence suggests that naturally occurring bioactive compounds may provide such multitarget benefits. Plant-derived polyphenols, medicinal herbs, culinary spices, and functional foods have demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, hypoglycemic, hypolipidemic, and insulin-sensitizing properties in experimental and clinical studies. Compounds including curcumin, honey, garlic, fenugreek, cumin, shilajit, and guduchi have been reported to influence several molecular pathways involved in diabetes pathogenesis, including NF-κB-mediated inflammatory signaling, oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum stress, PPARγ activation, advanced glycation end-product fo…

title: Does TikTok Really Matter for Academic Achievement? Self-Regulation and Use Duration Among University Students
abstract: The increasing use of TikTok among university students has raised questions about its relationship with academic achievement. Previous studies have reported mixed findings. This study examined the association between self-regulated learning (SRL)-based TikTok use regulation and semester grade point average (GPA) in the full sample and two daily-use duration groups. It extends previous research by examining how students plan, control, and evaluate TikTok use beyond duration or problematic use alone. Separate subgroup analyses explored the association within each duration group. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey involved 197 university students. Analyses included descriptive statistics, Cronbach’s alpha, Pearson correlation, simple linear regression, and robustness checks. The full-sample association was near zero and nonsignificant (r = −0.038, p = 0.600). Associations were also nonsignificant in the groups reporting more than two hours and two hours or less of daily use. Spearman correlations were nonsignificant, and HC3 and bootstrap analyses provided no evidence of significant linear coefficients, although diagnostic concerns limit interpretation. The measured regulation score alone provided little information about differences in semester GPA in this sample. Broader academic behaviors warrant further investigation to clarify the practical relevance of digital self-regul…

title: From the Law of the Horse to the Workflow: Why Institutions, Not the Model, Decide the EU AI Act’s Effectiveness: Lessons from Hungary’s First-Wave Implementation
abstract: Abstract Whether a new technology needs its own law is an old question, and for artificial intelligence (AI), it has been posed at the wrong level of abstraction. Both the case against technology-specific law and the case for regulation by design treat the AI model as the regulated object, although a general-purpose model acquires its risk only when deployed. This article relocates the regulatory object to the deployment workflow, defined as the envelope of thresholds, escalation pathways and human checkpoints that surrounds a model in use, and reads the EU Artificial Intelligence Act as management-based regulation that works only where the workflow is specifiable and a standing supervisor examines it. Hungary’s first-wave implementation shows the second condition deciding the outcome: the same obligations are supervised by the central bank in finance and by a ministry with no examination relationship in employment, so the Act’s uniform text conceals uneven supervision within one Member State. The Digital Omnibus on AI, which postpones the high-risk obligations because standards and authorities are late, opens a window to build supervision deliberately: the priority is not better definitions but better supervision.

Hubungan Mindfulness dengan Self Regulation pada Mahasiswa STIKes Maharani Malang yang Sedang Mengerjakan Skripsi
abstract: Mahasiswa yang sedang mengerjakan skripsi sering menghadapi berbagai tekanan akademik yang dapat memengaruhi kemampuan mengatur pikiran, emosi, dan perilaku dalam menyelesaikan tugas akhir. Salah satu faktor yang diduga berperan dalam meningkatkan kemampuan tersebut adalah Mindfulness. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis hubungan antara Mindfulness dengan self–regulation pada mahasiswa STIKes Maharani Malang yang sedang mengerjakan skripsi. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain kuantitatif dengan pendekatan korelasional. Sampel penelitian berjumlah 100 mahasiswa semester akhir STIKes Maharani Malang yang sedang menyusun skripsi, yang dipilih menggunakan teknik purposive sampling. Pengumpulan data dilakukan menggunakan instrumen Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ) dan Short Self–Regulation Questionnaire (SSRQ). Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan uji korelasi Spearman. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara Mindfulness dengan self–regulation (P–value = 0,000; p < 0,05) dengan koefisien korelasi sebesar r = 0,700, yang menunjukkan hubungan positif dengan kekuatan korelasi yang kuat. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa semakin tinggi Mindfulness yang dimiliki mahasiswa, semakin tinggi pula kemampuan self–regulation dalam menghadapi tuntutan penyusunan skripsi. title: Rapid Consolidation and Mechanical Characterization of High-Entropy Particle-Reinforced Al-Cu-Mg Composites Through High-Frequency Induction Hot Sintering
abstract: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) and refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have received considerable attention as innovative reinforcements to replace traditional ceramics in lightweight matrices. However, understanding how different high-entropy systems interact under ultra-fast consolidation pathways remains an open challenge. This study compares conventional sintering (CS) and high-frequency induction hot sintering (HFIHS) in an Al-4.5Cu-1.5Mg matrix reinforced with AlCoCrFeNiTi (HEA) and WMoTaNbV (RHEA) particles at various concentrations, enabling a direct comparison of both reinforcement types under identical processing conditions. Results show that HFIHS achieves near-theoretical densification within minutes while restricting atomic mobility and precipitate coarsening through sustained pressure and short thermal exposure. Furthermore, the study observes a clear strengthening dependence on reinforcement content, with the HEA system exhibiting unexpectedly superior mechanical performance and load-bearing capacity compared to the RHEA. Finally, the correlations between ultra-fast sintering, phase evolution, and strengthening mechanisms are discussed, highlighting HFIHS as a promising route for developing high-strength lightweight composites.

title: Business Competition and Institutional Regulation in Explaining MSME Sustainability: Evidence from Strategic Resources and Practices
abstract: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play a critical role in economic growth and job creation, yet achieving long-term sustainability remains challenging in increasingly competitive business environments. Drawing on the Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory, this study examines the effects of digital marketing, circular economy practices, credit facilities, inclusive partnerships, distribution strategy, pricing strategy, and innovation strategy on business competition and MSME sustainability, with business competition as a mediating variable and institutional regulation as a moderating variable. A quantitative research design using a survey was employed to collect data from 250 MSME owners and managers in East Java, Indonesia. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings indicate that circular economy practices, distribution strategy, and pricing strategy significantly affect business competition. Circular economy practices, inclusive partnerships, pricing strategy, and institutional regulation have significant positive effects on MSME sustainability. Business competition has a significant negative effect on MSME sustainability, suggesting that intense competitive pressure may weaken long-term business performance. In contrast, digital marketing, credit facilities, and innovation strategy have no significant …
