title: SF-SRGAN: Shift-Free Transformer GAN with High-Frequency Enhancement for Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Image super-resolution refers to the process of recovering high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, existing methods face three critical challenges: GAN-based approaches suffer from training instability and artifacts; shifted-window Transformers have issues of computational cost and fixed receptive fields; and high-frequency detail modeling along with multi-source feature fusion remains insufficient. To address these issues, this paper proposes SF-SRGAN, a high-frequency enhanced shift-free Transformer generative adversarial network. The generator introduces a shift-free variable-window Transformer architecture that progressively increases window sizes across layers (4 × 4 → 8 × 8 → 16 × 16), achieving natural receptive field expansion without shift operations or masking overhead. A High-Frequency Positional Encoding module is designed to extract multi-directional high-frequency responses via Laplacian kernels and adaptively inject them through a content-aware gating mechanism. An adaptive dual-path fusion mechanism dynamically integrates global Transformer features with local CNN features. The discriminator adopts a multi-scale architecture combined with R1 gradient penalty and an auxiliary edge prediction loss to stabilize adversarial training and preserve high-frequency structures. Thermal radiation metamaterials for on-demand control of thermal emission: principles, designs, and applications
abstract: Thermal radiation is a fundamental channel for energy transfer and dissipation, playing a critical role in energy technologies, electronic thermal management, and defense-related applications. However, the intrinsically incoherent, broadband, and omnidirectional nature of conventional thermal radiation, typified by blackbody emission, makes it difficult to meet the growing demands of high-performance and actively tunable applications. The emergence of thermal radiation metamaterials has provided a route to overcome this limitation. By incorporating artificially engineered structural elements, thermal radiation metamaterials enable control over the spectrum, direction, and polarization of thermal emission, thereby establishing a new paradigm for on-demand tailoring of thermal emission. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the control mechanisms and micro- and nanostructures of thermal radiation metamaterials, as well as their applications in radiative cooling, thermal camouflage, and thermophotovoltaics. Finally, we identify key challenges, including scalable fabrication, broadband performance and dynamic tunability, environmental durability, and system-level integration, and highlight future opportunities enabled by artificial intelligence, inverse design, and data-driven materials discovery. We aim to provide a coherent framework for understanding, designing, and applying th…

title: Propagation Method Modifies the Response of Pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) cv. Bhagwa to Foliar Nutrition: A Comparison of Air-layered and Tissue-cultured Plants
abstract: Pomegranate orchards are established from both air layers and tissue-cultured plantlets, but whether the two kinds of planting material respond alike to foliar nutrition has seldom been tested in the same orchard. A two-year field experiment was conducted during the mrig bahar seasons of 2018–19 and 2019–20 at Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth, Parbhani, in a Factorial Randomised Block Design combining two propagation methods, air-layered (P₁) and tissue-cultured (P₂), in five-year-old Bhagwa trees with eleven foliar treatments comprising chelated micronutrients, gibberellic acid and the biofertiliser consortium Biomix at two concentrations each, their combinations and an unsprayed control, all applied as three sprays at 45, 90 and 135 days after flowering. Pooled over seasons, air-layered plants were significantly superior for every growth and yield attribute, attaining 241.13 cm plant height at 90 DAF against 198.36 cm, 13.76 branches per plant against 12.46, 15.37 kg yield per plant against 14.66 kg and 11.37 t ha⁻¹ against 10.85 t ha⁻¹. Prediction of Tumor Complete Response Using Genomic and Clinical Data in Solid Cancer Undergoing Definitive Radiation Therapy
abstract: In this retrospective, single-center observational study, targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) was performed on pre-radiation therapy (RT) tumor specimens to identify genomic features associated with RT response and clinical outcomes. This study included 77 eligible patients with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC, n = 23), non-human papilloma virus-related head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC, n = 24), and rectal adenocarcinoma (RAC, n = 30) treated between 2014 and 2020. Treatment was employed for definitive aim (chemoradiotherapy or pre-operative chemoradiotherapy followed by radical surgery). Treatment response was assessed using clinical and pathological criteria and was dichotomized as complete response (CR) versus non-CR. Targeted NGS was performed using a customized panel composing 161 genes. A total of 1263 nonsynonymous somatic variants were identified across 153 genes. The most commonly altered genes were TP53 (70.1%), APC (41.6%), NOTCH1 (41.6%), KMT2C (39.0%), NOTCH3 (36.4%), and NOTCH2 (35.1%). Overall, 25 (32.5%) and 52 patients (67.5%) were classified as CR and non-CR, respectively. APC (P = 0.008), KMT2C (P = 0.018), and KRAS (P = 0.012) alterations were associated with non-CR, whereas CD274 (P = 0.003), MSH3 (P = 0.011), and NOTCH3 (P = 0.048) alterations were associated with CR. title: The impact of plastic hinge properties on the nonlinear response of reinforced concrete (RC) frame structures
abstract: يُعد تحليل الدفع التدريجي اللاخطي (Nonlinear Static Pushover Analysis) من أكثر الأدوات استخدامًا في الهندسة الإنشائية نظرًا لكفاءته الحسابية وفعاليته العملية في تقييم الأداء الزلزالي للمنشآت. وتعتمد موثوقية هذا الأسلوب بشكل كبير على دقة توصيف السلوك اللاخطي للعناصر الإنشائية، والذي تحكمه خصائص المقاومة وقدرات التشوه، إلى جانب الفرضيات المعتمدة في عملية النمذجة. في الممارسات التقليدية، يُجرى تحليل الدفع التدريجي عادةً باستخدام خصائص المفاصل اللدنة الافتراضية المستندة إلى توصيات FEMA-356 و ATC-40. . تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى بحث الفروقات المحتملة في نتائج تحليل الدفع التدريجي الناتجة عن استخدام الخصائص الافتراضية مقارنةً بالخصائص المعرفة من قبل المستخدم للعناصر اللاخطية. ولتحقيق ذلك، تم اعتماد صيغ رياضية مختلفة لتعريف الخصائص اللاخطية للكمرات والأعمدة. كما تم اختيار مبنى خرساني مسلح مكوّن من خمسة طوابق، يمثل نموذجًا للمنشآت المنخفضة إلى متوسطة الارتفاع، ليكون حالة الدراسة. أظهرت النتائج أن معاملات نمذجة المفاصل اللدنة المختارة تؤثر بشكل ملحوظ على القدرة التشوهية للمنشأ. وعلى وجه الخصوص، تبين أن زيادة كمية التسليح العرضي تسهم في تعزيز القدرة التشوهية وتحسين الأداء اللاخطي الكلي للهيكل الإنشائي.

title: Response to letter regarding “barriers and interventions for promoting physical activity and sport among afghan Immigrants in Iran: a qualitative study”
Physically Constrained Temporal Fusion Transformer with LLM-Assisted Hyperparameter Optimization for Multi-Scenario Energy Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of battery state of health (SOH), wind power, and photovoltaic (PV) power is challenged by non-stationarity, multiscale dependencies, and physically implausible outputs. This study proposes a physically constrained Temporal Fusion Transformer (PC-TFT) that coordinates enhanced temporal representation, physical regularization, and LLM-assisted Bayesian optimization. Mogrifier-LSTM and a feature-enhanced attention module capture transient fluctuations and long-range dependencies, while spectral normalization stabilizes training under physical constraints. Scenario-specific differentiable penalties discourage unrealistic battery SOH rebounds, wind-power boundary violations, and inconsistent PV irradiance–power relationships. An LLM incorporates domain knowledge to refine the hyperparameter search space, while numerical optimization determines the final configuration. Experiments on three energy datasets show that, relative to the standard TFT, PC-TFT reduces RMSE by 62.7%, 13.8%, and 15.8% for battery SOH, wind-power, and photovoltaic-power forecasting, respectively, while achieving R2 values above 0.97. These results demonstrate improvements in forecasting accuracy and physical consistency across the evaluated datasets, highlighting the potential of PC-TFT for forecasting-assisted energy management.

title: Patient Characteristics and Outcomes Associated With Home‐Based Cardiac Rehabilitation
abstract: Background Referrals to and participation in cardiac rehabilitation programs remain suboptimal. We examined factors associated with home‐based cardiac rehabilitation (HBCR) referral and participation and associations of referral and participation with outcomes. Methods In this retrospective cohort study, we included adults ≥18 years of age from Kaiser Permanente Southern California with a HBCR‐qualifying event or procedure between January 2021 and September 2024. HBCR referral and, separately, participation was identified within 90 days. Outcomes included 30‐, 180‐, and 365‐day hospitalizations and all‐cause mortality. Results Among 44 468 adults, 13 164 (29.6%) received a referral within 90 days. Those receiving versus not receiving a referral were younger (mean age 65.6 versus 70.6 years) and more often male (71.4% versus 59.5%). Referral was associated with a lower likelihood of 180‐day all‐cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (prevalence ratio [PR], 0.86 [95% CI, 0.82–0.91] and PR, 0.76 [95% CI, 0.66–0.82]), and 365‐day all‐cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (PR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.79–0.86] and PR, 0.70 [95% CI, 0.66–0.75]). Participation was associated with a lower likelihood of 30‐day all‐cause hospitalization (PR, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.66–0.92]), 180‐day all‐cause and cardiovascular disease hospitalization (PR, 0.83 [95% CI, 0.75–0.91] and PR, 0.85 [95% …

title: Does Price Promotion Drive Repurchase Intention? A Study of Live Shopping E-Commerce
abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of price promotion on repurchase intention in the context of live shopping e-commerce through the mediating role of perceived value, and to examine the role of post-purchase regret as a moderating variable in this relationship. Employing a quantitative approach, data were collected from 205 respondents selected through purposive sampling via questionnaires. The data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS 4. The research adopts the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework to explain how price promotion (stimulus) influences consumers’ internal evaluations via perceived value (organism), ultimately resulting in repurchase intention (response). Additionally, Cognitive Dissonance Theory is applied to explain the psychological discomfort consumers experience due to post-purchase regret. The results demonstrate that perceived value has a dominant effect on repurchase intention; however, post-purchase regret does not moderate the relationship between price promotion and repurchase intention. These findings indicate that the degree of post-purchase regret experienced by consumers does not significantly alter the impact of price promotion on repurchase decisions.

title: The Lessons from 1970s Price Controls
abstract: Abstract There has been a recent revival of interest in both voluntary and mandatory controls of prices to reduce the impact of inflation on low‐income groups. This article reviews the use of voluntary schemes of price restraint by the 1974–9 Labour government, in particular the ‘red triangle’ scheme in operation between February and August 1976. This was facilitated by more coherent representation of the retail sector. However, low‐income groups may be better served by income support than price restraint.

title: What Really Drives Coffee Shop Choices? The Roles of Price, Facility Quality, and Service Excellence in Tasikmalaya
abstract: This research investigates the effect of facility quality, price, and service quality and their effects on customers’ decision to buy coffee for consumption in coffee shop in Tasikmalaya. It further explores whether service quality moderates the influence of facility quality and price on purchasing decisions. The analysis uses a quantitative method using PLS-SEM modelling and is based on a dataset from 117 coffee shop customers in Tasikmalaya. The findings indicate that both price and characteristics of facilities have a positive and significant impact on customers' intention to buy coffee, with facility quality exerting the strongest influence. But when we look to see if the quality of service moderates how important price and facility quality are in consumers’ decision making, the results do not support that notion. These results suggest that customers evaluate price and facility quality independently, with facility experience being the most influential factor. Additionally, service quality does not significantly affect the relationship among price, facility quality, and purchasing decision are connected.

title: Rice Price Dynamics during the 1945--1947 Famine in Post-War Taiwan: A Quantitative Reassessment
abstract: We compiled the first high-frequency rice price panel for Taiwan from August 1945 to March 1947, during the transition from Japanese rule to China rule. Using regression models, we found that the pattern of rice price changes could be divided into four stages, each with distinct characteristics. Based on different stages, we combined the policies formulated by the Taiwan government at the time to demonstrate the correlation between rice prices and policies. The research results highlight the dominant role of policy systems in post-war food crises.

Revenue Optimization in Higher Education under Price Dependent Demand: A Scholarship Allocation and Tuition Pricing Model
abstract: Higher education institutions operate in increasingly competitive environments where student demand and institutional revenue are strongly influenced by scholarship policies and tuition fees. Under price-dependent demand, this study proposes an optimization framework for revenue management in colleges based on the optimal allocation of scholarship categories across multiple academic programs. Demand is modeled using piecewise-linear demand functions derived from observed price–demand data. The resulting model integrates capacity constraints, institutional scholarship policies, and demand elasticity within a mixed-integer optimization framework. Computational experiments using data from multiple academic programs demonstrate how tuition levels and scholarship allocation interact with demand elasticity to determine optimal enrollment and revenue outcomes. The proposed framework provides decision support for college administrators seeking to balance financial sustainability with student access objectives.

title: Forecasting compound sea level extremes: the 29–30 October 2018 Adriatic storm surge and meteotsunami extreme
abstract: Abstract On 29–30 October 2018, an extreme sea level occurred in the Adriatic Sea, driven by a combination of long-period (storm surge) and short-period (meteotsunami) oscillations. Storm surges were strongest in the northern Adriatic, while shorter-period oscillations dominated in the middle Adriatic, where a meteotsunami was observed and recorded in Vela Luka Bay (Korčula Island). This type of extreme sea level event, arising from the combination of a storm surge and a meteotsunami, is termed a compound extreme and poses both a major threat and a forecasting challenge. Using this event as a case study, we evaluated two different approaches to forecasting compound sea level extremes. The first approach relies solely on numerical modelling: sea level response was modelled using the Semi-implicit Cross-scale Hydroscience Integrated System Model (SCHISM), forced by outputs from the Weather Research and Forecasting atmospheric numerical model (WRF). This approach reproduced the storm surge but failed to reproduce the shorter-period oscillations, including the observed meteotsunami. The second, hybrid, approach combines the first approach for modelling the storm surge component with the shorter-period sea level oscillations obtained from SCHISM forced by the high-frequency component of measured air pressure time series. As the meteotsunami was strongest in Vela Luka, the second app…

Predicting Indie Game Success: A Diverse Stacking Ensemble Approach for Consumer Demand Forecasting
abstract: As consumer expectations escalate across the video game market, accurately understanding player preferences is crucial for maximizing profitability and long-term retention. This is particularly challenging for independent (indie) developers who lack the resources of AAA studios. However, forecasting game ownership using the vast, heavy-tailed data from digital distribution platforms remains a significant hurdle. To address this gap, we propose a specialized, robust machine learning framework exclusively tailored for the indie market segment. Our approach utilizes a Diverse Stacking Regressor ensemble—integrating Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost algorithms alongside a Huber meta-learner—to predict game ownership based on comprehensive SteamSpy data. Compared to standalone baselines, such as a traditional Random Forest which achieved an $R^2$ score of 0.69 and a Median Absolute Error (MedAE) of nearly 100,000, our stacking approach demonstrates superior accuracy. It yields an $R^2$ score of 0.72, lowers the Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) to approximately 20\%, and reduces the MedAE from approximately 100,000 to under 5,500. Ultimately, this predictive framework empowers indie developers to systematically interpret large-scale consumer data, facilitating optimized resource allocation and data-driven game design.

Lipoprotein(a) and Coronary Artery Disease Polygenic Risk Scores Do Not Improve Secondary Manifestations of Arterial Disease Score Prediction of Coronary Events After Ischemic Stroke
abstract: Background Survivors of ischemic stroke are at high risk for coronary artery disease (CAD), but individual risk varies. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and CAD polygenic risk scores (CAD‐PRS) improve risk prediction in primary prevention; however, their prognostic value after stroke remains uncertain. We assessed whether Lp(a) and CAD‐PRS add predictive value to the Secondary Manifestations of Arterial Disease (SMART) secondary prevention score. Methods We analyzed 1202 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry with prior ischemic stroke and no CAD at baseline (2006–2022). Baseline clinical characteristics, Lp(a), and CAD‐PRS were recorded. The primary outcome was incident CAD, identified from hospital, primary care, and death records. Competing‐risk models compared SMART alone with SMART plus Lp(a), CAD‐PRS, or both. Ten‐year model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve and Brier score. Prespecified subgroup analyses examined age, sex, diabetes, and low‐density lipoprotein cholesterol. Results During a median follow‐up of 13.4 years, 155 participants (12.9%) developed CAD. SMART alone provided moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.69 [95% CI, 0.64–0.75]) and a Brier score of 0.08. Adding Lp(a), CAD‐PRS, or both did not improve prediction (change in area under the receiver operating charac…

Building-Held-Out Validation of Thermal-Sensation Prediction: Implications for Building Design and Operation Across 554 Buildings
abstract: Machine-learning models used to inform building thermal-environment design and operation are often assessed by random record splits, whereas application in a new building needs an unseen-building test. We analyzed 49,231 thermal-sensation records from 554 buildings in the ASHRAE Global Thermal Comfort Database II. With fixed configurations, record-wise five-fold validation favored extremely randomized trees (ET; record-weighted mean absolute error [MAE] 0.806), while building-held-out validation favored histogram gradient boosting (HGB; 0.883 versus ET 0.902). For HGB, building-held-out MAE exceeded record-wise MAE by 0.061 sensation units (95% building-cluster bootstrap interval 0.044–0.081). In a separate nested four-candidate-per-model sensitivity analysis, building-held-out ET and HGB MAE were 0.889 and 0.885; their paired difference was 0.004 (95% interval −0.003–0.011), and their building-macro MAEs were likewise close. PMV had MAE 1.044 on 33,791 matched records, compared with 0.899 for HGB retrained solely on PMV-available training records; availability and study-source concentration limit generalization. An exploratory same-building offset sensitivity found that 1–5 calibration labels worsened error; 20 labels offered only a modest mean benefit across eligible buildings, with a majority of buildings worsening. The findings support matching validation units and evidence…

title: Experimentally Anchored, MHC-Agnostic Prediction of Immunogenicity and Cytokine Release
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate prediction of anti-drug antibody (ADA) responses remains a challenge in biologics development, as current tools primarily rely on major histocompatibility complex (MHC) binding affinity, which does not capture the full complexity of immune activation. Methods We developed EPITOP™, a protein language model trained on epitopes experimentally verified via cytokine release assays, enabling direct immunogenicity prediction. This was combined with IMMUNOTOP™, which aggregates EPITOP™ outputs into protein-level scores. Results EPITOP™ achieved an AUC of 0.73 on the independent test set, demonstrating performance comparable to existing methods while providing biologically grounded and interpretable outputs for immunogenicity risk assessment. It also enables identification of immunogenic hotspots. Conclusions Beyond hotspot identification, the model can serve as a surrogate for peptide-level IFNγ-associated immunogenicity when experimental measurement is impractical and may be useful for modalities in which experimental cytokine testing is difficult, although systemic cytokine release depends on additional biological factors not modeled here.

title: Lightweight Cross-Condition Tool Wear Prediction via Transfer Learning for Resource-Constrained Edge Manufacturing
abstract: In resource-constrained manufacturing environments, accurate prediction of tool wear under variable cutting conditions remains challenging due to the trade-off between computational overhead and prognostic reliability. Conventional signal processing and deep learning methods suffer from high model complexity, cross-domain distribution discrepancies, and excessive computation cost, limiting their practical deployment on edge devices. This paper proposes an optimized cloud–edge collaborative transfer learning framework for lightweight remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of milling tools. On the cloud side, a low-complexity stacked auto-encoder built on a 1D-SqueezeNet is trained with cross-domain adaptation constraints to improve generalization across working conditions. Pretrained model parameters are then transferred to edge hardware for deep feature extraction. A kernel extreme learning machine (KELM) is further adopted for fast on-site tool wear regression prediction. When validated on full-lifecycle milling vibration data collected under real machining conditions, the proposed approach achieves nearly identical prediction performance on edge devices compared with cloud-side inference while also reducing edge inference latency to 0.01–0.021 s. These results demonstrate that the presented framework can deliver accurate prediction of milling tool RUL and provide rapid respon…

title: Optimal Trajectory Prediction System for Automated Driving using Deep Learning
abstract: Research in the field of autonomous driving has revealed that one of the main focuses is on predicting the future trajectories of vehicles. These accurate forecasts enable safe navigation and efficient route planning. A hybrid Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) framework integrated with the Robot Operating System (ROS) is presented in this work. The aim of the framework is to estimate future vehicle trajectories in real time. The network was trained using vehicle motion data from the Argoverse Motion Forecasting dataset. CNN layers extract local temporal and kinematic patterns from input sequences, and LSTM layers model their temporal evolution. Once trained, the model is incorporated into an ROS-based pipeline where nodes dedicated to processing incoming trajectory information publish predicted paths for real-time visualisation in RViz. Performance of the model was evaluated using Mean Squared Error (MSE), Average Displacement Error (ADE) and Final Displacement Error (FDE), and was then compared to that of classical motion prediction methods. Research results are promising, as they enable the computational efficiency required for real-time operation alongside predictive accuracy. Additionally, robotic middleware, deep learning and a publicly available benchmark dataset were combined to develop a reproducible experimental framework that will facili…

The Relationship Between Vital Lung Capacity and Leg Muscle Power on VO₂Max in Trail Running Athletes
abstract: Trail running has physiological characteristics that differ from conventional running due to variations in elevation and unstable terrain. This study aimed to analyze the relationships between vital lung capacity, leg muscle power, and VO₂max in trail running athletes. A cross-sectional correlational design was used with 60 trail running athletes from clubs in Bandung, selected through purposive sampling. Vital lung capacity was measured using a spirometer, leg muscle power using the vertical jump test, and VO₂max using the 15-minute Balke test. Data were analyzed using Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression. Vital lung capacity showed a very strong positive relationship with VO₂max (r = 0.904; p < 0.001), while leg muscle power showed a strong positive relationship with VO₂max (r = 0.801; p < 0.001). Both variables were simultaneously and significantly associated with VO₂max (F(2,57) = 142.019; p < 0.001; R² = 0.833). These findings indicate an association between respiratory capacity, lower-limb neuromuscular capacity, and aerobic capacity in trail running athletes. The cross-sectional design limits the interpretation of the findings to associations between variables and does not establish causal relationships.

Building capacity for short food supply chains through food processing workshops: Experience from the Horizon Europe RURBANIVE project
abstract: Background Short food supply chains (SFSCs) are increasingly recognised as a means of improving the sustainability, resilience and economic viability of local food systems. However, many farmers and small-scale food producers lack the technological knowledge required to develop value-added products for direct sale. The Horizon Europe RURBANIVE project addresses these challenges through knowledge exchange, capacity building and innovation. Within this framework, practical food processing workshops were designed as multi-actor learning activities promoting collaboration between academia, farmers, food producers and public authorities and building their capacities. This study evaluated participants’ perceptions of the workshops and the potential contribution of those practical courses and digital learning platform for shortening the food supply chains. Methods Between 2025 and 2026, eight practical workshops on dairy, bakery, meat and brewing technologies were organised at the Czech University of Life Sciences Prague. The workshops combined theoretical lectures with hands-on demonstrations on pilot-scale processing lines. Overall, 122stakeholders participated, but only 92 (75.4%) of them completed an anonymous post-workshop questionnaire evaluating nine aspects of the educational activities. title: Rate‐Dependent Capacity Evolution and Time‐Controlled Degradation of MnO 2 Cathodes in Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
abstract: The excellent cycling stability of MnO 2 cathodes in aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs) at high current densities often deteriorates at lower current densities, yet the origin of this rate‐dependent behavior remains unclear. Here, we uncover the interplay between current density and cumulative cycling time by tracking the electrochemical and structural evolution of α ‐MnO 2 cathodes in Mn 2+ ‐containing electrolytes. Low current densities promote more extensive Mn 2+ ‐mediated dissolution–deposition, leading to greater accumulation of a porous, metastable Zn–Mn–O intermediate and pronounced capacity enhancement. Notably, while the magnitude of the capacity enhancement strongly depends on current density, the capacity maximum occurs within a relatively narrow cumulative cycling time of ~350–450 h across the tested current densities in 2 M ZnSO 4 + 0.2 M MnSO 4 electrolyte. Upon prolonged cycling, the metastable Zn–Mn–O intermediate gradually diminishes, accompanied by the emergence of crystalline ZnMn 2 O 4 , increased electrode polarization, and rapid capacity fading. These findings reveal that current density affects the extent of capacity enhancement, whereas cumulative cycling time provides a more consistent measure of the subsequent capacity evolution than cycle number. This time‐domain understanding explains the contrasting cycling behavior of MnO 2 cathodes at different c…

title: Confined Phase Transition Infiltration Coupled With In Situ Pore Sealing: Constructing Hard Carbon Rich in Closed Pore for Plateau‐Capacity‐Dominated Sodium Storage
abstract: Biomass‐derived hard carbon (HC) is a promising candidate for anode materials in sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, abundant open pores generated during activation process often lead to severe proliferation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) and irreversible Na + consumption, severely compromising the initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) and low‐voltage plateau capacity. This work proposes a synergistic strategy of confined phase transition infiltration and in situ pore sealing, using waste green tea as a precursor to construct a HC anode dominated by plateau capacity. Low dose of ZnCl 2 induces controllable hydrolysis and aromatization of cellulose and generate nanoscale open pores. These pores act as confined microreactors, inducing an in situ chemical vapor deposition like carbon growth that effectively “stitching” the open voids into solvent sieving closed pores. Consequently, it delivers a remarkable ICE of 79.1%, a high reversible capacity of 342.3 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 , and robust cycling stability (86.2% retention after 1000 cycles at 1.0 A g −1 ). In‐/ex situ analysis reveals that its reversible sodium storage mechanism encompasses a triple synergy of defect adsorption, interlayer intercalation, and closed pore filling with quasi metallic sodium clusters. The confined pore sealing engineering strategy provides a robust paradigm for designing high‐performance …

title: Investigating Electro-Thermal Distribution in High-Capacity Large-Format Blade Batteries for Energy Storage
abstract: Batteries are regarded as a uniform heat source in traditional thermal management system design. Inconsistencies in electrochemical reactions across time and space are often ignored, which leads to an unreasonable battery thermal management system. This paper establishes a 2D electro-thermal fully coupled model based on the Kim model and NTGK model for a high-capacity blade battery. Based on the experimental results, the accuracy of the model was verified by examining terminal voltage, average battery temperature, and temperature distribution. The distribution characteristics of physical fields within the battery were analyzed using the electro-thermal model. The results indicated that the distribution of electrochemical reaction rates inside the battery shows a clear boundary between the near-tab area and the middle positions. In the initial stage of discharge, the electrochemical reaction rates were higher around the tabs. However, the electrochemical reaction rates were higher around the middle positions at the end stage of discharge. Thus, we proposed two schemes, a three-zone model and a five-zone model for 3D thermal analysis, according to the distribution characteristics of the physical fields. We found that the difference in the prediction accuracy of temperature distribution between the two schemes was small. Therefore, we recommended the three-zone scheme for 3D therm…

Reactive molecular dynamic simulation of water induced iron corrosion and its prevention mechanism
abstract: Corrosion of iron and mild steel in water and in chloride media is a costly problem for industry, and it also raises safety concerns. Organic molecules containing heteroatoms are commonly used to control it. In most of the reported work, though, the electronic structure of the inhibitor molecule and the breakdown of the metal-water interface have been treated as two separate problems. It is therefore still not clear how a simple electronic descriptor is related to the film that actually builds up on a corroding iron surface. Keeping this in view, our study evaluates the iron corrosion inhibition performance of five aromatic compounds, anthracene, anthrone, xanthene, xanthone, and xanthione, using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and reactive molecular dynamics simulations. Simulations revealed the real-time evolution of iron corrosion in aqueous media, showing the formation of iron oxide and hydroxide at the metal surface. Among all inhibitors, xanthione showed the most stable adsorption on the iron surface, driven by van der Waals and electrostatic interactions sustained by electron donation from sulfur and oxygen heteroatoms. This xanthione-surface interaction appears to form a stable interfacial barrier, which should suppress corrosion. Among the five molecules, xanthione has the smallest gap of 3.18 eV between the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) and th…

abstract: Abstract The refinement and uniformity of dendrite microstructures in single-crystal (SC) superalloys directly determine their high-temperature mechanical properties and service reliability. In conventional directional solidification (DS) processes, the macroscopic temperature and solute fields ahead of the solid−liquid (SL) interface are inherently spatially non-uniform, resulting in pronounced variations in primary dendrite arm spacing (PDAS) at different locations. This poses a significant challenge to achieving effective control over the overall uniformity of the solidification microstructure. In this study, leveraging the unique configuration of the Cusp magnetic field (CMF), we investigated its influence on dendritic growth behavior in directionally solidified SC superalloy specimens with different diameters. The results demonstrate that the CMF reduces the PDAS and improves its spatial distribution uniformity. Moreover, both effects are enhanced with increasing specimen diameter. Quenching experiments combined with macroscale multiphysics simulations reveal that thermoelectric magnetic convection induced by the CMF effectively compensates for the non-uniform thermal field from radiative heat transfer, thereby driving the macroscopic interface toward a planar morphology. Phase-field simulations further indicate that, the differences in dendrite tip migration kinetics at d…

Antisense Oligonucleotides that Are Toxic to Prion-Infected Mice Share an Emergent Mechanism
abstract: Some, but not all, gapmer antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) delivered into cerebrospinal fluid exhibit fatal subacute toxicity in late-stage prion-infected mice but not in uninfected mice. Here, we performed a battery of in vivo studies demonstrating that the toxicity is compound- and disease- stage-dependent, and not predicted by behavioral or molecular measurements in uninfected animals. A panel of toxic ASOs all elicited a consistent transcriptomic response signature in prion-infected mice, which emerged over the course of 7 days post dose. This signature, driven chiefly by decreased expression of a specific set of astrocyte-expressed genes, was absent in uninfected mice receiving the same ASOs, was absent, less intense, and/or more transient in infected mice receiving tolerated ASOs, and was distinct from the transcriptomic effect of prion disease itself. Our data argue that the toxicity is an interaction between ASO and prion disease at high doses for specific compounds, and does not represent an exacerbation of ASO toxicity nor of prion disease.

title: Curcumin Enhances the Sensitivity of 5-fluorouracil-resistant Colon Cancer Cells to 5-fluorouracil Through a Ferroptosis-related Mechanism: A Network Pharmacology and In Vitro Study
abstract: Background Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a common and deadly malignancy. Although 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) continues to be a standard therapeutic agent for CRC, the development of resistance substantially compromises its clinical effectiveness. Curcumin, a natural polyphenol, has shown potential in reversing chemoresistance, possibly through ferroptosis-related mechanisms. Purpose The present work explored the potential of curcumin to restore responsiveness to 5-FU in resistant CRC cells and examined the possible involvement of ferroptosis through a combined bioinformatics and experimental strategy. Materials and Methods Curcumin-related targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction, Super-PRED, and Herbal Ingredients’ Targets (HIT). Protein–protein interaction (PPI) networks, Gene Ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, as well as ferroptosis-related target screening, were performed using Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING), Metascape, and FerrDb. Genes associated with CRC and 5-FU resistance were retrieved from GeneCards and Genomics of Drug Sensitivity in Cancer (GDSC) databases, and intersecting candidates were subsequently mapped using Cytoscape software. In vitro experiments were conducted in HCT8/5-FU cells. Cellular proliferation and viability were evaluated with the Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-…

The 28 April 2025 blackout in the Spanish interconnected power system from a converter-technology perspective and the need for grid reinforcement
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of inverter-based renewable generation is changing the stability constraints of modern power systems. The Iberian blackout of 28 April 2025 provides a critical case for examining this transition. This study links converter behaviour, published laboratory experiments, reported event ordering and engineering reinforcement options. Public system-level records are consistent with voltage-led propagation: voltage excursions and generation disconnections preceded the steepest frequency decline under low demand, high photovoltaic output and reduced synchronous support. This interpretation does not constitute a full dynamic reconstruction or identify every initial trip cause. Spain continued renewable deployment: year-end installed power capacity reached approximately 142.6 GW, including storage but excluding self-consumption facilities, and renewables supplied 55.5% of generation excluding estimated self-consumption. The engineering assessment distinguishes static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs), extended STATCOMs with energy storage (E-STATCOMs) and high-voltage direct-current (HVDC) links. The Mehrum Nord E-STATCOM illustrates transmission-scale integration of dynamic reactive-power support, short-duration active-power exchange and grid-forming control. Manufacturer-reported capabilities include ±300 Mvar and a 200 MW supercapacitor unit; these ratings …

title: Experimental Investigation of Tungsten Carbide Tool Erosion During Electrochemical Discharge Machining of Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer Composite
Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
abstract: ABSTRACT All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

title: Unraveling the Mystery of Near-Infrared Emission in an Antimony Halide Dimer Driven by the Jahn–Teller Effect
abstract: Abstract Most zero-dimensional hybrid metal halides enable emission in the first near-infrared (NIR-I) region (650–950 nm), and the shorter wavelengths result in poor photon penetration depth. Here, we report the observation of an NIR-II emission signal (band gap = 1.13 eV) from a (BTBAC)2Sb2Cl8 single crystal at room temperature. Although a variety of mechanisms are involved in the explanation of such a broad band with a large Stokes shift, the exploration of the structural origin of the NIR optical activity remains challenging due to misconceptions about excitons and experimental limitations. A strategy that spatially confines 5s2 ions within edge-shared [Sb2Cl8]2– units with controlled lattice distortion is proposed to cause a Jahn–Teller effect (JTE) during the interconfiguration transition (3P1 → 1S0). A family of hybrid metal halides doped with Bi3+,In3+ or Bi3+/In3+ demonstrates that the fine interplay between the Jahn–Teller effect and spin–orbit coupling (SOC) takes into full consideration orbital degeneracy and electron flipping, thus boosting the photoluminescence quantum yield to 12%. TD-DFT calculations visualize the symmetry of the two lattices within a dimeric structure varying with specific modes, and the rational assignment of the energy gap (ground state: 3.69 eV; excited state: 1.22 eV) between 1S0 and 3P1 is highly consistent with the experimental findings (…

title: Bifunctional MXene-Pd multilayer electrodes enabling coupled electrochemical reforming and hydrogen evolution
abstract: Abstract Conventional water splitting requires high overpotentials, whereas electrochemical reforming offers a sustainable route to produce hydrogen while oxidizing alcohols. In this work, we report the rational design of structurally ordered multilayer thin-film electrodes via electrostatic layer-by-layer (LbL) assembly, employing palladium nanoparticles (Pd NPs) as active electrocatalytic sites for both methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), and MXene as a multifunctional conductive support. The sequential assembly of negatively charged MXene nanosheets and positively charged Pd NPs produced well-defined (MXene/Pd) multilayers, which delivered a high MOR current density of 9.38 mA cm − 2 . This performance significantly surpasses that of other Pd-based multilayer electrodes, primarily due to the role of MXene in preventing NPs agglomeration, providing superior electrical conductivity, and, in the case of HER, contributing its own intrinsic hydrogen adsorption-desorption activity, which synergistically enhances the overall catalytic performance together with Pd. Furthermore, in two-electrode full-cell configurations, peak voltages of 0.9 V with a Pt cathode and 0.65 V with a (MXene/Pd) cathode were achieved, both below the theoretical water-splitting voltage of 1.23 V. The cooperative integration of Pd and MXene thus maximizes both methanol ox…

title: Mortise‐and‐Tenon Molecular Joint Covalent Organic Frameworks With Tunable Topology for Photothermal‐Catalytic Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT The controllable regulation of dimensionality and interpenetration in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is crucial for optimizing photocatalytic performance, yet the translation of 3D COFs from structural construction to functional customization remains challenging. Here, we successfully designed a series of mortise‐and‐tenon molecular joint COFs by rationally engineering a twisted tetraphthaldehyde ligand bearing π‐conjugated “clips”. Stepwise extension of the “clips” enables topological evolution from 2D to twofold interpenetrated 3D, and ultimately to noninterpenetrated 3D structure. Notably, DHP‐CuPor‐COF with noninterpenetrated 3D structure amplifies light‐harvesting efficiency and substrate accessibility, enabling superior photothermal conversion and catalytic performance over its 2D and twofold interpenetrated 3D counterparts. To the best of our knowledge, it delivers highly efficient photothermal‐catalytic C─X (X = O, S) bond formation for selective transformation of phenolic compounds via cross‐dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reactions (conv., >90% and yield, >80%), markedly outperforming conventional thermal catalysis. The high efficiency arises from the synergistic of open 3D channels, abundant Cu‐porphyrin active sites and strong photothermal effect. This work provides an innovative strategy to tune the topological chemistry of COFs for advanced photocataly…

Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor based Voltage Differencing Inverting Buffered Amplifier with Enhanced Analog Performance
abstract: This article describes how to develop and operate a Voltage Differencing Inverting Buffered Amplifier (CNTFET-VDIBA) using Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistors (CNTFETs). It utilizes the superior characteristics of CNTFETs to facilitate enhanced transconductance, a wideband range of operation, and a low power demand compared to conventional CMOS alternatives. The effect of increasing numbers of CNTs on device performance was thoroughly studied and characterized. Simulation results specify that by increasing the number of CNTs significantly improves transconductance. The proposed VDIBA, CNT has the highest transconductance of around 1.32mS, while maintaining the high BW. The 3-db BW was observed to be 7.9 GHz, enabling this proposed VDIBA to apply for high-frequency analog signals. These results demonstrate that CNTFET-based VDIBA is a feasible substitute to CMOS, providing ultra-low power consumption, scalability, and high-performance analog building blocks for future integrated circuits.

title: Solar-Driven CO2 Methanation at Industrial Interfaces: Technology Readiness, Process Integration, and Techno-Economics
abstract: Solar-driven CO2 methanation is being investigated as a pathway for carbon utilization and renewable-energy storage, yet deployment at industrial point sources, including ammonia–urea complexes, remains constrained by heterogeneous reporting, uncertain feedstock availability, heat-management requirements, and boundary-dependent process economics. This structured critical narrative review evaluates thermocatalytic Power-to-Methane, H2-fed photothermal and light-assisted methanation, and direct photocatalytic CO2-to-CH4 conversion across catalyst, reactor, and plant scales. A domain-specific evidence-grading framework is applied to distinguish comparatively well-supported mechanistic conclusions from studies with incomplete local thermometry, matched-temperature dark controls, photon-flux calibration, isotope tracing, or material and charge balances. The review further examines the stoichiometric and operational constraints governing residual process-CO2 availability at ammonia–urea sites and assesses how renewable-H2 supply, buffer storage, gas conditioning, heat recovery, and product specifications affect process integration. An illustrative industrial screening case for a 2000 t d−1 NH3/2000 t d−1 urea complex yields a nominal residual of 472.4 t d−1 CO2 before operational deductions, corresponding to 86.5 t d−1 H2 demand and an approximately 198 MW electrolyzer load at 55 kWh…

title: Extremal Hysteretic Energy Dissipation in a Dry-Friction Vibration Isolator with a Longitudinally Slit Cylindrical Shell and Deformable Filler
abstract: Vibration isolators based on a slit cylindrical shell with an elastic filler are proposed for the needs of the mining, oil and gas, and construction industries; in these devices, energy dissipation is provided by the effects of distributed positional dry friction between the contacting elements. Such vibration isolators are intended to operate under considerable loads and severe dimensional constraints, which requires a combination of high load-bearing capacity, sufficient compliance, and efficient energy dissipation. The aim of this work is an analytical study of hysteretic energy dissipation in the nonconservative contact system “slit cylindrical shell–deformable filler” with dry friction at the contact interface, and the determination of the conditions of maximum energy dissipation. A quasi-static model is developed in which the bending compliance of the slit shell is reproduced by an energetically equivalent orthotropic shell, while the filler is assumed to be elastic and incompressible. An analytical description of the hysteresis loop and an explicit expression for the energy dissipated per cycle are obtained. A nonmonotonic influence of the friction coefficient on energy dissipation is established: as friction increases, the dissipation first grows, reaches a maximum, and then decreases. The extremum is caused by the competition between the growth of the work of the frict…

title: The effect of Red Bull energy drink on strength, power, and jump performance in female volleyball players: A randomized cross-over trial
abstract: Background Red Bull (RB) is widely consumed by athletes in an effort to enhance performance through its stimulant content, primarily caffeine and taurine. Although its potential ergogenic effects have been studied, evidence regarding the impact of commercially available servings of RB on short-term anaerobic performance remains inconsistent. Aim This study examined whether acute ingestion of a standard commercially available serving of RB influences anaerobic power, handgrip strength, and jumping ability in female sub-elite volleyball players. Methods Fifteen female sub-elite volleyball players (mean age 21.3 ± 2.4 years) participated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study. Each athlete completed three physical tests (Wingate anaerobic test, jump test, and handgrip strength test) on two occasions, separated by 1 week, after consuming either RB or a placebo designed to mimic its taste and appearance. Participants ingested 250.7 ± 28.2 mL of RB, providing 80.3 ± 9.0 mg of caffeine (1.143 mg·kg −1 ). Performance testing began 33 min after ingestion. Performance outcomes were compared between conditions using paired t-tests. Summary None of the 13 measured performance variables showed statistically significant differences (p > 0.05) between RB and placebo trials. Eight participants reported mild nausea following RB consumption. Under the conditions of thi…

title: An Integrative Model Based on Artificial Intelligence for Enhancing Integration among Sciences in Interdisciplinary Learning and Scientific Research: A Field Study on Postgraduate Students at the Libyan Academy – Janzour
abstract: The recent rapid advancement in artificial intelligence technologies has brought about a fundamental transformation in higher education and scientific research institutions by providing new opportunities to enhance interdisciplinary learning and cognitive integration across various scientific fields. This study aimed to propose an integrative model based on artificial intelligence to analyze the impact of using AI tools in enhancing interdisciplinary learning and scientific research among postgraduate students at the Libyan Academy–Janzour. The study adopted the descriptive-analytical approach, and data were collected from a sample of (94) master's and doctoral students using a questionnaire specifically designed for this purpose. The reliability test results indicated that the study instrument possessed a high degree of reliability, with a Cronbach's alpha coefficient of (0.912). The results of the descriptive analysis indicated that the sample members possessed a high level of digital competence, with a mean score of (3.92) and a standard deviation of (0.64). The findings also revealed a high impact of using artificial intelligence tools on improving the quality of scientific research and research productivity, with a mean score of (4.15) and a standard deviation of (0.58), in addition to a positive role in enhancing interdisciplinary integration, with a mean score of (3.88) …

In Situ and Operando Techniques for Electrocatalysis in Renewable Energy Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalysis is essential for renewable energy conversion, yet the mechanisms governing catalytic performance remain poorly understood due to the complex nature of electrochemical interfaces. Advances in nanomaterial synthesis and high‐resolution characterization now allow detailed structural and compositional analysis, but static methods fall short of capturing the dynamic behaviors of active sites during operation. In this review, we focus on the growing role of in situ and operando techniques such as optical, X‐ray, and electron‐based, in resolving catalytic structure and reactivity under real‐life working conditions. These methods offer unparalleled access to the evolution of surface species, reaction intermediates, and interfacial topologies that govern catalytic functions. We highlight how in situ and operando studies have revealed transient phenomena and mechanistic details previously inaccessible, and discuss their critical roles in advancing systems for water splitting, CO 2 /N 2 reduction, and fuel cells related renewable energy applications. Beyond highlighting the real‐time transformations captured by operando and in situ methods, this review underscores how coupling operando datasets with theoretical modeling and machine learning can accelerate mechanistic discovery and enable rational catalyst design. By extracting hidden correlations and guiding clos…

title: Cross sections of the 20 Ne( n , α ) 17 O reaction in the 8.9 –11.5 MeV neutron energy region
abstract: Abstract State-resolved cross sections for the 20 Ne( n , α i ) 17 O ( i =0,1,2,3) reactions were measured in the 8.9 –11.5 MeV neutron energy region (11 energy points) at the HI-13 tandem accelerator of the China Institute of Atomic Energy (CIAE). The present measurements extend the data of the α 0 , α 1 , α 2 , and α 3 channels from 9.6 MeV to 11.5 MeV, where previous measurements reported only the summed ( α 0 + α 1 ) cross sections. A twin gridded ionization chamber (GIC) filled with a neon-based gas mixture was used as the charged-particle detection, with the neon gas serving as an active sample. Corrections for detector efficiency, background interference, and neutron-field non-uniformity were performed by combining experimental measurements and detailed Monte Carlo simulations. From 9.6 to 11.5 MeV, the measured 20 Ne( n , α 0 ) 17 O and 20 Ne( n , α 1 ) 17 O cross sections decrease as neutron energy increases, and are generally consistent with those in JENDL-5. The 20 Ne( n , α 2 ) 17 O cross sections are generally above those in JENDL-5, whereas the 20 Ne( n , α 3 ) 17 O cross sections are below those in JENDL-5. In detail, the measured excitation functions exhibit noticeable fluctuations that are not included in JENDL-5. The TALYS-2.2 calculations can describe the measured α 0 , α 1 and α 2 cross sections reasonably, whereas the calculated α 3 cross sections are gener…

ASSESSMENT OF INCREMENTAL HOUSING DEVELOPMENT AS A STRATEGY FOR AFFORDABLE HOUSING DELIVERY IN ABUJA
abstract: The persistent challenge of housing affordability in Abuja has increased the need for alternative housing delivery approaches that enable households to develop housing in line with their financial capacity. Hence, this study assessed incremental housing as an affordable housing solution in Abuja, focusing on its features, influencing factors, associated challenges and effect on housing affordability. A quantitative research design was adopted, with data obtained from 164 Real Estate Developers through a structured questionnaire. Weighted Mean Score, Factor analysis and correlation analysis was used to analyses the retrieved data. The findings indicate that staged construction, progressive expansion and owner-driven development constitute prominent features of incremental housing. The assessment of affordability showed that incremental housing enables households to distribute construction costs over time, although affordability varies across income groups. In addition, four (4) major factors influencing incremental housing development were identified, namely: financial/economic, land/institutional, construction/technical and social/household factors. The research further identified major challenges to include high costs of building-materials land costs, limited access to affordable finance, infrastructure costs and high lending rates. Furthermore, the study also established a st…

title: Sanayi Devrimi Döneminde Mekân Malzemesinin Kuramsal İnşası
abstract: Mekân tasarımında malzeme, tasarımı somut gerçekliğe taşıyan temel bir değerdir. Malzemeye dair kuramsal yaklaşımlar, mekân tasarımında malzemenin ele alınış biçimlerini etkilemiştir. Malzemenin kuramsal tarihine bakıldığında, Sanayi Devrimi dönemi yaklaşımları, belirleyici bir dönüm noktasını işaret etmektedir. Ancak malzemeye dair bu dönemde ortaya koyulan kuramsal yaklaşımların literatürde tanımlanmadığı gözlemlenmektedir. Bu çalışma, Sanayi Devrimi sürecindeki tasarım malzemesi kuramsal yaklaşımlarını inceleyerek, yaklaşımları ortaya koymayı ve tanımlamayı amaçlamaktadır. Bu amaç doğrultusunda araştırma, tasarım malzemesine dair kuramsal çerçevenin oluşumunda etkili olan ve sonraki dönemlere etki eden John Ruskin, Eugène Viollet Le Duc ve Gottfried Semper’in malzemeye dair değerlendirmelerini kapsam dahilinde ele alacaktır. Tarihsel araştırma yöntemi çerçevesinde yürütülen analizde, Sanayi Devrimi dönemi öncesi malzemeye dair kuramsal yaklaşımların genel odak noktası ortaya çıkartılacaktır. Sonraki bölümde Sanayi Devrimi dönemi mekân tasarım dinamikleri araştırılacaktır. Ortaya çıkartılan veriler sayesinde, kapsam dahilinde ele alınan kuramcıların malzemeye dair kuramsal yaklaşımlarının düşünsel dinamiklerini ortaya çıkartılacaktır. Bu sayede incelenecek kuramcıların, malzemeye dair yaklaşımları temellendirilecektir. Bu temel üzerinden, belirlenen kuramcıların malzemeye dai…

title: Sampling-based integrated design optimization of floating wind turbine substructures with Pywind
abstract: Abstract Design optimization of floating wind turbine (FWT) substructures remains computationally demanding due to the extensive time-domain simulations required to explore high-dimensional design spaces. This study builds upon the previously developed Pywind-based integrated design optimization (IDO) framework, extending it by comparing two sampling strategies: Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and Maximin LHS. A 15 MW semi-submersible FWT is employed to assess the performance of these methods in capturing design variability and coupled hydrodynamic and structural responses under stochastic environmental conditions. The analysis shows that Maximin LHS significantly improves space-filling uniformity, reducing the Voronoi coefficient of variation by 41.5% compared to Standard LHS. Additionally, Maximin LHS shows a 46.8% improvement in the mean Voronoi area, resulting in more even parameter-space coverage. This highlights the capability of the Pywind-based IDO framework to conduct efficient, scalable, and statistically robust time-domain optimization. The findings underscore the IDO framework's potential for probabilistic design exploration, supporting intelligent decision-making for the next generation of FWT systems.

Design and Optimization of an Asymmetric CLLC Resonant Converter with Interleaved Totem-Pole Front-End for Wide Voltage Range Single-Stage EV Charging
abstract: The increasing adoption of 800 V-class electric vehicles has created strong demand for single-stage onboard chargers capable of operating over a wide output voltage range while maintaining high efficiency and power density. This paper presents the design and multi-objective optimization of a single-stage bidirectional AC-DC converter that integrates a three-phase interleaved totem-pole front-end with an asymmetric CLLC resonant converter. The proposed topology eliminates large electrolytic DC-bus capacitors by using only small film capacitors and enables seamless operation across an ultra-wide battery voltage range of 100–850 V. The asymmetric CLLC parameters were optimized using a combination of fundamental harmonic approximation (FHA), time-domain analysis (TDA), and multi-objective particle swarm optimization (PSO) to achieve high voltage gain, wide zero-voltage switching (ZVS), and high efficiency. Simulations show a peak efficiency of 97.1%, an input-current THD of 2.8%, primary ZVS down to about 18% load, and bidirectional (V2G) operation. The design is a candidate for 800 V-class onboard chargers that must cover 100–850 V.

title: Sources, Transmission, and Control of Salmonella in Vertically Integrated Broiler Chicken Production: Farm, Hatchery, and Processing Plant
abstract: ABSTRACT Salmonella remains one of the most important foodborne pathogens associated with poultry products, despite substantial progress in processing hygiene and antimicrobial interventions. This review critically examines the sources, transmission routes, and control strategies for Salmonella in vertically integrated broiler production systems. Attention is given to contamination originating from breeder flocks, hatcheries, feed, water, litter, grow‐out farms, transport, processing environments, and finished products. Preharvest interventions, including biosecurity, breeder and hatchery control, vaccination, litter and water management, feed hygiene, probiotics, prebiotics, organic acids, essential oils, bacteriophages, and bacteriocins, are evaluated according to mechanism, evidence strength, and commercial relevance. Postharvest interventions, including scalding, picking, evisceration control, chilling, peroxyacetic acid application, carcass rinses, post‐chill treatments, and finished‐product verification, are reviewed in relation to microbial reduction and process control. The review also discusses quantitative bio‐mapping, surveillance design, whole‐genome sequencing, predictive modeling, and quantitative microbial risk assessment as tools for identifying contamination hotspots, persistent strains, and high‐risk control points. Overall, effective Salmonella control requir…

title: Spatial Overlap Between Wind Power Licensing Areas and Potential Grazing Lands in Greece: A National Screening Assessment
abstract: Wind energy expansion constitutes a central component of Greece’s energy transition. However, the spatial allocation of Wind Power Production Plants (WPPs) may coincide with potential grazing lands and Natura 2000 protected areas, creating potential land-use and conservation interfaces that require careful planning. This study provides a national-scale spatial screening assessment of the overlap between WPP licensing areas and potential grazing lands in Greece. Geospatial data from the Regulatory Authority for Energy (RAE), retrieved in February 2026, were intersected with CORINE Land Cover 2018 data using GIS-based vector analysis. Four alternative grazing-land classification scenarios were applied to account for uncertainty in the spatial definition of potential grazing lands. A spatial intersection was conducted between WPP licensing areas and Natura 2000 boundaries, followed by an assessment of potential grazing-land overlap within the resulting WPP-Natura 2000 areas. The results showed that, across the four scenarios, 65.89% to 70.34% of the total WPP polygon area overlapped potential grazing lands, while overlap within individual licensing stages ranged from 63.40% to 85.93%. Approximately 28.64% of the total WPP polygon area was located within Natura 2000 sites. Within these WPP-Natura 2000 areas, the proportion classified as potential grazing land ranged from 62.68% to …

title: The genome sequence of White Butterbur, Petasites albus (L. Gaertn., 1791) (Asterales: Asteraceae)
abstract: We present a genome assembly of Petasites albus (White Butterbur; Streptophyta; Magnoliopsida; Asterales; Asteraceae). The assembly consists of two haplotypes with total lengths of 2,845.89 megabases and 2,738.22 megabases. Most of the haplotype 1 assembly (94.48%) was scaffolded into 30 chromosomal pseudomolecules. Haplotype 2 was assembled to scaffold level. The mitochondrial sequences have lengths of 107.61, 154.81 and 46.65 kilobases and the plastid genome assembly has a length of 150.69 kilobases. Gene annotation of this assembly by Ensembl identified 43,211 protein-coding genes. This assembly was generated as part of the Darwin Tree of Life project, which produces reference genomes for eukaryotic species found in Britain and Ireland.

title: Photogenerated Charge Injection-Modulated Ultralow-Power ZnO/Sb2S3 Heterojunction Memristors for Artificial Visual Nociception and Persistence Systems
abstract: Abstract Bioinspired neuromorphic architectures featuring sensory-memory-computing integration offer a highly effective approach to overcoming the traditional von Neumann computing bottleneck. However, existing optoelectronic memristors universally face challenges such as high static power consumption and difficulties in modulating resistive switching behaviors during array-level integration. Here, an ultralow-power Ag/PMMA/ZnO/Sb2S3/FTO heterojunction memristor operating at the nanoampere scale is reported. By engineering a Type-II ZnO/Sb2S3 band alignment and incorporating an ultrathin PMMA tunneling barrier, the device achieves synergistic carrier regulation and broadband charge separation. Notably, light illumination significantly reduces the SET voltage from 5.0 to 2.65 V. A collaborative switching model, governed by photocarrier injection and electric-field-driven dynamics, is proposed to elucidate the mechanism of threshold modulation at the interface. Functionally, the device emulates essential synaptic plasticity and realizes an advanced artificial visual nociceptor featuring threshold-triggering, nonadaptation, and relaxation. Furthermore, simulation-based spatiotemporal image processing, including dynamic forgetting and visual persistence, is demonstrated. This work establishes a new mechanistic paradigm for ultralow-power, multimodal neuromorphic vision hardware, pa…

title: Temporal patterns in maximal relative power output among Czech youth ice hockey players (2019–2023): a repeated cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract The aim of the study was to examine recent patterns in maximal relative power output during ramp cycle ergometer testing among Czech youth ice hockey players between 2019 and 2023, and to quantify the proportion of players meeting historical performance benchmarks, which have previously been discussed in relation to paediatric fitness and cardiometabolic risk, while acknowledging that these power-based criteria do not directly measure cardiorespiratory fitness or health outcomes. Methods We analysed 1,433 ramp cycle ergometer tests performed in male ice hockey players aged 9–18 years at two accredited sports medicine centres, some players were tested repeatedly across different years. All tests followed an identical electronically braked incremental ramp protocol, and performance was expressed as relative maximal power output (W/kg). Results were classified as “within” or “below” benchmark values based on historical W/kg standards from adolescent athletes tested in the late 1970s. Between‑year differences in W/kg and anthropometric parameters (height, body mass, BMI) were assessed within age groups using the Kruskal–Wallis test. Results Overall, 49.1% (703/1,433) of tests achieved W/kg values within the benchmark range across 2019–2023, with marked age‑related differences. Only 16–38% of 9–12‑year‑olds met the benchmarks, compared with 80–89% of 15–18‑year‑olds. The pr…

AI-Driven Personal Virtual Assistants and Digital Alienation: Ownership, Ideology, and Subject Formation in Platform Capitalism
abstract: The article provides a framework through which one can interpret personal assistants powered by AI technology as ideological “interfaces” within platform capitalism. Rather than seeing these tools simply as tools of convenience, this article looks at how their corporate backgrounds, ownership structures, and platform ecosystems contribute to the way we come to view concepts such as assistance, personalization, closeness, neutrality, and trust. By making use of Marx’s theory of alienation and Saussurean and Barthesian structural semiotics, we argue that it is important to see ownership, not just as an economic relationship but also as a system of meaning through which corporations gain legitimacy. We focus on four personal assistants, Siri, Google Assistant, Alexa, and Bixby, fully integrated with their corresponding corporate platforms: Apple, Google, Amazon, and Samsung. The article does not provide an empirical analysis of users of personal assistants but instead presents a theoretical interpretation of how these tools facilitate the development of individual identity, the extraction of data, and the process of digital alienation in contemporary capitalist economies. Through demonstrating how assistive language and personalized experience obfuscate both ownership relations and the capitalistic infrastructure underpinning daily digital interactions, we add to existing discussi…

title: Nanotechnology-Enabled Strategies for Enhancing Plant Abiotic Stress Tolerance
abstract: Amid increasingly complex climate scenarios, abiotic stresses such as drought, extreme temperatures, and soil salinization have emerged as primary bottlenecks limiting the sustainable development of modern agriculture. Because of their unique nanoscale effects and physicochemical properties, nanoparticles (NPs) can penetrate plant tissue barriers, offering a novel approach to enhance crop resilience to environmental stresses. This review systematically summarizes the core mechanisms by which NPs enhance plant stress tolerance. NPs primarily mitigate the overaccumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and cellular oxidative stress by modulating antioxidant systems, thereby maintaining the physical integrity of photosynthetic apparatuses and cell membranes. Additionally, NPs regulate phytohormone signaling networks and the transcription of stress-responsive genes, while supporting ion compartmentalization and osmotic homeostasis in complex habitats such as coastal saline environments. Integrating multi-omics analyses, this review discusses plant metabolic responses to NPs and their dose-dependent toxicological effects. Addressing bottlenecks in practical application, we evaluate barriers to field-scale translation, the environmental release and migration of nanomaterials across water, air, and the food supply, and associated detection methods and safety risks, including the spe…

title: Long-Term Oceanographic Survey for Social Implementation of OTEC Plant in Okinotorishima (Seawater Temperature, Salinity, Dissolved Oxygen, Inorganic Nutrients and Density)
abstract: In order to implement ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC), it is necessary to maintain a stable temperature difference between surface seawater and deep seawater. Accordingly, numerous oceanographic surveys have been conducted to select sea areas suitable for OTEC deployment, not only around Japan but also in other countries around the world. However, long-term oceanographic survey data for the Okinotorishima area, a promising candidate for OTEC, are not yet available. While many studies have addressed OTEC design under generic conditions, designs based on specific areas have remained limited. However, the availability of oceanographic data necessary for conducting such studies is still limited. Therefore, a long-term oceanographic survey was conducted, starting in 2006. This study presents a systematic compilation of oceanographic survey results to lay the groundwork for evaluations for the installation of an OTEC plant. The survey items included the vertical profiles of seawater temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, and nutrients at each observation station. The results indicate that the temperature difference between surface seawater and deep seawater, which is the most important factor for OTEC, almost exceeded the threshold of 20 °C required for the realization of an OTEC plant. This study provides a foundational dataset for evaluating the feasibility of OTEC deploym…

What Does It Mean To Be Good at Physics? Peer Recognition in a High School Physics Classroom
abstract: ABSTRACT In the United States, the Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) call for science classrooms where students develop a wide range of skills, though students still often hold to narrow views of what it means to be good at science. Science identity provides a lens to examine what students believe being good at science means. A widely used framework describes science identity through the dimensions of competence, performance, and recognition. Many studies have found that recognition is a key element of a science identity. In spite of the clear importance of recognition, there has been little effort to describe what it looks like, especially between peers. This study used video of students working in small groups in a high school physics classroom and interviews with several of the students to develop a framework for peer recognition. The types of recognition students gave each other were categorized as explicit recognition, typically given for an answer or contribution students saw as correct, and implicit recognition, typically given over an extended period for contributions including asking questions and sharing incorrect ideas. The interviews provided insights into how students connected recognition to their science identity. When discussing what it meant to be good at physics or discussing the ways their peers were good at physics, students demonstrated a broad view …
