title: A critical review of electric vehicle sustainability from a life cycle and climate perspective
abstract: Abstract Electric vehicles (EVs) are central to transport decarbonization, but their environmental benefits depend on interactions among vehicle production, battery value chains, electricity supply, charging infrastructure, operational strategies, and end‐of‐life management. This review critically synthesizes EV sustainability from an integrated life‐cycle and climate perspective using a structured literature‐selection process that retained 224 studies for detailed evaluation. The assessment covers life cycle assessment (LCA) methodologies, raw‐material extraction and battery manufacturing, vehicle production, charging and energy‐delivery systems, use‐phase electricity consumption, recycling and circularity, climate‐mitigation potential, and artificial intelligence (AI) enabled electric mobility. The synthesis confirms that EVs generally offer lower life‐cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions than internal combustion engine vehicles, particularly under low‐carbon electricity systems, although the magnitude of this advantage remains strongly influenced by grid carbon intensity (CI), battery production, vehicle lifetime, driving and charging behavior, system boundaries, and recycling assumptions. Charging infrastructure emerges as an integral sustainability dimension because renewable integration, smart charging, vehicle‐to‐grid operation, station planning, and grid constraints aff…

title: Detector Response and Energy-Threshold Optimization for Imaging with Cosmic-Ray Muon-Induced Secondary Radiation
abstract: Imaging with cosmic-ray muon-induced secondary radiation complements muon transmission radiography and muon scattering tomography by exploiting the electrons and bremsstrahlung photons created along the muon track inside the target. Because these secondaries are produced predominantly at low energies, the performance of such a system depends critically on parameters that are usually treated as routine: the uniformity of the response of the surrounding scintillator array and the energy threshold applied during acquisition. This contribution reports the instrumental characterization of the muon camera (MUCA) setup operated at the University of Novi Sad, comprising a five-layer Close Cathode Chamber tracker and four large-area plastic scintillation detectors. Over a continuous run of about 24 h, the combined tracking efficiency was about 0.96 and stable at the percent level. Single-detector and joint spectra recorded with 137Cs and a bulk KCl source were used to equalize the high voltage across the array, and the acquisition threshold was set to approximately 230 keV. A direct comparison of images of a copper cylinder reconstructed with a 250 keV and with a 1 MeV analysis cut shows that the conventional MeV-level threshold discards the majority of the target-related signal. The corresponding limitation of the geometrical acceptance is also discussed. The design of the COMIS upgrad…

title: Renewable Energy, Energy Import Dependence, and Trade Balance in Türkiye
abstract: This paper analyzes how renewable energy use and dependence on imported energy influence Türkiye’s trade balance. The study is grounded in the argument that economies relying heavily on imported fossil fuels are more exposed to external balance pressures, whereas domestic renewable energy use may help reduce this exposure by replacing part of imported energy demand. Economic growth and the real exchange rate are added as control variables in order to capture demand-side conditions and relative price movements in foreign trade. The empirical investigation is based on annual data for Türkiye and applies a time-series methodology that allows for structural shifts and long-run linkages. First, the integration order of the series is examined through the ADF and Fourier ADF tests. The long-run connection among the variables is then assessed by employing the RALS Fourier ADL and Gregory–Hansen cointegration approaches. After confirming cointegration, the long-run parameters are obtained through the DOLS estimator, and causal linkages are explored with the Fourier Toda–Yamamoto procedure. The results show that renewable energy contributes positively to Türkiye’s trade balance, while energy import dependence has a deteriorating effect. The causality evidence also points to a two-way interaction between renewable energy use and the trade balance. Overall, the findings indicate that renew…

title: Evaluación del Impacto de Generación Distribuida Fotovoltaica y Almacenamiento en Baterías en el Perfil de Tensión de una Red de Distribución IEEE de 34 Nodos
abstract: La creciente incorporación de la generación distribuida (GD) está transformando la operación de las redes de distribución, tradicionalmente diseñadas para flujos de potencia predominantemente unidireccionales. La integración de fuentes distribuidas puede introducir condiciones operativas no previstas en el diseño original, como elevaciones de tensión, inversión de los flujos de potencia y variaciones en el intercambio de potencia reactiva. En este artículo se evalúa el desempeño eléctrico de una red de distribución ante distintos niveles de alojamiento de GD, identificando y cuantificando su impacto en variables clave como los perfiles de voltaje, las pérdidas eléctricas y los flujos de potencia activa y reactiva. El estudio se desarrolla mediante simulaciones en OpenDSS sobre un sistema de prueba IEEE, comparando un escenario base con escenarios de incorporación progresiva de GD. Asimismo, se analizan medidas de mitigación orientadas a mantener la operación dentro de los límites normativos, incluyendo estrategias de regulación de tensión y control de potencia reactiva. Los resultados muestran que, en régimen estacionario y mediante una adecuada coordinación de estos mecanismos de regulación, es posible incrementar el nivel de alojamiento de GD sin comprometer la calidad del servicio ni la seguridad operativa de la red, proporcionando fundamentos técnicos que respalden su integ…

title: Constraints Faced by Women Self-help Group Members in Vermicompost Production in the Kashmir Valley: A Constraint Facing Index Analysis
abstract: The study examined perceived constraints among women Self-Help Group (SHG) members engaged in vermicompost production in Bandipora and Baramulla districts of the Kashmir Valley, Jammu and Kashmir. A descriptive ex post facto design was used. The defined study frame comprised 11 SHGs supported by the Indo Global Social Service Society (IGSSS), including seven SHGs with 70 members in Bandipora and four SHGs with 37 members in Baramulla; all 107 members engaged in vermicompost production within this frame were included. Data were collected through personal interviews using a pre-tested structured interview schedule. Thirteen constraints were rated on a four-point continuum and ranked using a Constraint Facing Index (CFI) ranging from 0 to 300. Earthworms being eaten by natural enemies such as birds received the highest CFI (295.33), followed by non-availability of machinery (280.38) and overburdening in household and farm activities (233.62). Lack of proper guidance regarding vermicompost production (42.99) and mortality of earthworms during transfer (39.24) occupied the next two ranks. Constraints in bed preparation (3.74) and non-availability of earthworms (5.61) received the lowest CFI values. The findings identify perceived biological, infrastructural, workload, technical support and marketing constraints that may be considered when designing extension and enterprise-support i…

title: Largely Negative Energy Difference between the Singlet and Triplet Excited States and Ultrafast Delayed Fluorescence
abstract: Abstract Molecules exhibiting inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states, referred to as inverted singlet–triplet (IST) molecules, can show a short delayed lifetime below 1 μs and are therefore promising candidates for next-generation emitters in organic light-emitting diodes. However, the structural factors that govern this inversion remain insufficiently understood, limiting the rational molecular design of compounds with tunable photophysical properties. Here, we analyzed the relationships between excited-state energy levels and frontier molecular-orbital energy levels in heptazine derivatives. The results indicate that degenerate HOMOs and LUMOs are key factors for reducing ΔEST through enhanced mixing of multiple excitation configurations, whereas phenyl groups slightly increase ΔEST by enhancing the exchange interaction, K. Wave function-based quantum chemical calculations using EOM-CCSD estimated large negative ΔEST values of −0.244 eV and −0.238 eV for the heptazine derivatives, HzDA3 and HzTFE3, respectively. Temperature-dependent time-resolved photoluminescence, together with the onsets analysis of photoluminescence and phosphorescence spectra, confirmed their negative ΔEST values. HzDA3 and HzTFE3 exhibited fast reverse intersystem crossing rate constants exceeding 107 s–1, resulting in ultrafast delayed lifetimes of 76 and 341 ns, respectively. These…

Energia solar fotovoltaica na habitação de interesse social: evolução regulatória e integração ao Minha Casa, Minha Vida
abstract: This article analyzes the incorporation of photovoltaic solar generation into Brazilian social housing policy, focusing on the Minha Casa, Minha Vida (MCMV) program. The study updates a proposal formulated in 2020 and examines subsequent regulatory developments, especially Law No. 14,300/2022, Law No. 14,620/2023 and Decree No. 12,084/2024, which established the Clean Energy in Minha Casa, Minha Vida Program. A qualitative, exploratory and descriptive approach is adopted, based on bibliographic and documentary research involving federal legislation, regulatory documents issued by the Brazilian Electricity Regulatory Agency (ANEEL), information from the Ministry of Cities, and technical literature on photovoltaic systems. The findings indicate convergence between the original proposal and the public policy later implemented, particularly regarding lower household electricity expenses, broader use of renewable sources, and the integration of housing, energy efficiency and sustainability. However, photovoltaic adoption should not be treated as an isolated and uniform obligation: effectiveness depends on technical and economic feasibility, grid-connection rules, compensation arrangements, project quality, operation and maintenance, building efficiency and suitable financing mechanisms. The study concludes that solar energy can be a relevant social-housing policy instrument when int…

title: Wealth Without Stability: Oil Revenue Volatility and the Limits of Saudi Fiscal Diversification, 1980-2000
abstract: This paper argues that the central problem between 1980 and 2000 was not oil wealth itself, but oil-revenue volatility and the fiscal choices it induced. It examines the post-1981 contraction, the 1986 price collapse, and the 1998 crash through a mixed-method approach combining econometric analysis with archival evidence. A five-year rolling volatility variable is constructed from annual changes in petroleum export revenues, then tested through time-series OLS, sector-year panel regressions, and an interaction model measuring fiscal oil dependence. The results show that volatility damaged non-oil activity broadly rather than producing the tradable vs. non-tradable divergence predicted by standard Dutch Disease theory. The fiscal interaction is negative in the predicted direction for manufacturing, although the econometric evidence is suggestive rather than independently conclusive. Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency reports, Five-Year Development Plans, and IMF consultations clarify the mechanism: across all three crises, the state protected current expenditures while cutting development, infrastructure, subsidized credit, and industrial support more deeply. These repeated allocation decisions weakened the sectors on which diversification depended and compounded the effects of successive revenue shocks. The Saudi resource curse, therefore, emerged not mechanically from resource abun…

Influence of storage condition and sample age on the rennet induced aggregation of para-casein micelles
abstract: Abstract The growing use of novel casein-based functional materials beyond traditional food applications requires a detailed understanding of how storage conditions affect the aggregation behaviour of casein micelles. In this study, we systematically varied storage time (2, 7, 12 and 79 days) and temperature (5, 10 and 15 °C) as well as mechanical treatment (stirred vs. unstirred) and then monitored enzymatically induced aggregation by means of turbidity measurements. The aggregation kinetics were analysed using an asymmetric sigmoidal fitting model, which showed that the delay time and the time to reach the maximum aggregation rate generally decreased with increasing storage time and temperature. The maximum aggregation rate increased up to a storage period of 12 days, but longer storage – especially at elevated temperatures – resulted in reduced rates, suggesting structural rearrangements, pre-aggregation or partial micelle degradation. Stirring during storage had a temperature-dependent and time-dependent effect. At moderate temperatures and medium storage times, it generally resulted in a more homogeneous micelle dispersion and prevented reversible pre-aggregation, while at low temperatures and very short storage times, it helped to keep aggregation rates lower and samples more stable than in non-stirred controls. At elevated temperatures and longer storage times, stirring …

title: Toward Integrated Upcycling of Lithium‐Ion Battery: Advances and Outlooks
abstract: The imminent retirement of large batches of lithium‐ion batteries poses a critical challenge to sustainable resource management. While present recycling technologies have demonstrated certain advantages over conventional metallurgical methods, the comprehensive assessment of their environmental impacts has introduced additional requirements. These include adherence to the principles of closed‐loop processing, minimized waste streams, and high‐value‐added recovery. Herein, we offer a summarizing framework that emphasizes the integrated utilization of spent batteries, thereby shifting the research focus from maximizing extraction efficiency toward achieving holistic sustainability. By analyzing the evolution of reutilization strategies, we identify that complex separation processes generate nontrivial carbon footprints and water consumption. This review consolidates these critical aspects, with the aim of encouraging a more balanced perspective that considers both material recovery efficiency and battery upcycling potential.

title: Sequence-Conditioned Physics-Informed Neural Network for Lithium-Ion Battery State of Health Estimation Using Charging Segments at High State of Charge
abstract: Accurate and reliable state of health (SOH) estimation is essential for lithium-ion battery safety and lifetime management. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) integrate battery degradation knowledge with deep learning to improve the physical consistency of SOH estimation. However, existing PINNs insufficiently capture degradation evolution across consecutive cycles and show limited applicability across battery chemistries and charge/discharge protocols. To address these issues, we propose a sequence-conditioned physics-informed neural network (SC-PINN) that uses a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to encode local degradation states and incorporates a degradation dynamics consistency constraint and a monotonic degradation prior to improve prediction accuracy and physical plausibility. We also develop a general charging feature extraction method for different battery chemistries and charge/discharge protocols, extracting unified 18-dimensional health features from charging segments at high state of charge (SOC). The method is validated using 317 batteries and 197,024 valid cycle samples covering four battery chemistries across nine representative tasks. SC-PINN achieves a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.6285% and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.8924%, with the lowest RMSE in eight of nine tasks. Compared with other methods, the proposed method demonstrates good sta…

title: V─O─Ti Bridge‐Bond Polarity Boosts Na + Migration in V‐Based Fluorophosphates for Fast Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐based fluorophosphates are promising high‐energy‐density cathodes for next‐generation sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, the pronounced degradation of Na + diffusion at high voltage hinders their fast‐charging capability. Herein, a Ti 4+ ‐doping‐induced bridge‐bond‐polarity‐driven strategy is proposed to reshape the V electronic structure for facilitating V─O electron exchange. Correspondingly, voltage hysteresis, polarization, and structural distortion at high voltage are suppressed, accompanied by enhanced electronic conductivity. Meanwhile, the polar V─O─Ti bridge bonds expand the dominant one‐ and two‐dimensional Na + transport channels by inducing bridging‐O displacement, further boosting Na + migration capability. Therefore, Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 with V─O─Ti delivers high capacities of 121.8 and 62.1 mA h g −1 at 0.1C and 50C, respectively, while maintaining excellent cycling stability. Additionally, the 0.92‐Ah Na 3 V 1.92 Ti 0.08 O(PO 4 ) 2 F 2 //HC pouch cell exhibits 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1C. At the 9 Ah scale, the pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 154 Wh kg −1 . This synergistic reinforcement strategy driven by bridge‐bond polarity paves the way for sustainable high‐power polyanionic SIBs.

title: Stochastic Convex Optimization for Day-Ahead Shared Battery Storage Scheduling in Solar Energy Communities
abstract: Energy communities represent a transformative paradigm for decentralized renewable energy integration, enabling collective investment in photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) to achieve economic and environmental benefits. However, the optimal operation of these communities faces significant challenges due to inherent uncertainties in solar generation, load consumption, and electricity prices. This paper presents a stochastic optimization framework for day-ahead scheduling of shared battery energy storage in solar-powered energy communities under multiple uncertainty sources. The problem is formulated as a stochastic mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) model that minimizes the expected daily operational cost, including energy procurement from the grid, PV operation and maintenance (O&M), battery operation costs, and degradation-induced expenses. A battery degradation model based on equivalent full-cycle counting captures the economic impact of cycling under uncertain conditions. The proposed approach employs a scenario-based Monte Carlo method to represent uncertainties and reformulates the MINLP as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) through exact linearization of the absolute-value terms in the degradation cost, enabling efficient solution with commercial solvers. The framework is applied to an aggregated energy community whose installe…

title: Emergency Vehicle Car-Following Across Driving Regimes with Retrospective and Past-Only Regime Assignment
abstract: This study examines whether regime-specific calibration improves the local acceleration representation of emergency-vehicle following episodes. Field trajectories of ambulances performing emergency-response tasks were obtained from two monitoring sites on Shaoshan East Road in Xiangtan, China, during February–December 2025 and screened into 499 valid following pairs. Standardised window features were reduced by principal component analysis and clustered using training pairs only. Three assignment protocols were compared: retrospective windows with acceleration, retrospective windows without acceleration, and acceleration-free windows completed strictly before the response time. Five car-following models were calibrated with fixed or regime-specific parameters and evaluated on identical observations. In the primary past-only analysis, the common test support comprised 1678 observations from 69 pairs. The Longitudinal Control Model (LCM) had the lowest test RMSE, 1.0478 m/s2, and reduced RMSE by 13.43% relative to its fixed-parameter counterpart; the paired pair-level bootstrap interval for the RMSE difference was [−0.2225, −0.0973] m/s2. Improvements for the other four models were smaller and their intervals included zero. LCM retained the lowest error with two and four clusters and under expanded parameter bounds, although its fitted parameters remained sensitive to constraints…

title: Deposit-Escrow EV Charging on Avalanche with zk-SNARK Billing Proofs: Prototype Scope and Security Limits
abstract: Electric-vehicle (EV) charging workflows expose billing and session information through centralized services or transparent ledgers. This study integrates deposit escrow, a Groth16 billing-arithmetic proof, and settlement on the Avalanche Fuji testnet. Its contribution is a proof-of-concept workflow linking authorization, payment, refund, and timeout handling, together with an analysis of the boundary between the implemented proof and a proposed station-authenticated protocol. Across five runs per setting, mean deposit and settlement confirmation times are 1.8 s and 2.1 s, respectively; proof generation averages 0.21 s on a desktop PC; and settlement consumes approximately 320,000 gas. These descriptive results apply to a simplified circuit that checks billing arithmetic with a placeholder binding. Station signatures are checked only by the off-chain harness, so station-authenticated billing and resistance to substituted energy witnesses remain unvalidated. Normal settlement provides meter-field omission, not consumption confidentiality: under the exact public linear tariff, energy E is recoverable from public payment C and positive tariff p as E = C/p. The results support feasibility of the escrow-and-arithmetic-proof workflow; authenticated witness binding, complete reproducibility artifacts, and stronger experimental validation remain prerequisites for a secure deployment.

title: A Multi‐Objective Optimization and Decision‐Making Framework for Safety‐Critical Ground Vehicle Endurance Tests
abstract: ABSTRACT Accelerated endurance testing for safety‐critical ground vehicles requires reproducing field‐induced fatigue within limited time while maintaining stable and reliable evaluation conditions. However, conventional procedures rely on empirical rules or component‐level metrics, offering limited capability for balanced and system‐consistent fatigue reproduction. This study presents an integrated, data‐driven framework combining Multi‐Objective Optimization (MOO) and Multi‐Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) to systematically support endurance test design for safety‐critical ground vehicles. For this, an NSGA‐II formulation was used to identify terrain–direction–speed combinations that satisfy mileage requirements while keeping each component within acceptable fatigue ranges. Subsequently, the CRITIC method derived objective criterion weights, and the non‐compensatory PROMETHEE II approach was used to rank Pareto‐optimal solutions to ensure robust and stable rankings. Prediction accuracy and loading consistency were evaluated using the Geometric Mean Relative Absolute Error (GMRAE) and the Factor of Damage Ratio (FDR). The framework successfully reproduced target fatigue damage, yielding optimal solutions with GMRAE values below 1.0 for most component groups and extreme channel rates below 3%. Crucially, the CRITIC‐PROMETHEE II integration demonstrated stable rank consistency un…

title: Vehicle dynamics simulation considering multipoint contact between wheel and rail during earthquakes
abstract: Large earthquakes occurred repeatedly in Japan, and, in some cases, railway vehicles derailed and overturned during earthquakes. Safety measures are being implemented in various railway sectors, and it is important to continue investigating ways to improve safety. The vehicle dynamics simulator (VDS) developed by Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI) has been used to analyze the behavior of railway vehicles in the event of earthquakes; however, this simulation program has some limitations in terms of the wheel-rail contact problem, which is essential for the vehicle dynamics of rolling stocks due to the performance limitations of the computers at that time. This study developed a new simulation program, i.e., the VDS-X, which includes a multipoint-contact-capable online contact calculation algorithm, thereby enabling analyses that consider the changes in contact conditions that were not fully considered by conventional methods. Using the VDS-X, the results of safety limits for sinusoidal excitations are compared with those obtained by the conventional VDS, and the differences in wheelset behavior between stopped and running conditions are investigated. The results confirm that the trends in safety limits were reproduced in a manner consistent with the conventional method. Furthermore, a detailed analysis of the contact state revealed fundamental differences in the wheel-r…

title: On operational adaptability of wear-resistant coatings for key components in electric vehicle differentials: A case study
abstract: During starting, rapid acceleration, and energy regeneration (with alternating forward and reverse rotation), EV differentials endure much higher instantaneous torque than conventional vehicles, greatly increasing wear and failure risk. Surface coating technologies thus offer a key strategy to enhance differential durability. However, conventional evaluation methods deviate from real service conditions, making it difficult to assess coating adaptability. This study targets the planetary gear shaft—the most wear-prone component—and develops a shaft-ring tribological test bench. Finite element simulations determined benchmark loads, replicating actual contact and motion. Wear tests on electroless nickel and DLC coatings were conducted under varying loads and lubrication. Results show electroless nickel, with lower hardness, exhibited wear under all conditions but retained partial coverage even under severe loads, maintaining surface protection. In contrast, DLC, with much higher hardness, showed negligible wear in most cases but failed catastrophically under high load and poor lubrication, where local damage propagated rapidly, exposing the substrate and causing severe adhesive wear. Thus, electroless nickel is preferable under high load/impact to prevent catastrophic failure, while DLC is favored under stable conditions for its superior hardness. These findings provide a scienti…

title: Bridging Autonomous Driving and Electric-Mobility Systems: From Technical Interfaces to Cross-System Validation
abstract: Road-transport electrification and driving automation increasingly connect vehicle actions with charging services and urban electricity demand. This review combines two Web of Science Core Collection result sets with abstract-level term analysis and a structured synthesis of technical studies to examine that connection. The broader searches yielded 60,043 and 16,458 records, respectively; recent exports contained 10,926 and 4502 records. Rule-based analysis of nonempty abstracts and the technical synthesis identify four intersections: energy-aware route-charging decisions, station selection and automated access, fleet scheduling, and coupled evaluation. Across the studies examined, vehicle execution, station-session events, and distribution constraints are often represented at different boundaries. The resulting evidence supports a common evaluation of mobility, charging service, and feeder operation, with the five-stage pathway serving as a framework for progressively stronger validation. In a two-hour extreme-condition illustration, on-time charging completion rises from 75.5% without guidance to 97.1% with authorized automated execution, while total vehicle travel time decreases. The review thus identifies measurable interfaces for testing cross-system coordination while keeping field deployment claims tied to their validation level.

title: Deep Defence on Wheels: A Dual Intrusion Detection System Architecture for Comprehensive In-Vehicle Network Security
abstract: The combination of increasing connectivity to the outside world and the lack of inbuilt security mechanisms has made legacy intra-vehicular networks extremely vulnerable to cyberattacks. Consequently, significant research has been devoted to analysing the impact of potential attacks, yielding datasets crucial for developing effective mitigation schemes like intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDSs/IPSs). Initial research addressing this problem focused heavily on maximising attack detection accuracy (for both known and unknown attack vectors), often relying on large, full-precision machine learning models. However, embedding IDS into complex vehicular electronic systems adds challenges beyond accuracy, including the need for low detection latency (e.g., 2,000 CAN frames/sec), energy efficiency, and minimal overhead in electronic control unit (ECU) resources like silicon area, memory, and processor use. To address these deployment constraints, recent research has focused on lightweight machine learning models that balance high classification accuracy with these practical limitations. In this work, we propose a dual IDS framework comprising both supervised and unsupervised learning-based solutions, each optimised for real-time, resource-constrained deployment on embedded automotive platforms. We present a quantised LSTM-based IDS (QLSTM-IDS) that achieves over 99.9% detec…

title: A Peripheral Sulfonium Moiety Engineering Strategy to Enhance AIEgen-Based Antitumor Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: Abstract The therapeutic efficacy of photosensitizers (PSs) strongly depends on their capacity to efficiently generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a peripheral sulfonium moiety engineering strategy and identify a lead aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-based PS, S12. The sulfonium moiety enhances the photosensitization of S12 primarily by increasing spin−orbit coupling (SOC) and reducing ΔEST, thus boosting ROS generation. Moreover, the sulfonium unit enables S12 to simultaneously produce both Type I and Type II ROS, rendering its photosensitization weakly dependent on O2 concentration. Owing to its cationic character and the inherent amphiphilicity of the AIE core, S12 exhibits dynamic organelle-targeting behavior, initially anchoring to membranes and subsequently accumulating in lipid droplets. Such localization facilitates ROS-triggered ferroptosis, leading to potent in vitro antitumor photodynamic therapy activity and effective tumor suppression in a 4T1 mouse model. Overall, this work provides a rational design strategy to advance AIE-based PSs with enhanced therapeutic potential.

title: Diffusion-Selective Modulation Strategy for Enhanced Propane Dehydrogenation via Mixing Inert CHA Zeolite
abstract: Abstract Achieving a high propane conversion in propane dehydrogenation to propylene (PDH) carries tremendous scientific and economic value, particularly if achievable with established industrial units. Here we propose a diffusion-selective modulation strategy driven by large-scale machine-learning computation, where the key to success lies in finding auxiliary materials to drive the PDH reaction forward by enlarging the diffusion-rate difference between H2 and C3 species. This strategy is demonstrated theoretically via high-throughput computation and then validated experimentally through the introduction of inert siliceous CHA zeolites as a diffusion-selective modulator within the catalyst bed. By simply physically mixing CHA with various PDH catalysts, we show that the single-pass propane conversion can increase by 1–5% from industrial space velocities (10 h–1) to significantly higher throughputs (256 h–1), consistently improving performance across multiple reported catalysts without compromising stability. This “plug-and-play” methodology can be directly implemented in existing industrial PDH units without altering either the catalyst formulation or the reactor configuration, providing a readily implementable and scalable route for upgrading current PDH infrastructure.

title: Dietary Management as a Strategy for Reducing Inflammaging in Aging Population
abstract: As more people live into older age, researchers have started to focus on chronic, low-grade systemic inflammation—called inflammaging—as a key biological factor behind cardiovascular disease, cognitive decline, and frailty in later life. Franceschi et al. (2000) describe inflammaging as a progressive, chronic, low-grade pro-inflammatory state that becomes more pronounced with age, driven by multiple interacting mechanisms including senescent cell accumulation and SASP signaling, mitochondrial dysfunction and the release of DAMPs, gut microbiome shifts, and failures in immune regulation. This literature review examines how dietary patterns influence inflammaging through measurable biomarkers such as hs-CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α. Evidence indicates that pro-inflammatory dietary components including saturated fatty acids, trans fatty acids, and high–glycemic index carbohydrates tend to elevate these markers, while omega-3 fatty acids, dietary fiber, MUFAs, flavonoids, carotenoids, and magnesium are associated with reductions in them. A two-year Mediterranean diet intervention reported significant decreases in hs-CRP, IL-6, IL-7, and IL-18 compared to a control diet, suggesting that changing dietary patterns can causally lower inflammatory biomarkers. Taken together, these studies suggest that using anti-inflammatory dietary patterns is a realistic and practical strategy to help manage …

title: Triple-Laser Synergistic Etching: An Effective Strategy for Contour Error Suppression in Diamond Cutting Tool Edges
abstract: Diamond tools hold a pivotal position in ultra-precision and micro-machining within the high-tech manufacturing sector, owing to their remarkable cutting performance. However, the manufacturing precision of these tools is often affected by their inherent anisotropy. This study proposes a novel triple-laser combined etching strategy (consisting of CO2, YAG picosecond, and femtosecond lasers) to investigate methods for improving the surface quality of single-crystal diamond tools and reducing the waviness of the cutting edge. During conventional mechanical removal, the variation in hardness across different crystallographic planes of natural diamond induces uneven material removal and cleavage-induced microcracks. Meanwhile, in single-laser processing, the high dissociation energy of sp3 bonds necessitates intense localized energy input, which, coupled with anisotropic thermal expansion, generates non-uniform and significant thermal stresses. To tackle this issue, the proposed multi-laser process employs a hierarchical energy transfer mechanism. Initially, a CO2 laser provides uniform thermal pretreatment, converting the diamond surface into a highly absorptive graphitized (sp2) layer. Subsequently, a YAG picosecond laser achieves selective microstructural refinement, removing coarse graphite and curbing the propagation of microcracks. Finally, a femtosecond laser performs nanosc…

abstract: يهدف البحث الحالي الى(ا لتعرف على اثر استراتيجية شبكة الاسئلة في الفهم القرائي عند طالبات الصف الاول المتوسط ،ولتحقيق هدف البحث،اعتمد المنهج التجريبي ، وبلغت العينة( 60 ) طالبة من طالبات الصف الاول المتوسط وزعن على مجموعتين تجريبية وضابطة وكل مجموعة كانت ( 30 ) طالبة ، وكافأت الباحثة بينهما بالمتغيرات ( العمر الزمني ،ودرجات العام السابق ) وبعد التحقق من التكافؤ اعدت المستلزمات البحثية( من تحديد المادة الدراسية ،وصياغة الاهداف السلوكية ،واعداد الخطط التدريسية ،واختبار الفهم القرائي ، وللتأكد من الخصائص الاحصائية تم تطبيق الاختبار على عينة استطلاعية تكونت من ( 100 ) طالبة من ضمن مجتمع البحث وتحققت من صدقه وثباته واستخرجت معاملات الصعوبة والتمييز وفعالية البدائل ، ومن ثم طبقت تجربتها التي استمرت لفصل دراسي من يوم الاحد الموافق 19/10/2025 لغاية يوم الاحد الموافق 18/1/2026 لتطبق في نهاية التجربة اختبار الفهم القرائي وبعد جمع البيانات وتحليلها احصائيا باستخدام الاختبار التائي ظهر تفوق طالبات المجموعة التجريبية على طالبات المجموعة الضابطة . ان هدف تعلم اللغة العربية هو تعلم مهاراتها واتقانها بدرجة مقبولة بحسب المراحل الدراسية ومن ثم تزداد درجة اتقان هذه المهارات عند تقدم النرحلة الدراسية حتى الوصول الى درجة اتقان عالية تصل الى تمكن المتعلم من مَلَكة اللغة بنسبة كبيرة ، ومهارات اللغة ( الاستماع والحديث والقراءة والكتابة ) متسلسلة باهميتها اللغوية ، لذا فمن المهم جدا اتقان المتعلم مهارة اللغة جميعها عند وصوله الى المرحلة المتوسطة لاعتماد المواد الدراسية الاخرى على هذه المهارة وان اي ضعف…

title: APRENDIZAGEM BASEADA EM PROJETOS COMO ESTRATÉGIA PARA O ENSINO DE REUTILIZAÇÃO DA ÁGUA: UM RELATO DE EXPERIÊNCIA
abstract: Este estudo apresenta e analisa a utilização da Aprendizagem Baseada em Projetos (ABP) como estratégia didático-pedagógica no ensino da reutilização da água no contexto da educação superior. Trata-se de um relato de experiência de natureza qualitativa, desenvolvido no âmbito de uma disciplina de pós-graduação, no qual os discentes foram desafiados a elaborar projetos sustentáveis voltados ao reaproveitamento de recursos hídricos. Os resultados evidenciam que a ABP favorece a articulação entre teoria e prática, promove a aprendizagem significativa e contribui para o desenvolvimento de competências como pensamento crítico, resolução de problemas e responsabilidade socioambiental. Conclui-se que a metodologia se mostra adequada às demandas contemporâneas da educação, especialmente no campo da educação ambiental.

abstract: تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تحليل استراتيجية قطر الوطنية للأمن السيبراني 2024–2030، وتتبع انتقالها من نموذج يركز على حماية البنية التحتية الوطنية الحرجة إلى نموذج شامل يدمج بين الصمود السيبراني، والحوكمة والتشريعات، وبناء القدرات البشرية، وتوظيف التقنيات الناشئة، والتعاون الدولي والدبلوماسية السيبرانية في إطار متكامل. وقد اعتمدت الدراسة على المنهج الوصفي التحليلي لتحليل مكونات الاستراتيجية وركائزها، والكشف عن العلاقات المتبادلة بينها، وتقييم مدى تكاملها في تحقيق الأهداف الوطنية. وتوصلت الدراسة إلى أن الاستراتيجية القطرية تمثل نقلة نوعية من مفهوم الحماية التقليدية إلى نموذج صمود وطني متعدد الأطراف، وأن حماية البنية التحتية الوطنية الحرجة لا يمكن فصلها عن الحوكمة والقدرات البشرية والتعاون الخارجي، كما كشفت النتائج أن التعاون الدولي في الاستراتيجية يُنظر إليه بوصفه امتدادًا طبيعيًا للأمن الوطني وليس مسارًا منفصلًا عنه، وأظهرت أن الاستراتيجية تولي اهتمامًا بالغًا ببناء القدرات البشرية والوعي المجتمعي، وبالاستثمار في التقنيات الناشئة كالذكاء الاصطناعي. وأكدت النتائج أن الاستراتيجية تمثل نموذجًا متقدمًا في المنطقة العربية من حيث شموليتها وتكامل أبعادها. وخلصت الدراسة إلى مجموعة من التوصيات العملية التي يمكن أن تسهم في تعزيز فعالية الاستراتيجية الوطنية وتحقيق أهدافها على نحو أفضل، ومن أبرز هذه التوصيات: تطوير مؤشرات قياس واضحة ودقيقة لدرجة الصمود السيبراني على مستوى الدولة والقطاعات الحيوية، تمكن من التقييم الدوري للأداء وتحديد مجالات التحسين، وتوسيع نطاق تمارين الاستجابة الوطنية المشتركة وإ…

title: Distinct Modes of Quantum Information Transfer in Power–Law Long-Range Spin Networks
abstract: We identify different regimes of quantum state transfer in long-range coupled spin-12 systems, where naturally occurring power–law interactions enable rapid, high-fidelity transfer with minimal engineering. Across a broad range of interaction profiles, from effectively nearest-neighbour coupling to Coulomb interactions, we show how long-range connectivity fundamentally reshapes the mechanisms underlying information propagation within such systems. For effectively short-range interactions, transfer follows familiar ballistic transfer dynamics: an initially localised excitation spreads across many eigenmodes concentrated within the approximately linear region of the spectrum, enabling robust wavepacket motion. In contrast, increasing long-distance interactions via lowering the power–law exponent α (α=1−2) drives a striking transformation, where the initial state becomes confined to progressively fewer eigenmodes, ultimately reducing the dynamics to the coherent participation of only a few states corresponding to the highest eigenenergies. This spectral localisation gives rise to emergent long-range oscillations between distant sites, revealing a distinct—and faster—transfer mechanism arising from the intrinsic structure of long-range quantum interactions rather than from full-system engineering pathways.

Shaping power and strategic security framing: China’s Global Security Initiative in Africa, the development–security nexus, and the case of Ethiopia
abstract: This article examines widely overlooked shifts in China’s interactions with African states resulting from the all-encompassing securitization of politics under Xi Jinping. It argues that Beijing seeks to increase China’s discursive and shaping power capacities through strategic security framing, reaching out to the group of African states via the Forum on China−Africa Cooperation. The Global Security Initiative (GSI) illustrates China’s aspiration to universalize its security concepts and create an international environment that aligns with its strategic interests. Chinese academic discourse viewed Ethiopia as a critical case for exploring the practical implementation of the GSI. By analysing China’s engagement with Ethiopia, this article evaluates the potential and limits of Chinese influence − or, as China frames it, ‘shaping power’. The findings indicate that while China’s discursive power has expanded, this has not yet translated into significant political influence on the ground.

title: Physics-Guided Graph Safe Reinforcement Learning for High-Fidelity and Scalable Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow
abstract: The alternating current (AC) optimal power flow (AC-OPF) problem is crucial for efficient power system operation, yet it remains challenging due to its nonlinear, nonconvex structure and numerous operational constraints. This paper introduces a Physics-guided Graph Safe Reinforcement Learning (PGSRL) framework that provides accurate, scalable, and physically consistent solutions to AC-OPF. The proposed PGSRL framework first models the power system as a weighted graph, encoding voltage magnitudes, load demands, and transmission line impedances to capture existing spatiotemporal correlations among power system buses. A Graph Mamba encoder with selective State Space Modeling extracts spatiotemporal correlations, which are used to define the system states within a constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP). To solve this CMDP, we design a physics-guided safe Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) architecture containing twin critics and deterministic actors, guided by physics-informed reward functions that promote feasibility through penalty-based soft constraints. By interacting with a simulated power system environment, the introduced PGSRL learns optimal generator dispatch strategies in continuous action spaces while honoring AC-OPF constraints. Experimental results on six test benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of PGSRL compared with traditional numerical sol…

title: Architecture and the Limits of Experience: Spatial Apparatuses of Knowledge, Power, and the Self
abstract: This article examines the problem of experience in architectural discourse by proposing a historico-critical framework that reconceptualizes architecture as a technology of framing. Drawing on Bernard Cache’s approach to architecture as a generative system of frames and Michel Foucault’s analyses of technologies of knowledge, power, and the self, the study examines how spatial configurations produce historically specific fields of experience rather than merely accommodate them. Methodologically, the authors use Foucault’s tripartite framework of archaeology, genealogy, and problematization to develop a comparative analytical matrix applied to three spatial dispositifs: camera obscura, concentration camp, and confessional booth. Each case is analyzed through a six-part schema addressing their historical specificity, architectural diagram, regime of truth, subject formation, primary relational structure, and experiential output, followed by their micro-operational logic. Findings show that, despite their historical and functional differences, these dispositifs share a common diagrammatic structure in that they all isolate bodies, regulate regimes of contact, and generate distinct corporeal repertoires that organize perception, domination, and self-relation. By foregrounding architecture’s role in materializing the “historical a priori of possible experience,” the article argues f…

Research on the innovation path of retail business models based on the cognitive profiling of Generation Alpha
abstract: Generation Alpha, the first cohort to grow up with artificial intelligence, is expected to become the largest consumer segment in history. However, academic research on their cognitive characteristics and consumption behaviour remains limited. This study aims to construct a multi‑dimensional cognitive profile of Generation Alpha and to examine how this profile drives retail business model innovation. A structured questionnaire survey was conducted with 316 parents of Generation Alpha children in China, covering four cognitive dimensions: behavioural patterns, product preferences, social concerns, and brand acceptance. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis were used to analyse the data. The results show that Generation Alpha children exhibit moderate levels across all four cognitive dimensions. Product preference emerged as the strongest predictor of brand acceptance (β = 0.318, p < 0.001), followed by social concern (β = 0.218) and behavioural profile (β = 0.213). The model explained 31.8% of the variance in brand acceptance. These findings provide empirical support for three retail innovation pathways: product creativity enhancement, channel transformation, and communication upgrading. The study offers both theoretical contributions to generational consumer behaviour research and practical guidance for retailers seeking to engage Genera…

title: Factors Driving Sales and Retail Pricing Practices of ITC Connect: A Field-Based Case Study of Retail Execution in Osmanabad, Maharashtra
abstract: This paper reports a field-based case study of retail sales and pricing practices for ITC Connect, a slim-cigarette brand in ITC Limited’s FMCG – Cigarettes portfolio, in Osmanabad territory, Maharashtra. Drawing on primary field data collected during a sales-and-distribution internship — stock audits and visibility ratings at the top 10 outlets on each of 7 distributor-salesman (DS) routes (N = 70 outlets, 16 localities), conducted between 22 June and 1 July 2026, together with semi-structured retailer feedback recorded in a parallel visit tracker — the study examines how product availability, shelf visibility, and competitor presence jointly shape Connect’s market performance. Descriptive analysis shows an average of 4.87 Connect units per outlet (341 units total) against 7.81 units of the leading competing brand, referred to here as Stellar Shift (547 units total, singles and duos combined), with the competitor holding a stock advantage in 55 of 70 outlets (78.6%). Field price observations placed Connect’s actual retail selling price at approximately ₹25–30 against approximately ₹20 for the competitor. Pearson correlation analysis, however, found no significant inverse relationship between Connect and competitor stock levels at the outlet level (r ≈ −0.02 to −0.10, p > 0.40 in every case), indicating that the two brands’ shelf presence is not a simple zero-sum trade-off, and…

title: A Hybrid Multi-Objective Colour Recommendation Framework for Interior Wall Painting Using NSGA-II and Retail Service Integration
abstract: Selecting interior wall paint involves multiple conflicting objectives such as aesthetic colour harmony, material cost, and vendor reliability. Traditional e-commerce platforms offer fragmented services and lack integrated visualization or professional painter booking. Earlier research works mainly focused on Interactive Genetic Algorithms and automated material suggestion for 3D indoor scenes, but they did not combine colour optimization with real-world retail logistics and on-demand labour services. This paper presents a hybrid Multi-Objective Colour Recommendation System that bridges this gap. The proposed system integrates a Zomato-style paint delivery model, an Urban Company-style painter booking model, and a Policy Bazaar-style multi-brand comparison approach. Using K-Means clustering for dominant colour extraction from room photographs and NSGA-II for multi-objective optimization, the system generates Pareto-optimal recommendations that simultaneously balance colour harmony, cost, and vendor reliability. Keywords: Multi-Objective Optimization, NSGA-II, K-Means Clustering, Colour Recommendation, E-Commerce Integration, Pareto Front.
venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management

title: A Contract Management Practices Framework for Managing Supplier Complaints in Food Retail Manufacturing Organizations in Zimbabwe
abstract: This study investigates how contract management practices encompassing payment compliance, contract compliance, change-order management, and contract administration relate to supplier complaints in two Zimbabwean food retail manufacturing organizations, Baker's Inn and Lobels Pvt Ltd, using a pragmatist mixed-methods design with parallel triangulation utilizing one hundred and eighty-seven questionnaires and twelve interviews. The study addresses an under-researched African context and draws on internal complaint registers containing two hundred and ninety-six records spanning from 2022 to 2025 alongside primary survey and interview data. The findings indicate that while organizations perform relatively well in establishing formal payment periods, internal approval controls, and contractual procedures, significant weaknesses persist in compliance monitoring, payment exception resolution, supplier consultation during contract variations, and the accessibility of centralized contract records, all of which contribute significantly to supplier complaint recurrence and prolonged resolution times. The research provides practical implications for improving supply chain governance and proposes an integrated contract management framework tailored for food retail manufacturing organizations.

title: SNAP Food Purchase Restrictions and Retailer Availability: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
abstract: Abstract Introduction States have begun implementing waivers that prohibit Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits from being used to purchase selected foods and beverages. We assessed whether these restrictions were associated with changes in the availability of SNAP-authorized convenience stores, supermarkets, and superstores. Methods We analyzed repeated observations from 83,697 Census tracts from January 2025 through June 2026. Difference-in-differences models compared changes in retailer availability in states implementing waivers with concurrent changes in states without implemented waivers. Results Waiver implementation was associated with a 1.4% decline in SNAP-authorized convenience stores, equivalent to 3.0 fewer stores per 100 tracts (95% CI, −5.7 to −0.4; P=0.03), but not with a significant change in supermarkets or superstores. The largest declines in convenience stores occurred among states restricting beverages and candy (−2.2%; −4.9 stores per 100 tracts; 95% CI, −6.9 to −2.9; P<0.01). Conclusion SNAP food restrictions were associated with reduced availability of SNAP-authorized convenience stores but not supermarkets or superstores. Continued monitoring is warranted as these policies expand.

title: A compartmental modelling approach for incorporating larva source management into malaria control strategy in Zamfara State, Nigeria
[La3Br][GeS4]2: Cationic-Moiety-Guided Strategy Enables Record Birefringence and Broad Optical Window
abstract: Abstract Birefringent crystals are essential for polarization control in optical systems, yet achieving both large birefringence (Δn) and a broad transmission window from ultraviolet to infrared remains a significant challenge. Here, we synthesize a novel birefringent crystal [La3Br][GeS4]2 (LGSB) with ultrahigh birefringence and a broadband optical transparency window, where a trigonal-planar [La3Br] cationic moiety serves as a structural “puppeteer” to modulate the ordered assembly of [GeS4] tetrahedra. More notably, theoretical calculations confirm that the non-bonding S 3p in [GeS4] and the non-bonding Br 4p in [La3Br] are both aligned and spread along a consistent direction. These unique traits endow LGSB with exceptional birefringence (Δnobv. = 0.344@546 nm), surpassing currently reported sulfur-containing chalcogenide halides, even outperforming benchmark crystals YVO4 (0.230@546 nm) and TiO2 (0.300@546 nm). Meanwhile, it delivers an ultrabroad transmission range of 0.36−23.2 μm. Thus, LGSB sets a new standard for wide-bandwidth, high-anisotropy materials and shows strong prospects for multi-band optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) and advanced photonic devices.

title: KNOW-WANT TO KNOW-LEARNED STRATEGY, ACHIEVEMENT, AND RETENTION IN LEARNING THE GRAMMATICAL FUNCTIONS OF ENGLISH NOUN PHRASE AMONG SECONDARY STUDENTS IN MAKURDI, BENUE STATE
abstract: This study investigated the “Know-Want to Know-Learned Strategy, Achievement, and Retention in Learning the Grammatical Functions of English Noun Phrase among Secondary Students in Makurdi, Benue State”. Two objectives and two research questions guided the study. While two hypotheses were formulated and tested at 0.05 level of significance. Quasi experimental research design of pretest, posttest and post-posttest of non-randomized and non-equivalent experimental and control groups design was adopted. The study adopted one theoretical framework- constructivist learning theory of 1952 by Jean Piaget. The study also adopted the quasi experimental research design using pretest, treatment, posttest and post-posttest. The population of the study was 1782 SS2 students in public secondary schools in Makurdi Local Government Area of Benue State, 2025/2026 academic session. The sample size was 97 SS2 students obtained through simple random sampling technique from two intact classes of two public secondary schools in Makurdi Local Government Area, Benue State. One instrument- English Noun Phrase Achievement Test (ENPAT) was developed by the researchers and used for data collection. title: Refining the first Global Strategy for the Occupational Therapy Workforce: results from a mixed-methods survey and multimodal expert feedback
Resolving the Sensitivity–Specificity Trade‐Off in Fluorescent Probes via a Tandem‐Activatable Shielding Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT For precise tumor diagnosis, the intrinsic trade‐off between sensitivity and specificity in fluorescent probes remains a longstanding bottleneck, underscoring an urgent need for strategies to break this fundamental constraint. To address the specificity limitation, we exploited a highly polarity‐sensitive fluorescent scaffold to construct a tandem‐activatable probe, enabling sequential activation by the acidic tumor microenvironment and the angiogenic marker aminopeptidase N. Whereas the single‐locked counterpart is prone to premature activation in circulation, the tandem‐locked probe remains inactive owing to a maleamic acid‐based shielding unit and is activated only upon encountering these two tumor hallmarks. Furthermore, this shielding strategy increases probe hydrophobicity, enhancing tumor uptake and driving accumulation of released fluorophores in low‐polarity lipid droplets, where fluorescence is markedly amplified to improve imaging sensitivity. The probe exhibits rapid and specific activation across various solid tumors with minimal toxicity, thus effectively resolving the sensitivity‐specificity trade‐off in probe design for in vivo applications.

title: The strategic interplay of information sharing and encroachment: how consistent pricing alters incentives
abstract: Abstract This paper investigates the strategic interplay between supplier encroachment, pricing consistency, and information sharing in a hybrid marketplace platform with asymmetric demand information. We develop a game‐theoretic model to examine how the supplier's downstream pricing architecture reshapes the platform's vertical information‐sharing incentives. Our analysis reveals that a consistent pricing commitment creates an unexpected commitment trap: the platform withholds information because sharing enables the supplier to condition the wholesale price on realized demand and shift expected surplus upstream. Conversely, under inconsistent pricing, information sharing can become mutually beneficial by enabling demand‐responsive agency pricing, which can generate a commission‐revenue gain for the platform. We further show that the supplier can use the pricing scheme to shape the platform's information‐sharing incentives. Extension analyses confirm the robustness of these mechanisms under alternative strategic sequences, pricing rights, and competitive environments. These findings provide new insights into pricing governance and channel coordination in digital platforms.

title: Developing Arabic Listening Comprehension of University Students through Authentic Audio-Visual Materials and Metacognitive Strategy Instruction
abstract: Listening comprehension is often the least developed skill among Uzbek students of Arabic, whose training traditionally focuses on reading and the grammatical analysis of written texts. This article analyses the cognitive nature of listening, the specific difficulties that Arabic speech presents to Uzbek-speaking learners, and the methodological conditions for developing this skill at university level. Particular attention is paid to the use of authentic audio-visual materials and to metacognitive strategy instruction, which teaches learners to plan, monitor and evaluate their own listening. Criteria for selecting authentic materials by level are proposed, and a lesson cycle combining top-down and bottom-up processing with metacognitive reflection is described. The article concludes that listening should be taught as a process rather than merely tested as a product.
venue: The Journal of Interdisciplinary Human Studies

title: Cerium-Incorporated Carbon Catalysts Prepared via a Biomass–Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework Hybrid Strategy for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
abstract: Cerium (Ce)-incorporated carbon catalysts, particularly Ce catalysts with Ce–N active sites supported by carbon, have emerged as promising alternatives to noble metal-based catalysts for electrocatalyzing the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). However, most carbon-supported Ce catalysts featuring Ce–N active sites remain at the proof-of-concept stage, with challenges in synthesis, including the lack of facile synthesis strategies compatible with scalable production. Herein, we present a simple and direct method for preparing Ce-incorporated carbon catalysts by carbonizing a mixture of vital wheat gluten, a type of renewable biomass, and Ce-doped zeolitic imidazolate framework-8. The optimized catalyst exhibits a half-wave potential of 0.82 V and good stability in an alkaline electrolyte. Structural and electrochemical analyses indicate that both CeO2 nanoparticles and Ce–N moieties exist in the obtained catalyst, while the Ce–N moieties are responsible for its efficient ORR activity. A zinc-air battery based on this catalyst delivers a higher peak power density and better durability (90 h) than one based on Pt/C. These results should pave the way for the biomass-assisted synthesis of Ce-incorporated carbon catalysts for ORR, providing a foundation for future scalable production.

title: A Review of Machine Learning in Species Distribution Modeling under Climate Change in West Africa
abstract: Species distribution modelling (SDM) has become a central instrument for anticipating how biodiversity is redistributed under climate change, and machine learning now supplies most of the algorithmic capacity behind these predictions. West Africa combines high climatic exposure, dense reliance on wild biological resources, and thin biodiversity records, so the region is a demanding setting in which the strengths and weaknesses of machine learning SDMs are exposed. Scope. Peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026 were synthesised to describe how correlative SDMs, tree-based ensembles, and deep learning have been applied to West African flora, fauna, disease vectors, and agricultural pests, and to assess the treatment of data quality, model transferability, and reporting standards. Key findings. Maximum entropy modelling remains the dominant approach, yet tree-based ensembles and, more recently, deep neural networks are being adopted where occurrence volume permits. Reported discrimination is high across algorithm families, with area under the curve values frequently above 0.90, though internal validation was shown to overstate reliability when sampling bias and extrapolation into novel climates were left uncorrected. Plant studies concentrated in Benin, Togo, Nigeria, and Burkina Faso projected habitat contraction for a majority of exploited woody species, with north…

title: Prioritization of Time Management Skills in the Teaching- Learning Basic Graders Mathematics Academic Productivity
abstract: This study assessed time management strategies and the level of academic performance of Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary Schools at Madridejos District, DepEd Cebu Province Division during School Year 2025-2026, as basis for Time Management Skills Activities. This study employed descriptive-quantitative method of research. The respondents of this research were the Grade 5 Mathematics learners among the select public elementary schools in Madridejos District of Cebu Province Division during the School Year 2025 – 2026. The population has a total of 65 respondents with 10 teachers and 55 learners. The quality of Mathematics instruction is closely associated with teachers' professional competence, continuous learning, and instructional experience. Significant relationship between status of the time management strategies and the academic performance of the grade 5 mathematics learners stating that there is no significant relationship between the status of the time management strategies and the academic performance of the Mathematics learners is partially rejected. The hypothesis is rejected for the dimensions and competencies where the computed probability values are less than the 0.05 level of significance, particularly in setting boundaries in Completing Homework, Balancing Time for School Work, and Balancing Time for Playing, while it is retained f…
venue: The International Review of Multidisciplinary Research

title: SemLRA: Lightweight Robust Aggregation Against Poisoning Attacks in Semantic Federated Learning
abstract: Semantic federated learning couples task-oriented semantic communication with distributed training, reducing on-device training burden and end-to-end inference latency. However, poisoning through local data, task labels, or transmitted semantic features can degrade task performance and system reliability. We propose semantic lightweight robust aggregation (SemLRA) for an information-separated dual-server architecture. SemLRA calibrates task losses already generated during split training using the within-round median and median absolute deviation to construct bounded client reliability coefficients. These coefficients jointly reweight client- and server-side model aggregation and regulate subsequent server-side optimization. SemLRA estimates reliability without reference data, client-update inspection, or prior knowledge of the malicious-client count or fraction, while retaining FedAvg-order aggregation complexity. On CIFAR-10, SemLRA maintains accuracy close to its clean-training level under continuous attacks, exceeding the strongest competing defense in mean final-stage accuracy by 3.77 percentage points under label flipping. Under burst attacks, SemLRA provides the strongest accuracy retention across all evaluated scenarios. Measured training runtime shows negligible additional overhead.

title: Robust PD-Type Iterative Learning Fault-Tolerant Control for Discrete Systems with Polytopic Uncertainties and Actuator Faults
abstract: For a class of discrete systems with polytopic uncertainties and actuator faults, a robust PD-type iterative learning fault-tolerant control scheme is investigated in this article. By providing a two-dimensional analysis of the learning process, the fault system of a repetitive nature is equivalently converted into an uncertain linear repetitive process. Additionally, employing repetitive process stability theory, new sufficient conditions with less conservatism for the robust stability of the designed fault-tolerant controller are derived in terms of linear matrix inequality constraints. The controller gain matrices are exactly given as well. Finally, simulation results of an industrial SCARA robot demonstrate the efficiency and feasibility of the proposed strategy in comparison to the developed robust P-type iterative learning fault-tolerant control strategy.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Neural Networks for Latent-Driven Non-Gaussian Outputs
abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) is essential for reliable predictions in artificial neural networks when latent sources of randomness produce non-Gaussian outputs for a given deterministic input. We propose UQ-ANN, a data-driven framework composed of two coupled subnetworks. The first subnetwork contains two feedforward neural networks: ANN1 predicts the conditional mean and ANN2 the conditional covariance of a reduced representation obtained by principal component analysis (PCA) of the outputs. The second subnetwork is an analytical stochastic generator and requires no training. It is based on a sparse Gaussian kernel density estimator (GKDE) constructed by adaptive clustering. The sparsification replaces the kernels associated with the training points by a reduced set of cluster-based kernels, while third- and fourth-moment descriptors are included in the merging criterion to preserve non-Gaussian features. Independent realizations in the reduced space are then generated, transformed to reproduce the conditional mean and covariance predicted by the first subnetwork, and mapped back to the original output space. They provide conditional statistics, conditional probability density functions, and conditional prediction intervals. A marginal log-density diagnostic is also used to assess the stochastic approximation. Numerical tests on synthetic datasets evaluate the sparse GKDE, …

title: Robust Model Predictive Control of a Drum Boiler with Online Uncertainty Estimation
abstract: In drum boiler control, model predictive control can provide accurate tracking under constraints, but residual model uncertainty still causes safety violations when parameters drift. Purpose. The study developed a robust model predictive controller for a drum boiler in which the safety margin is adjusted online according to the uncertainty level. Methods. А Takagi—Sugeno model with recursive least squares parameter adaptation described the nonlinear plant. Uncertainty was estimated from two sources: the covariance of the identified parameters and a sliding window of prediction errors. The combined estimate tightened output constraints and adjusted control smoothing. The robust layer does not require robust invariant set computation. Results. Numerical experiments on a drum boiler model compared four controller configurations during a 3000-step scenario with three phases of parameter drift. The configuration that combined model adaptation with the robust layer reduced the integral absolute error by 58.3 percent and reduced the number of constraint violations by 47.8 percent relative to the nominal controller. The maximum violation magnitude decreased by 33.8 percent. The configuration with the robust layer alone achieved the smallest number of violations, although it produced less accurate tracking. The average computation time per control step was 2.6 ms. Practical relevance. T…

title: A picture fuzzy SWARA–VIKOR framework for evaluating drone-swarm navigation and mission-coordination strategies under uncertainty
LoGicAl: Local ancestry and genotype calling uncertainty-aware ancestry-specific allele frequency estimation from admixed samples
abstract: Abstract Motivation In admixed groups, it is of interest to estimate allele frequencies of their ancestral contributing populations. These ancestry-specific allele frequencies inform genetic drivers of disease etiologies, facilitate genome-wide association study interpretations, enhance polygenic risk prediction and portability, and provide insights into demographic history. Their estimation leverages inferred locus-specific ancestry background, i.e., local ancestry, generated by tools like RFMix. However, existing estimation methods lose accuracy and incur biases by failing to model uncertainty from upstream local ancestry inference and genotype calling. Results Here, we introduce LoGicAl, a novel likelihood-based method for estimating ancestry-specific allele frequencies from admixed samples, simultaneously accommodating uncertainty from ancestry calling, genotyping, and statistical phasing. We demonstrate that modeling these uncertainties substantially reduces estimation errors, resulting in superior accuracy for both sequence-based and array-based genotyping with different levels of local ancestry inference quality. By integrating an accelerated fixed-point algorithm, LoGicAl achieves high scalability and enhanced computational efficiency compared with existing approaches. Applying LoGicAl to admixed cohorts in the 1000 Genomes Project, we illustrate the benefits of local-a…

title: Gausplat: disentangled geometry–appearance–uncertainty latent representation for generalizable novel view synthesis
Web Phishing Detection Using a Modified Spider Monkey Optimization Algorithm
abstract: In today's digital age, technology is both a powerful tool and a potential threat, with its widespread adoption bringing significant advancements as well as new vulnerabilities. As we increasingly rely on digital solutions for everyday tasks, the importance of safeguarding against cyber threats has become paramount. This is particularly true in the context of web security, where cybercriminals are continuously developing more sophisticated methods to exploit online systems. Given the increasing sophistication and frequency of phishing attacks, traditional phishing detection methods remain necessary. However, more advanced methods are needed to detect new attacks. This study presents a web phishing detection approach using machine learning (ML) algorithms and an enhanced feature selection (FS) through the modified Spider Monkey Optimization (SMO) algorithm. The SMO algorithm was modified by adding an effective crossover function to improve the algorithm's performance. The study employs Mendeley phishing datasets containing features extracted from both phishing and legitimate web pages. In binary classification, the proposed detection model consistently demonstrated strong performance using XGBoost, LightGBM, and Random Forest.

Multi-Objective Distributed Operating Room Scheduling in Collaborative Hospital Networks: Balancing Operating Costs, Patient Deterioration, and Patient Utility
abstract: Collaborative hospital networks are hospital groups that collaborate to provide healthcare services and share medical resources. They are an important part of the accessibility and efficiency of healthcare delivery. Nevertheless, existing research pays limited attention to multi-hospital scenarios. Furthermore, most studies adopt optimization objectives from the perspective of healthcare providers rather than prioritizing patient-centered service quality. Accordingly, this paper investigates the multi-objective distributed operating room scheduling problem (MDORSP), with the objectives of simultaneously minimizing operating costs and patient deterioration and maximizing patient utility. A multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming model is formulated for the MDORSP. Within this model, to embed patient-centered healthcare considerations, heterogeneous patient preferences for surgeons of varying professional qualifications are quantified based on random utility theory. To tackle this NP-hard MDORSP, a problem-tailored multi-objective evolutionary algorithm is developed. It incorporates priority-based chromosome representation, a heuristic initialization strategy, custom decoding and repair mechanisms, and a refined selection strategy. Extensive computational experiments show that the proposed algorithm obtains higher HV values than TLMOVNS on all benchmark instances and sur…

title: An Adaptive Weighted Interpretable Multi-Scale CNN Model for Multi-Class Skin Lesion Classification
abstract: Health issues are among the major concerns for people nowadays. Cancer remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide, and many are suffering from it. Out of these, skin cancer is also one of its kind and the deadliest. According to estimates, the number of new melanoma cases has surged in recent years, and the death rate from these instances has also sharply increased. By 2040, the number of melanoma cases will have sharply increased if this trend continues. So, finding and diagnosing it in the earliest stage is one of the most powerful and best ways to improve a skin cancer patient’s chance of survival. It is also essential to determine the type of cancer to ensure effective treatment. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has shown remarkable progress in medical image analysis, especially in Machine Learning and Deep Learning, for detecting and classifying skin cancer types. There are many revolutionary changes with the CNN models. Even though CNNs have become popular, these networks are called black boxes because we are unsure where the models focus in input images.These results are insufficient for medical practitioners to confirm it.Therefore, we require additional information on the model's explainability. Visual Interpretability is one of the techniques we used to address this issue. Grad-CAM is one of the XAI tools for visualizing where a CNN Network focuses. In this …
