Some Criticisms and Policy Recommendations Regarding the Crypto Ecosystem: Innovative Financial Products and Services
abstract: The decentralized nature of the bitcoin ecosystem, in contrast to traditional banking techniques, attracts attention due to the advantages of speed and flexibility offered by digital technology. This study examines the possible effects of cryptocurrencies and cutting-edge financial technology on economic development. We tried to highlight the need for rules that enable innovative financial services and products while simultaneously protecting investors and consumers to ensure growth of the cryptocurrency ecosystem. The study attempts to provide policy makers with a roadmap for regulating cryptocurrency assets. In this context, it seems that there is a need for common regulatory standards at global level and that crypto assets require monitoring in terms of taxation and the fight against money laundering and the financing of terrorism. To maintain a sustainable crypto ecosystem, nations should also shape public-private sector and university alliances, entrepreneurial incentives, technology transfer offices, incubation centers, training programs, and awareness-raising initiatives.

title: TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT OF SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN NIGER STATE, NIGERIA
abstract: This study examined transparency and accountability in the financial management of secondary schools in Niger State, Nigeria. The study investigated how transparency and accountability influence effective utilization of financial resources in secondary school administration. The research adopted a descriptive survey design involving principals, vice-principals, bursars, and teachers from selected secondary schools in Niger State. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Findings revealed that transparency in financial reporting, regular auditing, stakeholder participation, and accountability mechanisms significantly improve financial management practices in schools. The study further established that inadequate monitoring, poor record keeping, political interference, and insufficient financial training remain major challenges affecting accountability in school finance management. The study concluded that effective financial management in secondary schools depends largely on transparent procedures and accountability systems. Recommendations include regular auditing, capacity building for school administrators, and stronger government oversight of school finances.
venue: International Journal of Business Economics and Management Science

title: Advanced Imaging of the Right Heart and Pulmonary Circulation: The Role of Echocardiography and Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
abstract: Echocardiography and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) have substantially advanced the non-invasive evaluation of the right heart and pulmonary circulation. This review provides a comprehensive overview of contemporary and emerging applications of these modalities across nine selected, clinically relevant right-heart and pulmonary vascular disorders including pulmonary arterial hypertension, pulmonary embolism, and more. We summarize established diagnostic criteria and prognostic parameters derived from both modalities, highlighting the complementary roles of echocardiography—as the first-line, real-time assessment tool—and CMR, which provides the reference standard for right ventricular volumetry, tissue characterization via late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and parametric mapping, and quantitative flow assessment. Emerging techniques, including speckle-tracking and feature-tracking strain imaging, four-dimensional flow CMR, exercise CMR, and hybrid PET/MRI, are discussed with respect to their current evidence base and potential for integration into clinical practice. The potential of artificial intelligence-assisted image analysis to enhance diagnostic efficiency is also addressed. A multimodality imaging strategy, tailored to the clinical context, represents the current standard of care in right heart disease.

title: Finite-Time Fault Detection for Nonlinear Delayed Systems with Sensor Saturation Constraints Under the Token Bucket Protocol with Deterministic Transmission
Board characteristics and financial misconduct
abstract: This paper investigates how three features of board structure relate to financial reporting misconduct in China. The analysis covers 63,650 firm-year observations for A-share companies between 2000 and 2025 and considers the proportion of independent directors, the combination of the CEO and board-chair positions, and female representation on the board. Financial restatement serves as the observable measure of misconduct. The estimates show that CEO duality is associated with fewer restatements. Board independence also has a negative coefficient, although the association weakens and loses statistical significance when the other board attributes are included. Female board representation has the most stable result: firms with more female directors have a significantly lower probability of restatement. Additional tests indicate that ownership type moderates the association with CEO duality but not the associations with board independence or female representation. These results show that board attributes differ in their relation to reporting outcomes and that the consequences of leadership structure depend on institutional context.
venue: Journal of Applied Economics and Policy Studies

title: Beyond Financial Health: Community Pharmacy Sustainability and Access to Affordable Medicines
abstract: Community pharmacies must remain financially viable without weakening access to affordable medicines. This public commentary examines Panga and Galvez's survey of financial sustainability practices among small and medium-scale pharmacies in Naga City. The study provides useful local evidence on cost optimization, customer needs, inventory management, staffing shortages, drug costs, and regulatory requirements. Its conclusions, however, are based on employee perceptions rather than verified financial and patient-access outcomes. Interpretation is further limited by unclear establishment-level sampling, unequal respondent access to financial information, and incomplete reporting of inferential statistics. Future research should treat the pharmacy as the principal unit of analysis and pair objective financial indicators with stockouts, prescription fulfillment, generic availability, and medicine affordability. This approach would provide stronger evidence for policies that support business continuity and equitable access to medicines.
venue: International Journal of Sustainable and Integrated Studies

title: Did Congress Trade Ahead of the 2026 Iran War? Disclosure Delays and the Value of Early Entry
abstract: Did Congress trade ahead of the 2026 Iran War? We examine 135 disclosed transactions made by members of Congress in ten geopolitically exposed industries during the escalation. Members traded heavily in industries that subsequently rose, and congressional trading volume peaked roughly two months before public attention, but they earned no first-mover advantage. We compare portfolios that track congressional transactions at trade dates against portfolios entering at public disclosure dates. Entering positions at transaction dates offers no tangible edge: Under member-clustered inference, the disclosure delay advantage, trade timing, and any committee premium are indistinguishable from zero. Members of the Armed Services and Intelligence committees show no return edge over other members. The Senate result reduces to four trades by three senators, of which three timely oil purchases supply the bulk of the advantage. The two exceptions are purchases in positively exposed industries, which earned a 7.28% abnormal return over the disclosure window across seven members, and marginally significant sales in the negatively exposed industries. Neither can be separated from informed reading of public escalation signals. Despite intense media scrutiny of congressional trading during the escalation, we find no evidence sufficient to attribute these returns to private information.
venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management

title: Technology Investment Intensity and Financial Performance of Islamic Banks in Indonesia
abstract: Financial performance in Islamic banks is influenced not only by financing structures but also by banks’ ability to develop technological capabilities that strengthen information management, monitoring, and financing risk management. This study examines the effects of musharakah, mudarabah, murabaha, ijarah, and istisna financing on Islamic banks’ financial performance and investigates the role of Technology Investment Intensity (TII) as a mediating mechanism in profit-sharing financing. The study employs an unbalanced panel dataset comprising 120 bank-year observations from 10 Islamic commercial banks in Indonesia over 2012–2022. Financial performance is proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), while TII is measured as the ratio of capital expenditure to total assets. Panel data regression with bank-specific and year fixed effects is employed, while mediation effects are assessed through indirect effects using 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. The results show that musharakah, murabaha, and ijarah financing have positive and significant effects on ROA, whereas mudarabah and istisna financing have no significant direct effects. Musharakah and mudarabah financing positively and significantly affect TII, which positively and significantly affects ROA. TII does not mediate the musharakah ROA relationship but significantly mediates the mudarabah–ROA relationship. These findings indicat…

title: Indigenous Media Ecologies: Ritual Communication and Knowledge Transmission in the Nyishi Community of Arunachal Pradesh
abstract: This study examines the traditional communication and knowledge systems of the Nyishi tribe in East Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh, India, through media ecology and ritual communication theory. Drawing on 6 months of critical ethnographic fieldwork—comprising 30 semi-structured interviews, six focus groups and sustained participant observation—the research analyses how the community encodes and transmits traditional ecological knowledge (TEK) through oral traditions, ritual performance and symbolic networks. Data were analysed using NVivo 14, following Braun and Clarke’s (2006, Qualitative Research in Psychology, 3 , 2, 77–101) reflexive thematic analysis protocol, producing three master themes from 147 initial codes. Findings reveal resilient non-technological media ecologies that preserve environmental knowledge while adapting to the pressures of digital convergence and infrastructural modernisation. The study argues that Nyishi communication systems constitute subaltern counter-publics that challenge technological determinism in media theory and advance the decolonisation of communication studies. By centring a South Asian indigenous context, the article expands media ecology beyond its predominantly Western, technology-centric applications.

title: Construction of Witness Standardization on Sharia Financing Deeds in Sharia Financial Institutions within Tasikmalaya City Region
abstract: This study addresses the critical challenge of legal uncertainty in Sharia financing deeds by proposing a transformative framework based on witness standardization. The research aims to construct a standardized model for witness requirements in Sharia financing contracts within Sharia financial institutions in the Tasikmalaya City region. Utilizing a qualitative case study methodology with a normative-empirical approach, data was collected through in-depth interviews, document analysis, and focus group discussions with Sharia financial institution managers, notaries, and relevant stakeholders in Tasikmalaya City. The findings culminate in a four-stage Witness Standardization Framework (WSF), comprising Selection, Verification, Competence, and Documentation. This model shifts the paradigm from informal and inconsistent witnessing practices to a structured, legally robust, and Sharia-compliant witnessing system. The study concludes that systematically applying witness standardization is essential for enhancing legal certainty, reducing dispute risks, and strengthening the integrity of Sharia financing deeds. This framework offers a practical blueprint for Sharia financial institutions, notaries, and regulators in improving the legal quality and accountability of Sharia financing transactions.

Amanah-Based Financial Governance: Readiness for Digital Accountability among Pesantren in the Former Banyumas Residency
abstract: Introduction: Pesantren managed educational fees, philanthropic funds, government assistance, and business-unit revenues with distinct mandates, beneficiaries, and accountability obligations; however, previous studies tended to separate amanah as an ethical principle from digitalisation as a technical issue. This study aimed to explain how amanah was institutionalised in financial governance and how it shaped institutional readiness for digital accountability among four pesantren in the former Banyumas Residency. Methods: The study employed a post-positivist qualitative approach and a collective case-study design. Cases were purposively selected to maximise governance variation. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, limited observation, and document review, then analysed thematically through within-case, cross-case, and normative-empirical analyses. Results: The findings revealed three governance configurations: centralised leadership, treasurer-based management, and collective governance. Institutional readiness was stronger where fund status and purposes were explicit, authority was clearly allocated, transaction records were traceable, and reporting was integrated; it remained limited where recordkeeping and application use were partial and fragmented. Conclusion and suggestion: The study concluded that readiness for digital accountability depended primaril…

Tax Avoidance and Corporate Governance: Mapping the Intellectual Structure, Emerging Trends, and Future Research Frontiers
abstract: In spite of a considerable amount of attention being paid to the interaction between tax avoidance and corporate governance across the globe, this study aims to provide a detailed bibliometric evaluation concerning the productivity, performance, and intellectual structure of scientific production on tax avoidance and corporate governance. All data used in this study were gathered from the Scopus database using documents published from 2006 to 2025, which made the total number of documents reach 295. In this study, both VOSviewer and Biblioshiny were used to conduct a bibliometric analysis of this corpus. The findings of this research revealed a remarkable annual increase in publication rate equal to 25.77%, showing an increasing trend in academic research concerning the role of corporate governance in shaping corporate tax avoidance behavior. The most productive journals that have been identified as the main sources are Accounting and Finance, Journal of Corporate Finance, Journal of risk and financial management and Cogent Business and Management. Moreover, Richardson G. and Taylor G. have been found to be the most productive authors in terms of the number of documents published in this field, whereas China, Indonesia, and the USA are the leading countries in terms of the number of affiliated documents. There are seven major clusters discovered based on co-occurrence analysis,…

A Comparative Analysis of Open Data Portals: The Cases of Ordu and Tampere
abstract: Open data has become an important component of contemporary urban governance, contributing to transparency, accountability, and data-driven decision-making. However, the effectiveness of open data systems depends not only on data availability but also on interoperability, standardization, and the ability of data infrastructures to support reuse and integration within urban service ecosystems. In this context, the distinction between data publication and service-oriented data governance is increasingly relevant in assessing municipal digital maturity. This study presents a comparative analysis of the open data portals of Ordu Metropolitan Municipality in Türkiye and the City of Tampere in Finland, representing different institutional and digital governance capacities. The research employs a qualitative comparative framework focusing on dataset composition, format standardization, update frequency, interoperability mechanisms, metadata structures, and user-oriented functionalities, with particular attention to spatial data infrastructures and GIS-based applications. The findings indicate that Ordu’s open data portal is primarily characterized by a data publication-oriented structure, relying largely on static formats and offering limited interoperability, despite a relatively high number of datasets. In contrast, Tampere demonstrates a more integrated and service-oriented data ec…

title: Diseño e Implementación de un Protocolo de Preparación y Sensibilización Escolar para la Reincorporación Integral de Alumnos en Duelo
abstract: El artículo documenta el diseño y la implementación de un Protocolo de Preparación y Sensibilización Escolar, cuyo propósito es facilitar la reincorporación integral de alumnos en duelo, promoviendo su bienestar emocional y su adaptación al entorno escolar. Se utiliza un enfoque mixto; análisis estadístico cuantitativo para la descripción del problema y el enfoque cualitativo con orientación investigación-acción, para el diseño de la intervención. El muestreo es intencionado o por conveniencia; la colaboración es voluntaria, y en todo momento se garantiza el bienestar emocional y el respeto a la privacidad de los participantes. El proyecto contó con la participación de los miembros de la comunidad educativa de las escuelas primarias estatales pertenecientes a la Zona Escolar 02 de Gómez Palacio, Durango, quienes son los protagonistas del proceso de análisis, diseño e implementación del protocolo de preparación y sensibilización escolar: directores, docentes, alumnos y padres de familia; se buscó integrar diferentes voces y perspectivas, para que el protocolo reflejara experiencias reales. Con base en el análisis sistemático de los datos estadísticos, resultado de la aplicación de encuestas al personal docente y directivos, se define la necesidad imperante de un protocolo de reincorporación escolar en las escuelas, que oriente la incorporación de los alumnos que recién han exper…

title: Comprehensive budget performance management reform, budget deviation, and local governance effectiveness: an empirical study
Air Quality and Emission Trends Following the 2021 Environmental Code Reform in Kazakhstan Across Regions and Industrial Sectors
abstract: The 2021 revision of the Environmental Code of the Republic of Kazakhstan was introduced to align with the World Health Organization (WHO) air quality guidelines and the national carbon neutrality strategy for 2060. The revised Code reflects a transformation of environmental governance, including the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-oriented policy framework, the tightening of air quality standards, the strengthening of environmental monitoring, the expansion of region-specific regulatory mechanisms, and increased emphasis on the implementation of Best Available Techniques (BAT). This study presents a comparative analysis of atmospheric pollutant emissions across regions and industrial sectors, including major pollutants such as PM2.5, SO2, CO, NO2, and others. The analysis considers ambient air quality indicators, pollutant composition, the chemical composition of atmospheric precipitation, regional industrial profiles, and changes observed during the reform period. The findings demonstrate substantial regional and pollutant-specific heterogeneity in air-quality dynamics. Although stationary-source emissions decreased by approximately 5–6% between 2021 and 2024, no statistically significant improvement in the assessed ambient-air indicators was identified between 2021 and 2025. Persistent high pollution levels and episodic particulate matter exceedances remained evi…

title: El error de tipo y el error de prohibición en el Código Orgánico Integral Penal tras la reforma de 2019
abstract: El artículo analizó el error de tipo y el error de prohibición en el Código Orgánico Integral Penal ecuatoriano, incorporados de forma expresa en los artículos 28.1 y 35.1 por la reforma de 2019. Se desarrolló un estudio cualitativo de tipo jurídico-dogmático, basado en el análisis exegético y sistemático de esas disposiciones y en doctrina publicada en revistas arbitradas de Ecuador, Colombia, Chile, Perú y España. El análisis mostró que el error de tipo recae sobre los elementos objetivos del tipo y excluye el dolo, de modo que el invencible elimina la responsabilidad y el vencible da lugar a la modalidad culposa cuando existe; el error de prohibición recae sobre el conocimiento de la ilicitud y se ubica en la culpabilidad, de modo que el invencible exime de responsabilidad y el vencible atenúa la pena. Se concluye que la delimitación entre ambos errores exige criterios de vencibilidad explícitos.

title: Household Electricity Consumption Analytics using Google Cloud Platform Services
abstract: The increasing consumption of electrical energy at the household level has created a need for efficient monitoring and analytical systems capable of identifying consumption pat-terns and supporting energy management. Conventional electric-ity monitoring approaches often provide limited analytical capa-bilities and primarily present periodic consumption summaries. This paper proposes a cloud-based Household Electricity Con-sumption Analytics System using Google Cloud Platform (GCP) services. The proposed architecture integrates Google Cloud Storage for scalable data storage, Google Cloud Functions for automated data processing, Google BigQuery for analytical pro-cessing, and Looker Studio for interactive visualization. House-hold electricity consumption data in CSV format is uploaded to cloud storage and processed through an Extract, Transform, and Load (ETL) pipeline. The data is validated, cleaned, transformed, and subsequently loaded into BigQuery for SQL-based analysis. The system focuses on identifying consumption trends, peak usage periods, monthly consumption, and estimated electricity costs. The analytical results are presented through interactive dashboards to improve the understanding of electricity usage. The proposed approach provides a scalable and cloud-oriented framework for household electricity analytics and can serve as a foundation for future extensions involv…

title: Comparative Assessment of Uncertainty Representation Methods for Bilevel Stochastic Wind Power Investment
abstract: In this paper, we address the problem of optimal investment in wind power within an existing transmission network, in an organized electricity market environment. A wind power investor decides which wind power units to install, as well as their size and loca-tion, with the objective of maximizing the investor's expected annual profit. The problem is formulated as a bilevel stochastic model, whose upper level describes the investment decisions and whose lower level represents market clearing. The bilevel model is succes-sively reformulated into a Mathematical Program with Equilibrium Constraints (MPEC) and then into an equivalent Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) problem. The main contribution of this paper is the systematic comparison of two methods for repre-senting the two sources of uncertainty considered in the model, namely electricity demand and wind power availability: (i) scenarios constructed from load and wind duration curves and (ii) correlated scenarios obtained through K-means clustering. Both methods are evaluated within a common optimization framework, with the same network, investment budget, candidate buses, and deterministic system data, enabling a controlled assessment of how the adopted uncertainty representation affects the resulting investment and network outcomes. The analysis considers a 3-bus verification system and the IEEE 24-bus Reliability Tes…

title: Game-Theoretic Reinforcement Learning based Topology-Agnostic Defense for Virtual Power Plants
abstract: The rapid proliferation of distributed energy resources (DERs) aggregated by virtual power plants (VPPs) elevates cybersecurity risk by expanding the attack surface. A coordinated cyberattack has the potential to disrupt distribution-system, bulk-system, and market operations. Existing cyberphysical defense strategies largely assume access to grid network models and operating conditions, which may not be available to third-party aggregators. This paper proposes a novel hybrid, perturbation-based cyber-physical defense for VPP-operated DERs that blends game-theoretic planning with model-free reinforcement learning (RL) under a Bayesian belief-update framework. Topology agnosticism is defined from the VPP information and implementation perspective: the VPP does not require access to the feeder topology, line parameters, switching configuration, or full system state. This work advances the state of the art through three contributions: (1) a multi-output Gaussian process with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for discrete attacker-type inference, probability of detection, and confidence of detection for modeling the belief distribution; (2) moment-matched Gaussian propagation of posterior beliefs across episodes; and (3) an RL policy that adaptively integrates Stackelberg leader (VPP) actions with exploration. Furthermore, we establish equilibrium existence and derive an episode-level closed…

title: An Adaptive Cyber-Resilient Framework for P2P Energy Trading under Optimal Stealthy Attacks
abstract: The increasing adoption of peer to peer energy trading has enabled prosumers to actively participate in decentralized energy markets. However, the growing dependence of P2P energy markets on communication infrastructures and distributed coordination mechanisms introduces an expanded cyberattack surface, enabling sophisticated adversaries to manipulate market interactions while remaining concealed from conventional detection mechanisms. This paper first designs an optimal stealthy attack that maximizes economic disruption of the MicroGrids, while preserving the apparent convergence characteristics of the ADMM based market-clearing process. To detect such attacks, a Mahalanobis Boosting detector is developed using market layer features to effectively capture inter feature dependencies and distinguish compromised updates from normal market operation. An adaptive rho based mitigation strategy is then introduced to limit the propagation of compromised information and restore robust market operation once an attack is flagged. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through comprehensive case studies, achieving an attack detection accuracy of 98.49% while the proposed mitigation strategy reduces the operating cost by approximately 18.43% compared to the unmitigated attack case. The proposed approach provides a practical pathway toward trustworthy and cyber-secure d…

High Expression of Aurora Kinase A (AURKA) is Associated with Aggressive Tumor Biology and Therapeutic Response in ER+/HER2− Breast Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Aurora kinase A ( AURKA ) is a serine/threonine kinase that regulates mitotic entry, spindle assembly, and chromosomal segregation. AURKA overexpression has been linked to multiple malignancies. The biological and clinical significance of AURKA expression within estrogen receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (ER+/HER2−) breast cancer has yet to be fully elucidated. Methods A total of 8896 patients were analyzed across bulk transcriptomic datasets. Single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were also analyzed. ER+/HER2− tumors were divided into AURKA -high or -low groups according to the median AURKA expression within each cohort. Results AURKA expression was associated with Nottingham histological grade and Ki-67 expression ( p < 0.001) and enrichment of cell cycle-related pathways across The Cancer Genome Atlas, Molecular Taxonomy of Breast Cancer International Consortium, and Sweden Cancerome Analysis Network-Breast datasets (all false discovery rate <0.01; normalized enrichment score >2). AURKA expression was associated with genomic instability, increased mutational burden and enhanced DNA repair-related genes (all p < 0.001) and with increased infiltration of type 1 and 2 T-helper cells, M1-like macrophages, and total macrophages (all p < 0.001). Conversely, AURKA -low tumors were enriched for epithelial mesenchymal transition, my…

title: Power-law scaling of mitotic spindles with genome sizes across eukaryotes is driven by chromosome crowding
abstract: Abstract Genome size varies more than 10,000-fold across eukaryotes, yet how the mitotic spindle adapts to this range remains unknown. Here we show that metaphase plate width scales with genome size following a power law with an exponent of ~1/3 across eukaryotes. Comparative analysis and a physical model reveal that this scaling arises from the linear relationship between total chromosome volume and genome size, with chromosome number playing a secondary role. The same scaling holds across ploidy levels in cell lines, patient-derived cancer organoids and meiotic systems. Physical model and acute spindle compression demonstrate that chromosome crowding generates interchromosome pushing forces that set metaphase plate width. By contrast, spindle length is regulated by microtubule dynamics, cytoplasmic forces and cell size, indicating that spindle dimensions are independently controlled. The revealed scaling law provides a robust mechanism for accommodating large genomic variation and offers insight into the evolution of open mitosis and mitotic cell rounding, as well as polyploidy tolerance in tumours and during speciation.

title: Assessing the role of social media marketing in shaping brand awareness and loyalty: a study of customer satisfaction in the Indian telecom market
abstract: Purpose This research investigates how social media (SM) marketing activities influence brand loyalty and brand awareness in India’s telecommunications industry. It also aims to explore the role of customer satisfaction as a mediator in the relationship between SM marketing efforts and brand outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative method based on the stimulus–organism–response (S–O–R) theory was employed for this study. A quantitative research approach was utilized, employing a structured questionnaire distributed to 209 SM users of telecommunications service providers in the Tricity area of India (comprising Mohali, Chandigarh and Panchkula). The data were examined using partial least squares structural equation modeling via SmartPLS. Findings The findings indicate that SM marketing activities significantly enhance both brand loyalty and brand awareness. Furthermore, customer satisfaction serves an important mediating role, strengthening the connection between SM marketing and brand outcomes. The research underscores that active consumer engagement on SM platforms fosters improved brand perceptions. For telecom managers, these findings suggest that SM strategies focused on responsive, service-oriented customer interaction – rather than promotional content alone – are likely to be the most effective route to building both brand loyalty and brand awareness. Original…

title: Rethinking municipal electricity in South Africa: Rooftop solar PV, revenue and just energy transitions in the City of Johannesburg<sup> </sup>
abstract: South Africa’s deepening electricity crisis, marked by persistent load-shedding and escalating tariffs, has accelerated private solar photovoltaic (PV) installations. This rapid transition has raised concerns about municipal revenue erosion, cross-subsidisation and energy inequality. The City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality (CoJ) is at the centre of this transition, and is grappling with the implications for its business model and how private solar PV can be leveraged to support a just energy transition. This paper is written from the perspective of City officials, and examines the extent of rooftop solar PV and its impact on municipal revenue, finances and grid management. The paper draws on municipal records, internal meetings and reports, and an industry dataset. The analysis reveals that official records substantially underrepresent solar PV installations in the CoJ. Despite the concern that private solar PV erodes revenue, this analysis highlights that technical losses, load-shedding, and customer non-payment have a far greater financial impact. This paper challenges the assumption that distributed power undermines social justice, and rather points to the need for tariff reform, away from volumetric sales towards fixed network charges, to stabilise municipal finances. Rather than framing distributed solar PV as inherently threatening to municipal revenue and soci…
venue: Journal of Energy in Southern Africa

title: Determinants of foreign exchange reserve and exchange market pressure in Ethiopia
abstract: Purpose During the period from 1995 to 2024, Ethiopia experienced a declining trend in foreign exchange reserve adequacy and increase in exchange market pressure. Foreign reserve remained below three months of import coverage on average and the county’s currency gradually lost its value. This study aims at analyzing the determinants of foreign reserve and exchange market pressure in Ethiopia, emphasizing the effect of foreign price, domestic policy and international capital inflows in the form of remittance and foreign direct investment (FDI), which are not considered in the earlier works in case of Ethiopia. Design/methodology/approach Theories on motives for foreign exchange reserve holding and monetary approach to balance of payment are used as a theoretical basis. Seemingly unrelated regression model, justified by cross equation residual correlation, is applied to annual data from 1995 to 2024. Findings The result from seemingly unrelated regression shows that foreign reserve is affected by GDP, remittance, domestic credit and foreign price. Foreign reserve increases with a rise in GDP and remittance but declines with increase in domestic credit and foreign price. Exchange market pressure is affected by GDP, net export and domestic credit. Increase in GDP and net export reduces exchange market pressure while increase in domestic credit increases it. The results remain robus…
venue: Journal of Economic and Administrative Sciences

title: Change-point analysis of Altman Z″-score dynamics: structural regime detection in a capital-intensive emerging market firm
abstract: This study proposes an integrated quantitative framework combining the Altman Z″-score with Binary Segmentation change-point detection—using a least squares cost function—to examine corporate financial distress as a dynamic regime-shifting process amenable to structural analysis, addressing the gap in longitudinal distress monitoring for capital-intensive firms in emerging markets. The framework formally minimizes a piecewise least squares cost function over a financial time series of 56 consecutive quarterly observations (2011Q1–2024Q4), identifying endogenous breakpoints that delimit regimes internally homogeneous in mean level of financial deterioration. Because these breakpoints are selected endogenously, standard Chow test critical values are complemented by a supremum-Wald test accounting for the search over candidate break locations, which confirms the presence of at least one genuine structural break (sup-Wald = 38.61, exceeding the 1% asymptotic critical value). The framework is applied to Telefónica del Perú S. A. A.—a publicly listed capital-intensive telecommunications operator that filed a request to enter insolvency restructuring proceedings in February 2025—providing an empirical case with a formally observable ex post validation event. Five endogenously detected breakpoints—located at 2013Q2, 2014Q3, 2018Q2, 2020Q4, and 2022Q1—delimit six structurally differenti…
venue: Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics

title: AHAT-Fin: an adaptive hybrid attention and market-state-aware framework for financial time-series forecasting
abstract: Accurate financial time-series forecasting is essential for quantitative investment. However, existing methods often perform inadequately when handling the complex dynamics of financial data, including non-stationarity, volatility clustering, and market regime transitions. These characteristics can adversely affect both forecasting accuracy and the quality of investment decisions. To address these challenges, this study develops AHAT-Fin, an improved Transformer-based forecasting framework that integrates adaptive hybrid attention with market state perception. AHAT-Fin integrates dual-path adaptive hybrid attention, generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH)-based dynamic volatility adjustment, and hierarchical market-state perception based on multi-window long short-term memory (LSTM) networks. The model is evaluated using daily trading data from seven representative U.S. stocks and selected constituents of the CSI 300 Index. The results show that AHAT-Fin generally outperforms the benchmark models, achieving an average reduction of 20.2% in mean squared error, an 8.4% improvement in directional accuracy, and a 63.4% increase in the Sharpe ratio. Module-level evaluation further confirms that all three components contribute to the overall predictive performance, with the market state perception module playing a particularly important role in improving ris…

title: Farmers' Education, Adoption of Sustainable Practices, and Mitigation of Climate Change Effects of Land Clearing
abstract: The relationship of human with the natural environment is at a critical juncture, with deforestation driven by agricultural expansion being a significant contributor to climate change. The study discusses the awareness of climate change and the environmental impact of farming practices among large landholders in the Kalabuargi district of Karnataka, India. Using a structured questionnaire, data were collected from 150 farm households across the region. The methodology involves multistage and random sampling, with econometric analyses such as linear, probit, and logit regression models employed to estimate sustainable practice adoption likelihood and the relationship between education and climate awareness. The findings show a significant gap in farmers' awareness regarding the broader implications of land clearing on climate change despite the econometric benefits derived from tree cutting and increased productivity. Educational interventions and access to information were identified as critical factors influencing the adoption of sustainable practices. The study concludes that educational programs and community involvement to raise awareness and promote sustainable farming practices.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Service Delivery: A Panacea for Global Governance Challenges Using the Nigerian Experience
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly presented as a transformative tool for addressing longstanding governance challenges, including bureaucratic inefficiency, corruption, poor transparency and weak citizen responsiveness. Yet whether AI can genuinely serve as a panacea for these challenges within a large, institutionally complex federation such as Nigeria remains an open empirical question. This study examined artificial intelligence and public service delivery as a panacea for global governance challenges, drawing on the Nigerian experience. Anchored on New Public Management (NPM) Theory and Digital Era Governance (DEG) Theory, the study adopted a descriptive survey design. A population of six hundred (600) public servants was drawn from five (5) selected federal public service institutions and the Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS), the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC), the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) spanning offices across Nigeria's six geo-political zones, out of which five hundred and fifty (550) copies of a structured questionnaire were administered and five hundred and thirty (530) were completed, returned and found usable, representing a 96.4 per cent response rate. Data were analysed using mean, standard deviation and chi-square statistics. …
venue: TRANSNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ARTS, HUMANITIES AND SCIENCES

title: BО‘LAJAK BОSHLANG‘ICH TA’LIM О‘QITUVCHILARINING KASBIY SHAKLLANISH INDIVIDUAL TRAYEKTОRIYASINI RAQAMLI TEXNОLОGIYALAR ASОSIDA LОYIHALASHNING PEDAGОGIK IMKОNIYATLARI
abstract: This study explores the pedagogical potential of designing individualized professional development trajectories for pre-service primary school teachers through the integration of digital technologies. The study aims to identify effective ways of using digital tools to support individualized professional development by taking into account students’ professional needs, career interests, individual capabilities, and prospective goals in teaching practice. A mixed methodological approach was employed, including the analysis of scientific and pedagogical literature, pedagogical observation, comparative analysis, questionnaires, diagnostic tasks, reflective assessment, and elements of pedagogical experimentation. The findings demonstrate that digital learning platforms, e-portfolios, individualized development maps, online monitoring systems, reflective assignments, and digital diagnostic tools can serve as effective pedagogical instruments for designing and supporting individualized professional development trajectories. The results also indicate that the purposeful integration of digital technologies enhances students’ engagement in independent learning, professional goal-setting, self- assessment, reflective practice, and continuous monitoring of personal and professional growth.

title: EKSTREMAL XIZMAT FAOLIYATI VA O'Z-O'ZINI SAFARBAR QILISH MUAMMOSINING METODOLOGIK YONDASHUVLARI
abstract: this article examines the theoretical and methodological foundations of self- mobilization in the context of extreme professional service activities. It analyzes the psychological changes occurring in the human psyche under extreme conditions and explains the interrelationship between psychological resilience, stress resistance, volitional regulation, and self-regulation mechanisms. The study also identifies the psychological factors that ensure the professional effectiveness of military personnel and presents the structural components of a self- mobilization model based on contemporary psychological approaches.

title: Actor engagement roles in collaborative settings: a theoretical framework and empirical typology
abstract: Purpose Despite the recognized importance of actor engagement in collaborative settings, little is known about actors' engagement practices and their influence on collaboration. This paper seeks to conceptualize actor engagement roles, reflecting actors' investment of resources. Moreover, it aims to identify engagement roles in an empirical context and examine their mutual influence, shedding light on the induced engagement dynamics. Design/methodology/approach This research draws on actor engagement as the domain theory and role theory as the method theory. Grounded in the actor engagement literature, we conceptualize actor engagement roles, using this framework as a sensitizing device for the empirical investigation. The qualitative study comprises 32 semi-structured interviews with students participating in collaborative seminars, with data analysed using the Gioia method. Findings The first finding is a theoretically derived framework for actor engagement roles. The second finding is a typology and constellation empirically derived within the specific collaborative setting, comprising eight actor engagement roles grouped into three overarching categories. By conceptualizing connectedness as the influence of engagement practices between the focal actor and others, we identify key engagement dynamics within the collaboration. Originality/value This research addresses the gap …

title: Developing a Resilient Workforce for a Technologically Disrupted Automotive Service Industry
abstract: The purpose of this workforce capability study is to quantify the magnitude of the challenge for tertiary education teachers. The automotive service sector is continuously evolving, so it is essential to stay updated on vehicle innovations and technological changes. As new technology is introduced in vehicles, the repair workflow changes and a technician cannot simply repair the fault, as sensors and software will need to be recalibrated for function. Hence, it is critical in the tertiary sector for teachers to remain current with automotive technological advancements. Available literature from global policy makers, vehicle manufacturers and national agencies were reviewed to determine the anticipated trends and disruptions to meet sustainability targets. Literature indicates that legacy technology combined with software will require a major reskilling across the service sector, requiring competencies and improving the development of human soft skills. Disruptions are hard to predict, and this study aims to identify how non-traditional skills will form the required workforce capability in the automotive service sector. Key industry leaders, service technicians and tertiary education teachers were interviewed, and findings from this study suggest industry stakeholders need to work collaboratively across the automotive service sector to develop service technicians’ knowledge and …

title: The problem posing capacities of pre-service post-primary mathematics teachers: insights from an Irish university
abstract: In Ireland and internationally, problem-solving is central to post-primary mathematics curricula. Enacting problem-solving in the classroom is challenging: it requires teachers to select or create problems appropriate to their students and the intended (mathematical thinking) learning outcomes. Despite the centrality of problem-solving in curricula in Ireland, post-primary students score higher in procedural tasks than problem-solving in the international assessments. Coinciding with this, in Ireland there is a reliance on textbooks with many tasks requiring low levels of cognitive demands. Combining these findings, there is an onus on teachers to be able to pose mathematical problems to expose students to problem-solving opportunities. This study investigates the problem posing capacities of two cohorts of pre-service post-primary mathematics teachers (PSMTs) in an Irish university. The participants were undertaking a module focused on mathematical problem-solving, with a focus on its teaching. PSMTs undertook activities in which they constructed new problems, constructed extension tasks to problems they had worked on themselves, and reformulated other mathematical tasks as problems. Each task generated by the PSMTs was classified against meeting the criteria of being a mathematical problem. Those which did not (non-problem tasks) were categorised using an inductive approach. …

title: Winning at service recovery: the power of empowering leadership and proactive employees
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social cognitive theory, the paper positions occupational self-efficacy as the mechanism linking empowering leadership to service recovery performance (SRP). Drawing on the job demands-resources model, it positions employee proactivity as the boundary condition on that mechanism. Design/methodology/approach The study applied a multi-wave questionnaire to 420 hospitality frontline employees. This study employed PROCESS models to test the hypotheses. Findings The main finding indicates that empowering leadership behaviors are not the ideal leadership for enhancing all subordinates’ occupational self-efficacy and SRP. High employee proactivity is a critical boundary for effectively handling empowerment and service recovery. Practical implications The study offers guidance for leadership and subordinate development programs, recruitment and selection, and recognition systems. Originality/value The study specifies employee proactivity as a boundary condition on the path from empowering leadership to service recovery through occupational self-efficacy.
venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Insights

title: Public service motivation as a predictor of career engagement among South African public servants
abstract: Orientation: Public servants increasingly need proactive career behaviours to remain effective in a demanding public sector. Public service motivation (PSM) is linked to positive work behaviours and warrants further understanding. Research purpose: This study investigated the relationship between PSM and career engagement (CE) among South African public servants and the variance in CE explained by PSM. Motivation for the study: PSM is a motivational disposition to serve the public interest, while CE denotes observable, proactive career behaviours; despite conceptual overlap, the constructs are theoretically distinct. No prior study has examined PSM as an antecedent of CE, rather than merely an overlapping construct in the South African public sector. Research approach/design and method: A quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used. Data were collected from 301 public servants using an established PSM scale and an established Career Engagement Scale (CES). Confirmatory factor analysis, Pearson’s corre

title: Spatiotemporal associations between ecosystem service value and human activity intensity: a case study of the Chengdu metropolitan area, China
abstract: Understanding the spatiotemporal association between ecosystem service value (ESV) and human activity intensity (HAI) is essential for coordinating regional ecological protection with sustainable socioeconomic development. Using geospatial data for the Chengdu Metropolitan Area from 2000 to 2020, this study estimated ESV and HAI with an ESV accounting model and an HAI assessment model, and examined their spatiotemporal patterns and associations using bivariate spatial autocorrelation and coupling coordination degree models. The results showed that: (1) Temporally, total ESV initially increased and subsequently decreased, with an overall decline of CNY 37 million. Spatially, ESV decreased outward from the Longmen Mountains in the west and Longquan Mountains in the central area, with high-value zones occurring mainly along the Tuojiang and Minjiang rivers. (2) HAI increased continuously. Low values were concentrated in the western Longmen Mountains and eastern hilly areas, whereas high values were centered in Chengdu’s main urban area and expanded into surrounding areas. (3) HAI and ESV exhibited a significant and increasingly strong negative spatial correlation. High-low clusters were concentrated in Chengdu’s main urban area and adjacent built-up areas, low-high clusters remained stable in the densely vegetated western Longmen Mountains, and low-low clusters were widespread acr…

title: Development of a Web-Based Correspondence Service Information System to Improve the Administrative Efficiency of Wonowoso Village
abstract: Correspondence administration in Wonowoso Village relied on conventional procedures that lacked an integrated digital workflow for citizen submissions and administrative records. This study aimed to develop a web-based correspondence service information system to support more orderly village administration. Development comprised requirements mapping, system design, implementation, and functional verification. The application was built using Node.js, Express.js, EJS, MongoDB, and Mongoose, with Multer, express-session, bcryptjs, and Nodemailer supporting document uploads, administrator sessions, password security, and rejection notifications, respectively. Verification combined source-code inspection, desktop interface rendering, and examination of a MongoDB backup snapshot. The developed system provides four service types and connects citizen submissions with administrator processing through Pending, Approved, and Rejected statuses. Citizens can review service requirements, complete application forms, and upload supporting documents, while administrators can examine applications, assign letter numbers, preview letters, approve requests, and record reasons for rejection. The database snapshot contained four applications: one Approved and three Rejected. The system supports a more organized administrative workflow through centralized records, online submissions, and structured st…

title: User Experience und Service Design in Bibliotheken
ДИДАКТИЧЕСКИЕ ПРИНЦИПЫ РАЗВИТИЯ ИНКЛЮЗИВНЫХ КОМПЕТЕНЦИЙ У БУДУЩИХ УЧИТЕЛЕЙ
abstract: This article presents a systematic analysis of the pedagogical and didactic foundations for developing inclusive competence among pre-service teachers in a digital learning environment. The author groups the conditions that support the formation of inclusive competence into three broad categories (value-motivational, cognitive-methodological, and technological-environmental) and elucidates the systemic principles operating within each. The study classifies didactic principles into three clusters (rights-based and social, organizational and environmental, and procedural and methodological) and substantiates their interrelationship.

title: Corrosion behavior of long-term service-exposed ductile iron for water pipelines in chloride-containing media
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the corrosion behavior of ductile iron recovered from a municipal water pipeline after approximately 30 years of service, with particular emphasis on the effects of anion species and temperature on electrochemical response, rust-layer evolution and graphite–matrix-associated localized damage. Design/methodology/approach Electrochemical measurements were conducted in NaCl, Na2SO4 and NaHCO3 solutions at 5, 20 and 35 °C, while immersion tests were performed in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 20 and 35 °C for up to 168 h. The corrosion products, rust-layer morphology, and underlying substrate damage were characterized using X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy, and confocal laser scanning microscopy. Findings Among the investigated electrolytes, NaCl produced the lowest polarization resistance, whereas Na2SO4 yielded the highest values. Increasing temperature reduced the polarization resistance and promoted interfacial corrosion processes. γ-FeOOH was identified as the dominant crystalline corrosion product; however, the rust layer formed at 35 °C was coarser, more porous and less protective. The overall corrosion damage was dominated by widespread dissolution of the ferritic matrix, accompanied by preferential attack at graphite–matrix interfaces. After prolonged exposure t…

title: Integrated child and adolescent psychiatry within a specialist child sexual abuse service in Ireland: a two-year retrospective cohort study
abstract: Abstract Background: Child sexual abuse (CSA) is associated with substantial psychiatric morbidity, yet the nature and scope of integrated child and adolescent psychiatry within specialist CSA services in Ireland are poorly described. Methods: This retrospective chart review included all children and adolescents referred to an embedded child and adolescent psychiatry clinic within The Alders Unit, a specialist CSA service, between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2025. Data included demographics, psychosocial adversity, referral characteristics, psychiatric diagnoses, psychotropic prescribing, prior Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service (CAMHS) involvement and onward referrals. Descriptive statistics summarised sample characteristics, and associations between categorical variables were examined using chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests. Results: Fifty young people (approximately 5% of Alders referrals) were seen by psychiatry (mean age 15.7 years, predominantly female). Nearly two-thirds experienced two or more psychosocial adversity domains, and 58% had a suspected or confirmed neurodevelopmental disorder. Depressive, anxiety and trauma-related disorders were the most common primary diagnoses. Acute risk related to self-harm or suicidality was the leading reason for referral and was associated with onward referral. Most young people required follow-up for more than 12 months…

title: Does health facility infrastructure predict performance? Disconnects between service readiness, process quality, and client experience in Ethiopia
Complex post-translational regulation of the plant shikimate pathway
abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) are crucial regulators of protein function, influencing most cellular processes in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. The fundamental effect of PTMs on metabolic control has been reported for most metabolic pathways in organisms ranging from animals and plants to bacteria and fungi. However, the impact of PTMs on the regulation of the plant shikimate pathway, which connects central carbon metabolism with the synthesis of aromatic amino acids and represents one of the largest metabolic fluxes on Earth, remains largely unexplored. In this study, we address the identification of PTMs affecting the enzymes of the shikimate pathway in Arabidopsis thaliana . Following a strategy based on transient expression in protoplasts, immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometric analysis, we have identified a large and varied collection of PTMs affecting the 20 alternative isoenzymes involved in the shikimate and phenylalanine (Phe) biosynthesis pathways. Our analysis revealed glycosylation, phosphorylation, methylation, nitration, and acetylation as the predominant modifications. Notably, we have identified multiple phosphorylation events that expand those previously reported. Additionally, we characterized two phosphorylation events affecting chorismate mutase 1 (AtCM1), the committed enzyme in the phenylalanine/tyrosine biosynthetic pathway. Enzymatic assa…

title: EEG-UDAF: A novel unsupervised domain adaptation framework leveraging dual-view frequency and spatio-temporal features for EEG-based emotion recognition
BOSHLANG‘ICH TA’LIMDA KOGNITIV FAOLIYAT DINAMIKASINI KUZATISH (idrok, asosiy ko‘nikmalar, regulyatsiya, tushunish va ifoda sohalari misolida)
abstract: This article examines the monitoring of cognitive activity dynamics among primary school students. A five-domain monitoring model is proposed, covering perception, foundational skills, regulation, understanding, and expression. The study applies systemic, comparative, component-based, and dynamic analysis to identify observable indicators for each domain. The proposed model focuses not only on students’ final learning outcomes but also on changes in their cognitive processes over time. It can support teachers in identifying individual learning trajectories, diagnosing difficulties, and adapting instructional strategies to students’ developmental needs.

title: Circadian Rhythms, Sleep Patterns, and the Regulation of Cravings for Sweet and Refined-Carbohydrate Foods
abstract: Cravings for sweet and refined-carbohydrate foods are commonly reported and can contribute to excess energy intake, although terminology and measurement vary across studies. This narrative review examines how sleep duration, sleep architecture, circadian timing, and meal timing are associated with appetite, food reward, and cravings for sweet and refined-carbohydrate foods. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched for English-language peer-reviewed human studies published primarily between January 2021 and August 2026, and selected foundational studies were included for historical and mechanistic context. Experimental sleep restriction has been associated with changes in appetite-regulating hormones and with heightened responses of neural reward circuits to palatable food, although hormonal responses are heterogeneous across protocols, sexes, and populations. Observational studies link shift work and social jetlag to poorer diet quality and altered eating behavior, and controlled trials indicate that late meal timing can increase hunger independent of energy content. Most of the available evidence concerns hunger, appetite, or highly palatable food intake rather than carbohydrate-specific craving, experimental samples are often small, and observational designs cannot establish causality. Overall, the evidence supports an association between circadian and sleep disruptio…

title: Low-Frequency Magnetic Field Mitigation Using Recyclable Sintered Pure-Iron Powder Compacts for Safer Power and Sensor Infrastructure
abstract: High-current carrying conductors, electrical machines, power-electronic systems, and sensors generate low-frequency magnetic fields that can cause electromagnetic interference and may result in higher magnetic-field exposure in occupied or sensitive environments. This study proposes a new low frequency shielding material in the form of sintered pure-iron powder compacts as an alternative to the conventional high-permeability magnetic shielding alloys. This material is manufactured by following controlled environment annealing, green compaction and sintering of high purity iron powder. The magnetic properties of the compacted specimen were determined by characterization according to IEC 60404-4 standard, and scanning electron microscopy was used to study the microstructural features, and chemical analysis was performed by using energy dispersive spectroscopy to validate purity of the iron powder. Experimentally determined magnetic properties were used in finite element simulations to evaluate the shielding performance when different shielding geometries manufactured from the proposed material are placed around a current-carrying conductor. Analysis was done when the conductor carries current of 1000 Amp with focus to evaluate different shielding topologies, including open, square, hexagonal and circular shapes. Analysis indicated that the circular closed-shielding geometry can a…

title: Frequency of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia in Symptomatic Women with Clinically Unhealthy Cervix Based on Colposcopic Assessment

title: FREQUENCY AND CLINICAL AND ENDOSCOPIC MANIFESTATIONS OF BILE ACID MALABSORPTION IN CHILDREN AGED 1 MONTH TO 18 YEARS WITH CHRONIC DIARRHEA: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY (COMPARISON OF CHILDREN WITH ELEVATED AND NORMAL FECAL BILE ACID LEVELS)
abstract: Bile acid malabsorption (BAM) is common in gastrointestinal disorders. In most cases, it is not an independent disease but is characterized by a persistent course and reduced quality of life. The frequency and clinical and endoscopic features of bile acid diarrhea in children have not yet been studied. Objective: to investigate the frequency and clinical and endoscopic manifestations of BAM in children with chronic diarrhea (CD). Materials and Methods: a cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 77 children of different ages with CD from December 2025 to June 2026. Clinical and anamnestic data and the results of fecal bile acid testing were analyzed. Two groups were identified: Group 1, children with bile acid diarrhea (n=48), and Group 2, children with normal fecal bile acid levels (n=29). Results: bile acid diarrhea was detected in 48 children (62.3%; 95% CI, 50.6–73.1%). Median age was 7.6 years [5.2; 13.2] in Group 1 and 11.9 years [9.7; 14.5] in Group 2 (p=0.010). Group 1 included 19 girls (39.6%) and 29 boys (60.4%), while Group 2 included 13 girls (44.8%) and 16 boys (55.2%). Median diarrhea duration was 18.3 months [5; 24] in Group 1 and 8 months [4; 24] in Group 2; the difference was not statistically significant (p=0.068). No differences were found in the nature of complaints or stool characteristics. Frequent stools occurred in every second patient in Grou…

title: Defect Detection in Rotor-Bearing-Gear Systems for Experimental Frequency-Domain Fault Diagnosis using FFT and Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Rotor bearing gear system is mostly used in rotating machinery in industries and has considerable susceptibility to defects such as wear, pitting, and failure in gears, corrosion of components, and damage to bearings under different operating conditions. This paper presents an experimental study of fault diagnosis implemented in the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and Machine Learning Techniques. In the Experimental study, the bevel gearbox test rig was exercised under various operating conditions (200 rpm to 1000 rpm, loading (20 N to 100 N)), and six types of faults were exercised for each case, including mutually imposed multiple fault conditions. For each fault condition, FFT analysis identified characteristic fault frequencies, harmonics, sidebands, and modulation effects were found by FFT analysis. We observed that as the fault level, speed, and load increased, vibration amplitude increased significantly. Frequency-domain vibration features were used in this study with machine learning classifiers to determine fault conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance applications.

title: COMPARATIVE CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY OF PSYCHOEMOTIONAL STATUS AND AUTONOMIC REGULATION IN ORPHANED CHILDREN AGED 10–16 YEARS EVACUATED FROM A COMBAT ZONE (NEW REGIONS OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION) AND CHILDREN PERMANENTLY RESIDING IN THE ROSTOV REGION
abstract: Orphans and children deprived of parental care who have experienced combat-related stress constitute a particularly vulnerable population. Comprehensive comparative data simultaneously characterizing their psychoemotional, somatic, and autonomic status remain limited. Objective: to investigate the psychological and physical characteristics of children who had lived in the new regions of the Russian Federation, were deprived of parental care, and had been exposed to combat-related stress. Materials and Methods: a cross-sectional comparative study with retrospective analysis of medical history data was conducted in residential institutions for orphans and children deprived of parental care in the Rostov Region from September 2025 to May 2026. The study included 56 children aged 10–16 years: 24 children evacuated from a combat zone to the Rostov Region (Group I) and 32 children who had permanently resided in the Rostov Region (Group II). The mean age was 12.33±2.06 and 13.17±2.32 years, respectively (p=0.188). The assessment included medical history analysis, anthropometry, evaluation of autonomic status using the Kerdo index, functional tests, and psychometric assessment with the PedsQL 4.0 Generic Core Scales, the Yakhin–Mendelevich Clinical Questionnaire for the Identification and Assessment of Neurotic States, the Buss–Durkee Hostility Inventory, the Eysenck Personality Questi…
venue: Pediatria. Journal named after G.N. Speransky

title: PAN/PI-Derived Carbon Nanofibrous Membranes with MXene-Assisted Contact Modulation for Heat-Resistant Piezoresistive Sensing and Thermal Warning Response
abstract: Abstract Flexible piezoresistive sensors for protective textiles should maintain pressure-responsive conductivity after thermal exposure, whereas many polymer-based sensing layers soften, degrade, or lose signal output under heat. Herein, we report a self-supporting PAN/PI-derived carbon nanofibrous membrane with MXene-assisted contact modulation for heat-resistant piezoresistive sensing and temperature-triggered warning. Electrospun PAN/PAA membranes were stabilized and carbonized to construct a thermally durable conductive fibrous framework, in which PAN serves as the principal carbon-forming precursor and the PAA-derived PI intermediate assists structural retention during thermal conversion. Surface-deposited Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets further introduce conductive junctions and pressure-responsive contact interfaces. The optimized PPNF-MX3 sensor exhibits a broad pressure range of 0.05–250 kPa, a low-pressure sensitivity of 8.16 kPa–1, and response/recovery times of 520/572 ms. It retains 97.51% of its electromechanical response after 10,000 bending-release cycles at room temperature and 83.16% after 1200 cycles following thermal exposure at 350 °C for 660 s. The carbonized membrane exhibits thermal-shielding behavior and flame-induced structural retention, while the integrated system enables repeatable temperature-triggered warning at 495 °C. These results demonstrate the pot…

title: Efficacy and safety of bone marrow mononuclear cell therapy for myocardial infarction: a dose–response meta-analysis
abstract: Background Bone marrow mononuclear cells (BMMNCs) have been investigated as a potential regenerative therapy for myocardial infarction (MI). However, whether their clinical benefits are sustained over time and what constitutes an optimal therapeutic dose remain uncertain. This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and dose–response relationship of BMMNC therapy in patients with MI. Methods Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing BMMNC therapy with standard therapy or placebo in patients with MI were systematically searched in relevant databases. Statistical analyses were performed using R. Continuous outcomes were summarized as mean differences (MDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), and dichotomous outcomes were summarized as risk ratios (RRs) with 95%CIs. Random-effects models were used for pooled analyses. Subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, meta-regression, and restricted cubic spline models were performed to explore the effects of follow-up duration and cell dose on treatment outcomes. Results A total of 43 RCTs involving 2,213 patients receiving BMMNC therapy and 1,686 control patients were included. BMMNC therapy significantly improved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) at 6 months (MD = 2.57%, 95%CI: 0.79 to 4.35; p = 0.007), but this effect was attenuated at 12 months and did not reach statistical significance (MD = 1.59%, 95%CI: −0…

title: Consistent associations of BMI with ovarian response and pregnancy loss risk across PCOS, DOR, and tubal factor infertility: a complete-case mediation analysis of 8,923 IVF cycles
A systematic benchmarking pipeline for demand forecasting and inventory-aware supply chain decision support
abstract: Demand forecasting has been shown to be one of the key facilitators of successful supply chain and inventory management. In this work, we introduce a benchmarking pipeline for demand forecasting in retail that includes data preprocessing, comparative benchmarking of different machine learning/deep learning (ML/DL) approaches, and decision-focused evaluation. Unlike other works that compare predictive performance of ML/DL models and end there, our pipeline links reproducible ML/DL benchmarking and decision-focused evaluation through cost of inventory management in order to derive costs from forecasting error/bias. We also present a scalability study on another retail dataset. Several standard forecasting models, such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Units (GRU), CNN-LSTM, and XGBoost, are compared using a unified experimental pipeline on benchmark retail datasets. The experimental results reveal that while the deep learning models efficiently identify temporal dependencies, tree-based ensemble algorithms, especially XGBoost, consistently deliver better results in terms of forecasting accuracy on structured retail demand datasets. A scalability case study on the Rossmann Store Sales benchmark evaluates the top-performing model on a larger, richer dataset. Moreover, the study shows the connection between forecast accuracy and th…

title: Variable zircon, titanite and apatite response during magma hybridization and autometasomatism
abstract: Abstract The U–Pb records of accessory minerals can become difficult to interpret when magmatic crystallization is overprinted by hydrothermal alteration and element redistribution. The Archibarca Pluton, in the shallow portion on the Paleozoic Famatinian Arc in northwestern Argentina, preserves a complex history of magma crystallization, magma mixing (hybridization), and autometasomatism that variably overprints the textures, chemistry and U–Pb record of zircon, titanite and apatite. We found that hydrothermal modification affects zircon U–Pb dates and trace element compositions, producing complex and apparently concordant date distributions. Nevertheless, after filtering analyses affected by metasomatic modification, zircon retains geochronological information that is consistent with the magmatic and hydrothermal history recorded by titanite and apatite. Thus zircon can preserve useful chronological information even in hydrothermally modified systems, but its U–Pb record should be evaluated together with textural and geochemical evidence and complemented by other accessory mineral petrochronometers to distinguish magmatic crystallization from subsequent fluid-mediated changes. Zircon displays a spectrum of preserved and modified domains, in which chemical alteration, expressed as Fe–Ti–P–Y-LREE enrichment or depletion, may be either coupled or decoupled from U–Pb dates. Altho…

title: Influence of self-reported vascular health and physical activity level on intravoxel incoherent motion imaging response to exercise in chronic low back pain
abstract: Introduction In individuals with chronic low back pain (CLBP), degenerative changes in paraspinal muscles, such as fatty infiltration and reduced vascularization, may impair muscles’ physiological response to exercise, limiting recovery potential. Intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) imaging enables assessment of muscle microvascular perfusion (D*) and intracellular diffusion (D) in response to exercise. Previous work demonstrated that individuals with chronic LBP exhibit attenuated IVIM responses to exercise, and that these responses predict clinical improvement following rehabilitation. Yet the mechanisms underlying these alterations remain unclear. Vascular comorbidities, frequently reported in individuals with CLBP, may impair exercise-induced vasodilation and limit microvascular perfusion in lumbar muscles, while reduced physical activity (PA) levels, also commonly observed, may contribute to alterations in muscle microstructure. This study investigated whether systemic vascular health and PA level moderate lumbar paraspinal IVIM responses to acute exercise in individuals with CLBP. Methods Seventy-nine participants with CLBP underwent lumbar IVIM imaging before and after a lumbar extension exercise. IVIM parameters D, D* and perfusion fraction (f) were measured for paraspinal muscles. Participants were classified as having a known vascular condition (n=26) or no vascular c…

title: Durable partial response with low-dose, intermittent nivolumab in combination with gemcitabine for high PD-L1 metastatic triple-negative breast cancer: a case report
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have improved outcomes in selected patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (mTNBC), particularly those with high programed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression. However, optimal dosing strategies balancing efficacy, toxicity, and cost remain unclear. We report the case of a 34-year-old woman with recurrent mTNBC and high PD-L1 expression (combined positive score, CPS ≥ 60; immunohistochemistry 22C3 pharmDx assay). She achieved durable disease control over 22 months (September 2024 to June 2026) using a combination of gemcitabine maintenance chemotherapy and low-dose intermittent nivolumab (40 mg fixed dose, administered 3-weekly). This de-escalated regimen was adopted due to early treatment toxicity and severe financial constraints. The patient achieved a confirmed partial response by RECIST v1.1 criteria (48% reduction in target lesion size), accompanied by manageable CTCAE Grade 2 hypothyroidism requiring oral levothyroxine replacement. This case illustrates that in biomarker-selected, PD-L1-high mTNBC, combination chemotherapy with low-intensity PD-1 blockade can maintain prolonged antitumor activity. These observations support the working hypothesis of a minimum effective immune dose, warranting prospective evaluation in resource-constrained clinical settings.
