A novel CAF-related gene signature for prognostic and immunotherapy response prediction in PDAC based on single-cell RNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq data
abstract: Increasing evidence shows that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) contribute to tumor progression, create an immunosuppressive microenvironment, and promote resistance to immunotherapy. However, the CAF-related gene signature in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains largely unexplored. In our study, we constructed a nine-gene CAF-related signature and found that it strongly correlated with the prognosis of PDAC patients in different cohorts. Subsequently, we found that the CAF-related gene signature was associated with the genomic alteration landscape, immune infiltration landscape and responsiveness to immunotherapy. GJB2 had the highest coefficient in our CAF-related gene signature, thus we explored the role of GJB2 in the interactions between CAFs and PDAC cells. The results showed that conditioned medium (CM) derived from the GJB2 knockdown group could suppress the malignant phenotype of PANC1 and MIAPaCa2 cells. In summary, this CAF-related gene signature is useful for prognosis prediction and precision therapy of PDAC patients.

title: Optimization of Soxhlet extraction conditions and preliminary phytochemical characterization of Urtica dioica leaf extract using response surface methodology
Durable biochemical and radiographic response during toripalimab treatment in MSI-high/TMB-high mCRPC: a case report
abstract: We present a 79-year-old male patient with MSI-H/TMB-H (91.5 mutations/Mb) metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who progressed following abiraterone and enzalutamide treatment. When toripalimab was started, his serum PSA was 102 ng/mL. We maintained androgen-deprivation therapy with leuprorelin and stopped enzalutamide. Toripalimab 240 mg was given intravenously every 21 days. His PSA dropped below 0.09 ng/mL after three treatment cycles. We retrospectively applied RECIST version 1.1 criteria and selected the locally invasive prostate-soft-tissue mass as our only measurable non-nodal target lesion. Its maximal diameter shrank from 119 mm at baseline to 43 mm after six cycles (63.9% reduction), and further to 31 mm after 25 cycles (73.9% reduction), satisfying criteria for partial response. Pelvic lymph nodes could only be classified as non-target disease because short-axis diameters were unavailable in imaging reports, though these nodes resolved on imaging after six cycles. Bone lesions were not included in RECIST response evaluation and were interpreted separately on serial bone scans. At cycle 31 (roughly 21 months after toripalimab commencement), PSA stayed undetectable without clinical or radiological signs of progression; the biochemical response persisted for about 19 months starting from cycle 3. As of manuscript revision, the patient remains on toripalimab p…

title: The Effect of Collaborative Leadership and Early Warning System on Community Preparedness Response through Community Participation in Madiun Regency
abstract: Disaster risks in Madiun Regency, particularly floods, landslides, and tornadoes, underscore the need for preparedness strategies that integrate early warning systems, stakeholder coordination, and community involvement. This study examined the effects of collaborative leadership and early warning systems on community preparedness response, including indirect effects through community participation. A quantitative explanatory design involved 400 respondents from purposively selected areas. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed through partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS 4. The structural model identified significant paths from collaborative leadership and early warning systems to both preparedness response and community participation. Community participation was positively and significantly associated with preparedness response and partially mediated the relationship between each predictor and preparedness response. These findings identify community participation as an intermediary linking collaborative leadership and early warning systems to preparedness. The study concludes that disaster preparedness efforts should integrate collaborative governance, warning systems, and community participation. The findings provide evidence to inform the strengthening of participatory disaster management policie…

title: Multi period MINLP framework for optimal operation of active distribution networks with integrated EVs and demand side management
abstract: Abstract This paper introduces a complete stochastic optimization framework for optimal operation of Active Distribution Networks (ADNs), taking into account the coordinated integration of Diesel Generator (DG), Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESSs), Electric Vehicles (EVs), and price-based Demand-Side Management (DSM). The suggested model includes AC power flow constraints, coordination of active and reactive power, and operating limits of all system components across a 24-hour scheduling period. The proposed approach is structured as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model, applied to a modified IEEE 33-bus Radial Distribution Network (RDN), and optimized using GAMS with the DICOPT solver. The model goal is to reduce overall operational expenses. Network power losses and voltage profile are evaluated as technical performance indicators resulting from the optimal scheduling strategy. EVs are designed with bidirectional charging capabilities (V2G/G2V), RES, DG, and BESS that facilitate both active and reactive power. DSM allows for load shifting in residential and commercial sectors in response to dynamic pricing signals. The efficiency of the proposed methodology is verified through several case studies. The results indicate that coordinating DG, RES, BESS, EVs, and price-based DSM enhances the operational efficiency of the distrib…

title: From Passive Barrier to Smart Response: The Evolution of Anti-Corrosion Fillers and Their Adaptive Protection Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Smart responsive anticorrosion fillers have significantly advanced metal protection by enabling a shift from passive physical barriers to dynamic, adaptive defense systems. This review systematically elucidates the evolutionary trajectory from traditional passive barrier fillers and inhibitor-loaded active systems to state-of-the-art smart responsive platforms that sense and respond to corrosive microenvironments. The fundamental design principles and response mechanisms are discussed, focusing on pH, chloride, electrochemical potential, and temperature/humidity stimuli. The critical role of micro/nanostructural engineering-including core-shell architectures, hierarchical porosity, and surface functional layers-in achieving on-demand inhibitor release is highlighted. Advanced strategies such as hierarchical release kinetics, synergistic inhibitor combinations, and multifunctional system-level integration are addressed. Finally, key challenges related to interfacial defects, long-term response decay, and extreme environment reliability are outlined. This work provides insights into the rational design of next-generation smart anticorrosion coatings for complex service environments. This review is expected to provide a theoretical foundation and design guidelines for the development of novel adaptive anticorrosion coatings tailored for extreme service conditions.

title: From listening to action: how social and behavioral evidence informed multisectoral cholera response in Zambia, 2023–2024
abstract: Rapid qualitative assessments and community feedback mechanisms are increasingly recognized as core components of risk communication and community engagement in public health emergencies, yet few documented examples exist of how this evidence has directly influenced outbreak response decision-making. This case study examines the 2023–2024 cholera outbreak in Zambia, analyzing how social and behavioral data generated through multiple rounds of rapid qualitative assessment, alongside national community feedback mechanisms, informed multisectoral response activities. Drawing on document review, consultations with response pillar members, assessment reports, feedback dashboards, and triangulation with epidemiological data, the study traces how community concerns, rumors, beliefs, perceptions and priorities were collected, analyzed and applied across health, water, sanitation and hygiene, and protection response pillars. Enabling factors included pre-existing technical capacity, strong partnerships between government humanitarian actors, and academia, and rapid feedback loops that supported near real-time adaptation. Challenges at different points in the response included delayed resource allocation, uneven subnational coordination, and limited capacity to process large volumes of feedback data. The Zambia experience demonstrates that community-generated evidence can meaningfully in…

title: From appraisal to adaptation: a dual-path model of construction project management professionals' job crafting in response to emerging smart technologies
abstract: Purpose Emerging smart technologies (EST) – such as building information modeling, big data, cloud computing and robotics – have profoundly reshaped workflows and workplace behaviors in the architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC) industry. Although extensive research has investigated the multi-level driving factors of EST implementation, little is known about its downstream effects on construction project management professionals' psychological and behavioral responses. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the transactional model of stress and self-determination theory, this study develops a “stress appraisal–psychological state–behavior response” theoretical model and empirically tests it using 315 construction project management professional samples. Findings The findings show that challenge appraisal of EST implementation is positively associated with role breadth self-efficacy, whereas hindrance appraisal is positively related to ego depletion. Furthermore, role breadth self-efficacy and ego depletion are found to mediate the relationships between challenge appraisal and hindrance appraisal and the three forms of job crafting, respectively. Moreover, conscientiousness strengthens the relationship between hindrance appraisal of EST implementation and ego depletion, while its moderating effect on the link between challenge appraisal and role breadth self-efficacy …

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Mental Health Assessment: A Systematic Review of Interpretability, Psychometric Reporting and Clinical Utility
abstract: The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) into qualitative data analysis has significantly sped up the coding, clustering, and pattern identification process at scale more than ever before. The surveys of the industry show that by 2024, it is expected that about 77 percent of academic research teams will have utilized some type of AI-assisted analytical tooling, an increase of nearly seven times compared to 11 percent in 2018. Nevertheless, despite this high level of diffusion, technologies that focus on automation endanger the interpretive, reflexive and context-sensitive epistemological principles of qualitative inquiry. The current paradigms offer a paradigm methodological dilemma that has been addressed through manual techniques that offer interpretive profundity and theoretical sensitivity, but are limited in scalability and time-efficiency, and AI-based systems that offer computational efficiency but epistemic overreach, lack of analytic transparency, and diminished construct validity. To fill this gap, this paper suggests the Human-Governed Qualitative Intelligence Model (HGQIM), which was based on the architectural concepts of the Qualivers platform. The HGQIM combines the computational processing and systematic human control, allowing researchers to confirm, alter or dismiss AI-generated interpretations in a transparent and reflexive system. The model is based o…

title: Can compassion drive firm innovativeness through organizational trust?
abstract: Purpose This paper addresses the escalating issue of suffering within organizations, emphasizing the pivotal role of compassion in mitigating the detrimental impacts of workplace suffering and enhancing the mental well-being of employees. Contrary to existing literature that has primarily focused on individual well-being, we propose to explore the broader organizational implications of compassion, specifically its influence on innovativeness. Design/methodology/approach To investigate the intricate relationship between organizational compassion and firm innovativeness, we employ a structural equation model. Our study encompasses a sample of Spanish companies spanning various sectors. A key element in our analysis is the inclusion of organizational trust as a mediator, aiming to elucidate how compassion at work might impact firm innovativeness through this intermediary variable. Findings The results of our study demonstrate a positive correlation between compassion at work and firm innovativeness. Moreover, we reveal that the influence of organizational compassion on innovativeness is mediated by organizational trust. This indirect pathway underscores the significance of trust in translating compassionate workplace practices into enhanced firm innovativeness. Originality/value This research contributes to the existing literature by offering a novel perspective on how organizatio…

title: Diagnosis and management of transthyretin amyloidosis (ATTRv) across ATTRv-PN and mixed phenotype: an international delphi consensus
abstract: Abstract Background Transthyretin amyloidosis is a progressive, potentially fatal genetic disorder primarily associated with polyneuropathy (ATTRv-PN) or cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). Disease presentation is heterogenous. Patients often present with a mixed phenotype. Although recent clinical recommendations for ATTR-CM management are well established, there is limited updated guidance for the diagnosis and management of ATTRv-PN or mixed phenotype ATTRv. This study aimed to identify gaps in practice and establish expert consensus to support optimal care. Methods A steering committee (SC) of four international experts experienced in ATTR amyloidosis management was convened. Three priority domains were identified and 45 statements were developed. Statements were distributed internationally as a 4-point Likert survey to neuromuscular neurologists and heart failure cardiologists experienced in managing ATTR amyloidosis. Pre-defined stopping criteria included a target of 100 responses and a threshold of ≥75% agreement. Surveys were fully anonymized. Results were discussed by the SC and recommendations were formulated based on observed agreement. Results A total of 100 clinicians participated,including neurologists (n=74) and cardiologists (n=26) from the United States (n=50), Canada (n=10), France, Germany, Italy, Spain, and the United Kingdom (n=8 each). Respondents stated high levels…

title: THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM IN SLOVAKIA AND ITS DENTAL COMPONENT: EXPERIENCE FOR UKRAINE
abstract: The article analyzes the modern healthcare system of the Slovak Republic with a focus on the organization of dental care. Reforming Ukraine’s healthcare system requires consideration of the experience of Central and Eastern European countries that have transitioned from post-socialist models towards systems based on universal healthcare coverage, mandatory health insurance, and regulated competition among healthcare providers. In this context, the experience of the Slovak Republic is particularly relevant. The aim of this article is to analyze Slovakia’s healthcare system and its dental care component, as well as to identify opportunities for applying the Slovak experience to the modernization of dental care in Ukraine. Materials and methods. The study employed methods of systems analysis and comparative analysis, as well as the synthesis of regulatory documents from the Slovak Republic and Ukraine, analytical materials from the European Commission, the OECD, and the WHO, and scientific publications regarding healthcare organization and dentistry. Results and discussion. Financing mechanisms, the role of health insurance, the structure of dental services, preventive measures, and accessibility of dental care for the population are examined. The key elements of the Slovak model that can be adapted in Ukraine in the context of healthcare reform and integration into the European h…

title: Implementation of a Modbus TCP-Based Energy Information System to Reduce Data Discrepancy and Improve Reporting Efficiency in the F&B Industry
abstract: Accurate energy data management is essential for improving operational decision-making in industrial environments; however, manual and semi-integrated data acquisition processes often cause discrepancies between internal metering and external billing data. This study aims to implement a Modbus TCP-based Energy Information System (EIS) to reduce energy data discrepancies, improve reporting efficiency, and evaluate user acceptance in a food and beverage manufacturing facility. The research employed a structured implementation approach consisting of system design, integration, performance evaluation, and user acceptance analysis. The proposed EIS integrated 117 power meters using a hybrid Modbus TCP/RTU architecture, supported by Node-RED middleware and a PostgreSQL time-series database for real-time data acquisition and centralized monitoring. System performance was evaluated using Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), while user acceptance was assessed using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) involving 23 respondents. The findings indicate that the implementation of EIS reduced energy data discrepancies from an average of 6.75% during the anomaly phase to 2.0% after stabilization, representing an improvement of approximately 70%. In addition, monthly reporting time decreased from 14 hours to 2.83 hours, improving …

title: From drawing lines to opening doors: the dynamic reconfiguration of defensive knowledge boundaries
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social information processing theory and boundary work theory, this study aims to examine how knowledge territorial behavior influences knowledge sharing through workplace ostracism and job crafting, and explores the moderating role of leader communication openness. Design/methodology/approach This study conducted a scenario-based experiment and a time-lagged field survey. Study 1 used a situational experiment in China (n = 200) to provide initial evidence for the proposed relationships under controlled scenario conditions. Study 2 used a three-wave, multisource questionnaire survey of full-time employees in Chinese organizations (n = 219). The hypotheses were tested using regression analyses and structural equation modeling. Findings Knowledge territorial behavior is indirectly associated with knowledge sharing through workplace ostracism and subsequent task and relational crafting. In addition, leader communication openness serves as a boundary condition for these effects. Originality/value This study offers evidence consistent with a dynamic knowledge boundary management process, demonstrating how competitive and collaborative boundary work coexist in knowledge-intensive workplaces. It advances social information processing theory in knowledge management by explaining how employees interpret workplace social cues and engage in relational and boundary repai…

title: From viewing to deciding: How YouTube videos impact medical decisions? An empirical investigation using S-O-R framework
abstract: Purpose The purpose of the study is to examine how the YouTube engagement cues influence users' perceived usefulness of health video content and their usage of YouTube for medical decision-making. Design/methodology/approach This study employs the stimulus-organism-response (S-O-R) framework to investigate the intricate dynamics shaping medical decisions. The present research adopted a cross-sectional design involving data from 408 respondents in India through a non-probabilistic sampling procedure. The two-stage structural equation modelling (SEM) approach was adopted to analyze the data. Findings Findings from the proposed framework show that the engagement cues positively influenced the perceived usefulness of YouTube videos, with information quality and reliability emerging as equally significant stimulus drivers. Perceived usefulness, in turn, strongly predicted users' intention to make medical decisions. The findings validate the heuristic systematic model (HSM) integrated S-O-R framework as a robust theoretical framework shaping health decision behaviour in the digital environment. Research limitations/implications Nevertheless, the significant contributions to YouTube medical decision-making literature, few limitations may give opportunities for future improvements. The study being cross-sectional may not describe causal relationships. Therefore, a longitudinal study ac…

title: The Influence of Secret Consumption, Interactivity, Emotion, and Intimacy on Consumers’ Brand Loyalty in Live Streaming Commerce
abstract: Driven by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021, live streaming shopping emerged as a prevalent consumer choice among residents in Hangzhou, China. This study focuses on exploring the impacts of consumer perceived privacy, platform interactivity, emotional intimacy, and touching emotion on consumer brand loyalty in the context of online live streaming commerce in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province. Essentially, beyond realising direct consumer interaction, the core goal of e-commerce live streaming is to enhance consumers’ recognition of live streaming brands and further consolidate their brand loyalty. In this research, structural equation modelling (SEM) was adopted to construct and verify the hypothetical research framework, and online questionnaires were utilised for data collection and empirical investigation. The empirical results demonstrate that live streaming interactivity and touching emotion significantly and positively promote the formation of consumer emotional intimacy. The results reveal that secret consumption exerts a significant negative effect on intimacy. Moreover, enhanced emotional intimacy is further verified to exert a positive effect on consumer brand loyalty. This research clarifies the internal influencing mechanism of key perceptual factors on brand loyalty in live streaming scenarios. The findings of this study can provide empirical data and practical references f…

title: Measuring Infinite Mindset: A Pilot Comparison of Lower- and Higher-Order Models With Mixed-Format Data
abstract: Infinite Mindset offers a long-term leadership framework, but its measurement hierarchy requires empirical scrutiny. This study assesses measurement feasibility and specification sensitivity using a documented 30-respondent pilot in a plantation-management research context. Reported partial least squares structural equation modeling results were compared across single-construct and repeated-indicator higher-order specifications, without respondent-level re-estimation. Composite reliability was 0.982 in both models, while average variance extracted was 0.689 and 0.690. Direct associations with administrative performance scores were positive, with coefficients of 0.404 and 0.397; neither proposed indirect pathway was statistically supported. An item loading of 0.694 on the overall construct coexisted with a loading of 0.855 on its designated dimension. Reported repairs produced full-rank reduced matrices, but their mapping to fitted item-level models remains unclear. The contribution is a conditional validation pathway separating data feasibility, measurement hierarchy, and external associations. Findings support further instrument development, not definitive validation, causal inference, or higher-order model superiority.

title: High-power spray coagulation as knife-based hemostasis improves procedural efficiency in colorectal underwater endoscopic submucosal dissection
Generative AI in Entrepreneurship: Applications, Opportunities, Challenges and Future Directions
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is transforming entrepreneurship by helping entrepreneurs generate ideas, analyze information, create content, develop business models, support marketing, and make decisions. This review examines the growing role of GenAI in entrepreneurial activities, with a focus on opportunity recognition, creativity, innovation, SMEs, emerging economies, and responsible AI use. GenAI can reduce resource constraints and provide affordable support to small businesses, but challenges such as inaccurate information, overdependence, privacy concerns, and unequal digital skills remain. The article highlights the importance of human–AI collaboration and introduces the concept of AI entrepreneurial capability, which includes AI literacy, effective prompting, evaluation of AI outputs, decision-making, and responsible use of AI. The review concludes that future entrepreneurship should focus not only on using AI to generate more opportunities but also on improving the quality, sustainability, and responsible development of those opportunities.
venue: International Research Journal on Advanced Engineering and Management (IRJAEM)

title: Building people-centered dynamic capabilities for sustainability: An exploratory multilevel study of sustainability-driven enterprises in Indonesia
abstract: Sustainability-driven enterprises (SDEs) in emerging economies depend on people, meaning committed leaders, engaged employees, and prepared successors, yet sustainable human resource management research has largely examined formal practices in large firms in developed economies. This study asks how SDEs in an emerging economy develop the people-based capabilities that sustainability requires, and how multi-stakeholder (Pentahelix) interactions across micro, meso, and macro levels shape that human capital development. Using an exploratory, multi-stage qualitative design based on the Gioia methodology, we interviewed ten experts spanning government, academia, industry, community, and media in Indonesia, then convened an expert panel to validate the emerging themes. The analysis identifies five reciprocal cross-level flows through which human capital for sustainability is built: top-down, bottom-up, a generative loop, informal social networks, and lateral interactions. Macro-level mandates and market pressures set the capability requirements a workforce must meet. Meso-level mechanisms such as management development programs, leadership schools, learning management systems, and “social bricolage” turn those requirements into training and orchestration routines. Micro-level moral agency, spiritual commitment, and value-internalization rituals such as weekly “Value Talks” keep peopl…

title: A system pharmacology framework to explore the therapeutic mechanism of Bushen-Yizhi formula against Alzheimer’s disease via integrating UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, network analysis, machine learning and experimental validation
abstract: Abstract Objective Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an incurable neurodegenerative disease, and Bushen-Yizhi formula (BSYZ) has shown clinical potential for AD treatment, yet its bioactive components and pharmacological mechanisms remain unproven. To explore the therapeutic mechanism of BSYZ against AD-like cognitive impairment, a systems pharmacology framework was established via the integration of UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS, network analysis, machine learning and experimental validation. Materials and methods Chemical composition of BSYZ was characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. A scopolamine (SCOP)-induced mouse model of AD-like cognitive impairment was used to evaluate neuroprotective effects via behavioral, histopathological, and biochemical assays. AD-associated targets were identified by differential expression analysis and WGCNA. Core targets were screened using 127 machine learning models with SHAP interpretation and validated by RT-qPCR. Stage-stratified transcriptomic analysis assessed gene expression across AD stages. Molecular docking and 100-ns MD simulations explored binding of core components to targets. Results One hundred five compounds were identified from BSYZ. In SCOP-treated mice, BSYZ ameliorated cognitive deficits, oxidative stress, cholinergic dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. Bioinformatics uncovered 81 potential AD targets, from which seven core genes (HIPK2, CXCR4, …

title: Mapping the health management journey of patients with cardiac-involved Fabry disease
Environmental, social and governance reporting, audit committee characteristics and readability of annual reports: evidence from an African emerging economy
abstract: Purpose The study examined the moderating effect of audit committee characteristics in the nexus between environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting and annual report readability. Design/methodology/approach The study used archival data from the audited annual reports of 30 firms listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange, spanning the period 2000–2023. A fixed-effects estimator was employed, helping to address the potential issue of unobserved firm-specific heterogeneity in the dataset. However, system GMM was also used for robustness testing and to minimise issues that come with endogeneity as far as econometric estimates are concerned. Findings The result revealed that although ESG reporting could impair the readability of annual reports, in the presence of audit committee characteristics, namely audit committee size, audit committee gender diversity and audit committee meetings, ESG reporting could enhance readability (i.e. understandability) of annual reports. Practical implications While firms may want to ensure accountability and transparency to their numerous stakeholders by way of ESG reporting, it is imperative they do so, having an effective audit committee in place. This can be achieved by way of ensuring a larger audit committee that is gender diversified, but must be cautious in terms of engaging in more meetings. Originality/value The study adds to extant litera…

title: The Relationship Between Assessor Training and Organizational Readiness For LSP Implementation In Higher Education Institutions
abstract: This study aims to analyze the relationship between assessor training and organizational readiness for the implementation of Professional Certification Bodies (LSPs) in higher education institutions. The study employed a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. A total of 23 prospective LSP assessors at Universitas Darunnajah participated as respondents using a saturated sampling technique. Data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model evaluation showed that all indicators met the established validity and reliability criteria based on outer loadings, Average Variance Extracted (AVE), Cronbach’s alpha, and Composite Reliability. The structural model analysis indicated that assessor training had a positive and significant relationship with organizational readiness for LSP implementation, with a t-statistic of 2.003 (>1.960) and a p-value of 0.045 (<0.05). The R-squared value of 0.321 indicates that the model explains 32.1% of the variance in organizational readiness, while the remaining 67.9% is not explained by the variables included in the model. These findings suggest that assessor training is one of the factors associated with organizational readiness in preparing for LSP implementation in higher education institutions. Therefore, comprehensive and con…

title: Infinite Mindset and Self-Assessed Rice Farmer Capacity: Digital, Dynamic, and Managerial Pathways in West Aceh, Indonesia
abstract: Long-term orientations may support agricultural continuity, but their relationship with rice farmer capacity depends on more operational capabilities. This study examines digital capability, dynamic capability, and managerial competence as parallel statistical pathways linking infinite mindset to self-assessed rice farmer capacity in West Aceh, Indonesia. Descriptive analysis and independent partial least squares path modelling used the same 90 rice farmers, retaining 32 indicators and the direct mindset–capacity path. One missing capacity response was replaced by its observed indicator mean; an 89-case complete-response model provided a sensitivity check. Inference used 5,000 respondent-level bootstrap resamples, supplemented by location-cluster resampling and alternative specifications. Infinite mindset was positively associated with digital capability (β = 0.363), dynamic capability (β = 0.551), and managerial competence (β = 0.447). In the primary model, only managerial competence had a capacity association excluding zero (β = 0.560; 95% interval: 0.300–0.781). Its indirect association was 0.250 (0.122–0.418) and remained positive across the principal checks. Digital-path inference changed under location resampling, while the primary direct, digital-indirect, and dynamic-indirect intervals included zero. Capacity R² was 0.447, but restrictive-model residual diagnostics limi…

title: Research on the Construction of an Ideological and Political Evaluation System for College English Courses Based on OBE
abstract: Against the backdrop of Great Ideological and Political Education, College English courses urgently need to construct a scientific evaluation system for ideological and political education, so as to address the existing problems in the current evaluation system, such as vague standards and missing process data. Under the guidance of the OBE concept and in combination with rubrics, this paper constructs a "four-dimensional" ideological and political evaluation system for College English courses. Driven by objectives, advanced through processes, and verified by outcomes, this four-dimensional system integrates diagnostic evaluation at the initial stage of teaching, dynamic formative evaluation and ability-integrated evaluation during the process, and summative evaluation after the course. This system can help teachers enhance their capacity to implement curriculum-based ideological and political education, and effectively improve the scientificity and operability of the ideological and political evaluation system for College English courses.

title: The influence of lakes and reservoirs on estimated flood peaks at hourly vs. daily timescale in the Alps
abstract: Water bodies such as lakes and reservoirs can play a crucial role in reducing estimated flood peaks, at both daily and hourly time resolution. While the effect of water bodies on flood peaks has been demonstrated in the past at different time resolutions, it remains unclear how water bodies affect the ratio between estimated daily and hourly quantiles, that is, to which degree their attenuation effect is scale dependent. Here, we analyse how water bodies influence this ratio using two approaches: (1) by comparing estimated daily and hourly flood peak quantiles upstream and downstream of reservoirs of four local case studies, and (2) by comparing daily and hourly flood peak quantiles across a large sample of catchments in Switzerland with various degrees of water-body influence. Our results show that reservoirs dampen hourly peak discharge much more strongly than daily peak discharge, which leads to similar daily and hourly flood peaks downstream of reservoirs. Specifically, our case study analysis highlights that (sub-)hourly peak discharge is attenuated by up to 70 % downstream of reservoirs during flood events with a 10-year return period. We also find that the attenuation effect is particularly pronounced in catchments that are heavily influenced by water bodies, i.e. those catchments where more than 60 % of the area contributes to water body inflow. title: Comparative Qualitative Phytochemical Profiling of Common Medicinal Plant Leaves Found in Kerala
abstract: The present study provides a comparative qualitative phytochemical screening of aqueous leaf extracts of four medicinal plants commonly available in Kerala, India: guava (Psidium guajava), karinochi (Vitex negundo), bottlebrush (Callistemon sp.), and vathakodi (Justicia gendarussa). Leaf extracts were prepared under two extraction conditions using 5 g of leaf material in 50 mL of deionised water: reflux extraction at 100 °C for 1 h and mild heating at 80 °C for 30 min. The resulting extracts were subjected to qualitative colour and precipitation tests to detect alkaloids, flavonoids, glycosides, saponins, steroids, tannins, phenols, terpenoids, carbohydrates, proteins, coumarins, quinones, anthraquinones, phlobatannins, and unsaturated compounds. All four plant extracts exhibited a diverse phytochemical profile, with flavonoids, glycosides, saponins, steroids, and unsaturated compounds consistently detected under both extraction conditions. Anthraquinones were not detected in any of the investigated extracts. Differences were observed in the phytochemical profiles depending on plant species and extraction conditions. Alkaloids were detected following extraction at 80 °C but were not detected after prolonged reflux at 100 °C, suggesting possible thermal degradation or alteration of alkaloid constituents. Developmental Trajectories of Alcohol, Mental Health and Physical Health among American Indian and First Nation Adolescents: Understanding the Role of Land-Based Cultural Engagement, Family, and Peers
abstract: Abstract We applied the Indigenous Traditional Ecological Knowledge (ITEK) framework to understand patterns of wellbeing among American Indian and First Nation (AI/FN) adolescents; risks and protective factors associated with alcohol use, mental health, and physical health that can be translated into prevention intervention strategies. Latent profile analysis and growth mixture modeling (GMM) were applied to identify and examine patterns of change among distinct subgroups of AI/FN youth (Wave 1 N = 735, M age = 11.09, 50.2% female) residing on or near a Tribal Nation or Reserve on the role of land-based cultural activity participation, family warmth and support, and having risk-taking peers at baseline. GMM explored how risk and protective factors were related to trajectories of alcohol use, mental health symptoms, and physical health across five waves. Four trajectory groups were identified: (1) Prosocial, low cultural engagement (62%); (2) High-risk profile (11%); (3) Risk-taking peers, mixed engagement (21%); and (4) Prosocial, high cultural and family engagement (5%). Having more risk-taking peers increased risk for alcohol use, symptoms of depression and anxiety, and lower physical health. High land-based cultural activity participation with high family warmth and support decreased risk for alcohol use and mental health indicators and lower physical health with trajectorie…

title: PCA-Lasso-based forecasting of agricultural water use and identification of key predictor variables in inland river basins of Northwest China
abstract: Introduction Agricultural water use in inland river basins of northwestern China is affected by multiple interacting factors, and the associated indicators often show strong collinearity. Methods To address these issues, this study developed a hybrid prediction model based on principal component analysis (PCA) and Lasso regression to establish an interpretable agricultural water-use prediction framework for arid inland river basins. Twenty indicators describing meteorology, water-use structure, water resources, and socioeconomic conditions in the Heihe River Basin from 2001 to 2023 were used for correlation analysis and PCA. An expanding-window time-series cross-validation scheme was then applied to determine the Lasso regularization parameter, and model performance was evaluated using R 2 , root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). Results Agricultural water use ranged from 24.01 × 108 to 32.20 × 108 m 3 , accounting for 77.26–85.72% of total water supply. It declined by 21.20% from 2001 to 2012, rebounded markedly in 2013, and generally decreased after 2014. Correlation analysis showed that several groups of indicators had correlation coefficients above 0.80. Marketing Margins, Distribution Efficiency, and Retail Price Gaps of MinyaKita Cooking Oil in Baturaja, Indonesia
abstract: Affordable cooking oil requires distribution arrangements that control costs without weakening consumer access. Evidence on how these objectives interact within regulated industrial food channels remains context dependent. This study examines MinyaKita distribution in Baturaja, Indonesia, using a descriptive comparison of interviews and observations involving two distributors, three sub-distributors, and thirty-two retailers. Marketing margins, recorded costs, profits, producer’s shares, and retail price gaps were examined, with separate arithmetic checks of respondent-level tabulations. The reported consumer price was 20,212 rupiah per liter in the channel involving retailers and 19,500 rupiah in the channel where a sub-distributor sold directly to consumers. Their respective marketing margins were 5,512 and 4,800 rupiah, while producer’s shares were 72.73% and 75.38%. Both prices exceeded the 15,700-rupiah retail ceiling. The shorter channel offered a relative price and recorded-cost advantage, but the longer channel provided more retail access points and a narrower range of profit-to-cost ratios. Appendix-based checks preserved the direction of the price comparison. The study contributes to a distinction between relative distribution performance and regulated affordability: reducing intermediation alone does not demonstrate price compliance, equitable returns, or superior co…

Chip price shocks and CO2 emissions in Brazil
abstract: Purpose We examined the impact of chip price shocks on fluctuations in Brazilian macroeconomic variables and carbon emissions (CO2). Design/methodology/approach Employing a global vector autoregressive model from January 1995 to December 2019, we constructed a representation of the world economy to capture spillover effects. Findings Our analysis revealed that chip price shocks lead to reductions in imports, industrial production and CO2 emissions. Investigation into transmission channels suggested that chip prices influence emissions through their effects on industrial production and international trade. Our shock identification underscored that supply chain disruptions lead to cleaner production processes, driven by increased green investments and renewable energy production rather than by the consumption of renewable energy. Our findings suggest that companies shift their operations toward cleaner energy sources. We further show that US carbon emissions significantly contribute to Brazilian CO2 variance. Practical implications These results emphasize the significant influence of chip prices in precipitating economic downturns, fostering cleaner production practices among companies and altering gas emissions in an emerging market economy. title: Development and external validation of an explainable machine learning model for identifying depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older adults with low haemoglobin: a prediction-model study
abstract: Background Early screening for depressive symptoms in middle-aged and older adults is important for timely risk identification. Low haemoglobin may identify a clinically accessible vulnerable subgroup in which chronic disease burden, fatigue, functional impairment, and reduced physiological reserve often coexist. However, it should be understood as a high-risk phenotype rather than a direct measure of nutritional deficiency or frailty. Evidence in this population remains limited. Methods This study developed a model using data from the 2015 China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), with CHARLS 2011 and a cross-sectional cohort from Gansu Provincial People’s Hospital used for temporal and external validation, respectively. Depressive symptoms were defined as a 10-item Centre for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale score ≥10. Candidate variables included sociodemographic, behavioural, health status, functional, cognitive, and comorbidity-related information. After least absolute shrinkage and selection operator feature selection, 16 variables were retained. Seven machine learning models were compared, and Random Forest was retained for interpretation and online tool development based on its balanced performance and interpretability. Deep learning-based prediction of diffusion MRI responses from microvascular OCT angiograms
abstract: Abstract Objective. Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) signals are sensitive to microvascular geometry and hemodynamics, but current approaches rely on computationally intensive simulations on optical coherence tomography (OCT)-derived vascular graphs. We investigated whether three-dimensional deep learning models can serve as fast surrogates that predict diffusion MRI responses directly from microvascular OCT angiograms. Approach. Five mouse cortical OCT angiograms were segmented into 4792 vascular subgraphs and converted into nine-channel image volumes encoding vascular geometry, magnetic field gradient, hematocrit, oxygen saturation, partial oxygen pressure, blood velocity magnitude, and three velocity components. For each sample, a physics-based framework generated spin echo (SE) and diffusion-weighted signals for three b -values (50, 100, 500 s mm − 2 ), three gradient timing pairs, and ten gradient directions. We trained five 3D architectures (AutoEncoder, BasicUNet, DenseNet169, EfficientNetB4 and ResNet) with late fusion of acquisition parameters and evaluated performance using MSE, MAE and R 2 . Main results. Under within-distribution (random-split) evaluation, test R 2 values were at least 0.87. DenseNet169 achieved the best overall accuracy (MSE = 0.0039 ± 0.0029 , MAE = 0.0397 ± 0.0161 , R 2 = 0.92 ) and maintained R 2 > 0.80 across all diffusion settings, w…

title: Explainable machine learning for preoperative prediction of acute kidney injury after intertrochanteric fracture surgery in older adults
abstract: Background Acute kidney injury (AKI) is an important postoperative complication in older patients undergoing surgery for intertrochanteric femoral fracture. This study aimed to develop and internally evaluate an explainable model for preoperative AKI risk assessment. Methods This retrospective study included 616 patients aged ≥60 years, including 54 (8.8%) who developed postoperative AKI. Candidate predictors were processed and selected using development-cohort data, and seven machine-learning algorithms were compared. Model performance was assessed across 100 repeated stratified 70/30 partitions and by 500-repetition model-specific and complete-pipeline bootstrap analyses. Calibration, decision-curve analysis, and SHAP were used to evaluate and interpret the selected model. Results The reported Naive Bayes model comprised baseline serum creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, chloride, uric acid, and chronic kidney disease or renal insufficiency. Across 100 repeated partitions, its mean validation AUC was 0.7231 (SD, 0.0260). The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.8004 for the fixed five-predictor Naive Bayes specification and 0.756 when the complete development pipeline was repeated; the latter analysis yielded a corrected Brier score of 0.084, calibration intercept of 0.02, and calibration slope of 1.70. title: Establishing standardized evaluation protocols for peptide-target interaction prediction: the PTI-TAPE consensus framework eDelphi
abstract: Computational peptide-target interaction (PTI) prediction has advanced rapidly as a tool for drug discovery, yet the field lacks agreed evaluation standards. Discrepancies in metrics, negative sampling strategies, and dataset construction across publications currently render cross-study comparisons methodologically intractable, ultimately impeding the clinical translation of therapeutic peptides. To resolve this, we present PTI-TAPE (Peptide-Target Interaction—Tasks Assessing Peptide Engagement), a standardised benchmarking framework developed via a structured three-round eDelphi consensus study with 15 international experts spanning computational biology, machine learning, and regulatory science. Operating under a robust consensus threshold (>80% agreement), the panel established 26 definitive standards across eight domains, governed by the new STRIDE (Standardisation, Transparency, Representativeness, Integration, Discovery, Evidence) framework. Key outcomes include mandating specific primary metrics for affinity and structure, enforcing a tiered negative sampling hierarchy that prioritizes experimental non-binders, and requiring mandatory temporal dataset splits. By providing a unified reporting checklist, benchmark specifications, and a biennial governance structure, PTI-TAPE ensures reproducible evaluation and fair method comparison, bridging the gap between computation…

Thermal Error Prediction of a Three-Axis CNC Machine Tool using an Artificial Neural Network with Optimized Hidden-Neuron Architecture
abstract: Thermal errors are one of the major factors that affect the positioning accuracy of CNC machine tools and hence the quality of the manufactured products. Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have been extensively used for modeling the thermal errors, but the impact of hidden-layer architecture on the prediction accuracy remains insufficiently explored. In this study, a Neuron-Optimized Artificial Neural Network (NO-ANN) model is proposed for predicting the thermal positioning errors of a three-axis CNC machine tool. The effect of the hidden-layer neuron configuration was systematically examined to determine the optimal configuration to capture the nonlinear relationship between the thermal variations and positioning errors. The model performance was assessed by Coefficient of Determination (R2), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error (MAE). The optimized architecture of 11 hidden neurons demonstrated the highest overall performance, with an R2 value of 0.998, RMSE of 1.3247 μm, and MAE of 0.6539 μm, and the model showed high accuracy in both training and testing sets, indicating its robustness and generalization ability. Compared with previously reported thermal error prediction models, the proposed NO-ANN achieved comparable or superior predictive accuracy while requiring only 11 hidden neurons, indicating reduced model complexity and improved computational effici…

Intelligent Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Power Transformers Using Machine Learning
abstract: Background: Power transformers play an integral role in power generation and transmission. Transformer failures can lead to service interruptions, reduce system reliability, and incur significant failure-related costs. Efficient transformer maintenance requires accurate condition assessment and effective maintenance decision-making. Objective: The purpose of this paper is to develop a machine-learning-based decision-support framework for power transformer maintenance that integrates health index estimation, Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, and Life Cycle Cost (LCC) evaluation. Methods: The framework draws on multimodal monitoring data from 166 oil-immersed power transformers collected over a ten-year period. Six machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Convolutional Neural Networks, Ridge Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbors) were evaluated using various feature sets. Results: Among the evaluated models, XGBoost achieved the best performance under the basic feature configuration, with an RMSE of 0.285 years, an MAE of 0.199 years, and an R² of 0.956. The robustness evaluation showed that the model retained satisfactory predictive performance under moderate feature reduction. Based on the Life Cycle Cost assumptions applied in this study, the predictive maintenance scenario was estimated to reduce the total cost of the transformer fleet b…

title: Prediction of flow maldistribution in 3D-printed water-flow distributors for thermal-fluid system design
abstract: Flow distributors are important components in water-flow and compact thermal-fluid systems because non-uniform flow division among parallel channels can disturb pressure balance and convective heat-transfer stability. However, evaluating distributor performance through repeated experimental trials and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations can be time-consuming during early-stage design. This work develops an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted framework for predicting and classifying flow maldistribution in 3D-printed water-flow distributors using combined experimental and CFD-supported data. The dataset was obtained from water-flow measurements of rectangular distributors, conical distributors with an obstacle, and conical distributors without obstacle, while the CFD-supported dataset included Volume of Fluid (VOF) and single-phase flow results for selected conical configurations. Distributor family, height, flow rate, data source, and simulation method were used as input variables, while the non-uniformity flow coefficient, Φ, was used as the prediction target. An Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) regression model was developed to estimate Φ, and a classification layer was used to assign maldistribution severity levels. Convxtmob-Net: A Quantum -Secure Stacked Ensemble Model for Diabetic Retinopathy Severity Prediction and Classification
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) is one of the leading causes of vision loss worldwide. With proper and timely diagnosis, vision loss can be prevented. Especially when grading is automated to improve timely decision-making by physicians. In this work, a new quantum-secure stacked ensemble approach to the DR severity classification task is proposed. To tackle the data leakage issue in clinical grading, the ConvXtMob-Net accepts out-of-the-ordinary predictions and collaboratively learns from multiple models with various topologies. Provides a Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (ML-KEM) for secure data transmission and simulated Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) for mathematically protecting proprietary model weights to tackle new security challenges in medical data transmission and edge development. ConvXtMob-Net implemented the solution and carried out a large number of experiments on the APTOS 2019 dataset, and the DDRs were 97.9% and 98.2%. Consistent Quadratic weighted kappa values of 0.97 testify to remarkable agreement in correspondence to the expert’s grading. The results indicate that the combination of stacked ensemble and post-quantum cryptography is a very precise, robust, and secure approach for automated clinical diagnostic systems.

title: HQML-ICU: hybrid quantum-classical machine learning for ICU mortality prediction using MIMIC-IV electronic health records
abstract: Accurate prediction of mortality in the intensive care unit (ICU) is crucial for informing clinical decision-making and optimizing resource allocation. Although machine learning methodologies have enhanced traditional severity-of-illness scoring systems, they encounter intrinsic limitations in modeling complex feature interactions within electronic health record (EHR) data. In this study, we introduced a hybrid quantum-classical machine learning (HQML) framework for predicting ICU mortality, evaluated using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV, version 2.2) database. Our methodology incorporates a classical autoencoder for dimensionality reduction (from 87 features to 16 latent dimensions), a 4-qubit parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) utilizing ZZFeatureMap encoding and RealAmplitudes variational ansatz ( L = 3 layers, 48 trainable parameters), and a classical post-processing layer. In a retrospective cohort of 38,624 ICU admissions (12.8% mortality rate), the HQML model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.871 (95% CI: 0.859–0.883), outperforming XGBoost (0.858; 95% CI: 0.844–0.872), deep neural network (0.847), random forest (0.838), logistic regression (0.813), and SAPS-II (0.771). The improvement over XGBoost was statistically significant (DeLong p = 0.012) and corroborated by 5-fold cross-validation. The m…

title: Explainable AI in educational data mining: LightGBM and SHAP for enhancing learner performance prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of learner performance is essential for adaptive educational systems and personalized learning. However, the integration of advanced gradient-boosting models with established educational frameworks remains underexplored, particularly when predictive performance and interpretability are considered jointly. This study evaluates Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) within three established learner-modeling frameworks—Item Response Theory (IRT), Performance Factor Analysis (PFA), and Dynamic Aspects of Student Skill with History (DAS3H)—across seven real-world educational datasets. LightGBM is compared with traditional logistic regression using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC) and accuracy as evaluation metrics. To further assess model interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are employed to identify the contributions of user-, item-, and skill-level features to learner performance predictions. Results show that LightGBM generally improves predictive performance compared with logistic regression, particularly in capturing nonlinear relationships, temporal patterns, and skill-dependent learner behaviors. The SHAP analysis further provides insights into the relative importance of different feature types, enhancing the interpretability of the predictive models. Machine learning prediction of rheumatoid arthritis using the gut microbiome shows limited cross-cohort generalizability
abstract: Abstract Machine-learning models trained on gut microbiome data often achieve encouraging performance within individual cohorts, but their ability to generalize across independent populations remains uncertain. Although rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with alterations in gut microbial composition, it remains unclear whether these differences yield robust and transferable predictive signatures. We analyzed 16 S rRNA gut microbiome profiles from 2,238 participants, including 1,034 with RA and 1,204 healthy controls (HC). Alpha diversity, Bray–Curtis beta diversity, and differential abundance were evaluated. Four machine-learning algorithms—least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression, random forest, support vector machine with a radial basis function kernel, and XGBoost—were benchmarked using 638 prevalence-filtered ASVs, an 80/20 stratified train-test split, and five-fold cross-validation. Model stability was assessed across 30 repeated stratified train-test splits. Secondary genus-level analyses used an independently tuned XGBoost model to evaluate abundance-transformation sensitivity and permutation-importance stability. Leakage-free ANCOM-BC2 feature selection was performed within each training partition, with independent tuning of the reduced-feature models. For external validation, raw paired-end FASTQ data from an independent Shanghai…

title: Candidate molecular endotypes and dynamic risk prediction in anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease: a systematic scoping review
abstract: Background Anti-melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 antibody-positive dermatomyositis (anti-MDA5+ DM) spans pulmonary states from no detectable interstitial lung disease (ILD) to rapidly progressive ILD (RP-ILD). We mapped molecular programs and prediction evidence to determine how recurrent biological states may support dynamic stratification. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, Ovid and Embase were searched from inception to 22 August 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR; evidence was synthesized across molecular and prediction domains. Results Of 4, 166 records, 2, 317 remained after deduplication, 349 underwent full-text assessment, and 95 sources (80 primary studies and 15 syntheses) were included. Type I/III interferon signaling was the most reproducible program. Myeloid inflammatory-remodeling, adaptive activation with lymphocyte or natural-killer-cell loss, vascular-coagulation injury, and immunometabolic disturbance formed additional overlapping axes aligned with pulmonary-state transitions. Clinical and radiomic models showed strong short-term discrimination; harmonized landmarks, calibration, geographic validation, and decision-timed molecular sampling would strengthen clinical use. Conclusion The evidence supports an integrated map linking recurrent molecular programs to dynamic pulmonary risk. A …

title: CapExchange: protocol for a pilot feasibility study of a capacity-exchange programme for mental health recovery
abstract: Abstract Background People living with severe mental disorders are often approached primarily through the lens of deficits and functional limitations. Yet many possess practical skills, relational capacities, and everyday knowledge that can circulate meaningfully within their environment. Recovery-oriented literature describes autonomy, empowerment, and social inclusion, but offers fewer operational models for recognising social contribution in the present moment. CapExchange is a psychosocial rehabilitation programme based on service exchange between service users and their community environment, grounded in the concepts of circular mutuality and micro-social contribution. This study aims to assess the feasibility and acceptability of CapExchange within a French overseas territory psychosocial rehabilitation service, and to inform a decision on progression to a definitive study. Secondary aims are to explore preliminary effects on well-being and self-perceived social contribution, and to document exchanges carried out during the programme. Methods This mixed-methods pilot feasibility study is conducted across three sites of the Psychosocial Rehabilitation Service, EPSM de la Guadeloupe: the Unité Passerelle (transitional inpatient rehabilitation unit), a day rehabilitation unit, and the UREPS (outpatient rehabilitation unit). Sessions are delivered in person in a minimum of tw…

title: How do middle-income states select vaccine partners? Projected capacity across sectors in Argentina
abstract: Abstract How do governments select vaccine-production partners when sector-specific capacity is incomplete? The COVID-19 pandemic made this question especially pressing, as vaccine nationalism constrained external supply and pushed middle-income states to expand domestic production despite unproven capacities. Tracing Argentina’s vaccine strategy from 2020 to 2022, this article develops the concept of projected capacity: a mechanism through which states infer potential capacity in one sector from firms’ resources, credibility, and structural position in another. Policymakers rely on proxies for vaccine-production capacity, including industrial legacies, firm–state familiarity, and alignment with health-sovereignty goals. State selection then provides firms with resources, alliances, and legitimacy, transforming projected capacity into sector-specific structural power. The article contributes to debates in political economy and public policy by showing that structural power is not only a pre-existing source of influence over the state; it can also be created through state decisions that select and support firms.

title: Organizational capacity supporting STEAM implementation in early childhood education: a mixed-methods study
abstract: STEAM education in early childhood settings requires not only teaching and learning resources but also organizational conditions that support their use in educational practice. This study examined resource provision and the broader organizational context associated with STEAM implementation in Lithuanian early childhood education institutions using a sequential mixed-methods design. The quantitative component drew on national survey data from 831 institutions and examined teaching and learning resource provision. The subsequent qualitative component involved open-ended responses from 38 educational leaders from institutions included in the quantitative dataset and explored their perspectives on resources, professional learning, collaboration, leadership practices, and barriers associated with STEAM implementation. The quantitative findings revealed variation in resource provision levels across curriculum areas and resource types. Within “Exploring and Understanding the Environment,” several resources showed provision levels above 70%, whereas the provision level for specialized STEAM laboratory kits was 30.01%. Qualitative findings showed that material resources and digital technologies were the most frequently identified resource subcategory ( n = 27), followed by teachers’ STEAM competencies ( n = 23). title: The impact of human-AI co-creation on perceived creativity in generative AI art: a serial mediation mechanism of psychological ownership, perceived agency, and creative flow
abstract: Introduction Generative AI is shifting digital art from one-step generation toward interactive human-AI co-creation. Across two between-subject experiments ( N = 600), we examined how creation mode and prespecified AI-involvement workflows related to perceived creativity. Methods In Study 1, participants completed digital art tasks under human-only creation, AI-only generation, or human-AI co-creation conditions. In Study 2, three workflows differing in AI involvement (low, moderate, high) were evaluated. Psychological ownership, perceived agency, creative flow, and perceived creativity were measured. Results In Study 1, human-AI co-creation produced higher perceived-creativity ratings than AI-only generation, with indirect effects consistent with a serial pathway through psychological ownership, perceived agency, and creative flow. In Study 2, the moderate-involvement workflow yielded higher perceived-creativity ratings and psychological states than the low- and high-involvement workflows. Discussion Perceived creativity in generative-AI art depends on how users experience contribution, control, and engagement during creation. Within the workflows tested, balancing generative assistance with consequential user choice fosters the most favorable subjective creativity evaluations.

Based on the skeletal-muscle dual stem cell chemotaxis and bidirectional differentiation mechanism to reinterpret the “sinew-bone interdependence” theory
abstract: The “sinew-bone interdependence” theory is a core paradigm in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) orthopedics and traumatology. Rooted in the visceral manifestation doctrine of “the liver governing sinews and the kidney governing bones,” this theory emphasizes the structural dependency, functional synergy, and pathological inter-transmission between sinews and bones. However, traditional interpretive pathways have largely remained at the level of descriptive deduction concerning anatomy, visceral manifestations, and biomechanics, failing to elucidate the cellular executors and molecular mechanisms underpinning the sinew-bone association. In this theoretical article, we propose a hypothesis that intercellular communication between skeletal muscle satellite cells (MuSCs) and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) may provide a cellular-molecular basis for this classical theory. This article systematically reviews the molecular identity of MuSCs and BMSCs, the molecular basis of stem cell chemotaxis centered on the SDF-1/CXCR4 axis, and the existing evidence for the bidirectional chemotaxis of these two stem cell types. It further analyzes the network characteristics of the Wnt/β-catenin, BMP/Smad, and Notch signaling pathways in regulating lineage specification and the research progress on multi-target interventions by Chinese herbal medicines. title: IJODIY TA'LIM MUHITIDA O'Z-O'ZINI TARBIYALASH TEXNOLOGIYALARI: REFLEKSIV MEXANIZM TAHLILI
abstract: The article analyses students' self-education technologies in a creative educational environment from the standpoint of the reflective mechanism. The aim of the study is to provide a theoretical justification of the reflective core of these technologies and to identify directions for their improvement. The study relies on theoretical analysis, conceptual differentiation, a systems approach and modelling. Drawing a distinction between "pedagogical technology" and "psychological mechanism", the author argues that the external, stage-based form of a technology must be separated from its internal driving core. The defining features of a creative educational environment - the absence of a single correct answer and the plurality of evaluation criteria - deprive external assessment of its regulatory monopoly, so the criterion has to migrate into the internal structure of the personality. The principal mechanism performing this transfer is reflection. The article identifies five pedagogical functions of reflection and proposes a seven-stage spiral model of the reflective mechanism. On this basis, six directions for improving self-education technologies are outlined, together with the risks of formalising reflection.

title: Specific expertise from diffuse feedback: A feedforward-gated mechanism
abstract: Perceptual learning improves sensory sensitivity through practice but is typically specific to trained stimuli. Two contrasting accounts have been proposed: fine-tuning of feature-selective neurons in early sensory cortex, which raises a stability-plasticity dilemma, and reweighting of stable sensory inputs by higher-level readout. To reconcile these views, we recorded neuronal populations in macaque visual area V4 during training on a camouflaged collinear contour detection task. Behavioral improvements were strictly orientation specific, yet learning-related neural enhancements were unexpectedly widespread, regardless of neuronal tuning. Critically, these enhancements were confined to late, feedback-influenced response components, whereas early feedforward activity remained stable. These results support a feedforward-gated feedback mechanism: Learning potentiates higher-order representations that deliver diffuse feedback, broadly recruiting early cortical neurons, while behavioral specificity arises because this modulation is gated by feature-selective feedforward inputs associated with the trained stimulus. Rather than being sequestered in a single locus or process, perceptual expertise emerges from hierarchical, bidirectional interactions that enable learning while preserving core sensory stability.

title: Perceived Effectiveness of Lupong Tagapamayapa’s Dispute Resolution Mechanism in Antipas, North Cotabato
abstract: This study examined the perceived effectiveness of the Lupong Tagapamayapa’s dispute resolution mechanisms in Antipas, North Cotabato and determined whether perceptions differed according to respondents’ age, educational attainment, and gender. The study employed a quantitative descriptive-comparative research design and included 260 respondents from the municipality’s 13 barangays. The respondents included Lupong Tagapamayapa members and barangay officials directly involved in dispute resolution, as well as community constituents with previous experience of or familiarity with the Katarungang Pambarangay process. Participants were selected through purposive quota and convenience-quota sampling. Perceived effectiveness was assessed in terms of arbitration, conciliation, and mediation using a structured questionnaire, while frequencies, percentages, means, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance, and post hoc comparisons were used to analyze the data. The Lupong Tagapamayapa’s dispute resolution mechanisms obtained a Very High overall perceived-effectiveness rating (M = 4.55, SD = 0.518). Arbitration obtained the highest domain mean (M = 4.68), followed by mediation (M = 4.51) and conciliation (M = 4.46). title: JWST detection of methane emission from a young brown dwarf
abstract: In recent studies, we used low-resolution spectroscopy (R∼100) with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) to uncover low-mass brown dwarfs (2--10 M_ Jup) in the young cluster IC 348 that exhibit the so-called 3.4 μm absorption band from aliphatic hydrocarbons. Atmospheric models have not predicted the presence of that band in brown dwarfs at any age. Instead, methane absorption is expected in the coolest newborn brown dwarfs, but it was not detected. We have performed JWST spectroscopy at a higher resolution (R on one of the brown dwarfs in IC 348, LRL 11001 (sim6 M_̊m Jup). The new measurement of the 3.4 μm band is fit well with four Gaussians that represent the CH stretching modes of CH_2 and CH_3 groups, indicating that the carrier is a large alkane (C_nH_2n+2). In addition, the spectrum contains emission lines at 3.324 and 3.333 μm, which we attribute to Q branches of CH_4 hot bands between the octad and dyad regions (primarily ν_3+ν_4̊ightarrowν_4) and the tetradecad and pentad regions. This is the first detection of 3.33 μm CH_4 emission from a young brown dwarf. The emission probably arises from the photosphere rather than a circumstellar disk given that no disks around stars or brown dwarfs are known to exhibit emission in these transitions. Modeling of the emission is needed to constrain the excitation mechanism, which could be either thermal (e.g., an accretion shock)…

title: Characteristics of fume components and dynamic emission behavior of crumb-rubber-modified asphalt
abstract: Introduction Crumb-rubber-modified asphalt (CRMA) facilitates the recycling of end-of-life tires but may release complex fumes during high-temperature processing. This study characterized the dynamic fume evolution and representative organic components of CRMA. Methods An integrated system combining controlled fume generation, real-time monitoring, and offline collection was developed. Volatile organic compound (VOC) responses from four asphalt binders were monitored at 120–200 °C. The H₂S and SO₂ responses of CRMA were quantified, and the detectable organic components in fumes from CRMA and its corresponding base asphalt were analyzed using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry. Results The VOC concentration–time profiles were reproducible, with relative deviations below 10% during the principal response stages. VOC responses increased with temperature, generally peaking before gradually approaching a slowly varying stage. At 200 °C, the peak VOC concentration of CRMA reached 3,719.1 mg/m³, approximately 5.5 times that of the base asphalt. As the temperature increased from 120 to 200 °C, the cumulative responses of H₂S and SO₂ increased from 265 to 1,035 ppm·min and from 3,785 to 5,715 ppm·min, respectively. CRMA also exhibited more resolved chromatographic peaks, with isoprene-related compounds, benzothiazole derivatives, benzothiophene, and dibenzothiophene forming representa…

Synergistic impacts of low-carbon city pilot policy and information consumption pilot policy on carbon lock-in
abstract: Introduction Carbon lock-in poses a significant barrier to the low-carbon transition, necessitating synergistic policy interventions. Methods Using a dual machine learning (DML) model, this study estimates carbon lock-in data for 262 Chinese cities and examines how the dual policy (the low-carbon city pilot and information consumption pilot policy) affects carbon lock-in. Results The dual policy significantly suppresses carbon lock-in, with a markedly stronger effect than implementing either policy in isolation. The analysis indicates that the dual policy works through industrial structure upgrading, government environmental support, climate technology innovation, and public climate concern. Additionally, the heterogeneity test reveals that the suppressive effect is more pronounced in non-resource-based cities, large cities, and those with high market vitality and strong financial regulation. Discussion Consequently, this study provides evidence for promoting the synergistic implementation of the low-carbon city pilot and the information consumption pilot policy, thereby breaking carbon lock-in.
