Plant Sugar Transporters (SWEET): An Emerging Role in Carbon–Lipid Homeostasis
abstract: Abstract In plants, the directed distribution of photosynthetic products from source organs to heterotrophic sink organs forms the material basis for biomass accumulation and crop yield. SWEETs (sugars will eventually be exported transporters) facilitate passive sucrose efflux to link source and sink transport during phloem loading for plant carbon allocation. However, it remains unclear how SWEET-mediated sugar transport coordinates carbon allocation and lipid metabolism. Therefore, this Review integrates the structural evolution, transport mechanisms, and physiological functions of SWEETs. It investigates how SWEET-mediated sucrose transport establishes carbon availability and potentially links sugar-signaling networks to fatty acid biosynthesis. Furthermore, it discusses how the SWEET-mediated carbon flux influences seed oil accumulation by modulating intracellular carbon flux and acetyl-CoA production. Finally, the potential applications of biotechnology to regulate SWEET gene expression are outlined to enhance the carbon-to-lipid conversion efficiency and develop crops with superior traits.
venue: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry

title: Proton-Exchange Surface Engineering Enables Air-Stable Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes for Carbon-Neutral Energy Storage
abstract: Abstract O3-type layered oxides have emerged as one of the most promising cathode candidates for sodium-ion batteries, which are widely regarded as a key enabling technology for carbon-neutral grid-scale energy storage. However, their practical application is hindered by surface degradation upon air exposure and structural distortion from Mn3+. Herein, we develop a two-step surface engineering protocol that combines proton-exchange washing with a short postcalcination to treat O3-type cathodes. Proton-exchange treatment removes surface carbonates and oxidizes Mn3+ to widen the interlayers for enhanced Na+ diffusion and Jahn–Teller suppression, while the subsequent short calcination heals residual defects and locks in the refined structure. The optimally treated Na0.82Cu0.19Fe0.39Mn0.42O2 cathode delivers a reversible capacity of 110.2 mAh g–1 at 0.2 C with 92.3% retention after 100 cycles (substantially outperforming the pristine sample at 48.6%), while retaining its superior performance even after one month of air exposure. This cost‑effective and scalable surface engineering approach thus removes a critical industrial bottleneck for sodium‑ion batteries, marking a tangible step toward sustainable storage technologies for the zero‑carbon transition.

title: Peatland Degradation Alters the Microbial–carbon–water Table Interactions that Regulate Carbon Storage
abstract: Abstract Peatlands store one-third of global soil carbon while covering only 3% of the world’s land area. Degradation through drainage, grazing, and fire can disrupt the microbial processes that regulate peat decomposition and carbon stabilisation. How these disturbances reshape microbial-carbon-water table interactions remains poorly understood. This study examined how peatland degradation influences microbial community composition and their interactions with peat organic matter chemistry and water table position. Three peatland sites including one degraded and two intact sites on the Bogong High Plains, Australia were studied. Our results demonstrated that microbial communities differed significantly between the three peatland sites and were associated with position relative to the water table, peat carbon chemistry, and depth in the profile. Notably, intact peats retained strong depth and water table dependent heterogeneity in fungal and prokaryotic communities, while these relationships were markedly weaker or absent in degraded peats. In intact peats, fungal and prokaryote community structure was strongly associated with carbon concentration and C:N ratio, while variations in the microbial community structure of degraded peats were more linked to labile and recalcitrant carbon functional groups (alkyl, N-alkyl, O-alkyl, di-O-alkyl, aryl, O-aryl and ketone). title: Hybrid Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube–Nanocellulose Networks as Current-Collector-Free Electrodes
abstract: Abstract Hybrid nanoarchitectures that combine structural functionality of nanocellulose (NC) with electrical conductivity of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) are of growing interest for electroanalytical electrode design. However, CNT:NC hybrid film electrodes reported to date typically rely on separate conductive substrates, require binders, and rarely establish systematic relationships between processing, structure, and electrochemical performance. Here, we develop intrinsically conductive hybrid electrodes with a straightforward design, comprising current-collector-free, binder-free active layer from long-length single-wall carbon nanotubes (LLSWCNTs) and TEMPO-oxidized cellulose nanofibers (TOCNFs), fabricated on insulating support. To evaluate the influence of composition and processing parameters, films were prepared at three LLSWCNTs:TOCNFs mass ratios (1:1, 2:1, 3:1) and three postmixing sonication times (5, 10, 30 min). The films were subsequently characterized in terms of their structure, interfacial chemistry, and electroanalytical performance. Noncovalent interactions produced interconnected conductive LLSWCNTs networks embedded within an insulating TOCNFs scaffold, where electrical transport occurs through percolating interbundle contacts. title: Unveiling the Ameliorative Potential of Organic Amendments on Microplastic-Induced Shifts in Soil Carbon and Microbiome
Physical properties of strong [O iii ] emission-line compact galaxies from LAMOST DR10 spectra
abstract: Abstract Strong [O iii] emission-line compact galaxies, including Green Peas, Blueberries, and Purple Grapes (BPGs), are local analogues of extreme high-redshift star-forming galaxies. We develop a Bayesian neural network (BNN) with self-attention to reproduce four reference parameters—dust attenuation ${E(B-V)}$, gas-phase metallicity, star formation rate (SFR), and stellar mass ($M_*$)—from preprocessed optical spectra. The model uses LAMOST DR10 spectra of 1269 galaxies as inputs and reference labels derived from Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) emission-line diagnostics and spectral energy distribution fitting. The BNN achieves the lowest point estimates of the overall normalized RMSE (0.0726) and MAE (0.0428) among the evaluated machine-learning and deep-learning models, although its performance is statistically close to that of the strongest deterministic baselines when bootstrap uncertainties are considered. Compared with MC Dropout, the BNN yields lower total predictive uncertainties for all four parameters while maintaining empirical coverage fractions close to nominal Gaussian expectations. This study evaluates uncertainty-aware spectral-to-label regression and calibration transfer rather than proposing an independent physical calibration or replacing classical emission-line diagnostics. Because no algebraic baseline based on LAMOST emission-line measurements is includ…

title: The JWST Proto-PAH project: Aromatic backbones with extensive aliphatic substitution account for both the aromatic and aliphatic emission
abstract: We find that the aromatic and aliphatic emission bands in four carbon-rich post-asymptotic giant branch stars with class D emission arise from a single carrier population: extensive aliphatic decoration of an aromatic skeleton, i.e. molecules with a coherent aromatic backbone and an unusually high aliphatic content. This conclusion is based on JWST NIRSpec and MIRI/MRS spectroscopy, covering 2.88--28.7 The aliphatic 3.4 feature is stronger than the aromatic 3.3 feature, reversing the ratio seen in sources with typical polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission. If the aromatic emission arose from nominal PAHs, the 3.3 feature -- unavailable in previous observations -- together with the mid-infrared aromatic features, would constrain them to be large (≳200 carbon atoms), compact, and at least partially ionized. These properties predict a strong 8.6 feature. However, the 8.6 feature is weak or absent in all four sources, ruling out PAHs as the source of the aromatic emission. Instead, the emission must arise from the same carriers as the aliphatic emission. The position of the 6.9 feature and the broadened 11–14 out-of-plane emission independently support this. The and feature strengths vary across the sample, with the class D2 sources showing higher content. These carriers are far more aliphatic than the PAHs of planetary nebulae and the interstellar medium. However, they re…

title: Surface temperatures drive strong seasonality in urban reactive carbon emissions
abstract: Urban air quality is affected by diverse volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and prior studies reveal a need to understand their seasonal sources. We combine high-resolution mass spectrometry with eddy covariance to quantify VOC fluxes from an urban/suburban New York site during summer and winter. Emissions are strongly seasonal: During summer, twice as many VOCs undergo surface-atmosphere exchange, and molar and reactivity-based fluxes are 2 to 4× higher than in winter. Temperature-dependent emissions from volatile chemical products (VCPs), vegetation, and residences dominate during summer. Ethanol alone accounts for ∼25% of the total flux. During winter, temperature-dependent emissions are reduced and traffic sources dominate. An updated inventory agrees with summer observations within 40% but overestimates winter fluxes by >2.5×. The winter discrepancy reflects overestimated VCP/cooking emissions and missing temperature-dependent volatilization. Results highlight the need to account for seasonal and temperature-dependent urban emissions to support pollution and mitigation assessment in the context of global change.

title: Relativistic Proton-Neutron Quasiparticle-Vibration Coupling Theory with Localized Exchange Terms and Tensor Couplings for Gamow-Teller Resonances and \texorpdfstring{$\beta$}{beta} Decay
abstract: Abstract We develop a relativistic proton-neutron quasiparticle random-phase approximation (pnQRPA) plus proton-neutron quasiparticle-vibration coupling (pnQPVC) model based on localized relativistic Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov theory with the PCF-PK1 density functional, which incorporates the localized exchange terms and tensor couplings. The localized exchange terms allow the residual interaction, espeically the isovector-pseudovector (tPV) channel, to be determined fully self-consistently without any phenomenological adjustment of the tPV coupling strength. We apply the newly developed relativistic pnQPVC model to the Gamow-Teller (GT) strength distributions in $^{116-134}$Sn and the $\beta^-$-decay half-lives of neutron-rich Ni and Sn nuclei as well as the $N=50$ and $N=82$ isotonic chains. Channel analysis at the pnQRPA and pnQPVC levels demonstrates that the isovector-tensor and tPV channels play key roles in both the GT response and $\beta$-decayhalf-lives. Beyond pnQRPA, QPVC correlations broaden and redistribute the GT strength, bringing the calculated resonance widths and peak energies into better agreement with experiment. QPVC correlations also substantially reduce the calculated $\beta$-decay half-lives and improve agreement with the experimental data.

title: Gated Memristive Coupling in a Hindmarsh-Rose Neural Network: Nonlinear Dynamics and Hardware Implementation
abstract: Abstract Inspired by astrocyte-mediated modulation in tripartite synapses, this study proposes a gated memristive coupling mechanism for neural networks. Unlike conventional pairwise coupling scheme with predefined interaction strengths, the proposed framework introduces an independent neuronal state to regulate the evolution of the gated memristive element's state variable, forming a dynamic modulation pathway. Through this mechanism, the coupling strength between two neurons can be continuously adjusted by the activity of a third neuron without directly modifying the intrinsic coupling coefficients. A three-neuron Hindmarsh-Rose network with gated memristive coupling channels is constructed to investigate the resulting nonlinear dynamics. Bifurcation analysis, Lyapunov exponents, and two-parameter maps reveal that the proposed architecture generates diverse transitions among periodic, multi-periodic, and chaotic firing regimes. Different coupling channels exhibit distinct regulatory characteristics, and their interaction produces complex distributions of dynamical regions in the parameter space. Furthermore, external excitation analysis demonstrates that neuronal inputs provide an additional control pathway by modulating the membrane potential of the gating neuron, thereby indirectly regulating the effective coupling strength. The feasibility of the proposed mechanism is vali…

title: Strong-coupling expansion and two-point Padé approximation for lattice ϕ 4 field theory
abstract: Abstract Reliable approximations for correlation functions at intermediate and strong coupling remain difficult to obtain in general quantum field theories. Perturbative expansions are often asymptotic or have a finite radius of convergence, which limits their applicability beyond weak coupling. In this work, we show that by combining perturbative expansions in both weak- and strong-coupling limits, one can use two-point Padé schemes to construct non-perturbative approximants to the correlation function. For lattice ϕ 4 theory, we show that this interpolation strategy yields accurate approximations across broad coupling regimes and compares favorably with standard one-point resummation methods such as Borel–Padé approach. We also provide heuristic explanations for the observed convergence behavior and discuss the practical range of validity of the approach.

title: Institutional determinants of sustainability awareness in higher education: advancing SDG 4.7 through curriculum integration, policy frameworks and campus engagement
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the impact of institutional mechanisms, including academic curriculum integration, policy frameworks and campus sustainability initiatives, on sustainability awareness among undergraduate students in higher education. Conducted within the context of Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) City Campus, this research contributes to global efforts in achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4.7 by promoting education for sustainable development through institutional innovation. It responds to calls for evidence-based practices in sustainability management within higher education institutions (HEIs), particularly in ASEAN contexts. Design/methodology/approach A cross-sectional, quantitative study was conducted using proportionate stratified random sampling among 311 undergraduate students from four faculties, which are the Faculty of Data Science and Computing, Faculty of Entrepreneurship and Business, Faculty of Hospitality, Tourism and Wellness and Faculty of Veterinary Medicine at UMK City Campus. Validated multi-item instruments were used to measure institutional determinants and sustainability awareness. Data were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to evaluate the measurement and structural models, with all significance tests conducted two-tailed. Vitamin D status and adiposity in children with low-energy fractures: a prospective case–control study
abstract: Abstract Fractures in children are influenced by both skeletal biology and mechanical factors. While alterations in vitamin D and other metabolic markers have been proposed as contributors to fracture risk, their role in predicting fractures in otherwise healthy pediatric populations remains unclear. This study aimed to determine whether biochemical markers of bone metabolism and body mass are independently associated with fracture occurrence and fracture patterns in children after low-energy trauma and to assess their impact on fracture patterns and anatomical distribution. We conducted a prospective case–control study including 100 children presenting after low-energy trauma (50 with radiographically confirmed fractures and 50 controls). Serum 25OH vitamin D (25OHD), parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) were measured within 1 week of presentation. Associations with fracture occurrence were assessed using multivariable logistic regression, including age, sex, body mass index z-score (BMI-z), an interaction term between 25OHD and BMI-z, and an additional exploratory model evaluating a 25OHD × season interaction. The discriminatory ability of 25OHD was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. title: The liver-heart-lung axis in pulmonary arterial hypertension: bidirectional mechanisms, prognostic biomarkers, and clinical integration
Macroscopic cerebral energy efficiency corresponds to neuron reorganization in awake and anesthetized mice
abstract: Introduction Non-invasive imaging of brain function and energy supply is crucial for diagnosing and treating brain disorders. Conventional imaging struggles to capture altered relationships between energy supply and demand caused by brain diseases. A novel method, thus far only tested non-invasively in human subjects, is to calculate relative power (rPWR) and relative cost (rCST) to assess cerebral energy efficiency. However, whether rPWR/rCST tracks individual changes and relate to neural activity remains unproven. Methods Our study examines awake and anesthetized male mice and compares rPWR/rCST with invasive two-photon microscopy. Results We found that rPWR/rCST distributions were similar between awake mice and humans, but changed in anesthetized mice, indicating a shift in the brain’s economic balance. Furthermore, changes in rPWR/rCST were linked to the reorganization of microscopic neural networks, observed with two-photon microscopy. Discussion Our work highlights the potential of rPWR/rCST for medical applications, and that neural network reorganization is linked to the brain’s economic balance.

title: Towards Raising the Marriage Age: A Culture-Based Integration Model for Stunting Prevention (Case Study in Beneraf Village, East Coast District, Sarmi Regency)
abstract: Background: Stunting remains a public health issue in Papua and is influenced by multiple factors, including early marriage. The implementation of Raising the Marriage Age (PUP) in indigenous communities is challenged by customary values that determine marriage readiness through social maturity rather than chronological age. Objective: This study aims to analyze the marriage rules of the Manirem indigenous community, the community’s response to the initiative to raise the marriage age, and the factors that support and hinder its implementation as an effort to prevent stunting in Beneraf Village, East Coast District, Sarmi Regency. Methods: This qualitative case study used observation, in-depth interviews, Focus Group Discussions, and document review. Informants included traditional leaders, a religious leader, youth leaders, women leaders, and the Head of Beneraf Village. Data were analyzed descriptively and thematically. Results: Participating community leaders generally expressed positive responses to PUP, although its implementation remains influenced by customary norms regarding adulthood and marriage readiness. Support comes from traditional leaders, religious institutions, village government, women, and youth, while limited education, reproductive health information, socioeconomic conditions, and institutional capacity remain barriers. The findings were synthesized into t…

title: Examining the effect of work-life integration on burnout among Indonesian employees
abstract: Background: Burnout remains a critical occupational health issue in Indonesia. While previous studies often focus on static Work-Life Balance, modern workplace requires a dynamic Work-Life Integration (WLI) approach, yet dimensions mitigating burnout remain unclear.Purpose: This study investigates how WLI affects employee burnout and identifies specific dimensions acting as protective factors or stressors, alongside demographic boundary conditions.Method: A cross-sectional survey involved 355 employees (Mage = 32.08, SD = 10; 67.9% male and 32.1% female) across Western, Central, and Eastern Indonesia. Data were collected using the Maslach-Trisni Burnout Inventory (𝛼 = .916) and transadapted Work-Life Indicator Scale with internal consistency for WLI dimensions ranging from 𝛼 = .664 to .837. Regression and correlation analyses were conducted using SPSS and Multigroup Analysis (PLS-MGA) using SmartPLS.Findings: Multidimensional WLI predicts burnout (R2 = 17.6%). Work Identity (b = -.269) and Boundary Control (b = -.131) protect against burnout, whereas Non-Work Interrupting Work acts as a stressor. PLS-MGA reveals that Work Interrupting Non-work intensifies burnout specifically among permanent and single employees.Discussion: Professional identity and boundary management appear more critical than role fusion in preventing burnout, highlighting the need for targeted, demographic-s…

title: Pediatric Mental Health Integration and Perceived Quality of Care
abstract: OBJECTIVE This study examined how access to behavioral and mental health (B/MH) professionals varied across general and subspecialty pediatricians and whether access to, and degree of, B/MH integration in clinical settings was associated with pediatricians’ perceptions of health care quality and moral distress. METHODS A voluntary survey was administered to pediatricians during enrollment in the 2022 American Board of Pediatrics Maintenance of Certification program. The survey assessed access to, and level of, integration with B/MH professionals in their clinical practice, perceived quality of care, and moral distress. Multivariable logistic regression estimated associations between constructs, adjusting for demographic and practice characteristics. RESULTS A total of 5321 respondents were included in this analysis (55.2% response rate). Overall, 68.3% (n = 3634) reported access to B/MH professionals in their primary clinical setting, most commonly a social worker (53.1%; n = 2825). Critical care pediatricians most frequently report access to B/MH professionals (97.9%; n = 279) compared with 55.4% of general pediatricians (n = 1797). Level of B/MH integration varied substantially across subspecialties. Availability of a B/MH professional was associated with a significantly lower odds of perceived suboptimal care quality (odds ratio, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.66–0.93) but was not signific…

title: Packing-accelerated consecutive NIR excitation (PACE) enables high energy photocatalysis and antitumor immunity in vivo
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) photocatalysis promises deep-tissue compatibilities but remains fundamentally constrained by two bottlenecks: insufficient photon energy and rapid charge recombination. Here, we report packing-accelerated consecutive excitation (PACE), a mechanism enabling low energy near-infrared (NIR) photons to drive high energy single electron transfer (SET) reactions. We design a self-assembling ruthenium complex, Ru-3 , that forms densely packed nanoaggregates exhibiting aggregation-stabilized excited states, a pronounced excited state absorption band at ∼1315 nm, and nanosecond scale triplet lifetimes. Under dual NIR-I/IIa irradiation (808 nm/1310 nm), Ru-3 nanoparticles exhibit photophysical behavior consistent with consecutive photon harvesting and access to a higher-energy reactive state that supports efficient SET catalysis under aqueous conditions. This PACE-driven reactivity enables robust oxidation of mitochondrial NADH to NAD + , disrupting electron-transport homeostasis, inducing cGAS-STING dependent pyroptosis, and reprogramming tumor-associated macrophages toward an M1 phenotype. In multiple murine tumor models, PACE-mediated photocatalysis elicits strong antitumor immunity and leads to tumor regression with minimal systemic toxicity. This work establishes PACE as a new photochemical paradigm that overcomes the intrinsic energy and charge-separation limits …

abstract: The rapid implementation of generative ai in education enhances personalization while escalating concerns regarding assignment authorship, assessment transparency, and academic integrity. The objective is to empirically test under what methodological conditions ai improves educational outcomes and how associated risks can be managed. A three-stage Ta’limda istiqbolli izlanishlar - xalqaro ilmiy-metodik jurnal № 9/2026 ISSN: 3060-527X experiment (pre-test, intervention, post-test) was conducted with experimental and control groups (n = 48 in each); questionnaire reliability was confirmed with cronbach’s α = 0.78. In the post- test, the experimental group outperformed the control group in ai readiness and academic achievement (cohen’s d = 1.06 and d = 1.44, respectively), accompanied by a moderate reduction in academic dependency risks (d = 0.58). The results demonstrate that methodologically regulated ai integration enhances learning quality, provided there is ongoing monitoring, clear assessment criteria, and established rules of academic integrity.

The impact of work–family integration enactment on emotional exhaustion: a perspective of role conflict and role enhancement
abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore the dual effects of work–family integration enactment (WFIE) on emotional exhaustion. Drawing on the conservation of resources (COR) theory, it examines the mediating roles of work–family conflict (WFC) and work–family positive spillover (WFPS), together with the moderating role of family role salience (FRS), to provide enhanced understanding of how WFIE influences employee well-being. Design/methodology/approach A three-wave survey was conducted with 204 employees in China. Structural equation modeling was employed to test the hypothesized moderated dual mediation model, assessing the relationships between WFIE, WFC, WFPS, emotional exhaustion and FRS. Findings The results reveal that WFIE has a dual effect on emotional exhaustion. It increases emotional exhaustion through WFC while reducing it through WFPS. Importantly, the mediating effect of WFC is significantly stronger than that of WFPS, indicating that resource loss outweighs resource gain in shaping emotional exhaustion. Additionally, FRS strengthens the loss-based pathway, such that employees with high FRS experience a stronger positive association between WFIE and WFC. Originality/value Employing COR theory, this study constructs a theoretical framework that specifies the dual pathways through which WFIE affects emotional exhaustion, thereby expanding the understanding of work–family…

title: Teachers’ perceptions of artificial intelligence integration in education: a multi-campus cross-sectional study from Riphah International University, Pakistan
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into education is accelerating worldwide, yet evidence on teachers’ perceptions remains scarce in the Global South, particularly in resource-constrained Pakistan. This cross-sectional study examined teachers’ perceptions of AI integration at Riphah International University, Pakistan. A 14-item Likert-scale questionnaire was administered to 270 in-service teachers (86.7% male, 13.3% female) across BS Undergraduate through PhD levels. Guided by a proposed Dual-Lens conceptual framework treating perceived benefits and risks as coexisting dimensions, the instrument assessed pedagogical advantages and structural concerns of AI. Descriptive analysis revealed a moderately favorable overall perception (composite M = 3.40, SD = 0.55). Teachers rated interactivity enhancement (M = 3.81), student enjoyment (M = 3.73), and assessment support (M = 3.72) most favorably, while AI replacing human teachers received the lowest endorsement (M = 2.96). An independent-samples t-test showed no significant gender difference (t(268) = −0.245, p = .807, d = −0.044). One-way ANOVA revealed significant effects for age (F(4, 265) = 3.200, p = .014, η 2 = .046) and level of instruction (F(3, 266) = 3.471, p = .017, η 2 = .038), with teachers under 29 and BS Undergraduate instructors holding less favorable perceptions. Qualification and experience showed no si…

title: Phenotyping of AMI patients using machine learning: integration of clinical, metabolic, and behavioral features to identify high-risk “frailty–inflammation” phenotype
abstract: Background Prognosis among patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) shows substantial heterogeneity, making precise identification of high-risk phenotypes essential for improving long-term outcomes. Machine learning techniques were used to identify such phenotypes by integrating multidimensional data and to examine their association with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Methods A total of 1,139 patients with AMI were enrolled from the First Affiliated Hospital of Harbin Medical University between March 2023 and June 2024. Multidimensional data, including clinical features, metabolic characteristics, and behavioral patterns, were collected. Phenotyping was performed using a hierarchical clustering algorithm. Associations between derived phenotypes and 1-year MACE were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier survival analysis and multivariable Cox regression models. Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) values derived from an XGBoost model were used to quantify the contributions of individual variables to cluster assignment. Results Hierarchical clustering identified two clinical phenotypes with differing pathophysiological characteristics. Cluster 2 ( n = 243, 21.3%) exhibited a high-risk “frailty–inflammation” phenotype, characterized by impaired activities of daily living, elevated risk of falls and pressure ulcers, increased high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) …

title: Targeted integration of extrachromosomal arrays in C. elegans using PhiC31 integrase
abstract: Extrachromosomal arrays are unique chromosome-like structures created from DNA injected into the Caenorhabditis elegans germline. However, they are unstable unless integrated into a chromosome. Current methods for integration using x-rays or CRISPR can damage DNA and exhibit low efficiency. We demonstrate that the viral integrase PhiC31, which mediates nonmutagenic recombination between short attB and attP sequences, can be used for extremely efficient and targeted integration of arrays. Arrays were integrated by PhIAT (PhiC31-mediated integration of arrays of transgenes) at attB sites on three chromosomes, including at a fluorescent landing pad. Moreover, integrations can be inserted at any arbitrary site in the genome by simultaneously co-injecting Cas9 ribonucleoprotein, an attB repair template, and the DNA components for the array—thereby providing sites on all six chromosomes. Single injections can integrate arrays ranging in size from 1 to 18 megabases. PhIAT makes it practical to study genomes of other organisms in the nematode; one of our strains incorporates 65% of the yeast genome at a single site in the worm genome. PhIAT will accelerate a shift from unstable extrachromosomal arrays to direct integration of arrays in C. elegans .

title: Lysosomes: a central hub orchestrating metabolic plasticity, signal integration, and proteostasis in adult stem cell quiescence
abstract: Abstract The quiescent state of adult stem cells is fundamental to their protection against exogenous damage, the maintenance of stem cell pool stability, and the preservation of long-term regenerative potential in tissues. Elucidating the underlying regulatory mechanisms is of profound significance for stem cell biology and the development of therapeutic interventions for related diseases. Over the past decades, our understanding of the lysosome has evolved from viewing it solely as a degradative compartment to recognizing it as a dynamic regulatory hub for the regulation of stem cell quiescence. This review synthesizes recent research progress on the multidimensional roles of lysosomes in governing the quiescent state of adult stem cells through three core mechanisms: metabolic regulation, signal integration, and the maintenance of proteostasis. We systematically delineate the relevant molecular pathways, key regulatory factors, and their physiological and pathological implications in maintaining tissue homeostasis. This article aims to provide novel perspectives for a deeper understanding of stem cell biology and the formulation of clinical strategies for associated disorders.

title: A Study on the Impact of AI-Assisted Teaching Integration in College English on Students’ Writing Performance: A Case Study of Hubei Polytechnic University
abstract: At present, there are some problems in college English writing teaching, such as students ' low interest in writing, lack of personalized guidance, and low feedback efficiency. Artificial intelligence technology provides new ideas for teaching reform. In order to explore the actual impact of artificial intelligence-assisted teaching on college students’ English writing ability, this study selected two non-English major classes in Hubei Polytechnic University to carry out a one-semester quasi-experiment: 55 students in the experimental group adopted artificial intelligence-assisted teaching, and 53 students in the control group adopted traditional teaching. After the experiment, data were collected through questionnaires and in-depth interviews (10 students in each group), and the teaching effectiveness was evaluated by combining quantitative and qualitative results. The results showed that the average scores of each dimension of writing ability in the experimental class were higher than those in the control group, but did not reach a statistically significant level (P > 0.05). In the interview, the students in the experimental class had a significantly higher positive evaluation of writing interest (80%), learning effect (70%) and classroom interaction (90%). At the same time, they also put forward the problems of imperfect AI tools and easy to produce technical dependence. The…

title: Climate resilience through economic development, energy transition and sustainable development: insights from wavelet coherence approach
abstract: Purpose Adjusted net savings (ANS) is a pivotal indicator of sustainable development, combining environmental costs, resource depletion and economic performance. While ANS fosters short-term environmental accountability, its focus on immediate economic gains may undermine long-term climate resilience by discouraging investments in clean energy and ecological innovation (ECI). This study aims to investigate the dynamic relationship between ANS, natural resource (NAR) management, clean energy transition (CLT) and ECI in China, providing actionable insights for achieving climate-resilient growth. Design/methodology/approach Using an innovative wavelet coherence approach, the authors analyse annual data from 1980 to 2020 in China to uncover time–frequency dependencies among key variables. Findings The authors’ results indicate that NARs drive short-to-medium-term CLTs and positively influence ECI in the medium term. However, the long-term relationship between NAR and ANS is negative, revealing a conflict between economic priorities and sustainable resource management. In addition, while CLT and ECI exhibit a strong short-to-medium-term synergy, this linkage weakens over time due to barriers in scaling green technologies and policy inertia. Notably, CLT negatively correlates with ANS in the medium term, suggesting that China’s resource-intensive growth model and short-term economic …

title: Single-electron capture in intermediate energy He 2+ + He collisions
abstract: Abstract A combined experimental and theoretical study on single-electron capture in 30 - 125 keV/u He 2+ + He collisions was performed. Single-electron capture state-selective and angular-differential cross sections were measured using a cold target recoil ion momentum spectroscopy, for which the longitudinal momentum resolution has been improved up to 0.066 a.u.. More details of electron captured to higher excited-states and transfer-excitation processes were obtained from angular-differential cross sections. It was found that the experimental angular-differential cross sections were in good agreement with the two-active-electron semiclassical asymptotic-state close-coupling calculation for the considered impact energies. It is shown that single electron capture mainly occurs at small projectile scattering angles (< 0.4 mrad), where prominent oscillatory structures resulting from Fraunhofer-type diffraction can be seen. While a significant contribution from large projectile scattering angles (> 0.6 mrad) was observed in the transfer-excitation process at 30 keV/u. From a quasimolecular interaction picture, it is shown that both the small internuclear distance radial coupling and rotational coupling at the united-atom limit are responsible for the large angle scattering mechanism at 30 keV/u.

title: Fatigue crack growth in elastomers for leading-edge erosion protection of wind turbine blades
abstract: Fatigue crack growth has been observed as a prominent damage mode in rain erosion of wind turbine blades, where it is driven by cyclic pulse loading from liquid droplet impacts. This study investigates fatigue crack growth in a thermoplastic polyurethane elastomer used for leading-edge protection, linking repeated droplet impacts to controlled cyclic loading in a lab test. The plane strain tensile double-slit test method is employed to determine the actual tearing energy during fatigue crack growth. A new analysis technique evaluates tearing energy throughout the test by tracking strain energy evolution with crack length. A novel test fixture with circular grip faces was developed to ensure efficient gripping of polymer sheets. It is examined how the interval between successive load pulses, the dwell time, affects fatigue crack growth per cycle, denoted as da/dN. The material exhibits pronounced visco-elastic behavior, including cyclic stress softening. It may take several hundred cycles to stabilize, with repeatable stress–strain loops, requiring a run-in period before crack growth assessment. Tests with shorter dwell times need more cycles to reach stabilization. Two dwell times are applied: 0.1 and 1 s. Longer dwell times allow greater recovery between load pulses, reducing cyclic softening. When da/dN is plotted against maximum strain, the cracks grow faster at longer dwell…

title: The Two-Variable Hypergraph Tutte Polynomial via Embedding Activities and Computation-Tree Activities
abstract: We generalize Bernardi's embedding activity definition for the Tutte polynomial from graphs to hypergraphs, and Gordon-Traldi-McMahon's computation-tree activities from matroids to polymatroids. Furthermore, we introduce a new variant of computation-tree activities, and show that they also yield a definition for the polymatroid Tutte polynomial. In all three cases, the key is to show that the given activity notion yields a Crapo decomposition. We also examine the relationship of these activity notions, and pose some questions about them.

title: Creativity in design education: an educational psychology model of motivation, cognitive load, and self-efficacy
abstract: Objective This study examines the statistical relationships among learning motivation, cognitive load, creative self-efficacy, and expert-rated creative performance among undergraduate design students. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted with 428 valid responses from undergraduate students majoring in design-related disciplines. Students first completed a design task, after which questionnaire data were collected and anonymized design works were evaluated by three independent experts. SPSS was used for descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, regression-based path analysis, and Bootstrap tests of statistical indirect effects; AMOS was used to evaluate the measurement model. Results Learning motivation and germane cognitive load were positively associated with creative self-efficacy. Creative self-efficacy showed the strongest positive association with design creative performance, and germane cognitive load showed a smaller positive direct association. Extraneous cognitive load was negatively correlated with creative performance at the bivariate level, but its adjusted direct path was not statistically significant; therefore, H5 was not supported. Intrinsic cognitive load was not significant. Bootstrap results indicated significant statistical indirect relationships through creative self-efficacy. Conclusion The findings suggest …

title: The aesthetics of applying 3D printing in the design and manufacture of sustainable bags for women
abstract: Introduction Three-dimensional (3D) printing has emerged as a promising digital manufacturing technology for fashion and accessories, providing opportunities for customization, design flexibility, and innovative production. Integrating digital fabrication technologies with Saudi cultural heritage may contribute to the development of contemporary fashion products that retain distinctive cultural characteristics. This study investigated the application of 3D printing in developing women’s handbags inspired by Saudi cultural heritage. Methods The study aimed to develop contemporary handbag designs integrating Sadu-inspired textile elements with 3D-printed components and to evaluate their aesthetic quality, perceived economic potential, and functional performance. Fourteen proposed handbag designs were evaluated using a structured questionnaire assessing aesthetic quality and perceived economic potential. Twenty-two specialists participated in validating the research instrument, while seven specialist evaluations per design were used for the design-level analyses. One-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted to examine differences among the proposed designs. Results The ANOVA results indicated statistically significant differences among the 14 designs in aesthetic quality, F (13, 84) = 36.082, p < 0.001, perceived economic potential, F (13, 84) = 19.680, p < 0.001, and …

title: Product evolution model (PEM): a functional semantic knowledge-driven framework for product technology landscape construction
abstract: Purpose The construction of a product technology landscape remains heavily reliant on patent-based methods despite its recognized value in supporting the systematic product planning and technology opportunity identification. These patented approaches, however, are typically constrained to document-level operations such as retrieval, clustering and keyword analysis, creating a critical gap in their capacity to support the generation of component-level solutions. To address this gap, this study aims to propose a product evolution model (PEM), a functional semantic knowledge-driven framework that integrates patent-derived component knowledge, function–object–property (FOP) representation, TRIZ-based evolution trend label mapping, multi-objective optimization and TOPSIS-based decision ranking. Design/methodology/approach First, patent claims are transformed into product-component and component-FOP knowledge using the structured information extraction. Moreover, functional community detection and topic modeling are then used to identify representative components, while evolution trend labels are mapped to candidate components and incorporated into a component-evolution trend association matrix. The PEM formulates product technology landscape construction as a three-objective optimization problem that maximizes implementation effect, maximizes functional coverage and minimizes compon…

title: Optimization of a ternary geopolymer paste through orthogonal experimental design, ANOVA and entropy-based multi-objective decision analysis
abstract: The optimization of geopolymer binders containing multiple aluminosilicate precursors is challenging because the governing mix parameters simultaneously influence mechanical performance, workability, and material cost. Existing studies primarily focus on individual performance indicators, resulting in suboptimal mix designs for practical engineering applications. Therefore, this study proposes an integrated multi-objective optimization framework for ternary Fly Ash, ground granulated blast furnace slag, metakaolin geopolymer paste by combining single-factor experiments, L16 orthogonal experimental design, analysis of variance, and a synthetic weighted decision model incorporating subjective and entropy-based objective weighting. Initial experiments established that curing at 60 °C for 24 h provided the most favourable geo-polymerisation conditions. Subsequently, the effects of GGBS content, MK content, NaOH molarity, alkaline activator ratio, and alkali-to-binder ratio on compressive strength, flowability, and material cost were systematically investigated. Effect analysis indicated that the alkaline activator ratio was associated with the greatest change in compressive strength, consistent with its role in enhanced dissolution and polycondensation of aluminosilicate precursors, and the alkali-to-binder ratio with the greatest change in flowability, although these effects could…

title: A SynNotch-PiggyBac gene circuit for inflammation-responsive IL-10 delivery in Alzheimer’s disease: a hypothesis and design framework
abstract: Chronic neuroinflammation driven by sustained microglial and astrocyte activation contributes to Alzheimer’s disease progression, yet no therapeutic strategy addresses it with precision or durability in the brain. Interleukin-10 occupies an unresolved position in this problem. Constitutive interleukin-10 overexpression in amyloid precursor protein transgenic mice increased plaque burden by suppressing microglial phagocytic activity, while interleukin-10 deletion has been reported to restrict amyloidosis in one setting and to worsen tau hyperphosphorylation in another. We interpret this pattern as evidence that interleukin-10 carries opposite signs on the two principal pathologies of Alzheimer’s disease, so that any therapy holding it at a fixed concentration is committed in advance to being wrong about one of them. We therefore propose a falsifiable hypothesis: conditional, inflammation-gated interleukin-10 expression may suppress damaging inflammatory signaling while limiting the impairment of microglial phagocytosis associated with continuous exposure. We present a design framework for a synthetic gene circuit combining an adeno-associated viral vector for delivery to the central nervous system, a synthetic Notch receptor that detects membrane-bound tumor necrosis factor alpha on activated microglia through juxtacrine contact, and a PiggyBac transposon intended to integrate t…

title: Impact of side hole design of drainage cannulas on flow velocity and predilection sites for low-flow areas in veno-venous ECMO circuits
abstract: Abstract Background Veno-Venous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VV-ECMO) (VV-ECMO) and Veno-Artial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation (VA-ECMO) have become evidence-based therapy options for patients with most severe heart and/or lung failure. Cannulas continue to play a central role as the direct interface between patients and extracorporeal circulation. However, severe side-effects, such as coagulation and haemolysis, may result not only from a blood pump but also from inappropriate cannula design. Methods Based on the multi-stage lighthouse design of a draining ECMO cannula, the area of the side holes was varied in both shape and size in the distal and proximal directions. Using a Computer-Aided Design (CAD)- Model of cannulas (19,21,23 French (Fr)) appropriate simulation models were created in the non-reactive plenum. The resultant numerical 3D simulations are based on physiological boundary conditions and on the flows covering different ECMO-flow rates. Results The current cannula design reveals no-flow zones, which induce thrombus formation, especially when using blood-flow rates below 2 L/min. New geometric cannula design variants revealed an improvement in pressure loss, but at the expense of pronounced no-flow zones in the distal region. During drainage, the largest proportion of the total volume flow drains through the proximal row of side holes. Here, the press…

title: User-centered design in academic library websites: insights from a comparative analysis
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to analyze the user interface design quality, including information architecture, navigation structure, discovery search box integration, and overall homepage design across 60 university libraries in the United States. While libraries progressively rely on digital interfaces to deliver services, it's important to understand how design elements impact usability, visibility, and accessibility. Design/methodology/approach The study is a systematic content analysis of the user interface (UI) design quality of library homepages across the United States. Content analysis was selected as a methodological approach; it allows for the systematic examination of visible interface elements and predefined criteria (Krippendorff, 2018). A mixed-methods framework was adopted, combining quantitative observable design scores with qualitative expert examination of interface effectiveness (Creswell and Plano Clark, 2017). The analysis focused on library homepages because they serve as the primary access point for users and provide an initial experience of library services. Four core elements were investigated: information architecture, navigation structure, discovery search box placement and visibility, and overall homepage design quality. Three expert reviewers independently assessed each website using a 1–5-point rating scale. The sample consists of 60 univer…

title: Analyzing GPT-5 performance in general chemistry
abstract: The ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) to outperform humans on many intellectual tasks has created a difficult landscape for assessing student work. One strategy is designing assignments to be specifically difficult for AI. However, LLMs have been shown to perform well on general chemistry problems across topics, and new models continue to make AI-proofing assignments more difficult. In this work, we evaluate the recently released GPT-5 Thinking model across a set of 1736 questions from the Openstax general chemistry textbook. While GPT-5 achieves near-perfect accuracy overall, categorizing questions by the types of cognitive skills required elucidates specific weaknesses. Notably, GPT-5 tends to make major errors when asked to create figures. These findings inform best practices for AI-resistant assignment design.

title: Design of a monolithic cellulose Janus-like membrane for oil/water separation
abstract: Abstract Janus membranes offer a good solution for oil/water mixtures due to their opposite wettability, but existing designs often suffer from limitations arising from complex, resource-intensive fabrication procedures. This study proposes a cellulose-based monolithic Janus-like membrane prepared by non-solvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) from cellulose acetate followed by alkaline deacetylation and unilateral silanization (TEOS/MTES). The resulting membrane exhibits asymmetric wettability (hydrophobic: 91°, hydrophilic: ~0°). Structural and chemical characterization (SEM, EDS, FTIR, and BET/BJH) confirms the formation of a siloxane-containing surface layer, the integrity of the cellulose network, and a distribution of the pores toward the nanoscale, with a specific surface area of 26.9 m 2 /g. Gravitational peanut oil/water tests reveal high fluxes (3300–5527 Lm −2 h − 1 ) with an apparent volumetric oil-retention efficiency of up to 95%, while for water/hexane, the apparent volumetric oil-retention efficiency reached 96.93% with a flux of 3950.62 Lm −2 h − 1 . The membrane retains excellent mechanical robustness (3.50 MPa), with a breaking force of 5.23 N, withstanding repeated deformations including axial rolling, compression, and bending, without cracking or delamination. This Janus-like membrane mimics the properties of Janus membranes while relying on a simplified, e…

title: Book Review: “Museum of Modern Aluminum” – Bridging Industry and Art through Sustainable Design
abstract: The book Museum of Modern Aluminum from Manufacture to Architecture documented an innovativearchitectural project by HAS Design and Research Company that redefines the application of aluminum incontemporary architecture. Inspired by the organic form of a dandelion and the ecological landscape ofThailand’s Koh Kret Island, the Museum of Modern Aluminum (MoMA) integrates aluminum as both a structuraland aesthetic element, showcasing its lightweight, malleable, and sustainable properties. The design featuresa dynamic façade composed of modular aluminum strips, paired with energy-efficient LED lighting that simulatesthe glow of fireflies, and landscape spaces that blend artificial and natural elements. This project not onlyhighlights the potential of aluminum in green architecture but also explores cultural transplantation, urbanmemory, and the balance between innovation and tradition. Through detailed case studies and reflections onmateriality, this book offers insights into sustainable design practices and reveals the evolving role of aluminumin shaping future-built environments.

title: Online dispute resolution for crypto-asset disputes: AI, smart 1 contracts and digital inclusion by design
abstract: Crypto-asset disputes create distinctive barriers to effective remedies because they combine technical opacity, cross-border legal fragmentation, pseudonymous actors, irreversible transactions and uncertain enforcement pathways. These barriers are especially significant for vulnerable and non-expert users, who may be unable to identify the legally relevant harm, organize blockchain-based evidence, select an appropriate forum or obtain practical enforcement. This article develops a conceptual, normative and legal-design proposal for a hybrid Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) architecture that integrates off-chain artificial intelligence (AI) assistance with a minimized on-chain smart-contract layer. The model assigns AI systems a supporting role in legal information, triage, claim classification, evidence organization, explanation and negotiation, while reserving contested legal determinations for human review. A permissioned distributed ledger records only hashes, timestamps, procedural events, escrow states and execution proofs; personal data, communications, evidence and AI processing remain off-chain. Smart contracts are used as bounded enforcement tools for registration, escrow and execution of validated settlement terms, rather than as autonomous adjudicators. The article applies the architecture to three illustrative scenarios: asset seizure and recovery, exchange failure a…

title: Emotional design and advertising: a systematic review of the literature on consumer behavior
abstract: Introduction Emotional design integrates sensory, functional, social, and symbolic elements to elicit affective responses that may influence consumer perception, attitudes, and behavior. This study aimed to analyze the relationship between emotional design, advertising, and consumer behavior based on recent scientific literature. Methods A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA guidelines. Searches were performed in Scopus and Web of Science, and 66 primary studies published during the last ten years were included. Results The reviewed evidence shows that emotional design strategies incorporate perceptual stimuli, user experiences, and meaning-making processes. Color, shape, texture, packaging, and multisensory stimuli contribute to attraction, attention, and perceived quality, while usability, ergonomics, interactivity, and demonstrations enhance the user experience. Storytelling, cultural identity, sustainability, and personalization contribute to meaning construction and strengthen consumer-brand connections. The literature also identifies positive, negative, and complex emotions, including pleasure, trust, fear, guilt, nostalgia, attachment, and identification, which are associated with purchase intention, satisfaction, loyalty, repurchase, and other consumer responses. Discussion The findings indicate that emotional design operates across sensory, …

title: Explainable fine-grained feature enhancement framework for strawberry diagnostic decision making
abstract: As the number of smart agricultural automation systems increases, accurate disease diagnosis is essential to maximize production efficiency. However, early-stage symptoms of strawberry diseases (e.g., Tipburn, Phytophthora blight, and Fusarium wilt) often manifest as low-contrast micro-symptoms that are visually similar to the inherent complex texture of strawberry leaves, leading to high technical difficulties in achieving an accurate diagnosis. Furthermore, providing an explanation for the diagnosis remains challenging, which hinders trust in field applications. We present EN-FDEA, a deep learning framework that integrates an EfficientNetV2 backbone with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and a Fine-grained Discriminative Enhancement (FDEA) module combining depthwise separable convolution, parallel feature amplification, and channel recalibration, and we evaluate it together with a provenance audit of the corpus on which it is trained. Parsing the acquisition metadata embedded in every file name showed that the 1,000 abnormal images of each disease originate from only 33–73 individual plants, and that normal and abnormal images share no greenhouse; under the image-level cross-validation used in the original design, 91.9–99.8% of abnormal plants appear in both the training and the test partition of a fold. All results reported here are therefore obtained under plant…

title: Microbial biotransformation of plant-derived bioactive compounds: structural modifications, enhanced bioavailability, and functional food applications
abstract: Abstract Plant-derived bioactive compounds, including polyphenols, polysaccharides, alkaloids, terpenoids/saponins, lignans and glucosinolates, are widely valued for their health-promoting potential, yet poor bioavailability and, in several cases, biological inactivity in native form limit their translation into functional food ingredients. Microbial biotransformation, carried out by naturally occurring gut microbiota, food-fermentation microorganisms and plant-associated endophytic fungi, offers a means of overcoming these limitations through mild, highly selective enzymatic modification. This review synthesizes current evidence on microbial biotransformation across five major classes of plant bioactive compounds, examining the natural microbial sources involved, the core enzymatic mechanisms, including glycosidases, esterases, oxidoreductases, decarboxylases and demethylases, responsible for these conversions, and the resulting changes in bioavailability and bioactivity for each compound class. Beyond the compound-specific discussion, we identify a smaller set of structural modifications, namely deglycosylation, molecular weight reduction, hydroxylation, demethylation, ring cleavage and decarboxylation, that recur across otherwise unrelated compound classes and account for much of the functional benefit associated with microbial processing. We discuss current applications in …

title: Machine learning–assisted directed evolution of plant Rubisco
abstract: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) is foundational to life on Earth, catalyzing carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) fixation to generate biomass. However, Rubisco is a slow and inefficient enzyme that has proven challenging to engineer. We applied the structure-informed machine learning (ML) model ESM-IF1 to identify plausible amino acid sites in the large subunit of Nicotiana tabacum Rubisco to target for directed evolution. ML-assisted library design followed by selection in Rubisco-dependent Escherichia coli identified multiple enriched variants displaying improved catalytic efficiency. Several improved variants carried amino acid changes not found in the evolutionary lineage of plants, despite being assembly competent in plant chloroplasts, demonstrating that ML-assisted protein design can explore functional sequence space beyond what is observed from natural sequence diversity. Most prominently, the T391I substitution improved carboxylation rate by 29% and aerobic carboxylation efficiency by 43%. Our findings illustrate the utility of ML-assisted evolution for engineering Rubisco with improved carboxylation efficiency and potential for enhancing crop productivity.

title: Power drop guided incremental conductance MPPT algorithm for ladder configured PV systems to enhance maximum power and tracking efficiency
abstract: Abstract Partial shading conditions (PSCs) introduce multiple local maximum power points (LMPPs) in photovoltaic (PV) arrays, causing conventional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) methods to converge to suboptimal operating points and reduce energy harvesting. This paper proposes a power drop guided incremental conductance (PDG-INC) MPPT algorithm that combines event-triggered stochastic duty-cycle relocation with deterministic incremental conductance (INC) refinement for improved maximum power point tracking under partial shading conditions. The proposed controller is evaluated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations using a 3.97 kW 8 × 8 ladder-configured PV array under nine representative PSCs and experimentally evaluated under individually applied PSCs using a laboratory-scale hardware prototype comprising a Chroma 62050H-600S PV simulator, TI DSP (F28379D), and a boost DC-DC converter. Performance is assessed using tracking efficiency, energy efficiency, transient response, ripple characteristics, and duty-cycle stability. For comparative evaluation, the proposed PDG-INC algorithm is compared with the step modified incremental conductance (SM-INC) and trap escape (TE) algorithms, while simulated annealing (SA) and the conventional perturb and observe (P&O) algorithm are employed as benchmark MPPT methods under the same investigated PSCs within the respective simulation and …

title: The Impact of Virtual Dental Clinic Color and Image Modifications on Anxiety Reduction in Undergraduate Dental Students
abstract: Dental students often experience stress due to the curriculum’s theoretical and practical demands, whichcan negatively affect their well-being. Previous research suggests that room colors and images can reduceanxiety in certain populations. However, no studies have examined this effect among dental students. Therefore,this study investigated how color and visual imagery in dental clinics affect anxiety levels in dental students.Participants were dental students experiencing state anxiety. They completed a modified version of the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) Form Y-1 before and after entering a virtual reality (VR) dental clinic with alteredenvironmental features. Three types of visual interventions were tested: 1) changing wall colors to blue, green,or yellow; 2) adding images of mountain, sea, or nautilus shell; and 3) combining the most preferred color andimage. Paired t-tests were used to analyze changes in anxiety scores, and intergroup differences were examinedusing the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by the Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test. Anxiety significantly decreased afterexposure to blue and yellow wall colors (p < 0.05), with blue being the most preferred. Notably, blue increasedpositive anxiety scores (PA) and decreased negative anxiety scores (NA) significantly (p < 0.05), while yellowonly decreased NA scores significantly (p < 0.05). Mountain and sea images also …

title: Functional redundancy and synthetic haploinsufficiency among Arabidopsis ATP-citrate lyase genes
abstract: ATP-citrate lyase (ACL) catalyzes the formation of cytosolic acetyl-CoA, which is the precursor for the generation of a variety of metabolites that have significant roles in plant growth and development. In Arabidopsis thaliana , ACL is encoded by three ACLA and two ACLB genes. The genetic functions of these genes were characterized by using combinations of null alleles of each subunit-gene. Individual acla mutants and double mutants that retained only the functional ACLA1 or ACLA3 gene exhibited normal growth, indicating substantial functional redundancy among the ACLA paralogs. These mutants showed minimal effects on cytosolic acetyl-CoA-derived metabolites, although anthocyanin content consistently increased. In contrast, aclb1; aclb2 double mutants were not recoverable, rather embryo development was arrested at the torpedo stage, demonstrating that ACL activity is essential for embryogenesis. Moreover, ACLB paralogs were not functionally equivalent during vegetative growth. Plants carrying a single functional ACLB2 allele in the absence of ACLB1 functionality displayed a severe dwarf phenotype, whereas plants carrying a single ACLB1 allele in the absence of ACLB2 appeared wild type, revealing synthetic haploinsufficiency of ACLB2 . Reduced ACLB2 dosage also decreased cuticular wax accumulation in a gene dosage-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that …

title: Potential Native Plant Selection for Sustainable Landscape Architecture in Wangchan Forest, Rayong, Thailand
abstract: Landscape architecture in Thailand still relies heavily on commercially propagated species. While convenient,this dependence narrows the design palette and promotes inclusion of exotic species or ecologically unsuitableplants, undermining biodiversity, long-term sustainability, and ecological resilience. By contrast, sustainablelandscape architecture prioritizes indigenous and locally adapted species that are visually expressive yetecologically matched to local conditions, thereby reducing maintenance, supporting native biota, and articulatingregional identity. This research investigated the Wangchan Forest in Rayong Province to develop a systematicprocess for identifying and selecting native plants for landscape use. The study objectives were to: (1) developa framework for selecting native species; (2) compile a list of native plants in Wangchan Forest; and (3)recommend species suitable for sustainable landscape design. The study combined botanical database analysiswith ethnobotanical inquiry. Data were drawn from Thai Plant Names by Tem Smitinand for the SoutheasternFloristic Region and complemented by semi-structured interviews with herbal doctors, local pioneers, andformer loggers with experiential knowledge of the forest. Species were evaluated using criteria emphasizingecological adaptability, microclimatic and edaphic compatibility, water requirements, and functional rol…

title: ZnO and SiO2 nanopriming enhancing seedling performance and changing volatile profiles of Melissa officinalis under drought and salinity stress
abstract: Introduction Melissa officinalis L. is an important medicinal and aromatic plant whose germination, seedling establishment, and secondary metabolism can be adversely affected by drought and salinity. This study investigated whether ZnO and SiO 2 nanopriming could mitigate these effects and modify the volatile profile of M. officinalis . Methods Two independent factorial experiments were conducted under drought and salinity stress. Seeds were hydroprimed as the control or nanoprimed with ZnO or SiO 2 at 50 or 100 mg L −1 . Drought treatments were 0, −0.2, −0.4, and −0.6 MPa, while salinity treatments were 0, 4, 8, and 12 dS m −1 . Germination and early seedling traits were evaluated. Selected 50 mg L −1 treatments under moderate stress conditions were subsequently subjected to volatile profiling by GC/GC-MS. Results Nanopriming significantly improved several germination and early seedling traits, with the strongest responses generally observed at 50 mg L −1 . title: Moderate reductions in water and nitrogen inputs enhance lodging resistance of spring wheat under a novel drip irrigation pattern in Xinjiang
abstract: Introduction Drip irrigation improves water and fertilizer use efficiency in wheat. However, it may promote excessive stem elongation and shallow root development, increasing lodging risk. Although optimized water and nitrogen management can enhance lodging resistance in drip-irrigated wheat, the regulatory thresholds and underlying mechanisms remain unclear, particularly under the novel TR6S pattern. Methods A two-year field experiment was conducted in 2024–2025 to systematically investigate the effects of water–nitrogen interactions on the lodging resistance of spring wheat under the TR6S pattern. Four irrigation levels were applied: 4500, 4200, 3900, and 3600 m 3 ·ha −1 , designated as W4500, W4200, W3900, and W3600, respectively. Three nitrogen application levels were applied: 300, 270, and 240 kg·ha −1 , designated as N300, N270, and N240, respectively. Results Wheat lodging rate exhibited a decreasing–increasing trend with reductions in both irrigation and nitrogen inputs. Compared with the traditional treatment (N300–W4500) (CK), moderate reductions in water–nitrogen inputs (N270–W4200) significantly increased the grain yield by 7.88–8.35% and reduced the lodging rate by 56.18–56.99%, achieving a favorable balance between yield (8.65–8.87 t·ha −1 ) and lodging rate (12.14–14.20%). Further reductions in water and nitrogen inputs decreased the lodging rate to some extent, …

title: Fine-tuning improves deep learning-based digital phenotyping of lettuce genetic resources
abstract: Introduction Morphological characterization of agricultural genetic resources relies largely on visual assessment by experts, and applying the same criteria repeatedly to large collections is labor-intensive. Image-based deep learning can support this process, but systematic evidence on training strategies suited to genebank trait data remains limited. Methods This study targeted six morphological traits of lettuce genetic resources characterized according to the test guidelines of the International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV). Using genebank images accumulated from 2012 to 2025, six convolutional neural networks were trained with three training strategies under identical conditions, and their performance was compared. Results Fine-tuning achieved the highest mean macro F1-score in 35 of the 36 backbone–trait combinations and significantly outperformed training from scratch and feature extraction, whereas no single backbone was superior across all traits. Misclassifications were concentrated in morphologically adjacent classes rather than randomly distributed, and for the ordinal traits, errors spanning two or more class levels were rare. Discussion These patterns suggest that the remaining classification difficulty was associated in part with the morphological continuity between neighboring classes. Genomic differentiation and conservation relevance of isolated marginal Primula farinosa populations in Central-Eastern Europe
abstract: Introduction Quaternary climatic oscillations produced heterogeneous range dynamics in European cold-adapted plants. Primula farinosa L. has been discussed in the context of the interglacial expansion model for moisture-demanding cold-adapted species. However, it remains unclear whether isolated low-elevation populations in Central European calcareous fens and wet meadows represent long-term relicts or recently established populations. Methods We used RADseq-derived SNPs from four sampling localities in the Balaton Region of Hungary and one low-elevation comparative locality at Lipce in the Julian Alps, Slovenia, to assess population-genomic structure, differentiation, allelic diversity and demographic history. Population structure was analyzed using SNP-based maximum-likelihood tree inference, PCA, model-based ancestry clustering and pairwise F ST estimates. We further quantified rarefied allelic richness and private allelic variation and performed exploratory population-specific historical effective population-size trajectories from folded site-frequency spectra. Results Population structure analyses revealed pronounced differentiation between Lipce and the Hungarian samples. title: Integrated AMMI, GGE Biplot, and MTSI analyses reveal yield stability and adaptation patterns in cowpea in Ghana
abstract: Introduction Genotype × environment interaction (G×E) complicates the identification of high-yielding and stable cowpea genotypes across variable production environments. This study evaluated 20 advanced cowpea breeding lines for grain yield, stability, and multi-trait performance across five location-year environments in Ghana during the 2024 and 2025 cropping seasons. Methods Trials were conducted using a randomized complete block design with three replications. Both seasons were drought-prone, although moisture stress varied among location-year environments because of erratic rainfall distribution. Grain yield was analysed using additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) and genotype plus genotype × environment (GGE) biplot analyses, while grain yield, biomass yield, harvest index, hundred-seed weight, and days to 95% pod maturity were integrated using the Multi-Trait Stability Index (MTSI). Results Analysis of variance revealed significant (p < 0.001) effects of environment, genotype, and G×E. The first two interaction principal components explained 92.15% of G×E variation, with Wa_2025 showing the largest IPCA1 score. Tuzievallenga had the highest mean grain yield (1149 kg ha −1 ), whereas IT17K-2030–2 had the lowest AMMI Stability Value (ASV = 114.54). Five genotypes combined high yield with relative stability: Tuzievallenga, IT17K-2030-2, IT17K-1095-2…

title: Medium-term clinical and economic outcomes of a multi-course medical preventive programme for machine-building plant workers exposed to occupational noise
abstract: Introduction. A shortage of skilled workers increases the relevance of programmes aimed at extending occupational longevity for employees with early signs of exposure to occupational hazards, including noise. However, evidence of the effectiveness of such programmes is limited.The aim of the study is to evaluate the medium-term clinical and economic outcomes of a medical preventive programme for machine-building plant workers with early signs of occupational noise exposure.Materials and methods. A historical closed cohort of 113 workers (mean age 55.8 years, work experience 26.1 years, equivalent sound level 89.7 dBA) was followed up from 2013 to 2025. Workers received two or three courses of the medical preventive programme (median duration 4 years) between 2013 and 2023. Shifts and rates of shift in hearing thresholds at frequencies of 500, 1000, 2000, and 4000 Hz, as well as the binaural pure tone average (BPTA), were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. The rate of threshold shift was compared with the age-related reference vales of ISO 7029-2017, and the number of cases of occupational noise-induced hearing loss (ONIHL) assessed against that predicted by the ISO 1999‑2017 model and the comparison group (113 workers selected using a matched-pair design). title: Linguistic inequity in academia: evidence from publication patterns in philosophy, 1975–2021
abstract: Abstract Linguistic inequity affecting non-native English speakers is widely documented in academia. This inequity is especially visible in philosophy, where success depends unusually heavily on the quality and nuance of written expression. Yet existing studies rely on small samples from a handful of elite journals, limiting their generalizability. We address this gap with the most comprehensive empirical analysis to date, covering 103,595 articles published across 223 journals between 1975 and 2021. Using two automated classifiers based on institutional affiliation and PhD country (accuracy above 89%), we estimate authors’ linguistic backgrounds at scale. We find strong evidence of severe underrepresentation of non-native authors in top philosophy journals across all classifiers, while evidence for underrepresentation in non-top journals is mixed. Moreover, while representation has improved since 1975, progress has been slower in elite journals. We investigate three potential explanations for the gap between high-prestige and non-top journals: language quality, active discrimination, and differences in research interests. We find at best suggestive evidence for the language-quality hypothesis; evidence that the adoption of double-blind review is associated with improved non-native representation (a pattern consistent with active discrimination); and evidence that prestigious j…

During this stage, peer groups can significantly influence adolescents’ behavior, self-perception, social status, communication experience, and value orientations. The article explores the psychological mechanisms through which social support, mutual trust, empathy, communication culture, a sense of group belonging, and social status affect adolescents’ adaptation to their social environment. Particular attention is given to the interaction between the family environment, educational institutions, peer groups, and digital communication spaces in creating conditions for successful social adaptation. title: The moderating role of athletic mental energy in the relationship between pessimism and burnout among athletes competing in university sports competitions
abstract: Purpose This study aimed to examine the moderating role of athletic mental energy in the relationship between pessimism and athlete burnout among athletes participating in the Turkish University Athletics Championships. Methods A correlational research design was employed in this study. The sample consisted of 235 track and field athletes, including 85 female and 150 male athletes. Data were collected using the Athletic Mental Energy Scale, the Sport Pessimism Scale, the Athlete Burnout Scale, and a Personal Information Form. Pearson’s correlation analysis and moderation analysis using Hayes’ PROCESS macro were conducted to analyze the data. Results The research findings revealed a significant positive association between pessimism and athlete burnout ( r = 0.334, p < 0.01). Athlete burnout was also significantly and negatively associated with the vigor ( r = −0.171, p < 0.01) and motivation ( r = −0.159, p < 0.05) dimensions of athletic mental energy.
