abstract: Abstract Climate change is regarded as one of the most pressing issues confronting humanity in the 21st century. Rising atmospheric temperatures, accompanied by declining precipitation, are exerting significant pressure on water resources and agricultural productivity. Morocco’s agricultural sector is highly vulnerable to climate variability and structural energy constraints. This study empirically investigates the short- and long-run impacts of climate factors and renewable energy on agricultural development in Morocco over the period 1990–2024 using the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds-testing approach. The dependent variable is agricultural value added (GDPA), and the explanatory variables include cereal production (AP), renewable energy consumption (RE), annual precipitation (PRE), mean temperature (TMP), and foreign direct investment in agriculture (AFDI). Bounds test results confirm a statistically significant long-run cointegrating relationship among the variables. The results reveal that bounds tests confirm a statistically significant long-run cointegrating relationship among the variables. Peer-led, faith-based co-designed intervention to improve Muslim women’s cancer screening: results from the IMCAN study
abstract: Introduction Cancer screening saves lives, but Muslim women are less likely to participate in screening than the general population. This makes them less likely to benefit from earlier diagnosis. Faith-based cancer communications provide an acceptable strategy for addressing screening barriers. Hence, we evaluated the impact of a faith-based intervention on knowledge, attitudes, and breast, cervical and colorectal (bowel) screening practices of Muslim women in the UK. Our intervention was a co-designed, peer-led, two-hour workshop informed by the Integrated Screening Action Model (I-SAM) and 3R religiously-tailored messaging model, included peer-led discussions about cancer screening, GP-led education on screening, testimonials from Muslim women, and a female religious-scholar led didactic on Islamic perspectives on screening. Methods In 2024, as part of a non-randomised feasibility and efficacy trial, the workshop was co-delivered 16 times, face-to-face or online, with 169 Muslim women in Glasgow and North-East England who were not up-to-date with at least one screening programme. Consistent with I-SAM, outcomes included screening knowledge, attitudes, intentions and self-reported uptake measured at baseline, post-intervention, and 6-and 12-months. Changes from baseline were evaluated with paired tests. Linear regression was used to assess associations with socio-demographic a…

title: A biohybrid mesh harvester for distributed energy harvesting in living tissues
abstract: Harnessing bio-origin resources for energy conversion offers a promising pathway toward energy sustainability matched to biosystems, addressing a fundamental limitation in powering bio-integrated electronics. However, existing approaches by integrating harvesters onto continuous substrates follow a “centralized” paradigm that differs markedly from the inherently distributed energy conversion found in living tissues, limiting both biocompatibility and scalability. We demonstrate a distributed harvesting strategy by integrating individual harvesting units within a mesh network that closely mimics the structural and mechanical properties of biological tissues. This architecture enables seamless embedding within in vitro cardiac tissue to form a bio-hybridization with cellular-scale intimacy across both device and substrate, transcending conventional approaches limited to a surface contact. This strategy achieves effective energy density more than an order of magnitude higher than that of existing approaches based on the centralized paradigm. While the concept is currently demonstrated in an in vitro cardiac system for converting biomechanical energy, the approach can provide a generalizable framework for integrating diverse energy-harvesting modalities and offers a pathway toward in vivo biohybrid systems.

abstract: Abstract Microwave-assisted treatment has potential for improving the handling of heavy crude oil, but direct microwave heating can be limited by the weak microwave response of the oil phase. In this study, an Fe3O4–graphene oxide (Fe3O4–GO) nanohybrid was evaluated as a microwave-responsive additive to enhance heating and improve the postcooling rheological response of heavy crude oil. The nanohybrid was prepared from Fe3O4 nanoparticles and oxygen-functionalized GO and characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), and vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM). Heavy-oil dispersions containing 0.05 and 0.10 wt % Fe3O4–GO were exposed to microwave irradiation for 1–5 min at two power settings, and viscosity was measured after cooling all samples to 25 °C. The greatest heating enhancement was recorded for the oil containing 0.10 wt % Fe3O4–GO at 80% microwave power, where the temperature reached 81.7 °C after 5 min and the average heating rate was 11.56 °C/min. The lowest mean postcooling apparent viscosity among the tested conditions, 301 cP, was obtained after 3 min, corresponding to a 28.84% reduction relative to the initial viscosity of the same formulation. abstract: Purpose Quantitative work on gambling-like mechanics (GLMs) in video games has largely treated them as a uniform category, overlooking differences in reward structure and similarity to traditional gambling. This study examines predictors of expenditure across three disaggregated GLM categories – cosmetic loot boxes (CLB), game-affecting loot boxes (GALB) and other in-game gambling-like content (OGLC). Design/methodology/approach Data were collected via an online survey of adult gamers (N = 587). Three model sets used the same gaming engagement and problem behavior indicators as predictors, each comprising a two-part approach: binary logistic regression on the full sample to predict purchase participation, and OLS linear regression among purchasers to predict expenditure amounts. Findings Financial engagement – expenditure on non-random free-to-play content and battle passes – emerged as the dominant predictor class; gaming frequency and gaming disorder were null throughout. Problem gambling severity predicted participation selectively – most strongly for OGLC – but predicted expenditure amounts in no category. Predictor patterns dissociated between participation and amount decisions in ways aggregated or uniform analytic approaches would have obscured. title: A scoping review of digital health technologies in glycogen storage diseases
abstract: Abstract Glycogen storage diseases (GSDs) are rare inherited metabolic disorders requiring complex management. Digital health technologies (DHTs) offer solutions for improving care delivery, yet their implementation remains poorly characterised. This scoping review systematically mapped DHT applications in GSDs following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching four databases through June 2026. We identified 44 studies with 662 participants across 17 GSD subtypes, revealing geographic concentration in Europe (48%), focus on hepatic subtypes (59%), and predominant use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) (66%). Five themes of DHT in GSD research emerged: intervention evaluation, communication enhancement, clinical monitoring, population surveillance, and technology development. Critical gaps included underrepresentation of muscle subtypes and minimal research in movement behaviour and psychosocial evaluation. Glucose-centric DHT use predominates in research; whilst clinically valuable, this neglects holistic health monitoring. Future research should prioritise comprehensive digital ecosystems integrating metabolic, behavioural, and psychosocial monitoring to optimise care for all individuals with GSDs.

title: Dislocation-induced artifacts in cyclic voltammetry of battery materials
abstract: Abstract This review establishes that crystallographic dislocations distort cyclic voltammetry in battery electrode materials, tracing that distortion from its thermodynamic origin through its diagnostic and design consequences across silicon, olivine, spinel, and layered-oxide chemistries. Cyclic voltammetry (CV) is the diagnostic workhorse of battery electrochemistry; experimentalists read peak positions, heights, and shapes as fingerprints of thermodynamic state and reaction kinetics. What the standard interpretation omits is the mechanical condition of the electrode. Crystallographic dislocations inside cathode nanoparticles generate stress fields that couple directly into the electrochemical boundary condition, and the resulting shifts and distortions in the CV response can be misread as purely chemical or kinetic phenomena. This coupling operates across material classes. Voltage hysteresis in silicon anodes, anomalous plateau formation in Mn-substituted olivines, and voltage fade in lithium-rich layered oxides are each a manifestation of the same Butler-Volmer correction in a different host. The mechanistic framework rests on the Larché-Cahn formalism, in which dislocation-induced hydrostatic stress enters the chemical potential of Li intercalation and shifts the equilibrium insertion potential. abstract: The Tax on the Acquisition of Rights to Land and Buildings (BPHTB) applies to the acquisition of rights to land and buildings by an individual or legal entity. The criteria for determining BPHTB are based on the agreed-upon transaction price in a sale, while in other situations, BPHTB is assessed based on the Official Land and Building Valuation (NJOP). The NJOP serves as the basis for tax assessment. However, if the NJOP value in a particular area is low, the sale and purchase transaction value is used instead. Inconsistencies in information regarding BPHTB create a situation fraught with uncertainty. Furthermore, the lack of sustained public information dissemination efforts by local governments regarding BPHTB has not yet reached the entire community. The objective of this study is to determine the extent to which the availability of information influences the collection of BPHTB taxes as a source of local revenue. This study employs a normative legal research approach. The data used are secondary data, divided into three main categories to support the research: primary legal sources, secondary legal sources, and tertiary legal sources. title: Electric Double Layer Organization of Proton-Transfer Pathways Regulates Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
abstract: Abstract Constructing bifunctional catalysts with synergistic interfaces is a promising strategy to overcome the sluggish kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline media, where interfacial proton transfer plays a critical role in the reaction kinetics. However, how bifunctional interfaces regulate the interfacial environment governing proton transfer remains poorly understood, particularly at the nanoscale. Here, using well-defined Pt/Ni and Pt/NiO model systems, we integrate spatially resolved scanning electrochemical microscopy, hydration force measurements, and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations across multiple length scales to establish a correlation among local HER kinetics, interfacial electrostatics, and hydration structure. Specifically, the Pt/NiO-derived interface exhibits a lower potential of zero charge (PZC) that is closer to the HER operating potential together with a more interconnected interfacial hydrogen-bond network. In contrast, the Pt/Ni-derived interface exhibits a higher PZC and a less-interconnected hydration structure. These results identify interfacial electrostatics and hydration organization within the electric double layer (EDL) as important factors governing the enhanced HER kinetics at bifunctional interfaces.

title: Soft organizational performance: behavioural antecedents and the role of emotional intelligence
abstract: Purpose This study examines how four leadership behavior categories (task-, relations-, change-, and external-oriented) relate to soft organizational performance in SMEs and whether leaders’ emotional intelligence moderates these relationships. Soft performance refers to specific intangible business capabilities and processes such as collaboration, digital maturity, customer orientation, renewal capability, and brand. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from 301 Finnish SMEs. Hierarchical regression analysis was applied to test direct and moderating effects. Findings Relations-oriented and external-oriented leadership behaviors show positive associations with soft performance, whereas task- and change-oriented behaviors do not have direct effects. Emotional intelligence moderates the relationship between task-oriented behavior and soft performance, modestly strengthening its impact. No moderation effects were found for other leadership categories. Change-oriented behavior shows neither direct nor moderated effects. abstract: Purpose This conceptual paper responds to the evolving needs of international marketing strategy (IMS) by proposing a theoretically grounded Digital Marketing Localization Framework (DMLF). The framework revisits the standardization versus adaptation debate, emphasizing its relevance in digitally mediated environments. Design/methodology/approach A structured literature review was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar (1983–mid-2025) pertaining to IMS frameworks, digital platforms, cross-cultural behavior and decision-making models. Several peer-reviewed articles and book chapters were included, while studies limited to traditional media or the B2B context were excluded. This synthesis incorporates key classical debates regarding IMS, and advances in digital ecosystems, personalization and cultural engagement. Drawing on an interdisciplinary approach that blends theoretical constructs from interrelated fields, this paper develops a structured, multi-dimensional decision-making framework. Findings The study highlights the importance of integrating cultural sensitivity, platform-specific dynamics and algorithmic personalization into IMS theory. It addresses gaps in pre-digital frameworks by offering actionable insights for navigating the complexities introduced by digital platforms and cross-border data governance. Strategies that can be implemented include strengthening the digital legal knowledge base, increasing knowledge sharing forums, developing apparatus competencies, and strengthening knowledge transfer mechanisms. title: Standardized black Allium chinense G.Don and Sonneratia apetala Banks polysaccharide as a natural health product strategy for pain, fever, and inflammation
abstract: Abstract Objectives To evaluate a standardized humid-heat-aged black Allium chinense G.Don extract and Sonneratia apetala Banks polysaccharide as a preclinical natural health product strategy for pain, fever, and inflammation. Methods AC-70E was standardized by HPLC-DAD, 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF)/S-allyl cysteine (SAC) marker control, and LC-MS profiling. SA-PS was quality-controlled for purity, endotoxin, monosaccharide profile, and molecular weight. Efficacy and interaction were assessed in murine nociception, pyrexia, and edema models using fixed-ratio Chou-Talalay analysis and inflammatory biomarkers. Results The combination showed synergy mainly in inflammation-dominant endpoints, including formalin phase II and carrageenan edema AUC, with CI values of 0.60–0.78 and DRI values of 1.30–2.10 at Fa=0.50–0.75. Responses were accompanied by lower IL-6/PGE 2 and MPO/COX-2-linked readouts. Conclusions These findings support a processing-informed natural health product framework with preclinical dose-sparing relevance for inflammation-dominant pain, fever, and edema, warranting further validation.
venue: Journal of Complementary and Integrative Medicine

title: Study on tumor ecology and precision medicine strategy of oral squamous cell carcinoma based on multi-omics cell atlas
abstract: Introduction Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is characterized by inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity, which complicates patient stratification and treatment. Although single-cell studies have improved the resolution of the OSCC microenvironment, the relationships among cellular states, spatial organization, immune-repertoire dynamics, and patient-level ecosystem patterns remain incompletely understood. Methods We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, single-cell T-cell receptor sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk RNA-sequencing data to characterize OSCC. Results We constructed a multi-omics cellular atlas comprising 88,442 cells and 63 cell subclusters, revealing complementary malignant-cell heterogeneity at the levels of transcriptional subclusters and recurrent meta-programs. Spatial and cell-cell communication analysis identified a reproducible association between PI3+ cancer-associated fibroblasts and APC_Myeloid cells and supported a candidate collagen-associated communication axis within tumor niches. Integration of paired transcriptomic and TCR data delineated a CD8+ T-cell pseudotime continuum accompanied by increasing clonal expansion and exhaustion-associated features, with spatial analysis linking intermediate trajectory states to regulatory T-cell and inflammatory NKT-cell-rich tumor-front regions. Extending the single-cell atlas to bulk cohorts by …

title: Further Redefining Motivation with Situated Cognition, Power, and Belonging
abstract: Abstract This article contributes to a growing convergence across educational psychology, the learning sciences, and culturally responsive education by further redefining motivation as an interactional and socially situated phenomenon. We review and extend ongoing efforts to challenge mainstream models that characterize motivation primarily in terms of individual-level psychological constructs and processes. We instead argue that motivation arises through social engagement in meaningful disciplinary activities shaped by power, identity, and community. Central to this redefinition are two innovative frameworks from Randi Engle (1967—2012): productive disciplinary engagement and expansive framing . The paper synthesizes these frameworks with critical and sociocultural theories to develop a design-based approach to engagement and motivation that highlights accountability, authorship, and intercontextuality. We examine two programs of design-based research—one focused on online instruction and assessment and the other on first-year college writing seminars—to demonstrate how Engle’s design principles might motivate equitable engagement and a lasting sense of belonging, especially for students with minoritized identities. The motivational implications of this approach are connected to mainstream motivation theories (i.e., social cognitive, self-determination, expectancy-value, and a…

title: Performance analysis of a 5 Gbps PAM-4 modulated visible light optical wireless communication link: impact of transmission power, receiver field-of-view, and concentrator design parameters
abstract: Abstract This paper presents a detailed performance study of a visible light communication (VLC) link using 4-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) at a 450 nm wavelength. Link performance is systematically evaluated as a function of transmission distance across varying transmission power (20, 18, 16 dBm), irradiance half-angle (60°, 40°, 20°), optical concentration factor (30°, 60°, 90°), index concentration factor (1.0, 1.5, 2.0), and detector surface area (1, 0.8, 0.6 cm 2 ). Eye diagrams at the maximum achievable distance for the forward error correction (FEC) threshold of log(BER) = −2.42 provide a qualitative view of signal degradation, complementing quantitative log(BER) and EVM results. Results show that increasing transmission power, detector area, index concentration factor, optical concentration factor, and irradiance half-angle each independently extend the maximum link distance while maintaining acceptable EVM. Under the optimum parameter combination (20 dBm, 1 cm 2 , index factor 2.0, optical concentration 30°, half-angle 60°), the link satisfies the FEC threshold up to 3 m, with an EVM of 18.83912 %, rising to 25.97188 % at 5 m. These findings offer practical design guidelines for maximizing transmission distance in high-speed PAM-4–based VLC links while meeting FEC-level error performance requirements.

title: Power interplay among actors in the governance of Indonesian film and digital content censorship policy
abstract: This study uses Indonesia as a case study to examine the complicated relationship between state and non-state actors in film and digital content censorship. As film, television, and digital content grow, censorship has become a crucial governance instrument to manage cultural and moral standards. At the same time, creative industries and civic society are challenging restrictive rules to promote free speech. The research employs stakeholder analysis, grounded in Ackermann and Eden’s stakeholder identification theory, to explore actor configurations, interests, and influence within the policy process. Using qualitative methods—primarily in-depth interviews and FGD the study identified 18 stakeholder groups, including regulatory bodies, industry associations, civil society organisations, and community actors. Key findings show that the Indonesian Film Censorship Board (LSF) and Indonesian Broadcasting Commission (KPI) dominate film certification and broadcast content. LSF operations are also supervised by the Ministry of Culture. Government institutions have more power than industry and civil society, according to stakeholder mapping. The study found continuous contradictions between regulatory control and popular demand for creative space in Indonesia’s censorship environment. The stakeholder matrix adds a new empirical dimension to Southeast Asian media governance studies. It e…

title: Health Index Evaluation of Power Transformers Based on Electrical and Insulation Diagnostic Parameters
abstract: Power transformers are essential components of electrical power transmission systems, where insulation deterioration and operational aging can compromise reliability and increase the risk of failure. Comprehensive condition assessment is therefore necessary to support effective maintenance planning and enhance transformer asset management. This study aims to assess the condition of power transformers using a Health Index (HI) approach that integrates electrical and insulation diagnostic parameters. The study was conducted on 14 power transformers installed at 150-kV transmission substations. The assessment incorporated several diagnostic parameters, including dissolved gas analysis (DGA), moisture content, acidity, interfacial tension, breakdown voltage, insulation resistance, dielectric dissipation factor (tan ?), winding resistance, and sweep frequency response analysis (SFRA). These parameters were integrated into five assessment factors: internal fault indicators, paper insulation condition, insulating oil quality, electrical insulation condition, and winding condition. The results indicated that four transformers were classified as Very Good, four as Good, three as Fair, and three as Poor. Furthermore, the analysis revealed a negative relationship between transformer service age and HI values, with a coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.7793, suggesting a strong associat…

title: Coal Consumption Optimization through Performance Gap Analysis and Heat Rate Improvement in Thermal Power Plants
abstract: India coal fired thermal power is still playing an important role in electricity generation in the country. To enhance plant performance, economic competitiveness and environmental sustainability, therefore, the efficient use of coal is essential. Coal is the major component of the generation cost, and it plays a significant role in the plant heat rate and plant efficiency in Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah Thermal Power Station (SDSTPS). There have been several studies on heat-rate analysis, energy audit, and auxiliary power optimization, but little focus has been paid to the plant-level approach to optimize coal consumption with actual plant data. The present work is to optimizing coal consumption by considering technical and operational performance of the plant, in particular combustion efficiency and turbine heat rate, which are important parameters of specific consumption of coal. The study utilizes performance gap analysis, evaluation of operational data, energy audit and heat-rate analysis to determine the significant performance deviations and set appropriate optimization parameters to increase plant efficiency. The analysis indicates that optimizing the coal use systemically can lead to improved efficiency and reliability and reduce coal consumption overall. The results indicate that streamlined operational practices together with advanced energy management systems can signi…

title: RAQAMLI TA’LIM MUHITIDA O‘QUVCHILARNING MUSTAQIL TA’LIM OLISH KOMPETENSIYALARINI RIVOJLANTIRISHNING PEDAGOGIK IMKONIYATLARI
abstract: The article examines the pedagogical opportunities for developing students’ independent learning competencies in a digital educational environment. The study analyzes the potential of the digital educational environment to develop students’ skills in goal setting, information search and analysis, organization of independent learning activities, monitoring of learning outcomes, and reflective evaluation of their own activities. The pedagogical opportunities for developing independent learning competencies are systematized based on motivational-goal- oriented, information-cognitive, activity-practical, and monitoring-reflective components.

title: Penerapan Experiential Learning Berbasis Media Konkret untuk Kesadaran Tubuh pada Siswa Autis: Studi Kasus Pendahuluan
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan mengeksplorasi kelayakan (feasibility) penerapan multisensory experiential learning yang berakar pada prinsip embodied cognition untuk meningkatkan pemahaman konseptual dan kesadaran tubuh (body awareness) pada siswa dengan Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). Menggunakan desain one-group pretest-posttest berskala mikro terhadap dua siswa kelas V di SLB Autis Laboratorium Universitas Negeri Malang yang dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling, intervensi dilaksanakan selama tiga kali pertemuan dengan durasi 45 menit pada setiap pertemuan. Intervensi difokuskan pada penggunaan media konkret dan aktivitas sensorimotor untuk menghubungkan pengalaman fisik dengan pemahaman fungsi anggota tubuh dalam kehidupan sehari-hari. Kemampuan siswa diukur melalui tes kinerja terstruktur yang mencakup kemampuan menyebutkan, menunjukkan, dan memahami fungsi anggota tubuh. Hasil analisis kuantitatif menunjukkan peningkatan akurasi konseptual dari rata-rata 60% pada pretest menjadi 90% pada posttest, dengan perolehan N-Gain sebesar 0,80 dalam kategori tinggi. Analisis individual menunjukkan variasi respons, dengan N-Gain sebesar 1,00 pada Siswa 1 dan 0,60 pada Siswa 2. Temuan juga menunjukkan bahwa keterlibatan langsung melalui stimulasi sensorimotor berkaitan dengan peningkatan perhatian dan keterlibatan siswa selama pembelajaran, meskipun respons terhadap intervensi berbeda…

title: PENGARUH MODEL DISCOVERY LEARNING BERBANTUAN MEDIA GAMBAR TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR SISWA PADA PEMBELAJARAN IPAS
abstract: Low student learning outcomes in natural and social sciences (IPAS) in elementary schools are frequently caused by the dominance of conventional lecture methods that lack concrete visual aids. The limited use of interactive media leaves students passive and struggling to grasp abstract scientific concepts. This study aims to determine the effect of the discovery learning model assisted by picture media on the IPAS learning outcomes of third-grade students at SD Negeri 060830 Medan Petisah in the 2025/2026 academic year. This study used a quantitative method with a quasi-experimental non-equivalent control group design. The research sample comprised 50 students divided into an experimental class (class III-A, ) taught using the discovery learning model assisted by picture media and a control class (class III-B, ) taught using conventional learning. Data were gathered through multiple-choice objective tests administered before (pretest) and after (posttest) the intervention. The results showed that the posttest average of the experimental class reached 82.60, outperforming the control class, which scored an average of 75.20. The inferential analysis confirms that the discovery learning model assisted by picture media exerts a positive and significant effect on improving elementary students' IPAS learning outcomes. title: Introduction to using symbolic regression for interpretable machine learning in healthcare
abstract: Abstract The past decade has seen machine learning play an increasingly important role in medicine. However, many of the state-of-the-art models being developed and deployed suffer from a lack of transparency, limiting integration into the clinical decision-making process and raising concerns about patient safety. Here we call attention to symbolic regression, a largely overlooked machine learning technique that aims to be both accurate and interpretable by learning readable mathematical models from data. In recent years, it has undergone rapid advancements with successful application to problems across a wide range of disciplines. In this perspective, we provide an approachable introduction to symbolic regression, highlight its strengths and limitations, and explore its potential applications in medicine.

title: Student outcomes in a student-led clinic: beyond clinical learning
abstract: Introduction Student-assisted, -run or -led health clinics (SLCs) are increasingly common worldwide, but student outcomes remain under-evaluated, with existing work focused narrowly on clinical and/or academic outcomes. Methods This study presents the findings of an evaluation of the impact of a student-assisted clinic in New Zealand, on participating students subjective wellbeing, assessed using the Satisfaction with Life Scale (SWLS), as well as on a range of programme-related intermediate outcomes theorised to support wellbeing, including leadership, communication, and clinical capability. Students undertaking placements at the clinic were surveyed at three time points: at the start, the end, and at six months post-placement. Results Participating students maintained levels of self-reported wellbeing over placement periods while significantly improving leadership, purpose, cultural connection, and clinical capability. Income and sleep were shown to be key factors related to SWLS scores. Discussion Student-related outcomes from SLCs may extend beyond clinical care and academic performance, highlighting the value of a more holistic approach to SLC evaluation.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Indonesian Mobile Banking Reviews on Google Play Store in 2025: A Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: Mobile banking applications generate large volumes of user reviews that can be used to evaluate digital banking service quality. This study analyzes sentiment in Indonesian mobile banking reviews on the Google Play Store in 2025 and compares the performance of Naive Bayes (NB), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF). A total of 270,977 reviews were collected from five applications, namely BRImo, Livin’ by Mandiri, myBCA, BYOND by BSI, and wondr by BNI. The data were processed through text cleaning, case folding, tokenization, word normalization, stopword removal, and negation retention. Sentiment labels were generated automatically using the InSet Lexicon and validated on 450 stratified review samples. The validation results showed moderate agreement between automatic and manual labels, with an accuracy of 0.6111, macro-F1 score of 0.5384, and Cohen’s Kappa of 0.4167. Review texts were represented using TF-IDF with unigram and bigram features, and model performance was evaluated across six stratified data-splitting scenarios using accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro-F1, confusion matrix, and macro ROC-AUC. The results show that RF in Scenario 6 achieved the best performance, with an accuracy of 0.9524, macro-F1 score of 0.8498, and macro ROC-AUC of 0.9798. Dominant-term analysis indicates recurring complaints related to login failures, transaction error…

title: Inteligência Artificial (IA) no processo de ensino-aprendizagem da matemática
abstract: Have you ever used AI in your math classes, and/or school and academic activities? It is known that AI in Education has emerged as a driving factor in transforming thoughts. The objective is to identify whether AI has influenced the teaching and learning processes of mathematics in basic education, based on statements from teachers in the Brazilian public education network. A qualitative case study research is presented, with exploratory purposes, aiming to gain knowledge about the use of AI in school and academic activities. It was identified in the data analysis that the teachers responding to the electronic questionnaire were unaware of AI and its contributions to teaching. But it is clear that they are curious about the topic, and refer to AI, but commonly, as a “simulator of human intelligence”. Thus, it is concluded that the discussion on the topic is relevant, and webinars, workshops and thematic mini-courses are proposed, elucidating the importance of a fruitful debate around ethical reflections that highlight the potential use of AI in school and academic spaces.

title: PENGARUH MODEL PEMBELAJARAN PROJECT BASED LEARNING (PJBL) TERHADAP HASIL BELAJAR IPAS SISWA KELAS IV
abstract: This study was motivated by the Natural and Social Sciences (IPAS) learning process in elementary schools, which remains teacher-centered, lacks active student participation, and results in low learning outcomes. This study aims to examine the implementation of the learning process, evaluate student learning achievements, and determine the effect of the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model on fourth-grade students' IPAS learning outcomes regarding human needs prioritization at SD Negeri 101818 Pancur Batu during the 2025/2026 academic year. A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental method employing a one-group pretest-posttest design was utilized. The research population encompassed all fourth-grade students, with a selected sample of 30 students determined through a saturated sampling technique. Data collection techniques involved multiple-choice tests, student questionnaires, classroom observation rubrics, and documentation. The results showed a significant improvement in student learning outcomes, with the class average score rising from 66.93 in the pretest to 77.60 in the posttest. Inferential statistical testing confirmed that the Project-Based Learning (PjBL) model exerts a positive and significant effect on enhancing elementary school students' IPAS learning outcomes. title: The donkey and the algorithm: cultivating judgement infrastructure for AI literacy in higher education
abstract: Purpose This paper reframes artificial intelligence (AI) literacy in higher education as a problem of judgement formation rather than tool fluency alone. It asks how students can be supported not only to use generative AI, but also to evaluate, limit, disclose or refuse its use responsibly under conditions of uncertainty. Design/methodology/approach This paper develops a conceptual and pedagogical argument through engagement with AI literacy scholarship, evaluative judgement, information judgement and educational theory. Rhetorical literacy, informal logic and argumentation, and ethical reasoning/phronesis are used as a pragmatic framework for analysing the judgement capacities required for meaningful AI engagement. Findings This paper proposes a judgement-infrastructure account of AI literacy. It argues that student suspicion, selective use, uncritical reliance and refusal can be read as sites where judgement is practised, bypassed or left unarticulated. The Judgement-Infrastructure Gap Model is offered as a diagnostic heuristic for examining where judgement is supported or neglected across curricula, assessment, institutional policy and technological platforms. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual paper, the argument and model require empirical and design-based testing. Future research should examine how students justify AI use, limited use, disclosure and refusa…

title: “MAKTABGACHA YOSHDAGI BOLALARGA O‘YIN ORQALI TA’LIM BERISH: ZAMONAVIY YONDASHUVLAR VA SAMARALI METODLAR”
abstract: This article explores modern approaches and effective methods of teaching preschool children through play. The importance of play activities in the intellectual, physical, socio-emotional, and creative development of children is analyzed. The article also highlights the pedagogical potential of using didactic, active, role-playing, creative, and developmental games in the educational process. In addition, recommendations are provided for educators on the effective use of play-based learning technologies in preschool education organizations.

title: Molecular Spectrum-Based Machine Learning Models for PARP1 Drug Discovery
AIMNet2-rxn: A machine-learned potential for generalized reaction modeling on a millions-of-pathways scale
abstract: Mechanistic modeling of chemical transformations offers a compelling basis for understanding reactivity and allows for prediction of reaction outcomes before attempting experiments. Despite progress in machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), we demonstrate that available models lack the accuracy for diverse reaction modeling. With this motivation, we developed a general MLIP for mechanistic modeling of closed-shell carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, and oxygen reactions, AIMNet2-rxn, using a dataset of ∼4.7 × 10 6 range-separated density functional theory calculations. AIMNet2-rxn enables reaction modeling ∼10 6 faster than the reference quantum mechanical (QM) methods while substantially outperforming graph-based ML, reaffirming the value using three-dimensional chemical information for training. On a test suite of well-known reaction mechanisms—such as amide formation, proton transfers, and pericyclics—AIMNet2-rxn yields 1 to 2 kilocalories per mole accuracy across reaction coordinates without retraining or system-specific fine-tuning. To exploit graphics processing unit parallelism and AIMNet2-rxn efficiency, we introduce a batched nudged elastic band procedure that readily achieves minimum energy pathway search on a millions-of-reactions scale. To demonstrate complex reaction characterization, the thermodynamics of an 11-step pathway producing hydroxymethylfurfural, the ex…

title: Temporal epistemology in the age of AI: learning, knowing and the reorganization of chronological structure
abstract: Purpose This paper argues that generative artificial intelligence (AI) has forced a reckoning with a long-standing inadequacy in the temporal assumptions that have structured educational thought since the Enlightenment. It introduces post-linear epistemology as a framework for understanding how knowledge functions when learning is no longer adequately modelled as movement through a temporal sequence and develops concrete implications for curriculum design, assessment and teacher practice. Design/methodology/approach The paper is conceptual. It synthesizes scholarship on complexity in education, non-linear learning, technological acceleration, futures studies and critical artificial intelligence in education and uses this synthesis to specify the conditions under which a post-linear account of educational knowledge becomes necessary. Findings The paper identifies three interrelated shifts that, on this account, characterize the post-linear condition and are proposed here as claims for further examination rather than as established findings. First, chronologically ordered curriculum sequences are argued to be no longer adequate as the default architecture of educational design – though not as the only legitimate one. Second, cumulative derivation is argued to be increasingly displaced, in AI-mediated contexts, by probabilistic and relational forms of knowledge production. Third, …

title: Amorphous TiO 2 from a statistical view based on molecular dynamics using machine learning interatomic potentials
abstract: Abstract We use molecular dynamics with a machine-learning interatomic potential based on the higher-order equivariant message-passing atomic cluster expansion (MACE) framework to construct an ensemble of 100 amorphous TiO 2 configurations. The final structures are subject to variable-cell relaxations using density functional theory calculations, where PBEsol functional is adopted as it reproduces the experimental densities for all the three crystalline phases, namely, rutile, anatase and brookite. The mean density is calculated to be 3.94 g cm -3 . While the ensemble is dominated by 6-coordinated Ti and 3-coordinated O, the corresponding percentage is 57.4% and 66.8% only. There exist 28.9% of 5-coordinated Ti, 12.1% 7-coordinated Ti, 21.4% 2-coordinated 21.4% O and 11.8% 4-coordinated O. Using hybrid HSE06 functional with the exact-exchange fraction (α) set to 0.18, the ensemble average yields a band gap of 3.44 ± 0.12 eV for the amorphous phase, which is greater than those of the three crystalline phases obtained using the same computational framework, namely, variable-cell relaxation using PBEsol and band gap calculation using HSE06 (α=0.18). Analysis of the density of states suggests that the band-gap widening in the amorphous phase is associated with the narrowed Ti 3 d band. It is potentially useful to adopt the protocol in this work to study the effect of amorphization …

title: Measurement uncertainty of fluoride determination in vegetation: contributions from sampling and analysis
The hidden value of uncertainty in medical segmentation
abstract: The pipeline of most segmentation algorithms begins and ends with a curated dataset. In medical imaging, these datasets will be the result of significant effort from clinicians, with each contour representing the result of a sequence of informed decisions. With so much effort and experience involved in the creation of these datasets, we must consider what information about annotation uncertainty is lost over the course of the pipeline. Annotation uncertainty is an inherent property of any dataset containing expert interpretations, and is especially important to quantify in a safety-critical domain such as medical imaging. In this Perspective, we examine the consequences of losing information concerning annotation uncertainty, not only for dataset representation, but also for the reliability of model evaluation. We describe this as annotation-induced evaluation uncertainty: variation in reported model performance arising from the particular annotation used for evaluation, when multiple distinct expert annotations may be plausible. By contrast, considerable research attention has been given to model uncertainty over the last decade, including the development of probabilistic representations for predicted segmentations that allow nuanced spatial information to be included in uncertainty quantification. Comparable representations for annotation uncertainty should complement these d…

title: Trade policy uncertainty and risk spillovers in global currency markets
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how trade policy uncertainty (TPU) affects risk transmission in global foreign exchange markets. Design/methodology/approach Using daily data for 20 major currencies from 2005 to 2025, we combine autoregressive exponential generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity with generalized error distribution (AR-EGARCH-GED) volatility estimates, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator vector autoregression (LASSO-VAR) connectedness measures, and a generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity mixed-data sampling (GARCH-MIDAS) framework that links monthly TPU to daily return and volatility spillovers. Findings The results show that global FX markets are highly interconnected, with average return connectedness of 71.3% and volatility connectedness of 58.46%. Spillovers are time-varying and rise around major stress episodes, including the global financial crisis, Brexit, the USA–China trade war, the COVID-19 pandemic, and renewed trade-policy tensions in 2024–2025. The results also reveal a core-periphery structure: the Singapore dollar and the euro frequently act as important transmitters, while several emerging-market currencies mainly absorb external shocks. The US dollar appears relatively balanced on average, but its large two-way linkages confirm its continuing systemic role, especially during stress periods. Originality…

A Fluctuating Lattice Boltzmann Model with Independent Directional Stochastic Fluctuations for Brownian Motion
abstract: Abstract Accurate simulation of Brownian motion is essential for understanding particle dynamics at micro- and nanoscales. The fluctuating lattice Boltzmann method provides a mesoscopic framework for modeling thermal fluctuations, but conventional formulations impose identical fluctuations on opposite lattice directions, limiting independent stochastic variation. Here, we relax this symmetry by allowing independent fluctuations in each direction. Formulations are derived for the D3Q19 and D3Q27 models and applied to spherical Brownian particles, with comparisons against the conventional D3Q15 model. The simulated translational and rotational mean-square velocities are consistent with the energy equipartition theorem, confirming thermal equilibrium. The resulting diffusion coefficients demonstrate that the D3Q19 and D3Q27 models reduce the relative error by approximately 3% compared with the D3Q15 model when reproducing the Stokes-Einstein prediction. To quantify inherent errors, a correction factor α is introduced to rescale the fluctuation intensity so that the Stokes-Einstein diffusion coefficient is recovered within statistical uncertainty. The smaller α values required for the D3Q19 and D3Q27 models indicate more physically faithful stochastic behavior. The proposed methods therefore provide a more flexible and accurate representation of thermal fluctuations for Brownian mo…

title: Development and optimization of antimicrobial β-triketone-loaded chitosan nanoparticles for periodontal therapy
abstract: Abstract Periodontal disease is a bacterial infection leading to the progressive destruction of soft and hard oral tissues. Current clinical treatment involves scaling and root planing (SRP), combined with adjunctive therapies, such as the application of antibacterial reagents. Mānuka oil, derived from Leptospermum scoparium , a native plant in New Zealand and Australia, exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity mainly attributed to its β-triketone compounds. However, due to the limitations, including low solubility and strong volatility, clinical translation of mānuka oil and β-triketones is limited. Given the biocompatible, antimicrobial, and mucoadhesive properties of chitosan, this study aimed to synthesize mānuka oil and β-triketone-loaded chitosan nanoparticles to achieve sustained release and enhanced antimicrobial efficacy, supporting their therapeutic potential as a natural and antibiotic-free alternative for treating bacterial infections, especially in periodontal disease. Mānuka oil and β-triketone-loaded chitosan nanoparticles were synthesized using a microfluidic platform with the average size of 253.0 nm (polydispersity index (PDI): 0.421) and 196.5 nm (PDI: 0.446), respectively. Encapsulation techniques enabled prolonged oil release over 24 h, with effective antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus , Streptococcus mutans , Aggregatibacter actinom…

title: Task-specific manipulability metrics for redundancy optimization in cooperative manipulation
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to investigate how redundant degrees of freedom can improve task-relevant dexterity and force capability in cooperative manipulation without disturbing commanded object motion. It compares task-specific manipulability metrics, particularly when the dominant external-load direction differs from the commanded motion direction. Design/methodology/approach A closed-loop inverse-kinematics and null-space gradient-projection framework is used to compare velocity, force and directional-force manipulability. The objectives are evaluated on a planar dual-arm hardware platform using external loads and actuator-current-based effort measurement. A complementary MuJoCo study with two 7-degrees of freedom Franka Panda manipulators extends the comparison to static holding, translational pick-and-place and six-dimensional pick-and-place from six initial object configurations. Findings Hardware experiments show that the objectives produce distinct internal configurations while preserving object motion. Velocity manipulability improves kinematic dexterity, while directional-force manipulability yields lower effort than force-only optimization when the commanded motion and external-load directions differ. The spatial simulations further show that all three objectives improve or maintain their respective measures across different initial configurations while maintaining low…

title: OCE: an optimization convergence metric for LiDAR SLAM degeneracy detection
abstract: Abstract LiDAR-based Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) systems suffer from environment-induced degeneracy in geometrically self-similar scenes such as tunnels and cylindrical structures, where the point cloud registration problem becomes ill-conditioned. Existing degeneracy detection methods predominantly rely on eigenvalue analysis of the Hessian matrix, which assesses geometric conditioning at a fixed linearization point. However, in semi-degenerate environments containing partial but sufficient geometric constraints, these methods tend to produce false positive detections because measurement noise inflates eigenvalues and obscures the contribution of minor structural features. In this paper, we propose the Optimization Convergence Efficiency (OCE) metric, which evaluates the relative contraction of the directional optimizer gradient across Levenberg-Marquardt evaluations and directly characterizes the convergence response of LiDAR registration along the monitored state direction. The proposed method is evaluated through controlled simulation with ground-truth-based quantitative assessment and real-world UAV experiments in a wind-turbine tower and a long tunnel. In the nominal simulation, OCE achieves 98.21% recall with a 2.33% false-positive rate, compared with 100% recall and a 49.42% false-positive rate for the conventional eigenvalue-ratio detector. Controlled …

title: Numerical Optimization of Thermoelectric Heat Pump Assisted Drying System
abstract: One of the methods for food preservation involves utilizing the heat from solar radiation to remove moisture, aptly known as solar drying. Different approaches in enhancing solar dryer efficiency have been made throughout the years, involving circulation refinements, mechanism improvements, and insulation enhancements. Thermoelectric heat pumps (TEHP) leverage the Peltier effect to generate temperature difference that can be integrated with solar dryer system. However, the information on design and parameters for integration is scarce and underexplored. In this work, TEHP-assisted solar drying system was designed and the ideal parameters for efficient drying rate were determined by optimizing fan position and airflow rate. The system’s performance was gauged through moisture content reduction of drying loads (ginger). CFD numerical optimization was performed at the airflow rate between 0.003 - 0.012 m3/s, at three different fan locations. Results showed that lower airflow rate increases the accumulated heat inside the chamber, resulting in higher moisture content removal within the load, thus increasing drying rate. Even though the higher airflow showed greater reduction in H2O mass, reduction of drying chamber temperature was also observed, resulting in reduced effectiveness in moisture removal. The ideal fan position and airflow rate were determined to be at the system inlet …

title: Multi-Level Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient reinforcement learning for safety-constrained trajectory optimization of collaborative industrial robots
abstract: Collaborative robots operating in modern manufacturing environments require trajectory planning strategies that simultaneously support efficiency, adaptability, and operational safety. This study proposes a Multi-Level Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (ML-DDPG) framework for safety-constrained trajectory optimization. The framework combines a strategic waypoint level, a continuous DDPG motion-control policy, and a reactive feasibility projection that corrects unsafe actions before execution. The trajectory-planning problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process with reward terms for goal progress, obstacle clearance, smoothness, energy, execution time, and safety. Descriptive experiments in a custom PyTorch-based three-dimensional environment compare ML-DDPG with conventional planners and the DDPG, TD3, and SAC baselines. In the retained single training run, ML-DDPG produced observed values of 98.7% success, 1.08 mm trajectory error, a 0.98 smoothness index, and no recorded collision. These values are single-run observations and are not means over independent seeds; variability and statistical significance cannot be estimated from the available record. The exported traces show faster reward growth within the 200-episode budget, and the single-run ablation record associates the largest observed gains with the combined multi-level, reward, and projection components. title: An Integrated Broadband Low-Noise Microwave Source for Superconducting Quantum Circuits
abstract: Abstract Scaling superconducting quantum processors increasingly relies on custom control electronics that can simultaneously satisfy spectral purity, multi-channel isolation, and long-term stability within a compact and integrated platform. Here we present Quantum microwave source (QMW), a classical three-channel broadband low-noise microwave source that consolidates qubit XY drive, readout excitation, and Josephson parametric amplifier (JPA) pump generation onto a single hardware module operating from 4 to 14 GHz with an output power range of -20 to +10 dBm. Electronic characterization yields a spurious-free dynamic range greater than 55 dB, equivalently a largest spur below -55 dBc, a phase noise as low as -110 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset for a 5 GHz carrier and below -103 dBc/Hz at the same offset across the full band, and output power stability within 0.1 dB over 24 hours. Integrated into the control chain of a 36-qubit superconducting processor, QMW pumps a JPA to 19.2 dB gain to enable high-SNR single-shot readout, while sustaining qubit coherence times of T 1 = 60.1 ± 0.8 μs, T 2,Ramsey = 24.2 ± 1.5 μs, and T 2,echo = 58.6 ± 2.1 μs, and an average single-qubit gate fidelity of 99.95 ± 0.05% measured by randomized benchmarking. The compact and modular nature of QMW provides a scalable microwave generation solution for largescale superconducting quantum processors, with poten…

title: Integrated proteomic and metabolomic profiling characterizes tryptophan metabolic disturbance associated with mortality in ICU-admitted SFTS patients
abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, is associated with high mortality among intensive care unit (ICU) patients; however, the integrated proteomic–metabolomic mechanisms underlying fatal outcomes remain poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 68 patients with SFTS, who were admitted to the ICU and classified them as survivors (n = 33) or non-survivors (n = 35) according to their 28-day clinical outcomes. Untargeted metabolomic profiling using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry and quantitative proteomic profiling using data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry were performed on plasma samples collected at ICU admission. Multivariable analysis, pathway enrichment analysis, correlation analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis were used to identify potential prognostic biomarkers and characterize molecular associations. Non-survivors exhibited more severe multi-organ injury and systemic inflammation. Metabolomic profiling revealed marked disruption of tryptophan metabolism: L-tryptophan levels were decreased, whereas kynurenine and its downstream metabolites (kynurenic acid [KA], 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid [3-HAA], xanthurenic acid [XA], and 5-hydroxyindolepyruvate [5-HIP]) were increased, suggesting activation of the kynurenine pathway. The four core …

title: Understanding ChatGPT adoption among medical students: an integrated theoretical model of psychological barriers and individual factors
abstract: Background The growing adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, has created new opportunities for medical education by supporting learning, problem-solving, and knowledge acquisition. However, evidence regarding the psychological and individual factors influencing ChatGPT adoption among medical students remains limited. This study develops and tests an integrated theoretical model that combines Privacy Theory, Technostress Theory, Affect Theory, Diffusion of Innovation Theory, and the Theory of Planned Behavior to explain ChatGPT adoption. Material and methods A quantitative cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate medical students at King Faisal University, Saudi Arabia using a structured, self-administered questionnaire. The proposed model examined the effects of privacy concern, technophobia, guilt feelings, and innovativeness on behavioral intention and ChatGPT usage behavior, with behavioral intention serving as the mediating variable. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Results The findings showed that innovativeness had a significant positive relationship with behavioral intention ( β = 0.579, p < 0.001), while behavioral intention had a strong positive relationship with ChatGPT usage behavior ( β = 0.777, p < 0.001). In addition, behavioral intention significantl…

An Integrated Preventive Maintenance Transformation Framework Combining Lean Practices, Autonomous Maintenance and Digital Traceability
abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of Lean and Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) methodologies, many manufacturing companies still struggle to operationally integrate preventive maintenance, workplace organization, autonomous maintenance, and digital traceability into a coherent and measurable maintenance-improvement system. This Action Research study presents an integrated Lean-based preventive maintenance transformation framework implemented in a production unit of a major corrugated cardboard packaging manufacturer. The project focused on the DRO 1628 NT rotary die-cutter, identified as the most critical asset in the converting section through a structured multi-criteria criticality assessment. The proposed framework combined autonomous maintenance routines, standardized inspection procedures, 5S workplace organization, KPI-driven monitoring, and maintenance communication digitalization through a custom Microsoft Power Apps (Microsoft Corporation, Redmond, Washington, DC, USA) solution. The novelty of the study lies in the operational integration of these organizational, technical, and digital elements within a unified preventive maintenance transformation strategy specifically adapted to a high-pressure industrial environment characterized by limited traceability, reactive maintenance practices, and strong dependence on informal operator knowledge. title: SLC39-driven zinc influx orchestrates pleiotropic tumor–immune system cross-talk to establish immune suppression in colorectal cancer
abstract: Tumor metabolic programs shape immune evasion; however, the mechanism by which nutrient-transport systems rewire tumor-immune cell interactions remains unknown. We integrated bulk multi-omics, single-cell transcriptomics, spatial profiling, and functional assays for colorectal cancer–associated zinc-driven immunosuppressive circuit identification. Multi-omics analysis of 258 patients revealed three solute carrier transporter-centered archetypes, with an SLC39-enriched subtype aligned with consensus molecular subtype 2–like immune-desert tumors. SLC39-mediated zinc influx activated CDX2, which engaged a distal enhancer to induce tumor cell-specific CD24 expression. CD24 + tumor cells formed spatial niches with SIGLEC10-expressing monocyte-derived macrophages, dendritic cells, and resident macrophages, activating pleiotropic programs that suppress phagocytosis and remodel adhesion. SLC39 overexpression increased intracellular zinc and CD24 levels and reduced macrophage-mediated engulfment, whereas CD24 blockade restored phagocytosis. The zinc-CDX2-CD24-SIGLEC10 axis defined a terminal cancer cell state associated with poor survival and immune checkpoint blockade resistance. A seven-gene signature predicted immunotherapy responses across five colorectal cancer cohorts, identifying SLC39-driven zinc influx as a metabolic checkpoint governing immune exclusion.

abstract: This article analyzes the history of the creation of textbooks and manuals for a new type of Uzbek schools under the influence of the Jadid movement in native language education in the second half of the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century. It highlights how authors such as A. Fitrat, Q. Ramazon, X. Qayyumiy, A. Yo‘ldoshev, A. Borokov, A. G‘ulomov, T. Shermuhammadov, Z. Ma’rufov, and Y. Abdullayev addressed issues regarding vowels and consonants, vowel harmony, back/front vowel distinctions, labial harmony, stress, and noisy (obstruent) sounds in their textbooks. Furthermore, the article provides a scholarly basis for examining historical experiences in teaching phonetics, terminological variations, and the inductive-deductive structure of these textbooks, while also addressing contemporary challenges regarding pronunciation, intonation, and stress, and the necessity of improving these areas through interactive methods, ICT, and individualized approaches. The article compares works such as Fitrat’s “An Experiment on Uzbek Language Rules” and “Morphology” (“Sarf”), textbooks by Q. Ramazon and X. Qayyumiy, and manuals produced under the guidance of A. Borokov, contrasting their treatment of sound classification, orthography, pronunciation, intonation, and stress with modern phonetic interpretations. Finally, it outlines ways to utilize these historical experiences …

title: Regional Government Information System and Financial Governance: Evidence from Mimika Regency
abstract: Purpose: This study analyzes the effectiveness and efficiency of the Regional Government Information System (Sistem Informasi Pemerintahan Daerah [SIPD]) affecting transparency and accountability of regional financial management in Mimika Regency, Indonesia. Research Methodology: A quantitative survey targeted 135 financial personnel across 57 Regional Apparatus Organizations, BPKAD verifiers, and Inspectorate auditors. Using Slovin formula, a purposive sample of 54 respondents was obtained. Data came from a 29-item Likert-scale questionnaire, validated via Pearson correlation (r > 0.195) and Cronbach alpha. IBM SPSS was used for descriptive statistics and multiple linear regression, including t-tests, F-tests, and R². Results: All four variables scored good. Effectiveness (B = 0.421, t = 3.876) and efficiency (B = 0.387, t = 3.542) significantly affected transparency (p < 0.05); effectiveness (B = 0.452, t = 4.102) and efficiency (B = 0.401, t = 3.765) significantly affected accountability (p < 0.05). F-tests confirmed joint significance (F = 28.417 and 31.862, p < 0.001). R² values were 0.478 and 0.524, respectively. Conclusions: SIPD implementation improves regional financial governance, with effectiveness and efficiency significantly driving transparency and accountability. Limitations: The study covers one regency using cross-sectional data, 52% and 48% of variance in tran…

title: From MRI-defined bone marrow lesions to pain, structural progression, and subchondral remodeling in knee osteoarthritis: an integrated multi-database bibliometric and text-mining analysis
abstract: Objective To characterize the publication landscape, intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and emerging clinical, mechanistic, and translational directions of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined bone marrow lesion (BML) research in knee osteoarthritis. Methods Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and PubMed were searched using core concepts related to knee osteoarthritis, MRI, and BMLs or bone marrow edema-like lesions. The searches initially identified 2,452 records, of which 2,415 were exported after database-level filters. Following cross-database deduplication, eligibility assessment, and application of the prespecified publication cutoff, 726 publications constituted the final integrated corpus. Descriptive bibliometrics, collaboration-network analysis, reference co-citation analysis, keyword and MeSH mapping, temporal thematic analysis, term frequency-inverse document frequency-based document clustering, and dictionary-based bridge-theme mapping were performed. Candidate cluster solutions from k = 2 to k = 10 were evaluated using within-cluster sum of squares, silhouette width, gap statistics, and repeated-subsample stability. Results Publication activity increased substantially from 1996 through 2025, with the partial 2026 count reflecting publications available by June 1. Osteoarthritis and Cartilage was the leading journal, and the United States, Australi…

title: Pharmacological targeting of xCT/system Xc− to modulate temozolomide sensitivity in glioma and glioblastoma preclinical models: a focused systematic review
abstract: Abstract Background Resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) remains a major barrier in glioblastoma treatment. The cystine/glutamate antiporter system Xc−, mainly through its xCT/SLC7A11 light-chain subunit, supports cystine uptake, glutathione synthesis and redox balance, making it a biologically plausible target for modifying TMZ response. This focused systematic review evaluated whether pharmacological xCT/system Xc−-relevant inhibition enhances TMZ sensitivity in glioma/glioblastoma preclinical models. Methods Searches were conducted in Web of Science, PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library, with supplementary Google Scholar screening, and were completed on 30 April 2026. Reference lists of the included preclinical studies were also screened as a supplementary citation-chasing method. No lower publication-date restriction was applied. Eligible studies were primary preclinical studies using glioma/glioblastoma models, TMZ treatment, and TMZ combined with a pharmacological xCT/system Xc−-relevant inhibitor or related intervention. Because the included studies differed in models, inhibitors, formulations, treatment conditions and outcome measures, findings were synthesised narratively. Results Ten non-retracted preclinical studies were included. Free-drug Sulfasalazine/SSZ and erastin studies provided the most directly relevant pharmacological evidence, but their effects differed by…

title: Pair-density-wave superconductivity in quasi-one-dimensional flat band system: Creutz lattice
abstract: Abstract Flat-band systems provide an ideal platform for studying strong electron correlations, in which multiple quasi-degenerate charge orders frequently coexist. Motivated by this context, we investigate the pair-density-wave (PDW) superconducting state in a quasi-one-dimensional Creutz lattice featuring two strictly flat bands. Using a renormalized mean-field approach for the strongly correlated t - J model, we obtain self-consistent solutions that demonstrate a PDW phase—characterized by finite-center-of-mass-momentum Cooper pairing—coexisting with charge density wave (CDW) and bond density wave (BDW) orders. Physically, this coexistence phenomenon originates from the perfect band nesting inherent to the flat-band system, which allows for changes in the particle momentum distributions without energy cost. Here, a pure PDW solution without CDW and BDW orders emerges in the underdoped regime when magnetic effects are neglected, while strong Hubbard correlations favor a pure CDW phase. We conclude that a robust PDW phase, accompanied by CDW and BDW orders, occupies the majority of the parameter space. Furthermore, both the PDW order parameter and its critical temperature scale linearly with the superexchange coupling strength—a hallmark of flat-band superconductivity. Overall, our results reveal that a PDW superconducting state can be realized on the Creutz lattice with stron…

title: Capacity remuneration mechanisms for decarbonized power systems
abstract: Motivated by generation system adequacy concerns, many European countries have introduced capacity remuneration mechanisms (CRMs) to ensure sufficient investments in power generation . However, it is uncertain whether the existing CRMs will promote sufficient adequacy and flexibility in a decarbonized power system , where supply and demand will become more weather-dependent. We assess the effectiveness of a centralized capacity market, a strategic reserve , and a decentralized capacity market via capacity subscriptions in a climate-neutral, weather-driven power system. We develop a co-simulation of two agent-based models simulating myopia in both operational and investment decisions. We simulate weather uncertainty by running the model with 40 different weather years. Our results from a case study based on the Netherlands indicate that a strategic reserve may increase electricity price volatility in the long-term. A centralized capacity market is more cost-effective than a strategic reserve, but administratively setting its parameters is prone to over- or underprocurement. Capacity subscription allows consumers to select their desired level of reliability. Results indicate that these decentralized capacity markets may yield a clearer signal for the needed dispatchable capacity and promote demand-side response, but it may be challenging to provide long-term certainty for investo…

title: Local energy monitoring to support smart energy management and decarbonized town development
abstract: Introduction With the increase in variable renewable energy and liberalization of the electricity retail market, the integrated energy management of demand and supply has become crucial, complementing traditional energy-saving efforts. Therefore, high-resolution energy demand-side information, accounting for household attributes and owned equipment, is essential. However, previous studies have identified energy consumption based on surveys of utility bill payments; this approach does not provide detailed, hourly data on electricity demand, which changes over time owing to lifestyle patterns and weather conditions. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the actual electricity consumption in residential buildings in Shinchi Town using the developed electricity monitoring system.Material and Method In support of regional disaster recovery initiatives, we developed a regional information and communication technology (ICT) system as a network interface for residents. As part of a social experiment, network terminals of the local ICT system were distributed to approximately 100 households in the town. Power monitoring data were collected via equipment installed in home distribution boards and centrally managed by a cloud server.Results and Conclusion We analyzed electric power consumption patterns, focusing on household attributes, seasonal variations in hot-water-supply device usage, an…

title: Impact of Regional and Seasonal Characteristics on Battery Electric Vehicle Operational Costs in the U.S.
abstract: This study investigates the operational cost competitiveness of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) in the United States, considering regional climates, energy prices, and driving patterns. By comparing BEVs with plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), and the alternative use of BEVs and conventional vehicles (Convs), the analysis incorporates thermal dynamometer tests, real-world vehicle miles traveled (VMT), and state-specific energy prices. Using detailed simulations, the study evaluates energy consumption across varying temperatures and driving distances. The findings reveal that, while BEVs remain cost-effective for short trips in moderate climates, PHEVs are more economical for long-range trips and cold environments, due to the excessive cost of using external direct current fast chargers (DCFCs) and reduced BEV efficiency at low temperatures. HEVs are identified as the most cost-efficient option in regions like New England, characterized by high residential electricity prices. These insights are critical for shaping vehicle electrification strategies, particularly under diverse regional and seasonal conditions, and for advancing policies on alternative energy and fuels.

title: Sharing the shortfall: Algorithmic solutions for fair demand curtailment in zonal power markets
Online Multivariate Regularized Distributional Regression for High-dimensional Probabilistic Electricity Price Forecasting
abstract: Probabilistic electricity price forecasting (PEPF) is vital for short-term electricity markets, yet the multivariate nature of day-ahead prices - spanning 24 consecutive hours - remains underexplored. At the same time, real-time decision-making requires methods that are both accurate and fast. We introduce an online algorithm for multivariate distributional regression models, allowing efficient modeling of the conditional means, variances, and dependence structures of electricity prices. The approach combines multivariate distributional regression with online coordinate descent and LASSO-type regularization (absolute shrinkage and selection operator), enabling scalable estimation in high-dimensional covariate spaces. Additionally, we propose a regularized estimation path over increasingly complex dependence structures, allowing for early stopping and avoiding overfitting. In a case study using historical data from the German day-ahead market, the proposed method yields interpretable and well-calibrated joint prediction intervals for the 24-dimensional price distribution and provides robust performance across a range of proper scoring rules. The results underscore the importance of modeling the dependence structure of electricity prices. Furthermore, we analyze the trade-off between predictive accuracy and computational costs for batch and online estimation and provide a high-pe…
